text: This paper proposes the use of asymmetric Gaussian-based statistical models for image categorization, utilizing Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques for accurate feature extraction and modeling. Adaptation models are employed to ensure the models are flexible and applicable to a variety of image types. Mixture models are also utilized to capture the complex structure of image data, while visualization techniques allow for easy interpretation and analysis. The proposed approach is applied to sports imagery, using the Gaussian distribution to model the features and accurately categorize images. Results show that this approach outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, providing a promising direction for future research in image categorization.

Association rule mining (ARM) has been paid more attention of both data mining users and database researchers in the last decade. Generation of various association rules from large distributed databases is the crucial task due to its intrinsic distribution of data sources. Identifying these type of distributed data sources requires a deep knowledge on data mining and planning for deployment in distributed environment. In this paper, a survey of the distributed framework for ARM is presented. It is observed that the parallelized nature of Apriori, Hadoop, MapReduce and Spark proves to be very efficient in Distributed association rule mining (DARM) environment. We expect that, the comprehensive review, references cited will convey foremost hypothetical issues and a guideline to the researcher in interesting research direction.

In order to obtain high classification accuracy and reduce time consumption for large-scale polarimetric synthetic-aperture radar (PolSAR) data. In this letter, we propose a fast semisupervised classification algorithm using histogram-based density estimation (called FSHDE). First, a noniterative collaborative training using our proposed Wishart-clustering selection strategy is designed to expand the labeled sample set from unlabeled samples. Second, a fast feature mapping based on histogram density estimation is employed to reliably capture the interaction of nonlinear features. Third, submodular optimization is used to select optimal subspace features to reduce feature correlation. Experimental results on synthetic and real PolSAR data indicate that FSHDE greatly reduces the time consumption and improves the accuracy for terrain classification compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

The prevalence and sophistication of port scanning attacks on computer networks have been a major cause of concern for security practitioners. In this paper, we propose a novel approach based on the immune system and artificial intelligence concepts to detect malicious TCP port scanning activities. Our proposed approach employs anomaly detection techniques coupled with classification algorithms to classify network traffic as either benign or malicious. The core of our approach is the dendritic cell algorithm, which simulates the immune system's capability to detect foreign entities. We designed and implemented a prototype system that monitors network traffic, captures TCP/IP packets, and analyzes them to detect port scanning activities. Our experimental results using publicly available datasets showed that the proposed approach performed well in detecting malicious port scanning activities with high accuracy rates. Given the increasing complexity of port scanning attacks, we believe that our approach can provide a valuable contribution to computer architecture and network security by detecting and mitigating such attacks. Finally, we discuss potential future directions, including integrating password policies in the detection process, which could further enhance the system's effectiveness.

Cloud computing has become a popular approach to delivering computing resources and services for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, the energy consumption of cloud computing has become a major concern due to the increasing demand for energy-efficient cloud computing systems. In this paper, we propose an energy-aware virtual machine scheduling method for cloudlets in wireless metropolitan area networks (WMANs). It aims to optimize the energy consumption of cloudlets while maintaining high performance evaluation. Our proposed method considers the green computing aspect to reduce the carbon footprint of cloud computing. Furthermore, our method also takes into account social computing aspects, which enable social interactions between VMs for better resource utilization. Finally, we explore the potential of blockchain technology to enhance the security and privacy aspects of the proposed method. Overall, this paper presents a novel approach to address the energy efficiency challenge in cloud computing and paves the way for future research in this field.

This paper presents the design and implementation of an iris and voice recognition system for a smart doorbell. The system utilizes iris recognition technology for personal identification and authentication, and voice recognition to enable hands-free and personalized access control. The paper discusses the key steps of the implementation process, including feature extraction and task analysis, as well as the selected hardware components, such as switched mode power supplies and field programmable gate arrays. Furthermore, the paper outlines the computer architecture and integration of the system into smart homes for seamless user experience. The successful implementation of this system could lead to improved security and accessibility in households and other applications.

Information-centric wireless networks have become increasingly popular due to the widespread use of wireless networks and the internet. The emergence of games and delays in the delivery of content has prompted the development of edge cache-based intelligent content delivery. This method aims to reduce delays and improve the quality of content delivery. Furthermore, the significant increase in demand for green products has led to the optimization of network infrastructure to reduce energy consumption. Conference organizers have also adopted this method to ensure high-quality multimedia content delivery. The future of edge cache-based intelligent content delivery is promising, and it is likely to play an essential role in meeting the increasing demand for quality multimedia content delivery. The continued evolution of wireless networks and the increasing adoption of the internet as a primary source of information will undoubtedly continue to drive the development of information-centric wireless networks.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is increasingly becoming more prevalent in our daily lives, with smart phones and other connected devices serving as gateways to these systems. However, this interconnectivity also creates new opportunities for malicious actors to exploit vulnerabilities in these systems and disrupt their operations. In order to address these emerging security concerns, this paper proposes a Bayesian model updating method for detecting malware in IoT services. By leveraging the power of classification algorithms and Bayes methods, this approach is capable of effectively analyzing and identifying potential threats in IoT systems. The proposed method is tested and evaluated through a series of experiments, demonstrating its efficacy in both training and live server environments. This work represents an important advance in our ability to detect and prevent malware in the rapidly evolving landscape of IoT services.

The integration of wearable wireless devices and cloud computing in e-health systems has significantly improved their effectiveness and availability. Patients can upload their personal health information (PHI) files to the cloud, from where the health service providers (HSPs) can obtain appropriate information to determine the health state. This system not only reduces the costs associated to healthcare but also provides timely diagnosis to save lives. However, a number of privacy concerns arise while sharing sensitive information. In this paper, we propose a novel privacy-preserving patient health information sharing scheme, which allows HSPs to access and search PHI files in a secure yet efficient manner. We make use of the searchable encryption technique with keyword range search and multikeyword search. The proposed privacy-preserving equality test protocol allows different types of numeric comparison searches on encrypted data. We also use a variant of bloom filter and message authentication code to classify PHI files, filter false data, and check integrity of search results. The simulations on real-world and synthetic data show the feasibility and efficiency of the system, and security analysis proves the privacy-preservation properties.

Vehicular Ad Hoc Networking (VANET) is an emerging technology defined with main motive of avoiding on road accidents and provide safety and life critical applications to users in a well-organized manner. We present current challenges in designing VANET protocols through extensive survey from the perspective of decentralized congestion control (DCC) strategies. The challenges in routing and security applications are also outlined briefly. Internet of things (IoT) will be the future networking system in which all things will be connected to interact. In the near future, VANETs will be the main part of IoT networks because of its safety and infotainment applications. A lot of work is done in this area, still, the industry thrusts for more efficient and robust design. This paper highlights various research challenges, which will help other researchers who wish to work in this area.

It is essential to develop proper energy management strategies (EMSs) with broad adaptability for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). This paper utilizes deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to develop EMSs for a series HEV due to DRL's advantages of requiring no future driving information in derivation and good generalization in solving energy management problem formulated as a Markov decision process. History cumulative trip information is also integrated for effective state of charge guidance in DRL-based EMSs. The proposed method is systematically introduced from offline training to online applications; its learning ability, optimality, and generalization are validated by comparisons with fuel economy benchmark optimized by dynamic programming, and real-time EMSs based on model predictive control (MPC). Simulation results indicate that without a priori knowledge of future trip, original DRL-based EMS achieves an average 3.5% gap from benchmark, superior to MPC-based EMS with accurate prediction; after further applying output frequency adjustment, a mean gap of 8.7%, which is comparable with MPC-based EMS with mean prediction error of 1 m/s, is maintained with concurrently noteworthy improvement in reducing engine start times. Besides, its impressive computation speed of about 0.001 s per simulation step proves its practical application potential, and this method is independent of powertrain topology such that it is applicative for any type of HEVs even when future driving information is unavailable.

These studies demonstrate a combination of tested methods to separate lung and heart sound signals' (LS-HS) principal components recorded using a digital dual stethoscope. Initially, when these raw signals are acquired, their principal components intertwine in the characteristics of the frequency and time domains. Applying Independent Component Analysis (ICA) combined with Empirical Mode Decomposition allows separation of their origin. Further, Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) were utilized to determine to which specific class of components they belong. Each set of recorded signals was evaluated and the outcomes were compared against the verified reference group. As cardiopulmonary diseases represent a major global health concern, this can be helpful in an early screening for distinct cardiopulmonary problems manifested by peculiar acoustic indicators.

In a geological study, an important step is to determine the type of sedimentary rock or its grain size. Such a determination requires accurate analysis in the field or in a laboratory. As the size of the study area grows, this activity can be time consuming and error prone because the number of specialists working under rigid criteria also increases. This paper proposes a novel methodology to classify grain size using unique wavelength reflectance data and artificial neural networks. The results indicate that the proposed method can be reliably used in the field.

This research paper aims to optimize the execution of dynamic robot movements through learning control. The study focuses on the use of adaptation models to improve the trajectory of robot movements, which is important since robots are expected to perform dynamic tasks with precision and efficiency. Computational modeling is used to predict the outcome of different controls in executing dynamic movements, and stability analysis is conducted to ensure the success of robot movements. Tracking is also an important part of the study, as it helps in monitoring the performance of robots during dynamic movements. Lastly, task analysis is conducted to optimize the execution of robot movements by identifying the necessary controls and adaptations required in different tasks. Overall, this research work presents a promising approach to improving the performance of robots in executing dynamic movements through learning control.

This paper presents an interactive AI system for linguistic education built on a virtual reality environment utilizing user generated content. The system is designed to enhance the learning experience through the integration of Google's artificial intelligence technology, interactive games, and speech recognition. Additionally, the system incorporates databases and engines to provide personalized feedback to users, allowing for a more effective language learning process. Through the use of virtual reality, users are able to immerse themselves in a dynamic and engaging environment, promoting interactive learning and retention of linguistic concepts. The incorporation of user generated content allows for a dynamic and evolving platform, providing users with the ability to create and share their own educational materials. Overall, this interactive AI system provides an innovative approach to linguistic education utilizing cutting-edge technology and user-driven content creation.

This paper considers the transceiver design for uplink massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems with channel sparsity in the angular domain. Recent progress has shown that sparsity-learning-based blind signal detection is able to retrieve the channel and data by using massage-passing-based sparse matrix factorization methods. Short pilot sequences are inserted into user packets to eliminate the so-called phase and permutation ambiguities inherent in sparse matrix factorization. In this paper, to exploit the knowledge of these short pilot sequences more efficiently, we propose a semi-blind channel-and-signal estimation (SCSE) scheme in which the knowledge of the pilot sequences are integrated into the message passing algorithm for sparse matrix factorization. The SCSE algorithm involves enumeration over all possible user permutations, and so is time-consuming when the number of users is relatively large. To reduce complexity, we further develop the simplified SCSE (S-SCSE) to accommodate systems with a large number of users. The numerical results show that our semi-blind signal detection scheme substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art blind detection and training-based schemes in the short-pilot regime.

Lung nodules that overlap with ribs and clavicles in chest radiographs can be difficult to be detected by radiologists as well as by computer-aided detection systems. Removing bony structures would result in better visualization of undetectable lesions. Our purpose in this study was to develop a deep-learning scheme to separate ribs and clavicles from soft tissue in chest radiographs. To achieve this, we developed a mixture of anatomy-specific, orientation-frequency-specific (ASOFS) deep neural network convolution (NNC) experts. Anatomy-specific (AS) architecture was designed to separate bony structures from soft tissue in different lung segments. The orientation-frequency-specific (OFS) was designed to decompose bone and soft-tissue structures into specific orientation-frequency components of different scales using a multi-resolution decomposition technique. For evaluation, we used a database of 118 chest radiographs with pulmonary nodules. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation showed that our ASOFS NNC was superior to a state-of-the-art bone-suppression technique. Particularly, our NNC scheme separated ribs and clavicles from soft tissue, while it was better able to maintain the conspicuity of lung nodules and vessels, comparing to the reference technique. Therefore, our deep-learning scheme can be useful for radiologists as well as CAD systems in detection of lung nodules in chest radiographs.

In this paper, we introduce a method for the segmentation and classification of lung nodules using Split Bregman and SVM Classifier. The proposed approach is based on the concept of image segmentation, with a focus on lung nodules detected through computed tomography scans. The use of Support Vector Machines (SVM) is proposed for the classification of lung nodules, utilizing feature extraction and nonhomogeneous media to improve accuracy. The proposed method is validated using computational modeling, demonstrating promising results in the segmentation and classification of lung nodules. The potential applications of this approach include improving the diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer, which is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally. Overall, our approach provides a new perspective on the use of sophisticated image analysis techniques, which can lead to more accurate and reliable diagnosis of lung nodules.

In this paper, we propose an algorithm that can prove the objectivity of the image reading that depends on personal / subjective judgment in the clinic and can prove it by the scientific method. We analyze the characteristics of liver cancer in ultrasound images by using the deep - run algorithm, and propose an algorithm that can diagnose lesions using extracted features.

This paper presents an analysis of hate speech detection using recurrent neural networks (RNNs) on Twitter. RNNs have been proven effective in various natural language processing tasks including speech recognition and data mining. The primary focus of this study is on the training of the RNNs with respect to data mining techniques to identify and classify hate speech. The study analyzes the use of RNNs in identifying and classifying hate speech in Twitter data. Results indicate that RNNs are a promising approach for identifying hate speech in social media platforms. The study provides insights into the potential of RNNs in addressing hate speech and highlights the importance of continued research in this area.

In this study, we obtain life log data from visibility information using smart glass which is a wearable device. In the proposed system, it consists of a text data collection part by cooperation between smart glass and image recognition API and activity recognition part. The activity recognition part incorporates multidimensional scaling analysis method and correspondence analysis for classifying data. As a result of utilizing the development system in real life, it was able to detect similarities and events for behavior from the difference of the object caught on sight.

In this paper, a robust neural network fault estimation approach is proposed for nonlinear dynamic systems, with a specific application to wind turbine systems. The approach utilizes mathematical models, observers, and neural networks to accurately diagnose faults and predict system behavior. The algorithm is designed to be robust against measurement noise and model uncertainties. Furthermore, stability analysis is performed to ensure the stability of the closed-loop system. Experimental results performed on wind turbine systems demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed approach in fault diagnosis and detection. The combination of neural networks and mathematical modeling provides a powerful tool for real-time and accurate estimation of faults in complex, nonlinear systems such as wind turbines.

The study intends to improve walkability in the walkways by providing better illuminance levels. Firstly, the study has defined the existing typology of walkways in the campus then selected the worse type-with less protection from the sun-for further improvement. The methodological tools used in the study were: a field survey, illuminance meter, and an Integrated Environmental Solution Virtual Environment (IESVE) software packages. The questionnaire was used to understand the right feedback on the existing walkways. The lowest ranked satisfactions received from the respondents were from excessive brightness and temperature in the walkways. Thus, this paper proposes a successful envelope layout solution that provides better lighting levels and glare-free spaces. The Islamic style pattern used in the campus design was considered for the proposed simulations. Light meter was used to measure the existing illuminance levels in the corridors. Accordingly, four cases with several parameters such as the integration of shading elements: fully or partially, and vertically or horizontally in addition to the flooring materials were conducted in the simulation. Lastly, the study could provide a design layout as a proposal that provides glare-free walkways.

This paper presents an approach for short-term forecasting of stock prices using long short term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks (RNNs). The stock markets are a complex and dynamic system that requires accurate forecasting methods to provide traders with useful information for decision-making. LSTMs are a type of RNN that are capable of capturing long-term dependencies in time series data. This approach is based on designing a neural network architecture that includes logic gates and optimization techniques to enhance the prediction accuracy. The network is trained on historical data to learn the underlying patterns and relationships that exist between the input features and the target output. The model is evaluated on real market data and achieves promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This study demonstrates the potential of using LSTM RNNs for short-term forecasting of complex financial systems like the stock markets, and emphasizes the importance of effective data models and optimization methods for achieving accurate predictions.

With the increasing demand for Internet of Things (IoT) devices, there is a need for an efficient and reliable communication system. The use of sensors in the IoT network has enabled monitoring of various environments, leading to the development of distributed wideband sensing-based architecture. This architecture has enabled the use of unlicensed radio frequencies for massive IoT communications, thereby reducing the cost and increasing flexibility. The use of wireless fidelity (Wi-Fi) has enabled the communication between IoT devices and improved the reliability of the system. However, the system still faces challenges such as the allocation of resources, especially in the presence of narrowband signals. Resource management is therefore required to ensure efficient communication and minimize interference. In conclusion, the distributed wideband sensing-based architecture is a promising solution for unlicensed massive IoT communications, and further research is required to address the challenges associated with resource management.

In this paper, we present the implementation of a prototype for detecting and diagnosing cotton leaf diseases using a rule-based system. Cotton is a significant crop, and diseases can significantly impact its yield and quality. Our system aims to provide farmers with an efficient and convenient tool to identify diseases early and take appropriate measures. The system uses servers to store data on common cotton leaf diseases and their symptoms, as well as data on microorganisms responsible for these diseases. The system also employs expert systems to process input data, and based on it, generate diagnostic reports with recommended measures to control or treat the disease. The rule-based system ensures that the output is consistent with the input and maximizes the accuracy of the diagnostic report. Overall, this prototype system provides a powerful tool for farmers to effectively diagnose and manage cotton leaf diseases, leading to higher crop yields and better quality.

This paper presents a practical procedure regarding inertia estimation and speed loop auto-tuning for sensorless interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drives. In many applications, well-tuned speed controller is essential to enable dynamic and stable drive operations. However, high-performance speed controller design requires system parameters such as inertia which are unknown at the beginning of drive commissioning. Manual trial-and-error tuning is unattractive due to its blind, lengthy, non-optimal, and potentially unsafe nature. On the other hand, model-based tuning through inertia estimation has unique challenges at this step of self-commissioning. Determining the test torque for a safe and reasonably short test in inertia estimation is a real practical problem because the total inertia can be in wide range in different mechanical systems. Furthermore, feedback controllers are not usable to automatically determine the test torque due to unknown motor parameters. As a solution, this paper proposes an automated test torque selection procedure. Then it identifies the inertia and lastly tunes the speed controller using the identified parameter. Overall, a fully automated speed-loop auto-tuning method is proposed which aims minimal operator involvement. The findings are experimentally verified on an IPMSM drive. In addition, the proposed method can easily be extended to different motor types and sensored or sensorless vector control strategies.

This paper presents a novel approach to wireless resource management using constrained deep learning. The proposed method incorporates a task analysis to identify the optimal resource allocation for a given set of tasks, and uses a cost function to guide the learning process. The training process involves a deep neural network with constraints imposed on the output, ensuring that the allocation of resources is consistent with the task requirements. The proposed method is tested on a wireless network and shows significant improvements in resource allocation compared to traditional methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of using constrained deep learning for wireless resource management, highlighting the potential for future research in this area.

In the present age of the Internet of Things (IoT), the authentication of edge devices is a crucial challenge. This paper presents a Protean Authentication Scheme, which is a time-bound dynamic key generation-based authentication technique for IoT edge nodes in outdoor deployments. The proposed scheme utilizes logic gates and microprogramming to generate set of dynamic keys that enhances the security of the system. The Protean Authentication Scheme employs a time-bound approach that ensures that the system is secure during the entire key lifecycle. Moreover, the scheme also utilizes random access memory to store and handle large keys efficiently. The scheme employs cryptography to ensure the safety of sensitive data and to keep the keys secure during transmission. The proposed scheme is compared with the existing approaches, and the simulation results show that the Protean Authentication Scheme outperforms the existing methods in terms of security, efficiency, and key management. Overall, the Protean Authentication Scheme presents an effective approach to the authentication of IoT edge nodes in outdoor environments.

Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) refers to a group of sensors used for monitoring and recording the physical conditions of the environment and organizing the collected data at a central location. WSN has no mechanism that can organize or check the broadcast of information through the nodes. Nodes themselves are able to transmit the sensed information towards the Base Station, causing greater vulnerability of data being gathered and fiddled with. Amongst many such attacks, Rushing Attack specially is a frequently adapted strategy in On-demand protocol. The counter measure available for such kind of attack is not effective enough as most of the approaches have their own limitations. This work focuses on ill effects of Rushing Attack under different conditions with an intend to find out such limitations of each of the earlier adopted counter measures.

Security assurance in a computer system can be viewed as distinguishing between self and non-self. Artificial Immune Systems (AIS) are a class of machine learning (ML) techniques inspired by the behavior of innate biological immune systems, which have evolved to accurately classify self-behavior from non-self-behavior. This work aims to leverage AIS-based ML techniques for identifying certain behavioral traits in high level hardware descriptions, including unsafe or undesirable behaviors, whether such behavior exists due to human error during development, or due to intentional, malicious circuit modifications, known as hardware Trojans, without the need for a golden reference model. We explore the use of Negative Selection and Clonal Selection, which have historically been applied to malware detection on software binaries, to detect potentially unsafe or malicious behavior in hardware. We present a software tool which analyzes Trojan-inserted benchmarks, extracts their control and data-flow graphs (CDFGs), and uses this to train an AIS behavior model, against which new hardware descriptions may be tested. The proposed model is capable of detecting the specified (Trojan or Trojan-like) behavior with an accuracy of ~85% and an average false negative rate of 12.6% for Negative Selection and 12.8% for Clonal Selection.

The concept of qualitative simulation is central to qualitative reasoning, so it is worth considering its properties in more detail. Some of these properties have been extensively worked out and proven formally to apply to any theory of qualitative dynamics. Others are based more on experience with qualitative simulation techniques applied to a variety of problems and domains. We begin by summarizing the basic ideas, bringing together concepts introduced in chapters 5, 6, and 7. Then we discuss how existence and continuity interact with reasoning about change. Finally, we discuss some formal properties of qualitative simulation, ending with an open question.

In this paper, we propose an observer-based super-twisting sliding mode control with fuzzy variable gains (OST-FVG) for general second-order nonlinear systems. First, the super-twisting observer with fuzzy variable gains is designed for state estimation, for which we show finite-time convergence of the estimation error to zero under the bounded disturbance. Then, together with the proposed observer, the sliding mode control with fuzzy variable gains is designed to ensure precise tracking control performance and to alleviate the chattering phenomenon. We apply the OSTFVG to the overactuated quadrotor modeled by the second-order nonlinear system within the quaternion framework, which resolves underactuation and singularity problems appeared in standard quadrotors. In simulation results of attitude and position control, the fuzzy mechanism implemented in the OSTFVG guarantees faster convergence of the quadrotor to the desired position and more precision tracking performance compared to the standard observer-based super-twisting sliding mode control.

This paper presents improved probes that enable fully-passive wireless recording of neural activation. The probes utilize wireless communication and operate within the radio frequency (RF) range. To improve sensitivity and performance, the probes incorporate impedance matching techniques. The authors compare their new probes to existing ones through the use of phantoms and particle measurements. Overall, the improved probes provide a promising solution for wireless sensor networks used in neural recording.

Feature extraction is to transform a text document from any format into a list of features that can be easily processed by text classification techniques. Feature extraction is one of significant preprocessing techniques in data mining and text classification that computes features value in documents. Hence, efficient feature extraction techniques like the BM25 and term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) techniques are normally utilized in term weighting. Nevertheless, BM25 is not a single function that is utilized to exceedingly correct very long documents. This problem cannot denote the helpfulness or importance of confident features, and decreases the efficiency of classification. This paper presents a comparative study of feature extraction techniques. Two techniques were evaluated BM25 and TF-IDF to weight the terms on Twitter. In this paper, TF-IDF feature extraction technique is presented to compare between the two techniques. The experiments show that TF-IDF improves the performance evaluation of feature extraction according to the maximum value of F1-measure is 89.77 for TF-IDF and 89.16 for BM25.

Existing forensic techniques for image manipulation localization crucially assume that probe pixels belong to one of exactly two classes, genuine or manipulated. This letter argues that this convention fuels mis-labeling particularly in unsupervised settings, where singular but genuine content or the presence of multiple distinct manipulations may easily induce non-optimal partitions of the feature space. We propose to relax constraints via a greedy n-ary clustering approach, which we instantiate exemplarily in the popular pixel descriptor space of residual co-occurrences. Experimental results on widely used public benchmark datasets highlight the benefits of our approach.

The use of networked medical devices in providing medical services has been increasing rapidly in recent years. However, the security of these devices has become a critical concern. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the security vulnerabilities, attacks, countermeasures, and regulations of networked medical devices. The review covers the wired and wireless communication protocols, monitoring and control mechanisms, and sensors used in medical devices. Several security issues are identified that include unauthorized access to patient data, hacking of medical devices, and denial-of-service attacks. To counter these threats, various security strategies have been proposed such as encryption, authentication, and access control mechanisms. Additionally, regulatory frameworks for medical devices are discussed including FDA regulations, HIPAA privacy rules, and cybersecurity guidelines. It is concluded that the security of networked medical devices is a complex issue and requires substantial efforts from stakeholders such as policy-makers, device manufacturers, and healthcare providers to ensure that patient safety and privacy are not compromised. The concept of the Body Area Network is also introduced as a possible solution to increase device security.

The application of data mining and machine learning techniques in the field of agriculture has the potential to revolutionize the industry. This paper focuses on the utilization of support vector machines and Bayes methods in analyzing agricultural data. The issue of null value in the data is addressed, and various techniques for handling it are discussed. The importance of training data is also highlighted, and the role of communication systems in the process of data analysis is explored. The results of the analysis are expected to assist farmers in making more informed decisions, leading to increased productivity and better crop yields. Overall, this paper highlights the potential of data mining and machine learning techniques in the agriculture industry and provides insights into the techniques that can be used.

Text classification is an important research area in intelligent systems. Multinomial Naive Bayes is a commonly used method for text classification. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical scheme for assigning components in Multinomial Naive Bayes text classifier. The proposed scheme uses histograms to represent the frequency of words in a document and divides the vocabulary into subgroups. The classifier is trained on the training data, and the measurement of the classifier performance is based on the estimation of the probability of a document belonging to a particular class. The proposed scheme increases the efficiency of the text classification task and simplifies the task analysis. The experimental results show that the proposed hierarchical scheme achieves a better accuracy than the traditional approach. The proposed scheme can be applied to various text classification tasks and can provide valuable insights into the classification process.

This paper provides an overview of machine learning methods for identifying malware in the Android platform. Malware is a significant threat to mobile devices and can cause data breaches and financial losses. Feature extraction is an essential technique used to extract the most relevant characteristics of malware, including code and behavior patterns. Several tools have been developed to automate the process of feature extraction, such as Androguard and Apktool. Radio frequency is also a useful tool for identifying malware by analyzing a device's wireless signals. Support vector machines are an effective machine learning method for detecting malware by classifying extracted features. Static analysis is another useful method for identifying malware that involves analyzing the code without executing it. Machine learning methods have proven to be effective in detecting and identifying Android malware, and the hope is to continue developing more powerful and accurate methods for the future.

This paper proposes a longitudinally misalignment-insensitive dual-band wireless power and data transfer system for fast-moving vehicles' position detection. The system comprises transmitting antennas and receiving antennas, which are connected to wireless sensor networks for communication purposes. The system enables wireless communication between the transmitting and receiving antennas, thereby facilitating the transfer of both power and data. In addition, the system employs couplings to ensure that the dual-band wireless power and data transfer are insensitive to misalignments. The results of the study show that the proposed system achieves high efficiency and robustness, making it a reliable solution for fast-moving vehicle position detection. This paper contributes significantly to the development of wireless power and data transfer systems, which are essential components of many modern technologies.

A new recursive identification algorithm with output weighted cosine basis functions (WCS) is investigated for the time-varying systems. After introducing a weight factor to the output of a time-varying process within the current time window, the weighted time-varying parameters, which are expanded into the virtual even periodic functions, are explicitly approximated by the cosine series. Following the orthogonality of the trigonometric functions, the parameter estimation problem becomes to the estimation problem of the series coefficients with respect to each degree of the cosine harmonic term in recursive manner. It is demonstrated that weight factor decreases the degree of cosine series and suppress the series approximation error so that the proposed algorithm has better tracking performance for rapid-variation than the conventional basis functions based identification algorithms and the existing standard methods such as RLS, LMS/NLMS, AP/BOP.

In computer numerical control machine tools, using machining simulation to prevent collision have become more popular due to higher machining speed. The 3D reconstruction of objects is one of the main goals for 3D machine vision is presented in this paper. In the stereo vision, a 2D edge feature detection algorithm designed by integration of vision base image processing which can generate a new straight line on the edges of the object. The matching comparison process is solved with the Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) to obtain the results of a new straight line matching to find disparity from distance between feature points on plane. The disparity can be obtained from two cameras by overlapped two objects that show the different positions of two objects in horizontal using the principles of geometry of two cameras. The different position results can find the coordinates of 3D (x, y, z) to be generating the straight lines on edge of the 3D objects. This method is simply and easier in the computing process for the reconstruction of the object. The results obtain are presented with an effective and accurate model and can take results input into the 3D recognition process.

This paper proposes a multi-criteria model for users trust management in ad-hoc mobile cloud computing. The concept of cloud computing and its applications in mobile handsets and peer-to-peer computing is introduced. The trust management mechanism for mobile nodes in ad-hoc mobile cloud computing is a challenging issue which needs to be addressed. The proposed model considers different criteria such as reputation, reliability, similarity and social relationships for assessing the trustworthiness of the mobile nodes. The use of web services for implementing the proposed model is also discussed. This multi-criteria trust management model for ad-hoc mobile cloud computing can enhance the trustworthiness of the mobile nodes and improve the overall security of the system.

In recent years, speech separation has become an important research field in speech processing. This paper proposes an audio-visual deep clustering model for speech separation, which utilizes both audio and visual information to improve robustness in noisy environments. The model includes visualization of the spectrogram and lips, as well as the use of hidden Markov models for training. Results show that incorporating visual information improves the accuracy and robustness of speech separation. This approach has potential applications in various domains, such as noise suppression in phone calls and improving speech recognition in videos.

Text steganography involves concealing secret information within a cover text in a manner that is not easily detectable. Conversely, text steganalysis aims to identify the presence of hidden information within a text. In recent years, there has been increased interest in the use of machine learning techniques for text steganalysis. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for text steganalysis based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). We explore the role of feature extraction, correlation and data mining in improving the performance of the TS-RNN algorithm. Specifically, our approach uses RNN models to capture the semantics of text and probability distribution of word sequences in order to detect hidden messages. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art steganalysis techniques, achieving higher accuracy and lower false positive rates. Our findings suggest that RNNs have great potential for application in text steganalysis and can be used as an effective tool for detecting hidden information in textual data.

This paper proposes a method of using synthetic aperture radar imaging to study the interior of comets through time-domain back-projection. The analysis of time-domain is applied, and the dielectrics are considered to advance the computing of imaging. Finite difference methods are used to model the mathematics of this approach, and computational modeling techniques are implemented to simulate the behavior of electromagnetic waves inside comets during the imaging process. The results show that this method has great potential to improve our understanding of the interior structure of comets, such as their density distribution and the presence of subsurface layers. Moreover, the proposed technique has the advantage of being non-destructive to the object under study, making it a valuable tool for the scientific community to explore the universe.

This work evaluates strategies to reduce the computational cost of Gabriel graph-based classifiers, in order to make them more suitable for hardware implementation. An analysis of the impact of the bit precision provides insights on the model's robustness for lower precision arithmetic. Additionally, a parallelization technique is proposed in order to improve the efficiency of the support edges computation. The results show that the lower bit precision models are statistically equivalent to the reference double-precision ones. Also, the implementation of the proposed parallel algorithm provides a significant reduction in the running time when applied in large datasets, while maintaining its accuracy.

Relationship between the delay and Doppler shift with the radar return is nonlinear in nature. Therefore, a nonlinear estimator based on sparse kernel least mean square algorithm is proposed. Further, an adaptive kernel width optimization technique is proposed to lower the computational complexity and for simple implementation. An expression for the Cramer-Rao lower bound is derived and validated for the proposed estimator over linear frequency modulated, and orthogonal frequency division multiplexed radar systems.

Enhancing the contrast of target and clutter is a crucial issue in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image target detection. In this paper, we define a novel subspace, called minimal clutter-to-signal ratio (MCSR) subspace, which can minimize the clutter-to-signal ratio (CSR) by projecting the feature vector to the subspace. Based on MCSR, a novel polarimetric contrast enhancement method is proposed. The MCSR subspace is learned based on the commonly used polarimetric feature vectors extracted from the labeled training SAR image pixels. The feature vectors extracted form candidate SAR image pixels are projected to the MCSR subspace. By calculating the square norm of each transformed feature vector, an enhanced image can be obtained. It is demonstrated that the existing optimization of polarimetric contrast enhancement (OPCE) is a special case of the proposed method to some extent. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the traditional OPCE method on the RadarSat-2 SAR data.

The packaging and delivery of web systems is an essential aspect of software engineering that requires comprehensive attention to various factors such as computational modeling, ISO standards, quality management, and software as a service. The key objective of this paper is to present a real approach towards web systems packaging and delivery, which can help developers and system administrators to overcome the challenges associated with the process. The computational modeling techniques can enable developers to determine the appropriate packaging and delivery mechanisms for web applications, while adhering to the ISO standards can ensure the compatibility and interoperability of the systems. In addition, employing quality management practices can help to ensure the reliability and robustness of the systems, while software as a service can offer cost-effective and flexible solutions for delivering web systems to end-users. The proposed approach can serve as a useful guideline for the development and deployment of web systems in various domains, ranging from e-commerce and e-learning to healthcare and finance.

This paper proposes a new technique named Canonical ELM for improving the performance of Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) on multivariate regression tasks. Canonical ELM utilizes canonical correlations, a set of measures that quantify the strength of the relationship between linear combinations of two sets of variables, to identify the most relevant input features for multivariate regression. By incorporating canonical correlations into the training process of ELMs, the proposed method achieves superior accuracy compared to traditional ELMs. The application of Canonical ELM in signal and prediction algorithms demonstrates its effectiveness in improving the performance of supervised learning on predictive models through multivariate regression. This study highlights the significance of incorporating correlation analysis into the development of machine learning algorithms to achieve better prediction accuracy.

This paper proposes a novel approach to template-based face recognition by discovering identity-specific activation patterns in deep descriptors. The use of deep learning has greatly improved the performance of face recognition systems. However, most existing methods do not take into account the identity-specific features of each individual. To address this issue, the proposed method utilizes a training pipeline that considers the unique characteristics of each individual's face. By analyzing the measurement of the activation patterns of deep descriptors, identity-specific features are identified and utilized during the face recognition process. The proposed approach is evaluated on several standard face recognition protocols and achieves state-of-the-art performance. This novel method has the potential to greatly improve the accuracy and reliability of face recognition systems, especially in complex real-world scenarios where individual identities need to be reliably identified.

Three-dimensional displays have become increasingly popular in recent years, with many applications in everyday life. However, the accurate detection of objects in such displays remains a challenge. This paper proposes MCF3D: Multi-Stage Complementary Fusion for Multi-Sensor 3D Object Detection, a method that leverages the use of multiple sensors, including laser radar and cameras, to enhance object detection accuracy. The proposed approach utilizes a multi-stage fusion process, enabling the complementary fusion of proposals, feature extraction, and two-dimensional displays across sensors. Through extensive experimentation, MCF3D has been shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance in 3D object detection, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods. The proposed approach has significant implications for the development of improved object detection in 3D displays, enabling more accurate and efficient object tracking and recognition in a variety of settings.

Measures of node centrality that describe the importance of a node within a network are crucial for understanding the behavior of social networks and graphs. In this paper, we address the problem of distributed node centrality identification. In particular, we focus our attention on alpha-centrality, which can be seen as a generalization of eigenvector centrality, particularly suitable for graphs with asymmetric interactions. In this setting, our contribution is twofold: first we derive a distributed protocol where agents can locally compute their alpha-centrality index by means of local interactions; then we propose a novel consensus-algorithm running in parallel to the alpha-centrality estimator, which converges towards a weighted average of the initial conditions, where the weights are dictated by the alpha-centrality vector. The proposed algorithm finds application in social networks, where agreement protocols typically place more value on experts and influencers than on the rest of users. Simulations results are provided to corroborate the theoretical findings.

Alfa-Beta method has extensively used since its formulation by Akagi in 1983 [1] and become the classical wide spread solution for shunt active power filtering.For majority of situations this has a good efficiency and simplicity both for analogical and digital implementation. The development of vector 3D method gives o more rigorous approach, with the price of a more complex and expensive implementation, sometimes unjustified. However, for some special cases its utility is revealed.The purpose of the paper is to derive a comparative analysis of these methods, in a unitary way, based on geometrical representation and vector variables which enable a good evaluation from qualitative and quantitative point of view of characteristics and specific problems. Thus, may be revealed the steps and connections where problems occur with corresponding effects.The tools implied are 2D and 3D simulations for the parameter evolution when the algorithms are suited. The Mathcad mathematical interpreter enables a natural representation of vector operations, easy to be verified formally.

The aim of this short paper or extended abstract is develop an intelligent lifelong learning cancer care framework that will be adapted by the King Hussein Cancer Center in Jordan. Cancer Care is defined as "Comprehensive care for the cancer patient as a whole including all their needs - not just the medical and physical ones - using the services of many professionals working together" [3] . Lifelong learning is about continuous development throughout a life time. Our lives, as humans, span many decades in which the environment we grew up in is in a continuous state of change. Therefore, we need to be empowered to deal with emerging challenges and thrive in a continuously changing environment. Clearly, there are multiple interactions that take place between an individual human and the surrounding environment. The Oxford dictionary defines "interaction" as "Communication or direct involvement with someone or something". Another definition: "A particular way in which matter, fields, and atomic and subatomic particles affect one another, e.g., through gravitation or electromagnetism" [4] . Therefore, communication though interactions takes place and in certain times for precious causes and purposes. On the one hand, such communication is didactic with complex interactions between an individual and the environment, and on the other hand between an individual and other members of the community - who themselves are continuously changing.

JavaScript plays an important role in web applications and services, which is used by millions of web pages in optimizing interface design, embedding dynamic texts, reading and writing HTML elements, validating form data, responding to browser events, controlling cookies and much more. However, since JavaScript is cross-platform and can be executed dynamically, it has been a major vehicle for web-based attacks. Existing solutions work by performing static analysis or monitoring program execution dynamically. However, since the heavy use of obfuscation techniques, many methods no longer apply to malicious JavaScript code detection, and it has been a huge challenge to de-obfuscate obfuscated malicious JavaScript code accurately. In this paper, we propose a hybrid analysis method combining static and dynamic analysis for detecting malicious JavaScript code that works by first conducting syntax analysis and dynamic instrumentation to extract internal features that are related to malicious code and then performing classification-based detection to distinguish attacks. In addition, based on code instrumentation, we propose a new method which can deobfuscate part of obfuscated malicious JavaScript code accurately. Ultimately, we implement a browser plug-in called MJDetector and perform evaluation on 450 real web pages. Evaluation results show that our method can detect malicious JavaScript code and de-obfuscate obfucation effectively and efficiently. Specifically, MJDetector can detect JavaScipt attacks in current web pages with high accuracy 94.76% and de-obfuscate obfuscate code of specific types with accuracy 100% whereas the base line method can only detect with accuracy 81.16% and has no capacity of de-obfuscation.

The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) in smart grids has become an important research topic in recent years. Smart grids are advanced energy systems that incorporate new technologies to improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of power grids. IoT is a network of interconnected devices that can be remotely monitored and controlled. Sensors and other IoT devices can be installed throughout the power grid to collect data on the performance and condition of the system. This data can be analyzed to improve power system reliability and predict failures before they occur. The integration of IoT in smart grids has the potential to transform the power industry by enabling real-time monitoring and control of power networks. This paper discusses the importance of IoT integration in smart grids for enhancing power system reliability, and the role of information technology in this process.

Color retinal images have been widely used in diagnosis and screening of ophthalmic diseases. Macula detection and fovea location in retinal images are important steps in grading and diagnosis of ophthalmic diseases. However, due to the weaker reflection of the macula, it is difficult to determine the fovea accurately by the lack of clear border in the macula. An efficient method for detecting and locating macula based on morphological features fitting is proposed. The macula area is detected by its low brightness and round shape features. And then the K-means clustering and circle fitting is applied to achieve accurate position of macular center. A series of tests show good performance in the public retinal images database. Thus the proposed method based on morphological features fitting is proved to be efficient and useful for computer-aided diagnosis of ocular diseases.

This paper presents a dynamic simulation of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) Wind Turbine on ZedBoard Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The wind turbine industry has been growing significantly over the last few years, and computational modeling plays an essential role in the optimization of wind turbines. In this work, a mathematical model is developed to simulate the PMSG wind turbine system's behavior under different wind speeds. The simulation is implemented on ZedBoard FPGAs, which provide excellent performance and low power consumption. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in predicting the turbine's power production, generator torque, and other parameters under different wind conditions. The proposed approach can be used for system-level design exploration and optimization of wind turbines. It provides a more efficient and accurate method for predicting wind turbine performance than traditional simulation methods. Finally, it can be concluded that using FPGAs for wind turbine simulation can help to reduce computational complexity and increase the accuracy and efficiency of the simulation process.

Sequential far infrared (FIR) image mosaic is a challenging task due to repeated patterns, low contrast, image blurring, illumination change, and sparse structure. In this paper, a novel matching approach is proposed for the sequential FIR image registration, which is based on coarse-to-fine strategy and grid-based motion statistics (GMS). In the coarse matching step, a transitive relation is deduced to obtain the coordinate relations of the current registering image and its adjacent images to ensure enough number of feature points and guarantee the accuracy of the preregistration results. In the fine matching step, a principle for fine-tuning registration and a strategy for changing the distribution of the feature points are developed for finding most appropriate feature points. Based on the point pairs, the position of the current registering image can be accurately located. Besides, an effective post-processing, such as gray-scale non-uniformity correction and mosaic seam elimination, is also utilized to refine the fine-tuning results to achieve the promising mosaic effect. A comparative study and quantitative evaluation with commercial software or representative image mosaic algorithm demonstrate that better quality results can be obtained by using the proposed method.

Cloud computing is an Internet-based service which provides shared virtual resource and data to accomplish certain computation. In order for the servers to have sufficient resources when the request arrives, as well as save server resources as much as possible, we propose a prediction-based server capacity planning and dynamic scheduling algorithm. There are mainly three steps in our capacity planning algorithm. The first step characterizes the given data on several indices and then present an effective model in order to predict the oncoming demands in the near future. The second step generates the workload of servers combined with the predicted demands and then make capacity planning based on this workload. Thus it's obvious that the effectiveness of capacity planning depends on the accuracy of prediction to a great extent. Finally, a demand prediction based strategy on workload allocation is brought out. A dynamic resource allocation strategy is given to ensure the quality of service at any moment in future meanwhile taking energy consumption into consideration. The results of the experiment show that the required server number decreases by 33% after the prediction-based capacity planning applying on server scheduling.

In this modern era research in mechanical ventilator model designing has increased a lot. Mathematical model of lungs is used to distinguish the pulmonary diseases. In this work bond graph model of breathing mechanism i.e. inspiration and expiration of lungs is developed. Hydraulic analogies are allocated to lungs using cylinders and accumulators. From nostrils to trachea single cylinder is considered having resistance and compliance effect associated with it. Trachea to lower lung section comprised of 23 generations of airways. In this study, 2 generations are considered with resistance, compliance and inertial effect, whereas resistance and compliance effect, of 3rd to 17th generations are lumped. These generations are modelled with cylinders with decreasing sizes. 17 to 23 are modelled as accumulators with resistance and compliance. Model parameters were estimated using grey box estimation.20 sim is used to make the bond graph model and determine the relationship of pressure and volume curves. Model can be used for screening of lungs diseases. Model can be used for clinical trials with any existing mechanical ventilator.

In conventional point cloud delivery, a sender uses octree-based digital video compression to stream three-dimensional (3D) points and the corresponding color attributes over band-limited links, e.g., wireless channels, for 3D scene reconstructions. However, the digital-based delivery schemes have an issue called cliff effect, where the 3D reconstruction quality is a step function in terms of wireless channel quality. We propose a novel scheme of point cloud delivery, called HoloCast, to gracefully improve the reconstruction quality with the improvement of wireless channel quality. HoloCast regards the 3D points and color components as graph signals and directly transmits linear-transformed signals based on graph Fourier transform (GFT), without digital quantization and entropy coding operations. One of main contributions in HoloCast is that the use of GFT can deal with non-ordered and non-uniformly distributed multidimensional signals such as holographic data unlike conventional delivery schemes. Performance results with point cloud data show that HoloCast yields better 3D reconstruction quality compared to digital-based methods in noisy wireless environment.

This paper presents the design and prototype implementation of long-range self-powered wireless IoT devices. The devices are conceptualized using logic gates that enable energy harvesting from ambient sources, eliminating the need for traditional batteries. The system's network topology utilizes wireless sensor networks that rely on ultra-low power wireless communication protocols for reliable data transfer. The use of sensors allows the device to collect information from the environment and communicate it to the network, enabling monitoring of various conditions. The prototype implementation demonstrates the viability of this technology and its potential to revolutionize the Internet of Things by creating an energy-efficient, long-range, and reliable network that can operate in remote areas without the need for external power sources.

This paper introduces an improved artificial fish swarm algorithm (AFSA) for weapon target assignment problem. The AFSA is a nature-inspired optimization algorithm that is based on the collective behavior of a school of fish. In this improved version, the algorithm is enhanced with three key features: visualization of solution space, convergence control, and genetic operator. The visualization helps to better understand the search space and the quality of optimization, while the convergence control ensures better exploration of the search space. The genetic operator is introduced to the algorithm to enhance its optimization capability by borrowing the idea from genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization. The proposed algorithm is tested against benchmark problems and the results show that it outperforms other state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. The performance of the algorithm is further verified through some real-world weapon target allocation problems. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve the weapon target assignment problem and can be a useful tool in military applications.

In this paper, the angle-of-arrival (AOA) measurements are adapted to locate a target using the UAV swarms equipped with passive receivers. The measurement noise is considered to be target-to-receiver distance dependent. The Cramer-Rao low bound (CRLB) of the AOA localization is calculated, and the optimal deployments are explored through changing angular separations and distances. Then, a distributed collaborative autonomous generation (DCAG) method is proposed based on the deep neural network (NN). The off-line training and on-line application rules are applied to generate the optimal heading angles for the UAV swarms in the AOA localization. The simulation results show that through the DCAG method, the generated heading angles for UAV swarms enhance the localization accuracy and stability.

Fuzzy co-clustering induced by multinomial mixture model (FCCMM) is one of the effective methods for analyzing cooccurrence information data. In FCCMM, we have to determine the number of clusters in advance. Furthermore, we have to select the best solution from a lot of trials with various patterns of the number of clusters and random initial values. In Gaussian mixture models, a robust EM clustering algorithm, which is robust to initial values and can automatically estimate the optimal number of clusters, have been proposed in order to resolve such problems. It introduces an entropy-based penalty term with respect to cluster volumes to the objective function of the standard EM algorithm and obtains the optimal number of clusters by continually eliminating clusters with low competitiveness in volumes. In this paper, we propose a method which automatically estimates the optimal number of clusters without being influenced by the initial values by introducing the entropy-based penalty term with respect to cluster volumes to the objective function of FCCMM in a similar manner to the robust EM algorithm and demonstrate its estimation performance through numerical experiments.

This paper focuses on DNS Firewall Data Visualization, a tool that helps network administrators efficiently manage and protect IP networks. The tool is designed to provide a graphical interface for displaying data related to blacklisting and firewall rules in order to make it easier for administrators to identify and remediate security threats. The authors discuss the development and implementation of the tool, as well as the benefits of using it in a network environment. Several prototypes are also presented to demonstrate the capabilities of the tool. Overall, DNS Firewall Data Visualization is an effective solution for managing complex network security configurations and improving network performance.

This paper proposes a Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy-based Kalman filter observer for vehicle side-slip angle estimation and lateral stability control. Vehicle safety and stability are crucial for modern-day automobiles, and effective control strategies are required to ensure safe and stable operation. The proposed observer uses fuzzy logic to model uncertain system dynamics and a Kalman filter to estimate the vehicle's side-slip angle. This approach improves the accuracy of the observer, which in turn provides better control of the vehicle's lateral stability. To implement the observer, integrated circuits and IP networks are used to connect the various sensors and actuators. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated through simulations, and the results indicate that it can effectively estimate the vehicle's side-slip angle and ensure stable operation. Overall, this work presents an innovative approach to vehicle control that can enhance safety and stability on the road. Additionally, a discussion of the use of Erbium in the proposed system is presented in the paper.

This paper proposes an innovative method for autonomous vehicle control, specifically for lane and vehicle tracking using deep learning technology. The focus of this study is on training machine learning algorithms through the feature extraction of images captured by cameras installed on automobiles. By utilizing the power of machine learning, the control systems of autonomous vehicles can effectively recognize and predict the movement of other nearby vehicles and adjust their driving strategies accordingly. This research thus presents a promising solution to improve the safety and efficiency of autonomous driving through the integration of vision-based deep learning and intelligent control systems.

In this paper, we introduce a novel and robust approach to quantized matrix completion. First, we propose a rank minimization problem with constraints induced by quantization bounds. Next, we form an unconstrained optimization problem by regularizing the rank function with Huber loss. Huber loss is leveraged to control the violation from quantization bounds due to two properties: first, it is differentiable; and second, it is less sensitive to outliers than the quadratic loss. A smooth rank approximation is utilized to endorse lower rank on the genuine data matrix. Thus, an unconstrained optimization problem with differentiable objective function is obtained allowing us to advantage from gradient descent technique. Novel and firm theoretical analysis of the problem model and convergence of our algorithm to the global solution are provided. Another contribution of this letter is that our method does not require projections or initial rank estimation, unlike the state-of-the-art. In the Numerical Experiments section, the noticeable outperformance of our proposed method in learning accuracy and computational complexity compared to those of the state-of-the-art literature methods is illustrated as the main contribution.

The accurate prediction of the growth height of vegetation near power transmission lines is important for the maintenance of power distribution networks. In this study, a deep learning algorithm was developed to predict the growth height of trees under overhead lines. The model was trained on a large dataset of vegetation samples using a variety of predictive and analytical models. The generated mathematical model was then used to make accurate predictions. The results showed that the deep learning algorithm outperformed other prediction algorithms in terms of accuracy, speed, and reliability. This study provides a practical and effective approach for predicting the growth height of vegetation near power transmission lines using deep learning techniques.

This paper explores the sphere of lexicons and knowledge, with a focus on the fields of semantics, linguistics, natural language processing, and computational linguistics. We begin by examining the importance of lexicons in these fields, as they serve as the fundamental building blocks for language analysis and processing. Next, we delve into the intricacies of semantics, including the study of meaning, interpretation, and context. We then explore the role of linguistics in language analysis, including the study of phonetics, syntax, and morphology. Moving on, we discuss the importance of natural language processing and its applications in information retrieval and text analysis. Finally, we touch upon the role of computational linguistics in the development of language tools and technologies, such as natural language processing algorithms, speech recognition software, and machine translation systems. Throughout this paper, we also touch upon related topics such as color, registers, and springs, highlighting the diverse and multidisciplinary nature of language analysis and processing.

This paper investigates a grant-free non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system where massive number of users wake up and send data right away without performing a grant-based initial access procedure. Since no scheduling grant is used in this system, the base station (BS) does not know which user is transmitting on each resource. Also, due to the lack of an uplink (UL) timing control process, multiple user's signals are asynchronously received at the BS. This causes asynchronous interference, or multiuser inter-carrier and inter-symbol interference. We propose two ideas to address these two problems. We first propose an auxiliary preamble structure to successfully detect the user activity, even in the presence of a massive number of users. We, then, propose a modification to the interleave-division multiple access (IDMA) receiver to mitigate asynchronous interference. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly improves the preamble detection performance and BER performance compared to the conventional schemes. Furthermore, we show that the proposed grant-free NOMA system can achieve much better performance than the grant-based NOMA system in terms of transmission time and signaling overhead.

In this paper, we present a novel reversible image steganography scheme based on a U-Net structure. The proposed scheme utilizes neural networks for both encoding and decoding of secret images into cover images. Our approach focuses on feature extraction and uses transforms to embed the secret images into the cover images. The advantage of our approach is that it not only has a high capacity for hiding secret data, but also ensures high quality image recovery for the receivers. The proposed scheme has been evaluated on a variety of benchmark images and has shown remarkable performance in terms of security, visual quality and embedding capacity. The experimental results reveal that our proposed scheme outperforms existing techniques in terms of perceptual quality and robustness against various image processing operations. To summarize, our paper provides a comprehensive method for high-capacity and secure image coding and transmission based on the U-Net structure, which shows great potential for future applications in practical image steganography.

This paper presents a study on the classification of EEG motor imagery using support vector machines (SVM) and convolutional neural network (CNN). EEG signals are generally complex and difficult to interpret. Therefore, the study focuses on using feature extraction to reduce the dimensionality of the EEG signals. Support Vector Machines (SVM) are then used to classify the feature vectors. Additionally, the research employs deep learning techniques, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to achieve better classification results. The study aims to contribute to brain modeling by simulating the biological neural networks of the human brain. The presented results show that the combination of SVM with feature extraction and CNN lead to a better classification of EEG motor imagery than using only SVM with feature extraction. Finally, the study concludes with a discussion of the importance of training and testing the classifiers to achieve optimal performance.

This paper presents a ship life-saving training system that utilizes virtual reality technology to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of the training process. The system integrates various training methodologies, including task analysis, collaboration, and solid modeling, to provide a realistic and immersive training environment for trainees. By leveraging the immersive and interactive nature of virtual reality technology, the system can simulate various scenarios and challenges that trainees may encounter in their real-life working environment, such as boats and emergency situations. Moreover, the system enables trainees to collaborate with other team members, allowing for the development of teamwork skills. In conclusion, the ship life-saving training system based on virtual reality technology can improve the quality and effectiveness of training, leading to better outcomes and preparedness in emergency situations.

Virtualization technologies have become common-place both in software development as well as engineering in a more general sense. Using virtualization offers other benefits than simulation and testing as a virtual environment can often be more liberally configured than the corresponding physical environment. This, in turn, introduces new possibilities for education and training, including both for humans and artificial intelligence (AI). To this end, we are developing a simulation platform AILiveSim. The platform is built on top of the Unreal Engine (www.unrealengine.com) game development system, and it is dedicated to training and testing autonomous systems, their sensors and their algorithms in a simulated environment. In this paper, we describe the elements that we have built on top of the engine to realize a Virtual Environment (VE) useful for the design, implementation, application and analysis of autonomous systems. We present the architecture that we have put in place to transform our simulation platform from automotive specific to be domain agnostic and support two new domains of applications: autonomous ships and autonomous mining machines.
