We describe the important specificity of each domain in regard to simulation.In addition, we also report the challenges encountered when simulating those applications, and the decisions taken to overcome these challenges.

In this paper, we propose a semi-blind channel-and-signal estimation scheme for uplink massive MIMO communication systems with channel sparsity. By exploiting the sparsity of the channel matrix, the proposed scheme is able to estimate the channel and signal parameters with limited pilot overhead. Specifically, we employ a sparse Bayesian learning algorithm to estimate the channel matrix, and exploit the estimated channel information to derive the optimal signal estimator. Moreover, we propose a novel algorithm to estimate the number of active transmitters based on the sparsity of the received signal vector. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms existing schemes in terms of estimation accuracy and spectral efficiency. In addition, our scheme has the advantage of requiring only a small number of antennas at the receiver, which makes it suitable for practical implementation in massive MIMO systems.

This paper aims to investigate the performance of Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) models by employing different scattering partitioning methods. The ANFIS models are popular predictive models that are widely used in computational modeling due to their ability to incorporate both neural networks and fuzzy sets. In this study, the clustering method and mathematical model were used to create different scattering partitioning methods, and their impact on the ANFIS model was evaluated. The performance of each ANFIS model was compared through simulations and it was found that the clustering method outperformed the mathematical model, producing ANFIS models with superior predictive power. This research provides a valuable contribution to the development of ANFIS models and highlights the importance of selecting the appropriate scattering partitioning method to optimize system performance.

Creative problems are ill-defined, and thus experimentation, evaluation, and iteration are key elements of creative problem solving. We present a computational theory of evaluation in creative design. Our technique evaluates a design concept by analogically comparing it with alternative articulations of the concept. We operationalize this theory of analogical comparison in the context of biologically inspired design that uses biological analogies for conceptual design of technological systems. Our technique of analogical comparison supports evaluation of prior technological designs, biological source cases, as well as candidate conceptual designs through analogical mapping between alternative functional models of these design concepts. Given a functional model of a design concept and an alternative functional model of the same design concept, analogical comparison leverages a novel hierarchically organized analogical mapping technique to align the two models and identify the differences between them. Our technique is implemented in an operational artificial intelligence agent called Design Evaluation through Simulation and Comparison (DESC). We evaluate DESC through computational experimentation across several models to illustrate its strengths and limits and to highlight areas for future research.

This paper proposes a multimodal fusion approach for Chinese sign language recognition using Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. The proposed approach aims to improve the accuracy of gesture recognition by combining the visual and motion-based features extracted from the input data. The feature extraction process includes image segmentation and various transforms on gray-scale images. The HMM and LSTM-based models are used for gesture classification and multimodal fusion, respectively. The proposed approach shows promising results for Chinese sign language recognition, which can be particularly beneficial in developing assistive technologies for the hearing-impaired individuals.

Ultra Dense Networks (UDN) have become one of the key technologies for 5G wireless communications, which can meet the requirements of high-traffic, high-density wireless terminal access. Compared with LTE, there are a large number of heterogeneous cells in UDN. If a failure occurs and can't be alleviated its effect in time, it will lead to a significant drop in network performance. Therefore, the cell outage compensation (COC) problem in the UDN is very important. Although deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been applied to many scenarios related to the self-organizing network (SON), there are fewer applications for cell outage compensation. In this paper, aiming at the cell outage scenario in the UDN with the goal of maximizing the sum of the throughput of all users while meeting service quality demands of each mobile user, and present a framework based on DRL to solve it. Specifically, we first allocate compensation users to adjacent BSs by using the K-means clustering algorithm, then apply a deep neural network (DNN) to approximate action-value function. The simulation results show that the algorithm converges quickly and tends to be stable, and reach 99.53% of the maximum throughput. It verifies the efficiency of the DRL-based framework and its effectiveness in meeting the requirement of user rates and handling cell interrupt compensation.

This paper presents a novel approach for emotion recognition using sequence mining. The proposed method utilizes deep learning techniques to extract features from input data, which are then analyzed using mathematical models to identify patterns associated with specific emotions. The key contribution of this work is the use of logic gates to enhance the performance of the numerical models by classifying the input sequences into discrete categories based on their emotional content. The proposed approach has potential applications in market research, where it can be used to better understand consumer behavior and preferences by analyzing social media data. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, thus showing its potential for practical applications.

Business process and requirement specification are crucial phases in the software development process. Yet, business and requirement modeling are often carried out separately by different languages and design teams, leading to misaligned models. The degree of misalignment grows continuously with their independent evolution. Thus, the potential of model-driven software development cannot be fully exploited. There is a considerable agreement among researchers about the integration technique roles to bridge the gap between heterogeneous models. Therefore, this approach is based on this technique to align the business world represented by BPMN and the software requirement world represented by the UML use case. We define an integrated meta-model that incorporates all BPMN and use case elements as well as new others to map traceable elements. Further, we define a new diagram that provides a means to visualize and combines their use within an integrated model. Our approach supplements CASE tools with additional information and relationships to maintain the global system consistency. To illustrate it, we implement an editor for designing the proposed diagram, and we apply it in a topical case study.

This research paper provides a brief description of the wireless sensor network and the protocol to be used. Through this technology, benefits are obtained that provide the sensor networks together with greater freedom when placing the sensors in the vicinity of the target. In wireless sensor networks, routing is a critical and important aspect. The work focuses on the performance of the quality of services in the wireless sensor network (WSN) under the AODV routing protocol. This document tries to characterize the AODV protocol by performing simulations in the NS3 (Network Simulator Version 3) program. In the simulations of the AODV protocol, a set of metrics that can be used for comparisons in different scenarios are shown. The main objective of this document will be to offer a suitable simulation environment to determine the operation of the protocol to be used in wireless sensor networks.

This paper provides a comprehensive security analysis of a space-based wireless network. The study focuses on evaluating the security measures necessary for satellite communication in space. The growing importance of space communication for military and civilian applications demands high-security standards for wireless networks. The research presents critical challenges in defending space communication and addressing the increasing vulnerabilities in wireless networks. One of the significant challenges of a space-based wireless network is the lack of physical security due to its remote location. The security analysis assesses the risks in communication networks and proposes solutions to enhance security. For this, the paper proposes the use of military standards to establish secure wireless communication between base stations and communication equipment. The study concludes that space-based wireless networks are viable, efficient, and secure alternatives to traditional communication systems with the proper implementation of security measures.

In the field of cancer classification using DNA microarrays, gene selection is a critical task for achieving high accuracy rates. In this paper, an improved Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (iBPSO) approach is proposed for gene selection and cancer classification, incorporating the Support Vector Machines (SVM) algorithm. This new algorithm presents improved convergence, providing more accurate results than traditional methods. The proposed iBPSO algorithm also exhibits efficient computational modeling, which reduces the time needed for gene selection and cancer classification. Moreover, this methodology has the potential to establish standards for future studies in the field. Overall, the results suggest that the iBPSO-SVM approach is an effective and promising method for gene selection and cancer classification, demonstrating its potential impact on the accuracy of cancer diagnosis and treatment outcomes.

The accurate prediction of urban travel time is critical for improving traffic management and reducing congestion. This paper proposes a short-term travel time prediction model using dynamic time warping with disaggregate probe data. The proposed model utilizes computational modeling techniques, probes, data models, predictive models, adaptation models and artificial neural networks to predict travel times along urban links. The model is tested on real traffic data, and the results show that it can accurately predict travel times, which can be used for traffic control and other purposes. This approach provides a promising method for improving traffic flow in urban environments, and has the potential to reduce traffic congestion and improve overall mobility.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is a rapidly emerging technological innovation that has the potential to transform the fashion industry. Many fashion companies are exploring the use of AI and related technologies in areas such as inventory management, supply chain optimization, and personalization of customer experiences. For example, smart mirrors powered by AI can offer customized recommendations to customers based on their preferences and purchase history. However, investment in AI technologies can be expensive and requires significant resources for successful implementation. Some companies are also exploring the use of avatars, or virtual assistants powered by AI, to interact with customers and assist with online shopping. Despite these challenges, the opportunities presented by AI in the fashion industry are significant and companies that embrace these technologies will likely gain a competitive edge in the market.

Features of different pattern complexity and extracted from multiple context scopes all provide important information for saliency prediction. Our model considers saliency can essentially be described by a combination of relatively simple features, and the scale of features varies. For this reason, improvements for saliency prediction model in three aspects are proposed to capture multiple contexts, and in final stage saliency prediction is made in a comprehensive way. The flexibility of proposed approach makes it possible to convert many existing convolutional neural networks into saliency prediction models. Experiments on two benchmark datasets show that the proposed approach is capable of converting a VGG base model into a competitive saliency prediction model.

The effectiveness of machine learning algorithms depends on the quality of the supplied training data. Any problems embedded in the nature of data will result in obtaining incorrect classification models, especially imbalanced data distribution is among the most significant learning difficulties that can affect classifiers. As one of the classes has much more instances than the other, the learning process becomes biased towards it. Therefore, methods for alleviating the impact of skewed distributions are highly sought after. Ensemble learning has emerged as one of the leading paradigms for imbalanced data. Creation of an efficient pool of classifiers is not a trivial task and one needs to carefully select which classifiers should be combined to obtain the best predictive power. In this paper, we propose a compound ensemble pruning algorithm for imbalanced data. It aims to retain classifiers that offer the best performance on both minority and majority classes, and display a high level of diversity. Remaining learners are discarded from the pool. This is achieved by the means of a multi-criteria evolutionary algorithm. Extensive experimental study show that our proposal is able to create smaller ensembles than the state-of-the-art methods, while offering an improved robustness to imbalanced class distributions.

The modern day robots can do a variety of tasks with great efficiency, however their utility is limited due to the non-social behaviour of the robots. For the same it is important to assess the human behaviour in diverse conditions to as to eventually make robots socialistic in nature. Object & people tracking is an excellent field of computer vision in which we have tried to detect and track multiple vehicles and people at outdoor traffic environment and indoor office environment respectively. A background subtraction algorithm is applied for vehicle detection. Kalman filter is used to predict the estimated position of every vehicle in the next frame and updating of new track. Some vehicles are also detected in cluttered scenes. Every moving vehicle is counted in video frames. Multiple face detection and tracking is an also attractive field of computer vision. The faces are behaviourally very different to vehicles and indoor scenarios are also very different to outdoor scenarios. Hence a different methodology to track people is used. In this paper, we have tried to detect and track face of multiple people on two different datasets with different height of camera. Point feature is extracted and compared it in the successive frames to track face of multiple persons. Every face is bounded by rectangular shape with unique identity. We have also counted total number of faces in the frame sequences. Results on both vehicle and face datasets show promising results and the proposed methodology can accurately track the trajectories. The output of the research is a good dataset to assess human behaviour to be used in social robotic applications of the future.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has grown tremendously in the last decade, and has had a significant impact on various industries. One such industry is healthcare, where IoT has been utilized in medical services and monitoring, particularly in biomedical monitoring. This paper provides an analysis of the past decade of IoT implementation in healthcare, considering its impact on medical diagnostic imaging and other medical tools. In addition to reviewing the evolving landscape of IoT, the paper also examines the challenges faced by healthcare providers in implementing IoT technologies. Through a comprehensive review of the literature, this paper provides an informative and thought-provoking analysis of the current state of IoT in healthcare and its future potential. Overall, the study highlights the need for continued investment in IoT-related healthcare innovations and efficient implementation strategies to achieve desired outcomes.

Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems have shown great potential for increasing data rates and improving the reliability of wireless communication. However, the performance of these systems is hindered by channel aging, which results in a degradation of the channel quality over time. In this paper, we propose a Kalman filter-based tracking algorithm for channel aging in uplink massive MIMO systems. The algorithm exploits the correlation between the channels of different antennas and base stations to estimate the channel state. The proposed algorithm is evaluated through simulations, and the results show that it outperforms traditional non-Kalman filter-based methods in terms of tracking accuracy and efficiency. The proposed algorithm has significant implications for the deployment and optimization of MIMO communication systems in the presence of channel aging.

In recent years, the use of smart grids has become increasingly popular due to their many benefits such as optimized power distribution and reduced carbon emissions. However, these devices are not immune to computer bugs and vulnerability to buffer-overflow attacks is a concern. To address this problem, researchers have proposed a method of detecting buffer-overflow vulnerabilities via automatic static analysis. This method involves utilizing feature extraction and syntactical analysis to develop analytical models. By applying static analysis to smart meter code, the models can detect and identify buffer overflow vulnerabilities, reducing the risk of cyber attacks.

The growth of the number of vehicles in the city of Manado is very fast causing a high level of congestion. For that requires smart traffic management, especially at crossroads. Timer (time)-based traffic light settings are inefficient, because the vehicle's volume state does not change according to conditions and situations (static). If the road segment is empty, the long duration of the lamp will cause the waiting time / delay for the vehicle on the other road to occur density. As a result there is an empty road section, while the other road segments are jammed, for that it is necessary to have an intelligent traffic light control system. By using Fuzzy Logic which is an algorithm on the system control, especially for dynamic and non-linear systems can increase the time of queue delay at traffic lights with optimal accuracy in real time time settings. So that the movement of the lights can follow the conditions or situations that are needed smartly.

Open source software has gained increasing relevance in the organizational and societal world. This paper aims to identify the main research topics in the context of open source and free software. To accomplish this objective, we carried out a bibliometric study in two different digital libraries, IEEE Explore and ACM Digital Library. The methodology intent was based on clusters co-occurrence of keywords and co-authorship. The results allowed to detect the clusters and themes that are more prominent in the Free Software ecosystem. Although an almost exponential growth in publications has been identified, formed by small groups of researchers and with few links between them.

Digital forensics is a crucial field that plays a significant role in modern-day crime investigation. Clustering algorithms have become popular in this field due to their ability to classify voluminous data in a short period of time. However, the performance of these algorithms is heavily dependent on the selected features. Feature extraction has been used in the past to improve the efficiency of these algorithms. In this paper, we propose the use of a memetic algorithm feature selection method for document clustering. This method combines the principles of memetics with partitioning algorithms to identify the most relevant features. This approach was tested using a benchmark dataset from Australia, and the results show that this method outperforms other feature selection methods. We conclude that the proposed memetic algorithm feature selection method has the potential to enhance the effectiveness of digital forensic analysis.

Mobile communication signal such as LTE is a good external illuminator for wireless sensing, since it is seamlessly covered and always on the air. Through channel estimation, we can find the variation of propagation channels, and then locate the moving objects passively. The basic idea of passive localization is to estimate the propagation delay of the dynamic reflection path, determine an ellipse based on the known positions of the transmitter and receiver, and finally solve the intersection point of multiple ellipses. However, the synchronization error, sampling clock drift, frequency offset and phase noise will severely impact the estimation performance. In this paper, we propose a set of methods to make the practical application of this kind of passive localization possible. A prototype system is built to test the performance in real environments, and various experiments have been done to verify its feasibility.

This paper presents an adaptive sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) damping controller for an AC/DC hybrid power system with high penetration wind power. The proposed damping controller is designed to mitigate the SSR caused by wind farm fluctuations while maintaining stable and efficient energy transmission. The adaptive system employs an online estimation algorithm to capture the dynamic behavior of the system and adjust the controller parameters accordingly. The controller is simulated using a high fidelity model of the system, including wind power generation and HVDC transmission. The simulation results show that the proposed controller effectively damps the SSR and improves the stability of the system, even under varying wind power conditions. In summary, the proposed adaptive SSR damping controller demonstrates significant potential for improving the overall performance of AC/DC hybrid power systems with high penetration wind power.

Self-organizing 5G networks have the potential to enable a vast number of innovative wireless communication applications. This article explores the use of machine learning techniques, specifically reinforcement learning, in optimizing the capacity and shortest path routing of 5G networks. The study focuses on load management and bit rate optimization as the main objectives for machine learning. The approach is applied to a wireless network consisting of multiple base stations, and the results show that it can achieve significant improvements in capacity and routing efficiency compared to traditional methods. In summary, this paper provides a new direction and a potential solution for optimizing self-organizing 5G networks using machine learning techniques.

This paper analyses the impact of parametric uncertainties of a mobile robot kinematic model on velocity and pose estimation, providing models and quantifiable knowledge about them. Most works neglect how the uncertainty regarding the robot's construction aspects (such as wheels radii, the distance between them, and the robot's center of mass) affects both velocities and pose estimation. To help readers understand the influence of such parametric uncertainties, we performed experiments in a simulator and used the collected data on the proposed models. The paper also analyses how the magnitude of velocities considered by the controllers and the followed path can decrease or increase the impact of the parametric uncertainties. The proposed models and presented analysis help understanding the influence (isolated or simultaneous) of different sources of uncertainty in the robot's velocities and pose estimation. This knowledge can be applied to estimate uncertainties for localization methods based on data fusion, complementing or even avoiding the experimental procedures. Also, the development of controllers, robot simulators and new methodologies for parameters' calibration and the design and construction of new robots can also profit from the results presented in this paper.

We propose a novel machine learning strategy for studying neuroanatomical shape variation. Our model works with volumetric binary segmentation images, and requires no pre-processing such as the extraction of surface points or a mesh. The learned shape descriptor is invariant to affine transformations, including shifts, rotations and scaling. Thanks to the adopted autoencoder framework, inter-subject differences are automatically enhanced in the learned representation, while intra-subject variances are minimized. Our experimental results on a shape retrieval task showed that the proposed representation outperforms a state-of-the-art benchmark for brain structures extracted from MRI scans.

In recent years, biomedical optical imaging has emerged as a promising tool for noninvasive diagnosis and monitoring of various diseases. However, reliable and accurate image segmentation remains a challenge in the field. This paper proposes a new method for the synthesis of the optical nerve head region of fundus image which involves training a convolution neural network (CNN) for image edge detection. Our method uses gallium nitride as the source material for the optical imaging system, which allows for high-resolution imaging of the fundus. The CNN is trained using a large dataset of fundus images and is able to accurately segment the optical nerve head region. The proposed method demonstrates promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency, and has the potential to significantly improve the diagnosis and monitoring of diseases that affect the optic nerve.

This paper presents a real-time model predictive control (MPC) approach for prioritizing energy management in autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The AUV is subjected to surges and other forces as it moves along a given trajectory, resulting in varying energy consumption rates. The proposed MPC algorithm optimizes energy consumption through computational modeling of the forces acting on the AUV and adjusts the trajectory as necessary in real-time. The energy management strategy aims to minimize the consumption of the available energy resources while still allowing the AUV to complete its mission. This approach has the potential to significantly improve the performance and extend the operational duration of AUVs.

Currently, mobile applications, such as interactive gaming, virtual reality, and natural language processing, are becoming more computational intensive, but the computing capacity of mobile devices is limited. An effective way to solve this problem is offloading the tasks to nearby cloudlets, which are some small mobile data centers deployed in wireless metropolitan area network (WMAN). and consume a large amount of energy. Excessive energy consumption brings about some negative effects, including increased carbon dioxide emissions, aggravating the greenhouse effect, etc. In view of this challenge, we propose an energy-aware virtual machine (VM) scheduling method for cloudlets in WMAN. Technically, an optimization model is designed to formalize our problem. Then, based on VM Live Migration Technology, a corresponding energy saving VM scheduling method abbreviated as MFEA is proposed to determine which VMs should be migrated and where they should be migrated. Finally, experimental data demonstrate that the proposed method is effective.

In the field of wireless communication, multicarrier spread spectrum techniques such as Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Multicarrier Code Division Multiple Access (MC-CDMA) are widely used due to their exceptional performance in terms of spectral efficiency. However, the issue of frequency offset is a major challenge in these techniques, which can cause interference in the transmission and reduce the overall efficiency. This issue has been addressed through various estimation techniques, which have been successful in mitigating the impact of frequency offset on the system performance. This paper analyses the distribution of frequency offset and suggests efficient estimation techniques to compensate for the same. The study further highlights the impact of frequency offset on the efficiency of multicarrier spread spectrum techniques, which emphasizes the need for robust estimation techniques to enhance the same. Finally, the study discusses the impact of frequency offset on the transmitters and the overall system performance, which is a key area of concern for researchers and practitioners working in this field.

This study aims to examine the reputation differences between women and men on the Stack Overflow online community platform, specifically within the software and programming professions. The research focuses on various tools and skills related to software engineering, as well as data mining techniques to analyze the reputation patterns. The investigation takes into consideration the gender disparities that exist in the engineering profession and evaluates the effect of these differences on reputation. The findings of this study could provide better understanding of the social dynamics of the online coding community and enable the development of strategies to reduce gender inequality.

This paper focuses on the application of deep learning techniques in dialogue systems for database mapping and asking clarification questions. The field of natural language processing has witnessed significant progress in recent years due to advancements in deep learning algorithms. Task analysis plays a crucial role in developing successful dialogue systems. Semantics of natural languages is an important aspect to be considered while designing such systems. Moreover, reinforcement learning also contributes to enhancing the performance of dialogue systems. Games and speech processing also help in improving the accuracy of dialogue systems. Overall, the use of deep learning for database mapping and asking clarification questions in dialogue systems brings immense potential for the development of efficient and reliable systems.

This paper proposes a robust technique for iris segmentation based on fully convolutional networks (FCN) and generative adversarial networks (GAN). The segmentation of images is an essential step for accurate iris recognition, and our method offers significant improvements in the accuracy of iris segmentation in biometric applications. The FCN is used for extracting features from the iris images, while the GAN is used for fine-tuning the segmentation masks. Our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, and the accuracy of our technique is increased by utilizing gallium nitride as the input material. Our experiments show that the proposed method can successfully segment iris regions in images with high accuracy, and it can be widely used in biomedical imaging and other related fields. In conclusion, the proposed method provides a robust and accurate technique for iris segmentation and feature extraction that can be utilized in various applications such as biometric identification, security systems, and medical diagnosis.

Nowadays, conventional learning methods where students are often passive or forced to work show more and more their limits, especially with the advent of the Internet, tablets and smartphones… Therefore, looking for alternative methods is required. In this work, we present three new methods of teaching that seem promising for engineering students: online tutoring, playing games and interdisciplinary projects. We propose to combine them in a new inter-semestrial course for engineering students, at the middle of their curriculum, and through an example focused on the Internet of Things.

Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) have gained tremendous popularity in recent years due to their ability to provide accurate measurements of voltage, current, and power in real-time. However, the optimal placement of PMUs in the power system is critical to ensure complete observability and effective monitoring of the system. In this paper, we present a brief study on the optimal placement of PMUs using genetic algorithms. The proposed method determines the best location for PMUs based on voltage, current, and power measurements. Simulation results show that the proposed method is effective in identifying the optimal placement of PMUs in the power system, thereby improving the system's overall observability. Additionally, the study highlights the importance of accurate voltage, current, and power measurements in maintaining the stability and reliability of the power system. Overall, this research work provides valuable insights into the role of PMUs and their optimal placement in the power system.

Bone age assessment is a crucial aspect of pediatric orthopedics and endocrinology. In this paper, we propose a two-stage deep neural network approach for automatic bone age assessment using X-ray imaging. The first stage applies a convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction, followed by image segmentation using a U-Net-like structure, which can accurately and efficiently segment the bones from the background. The second stage uses a fully connected neural network to estimate the bone age. The proposed method was evaluated on the public Bone Age Challenge dataset, and achieved state-of-the-art results. Moreover, we show that training the network with a curriculum learning strategy improves the accuracy and robustness of the algorithm. In summary, our method provides a powerful tool for bone age assessment that is both accurate and automated, which can potentially benefit clinical practice and improve patient care.

In recent years, crowd counting has become an important research topic in computer vision. It has a wide range of applications, such as traffic flow analysis, security and surveillance, and urban planning. Feature extraction is a key aspect of crowd counting, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown great potential in this area. CNNs are a type of deep learning method that can automatically extract useful features from images. In this paper, we propose a crowd counting method based on CNN with a global density feature. The proposed method utilizes convolutional layers to extract features from the input image and estimate the crowd density. The global density feature is calculated by convolution and used to refine the estimation results. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.  Overall, our proposed method provides an effective solution for crowd counting in various scenarios.

This paper describes a web-based gesture recognition system that enables users to control heterogeneous IoT devices using deep learning. The user interface of the system allows users to input their gestures and interact with their devices. The training of the system involves collecting a dataset of gesture samples and processing them using deep learning algorithms. The gesture recognition phase uses prediction algorithms to identify the gestures made by users. Testing of the system was carried out using cameras to capture the gestures made by users. The results indicate that the system can recognize a wide variety of gestures with high accuracy. This system has the potential to improve the usability and accessibility of IoT devices for users, particularly those with disabilities.

Due to the excessive number of databases, unbalanced development and behindhand sensing infrastructures, distributed network data suffers from inconsistency, data missing, large measurement error and other data quality problems, which hinder the development of smart distribution network. In order to discover more complex deep-seated rules and provide more effective decision support for power system decision-making, it is necessary to study data mining and analysis methods that are suitable for massive data under current situation. This paper studies on the method of identifying bad data for multi-temporal and multi-spatial data in distribution networks and propose a method to identify bad data using likelihood-ratio test for 3D spatio-temporal data. In order to speed up the data processing rate, a 3D-LRT method based on multi-threading and Hadoop parallelization methods is proposed.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a paradigm shift in the way people interact with smart devices and systems. As IoT grows, security becomes a significant concern as cyber threats evolve and impact the privacy and integrity of data transmitted over the network. In this paper, we propose a hybrid cryptographic method that addresses the security challenges in IoT deployments. Our method combines symmetric and asymmetric encryption techniques to ensure the confidentiality, authentication, and non-repudiation of sensor data and object recognition systems. The proposed hybrid cryptosystem is designed to provide an efficient and secure solution for IoT cybersecurity, making it a useful tool for organizations and researchers seeking to protect sensitive information in IoT networks. Overall, our research highlights the critical role that encryption and cybersecurity play in ensuring the trust and security of IoT-based systems.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly growing network of devices that communicate with each other to provide a range of services. As these devices become more prevalent, there is a growing need for secure group communication protocols that can authenticate users and protect sensitive data. This survey examines the current state of group communication protocols for IoT networks with a focus on authentication and security. The paper discusses the various security challenges that are faced by IoT networks and presents an overview of the current state of authentication protocols for IP networks. The survey also investigates the current state of secure group communication protocols for IoT networks and presents a classification scheme for these protocols. The paper concludes by discussing the limitations of existing protocols and the ongoing research efforts to develop more secure and efficient group communication protocols for IoT networks.

This paper presents a discrete-time terminal sliding-mode tracking control method with alleviated chattering for mechatronics systems subject to uncertainties. The proposed method uses a terminal sliding surface to guide the trajectory of the system towards a desired manifold, while minimizing the chattering phenomenon that may occur in traditional sliding-mode control. The convergence of the system is proven using Lyapunov stability analysis. The proposed method is tested on an acceleration-controlled mechatronics system, where the control performance is evaluated through simulations. The results show that the proposed method achieves excellent tracking performance with reduced chattering, indicating its effectiveness in the control of mechatronics systems subject to uncertainty. The proposed method also has potential applications in various fields beyond mechatronics, making it a valuable contribution to the field of control engineering. This study is carried out in Australia and provides a promising solution to improve the control performance of mechatronics systems in practical applications.

This paper presents an operating-point tracking method for enhancing the stability of sensorless induction motors in low-speed regenerating mode. The method focuses on controlling the stators and rotors of the motor to meet stability criteria. The resistance of the motor is also taken into consideration when tracking the operating-point. The proposed method ensures thermal stability of the motor by estimating the temperature rise caused by the regenerating process. This estimation is based on the stator, rotor and ambient temperatures, and the heat generated by the motor during the regenerating process. The results show that the proposed method effectively enhances the stability of the motor during low-speed regenerating mode, and ensures the thermal stability of the motor.

Authentication of human in an unobtrusive manner is important in modern technology to enrich society. Authentication of a person in an environment like smart home, car driving, etc., can lead to better man-machine conjugation. Advancement in sensor technology and machine learning makes it possible to obtain and analyze a significant amount of data. This paper explores the important aspects of human behavior daily routine in the home. Traditional approaches rely on the extraction of statistical features for machine learning algorithms. However, with an increased number of sensors, feature extraction may not be possible. Therefore, human identification in a smart home is performed using deep learning technique on the data obtained from multiple sensors placed at the various place and devices in the homes like a bed, bathroom, door. In this paper, both statistical, as well as deep neural networks, are implemented for human activity data. For humans in smart home deep learning has upper hand as compared to other machine learning techniques. Thus proposed approach can identify humans based on analysis of sensor data using various machine learning technique using unobtrusive sensory data.

This paper presents the design and application of an Internet of Things (IoT) technology based on WeChat control for monitoring and controlling the humidity and temperature in greenhouses. The system is designed using wireless sensor networks and hardware devices which are capable of measuring temperature and humidity. The wireless communication between the sensors and the control center via WeChat allows for real-time monitoring of the humidity and temperature in the greenhouses. The system design and implementation are discussed in detail in this paper. The proposed system offers an efficient solution for maintaining optimal humidity and temperature levels in greenhouses, improving crop yields and reducing resource wastage. Overall, this study demonstrates the practical application of WeChat-based IoT technology in agriculture, highlighting the potential of IoT technologies in solving real-world problems.

A specific pattern of morphological changes in the human brain is observed during the process of brain development and healthy aging. The age of subjects can be estimated from brain images by evaluating such patterns. This paper proposes an age estimation method using 3-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) from brain T1-weighted images so as to fully utilize the potential of volume data. Through a set of experiments using over 1,000 T1-weighted images of healthy Japanese, we demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits better performance on age estimation than the conventional methods using handcrafted local features and 2D-CNN.

The increasing of connected tiny, low-power, embedded devices, grouped into the generic definition of "Internet of Things" (IoT), raised remarkably the amount of in-situ collected data. However, at the time of writing, IoT devices have limited storage and computation resources if compared with a cloud computing or on-premises infrastructure. IoT devices often suffer for reduced connectivity due to the place of the deployment or other technical, environmental or economic reasons. In this work, we present the DagOn* workflow engine as a part of an IoT orchestration scenario oriented to operational environmental prediction. Our novel approach is devoted to join the two worlds of workflows, in which each task runs on a dynamically allocated computational infrastructure, with tiny jobs targeted to embedded devices hosting sensors and actuators. We show our preliminary results applied to a demonstration use case. We are confident that further development of the proposed technology will affect positively production applications for massive and geographically distributed data collection.

A growing body of research has uncovered the role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in multiple biological processes and tumorigenesis. Predicting novel interactions between diseases and lncRNAs could help decipher disease pathology and discover new drugs. However, because of a lack of data, inferring disease-lncRNA associations accurately and efficiently remains a challenge. In this paper, we present a novel network consistency projection for LncRNA-disease association prediction (NCPLDA) model by integrating the lncRNA-disease association probability matrix with the integrated disease similarity and lncRNA similarity. The lncRNA-disease association probability matrix is calculated based on known lncRNA-disease associations and disease semantic similarity. The integrated disease similarity and lncRNA similarity are computed based on disease semantic similarity, lncRNA functional similarity and Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity. In leave-one-out cross validation experiments, NCPLDA achieved outstanding AUCs of 0.8900, 0.8996, and 0.9012 for three datasets. Furthermore, prostate cancer and ovarian cancer case studies demonstrated that the NCPLDA can effectively infer undiscovered lncRNAs.

Alignment of large-scale serial-section electron microscopy (ssEM) images is crucial for successful analysis in nano-scale connectomics. Despite various image registration algorithms proposed in the past, large-scale ssEM alignment remains challenging due to the size and complex nature of the data. Recently, the application of unsupervised machine learning in medical image registration has shown promise in efforts to replace an expensive numerical computation process with a once-deployed feed-forward neural network. However, the anisotropy in most ssEM data makes it difficult to directly adopt such learning-based methods for the registration of these images. Here, we propose a novel deformable image registration approach based on weakly supervised learning that can be applied to registering ssEM images at scale. The proposed method leverages slice interpolation to improve registration between images with sudden and large structural changes. In addition, the proposed method only requires roughly aligned data for training the interpolation network while the deformation network can be trained in an unsupervised fashion. We demonstrate the efficacy of the method on real ssEM datasets.

Many audio forensic applications would benefit from the ability to classify audio recordings, based on characteristics of the originating device, particularly in social media platforms where an enormous amount of data is posted every day. This paper utilizes passive signatures associated with the recording devices, as extracted from recorded audio itself, in the absence of any extrinsic security mechanism such as digital watermarking, to identify the source cell-phone of recorded audio. It uses device-specific information present in low as well as high-frequency regions of the recorded audio. On the only publicly available dataset in this field, MOBIPHONE, the proposed system gives a closed set accuracy of 97.2% which matches the state of art accuracy reported for this dataset. On audio recordings which have undergone double compression, as typically happens for a recording posted on social media, the proposed system outperforms the existing methods (4% improvement in average accuracy).

Muscle synergies are fundamental to human movement, as they facilitate efficient and coordinated muscle activation during motor tasks. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the stability of muscle synergies during circle tracking using electromyography. We utilized task analysis to evaluate the muscle activation patterns during circle tracking and applied stability criteria to quantify the robustness of muscle synergies. Additionally, we implemented artificial neural networks to assess the effectiveness of different stability indexes and band-pass filters in detecting changes in muscle synergy stability. The results indicate that stable muscle synergies are essential for accurate and efficient circle tracking, and the proposed stability analysis framework can support the optimization of motor control strategies. Overall, this study provides insights into the importance of muscle synergy stability for motor behavior and offers a practical approach to measure and evaluate muscle synergy stability in a variety of applications.

A Least Squares Channel Estimation (LSCE) method is designated for a Massive MIMO system combined with Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM). The Mean Square Error (MSE) of LSCE is computed firstly in a Rayleigh fading channel. Secondly, if channel estimation was available at the receiver (Base Station), the data detection could be made by linear and nonlinear detectors i.e (ZF, MMSE) and (SNR-Based Ordering, OSIC-SINR-Based Ordering) respectively. Simulation results show that by increasing antennas number of Base Station (BS), the nonlinear detectors perform more in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER).

This paper proposes a deep learning based intelligent method for detecting and identifying radio signals considering two applications: first, cognitive radar for identifying micro unmanned aerial systems and second, an automated modulation classification scheme for cognitive radio, which can be used for aeronautical communication systems. Our proposed intelligent method is designed of a spectral correlation function based feature extractor and a low-complexity deep belief network classifier with low FPGA logic utilization.

Smart meters are becoming increasingly common in modern homes, allowing consumers and utility companies to better monitor power demand and usage. However, the use of smart meters also presents an opportunity for malware to be silently installed, with potentially dangerous consequences. This paper proposes a side-channel based approach for detecting malicious code on smart meters, using feature extraction and neural networks to identify patterns of behavior that are indicative of malicious activity. The proposed approach represents a novel and effective method for enhancing the security of smart meters and protecting against the growing threat of malware. By effectively detecting and neutralizing malicious code, utility companies can safeguard the integrity of their power systems and ensure that consumers remain protected.

Plant recognition systems that developed by computer vision researchers, help botanists in faster recognition and detection of unknown plant species. Until now, multiple studies focused on the process or algorithms that maximize use of botanical datasets for plants prediction modeling, but this method depends on leaf characteristics which can be changed with botanical data and different feature extraction techniques. On the other hand, recently, due to the popularity and successful implementation of deep learning-based methods in various areas such as image classification, object detection, and speech recognition, the researchers directed from traditional feature-based methods to deep learning. In this research, one more efficient method presented that use transfer learning to recognize plant for leaf classification, which first uses a pre-trained deep neural network model for learning useful leaf characteristics directly from the input data representation. Then use a logistic regression classifier for leaf classification. It is seen that transfer learning from a large dataset to limited botanical dataset in plant recognition task is well done. The proposed method is evaluated on two well-known botanical datasets, i.e., Flavia with 32 classes and Leafsnap with 184 classes, and has succeeded in achieving an accuracy of 99.6% and 90.54%, respectively. The results show that despite the large change in the number of classes in these two datasets, the proposed method, have a good performance and show the better result than methods based on the hand-crafted feature and other methods based on the deep learning in terms of memory and precision.

Inverse problems have been widely used in many fields of engineering, such as the calculation of forces or torques acting on a system. In order to accurately obtain the inverse dynamics, data-based design methods have become increasingly popular due to their advantages over traditional analytical models. In this paper, the authors propose a novel approach based on Gaussian processes to design the inverse dynamics of a system. The Gaussian process model provides a flexible and powerful way to model data, which is used here to construct a mathematical model for the inverse dynamics. The kernel function in the model plays an important role in determining the relationship between the data and the unknown function, and different kernel functions can be selected according to the characteristics of the data. Disturbance observers are also introduced to estimate the unknown disturbances affecting the system. Finally, computational modeling is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison to other methods. The results confirm that the proposed data-based design method based on Gaussian processes is both accurate and efficient in obtaining the inverse dynamics of a system.

Information recommendation methods mainly include collaborative filtering and content-based. The collaborative filtering method is the most widely used recommendation method. It mainly uses the preferences of a group with similar interest or shared experience to recommend information of interest to users, but it will encounter serious data sparseness and cold start problems. In this paper, we propose a film recommendation model based on word vector features. The Doc2Vec model is used to extract the semantics, grammar and word order of the sentence, transform it into a fixed dimension vector, and the similarity of the vector will be calculated and applied to the collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm. Experiments show that the recommendation results are improved in both accuracy and recall.

This paper proposes a method for accurate specified-pedestrian tracking from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The key challenge in the task of target tracking is feature extraction, which is hindered by the distance between the UAV and the target. To address this challenge, the authors incorporate image color analysis to enhance the feature extraction process. The proposed method also utilizes image reconstruction to generate a more detailed representation of the target, allowing for more accurate tracking. In addition, the authors explore the use of legged locomotion as another feature to aid in tracking pedestrians. Through experiments using various types of cameras, the proposed method demonstrated strong performance in accuracy and robustness. This research presents a promising approach to improve current state-of-the-art in target tracking using UAVs.

Nowadays, the ability to code is becoming increasingly important in industry and is often mentioned as a crucial skill for future employment. In maker culture, the ability to program along with other technical skills often exceeds this limitation and also includes fun activities through personally fabricated projects. In this paper, we examine computational design projects that are intended to be 3D printed and could potentially introduce coding learning actions. To find computationally rich designs that are appealing to learners, we conducted data analysis on an online makerspace which exploits computational design tools for personal fabrication. We found the most liked designs of the online makerspace and examined which of them included programming features (iterations, conditional statements and functions/modules) and could foster computational thinking elements such as abstract and algorithmic thinking, pattern recognition, and decomposition. The most liked category of designs was Figures (of animals and popular animation characters among other things) which surprisingly often also included programming features. We discuss the implications of our research for technologists, academics and teachers who wish to include 3D modeling and printing in coding learning activities.

Computer vision-based real-time applications demand robust image matching approaches due to disparity in images. This can be achieved using descriptor vector with scale and rotation invariance capability. This paper presents a rotation invariant descriptor vector formation based on line point duality. The proposed descriptor uses a simple consistent method of key point detection. For obtaining the descriptor vector, line segments present in the input image are used. These line segments are located within a region of interest around obtained key points in the input image. The obtained descriptor vector is used for matching of disparate images. Experiments are carried out for four different image sets with rotation at the range of angles to validate the performance of the proposed descriptor in real-time. For comparative study, normalized match ratio is computed using multi-layered neural network with two hidden layers.

Energy performance contracting and neural network prediction technologies have been proposed to improve the energy efficiency of distribution transformers. In this paper, we focus on the economics of implementing energy performance contracting in distribution transformer systems. We draw on the biological neural network model to develop an artificial neural network for predicting the energy performance of distribution transformers. Our results show that energy performance contracting can provide significant cost savings for companies by reducing energy consumption and overall operating costs. The use of artificial neural networks for energy performance prediction also allows for better decision-making and investment planning. Overall, the combination of energy performance contracting and neural network prediction can improve the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of distribution transformer systems.

In this work, we use a deep learning method to tackle the Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) problem in tactile material recognition by incorporating the advanced semantic information into a training model. Our main technical contribution is our proposal of an end-to-end deep learning framework for solving the tactile ZSL problem. In this framework, we use a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract the spatial features and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to extract the temporal features in dynamic tactile sequences, and develop a loss function suitable for the ZSL setting. We present the results of experimental evaluations on publicly available datasets, which show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Remote sensing image recognition has been widely used in civil and military fields. In view of plenty of interference factors in remote-sensing aircraft, such as shade, noise, the changing of perspective, etc. An improved target recognition algorithm in remote sensing image based on Faster-RCNN is proposed which uses a standard Region Proposal Network (RPN) generation and incorporates feature maps from shallower convolution feature maps. Convolution neural network is adopted to recognize aircraft target in complex environment, enhance the global context and local information to avoid information loss in the process of feature extraction, which improves recognition rate. Simulation results show that the feasibility of aircraft target recognition algorithm in remoting sensing image and the scale and posture changes of target can be overcome. Meanwhile, the proposed algorithm has higher recognition effect and stronger robustness than traditional Faster-RCNN and BP neural network and support vector machine ( SVM) methods.

LCR-Net++ is a novel method for detecting the 2D and 3D pose of multiple persons in natural images. The proposed system uses a multi-stage architecture which involves both top-down and bottom-up approaches. This allows for effective processing of multi-person scenes as it is able to simultaneously generate proposals and accurately estimate the poses of the individuals in the image. Additionally, LCR-Net++ employs a novel heatmapper module which improves the accuracy of joint detection. The system was trained on a large dataset of annotated images which comprises a diverse range of poses and activities, and was able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets. This method has potential applications in a wide range of industries, including those that rely on 3D displays and two-dimensional displays for visual output.

In wireless communication systems, it is important to have estimates of the channel in order to achieve high data rates and deliver services with the quality expected by the users. There are several channel estimation techniques used in OFDM systems, some of them based on training sequences and others on blind estimation techniques. In this paper we introduce a data aided channel estimation technique using the Vandermonde Matrix (VM)for the estimation and an interpolation through Frequency Domain Correlation (FDC). This results in a less complex method than LS or MMSE. Mean squared error (MSE)is shown for both techniques (VM and FDC)as a performance measure and it is compared to LS and MMSE. MSE performance is shown for the proposed method to be better than that of the LS and to be practically the same as the MMSE performance for low SNR values.

At present, all CNN-based fire identifications identify whether a fire is blazed with a single frame image, all of which have low accuracy under a strong interference or complex backgrounds such as flickering light or a high-brightness background. To address the issue, this paper proposes a neural network model which combines CNN with SRU. The scene content is extracted through CNN and combined with the dynamic characteristics of the flame extracted by SRU to improve the accuracy of fire alarm. There are three models proposed in the paper, including Resnet18+SRU, Resnet34+SRU and resnet18(Maxpool)+SRU. The models were validated on a test set containing intensive indoor environmental interferences and compared with CNN-based single-frame and multi-frame fire identification methods. The results show that the proposed methods are more accurate than the single-frame CNN fire recognition method by more than 25% and are more suitable for indoor environment fire alarms.

This paper presents DyCorC, an extractor and cleaner of web forums contents. Its main points are that the process is entirely automatic, language-independent and adaptable to all kinds of forum architectures. The corpus is built accordingly to user queries using expressions or item keywords as in research engines, and then DyCorC minimizes the boilerplate for further feature-based opinion mining and sentiment analysis, gathering comments and scorings. Such noiseless corpora are usually hand made with the help of crawlers and scrapers, with specific containers devised for each type of forum, entailing lots of work and skills. Our aim is to cut down this preprocessing stage. Our algorithm is compared to state of the art models (Apache Nutch, BootCat, JusText), with a gold standard corpus we released. DyCorC offers a better quality of noiseless content extraction. Its algorithm is based on DOM trees with string distances, seven of which have been compared on the reference corpus, and feature-distance has been chosen as the best fit.

This research is utilizing three different voltages for load flow forecasting to establish a short-term online forecasting. Upon completion of this research, several neural network learning algorithms will be compared that is an Adaptive Learning Recursive Prediction Error, Modified Recursive Prediction Error, Recursive Prediction Error and Back Propagation. A network entitled Hybrid Multilayered Perceptron Network is coupled to these training algorithms. By using an on-line model, it is applied to estimate the future trend. The future trend network model is train using nonlinear autoregressive moving average with an exogenous input. The projected data is collected from the utility power supplies of 33kV, 11kV and 415V at three different locations in MARA University of Teknologi, Penang, Malaysia. Three different sets of data are applied to evaluate the performance of these learning algorithms. From the investigational results gathered, it showed that Adaptive Learning Recursive Prediction Error learning algorithm can be more enhanced the performance of other learning algorithm as an online model in the series of 0.45 dB to 9.481 dB of Mean Square Error during validation.

Cloud computing has become an essential technology for enterprises to achieve cost-effective and efficient resource management. However, the dynamic and unpredictable demands of servers in the cloud environment pose a great challenge for cloud providers to allocate resources efficiently. In this paper, we propose a novel predictive resource allocation framework for cloud computing, which leverages prediction algorithms to forecast resource needs and improve the efficiency of resource utilization. Specifically, our framework utilizes virtual machining technology to simulate server workloads and generate accurate resource usage data, which is then fed into the prediction model to generate forecasted resource requirements. Our experimental results indicate that our proposed framework achieves higher resource utilization and lower overhead compared to traditional resource allocation strategies. Our framework can be easily integrated with existing cloud software and can be customized for varying resource demands.

In this paper, a perceptual-based High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) intra coding optimization algorithm using deep convolution networks is proposed. The primary focus of this research is to improve the efficiency of the video coding process while maintaining the quality of the encoded images. To achieve this, the proposed algorithm first extracts important features from the input image using deep convolution networks. Then, the features are further optimized to reduce the bit rate needed to encode the image. This optimization process is performed while taking into account the perceptual quality of the images to ensure that the encoded video is visually pleasing. Experiment results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both objective metrics and subjective perception, thus demonstrating its effectiveness in image coding optimization.

This paper proposes the development of a Unified Description Language (UDL) for simulations in cloud environments. The rise of cloud computing has brought about new forms of virtualization, such as containers, which allow for greater efficiency in resource usage. However, the lack of a standardized description language has hindered the adoption of these technologies in computational modeling. The UDL would address this issue by providing a common language for software tools to generate and interpret simulation configurations. The UDL would also consider the unique aspects of cloud computing, such as the distribution of resources and the architecture of cloud systems. With the development of a UDL, researchers and practitioners can more easily navigate the complexities of cloud simulations, leading to greater adoption and innovation in this field.

Humans have created many pioneers of art from the beginning of time. There are not many notable achievements by an artificial intelligence to create something visually captivating in the field of art. However, some breakthroughs were made in the past few years by learning the differences between the content and style of an image using convolution neural networks and texture synthesis. But most of the approaches have the limitations on either processing time, choosing a certain style image or altering the weight ratio of style image. Therefore, we are to address these restrictions and provide a system which allows any style image selection with a user defined style weight ratio in minimum time possible.

This paper introduces a dynamic exoskeleton system designed for hemiplegia people. The system purposes to help patients who suffer half body paralysis due to congenital causes, trauma, tumors, and stroke or caused by other illness. First, the mechanical system introduced through dynamical simulations in Catia. Second, the electronic circuit presented and detailed using a simulation in Proteus 8 and a modeling approach is proposed. Finally, an interaction system with a control algorithm proposed to help the patient to control the robot.

The optimal allocation of modular superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) in a microgrid is a critical task for efficient and reliable operation. Optimization techniques such as linear programming and genetic algorithms have been utilized to identify the ideal placement and sizing of SMES in a microgrid. Compared to batteries, SMES has the advantage of fast response time and longer cycle life, making it an attractive option for microgrid energy storage. The layout and state of charge of SMES are important factors that must be considered during the optimization process. By improving SMES allocation strategies, microgrid operators can enhance resilience, reduce operating costs, and enhance overall power quality.

Melanoma skin cancer is a deadly type of cancer that needs to be detected at an early stage for effective treatment. In order to assist clinicians in detection, a color-based approach is proposed for melanoma skin cancer detection in this paper. The proposed approach includes feature extraction, image color analysis, and image segmentation. The system performance of the proposed approach was evaluated on a dataset of skin images obtained from the ISIC melanoma project. Results showed that the proposed approach was able to achieve a high accuracy in terms of melanoma detection. Therefore, this approach can be considered useful for assisting clinicians in early detection and diagnosis of melanoma skin cancer.

In this paper a method is introduced that supports reuse and maintenance of design information. The method allows sharing design information in different levels of details tailored for the stakeholders according to their needs. In addition, it is possible to share the information in multiple formats to suite different purposes. The results are demonstrated in an industrial partner which is a supplier of tooling for manufacturing industry.

Accurately simulating of the flow field around the submarine is significant to predict the hydrodynamic performance of a submarine. In this paper, numerical calculations of the three-dimensional viscous flow field around the SUBOFF submarine with full appendages (AFF-8) are simulated by solving Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations with different viscous models including eddy viscosity turbulence models $(k-\epsilon, k-\omega $, and SST $k-\omega)$ and Reynolds stress turbulence models (SSG Reynolds stress, Omega Reynolds stress, and BSL Reynolds stress). It indicated that numerical implementations are creditable by comparing experimentally measured data with simulated results, results show closer agreement between the computed wake velocities at the propeller disc using SSG Reynolds stress models and the experimental data both quantitatively and qualitatively. Besides, three types of fillet are designed at the main body-stern appendage junctions to reduce horseshoe vortex production and intensity. Results show that the fillet in convex shape decreases circumferential nonuniformity of inflow of the propeller and improves the quality of the propeller disc flow.

Virtual Reality (VR) can cause an unprecedented immersion and feeling of presence yet a lot of users experience motion sickness when moving through a virtual environment. Rollercoaster rides are popular in Virtual Reality but have to be well designed to limit the amount of nausea the user may feel. This paper describes a novel framework to get automated ratings on motion sickness using Neural Networks. An application that lets users create rollercoasters directly in VR, share them with other users and ride and rate them is used to gather real-time data related to the in-game behaviour of the player, the track itself and users' ratings based on a Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ) integrated into the application. Machine learning architectures based on deep neural networks are trained using this data aiming to predict motion sickness levels. While this paper focuses on rollercoasters this framework could help to rate any VR application on motion sickness and intensity that involves camera movement. A new well defined dataset is provided in this paper and the performance of the proposed architectures are evaluated in a comparative study.

This paper presents a SDN-based hybrid electrical optical architecture that combines the benefits of both electrical and optical technologies. Optical switches and optical fiber networks are used to provide high-bandwidth and low-latency communication between servers, while the electrical networks are used to handle the management and monitoring tasks. The network topology is designed to ensure efficient communication and load balancing, and the bandwidth of the system is optimized to meet the demands of diverse applications. In addition, the architecture includes a monitoring system that enables real-time monitoring of network performance and ensures fast fault detection and recovery. The proposed architecture offers a scalable and flexible solution for computer architecture design that can be applied to different environments and applications.

Recent advances in deep visual attention methods accelerate greatly the research of image captioning. However, how to leverage hand-crafted features or deep features for the encoder of image captioning is not fully explored, due to the difficulty in finding a kind of all-purpose features to entail a set of visual semantics. In this paper, we introduce a cascade semantic fusion architecture (CSF) to mine the representative features to encode image content through attention mechanism without bells and whistles. Specifically, the CSF benefits from three types of visual attention semantics, including object-level, image-level, and spatial attention features, in a novel three-stage cascade manner. In the first stage, object-level attention features are extracted to capture the detailed contents of the objects based on the pretrained detector. Then, the middle stage devises a fusion module to merge object-level attention features with spatial features, thereby inducing image-level attention features to enrich the context information around the objects. In the last stage, spatial attention features are learned to unveil the salient region representation as a complement to two previously learned attention features. In a nutshell, we integrate attention mechanism with three types of features to organize context knowledge about images from different aspects. The empirical analysis shows that the CSF can assist image captioning model in selecting the object regions of interest. The experiments of image captioning on MSCOCO dataset show the efficacy of our semantic fusion architecture in depicting image content.

This paper proposes a novel approach to maximize the sum-rate of Device-to-device (D2D) communication in 5G cellular networks. The proposed approach incorporates joint power allocation and mode selection, to overcome the interference issues commonly encountered in D2D communication. The proposed approach optimizes both power control and mode selection to enhance the signal to noise ratio (SNR) of the receivers. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of sum-rate maximization and interference reduction. The proposed approach is also proven to be sensitive to changes in the network and can effectively handle dynamic and unpredictable environments. Overall, this study contributes to the development of efficient D2D communication in 5G cellular networks, and provides a valuable reference for future improvements in this field.

In this paper, we propose a Cascaded PCA Network (CPCANet) based on principal component analysis network (PCANet) for Individual identification of electrocardiogram (ECG). The CPCANet consists of three stages. In the first stage, ECG signals are preprocessed by normalization and spike removal. The R peak points in the preprocessed ECG signals are detected. Then, ECG signals are transformed into two-dimensional images to use as input of CPCANet. Here, we perform patch-mean removal and PCA algorithm as the same manner as PCANet from the transformed two-dimensional images. Also, we verified the influence of these parameters by modifying the key parameters of the experiment. The experiments are performed by the variation of patch size, number of filters, size of a block, and ratio of the lap from two databases. For this, we use a PTB ECG database which is benchmarking database. The experimental results clearly revealed that the proposed method showed good performance and effectiveness when compared with conventional algorithms such as PCA, auto-encoder (AE), extreme learning machine (ELM) and ensemble extreme learning machine (EELM).

As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to grow and expand, there is a need for reliable and efficient network protocols to enable seamless connectivity across wireless networks. The emerging concept of software-defined networking (SDN) offers a promising solution for enhancing the scalability and adaptability of IoT networks. However, one key challenge in SDN-based IoT is developing effective flooding mechanisms for disseminating control messages and data packets. In this paper, we propose Atomic-SDN, a new flooding approach that ensures synchronized and consistent updates across all nodes in a wireless sensor network. We leverage the IEEE 802.15 standard for low-power wireless communication to establish a reliable and efficient communication framework that supports atomic broadcast and multicast. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Atomic-SDN through extensive simulations and experiments, which show that it outperforms traditional flooding methods in terms of reliability, efficiency, and scalability. Our work provides valuable insights into the design and implementation of robust and efficient SDN-based IoT networks, and can serve as a foundation for future research in this area.

Brain abnormalities are the most challenging fatality in the current scenario of health care society.
