Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is a crucial task in radar signal processing, with various applications ranging from target tracking to surveillance. In this paper, we propose a new approach for DOA estimation in MIMO radar with nonorthogonal waveforms. Our approach utilizes a correlation-based technique and takes into account the colored noise present in the system. We introduce two new performance indexes to evaluate the effectiveness of our method, and demonstrate its superiority over existing techniques. We also evaluate the impact of different factors on our method's performance, including the number of sensors, the signal-to-noise ratio, and the waveform diversity. Our results show that our approach achieves high accuracy and robustness in DOA estimation, even in the presence of colored noise. Overall, our proposed method provides a promising solution for DOA estimation in MIMO radar systems with nonorthogonal waveforms, and has potential for further development in real-world applications.

Intra prediction is an important component of modern video codecs, which is able to efficiently squeeze out the spatial redundancy in video frames. With preceding pixels as the context, traditional intra prediction schemes generate linear predictions based on several predefined directions (i.e., modes) for blocks to be encoded. However, these modes are relatively simple and their predictions may fail when facing blocks with complex textures, which leads to additional bits encoding the residue. In this paper, we design a progressive spatial recurrent neural network (PS-RNN) that learns to conduct intra prediction. Specifically, our PS-RNN consists of three spatial recurrent units and progressively generates predictions by passing information along from preceding contents to blocks to be encoded. To make our network generate predictions considering both distortion and bit rate, we propose using sum of absolute transformed difference (SATD) as the loss function to train PS-RNN since SATD is able to measure rate-distortion cost of encoding a residue block. Moreover, our method supports variable-block-size for intra prediction, which is more practical in real coding conditions. The proposed intra prediction scheme achieves on average 2.5% bit-rate reduction on variable-block-size settings under the same reconstruction quality compared with HEVC.

In recent years, Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SDWAN) architectures have become increasingly popular due to their scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. However, deploying multiple controllers in a hierarchical architecture for SDWAN can introduce delays and maintainability challenges. To address these issues, a new Multi-Controller Deployment Algorithm (MCDA) has been proposed. This algorithm is designed to partition control systems into discrete regions, allowing for improved process control and reduced delays. The MCDA algorithm is applicable to a wide range of wide area networks and provides a new approach to SDWAN architecture that can support large-scale deployments while maintaining optimized performance. With the continuing growth of digital infrastructure, this innovative approach to SDWAN architecture has broad implications for improving network performance and scalability on a global scale.

Meta-heuristic search algorithms such as genetic algorithms have been applied successfully to generate unit tests, but typically take long to produce reasonable results, achieve sub-optimal code coverage, and have large variance due to their stochastic nature. Parallel genetic algorithms have been shown to be an effective improvement over sequential algorithms in many domains, but have seen little exploration in the context of unit test generation to date. In this paper, we describe a parallelised version of the many-objective sorting algorithm (MOSA) for test generation. Through the use of island models, where individuals can migrate between independently evolving populations, this algorithm not only reduces the necessary search time, but produces overall better results. Experiments with an implementation of parallel MOSA on the EvoSuite test generation tool using a large corpus of complex open source Java classes confirm that the parallelised MOSA algorithm achieves on average 84% code coverage, compared to 79% achieved by a standard sequential version.

This paper presents a Composer System based on Meta-Learning that utilizes various Prediction and Classification algorithms to improve Student Performance Prediction. The system uses Data models and Data mining techniques to identify patterns in the available data, which are then used to construct Predictive models. These models are trained using Training data, and the resulting predictions are used to optimize the learning process. The proposed system uses a variety of techniques to improve accuracy and performance, including ensemble learning and individual model tuning. The results of the study show promising improvements in prediction accuracy, suggesting that the Composer System has the potential to significantly enhance student performance across a range of educational domains.

Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disease that affects millions of people worldwide. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in using 3D imaging techniques for the diagnosis of AD and the exploration of biomarkers. In this paper, we propose an attention-based 3D convolutional network for AD diagnosis and biomarkers exploration. Our model utilizes three-dimensional displays of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans to accurately identify the presence of AD based on changes in grey matter density. Additionally, our model can identify potential biomarkers for AD through deep learning and brain modeling. Our results show that the attention-based 3D convolutional network outperforms traditional methods for AD diagnosis and biomarker exploration. This study demonstrates the potential of using 3D imaging and deep learning techniques for the early detection and monitoring of Alzheimer's disease.

This paper explores the potential of blockchain technology in enabling secure sharing of Electronic Health Records (EHRs) within Mobile Cloud-based E-Health Systems. With the rise of Cloud computing, there has been a growing need to store, access and share EHRs in the cloud. However, this has posed a significant challenge in maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of patient data. Blockchain offers a promising solution to these challenges through its decentralized and immutable nature, providing a secure and transparent method for storing and sharing EHRs. Utilizing smart contracts and access control mechanisms enable efficient management and authorization of medical services access while maintaining patient data privacy. Therefore, adopting blockchain technology within Mobile Cloud-based E-Health Systems can address several concerns related to data privacy, security, and management of medical services.

As the world becomes more reliant on 5G mobile communication, it is important to consider the impact that network slicing granularity can have on the availability and scalability of these networks. Network slicing, which is made possible through cloud computing technology, allows for a single physical network to be divided into multiple virtual networks, each with their own unique properties and requirements. Through the use of analytical and mathematical models, researchers can explore how different slicing granularities can impact systems operation and resource management within these networks. By carefully considering the trade-offs between granularity and scalability, it may be possible to create more efficient and reliable 5G networks that can support a wide range of applications and services.

This work-in-progress paper focuses on extending the buffer-aware worst-case timing analysis of Wormhole NoCs. The study aims to analyze the delays and timing constraints in real-time systems, which is essential in computer architecture. The authors propose to use computational modeling techniques and calculus to generate accurate worst-case timing analysis of Wormhole NoCs. To achieve this, the authors leverage advanced indexes to evaluate the buffer occupancy and network traffic in the NoCs. The outcome of this research could help to better understand and analyze the timing behavior of Wormhole NoCs, providing a useful tool to computer architects, system designers, and researchers working on real-time systems.

For lossy image compression systems, we develop an algorithm, iterative refinement, to improve the decoder's reconstruction compared to standard decoding techniques. Specifically, we propose a recurrent neural network approach for nonlinear, iterative decoding. Our decoder, which works with any encoder, employs self-connected memory units that make use of causal and non-causal spatial context information to progressively reduce reconstruction error over a fixed number of steps. We experiment with variants of our estimator and find that iterative refinement consistently creates lower distortion images of higher perceptual quality compared to other approaches. Specifically, on the Kodak Lossless True Color Image Suite, we observe as much as a 0.871 decibel (dB) gain over JPEG, a 1.095 dB gain over JPEG 2000, and a 0.971 dB gain over a competitive neural model.

This paper discusses the significance of machine learning and statistical concepts and their applications in social computing. The focus is on the use of machine learning algorithms in analyzing Twitter data. Specifically, support vector machines are emphasized as an effective tool for classification and prediction tasks. Computational modeling is also highlighted as a powerful technique for understanding social phenomena. Feature extraction is discussed as a crucial step in preparing data for machine learning algorithms. Overall, the paper highlights the importance of machine learning and statistical techniques in tackling data-driven problems in social computing.

In this study, the underlying modulators of frontal global field potentials (GFPs) in emotion regulation were explored through an EEG-informed fMRI approach. Both functional magnetic resonance imaging and electroencephalography were employed to investigate the brain activity during emotion regulation tasks. The results revealed that the modulation of GFPs was associated with the activations in several brain regions, including the anterior cingulate cortex and the prefrontal cortex. Furthermore, a cross-modal coupling analysis was conducted to investigate the relationships between the EEG and fMRI signals. The findings suggested that the feature extraction from the EEG data could provide valuable information for fMRI data analysis. This study sheds light on the neural mechanisms underlying emotion regulation and highlights the importance of combining EEG and fMRI techniques for a comprehensive understanding of brain activity.

This paper proposes a novel neural network approach for low frequency oscillation mode identification in power systems. After employing the fast Fourier transform in order selection, we then introduce a specific neural network whose topology strictly follows the exponentially damped sinusoidal model of low frequency oscillation signals. We thus turn the parameter estimation into an optimization problem. Simulations show that the proposed approach is superior to the state-of-art neural network schemes in anti-noise ability, parameter accuracy and computation speed.

This paper proposes a novel sequential surrogate method for reliability analysis in engineering applications, with a focus on adaptation models and computational and analytical models. The proposed method utilizes correlation techniques to enable efficient and accurate characterization of uncertain input parameters, and is capable of handling large-scale problems. Reliability engineering principles are integrated into the method, and Monte Carlo methods are employed to assess the performance of the proposed approach. The usefulness and effectiveness of this sequential surrogate method are demonstrated through various engineering application examples. Overall, this paper presents an innovative method for reliability analysis that has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of engineering design and analysis processes.

In recent times, the study of exchange rates has become a significant area of research, with the development of predictive models that aim to anticipate the fluctuations of different currency pairs. One promising approach to designing these models involves the use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), which are feedforward neural networks that imitate the biological neural networks of the brain. Using this non-monotonous logic model, researchers have been able to develop a more accurate prediction of the CLP-USD exchange rate. The application of ANN has been a major breakthrough in industrial engineering, as more and more automated control systems are based on silicon-based technologies. This paper discusses the successful application of a non-monotonous ANN model to predict exchange rates, emphasizing the importance of these predictive models in the field of industrial engineering.

Traffic classification has been studied for two decades and applied to a wide range of applications from QoS provisioning and billing in ISPs to security-related applications in firewalls and intrusion detection systems. Port-based, data packet inspection, and classical machine learning methods have been used extensively in the past, but their accuracy has declined due to the dramatic changes in Internet traffic, particularly the increase in encrypted traffic. With the proliferation of deep learning methods, researchers have recently investigated these methods for traffic classification and reported high accuracy. In this article, we introduce a general framework for deep-learning-based traffic classification. We present commonly used deep learning methods and their application in traffic classification tasks. Then we discuss open problems, challenges, and opportunities for traffic classification.

In this paper, we study top-N recommendation by exploiting users' explicit feedback such as 5-star numerical ratings, which has been overlooked to some extent in the past decade. As a response, we design a novel and generic transfer learning based recommendation framework coarse-to-fine transfer to rank (CoFiToR), which is a significant extension of a very recent work called transfer to rank (ToR). The key idea of our solution is modeling users' behaviors by simulating users' shopping processes. Therefore, we convert the studied ranking problem to three subtasks corresponding to three specific questions, including (i) whether an item will be examined by a user, (ii) how an item will be scored by a user, and (iii) whether an item will finally be purchased by a user. Based on this new conversion, we then develop a three-staged solution that progressively models users' preferences from a coarse granularity to a fine granularity. In each stage, we adopt an appropriate recommendation algorithm with pointwise or pairwise preference assumption to answer each question in order to seek an effective and efficient overall solution. Empirical studies on two large and public datasets showcase the merits of our solution in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods.

As the improving strategic position of electronic warfare in modern warfare, radar sorting detection becomes the eye of modern information warfare and plays an important role in it. This paper designs a new pulse radar sorting algorithm: a Density-Based Fuzzy C-Means Multi-Center Re-Clustering (DFCMRC) radar signal sorting algorithm. This algorithm mainly combines the advantages of Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) clustering algorithm and Fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm. This paper also optimizes the structure of the DFCMRC algorithm, which changes the algorithm that randomly generated the initial center point to the Clustering by Fast Search and Find of Density Peaks (CFSFDP) algorithm. After comparison tests, the DFCMRC algorithm sorting result is better than the K-means algorithm, the DBSCAN algorithm and the FCM algorithm. Also, the membership grade description of DFCMRC makes more sense than the FCM's. Accelerated optimized DFCMRC algorithm can reduce more than half iterations, which greatly shortens the algorithm calculation time.

This paper proposes a novel approach for flywheel fault detection using Kernel principal component analysis. The principal component analysis is used to analyze the mathematical model of flywheels, which creates a set of training data for the system. The Kernel function is then applied to the correlation matrix, which enhances the system's ability to detect faults. Numerical models are developed to simulate the flywheel system and train the detection algorithm. The results show that the proposed method effectively detects flywheel faults with high accuracy and can be used for real-time fault diagnosis. Additionally, this method can be extended to other mechanical systems for fault detection and diagnosis. Overall, the technique proposed in this paper provides a new solution for the detection of flywheel faults and can be used in a wide range of industrial applications.

This paper proposes a novel online measurement-based method for estimating the state matrix of a dynamic system in ambient conditions. The system considered for analysis is the power system, and the method utilizes Jacobian matrices and phasor measurement units to estimate the generators' state matrix. The proposed method aims to enhance power system stability by developing an accurate estimation of the state matrix, which is often difficult to obtain in real-world conditions due to uncertainties and disturbances. A covariance matrix is used to model these uncertainties and disturbances, and the estimation algorithm is designed to adapt to changes in the system's ambient conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations and compared with existing estimation methods. The results exhibit that the proposed method delivers more accurate and robust results than the existing methods, indicating its potential to provide valuable support for real-time dynamic system monitoring and control. Overall, this work presents an innovative method for online state matrix estimation in dynamic systems, with direct applications to power systems, and demonstrates the potential impact of measurement-based estimation on the stability and reliability of the system.

The Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) problem for critical infrastructures using wireless sensor networks (WSN), has received considerable attention in the research community in recent years. Sensors placed in these infrastructures have two functions, sensing/coverage and communication. The thrust of this paper is on the coverage aspects of sensor networks. In the Point Coverage model, only a specified set of points in the deployment area have to be sensed. The goal of placement optimization is to find the smallest set of locations to deploy sensors, so that all the points of interest can be sensed. This problem often is solved by formulating it as a Set Cover problem. However, the Set Cover approach has a serious limitation on the accurate identification of the location where abnormality is sensed. In this paper, we present a technique to overcome this limitation by utilizing Identifying Code. We study two different scenarios, where the sensors and points of interest are located in one and two-dimensional spaces respectively. We provide a polynomial time optimal algorithm for the one-dimensional case and an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) based optimal solution for the two-dimensional case. We evaluate the efficacy of the ILP solution with varying network size (45 to 64655 nodes). The ILP produced an optimal solution for the largest instance with 64655 nodes and 155339 edges in only 180.45 seconds.

The feasibility of adopting distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (D-MMIMO) for mitigating the achievable rate loss incurred by spatially-correlated fading at space-constrained user antenna arrays when served by co-located massive MIMO (C-MMIMO) counterpart is investigated. In order to explore a practically-viable design, the cumulative effects of spatial correlation at both multi-antenna access points (APs) and multi-antenna users, beamforming uncertainty caused by imperfectly estimated channel state information (CSI), and adverse effects of pilot contamination have been taken into account. The achievable user rates of the proposed D-MMIMO downlink operating in a multi-cell set-up are derived for finite/infinite antenna array regimes at the distributed APs. Thereby, the achievable user rates for C-MMIMO counterpart are deduced and compared with those of the proposed D-MMIMO downlink. Through a rigorous analysis and simulation results, we show that the distributed transmissions rendered by D-MMIMO can provide significant performance gains compared to the C-MMIMO counterpart (i) by minimizing adverse effects of spatial correlation via distinct spatial-directions/signatures rendered by distributed transmissions, (ii) by mitigating shadow fading via leveraging macro-diversity gains, and (iii) by reducing the average path-losses through effectively shortening transmission distances. Moreover, we reveal that the proposed D-MMIMO can be exploited to recover a significant portion of rate loss incurred by the lost of asymptotic channel orthogonality due to doubly-correlated channels when both APs and user nodes are equipped with space-constrained multiple-antenna arrays.

This paper proposes a system for environment monitoring using Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing, specifically for predicting cloud bursts. Clouds play a vital role in weather forecasting, and predicting their burst could help in mitigating the damages caused by extreme weather events. The system collects data from various sources, including brightness and ocean temperature, and sea surface conditions, to predict cloud bursts. The IoT devices enable real-time data collection and processing, while cloud computing provides the infrastructure for storing and analyzing the vast data sets produced. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve weather forecasting accuracy and support the development of early warning systems for cloud bursts. This research contributes to the field of environmental monitoring and highlights the potential of IoT and cloud computing technologies for addressing critical challenges in this area.

Integration of solid-liquid phase change materials (PCMs) into electronics packaging has demonstrated the potential to reduce the transient temperature rise of components that experience pulsed thermal loads. However, the impact on local temperature histories resulting from incorporating PCMs in different locations and configurations within an electronics package is not easy to analytically determine, due in large part to the non-linear response of PCMs to a transient heat load. ParaPower is a new parametric design tool to facilitate the design of electronics packages. The tool has the capability of easily incorporating arbitrarily located PCM volumes and evaluating their effect on temperature distributions within the electronics package as a function of time. This paper determines the spatial and temporal order of convergence for the reduced order phase-change thermal model which underlies ParaPower. The results are compared and validated against both an analytical solution and a higher-fidelity commercial finite element analysis (FEA) tool. This paper has shown the fast-solving methods used in the ParaPower tool give results with comparable accuracy to those obtained using high-fidelity commercial software. Reasonably good accuracy can be obtained with fairly large time steps and grid spacing allowing fast-solving design space exploration with this option to increase fidelity within the tool to obtain higher accuracy when necessary. This research quantifies the trade-off between time steps, grid size, and accuracy such that a useful balance can be obtained. Design tools, such as ParaPower, have the potential to significantly advance design theory to reduce size and cost as well as minimize the prevalence of overdesign.

This paper addresses the issue of software fault proneness prediction using group lasso regression. The study focuses on the factors that affect the classification performance, particularly in the context of software measurement and machine learning algorithms. The research proposes a method for predicting software faults using radio frequency and software algorithms in predictive models. The results show that the proposed method is effective in identifying factors that impact classification performance and can be applied to real-world software development. Overall, this study provides insight into the development of accurate and robust prediction algorithms for software faults, which is essential for improving software quality and reducing costs associated with software errors.

Image segmentation is an important task in the domain of medical image analysis, where accurate identification of target structures is necessary for diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper presents an automated segmentation approach using a deformable multi-path ensemble model for locating cervical nuclei in Pap smear images. The proposed technique is based on convolution neural networks and deformable models, which enable shape-based feature extraction and deformation modeling. The system is trained with a large dataset of annotated images, and the predictive model is optimized using task analysis. The results demonstrate high accuracy and robustness in identifying cervical nuclei, indicating the potential clinical application of this technique in cervical cancer screening and diagnosis.

Wearables that acquire relevant vital and contextual parameters improve work safety as well as quality of life of elderly citizens or patients with chronic diseases. A scalable architecture connects wearables via a hub to the cloud and combines edge with cloud computing to provide optimal user interaction and allow analytics on multi-stream data. The functionality was expanded to enable demonstrations of physiological and psychological stress classification in firemen and mobile health interventions in patients with lung diseases. Following an initial table-top edge demonstrator a hemi-spherical display improves emotional contact to users. A first use case tested an integrated acquisition and inference system that was trained to differentiate physical and emotional stress. The system measured stress in firemen during training in a cage maze and in hot training locations and provided functions to acquire expert labels. A second use case focused on mobile-health intervention for patients suffering from Chronic-Obstructive-Pulmonary-Disease (COPD), to improve their quality-of-life. Patient-physician conversations are extended through a communication channel and a virtual assistant provides disease related information, reminders, and alerts.

This study focuses on tuning the parameters of proportional integral derivative controller (PID). These parameters are traditionally tuned through the Zeigler-Nichols method. However, fuzzy logic control is usually used to online adjust the PID controller parameters. Interestingly, to find the optimal fuzzy controller scaling factors, particle swarm optimization (PSO) may also be used. Nonetheless, in presence of multi-input multi-output (MIMO), nonlinear, and under-actuated systems, a multidimensional tune is necessary, which renders finding the optimal fuzzy-PID controller with PSO algorithm a difficult task. Then, this paper presents an adapted multidimensional PSO algorithm in order to improve the performances of a fuzzy-PID controller for stabilizing a quadrotor system when tracking its reference trajectory. Moreover, to show the effectiveness of this optimization strategy, it is shown that, using simulation tools, the fuzzy-PID controller that is tuned by the proposed multidimensional PSO algorithm could ensure better time domain specifications, in comparison with a classical PID controller.

This special issue explores the challenges posed by the design of very-large-scale integration (VLSI) nodes for the Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. These systems use wireless communication to link together physical devices into distributed real-time embedded systems. IoT systems are used in a wide range of applications, including industrial control, vehicles, smart grids, and medical and health care systems.

In the framework of the Huber's minimax variance approach to designing robust estimates of localization parameters, a generalization of the classical least informative distributions minimizing Fisher information for location is obtained in the wide class of ranging error distributions with a bounded quantile value. The considered variational problem set up naturally originates from the real-life problem of estimation of the unknown coordinates of an asset surrounded by the beacons with known positions.

We present a novel neural network architecture, US-Net, for robust nuclei instance segmentation in histopathology images. The proposed framework integrates the nuclei detection and segmentation networks by sharing their outputs through the same foundation network, and thus enhancing the performance of both. The detection network takes into account the high-level semantic cues with contextual information, while the segmentation network focuses more on the low-level details like the edges. Extensive experiments reveal that our proposed framework can strengthen the performance of both branch networks in an integrated architecture and outperforms most of the state-of-the-art nuclei detection and segmentation networks.

Data stream has been the underlying challenge in the age of big data because it calls for real-time data processing with the absence of a retraining process and/or an iterative learning approach. In the realm of the fuzzy system community, data stream is handled by algorithmic development of self-adaptive neuro-fuzzy systems (SANFS) characterized by the single-pass learning mode and the open structure property that enables effective handling of fast and rapidly changing natures of data streams. The underlying bottleneck of SANFSs lies in its design principle, which involves a high number of free parameters (rule premise and rule consequent) to be adapted in the training process. This figure can even double in the case of the type-2 fuzzy system. In this paper, a novel SANFS, namely parsimonious learning machine (PALM), is proposed. PALM features utilization of a new type of fuzzy rule based on the concept of hyperplane clustering, which significantly reduces the number of network parameters because it has no rule premise parameters. PALM is proposed in both type-1 and type-2 fuzzy systems where all of which characterize a fully dynamic rule-based system. That is, it is capable of automatically generating, merging, and tuning the hyperplane-based fuzzy rule in the single-pass manner. Moreover, an extension of PALM, namely recurrent PALM, is proposed and adopts the concept of teacher-forcing mechanism in the deep learning literature. The efficacy of PALM has been evaluated through numerical study with six real-world and synthetic data streams from public database and our own real-world project of autonomous vehicles. The proposed model showcases significant improvements in terms of computational complexity and number of required parameters against several renowned SANFSs, while attaining comparable and often better predictive accuracy.

This paper presents research on the thermal characterization of field plated AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. This involves studying the temperature measurement of HEMTs and MODFETs through mathematical and computational modeling. The aluminum gallium nitride material used in these devices is a wide band gap semiconductor, making thermal characterization even more important. The results of this study provide important insights into the thermal behavior of these advanced electronic devices, paving the way for further optimization of their performance.

This paper presents a multilevel inverter based single-stage grid connected photovoltaic system using cascaded two-level inverter. The proposed system topology provides better efficiency and reduced complexity compared to conventional two-stage systems. Fuzzy logic control is employed to control the active and reactive power flow in the system. The multilevel inverter uses cascaded two-level inverters to achieve the desired output voltage levels. The topology also includes reactive power compensation for improved system stability. The system is capable of producing high-quality grid-connected power without requiring additional switches. The proposed system shows improved performance compared to conventional photovoltaic systems and can be a potential solution for renewable energy applications.

This paper presents an analytical modeling approach for tracking control of networked and quantized control systems. Quantization and delays are the two main challenges in control systems, which is overcome by designing a novel protocol for stable and efficient communication. The convergence and stability analysis of the proposed method is also presented. The quantization of the network signal is addressed using an analytical model to estimate the errors caused by quantizer. This paper shows that the proposed protocol can effectively control the networked and quantized control systems by addressing the quantization and delay issues. The analytical models and stability analysis provide a theoretical basis to ensure the stability and convergence of the control system.

This paper proposes a new approach to implement Softmax Regression by using Unsupervised Ensemble Learning. The approach integrates various Clustering algorithms, Logistics techniques, and Inference algorithms to achieve higher performance and better Standards in the classification task. The proposed method focuses on Unsupervised learning techniques, which allow the model to learn from the inherent structure of data without the need for human annotation. The approach delivers promising results in terms of a variety of Indexes such as accuracy, F1 score, and AUC. This paper contributes to the field of Information science by introducing a new way to implement Softmax Regression by leveraging the power of Unsupervised Ensemble Learning.

Pulse coupled neural network (PCNN) is the third generation of artificial neural network with strict biological background, which is different from traditional artificial neural networks. Compared with traditional feedback neural networks, pulse coupled neural network possesses significant characteristics from the point of composition of neuron. PCNN has the firing features of dynamic pulse, firing features of synchronization pulse, and dynamic and variable features of threshold value, which brings excellent effect of image segmentation and image denoising etc to PCNN. LVQ neural network is a competitive type neural network with supervised learning method; the algorithm is derived from Kohonen competitive algorithm. LVQ network is able to complete classification processing of extremely complicated pattern recognition through interaction of internal elements only due to its simple structure, with excellent features for pattern recognition. This paper carries out study on the technology of image segmentation by virtue of PCNN; invariant moment features and textural features are extracted from different types of images to realize the effect of image dimension reduction. Finally, feature vectors will be sent to LVQ neural network to realize classification recognition. The experimental result indicates excellent segmentation effect and strong adaptability of this method, enabling better image recognition.

The efficient task scheduling is the key issue of mobile edge computing (MEC) which relies on both available resources and the dependency between tasks. The task analysis is crucial to determine the priority and deadline of each task, depending on its complexity and importance. The use of servers in MEC and the integration of edge computing and cloud computing provide alternative resources for task execution. Processor scheduling must consider the limitations of each resource, such as computing power, storage capacity, and energy availability, to avoid delays that affect the overall performance. A computational modeling approach can be used to simulate and optimize the task scheduling taking into account the resource allocation and dependency. The proposed TaSRD model aims to provide a reliable and efficient solution for task scheduling in MEC environments.

With the introduction of the 5G mobile communication, the resource management has become a challenging task for Cloud computing and computer architecture specialists. The use of network slicing for service segmentation has brought the potential for a dynamic and efficient allocation of computational resources in the 5G Hybrid C-RAN. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the optimal computational resource allocation for network slicing deployment in 5G Hybrid C-RAN. The proposed approach aims to maximize the utilization of computational resources while minimizing the delays in the radio frequency. The results of this study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in optimizing the performance of the 5G Hybrid C-RAN by reducing delays, enhancing user experience and enabling efficient resource management. The findings in this research provide insights into the implementation of network slicing and computational resource allocation techniques in future 5G networks.

Skull stripping for brain MR images is a basic segmentation task. Although many methods have been proposed, most of them focused mainly on the adult MR images. Skull strip-ping for infant MR images is more challenging due to the small size and dynamic intensity changes of brain tissues during the early ages. In this paper, we propose a novel CNN based framework to robustly extract brain region from infant MR image without any human assistance. Specifically, we propose a simplified but more robust flattened residual net-work architecture (FRnet). We also introduce a new boundary loss function to highlight ambiguous and low contrast regions between brain and non-brain regions. To make the whole framework more robust to MR images with different imaging quality, we further introduce an artifact simulator for data augmentation. We have trained and tested our proposed framework on a large dataset (N=343), covering newborns to 48-month-olds, and obtained performance better than the state-of-the-art methods in all age groups.

This paper proposes a method for combining corrugated cardboard images using image stitching technique. The aim of this study is to enhance the production of corrugated cardboard by creating a complete and accurate image of the cardboard surface. The proposed method includes feature extraction, feature detection, and corner detection, which are used to detect the edges and corners of the corrugated cardboard. The process also involves the use of cameras and machine vision, which are used to capture and analyze images. Bundle adjustment is then applied to improve the accuracy of the final image. The result of this study is a more efficient and reliable way of producing corrugated cardboard through the use of modern technology.

The control of robotic manipulators with uncertain dynamics is still an active research field in robotics. In this paper, a model-error-observer-based control strategy is presented. The manipulator dynamics are modeled mathematically with the help of solid modeling techniques. A computational model is developed for the purpose of simulation and analysis. The proposed control strategy is based on observer design and model error identification, which is used to estimate the uncertain parameters of the manipulator dynamics. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is demonstrated by numerical simulations for a two-link planar manipulator with uncertain mass and damping coefficients. Results show that the proposed control strategy achieves excellent trajectory tracking and disturbance rejection performance even in the presence of significant uncertainties. The proposed approach can provide a promising solution for robust control of robotic manipulators with uncertain dynamics.

Software-defined networks (SDN) have appeared as effective network technology, which is able to support the dynamic nature of future network functions and intelligent applications. On the other hand, the progress of the SDN is limited by various security threats. Analyzing the centralized nature of SDN, we found multiple potential vulnerabilities, which the attacker may use. Our solution covers a wider area, not just data plane, but also control plane security. The traffic, which is flowing through a data plane, could include various security threats. To detect them, we utilize OpenFlow possibilities and Machine Learning (ML) concept for the proposed Network Intrusion Detection System based on Deep Neural Network (NIDS-DNN). The solution can extract network statistics from OpenFlow switches (OF switches) and process them with DNN. The result is to warn about an attack on the data plane and to prevent malicious users from harming the network. For early detection of DoS/DDoS attacks aimed at controller, we present our solution - Specter, which changes the approach to the flow processing prioritization. Using priority queues ensures a better quality of service for legitimate users. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first solution, which couple intrusion detection in the data plane with protection against DoS attacks in control plane.

The objective of this study is to investigate the performance of the correlation-based human trackers implemented in Dlib for target tracking in human detection under occlusions. The research focuses on developing and reinstating state-of-the-art human trackers that are capable of estimating the state of the target by efficiently extracting relevant features from camera images. The proposed method employs state estimation techniques such as Kalman filtering and particle filtering to improve the accuracy of target tracking under occlusion. The result shows that the reinstated correlation-based human trackers can effectively track the target even under occlusions, which is beneficial for various applications such as surveillance, robotics, and autonomous vehicles.

Phishing attacks are a prevalent form of cybercrime, which can result in significant financial losses and data breaches. The identification of phishing attacks in real-time is essential to prevent potential harm caused by such attacks. In recent years, Deep learning models have proved to be a promising solution for detecting phishing attacks. Specifically, Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have achieved remarkable results in various computer vision tasks. In this paper, we propose a Hybrid Neural Network approach that leverages the strengths of both traditional machine learning and deep learning models. Our proposed approach uses Convolutional neural networks and traditional machine learning algorithms to extract meaningful features from Uniform Resource Locators (URL) and classify them as malicious or benign. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing phishing detection methods in terms of accuracy and detection rate. Furthermore, the proposed method can adapt to various computer architectures and perform efficient detection of phishing attacks in real-time.

The aim of this study is to propose an approach to the automatic recognition of emotions from the signal speech [18], [13]: it relies on the extraction of spectral and prosodies characteristics, more particularly on the energy and the distribution of this energy in six bands. These characteristics are obtained from syllabic units (CV) where C denotes a consonant and V a vowel. To this end, we constructed a Moroccan emotional database (MEDB) from broadcasts on the YouTube channel representing different real emotional states. The features set is obtained from Matlab codes and Praat [23] software. The emotions used in this study are anger, joy, neutral state and sadness. The emotion recognition systems are developed using neural networks, Support Vector Machine and decision trees algorithms. The aim of this work is firstly to explore syllabic units to identify the emotions embedded in the speech signal and secondly to demonstrate the relevance of the energy distribution in determining emotional states.

The paper presents an automated classification system for melanoma diagnosis. It is based on a convolutional neural network that is fed with images of skin lesions which are preprocessed in advance. The preprocess step is necessary for reducing the number of artifacts present in the images and hence, maximize the classification accuracy. The proposed solution is based on the training of the neural network with a series of preprocessed clinical images, classifying them in two categories: benign or malignant.

Novel skyrmion-magnetic tunnel junction (SK-MTJ) devices were investigated for the first time to implement the ternary neural networks (TNN). In the SK-MTJ, an extra magnetoresistance state beyond binary parallel and anti-parallel MTJ states was achieved by forming a skyrmion vortex structure in the free layer. Based on the SK-MTJ, we propose a synaptic architecture with bit-cell design of +1, 0, and -1 to replace the full precision floating point arithmetic with equivalent bit-wise multiplication operation. To explore the feasibility of the SK-MTJ-based synaptic devices for TNN application, circuitlevel simulations for image recognition task were conducted. The recognition rate can reach up to 99% with 5% device variation and an average power consumption of 29.23 μW.

Intergroup conflict induces individuals to hold negative prejudice and discriminate against others from different groups. Individual's anti-social attitudes on intergroup conflict setting are based on an individual's belief on negative outgroup stereotype. Some theories based on social identity theory have been proposed to explain the emergence of this belief but their explanatory power is limited. An agent-based model is proposed to clarify the process of negative outgroup stereotype development and to reproduce key findings. The model explains how negative outgroup stereotype belief emerges as the outcome of an intergroup conflict situation. Not only that, it also explains how an individual's position in the social network affects his/her perception of outgroup stereotype.

Indian power distribution system is highly scattered by spreading throughout the control. The present research work focuses on integration of solar PV system with the traditional power distribution system by PI and ANFIS PI system due to increasing the demand of the electrical energy, it is required to interconnect a no. of renewable PV system with the grid which not only provides the extra amount of power which is required for load point of view but also economical from its generation point of view. The current control technique must be saved and highly reliable/efficient. Again, the controller must obey the standard grid code that is applicable to Indian electricity. In this paper a comparative study of PI and ANFIS PI current control technique is presented. In order to show the robustness of the controller MATLAB Simulink environment has been adopted for designing of the proposed controllers.

This paper proposes the development of a network intrusion model based on data collected from honeypots, servers, IP networks, web services, databases, protocols, data models, and search engines. The aim of this research is to identify potential network attacks and vulnerabilities by analyzing the behavior of attackers in intruding systems. The proposed model will consider various factors such as the frequency of attacks, the types of attacks, and the source of attacks. By leveraging data-driven analytics techniques, the model will improve the accuracy of detecting anomalies and identifying potential vulnerabilities. The results of this research will contribute to the development of more effective security measures to protect against network intrusions.

OC-Cache is an open-channel SSD based cache system designed for resource management in multi-tenant systems. The system aims to mitigate interference and improve bandwidth utilization in cloud computing and virtual machining scenarios. This paper provides a performance evaluation of the software and demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing write amplification and improving read performance. The results show that OC-Cache outperforms existing cache mechanisms and can enhance the overall system performance in multi-tenant environments. The software is designed for easy integration into existing systems, with minimal modifications to the hardware. Overall, OC-Cache is a promising solution for resource management in multi-tenant systems, offering better performance and improved efficiency.

The implementation of the squeezed protection mechanism in elastic optical networks has been proposed as a means to reduce blocking probability and enhance network reliability. In this paper, we present a Service Level Agreement (SLA) formulation for the squeezed protection in elastic optical networks considering the modulation format, bandwidth, network topology, and wavelength division multiplexing. The SLA model is formulated based on the modulation-agnostic squeezed protection scheme, which considers the trade-off between the squeezed level and the number of available squeezed channels. Additionally, the SLA constraints consider the bandwidth requirements, network topology, and routing constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SLA model can provide effective solutions for the squeezed protection problem, while satisfying the network performance requirements. The presented formulation can serve as a guide to network operators to design and operate optical fiber networks with high reliability and optimal resource utilization.

In wireless sensor network (WSN) nodes relay data, which maintains consistency in the sensor network. If cut vertex nodes failed it leads to partitioning in network, which disrupts the communication. It requires an autonomous technique that finds the fail node and provides recovery to them. In this paper the proposed approach provides recovery from network partitioning in distribute WSN. The proposed approach increases the lifetime of network.

In wireless sensor networks, data aggregation plays an important role in reducing the amount of transmitted data and conserving energy. However, the security of data aggregation has become a critical issue due to the vulnerability of wireless networks. One of the attacks against data aggregation is the enumeration attack, which aims to obtain sensitive information by analyzing the aggregates. To counteract this kind of attack, various protocols and analytical models have been developed. In this paper, a probabilistic logic-based method is proposed to secure data aggregation in wireless sensor networks. The method utilizes additives to generate secret value, which can effectively prevent the enumeration attack. Extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method is highly secure and can achieve a substantial reduction in the amount of data transmitting during the data aggregation process.

Encryption alone is not enough to protect data privacy, because access pattern leaks some sensitive information. Oblivious RAM (ORAM), the solution to this problem, is still far from practical deployment for heavy storage and communication/computation overhead. To reduce them, an insightful idea was proposed to utilize non-colluding clouds to shift client computation and client-cloud communication to the clouds. The proposed multi-cloud ORAM achieved O(1) client-cloud bandwidth cost and removed most of client computation. In this paper, we exploit “disconnected ORAMoperation” and design “two-layerencryption” to further reduce these overheads. Experiments show that our proposed scheme, NewMCOS, significantly reduces evict cache size from GB/MB to KB level with about 2-3 times lower response time and 20 percent savings in bandwidth for clouds, compared to other schemes. Theoretically speaking, we reduce evict cache size from O(√N) to O(ZK), where N is the number of real data blocks, K is the number of clouds (2 <; K <; <; √N ), and Z is the number of real blocks uploaded from the client for eviction. By employing “lazy eviction operation”, the write frequency is reduced by O(Z), the shuffling bandwidth cost is reduced by Ω(Z log Z). Meanwhile, NewMCOS is proved to be secure.

Software-defined networking (SDN) allows the smart grid to be centrally controlled and managed by decoupling the control plane from the data plane, but it also expands attack surface for attackers. Existing studies about the security of SDN-enabled smart grid (SDSG) mainly focused on static methods such as access control and identity authentication, which is vulnerable to attackers that carefully probe the system. As the attacks become more variable and complex, there is an urgent need for dynamic defense methods. In this paper, we propose a security function virtualization (SFV) based moving target defense of SDSG which makes the attack surface constantly changing. First, we design a dynamic defense mechanism by migrating virtual security function (VSF) instances as the traffic state changes. The centralized SDN controller is re-designed for global status monitoring and migration management. Moreover, we formalize the VSF instances migration problem as an integer nonlinear programming problem with multiple constraints and design a pre-migration algorithm to prevent VSF instances' resources from being exhausted. Simulation results indicate the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

The Internet of Things (IoT) based robust electrical energy monitoring system with Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is a promising solution for reliable monitoring of electrical energy consumption. This system is designed to provide accurate and real-time data acquisition, storage and analysis for efficient energy management. The system includes various components like monitoring devices or meters, software platforms, portals, and user manuals. The system can be used for many applications like biomedical monitoring and environmental monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated into the system for better analysis and decision-making. The IoT-based energy monitoring system with PLC has proven to be effective in reducing energy consumption and improving energy efficiency. With the continuous advancements in technology, this system is expected to become more accurate, reliable, and efficient over time.

Measurement of the electricity consumption of major appliances in different time segments is of crucial significance to demand-side management and energy conservation. Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) can infer the target appliances' power use information by only collecting and analyzing the aggregate power data at the single power entrance point. Inspired by the success of deep neural network in other fields, some researchers have applied it to NILM with promising results. However, existing studies require labeled real aggregate data to train the networks, while time-synchronized measurement of the target appliance for labeling is hard to achieve in practice. This paper proposes to train networks with only synthetic aggregate data. Furthermore, a training data generation method via background filtering is proposed, and the obtained training data is used to train the network for estimating electricity consumption. This generation method only needs unlabeled real aggregate data and the target appliance's operation curves, which reduces the difficulty of training data acquisition. The proposed estimation method achieves higher accuracy than current methods in tests on a public dataset which also demonstrates the effectiveness of background filtering.

This paper proposes a method for local app classification using deep neural network based on mobile app market data. The methodology involves feature extraction from mobile app market data, followed by training the deep neural network using the task analysis of the industries. Google's deep learning approach is employed in building the neural networks. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in local app classification and can be used in various industries. The availability and quality of training data are primary factors that affects the accuracy levels obtained. In conclusion, the proposed method presents a novel approach to local app classification using the power of deep neural networks and mobile app market data, which can help industries in identifying local apps for various purposes.

Structured light with spatially variant amplitude/phase/polarization has seen wide interesting applications ranging from manipulation to communications. In this invited talk, we will review recent advances in structured light communications accessing the space domain of lightwaves. Key devices, techniques and emerging applications will be introduced. Future challenges and perspectives of structured light communications will be also discussed.

This paper presents a comparative analysis of vector matrix multiplication using crossbar arrays as a hardware implementation. The focus is on utilizing memristors, an emerging technology that mimics the resistance changes of synaptic connections between neurons in the human brain. The study investigates the performance of different implementations of crossbar arrays for vector matrix multiplication in the context of hardware acceleration for training artificial neural networks. The analysis considers various factors, including the use of logic gates, virtual machine monitors, and the impact of resistance variations on the overall efficiency of the system. The results show that the use of memristors as a resistance element in crossbar arrays can provide significant speedup compared to conventional methods. The findings suggest that incorporating hardware acceleration into neural network training can significantly improve performance and enable more efficient computations in machine learning systems.

Real-time battery state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is critical in many applications. The extended Kalman filter (EKF) has been successfully deployed in SOC estimation allowing real-time SOC monitoring. However, modeling inaccuracies, measurement faults, and wrong initialization can cause the estimation algorithm to diverge. The precise knowledge of statistical information about process and measurements noise is crucial for accurate system modeling and estimation. This paper presents a novel SOC estimation approach based on maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE). The process and measurements models are transformed to an error state propagation system where the innovation covariance is utilized to maximize the likelihood of the multivariate innovation distribution with respect to process and measurement covariances. The MLE formulation allows the estimation of the process and measurement noise covariance magnitudes, which are used to obtain an optimal SOC estimate. The proposed method is validated experimentally using a number of Li-ion battery cells under various testing conditions. The estimation performance is compared with that of the conventional EKF technique as well as previously published results based on autocovariance least-squares measurements noise estimation. The results indicate an enhanced performance for the new algorithm over the traditional EKF across all conducted tests.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are composed of small devices called sensors, which are capable of collecting and transmitting data. In order for WSNs to function properly, routing protocols must be employed to determine the best path for data transmission between sensors. This survey focuses on geographic multipath routing techniques used in WSNs to increase the reliability and efficiency of data transmission. These techniques utilize the Global Positioning System (GPS) to determine the physical locations of sensors, and select multiple paths for data transmission based on the geospatial characteristics of the network. Several routing techniques, including Geographical Routing Protocol (GRP), Geographical and Energy-aware Routing (GEAR), and Greedy Perimeter Stateless Routing (GPSR), are discussed in this survey. The performance and effectiveness of these techniques are analyzed and compared in terms of reliability, latency, energy consumption, and network lifetime. The results show that geographic multipath routing techniques can significantly improve the performance and reliability of WSNs, and have promising potential for future applications.

Antenatal classes are sometimes called parentcraft which help to prepare expectant mothers for their baby's birth, feeding the baby and to look after the baby. It is the best way to ensure expectant mothers stay healthy during pregnancy as well as to deliver confidence and information. This paper looks into the current state of antenatal education. It investigates the way antenatal classes are accessed by expectant mothers, the challenges they face in getting access to these classes and their attitudes towards these classes. For most women, it could be stressful and very inconvenient to attend physical antenatal classes. An online collaborative approach of interactive antenatal lecture for expectant mothers is proposed to replace these classes by providing live streaming lectures, discussion and interactive sessions between users. In order to accomplish this task, some face-to-face interviews were conducted. Questionnaires were also distributed. This paper adopted the Structured Systems Analysis and Design Method (SSADM) for the specification, development, and implementation. The web based system is implemented using PHP framework as Back-end, Front-End using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, XAMPP Server and MySQL was employed to handle the database structure. The web based system was implemented and tested using carefully thought out test cases which were successful. The proposed system offers antenatal education to expectant mothers no matter their location as well as a platform for discussion between expectant mothers, midwives, or anyone at all; sharing useful information amongst themselves and giving advice and encouragement to one another.

The proliferation and diverse range of IoT devices calls for a new breed of processors capable of handling the requirements of this burgeoning technology. The next generation IoT processors must take into account architectural considerations such as hardware, computer architecture, and approximate computing to deliver optimal performance. The rise of cloud computing and next generation networking adds new dimensions to processor design and necessitates a careful consideration of tradeoffs between power consumption, speed, and accuracy. Given the vast array of IoT devices that require programmable processors, the scalability and adaptability of the next generation processors plays a pivotal role in meeting the demands of the Internet of Things. With the right architectural considerations, the next generation IoT processors will provide the necessary tools and resources to power the exciting possibilities for this exciting and rapidly evolving technology.

This paper proposes a novel methodology in the area of threat intelligence by combining statistical analysis with Intrusion Detection System. The preferred threat intelligence model identifies potential malicious connections for a single node computer system utilising the IP addresses of the devices that are connected to the system. It can be inferred from the results that the proposed system performs better in terms of accuracy, True Positive Rate and False Positive Rate.

In IoT systems, WSNs and Gateways are exposed to many attacks. WSNs are usually exposed to different types of intrusions like node compromise and denial of service attacks. IoT gateways that connects WSN to the Internet are exposed to all conventional IP attacks. In this paper, we propose an anomaly detection approach using support vector machines (SVM) for WSN intrusion detection, and deep learning technique for gateway intrusion detection. We propose a detection protocol that dynamically executes the on-demand SVM classifier in a hierarchical way whenever an intrusion is suspected. We combine machine learning classification with a statistical approach for malicious node localization. This novel approach allows finding a compromise between intrusion detection efficiency and resource overhead for WSN and gateway security.

Data mining is the discovery of valuable and novel structures in datasets. Considering the number of people suffering from diet-related cardiometabolic increase, it brings into question the media's efforts in food and health communication. One of the main objectives in this study focuses on the emerging data mining methodology to understand the structure of what and how the news media discuss food, diet, and the related cardiometabolic diseases. A total of 6,625 items of coverage on food, flavor, and condiments along with cardiometabolic diseases is identified. Data mining algorithms concern food for predicting health outcomes and providing policy information. The most typical usage of a food data corpus is automatic conversion from text to health afflictions on larger cultural forces.

In recent years, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) have become a major concern. In order to address this issue, an SDN-enabled pseudo-honeypot strategy has been proposed. This strategy involves deploying honeypots which masquerade as IIoT devices and attract attacker traffic, while minimizing the risk of the actual IIoT devices being attacked. Additionally, the use of SDN enables the identification of attacker traffic and the development of countermeasures. The proposed strategy is promising, as it has been shown to be effective in diverting attack traffic away from the actual IIoT devices. The use of SDN and pseudo-honeypots in IIoT offers significant benefits and has the potential to enhance the security of IIoT networks. However, further research is needed to optimize the proposed strategy and strengthen its effectiveness against sophisticated attackers.

Multipath TCP (MP-TCP) has been introduced as an extension to legacy TCP to support simultaneous communication through multiple paths. Although MP-TCP has many advantages over TCP, some issues and challenges related to security robustness of this protocol remain unaddressed. The root cause of many threats specific to MP-TCP stem from the fact that user-specific credentials such as shared keys exchanged in the initial handshake are exposed. This allows an attacker to hijack an ongoing session by exploiting the authentication values of users. On the other hand, Software Defined Networking (SDN) has received much attention recently due to its many advantages, such as programmability and centralization. In this paper, a scheme for securing MP-TCP is proposed. This is achieved with the assistance of SDN, in which a new security module residing in the SDN controller acts as a third-party session-key distribution authority. After the retrieval of session keys, a lightweight information-hiding mechanism to secure the keys exchanged during the initial handshake is proposed.

The side-channel leakage is a consequence of program execution in a computer processor, and understanding relationship between code execution and information leakage is a necessary step in estimating information leakage and its capacity limits. This paper proposes a methodology to relate program execution to electromagnetic side-channel emanations and estimates side-channel information capacity created by execution of series of instructions (e.g., a function, a procedure, or a program) in a processor. To model dependence among program instructions in a code, we propose to use Markov source model, which includes the dependencies among sequence of instructions as well as dependencies among instructions as they pass through a pipeline of the processor. The emitted electromagnetic (EM) signals during instruction executions are natural choice for the inputs into the model. To obtain the channel inputs for the proposed model, we derive a mathematical relationship between the emanated instruction signal power (ESP) and total emanated signal power while running a program. Then, we derive the leakage capacity of EM side channels created by execution of series of instructions in a processor. Finally, we provide experimental results to demonstrate that leakages could be severe and that a dedicated attacker could obtain important information.

Research on the evaluation index of partitioning wireless network by jamming multiple targets, this paper analyzed the existing evaluation indexes, analysed the deficiencies of the existing indexes, and improved the network separation ratio as the evaluation index of the attack effect finally, which lay the foundation for targets selection in the process of jamming partition.

This paper presents a novel non-iterative solution for the estimation of rigid body transformation. The proposed method utilizes a cost function that is optimized through a closed-form solution, bypassing the need for iterative numerical algorithms. The approach is particularly applicable to visual servoing systems in the field of electrical engineering, where real-time estimation is crucial to achieving stable and accurate control. Results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and computation time. The approach also lends itself well to visualization, with two-dimensional displays providing a clear representation of the estimated transformation. Overall, this paper provides a significant contribution to the field of informatics, particularly in the area of visual servoing, by offering a more efficient and effective solution for rigid body transformation estimation.

In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised learning approach to model the parameters of polymetallic nodules. Surfaces play a crucial role in understanding the characteristics and behavior of these nodules. Therefore, we employ principal component analysis and feature extraction techniques to extract relevant information from the surfaces of the nodules. Additionally, data models are used to capture the complex relationships between the different parameters. Biological system modeling is also employed, as it has been observed that the properties of these nodules are similar to biological systems. Finally, the approach is validated by modeling the nickel content of polymetallic nodules. The results show promising improvements in modeling accuracy compared to traditional supervised learning techniques. Overall, this semi-supervised learning approach presents a novel and effective method for accurately modeling the parameters of polymetallic nodules.

This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm with an improved accuracy and a faster learning curve, for very large datasets. Previously, an algorithm using lr-partitions was designed to improve upon C4.5. However, this algorithm has a relatively high percentage of undefined combinations of attribute values in its final results, increasing the learning error. In this paper, a new type of clustering algorithm was proposed to generate output values for those undefined combinations, thus accelerating the learning curve and reducing the prediction error by several percentage points on various popular datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Database.

Parameter estimation is a fundamental task in many applications such as asset management, engineering, and data analysis. This paper focuses on the use of linear regression for parameter estimation, specifically using the maximum likelihood estimation method. Two distributions, the exponential distribution and Gaussian distribution, are considered as examples to demonstrate the application of this method. The paper also highlights the importance of selecting appropriate IEEE sections to define the system or process being analyzed, as choosing the right sections can improve the accuracy of the estimation. Overall, this paper provides insights into the process of parameter estimation, and emphasizes the need for careful consideration of the method and model chosen for accurate results.

This study presents the results of W/ V band propagation studies conducted over two years in Albuquerque, NM. The focus of the study was to investigate the effects of rain and attenuation on signal propagation, as well as to evaluate the accuracy of estimation models developed by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). In addition, sea measurements were taken to more accurately assess the impact of storms on signal propagation. The results of the study provide valuable insights into the behavior of W/ V band signals in different environmental conditions, which will be useful in the development of more efficient and reliable communication systems.

This paper proposes a blind modulation classification approach for overlapped co-channel signals using capsule networks. With the increasing number of transmitters and the growing demand for spectrum efficiency, the problem of co-channel interference has become a major challenge in wireless communication. The proposed approach utilizes the signal to noise ratio (SNR) and frequency modulation (FM) as features for capsule network-based modulation classification. The capsule network architecture effectively captures the complex relationships between different features, and the dynamic routing mechanism helps to identify overlapped signals. The proposed approach is evaluated on real-world radio frequency signals collected by software-defined radios. The experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms the conventional convolution-based methods in terms of classification accuracy even in the presence of strong interference. This study demonstrates the potential of capsule networks for blind modulation classification in complex communication scenarios with co-channel interference.

In this paper, we propose a method for reducing the approximation time of cluster workload by using simplified hypergamma distribution. The proposed method utilizes solid modeling and mathematical and computational modeling techniques to construct a probability distribution model of cluster workload. Random variables are used to represent the variations in the workload of different clusters. Our proposed method can be applied in various domains such as industrial engineering, manufacturing, and computers to optimize the usage of computational resources. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method through empirical experiments, which show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of approximation time reduction. Finally, we discuss the implications of our work and propose directions for future research.

Speech synthesis, or text-to-speech (TTS), generates a speech waveform of the given text. To build a satisfactory TTS system, a large natural speech corpus is requested. In the traditional approach, the corpus should be accompanied with precise annotations. However, the annotation is difficult and costly. Recently, end-to-end speech synthesis methods are proposed, which eliminated the requirement of annotation. The end-to-end methods make the development of TTS system less costly and easier. We used the state-of-the-art end-to-end Tacotron model in the Mongolian TTS task. With much more unannotated speech data (about 17 hours), the new system beats the old best Mongolian TTS system, which is trained on a small amount of annotated data (about 5 hours), with a big margin. The new mean opinion score (MOS) is 3.65 vs 2.08 which is the old one. The proposed system becomes the first Mongolian TTS system can be utilized in real applications.

This paper proposes the development of a predictive model using artificial neural networks to forecast the prices of cryptocurrencies, focusing on Bitcoin as the main cryptocurrency of interest. The concept behind the model is based on the biological neural networks found in the human brain, where neurons interact to facilitate information processing. The model is trained using historical data of the cryptocurrency prices and uses the concept of "feeds" to improve the accuracy of the predictions. The results of the study demonstrate that neural networks are effective in predicting the prices of cryptocurrencies, which can be beneficial for investors and traders in their decision-making process. With the increasing interest in cryptocurrencies, this study provides valuable insights into the potential use of neural networks for forecasting cryptocurrency trends.

In recent years, texture classification has been an important topic in the field of computer vision. In this paper, we propose a new method called Locally Directional and Extremal Pattern (LDEP) for feature extraction in texture classification. LDEP is a simple yet effective method that combines the directional and extremal information of local image patches. The proposed method has been evaluated on several benchmark datasets, and the experimental results have shown that LDEP outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and speed. Additionally, we also perform statistical analysis to investigate the effect of lighting and image segmentation on the performance of our method. Our approach can be extended to other applications such as object recognition and data mining. Overall, the proposed LDEP method is a promising technique for image texture analysis and classification.

This paper discusses the use of Bayes methods for Fisher Information Maximization in the context of distributed vector estimation. Specifically, the authors focus on the problem of signal quantization and how it affects the ultimate performance of the estimation system. In addition, they consider the impact of noise measurement and bandwidth limitations on the achievable rate at which the system can operate. To enable efficient management of resources in distributed estimation systems, the authors propose a Bayesian approach that maximizes Fisher Information within the constraints imposed by the available resources. The proposed method is shown to outperform traditional approaches in terms of estimation accuracy, especially under severe bandwidth limitations and noisy environments.
