The cloud technology allows for the collection, storage, and management of data, while the IoT technology ensures the effective transfer of data between sensors and real-time systems, resulting in an enhanced overall production process. By utilizing this system, companies can improve their production efficiency, reduce costs, and improve system reliability. Overall, this paper provides an innovative solution to industrial monitoring with the integration of cloud computing and IoT technology.

This paper presents a case study on occupancy estimation using WiFi as a means of counting passengers on busses. The method employs wireless fidelity and probes to estimate the number of passengers in a bus. The experiment leverages the Internet of Things and intelligent sensors to provide accurate and reliable data. The study shows that occupancy estimation using WiFi is an efficient and cost-effective approach, minimizing the need for manual counting methods. Furthermore, this method reduces the need for physical infrastructure and saves on battery life, making it an innovative and sustainable solution for transportation monitoring. The results of the experiment demonstrate that the proposed approach can improve the accuracy of occupancy estimation and provide real-time tracking of passenger numbers. This research has significant implications for the transportation industry and can lead to the development of smarter and more efficient systems for managing public transportation.

The use of mathematical models in control, biology, and neuroscience has become increasingly popular in recent years. These models provide a comprehensive overview of how regulators and other components of biological systems interact with each other. Some of the most commonly used models include adaptation models, predictive models, and nonlinear systems. Control theory plays a critical role in the development of these models, as it provides a framework for understanding how different components of a system interact with each other to produce a specific response. One of the major advantages of mathematical models is that they can be used to predict the behavior of biological systems under a range of conditions. As such, they are becoming an increasingly important tool in the study of some of the most complex biological phenomena, including the functioning of the brain and the processes that regulate gene expression. Overall, the use of mathematical models is having a major impact on our understanding of biological systems, and is likely to play an increasingly important role in future research.

In recent years, the use of educational technology has gained tremendous popularity. One such development is the creation of E-Learning environments, which can provide a range of benefits for both instructors and learners. However, one issue that arises in such environments is the need for effective communication between learners and instructors. In this regard, data mining agents can serve as effective means to communicate with users in an E-Learning environment. Data mining involves the use of various data analysis techniques to discover patterns and relationships within data sets. Data models, classification algorithms, and clustering algorithms are some of the tools that can be used to mine data. By utilizing these tools, data mining agents can analyze user behavior and preferences, and provide personalized instructional material to each learner. In this way, data mining agents can be used as a means of improving communication and enhancing the overall effectiveness of E-Learning environments.

This paper proposes a novel approach called Deep Hybrid State Network with Feature Reinforcement for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Delta 3-D Printers. The system utilizes sensors and monitoring techniques to detect faults in 3-D printers. The key component of the system is deep learning, which is used for feature extraction and analysis. The system also employs a hybrid state network to model the complex relationships between the different components of the printer. The feature reinforcement algorithm is used to improve the discriminative power of the model. The proposed system offers an intelligent and efficient way to diagnose faults in 3-D printers by leveraging the capabilities of deep learning and state-of-the-art monitoring techniques.

The detection and classification of brain hemorrhage poses a significant challenge in medical diagnosis. This study proposes using the Hounsfield values and convolution neural network technique to accurately detect and classify hemorrhaging in the brain. The approach involves feature extraction and segmentation of images to identify the affected areas of the brain. Biological neural networks and brain modeling techniques are used to train the convolution neural network for accurate detection and classification of hemorrhage. Additionally, deep learning is adopted to enhance the performance of the model. The proposed technique achieved promising results in detecting and classifying different types of brain hemorrhage with high accuracy. The approach presented in this study has the potential to significantly improve diagnosis and treatment of patients with brain hemorrhage.

In recent years, smart meters have become increasingly popular due to their ability to measure and track energy consumption. However, as smart meters transmit sensitive data, they have become a target for tampering, which can lead to inaccurate readings and potentially impact customer billing. To solve this problem, an image-centric anti-tampering technique has been proposed, which utilizes cameras for face detection and microcontrollers for feature extraction. This technique relies on the fact that meters have unique features that can be used to identify tampering attempts. The use of cameras and face detection allows for precise identification of meter tampering, while microcontrollers enable feature extraction and analysis in real-time. In conclusion, this technique presents a promising solution for combating meter tampering and improving the accuracy and reliability of smart meter data.

This paper presents a study on a cortical learning algorithm that uses synapses, prediction algorithms, and heuristic algorithms to create intelligent systems that can dynamically adjust columns and cells. The goal of this algorithm is to optimize the logistics of neural networks by transforming them into more efficient and effective systems. The algorithm achieves this by using machine learning techniques to predict and adapt to changes in neural activity, leading to improved performance over time. The study provides insights into the potential of this algorithm to revolutionize the way we approach neural network optimization, and highlights the future potential of intelligent systems that can learn and adapt in real time.

Recently, people tend to purchase through websites. This change allows e-commerce sites to collect user behavior data from web logs. E-commerce marketing forces usually make use of such data to come up with subsequent promotional campaign to drive more traffic, and converting into paying customers. In this paper we consider a special kind of e-commerce companies which sell products with similar property and usually at a high price. Therefore, the recommendation becomes less important than prediction of items(if any) bought. We want to discover potential buyers and deliver ads or even coupons to them, expecting them to be real buyers. In this paper, we model the buying behaviors from clicking records with patterns extracted using feature engineering approach. Our solution was to model two kinds of browsing behaviors, namely hesitant and impulsive respectively. In the model, we define some interaction features from click-streams which uncover users' purchase intention with the product pages, how long the user stays on that page, and then build a model which can predict users' preference. Experimental results on a real dataset from an e-commerce company demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The approaches in our work can be used to model user purchasing intent and applied to e-commerce sites which sell high-end products.

This paper proposes a deep learning approach for building detection in satellite multispectral imagery. Specifically, the study focuses on the challenges of detecting buildings in such imagery, including image resolution, training, labeling, and satellite broadcasting. The proposed method utilizes deep neural networks to process multispectral data and generate accurate building segmentation maps. To train the model, a comprehensive dataset is developed that includes diverse building types and environmental conditions. The labeling process involves creating detailed annotations for each building in the dataset. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach through extensive experiments and evaluations. The results show that the proposed method can effectively detect buildings in satellite multispectral imagery, outperforming existing data models and image segmentation techniques. Overall, this research contributes to the development of deep learning methods for remote sensing applications and advances the state-of-the-art in building detection from satellite imagery.

This paper investigates the potential of Tactile Internet as a solution to measuring low latency heart disorientation in automobiles. To achieve this, a mathematical model is proposed to analyze the relationship between heart disorientation and various parameters related to roads, such as Markov processes and probability. This probabilistic logic is then incorporated into machine learning algorithms to train models that can accurately predict low latency heart disorientation in real-time. The results indicate that Tactile Internet is a promising solution for monitoring heart disorientation in automobiles, providing an efficient and reliable means of improving road safety. The study highlights the importance of further research into the application of Tactile Internet technology in the field of road safety, and the potential for this technology to have a significant impact on reducing the number of accidents on our roads.

The Internet of Things (IoT) and connected devices are impacting enterprises, public sector bodies, and citizens in many ways. In parallel, upcoming 5G and Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) are aiming to enable ultra low latency use cases for IoT. This paper proposes to utilize MEC and IoT based architecture for automatic agent reconfiguration in smart manufacturing floors. The EURECOM IoT Platform is extended to achieve this purpose.

The fifth generation (5G) wireless technologies serve as a key propellent to meet the increasing demands of the future Internet of Things (IoT) networks. For wireless communication security in 5G IoT networks, physical-layer security (PLS) has recently received growing interest. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive survey of the PLS techniques in 5G IoT communication systems. The investigation consists of four hierarchical parts. In the first part, we review the characteristics of 5G IoT under typical application scenarios. We then introduce the security threats from the 5G IoT physical-layer and categorize them according to the different purposes of the attacker. In the third part, we examine the 5G communication technologies in 5G IoT systems and discuss their challenges and opportunities when coping with physical-layer threats, including massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO), millimeter wave (mmWave) communications, nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA), full-duplex technology, energy harvesting (EH), visible light communication (VLC), and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications. Finally, we discuss open research problems and future works about PLS in the IoT system with technologies of 5G and beyond.

This paper proposes a statistical approach to estimate imbalance-induced energy losses for data-scarce low voltage networks, which has significant implications for improving energy resolution and reducing power distribution losses. The proposed method is based on time series analysis, which can accurately capture the dynamic variations in power consumption over time. The approach utilizes kernel density estimation to model the probability distribution of energy consumption across different phases of the low voltage network. By using this approach, we can estimate the magnitude and frequency of energy losses due to load imbalance, which can help utilities to devise effective measures to improve load balancing and reduce energy losses. The proposed method is validated using real-world datasets, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately estimating the energy losses. Overall, the proposed statistical approach is a promising tool for improving energy efficiency and reducing power distribution losses in low voltage networks.

The quest for evidence-based decision making in hearing health has largely remained unfulfilled up until now. One of the main reasons is that comprehensive information on hearing-health related factors entangled with the opportunity to make objective comparisons between potential interventions. EVOTION is expected to provide a game-change in this area, by developing a Big Data Informed Decision System to support hearing health policy making at several levels. A framework featuring relevant links between hearing health related factors and models, as the latter have been developed in EVOTION, along with their scientifically proven impact is hereby established to facilitate the investigation for more effective hearing health related strategies in the future.

This paper focuses on the real-time object recognition based indoor humanoid robots like Nao robots. Improving the perceptive ability of service robot has always been a research hotspot. The breakthrough of computer vision technology represented by object recognition provides a broader idea for this purpose. We deployed a micro-cloud layer that connects the robot with the computer vision, thereby realized the concepts of RaaS (Robot as a service). In this paper, in order to make the Nao robot to detect objects faster. We present an architecture about real-time object recognition on Nao, and offload the task of control and data collection from robot to a PC. Next, the image data is transmitted over Ethernet to the workstation, which runs multiple parallel image processing services. These services are built with the current popular deep neural network by TensorFlow and running on a GPU GTX1080 Ti. In the micro-cloud layer, we designed a universal robotic visual task queue model, and a PC registers the task queue to the LAN. There are multiple workers in the LAN, and each worker is an independent service processer. Service processer obtains the task queue from the network and processes the queue, and then the processer puts the results back to the manager. The experimental results of the Nao robot in the simulation and real word show that our model and method are effective. The robot can recognize about 90 kinds of common objects, and each frame of image processing time is about 100 milliseconds.

This study presents a novel active contour model (ACM) driven by weighted global and local region-based signed pressure force (SPF) to segment images in the presence of intensity inhomogeneity and noise. First, an adaptive weighted global region-based SPF (GRSPF) function as the driving centers is designed based on the global image information, which is based on the normalized global intensity to update the weights of the inner and outer regions of the curve during iterations. Second, by introducing the normalized absolute local intensity differences as the weighs of the inner and outer regions, an adaptive weighted local region-based SPF (LRSPF) function is similarly defined. Third, instead of setting a fixed force, a force propagation function is introduced to automatically balance the interior and exterior forces according to the image feature. Meanwhile, by combing the adaptive GWSPF and LWSPF functions, a weighted hybrid region-based SPF function is defined, which can improve the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed model. The experimental results on real images demonstrate that the proposed model is more robust than the popular region-based ACMs for segmenting images with intensity inhomogeneity and noise. The code is available at https://github.com/fangchj2002/WHRSPF.

With the exponential growth in the number of mobile devices, providing Internet access via WiFi in trains is rapidly becoming a necessity. However, providing persistent In-ternet access inside a moving train has many challenges. Cellular network is predominantly used for the backhaul connection to the train. However, high deployment cost of a cellular network and presence of coverage holes in the existing cellular networks of telecom companies may dissuade the railway companies to go for such solutions. In this paper, we propose an SDN based architecture to provide Internet connectivity inside trains. The backhaul connection to the train, in the proposed architecture, is provided via WiFi. Deployment of such an architecture is more cost-efficient than that of a cellular network of the same capacity. Moreover, this architecture can also be used to provide connectivity in the coverage holes of the existing networks of the telecom companies. Through simulation, we show that the architecture can provide high throughput while maintaining per packet delay within reasonable limits inside a train.

This paper proposes a Secret Handshakes-Based Fuzzy Clustering (SHFC) approach for sharing personal e-Health records. The SHFC protocol is designed to provide secure and efficient sharing of health records among different health care providers. The analytical models used in this approach are based on resistance analysis and computational modeling. To ensure privacy and secure sharing, authentication and cryptography techniques are used. The proposed approach has been compared with other clustering-based models and shown to provide better accuracy and efficiency in sharing health records. The results of this study demonstrate that the SHFC model can provide a secure and efficient method for sharing personal e-Health records.

This paper proposes a method that adopts deep autoencoders with binary distributed hidden units (BDAE) as feature extractors in generatively trained DNNs (GTDNN) for voice conversion (VC). In this method, the source and target speakers are modeled separately by two BDAEs, and the extracted high-level features are used to train a Bernoulli bi-directional associated memory network (BBAM) for feature mapping. Then, the estimated model parameters are copied to construct a DNN for voice conversion. Compared with other neural network-based features extractors, such as deep belief networks (DBN) and conventional deep autoencoders (DAE), BDAEs can obtain a better balance between reconstruction error and the degree of binarization of hidden units. Our experimental results show that the GTDNN using BDAEs achieved better naturalness and similarity of converted speech than the ones using DBNs and conventional DAEs. Further experiments show the BDAE model for target speaker played a more important role than the one for source speaker.

This paper proposes a method for detecting cutting tool wear based on convolution neural networks. The focus of this study is on the development of predictive models that can accurately detect wear based on data obtained from the cutting tool during machining. The authors utilize feature extraction techniques to identify key features from the collected data and use these features to build data models which are then used for training the convolution neural networks. The proposed method is evaluated on real-world machining data, and results show that the neural networks achieve high accuracy in detecting wear. By using convolution neural networks for tool wear detection, this study provides a promising approach for improving the reliability and efficiency of machining processes.

This work focuses on recognizing the unknown emotion based on the “Third-Order Circular Suprasegmental Hidden Markov Model (CSPHMM3)” as a classifier. Our work has been tested on “Emotional Prosody Speech and Transcripts (EPST)” database. The extracted features of EPST database are Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Our results give average emotion recognition accuracy of 77.8% based on the CSPHMM3. The results of this work demonstrate that CSPHMM3 is superior to the Third-Order Hidden Markov Model (HMM3), Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Vector Quantization (VQ) by 6.0%, 4.9%, 3.5%, and 5.4%, respectively, for emotion recognition. The average emotion recognition accuracy achieved based on the CSPHMM3 is comparable to that found using “subjective assessment by human judges”.

This paper focuses on the link adaptation strategies for IEEE 802.15.4 WPANs, which are wireless personal area networks based on the IEEE 802.15 standard. The authors study various protocol designs and evaluate their performance in terms of signal to noise ratio, modulation, and encoding. The main goal of link adaptation is to optimize the data transmission rate by adjusting the parameters of the transmitter based on the quality of the wireless channel. The paper analyzes different approaches to link adaptation, including dynamic rate selection, adaptive modulation and coding, and transmit power control. The authors also compare the performance of these strategies using simulations based on realistic channel models. The results show that link adaptation can significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of wireless data communication in WPANs.

The maximum value of an antenna array's sidelobe beampattern, or radiation pattern in the power domain, is an important parameter determining its performance. In this paper, when array antenna elements have random phase centers, we approximate the maximum sidelobe value, or peak sidelobe level, as a Gumbel distribution using the extreme value theory (EVT). Before the EVT result, an expression for the beampattern distribution at each angle in the array field of view is found. From this expression, the pointwise convergence of the difference between the beampattern and exponential distributions in the limit of a large number of antennas is obtained. Using the exponential distribution approximation, EVT is applied with samples of the beampattern. A bound is given for the difference between the beampattern sample maximum and its true maximum in the sidelobe region.

This case study examines the role of cognitive processes and remanence in computer-assisted control training and its subsequent impact on human performance. The study investigated the benefits of integrating visualization techniques and process control training to improve cognitive abilities and increase knowledge retention. The results showed that cognitive processes play a crucial role in effective computer-assisted control training, as remanence and knowledge retention are directly related to the cognitive processes involved in learning. The use of visualization techniques was found to be particularly effective in enhancing cognitive processes, which led to better training outcomes and improved performance. Moreover, the study identified training remanence as an essential factor in successful technology training, highlighting the importance of continued training and practice to maintain high performance levels. The findings of this study can have significant implications for the development and implementation of technology-based training programs, emphasizing the importance of cognitive factors and knowledge retention in achieving desired training outcomes.

Desirable properties of extensions of non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) include robustness in the presence of noises and outliers, ease of implementation, the guarantee of convergence, operation in an automatic fashion that trades off the balance between data approximation and model simplicity well, and the capability to model the inherently sequential structure of time-series signals. The state-of-the-art methods typically have only a subset of these aforementioned properties and seldom simultaneously possess them all. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that provides all these desirable properties by extending the automatic relevance determination framework in NMF from Tan and Févotte. Starting from an objective function derived from the maximum a posterior estimation of a Bayesian model, we develop majorization-minimization algorithms that work effectively to determine the correct model order, regardless of the impact of noise and outliers. Subsequently, we give a rigorous convergence analysis of the proposed algorithms. Moreover, convolutive bases are also incorporated in the basic model so that it is able to capture the richness of temporal continuity. We perform experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets to show the efficiency and robustness of our approach.

The Internet of Things (IoT) regulates millions of terabytes of data for everyday commercial, industrial, technical and personal usage. Considered as the greatest technological revolution, all IoT-based transformations are now occurring to increase productivity and create a coordinated world across business and technologies. However, the exchange, storage, processing and transfer of tremendous amounts of sensitive information has also given rise to severe security and privacy concerns that compromise the efficiency and usability of IoT. It has become a challenge for users to depend on such a vulnerable technology, where the IoT security risks outweigh its benefits. Several defense techniques, algorithms and solution models have been proposed and implemented to counter these attacks. However, there are limitations involved as robust incursions make these solutions obsolete. It is vital to have an overview of the research done and find loopholes to fill in the security gaps to ensure a safe IoT ecosystem. Realizing the need of enhanced problem-solving strategies, this paper provides a systematic review of the existing strategies for IoT security and privacy, and provides an analytical approach in identifying the concerns and solutions. It discusses IoT architecture, classifies the various domains of security and privacy and presents a taxonomy and a comparative analysis to outline the security goals, threats and attacks, and solutions proposed in recent years (2015-2018). Our research methodology comprises of thorough qualitative analyses and a literature review to help evaluate the questions asked in this survey. We also highlight the limitations of the previous studies and the open issues. Our survey results focus on the problems that require further attention to improve the IoT progression.

In this paper, we study the problem of achieving average consensus over a random time-varying sequence of directed graphs by extending the class of so-called push-sum algorithms to such random scenarios. Provided that an ergodicity notion, which we term the directed infinite flow property, holds and the auxiliary states of agents are uniformly bounded away from zero infinitely often, we prove the almost sure convergence of the evolutions of this class of algorithms to the average of initial states. Moreover, for a random sequence of graphs generated using a so-called time-varying B-irreducible probability matrix, we establish convergence rates for the proposed push-sum algorithm.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the low-altitude UAV air-to-air channels. The focus of the study is on atmospheric modeling, loss measurement, and throughput characterization of fading channels. The measurements are conducted using antenna measurements and vehicular ad hoc networks. The results obtained from the measurements are used to develop a model for predicting the performance of UAV air-to-air channels. This model can be used to optimize the design of UAV networks for improved performance. The study provides valuable insights into the behavior of UAV air-to-air channels and can be used to guide the development of future UAV networks. This paper is an important contribution to the area of UAV communication as it provides a detailed analysis of the performance of UAV air-to-air channels.

This paper presents a smart city system using a backend-as-a-service (BaaS) approach for Biskra city as a case study. The concept of smart cities is gaining attention worldwide, with the aim to improve the quality of life for citizens through the use of information and communication technology (ICT). The proposed system utilizes cloud computing to attain scalability and flexibility in data processing, storage and networking. The BaaS approach facilitates communication between application developers and cloud servers, allowing for rapid development and deployment of smart city applications. Measurement of system performance is carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed system. Preliminary results show that the BaaS approach is a promising solution for the development of smart city systems, with potential benefits including reduced costs, increased efficiency and improved quality of services for citizens.

This paper presents a novel adaptive neural-network output feedback control design for uncertain Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) systems with input saturation. The proposed approach utilizes the power of artificial neural networks (ANNs) for controlling chemical reactors. The developed method is generic and can be applied to any CSTR system with unknown nonlinearities, input saturation, and external disturbances. A key feature of this approach is the adaptive control design, which can handle systems with time-varying parameters. Moreover, the proposed control law utilizes only the measurable output feedback resulting in simpler implementation. The numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for a CSTR system with uncertainties and input saturation. The results show that the proposed approach can guarantee the stability and robust performance of the closed-loop system under various input saturation levels and external disturbances. Overall, this study provides a promising solution to the control design for the CSTR system using output feedback control and ANNs.

This paper presents a gesture-based incident reporting system that utilizes smart watches as input devices. The system focuses on the feature extraction and processing of motion data from wrist-worn accelerometers and gyroscopes. This data is then used to classify specific gestures that signal incidents or alarms. The increasingly connected world of the Internet of Things is leveraged to transmit this information to relevant parties, such as emergency services or building maintenance personnel. The use of wrist-based sensors in this system offers an unobtrusive and convenient method for reporting incidents. Furthermore, the system can be integrated with other smart devices to increase its functionality and usability. Overall, the system presents a novel approach to incident reporting by utilizing smart devices and gesture-based inputs.

To improve the accuracy of surface electromyography (sEMG)-based gesture recognition, we present a novel hybrid approach that combines real sEMG signals with corresponding virtual hand poses. The virtual hand poses are generated by means of a proposed cross-modal association model constructed based on the adversarial learning to capture the intrinsic relationship between the sEMG signals and the hand poses. We report comprehensive evaluations of the proposed approach for both frame- and window-based sEMG gesture recognitions on seven-sparse-multichannel and four-high-density-benchmark databases. The experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in sEMG-based gesture recognition compared to existing works. For frame-based sEMG gesture recognition, the recognition accuracy of the proposed framework is increased by an average of +5.2% on the sparse multichannel sEMG databases and by an average of +6.7% on the high-density sEMG databases compared to the existing methods. For window-based sEMG gesture recognition, the state-of-the-art recognition accuracies on three of the high-density sEMG databases are already higher than 99%, i.e., almost saturated; nevertheless, we achieve a +0.2% improvement. For the remaining eight sEMG databases, the average improvement with the proposed framework for the window-based approach is +2.5%.

The demand for high-speed and reliable wireless communications has significantly increased with the introduction of 5G mobile communication networks. However, the effectiveness of 5G in the indoor environment has been limited due to propagation loss and interference. This research focuses on indoor corridor and office propagation measurements at frequencies of 8, 9, 10, and 11 GHz. Antenna measurements and frequency measurements were conducted to determine the characteristics of the propagation path. Data models and computational modeling were developed to evaluate the loss measurements and channel models. The results of the study will aid in the development of effective 5G communication systems in a variety of indoor environments.

As the volume of big data continues to grow rapidly, security concerns related to data privacy have become increasingly pressing. In response, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution. This paper explores the intersection of blockchain, access control, cloud computing and big data security in order to develop an ecosystem for greater data security. The research examines the potential applications of blockchain within the context of access control and provides a conceptual framework for understanding how blockchain can be used to maintain a distributed, secure and decentralised environment for big data. The ecosystem consists of three key components: security features, access control mechanisms, and a governance model. The use of blockchain technology in cloud-based big data environments is proposed as a means of addressing the limitations of traditional access control and enhancing data privacy. This paper argues that the use of blockchain technology in big data access control ecosystems can significantly enhance the security and privacy of business data, thereby promoting the advancement of innovation in the field of big data.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has become an integral part of modern society, enabling the transfer of vast amounts of data in real-time. However, the delay and energy cost associated with IoT data transfers remain a major challenge. In this study, the delay and energy cost of IoT data transfers were modeled and compared. Analytical models were developed for data models, hardware and protocols to assess their impact on delay and energy consumption during data transfer. The results of the study indicate that the choice of data model, hardware and protocol have a significant impact on the delay and energy consumption associated with IoT data transfers. The study also suggests that a balance must be achieved between efficient data transfer and energy cost to maximize the benefits of the IoT. Overall, these findings provide valuable insights for developers and organizations looking to optimize IoT data transfers while minimizing their impact on energy consumption.

This paper presents a novel approach for online recognition of the mental states of drivers using a brain-computer interface (BCI) based on functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and deep neural network (DNN). The proposed system is capable of detecting the cognitive load, stress, and fatigue levels of the drivers in real-time, allowing for timely interventions to prevent accidents. The system is designed to operate in a realistic driving scenario, with participants wearing headphones to minimize external noise interference. The fNIRS-based BCI is capable of monitoring the biological neural networks of the drivers' brains and performing task analysis to recognize changes in their mental states. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in recognizing the mental states of drivers, demonstrating the potential of fNIRS-based BCIs for improving driving safety.

The new technological applications and the advancement of communication have allowed the generation of new applications for sending and receiving data, using low power and reduced costs, thus achieving the implementation of the Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). These networks allow the generation of measurements and analysis of data of short, medium and high scale, for which they have been taken in this investigation, obtaining a communication and sending of information, based on the following levels that are: Beginning of data transmission, process of the sending and receiving of the information received by the Gateway, storage of information and visualization and generation of information reports. In the transmission of data from nodes one and two to the Gateway, it was analyzed that the energy consumption in each sensor is approximately 74.4% (node 1) and 86.8% (node 2) on a bi-monthly basis. that the sensor one needs to be charged 5 times a year, while node 2 needs to be charged 4 times.

A multi-tenant Software as a Service (SaaS) application is a highly configurable software that allows its owner to serve multiple tenants, each with their own workflows, workloads and Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Tenants are usually organizations that serve several users and the application appears to be a different one for each tenant. However, in practice, multi-tenant SaaS applications limit the diversity of tenants by clustering them in a few categories (e.g. premium, standard) with predefined SLOs. Additionally, this coarse-grained clustering reduces the advantage of these multi-tenant ecosystems over single tenant architectures to share dynamically virtual resources between tenants based on their own workload profile and elasticity adaptation decisions. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-agent elasticity management where each tenant is represented by a reinforcement learning agent that performs elasticity adaptations based on a new technical debt perspective, and make use of debt attributes (i.e. amnesty, interest) to form autonomous coalitions that minimise the effect of the unavoidable imperfections in any elasticity management approach. We extended CloudSim and Burlap to evaluate our approach. The simulation results indicate that our debt-aware multi-agent elasticity management preserves the diversity of tenants and reduces SLO violations without affecting the aggregate utility of the application owner.

The combination of smart home platforms and automation apps introduce many conveniences to smart home users. However, this also brings the potential of privacy leakage. If a smart home platform is permitted to collect all the events of a user day and night, then the platform will learn the behavior patterns of this user before long. In this paper, we investigate how IFTTT, one of the most popular smart home platforms, has the capability of monitoring the daily life of a user in a variety of ways that are hardly noticeable. Moreover, we propose multiple ideas for mitigating privacy leakages, which all together form a “Filter-and-Fuzz” (F&F) process: first, it filters out events unneeded by the IFTTT platform. Then, it fuzzifies the values and frequencies of the remaining events. We evaluate the F&F process and the results show that the proposed solution makes the IFTTT unable to recognize any of the user's behavior patterns.

Object location determination has become an important research area in recent years due to its potential applications in various fields. Indoor positioning systems (IPS) and global positioning system (GPS) have been widely adopted for object localization. This paper proposes an advanced determination of object location by combining accelerometers, transceivers, IP networks, radio frequency and magnetometers. The proposed system enhances the accuracy and reliability of object location by utilizing the strengths of different techniques. Accelerometers provide accurate measurements of acceleration and velocity of the object movement, while transceivers and IP networks ensure effective communication between devices. Radio frequency and magnetometers are used for localizing the object with high precision, even in complex indoor environments. The proposed system can be particularly useful for applications that require accurate localization of objects, such as in healthcare, logistics, and navigation. Overall, the proposed IPS technique shows great potential in the determination of object location with high accuracy, sensitivity, and reliability in both indoor and outdoor environments.

This paper presents a wireless sensor system designed for traffic flow detection using measurement of Earth's magnetic field changes. The proposed system utilizes magnetic fields to detect the presence of vehicles on roads and wirelessly communicate the information to a central server, enabling real-time monitoring of traffic flow. The system makes use of advanced magnetic field measurement techniques to accurately detect even the smallest magnetic changes caused by passing vehicles. The developed sensor system is integrated with a wireless network, allowing for seamless communication with the central server. The system is designed for robustness, reliability, and low power consumption, making it well suited for long-term deployment in a variety of traffic monitoring applications. The proposed wireless sensor system has the potential to significantly improve transportation management through real-time traffic flow detection and monitoring, providing valuable insights for traffic engineers, planners, and decision-makers to optimize traffic management strategies.

Image similarity is a core concept in Image analysis due to its extensive application in computer vision. Our study of Quasi Euclidean distance metric displayed a potential in the metric viz-a-viz image similarity computation. Here, it has been used to calculate similarity between input images and images generated by the generative model, Wasserstein Auto-Encoder. Standard GANs are great generative models, but has the concerned training instability. Therefore, we have used Wasserstein Auto-Encoder, which also has proven to generate more accurate images, to produce images on which the performance of the metric has been observed.

Software Defined Network (SDN) is a new network construction. But due to its construction, SDN is vulnerable to be attacked by Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack. So it is important to detect DDoS attack in SDN network. This paper presents a DDoS detection scheme based on k-means algorithm in SDN environment. The establishment of this scheme is based on the two hypotheses that the daily network works normally most of the time, and there is a significant difference between the data characteristics of normal situation and abnormal situation. At the same time, these two hypotheses are also true to the daily network condition. After demonstrating the validity of k-means clustering algorithm, the paper proposes 5 flow table features that can be used to detect DDoS attacks. Finally, the DDoS detection scheme was tested by simulation experiment. The test results showed that the method proposed by the author could effectively detect DDoS, with an average success rate of 97.78%.

We propose UnLearnerVO, a jointly unsupervised learning framework for monocular depth, camera motion estimation from videos. UnLearnerVO is coupled with the relationships of 3D scene geometry and can estimate the 6-DoF pose of a monocular camera in an end-to-end pattern. There are two significant features of the proposed UnLearnerVO: one is an unsupervised depth learning pipeline based on the consecutive /inconsecutive frames, and the other is robustness in a scenario with large camera motion. Specifically, we deeply excavate the pose loop consistency loss, thus optimizing the camera pose and enforcing consistency of the estimated poses across consecutive and inconsecutive frames. Furthermore, a photometric loop consistency loss is proposed, which reduces the disturbance caused by factors such as the dynamic motion object and the photo inconsistency. The experiments on KITTI datasets show that our UnLearnerVO achieves the state-of-the-art results in large camera motion scenarios and performs better than the currently popular unsupervised approaches.

Most of the published research work mainly emphasizes one aspect of knowledge graph construction in isolation and neglects the big data processing flow in this process, which lacks of value in the practical construction of knowledge graph. Therefore, the paper proposes a construction method of domain knowledge graph based on big data-driven and build an artificial intelligence domain knowledge graph to prove the feasibility of this method, which covers artificial intelligence enterprises, patents, news, technology labels and other entities.

In this paper, we propose an intelligent road traffic management system based on a human community genetic algorithm. The genetic algorithm, which is inspired by natural selection, is used to optimize traffic flow and reduce traffic congestion on roads. The system is designed to take input from cameras, atmospheric measurements, and particle measurements, which are used to monitor traffic and ensure safety on the roads. By using the genetic algorithm, the system is able to learn and adapt to changing traffic conditions and improve traffic flow in real-time. The proposed system provides a novel approach to reducing traffic congestion and improving safety on roads, and has the potential to revolutionize our approach to transportation management.

This paper explores computational design methods for statically balanced planar spring mechanisms. The focus is on the use of topology optimization to achieve an ideal spring layout with maximum potential energy storage, while minimizing the internal forces required to maintain static balance. The study proposes and evaluates various design approaches, such as iterative optimization and navigation-based algorithms. The computational models developed in this study can enable the efficient design of spring mechanisms with superior performance and can be utilized in various applications, such as robotics and mechanical engineering. In conclusion, the results of this study suggest that through the proper application of computational modeling and optimization techniques, high-performance planar spring mechanisms with superior energy storage capabilities and low internal forces can be designed.

This paper proposes a discriminative neural embedding learning approach for short-duration text-independent speaker verification. The method utilizes neural networks for extracting features from speech processing data, and applies linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to optimize the feature embeddings for speaker verification. The proposed approach outperforms other analytical models in terms of verification accuracy and training efficiency. The paper concludes that discriminative neural embedding learning is a promising method for short-duration text-independent speaker verification, and can be applied in various speaker recognition applications.

This paper discusses Forward and Reciprocal Noisy Coded Networks, with a focus on precoding, topology, and error analysis. The study investigates the impact of network topology on the performance of precoding schemes and provides a theoretical analysis of decoding errors in such networks. The paper also examines the measurement of noise in these networks and offers insights into estimation theory. The findings of this study suggest that the selection of appropriate precoding schemes and network topology is critical for enhancing the performance of noisy coded networks, while accurate noise measurement and estimation play a crucial role in achieving better overall network performance. Overall, this research sheds new light on the design of noisy coded networks and may have important implications for the development of high-performance communication systems.

This paper presents a new technique that dynamically estimates and updates the coefficients of a digital predistorter (DPD) for power amplifier (PA) linearization. The proposed technique is dynamic in the sense of estimating, at every iteration of the coefficient's update, only the minimum necessary parameters according to a criterion based on the residual estimation error. At the first step, the original basis functions defining the DPD in the forward path are orthonormalized for DPD adaptation in the feedback path by means of a precalculated principal component analysis (PCA) transformation. The robustness and reliability of the precalculated PCA transformation (i.e., PCA transformation matrix obtained off line and only once) is tested and verified. Then, at the second step, a properly modified partial least squares (PLS) method, named dynamic partial least squares (DPLS), is applied to obtain the minimum and most relevant transformed components required for updating the coefficients of the DPD linearizer. The combination of the PCA transformation with the DPLS extraction of components is equivalent to a canonical correlation analysis (CCA) updating solution, which is optimum in the sense of generating components with maximum correlation (instead of maximum covariance as in the case of the DPLS extraction alone). The proposed dynamic extraction technique is evaluated and compared in terms of computational cost and performance with the commonly used QR decomposition approach for solving the least squares (LS) problem. Experimental results show that the proposed method (i.e., combining PCA with DPLS) drastically reduces the amount of DPD coefficients to be estimated while maintaining the same linearization performance.

Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a critical task that has attracted the attention of many researchers and practitioners. The accurate prediction of RUL is essential for timely maintenance and replacement of equipment, which can prevent costly downtime and ensure the reliability of the system. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction method based on a double-convolutional neural network architecture. The proposed method utilizes deep learning techniques to extract relevant features from the degradation data of the equipment, such as vibration signals. Moreover, the convolutional layers of the network enable the model to learn the spatial relationships and patterns in the data. The proposed method outperformed several state-of-the-art RUL prediction methods in terms of prediction accuracy and reliability. Therefore, the proposed double-convolutional neural network architecture serves as a promising approach for accurate RUL prediction in practical applications.

This paper proposes an efficient method for comparison and swap operations on fully homomorphic encrypted data, utilizing the concept of "aggregates" and various encryption libraries. With the increasing usage of cloud computing, the need for secure computation on encrypted data has become crucial. However, the computational efficiency of existing fully homomorphic encryption methods is still a major bottleneck. This paper aims to overcome this challenge and provide a more efficient approach for performing comparison and swap operations on encrypted data. The proposed method utilizes aggregates to represent encrypted data in a compact form, which significantly reduces the computational complexity. Additionally, various encryption libraries are utilized to enhance the computational efficiency of the proposed method. Overall, the proposed approach offers a promising solution for performing secure computations on encrypted data, particularly in the context of cloud computing.

The use of image processing technology for sports is increasing. By analyzing athletes and teams based on video analysis, scientific and objective analysis can be conducted separately from subjective analysis of experts, and individuals or teams can be evaluated with the same index. As can be seen from such a trend, recently, technological progress has made it possible to detect and analyze what can be visually confirmed in the sports video. It is certain that these technologies are helping coaches in the analysis of movement. However, these cannot play the role of coaches. The role is to judge what is important from what can be visually confirmed. There are also empirical and qualitative parts in coach's judgment, and no reproducibility of understanding the important parts unless it is a specialist. Based on this background, we thought that it would be useful to extract more important scenes during the game using quantitative information. Such technology can be applied to various sports, but this paper, we focused on tennis. In this thesis, the aim is to estimate which play was largely contributed to the tennis game result (score, failure). In addition, we don't use supervised information that can be obtained from an empirical point of view. This is to eliminate dataset dependency caused by using data created from qualitative information. Specifically, based on quantitative information such as athletes' movement and score result, we attempted to estimate the attention from unsupervised method.

A new feature-based forecasting framework of abnormalities is presented for early warning for cyber-physical control systems. The abnormalities may refer to intelligent cyber-attacks or naturally occurring faults and failures. Techniques presented here are aimed at protecting against unauthorized intrusions as well as fault prevention. Time series signals from system monitoring nodes are converted to features using feature discovery techniques. The feature behavior for each monitoring node is characterized in the form of decision boundaries, separating normal and abnormal space with operating data collected from the plant or by running virtual models of the plant. A set of ensemble state-space models are constructed for representing feature evolution in time-domain, where the ensembles are selected using Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering. The forecasted outputs are anticipated time-evolution of features, computed by applying an adaptive Kalman predictor to each ensemble model. The overall features forecast is then obtained through dynamic ensemble averaging. This is done by projecting evolution of feature vector to future times in a receding horizon fashion. The features forecast are compared to the decision boundary to estimate if/when the feature vectors will cross the boundary. Simulation results in a high fidelity GE gas turbine platform, show the effectiveness of our approach for forecasting abnormalities.

This paper presents a novel channel estimation scheme for massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) millimeter wave (mmWave) communication system with massive uniform linear array (ULA) at base station (BS) and hybrid architecture. Through practical channel modeling, each channel path is composed of angle information and channel gain information that can be estimated separately. We first propose a general iterative index detection-based channel estimation algorithm (IDCEA) that can obtain both direction of arrival (DOA) and channel gain of each channel path. We then design an enhanced hybrid precoding scheme from the angle domain viewpoint to reduce the inter-beam interferences. Simulation results show that the proposed channel estimation can be better than traditional methods. Finally, numerical examples are provided to corroborate the proposed studies.

In today changing world, Internet of Things (IoT) is creating a new world, where people and businesses can make more timely and better informed decisions about what they want or need to do. Over the last years, agriculture industry in few countries has been expended to smart agriculture. Nevertheless, the agricultural site in Myanmar needs to be technologically advanced with the practice of IoT techniques to provide smart agriculture. But, most of the existing IoT middleware are built to be used by IT professional because of the difficulty of IoT middleware. To admit end users (non-IT professional) to configure the IoT middleware efficiently and effectively, the IoT middleware need to be fully supported network, syntactic and semantic interoperable requirements without recognizing the latent technical details of heterogeneous sensors and devices. In this paper, we propose an interoperable and configurable middleware that incorporates IoT and semantic web techniques with the existing Global Sensor Network middleware to solve the above challenges. The proposed IoT middleware will be implemented and evaluated mainly in plant growth and yields of agriculture area of Myanmar with different types of users and in addition, more diverse services in agricultural domain.

Ultra-wideband (UWB) radars which are mainly focused on contactless detection of breath, heartbeat and other biological signals are generally referred to as biometric radars. It is expecting that these radars will find a whole range of applications from the medical field, through supporting emergency situation solution, up to monitoring people in their dwelling (e.g. ambient assisted living programs). Motivated by promising applications of biometric radars, we will focus in this paper on contactless measurement of breathing frequency and heart rate of static persons by UWB radar. At first, the algorithm for the estimation of the breathing frequency of a person will be outlined. Then, the main emphasis will be placed on the development of an efficient approach for the heart rate estimation. The proposed solution will include radar signal processing procedure for static person ranging, methods for improvement of low-level echo of target-to-clutter and noise ratio (exponential averaging, low-pass filter, Savitzky-Golay filter and single delay line canceller), and finally the heart rate estimation itself (peak-to-average power ratio, Welch periodogram). The good performance of the proposed algorithms will be illustrated by experimental results.

This paper presents a mathematical model for the hydrodynamics of a spherical vehicle used for underwater surveillance. The model incorporates drag and forces exerted on the vehicle during its movement. Computational modeling techniques were used to simulate the behavior of the vehicle in an underwater environment. The results indicate that the drag force increases as the vehicle's speed increases. The model also shows that the forces exerted on the vehicle depend on the orientation of the vehicle relative to the direction of motion. The research contributes to the development of more efficient underwater vehicles and robots for surveillance purposes. The findings suggest that spherical vehicles can be an effective means of underwater surveillance, and the mathematical model presented in this paper can be applied to other designs of such vehicles as well.

Shrimp is one of the most important aquaculture products in Taiwan but has suffered a decreasing breeding rate these recent years. It's difficult to observe their feeding, growth and health due to the muddy and turbid water conditions in shrimp farms. This paper presents the prototype of an underwater surveillance system, which consists of hardware and software to provide underwater observation and automatic analysis for the purpose of smart feeding control and water quality management, and thus improve the farm's productivity.

This paper proposes a possibility-based trust model for mobile wireless networks, which takes into account the uncertainty factors in the network environment. Possibility theory is used to represent and quantify uncertainty, which makes the trust model more suitable for the mobile computing environment. The reliability of nodes is evaluated based on both subjective and objective trust factors, which includes not only the node's past performance but also its potential reliability. The proposed model is particularly suitable for ad hoc networks where node reliability is constantly changing. Routing algorithms based on this trust model are able to make better decisions, leading to higher overall network performance. Finally, a measurement uncertainty analysis is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed trust model.

This paper proposes a self-taught semisupervised approach to dictionary learning. The method makes use of both labeled and unlabeled data during the training process, allowing for more efficient use of available resources. Machine learning techniques are employed to learn dictionaries that accurately represent the data in a low-dimensional space, helping to develop a better understanding of the underlying manifolds present in the data. Nonnegative constraint is incorporated to ensure that the learned dictionaries are easy to interpret and the computation is more efficient. Laplace equations are used to enforce smoothness during the learning process, and sparse matrices are employed to represent the data in a compact form, resulting in more efficient computations. The proposed method is evaluated on a wide range of tasks, including image classification, object recognition, and speech recognition. Results show that the approach is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance, making it a promising direction for future research.

Monolithic 3D ICs have gained popularity due to their high performance and power efficiency. However, power-supply noise is a critical issue during testing, which can affect the reliability of power delivery. In this paper, we investigate the analysis of power-supply noise and propose a reliable power delivery scheme to address the uncertainty in power supply during testing. This scheme not only improves the throughput but also enhances the gain and signal to noise ratio. Further, we study the impact of fading channels on power delivery and present a probability density function-based channel estimation technique to address channel variability. The proposed scheme can significantly reduce the occurrence of power failures and ensure reliable power delivery for high-performance 3D ICs.

This paper presents a low-power receiver architecture that is suitable for both 5G and IoT-oriented wireless information and power transfer applications. The proposed receiver utilizes detectors and Schottky diodes to convert the received signal into a low-voltage DC signal that can power the receiver circuitry. Additionally, the receiver employs wireless sensor networks and energy harvesting techniques to further enhance its power efficiency. The decoding process is performed using a low-power digital signal processing algorithm that ensures accurate and reliable data transmission. Overall, the proposed receiver architecture offers a promising solution for low-power wireless communication systems that can operate in energy-constrained environments.

With the introduction of Internet of Things (IoT), we are witnessing the greater use of the mobile Internet with the exponential explosion of smartphones, tablets, and laptops. The IoT paradigm is revolutionizing the way we live, work, and communicate. In this context, the availability of a connectivity technology, which is reliable, scalable, and efficient, will play a major role to develop the emerging IoT system. Certainly, the fifth generation (5G) networks are emerging as the key enabler supporting IoT systems. In this paper, we discuss the potential of 5G technologies and architecture for the future IoT systems. We review the main 5G enablers for the IoT systems. Besides, we also extensively discussed the security and privacy aspect of IoT system and the potential research directions.

This paper proposes a Fully Polarized SAR imagery classification method based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) technique using multiple polarimetric features. The proposed method embraces a new dimension of feature extraction which involves the task analysis of remote sensing images. The feature extraction step involves the use of multiple polarimetric features such as co-polarization scattering matrices, degree of polarization, and other image features that aid in the classification process. The DRL method is used to train the classification model which helps in the selection of optimal feature combinations that minimizes training time and increases classification accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method is tested on real SAR imagery datasets, where support vector machine (SVM) is used as the baseline classifier. Experimental results show that the proposed method has a superior performance compared to traditional machine learning techniques. The proposed approach benefits from the reinforcement learning technique, where the use of games creates a suitable environment for learning and adaptation to the remote sensing analysis task.

Multimedia researchers have exploited large collections of community-contributed geo-referenced images to better understand a particular image, such as its subject matter or where it was taken, as well as to better understand a geographic location, such as the most visited tourist spots in a city or what the local cuisine is like. The goal of this paper is to better understand location. In particular, we use geo-referenced image collections to better understand what occurs in different parts of a city at fine spatial and activity class scales. This problem is known as land use mapping in the geographical sciences. We propose a novel framework to perform fine-grained land use mapping at the city scale using ground-level images. Mapping land use is considerably more difficult than mapping land cover and is generally not possible using overhead imagery as it requires close-up views and seeing inside buildings. We postulate that the growing collections of geo-referenced, ground-level images suggest an alternate approach to this geographic knowledge discovery problem. We develop a general framework that uses Flickr images to map 45 different land-use classes for the city of San Francisco, CA, USA. Individual images are classified using a novel convolutional neural network containing two streams: one for recognizing objects and another for recognizing scenes. This network is trained in an end-to-end manner directly on the labeled training images. We propose several novel strategies to overcome the noisiness of our user-generated data including search-based training set augmentation and online adaptive training. We derive a ground truth map of San Francisco in order to evaluate our method. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through geovisualization and quantitative analysis. Our framework achieves over 29% recall at the individual land parcel level that represents a strong baseline for the challenging 45-way land use classification problem, especially given the noisiness of the image data.

CSRS, short for Chinese Seal Recognition System, is a novel system that integrates multi-task learning and automatic background generation to recognize Chinese seals accurately and efficiently. Seals have long been regarded as an important part of Chinese art and are widely used in many areas such as authentication and signature verification. Therefore, there is a high demand for a reliable recognition system, which is provided by the CSRS. The system is trained using a database of various seal images, which are annotated with different measurement parameters such as length, width, and thickness. In addition, the system also incorporates face detection, which helps in the extraction of seal features and improves recognition accuracy. The data models used in the system are optimized to improve training speed and reduce computational complexity. The CSRS also utilizes a novel feature extraction algorithm which is effective in extracting discriminative features from seal images. Overall, the system achieves high recognition accuracy and can be applied to various fields requiring Chinese seal recognition.

This paper proposes a method for improving color images of extremely low light scenes. The proposed approach includes noise reduction techniques and employs image edge detection and Discrete Cosine Transforms to enhance the image quality. The method involves estimating the noise in the image and then filtering it out to reduce the noise in the final image. The proposed technique has been tested on images taken with different cameras and has shown improved results compared to existing methods. The findings of this study are presented and discussed in detail at conferences and forums where image processing and computer vision research are topics of discussion. The proposed approach is expected to be useful in a wide range of applications, such as night-time surveillance, remote sensing, and astronomical imaging.

We have examined how people use qualitative models to reason about the continuous world. In exploring how analogy interacts with qualitative representations to simulate based on experience (chapter 12), we have seen the beginnings of how such knowledge might be learned. This chapter delves into learning and conceptual change in more detail. I start by laying out the broad theory that Dedre Gentner and I have been building about the range of types of human representations that get constructed in the course of learning in physical domains. Then I will drill down into particul ar aspects of this framework, beginning with how prototypical behavi ors are constructed and used to build initial qualitative models. Because many of our concepts come from our culture, rather than discovered on our own, a model for conceptual change is described that accounts for how models are changed in response to new information. The use of analogy to learn expert models, both within and across domains, is also discussed.

With the development of wireless communication, the issue of communication system security has become increasingly important. In recent years, the application of artificial intelligence and array signal processing technology in wireless communication has been widely studied. The introduction of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) provides a promising solution to improve the wireless communication system security. In this paper, we propose an optimization method based on linear programming to design the location and phase shift of the reflecting elements in the IRS. The proposed method aims to maximize the received signal power at the receiver end and minimize the interference from other sources. The optimization problem is solved using the gold-based algorithm, which guarantees high accuracy and efficiency. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving secure wireless communication via intelligent reflecting surface. Furthermore, this study provides useful guidance for the design and implementation of IRS-based wireless communication systems.

In the field of system on chip (SoC) verification, the use of virtual platforms has become an increasingly popular technique. This paper presents an industrial case study on seamless SoC verification using virtual platforms. The study focuses on a range of hardware and software tools, as well as the use of field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and IP networks. Additionally, the study examines a variety of libraries and industry-standard models to provide an insight into best practices for SoC verification. The results of the study demonstrate the effectiveness of virtual platforms in facilitating more efficient and cost-effective prototyping, with the potential to reduce development time and improve overall product quality. This research adds to the growing body of literature on virtual platforms for SoC verification and provides useful insights for those working in the field.

This paper presents a novel approach to reduce channels in speech recognition systems using surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. The focus is on the use of electrodes for electromyography and speech recognition. The proposed method involves feature extraction using band-pass filters, frequency-domain analysis, and data acquisition. The aim is to reduce the number of channels used in the system while maintaining a high level of accuracy. The results show that the proposed method can achieve a significant reduction in the number of channels without sacrificing accuracy. This approach has the potential to reduce the complexity and cost of speech recognition systems, making them more accessible to a wider range of users.

The Internet of things systems (IoT) has a significant impact on different aspects of our lives. For that reason, IoT systems should be in high quality and clean of defects. The quality measurements for IoT systems vary according to the type of the IoT system and its applications. Therefore, IoT systems should be quality measured differently considering the presence of heterogeneous objects bound together to build the IoT system. This diversity leads to a variety of quality measurement model, which makes the process of measuring quality more challengeable, less accurate, and less applicable. In this research, different quality models for IoT systems have been studied and compared regarding the quality factors. Besides, a new quality model for IoT has been proposed. The new model focused on all the characteristics related to IoT systems, by introducing quality factors that measure them.

In this paper, we present an experimental evaluation of Long-Term Evolution (LTE) throughput in cellular networks using Device-to-Device (D2D) multi-hop communications. The focus of this study is to investigate how the use of relays in D2D multi-hop communications can improve throughput in LTE networks. The performance of the system is evaluated using computer architecture and routing algorithms. The throughput of the downlink, which is the transmission of data from the base station to the user device, is also studied. Our experimental results show that the use of D2D multi-hop communications with relays can significantly improve throughput in LTE networks. Furthermore, we found that optimization of the routing algorithm is critical in achieving maximum throughput. Our research sheds light on the potential benefits of D2D multi-hop communications in improving network performance and provides insights for future research in this area.

This paper proposes a method for planning wireless terminal access network based on the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process. The proposed method takes into consideration various standards and requirements for wireless communication networks, such as color coding and base station deployment. The analytic hierarchy process is used to evaluate the different factors involved in network planning and optimization. The method also accounts for the increasing heterogeneity in wireless networks and provides a practical solution for optimizing network performance. Overall, this approach provides a comprehensive and effective strategy for planning wireless terminal access networks.

The paper presents a wavelet-fuzzy controller of a field-oriented control system of belt conveyor drive. A discrete wavelet transform is used to decompose the speed error signal into various frequency components. The transformed error coefficients and scaling coefficients are used to generate the motor control signal The proposed controller is satisfied the speed control problem for a closed control system. The field-oriented control scheme with a wavelet-fuzzy controller under various dynamic operating conditions was investigated. The results of the comparison of the work of the traditional PI controller and the proposed wavelet-fuzzy controller are presented. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed wavelet-fuzzy controller. Application of the proposed approach of the wavelet-fuzzy controller allows reducing of electromagnetic moment vibrations.

In the field of photography, the dynamic range of an image refers to the difference between the brightest and darkest points. The ability to capture a wide dynamic range in an image has been a challenge for cameras, especially in situations where lighting conditions are not ideal. This paper proposes a novel technique for generating low dynamic range image sets from a single image using neural networks. The technique involves training the neural network on a dataset of images with varying dynamic ranges and then applying the trained model to generate multiple low dynamic range images from a single input image. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, particularly in challenging lighting conditions such as direct sunlight. The proposed technique has potential applications in various fields, including digital photography, computer vision, and image processing.

The Microelectronics Cloud Alliances Project aims to strengthen the collaboration between the labor market and higher education by providing new open educational resources in the microelectronics field. The project is focused on microelectronics and cloud computing, two interconnected areas that are key for innovation in technology. Educational materials and resources are being created for companies and higher education institutions to use in training and educating the next generation of experts in the field. Integrated circuits are the basis for much of modern technology, and the need for well-trained professionals in this area is increasing. The project seeks to increase collaboration between companies and higher education institutions to ensure that the skills being taught are relevant and applicable in the workforce. The resources created as part of this project will be openly available for anyone to use and adapt, ensuring widespread access to the latest knowledge and skills in this important field.

As a nondestructive diagnosis method, hammering test is a popular approach for detecting defect on concrete surfaces. However, as the number of concrete structures that require inspection is increasing, it is an important issue in recent years to reduce inspection time and human cost during hammering test. This paper introduces a novel method to detect defect on concrete surfaces in real-time during hammering test. The proposed method has two features; 1) automatically analyzing the acoustic data based on the statistical data of hitting sounds without prior training data, 2) the diagnostic results immediately displayed by projection mapping to the hit positions. We show the effectiveness of the proposed system through the experiments by using test concrete block with defects.

ICT are one of the most important value for the economic growth. Technology, information, and knowledge has an important impact in peripheral regions when they want to participate in the global market.
