Exists a lot of discussion about the digital divide between countries but little in relation to the regions and especially Less Favoured Regions (LFR). There is a clear evidence that these internal disparities can lead to the continued marginalization of people and regions “disconnected” from global information networks, which support the modern economy and causing strong inequalities. By other side, data available about the ICT use are normally from central regions and not Less Favoured Regions. With this study, we made a study to understand the ICT use by small enterprises and entrepreneurs from peripheral regions from Portugal and Spain: 5 Spanish regions (Leon, Zamora, Salamanca, Valladolid, Ávila) and 2 Portuguese (Alto Tâmega e Terras de Trâs-os-Montes). For that, 433 surveys were carried out (170 in the Portuguese regions and 263 in Spanish areas), included in project COMPETIC.

In this paper, we propose a polarization-based power-splitting full-duplex relaying scheme design for SWIPT (Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer) system. The proposed scheme utilizes relays to aid in energy harvesting and information processing for wireless communication, while also incorporating recycling techniques to ensure maximum efficiency. In order to mitigate interference, the scheme uses polarization-based techniques to split the power between the relay and the receiver. Furthermore, the proposed design can be integrated into IP networks for seamless integration with existing communication systems. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in improving the performance and energy efficiency of SWIPT systems.

The stator winding structure of the main exciter of the brushless synchronous starter/generator (BSSG) is changed at high speed for flux weakening, leading to a sudden excitation decrease of the main generator (MG) of BSSG. Consequently, when proportional-integral (PI) current loop-based control strategies are applied, large current overshoots will occur due to the lack of fast current control ability. This paper adopts model predictive current control (MPCC) to replace PI current control for a better dynamic performance. Besides, a parameter estimation scheme, based on the recursive least square (RLS) algorithm, is proposed to provide MG parameters for MPCC. An effectiveness analysis of the RLS algorithm is performed and two rules are given. According to the two rules, rather than the parameter dynamic characteristics adopted by traditional methods, three MG parameters, dq-axes inductances, and excitation flux linkage are estimated with two decoupled RLS estimators. In addition, a method is proposed to adjust the forgetting factor to track fast changing parameters of MG when the excitation changes suddenly. With the estimated parameters, MPCC is conducted to start BSSG. Experimental results show that fast current control of MG is achieved and large current overshoots caused by the sudden excitation change are avoided.

In this paper, we propose a novel multiperson behavior feature generation model based on noise reduction using WiFi. The proposed model utilizes antennas to capture wireless signals and generate a mathematical model for feature extraction. The model takes advantage of Wireless Fidelity (WiFi) and wireless communication technologies to provide accurate information about the behavior of multiple individuals in a given space. The proposed model can be used in various applications, such as training and monitoring of individuals in different environments, such as classrooms, offices, and public spaces. The approach is capable of dealing with noise reduction to achieve high-precision feature generation in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The proposed model can enable monitoring and analysis of multiperson behavior in real-time, making it a viable solution in behavior analysis and monitoring systems. Overall, the proposed model provides a promising approach to improve the performance and accuracy of multiperson behavior feature generation in noise-prone environments.

Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of death among women worldwide. Early detection and diagnosis are crucial for effective treatment and management of this disease. In this regard, infrared imaging has been increasingly employed as a non-invasive and low-cost imaging modality for breast cancer diagnosis. However, the accurate classification of static and dynamic breast infrared images is still a challenge due to the complexity and variability of the breast tissues. To overcome this challenge, various methods have been developed. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for classification. The proposed approach showed promising results for static and dynamic breast infrared imaging classification, which can contribute to the early detection and diagnosis of breast cancer. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was evaluated on publicly available datasets using standard evaluation protocols. This study shows the potential of CNNs for feature extraction and SVMs for classification in improving the accuracy and reliability of breast cancer diagnosis using infrared imaging.

Machine fault diagnosis plays a crucial role in ensuring reliable and safe operation of industrial systems. In recent years, deep learning algorithms, especially neural networks, have shown great potential in this field. One important task in neural network-based fault diagnosis is to efficiently extract informative features from high-dimensional data. Manifold Sparse Auto-Encoder (MSAE) is a novel deep learning approach that combines the powerful feature extraction ability of auto-encoders with the manifold learning technique. MSAE is composed of two neural networks, encoding and decoding, that work together to minimize the reconstruction error and encourage the activations of neurons to exhibit a sparse distribution. By exploring the underlying manifold structure of the data, MSAE is able to extract meaningful and discriminative features for fault diagnosis. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of MSAE in comparison with other state-of-the-art methods. In summary, the proposed MSAE provides a promising approach for machine fault diagnosis by leveraging the advantages of both auto-encoders and manifold learning.

Traditional power grids are being transformed into smart grids (SGs) to address the issues in the existing power system due to uni-directional information flow, energy wastage, growing energy demand, reliability, and security. SGs offer bi-directional energy flow between service providers and consumers, involving power generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization systems. SGs employ various devices for the monitoring, analysis, and control of the grid, deployed at power plants, distribution centers, and in consumers’ premises in a very large number. Hence, an SG requires connectivity, automation, and the tracking of such devices. This is achieved with the help of the Internet of Things (IoT). The IoT helps SG systems to support various network functions throughout the generation, transmission, distribution, and consumption of energy by incorporating the IoT devices (such as sensors, actuators, and smart meters), as well as by providing the connectivity, automation, and tracking for such devices. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey on the IoT-aided SG systems, which includes the existing architectures, applications, and prototypes of the IoT-aided SG systems. This survey also highlights the open issues, challenges, and future research directions for the IoT-aided SG systems.

This paper investigates the use of digital predistortion techniques to improve the linearity of vertically cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) - single mode fiber (SSMF) based radio-over-fiber links. The authors introduce the concept of predistortion and discuss the implementation of a training algorithm to optimize the system's performance. The study also focuses on the application of this technique in the Long Term Evolution (LTE) standard for wireless communication, highlighting the benefits of increased linearity. The results demonstrate the efficacy of digital predistortion in reducing distortion and improving system performance. This approach shows promise in mitigating the effects of nonlinearity in VCSEL-based systems and contributing to the development of more efficient and reliable communication systems.

In this paper, we introduce a promising secure and privacy-preserving incentive mechanism in the vehicular cloud (VC). Such an incentive will convince vehicles with excess sensing data to join in the VC without the risk of privacy disclosure. The proposed scheme uses the Bargain Game theory to model the interactions between a VC server (VCS) and vehicles. With the proposed incentive mechanism, the VCS can select competent vehicles with which to collaborate for the announced task, while the vehicles can earn payment for participation. Further, our mechanism ensures fairness between all participants in terms of reward. We also exploit the signcryption technique to achieve mutual authentication between the VCS and vehicles as well as to prevent the private information of these vehicles from being disclosed. Simulation results are provided to show that the proposed privacy-preserving incentive mechanism is beneficial to both the VCS and vehicles, resulting in a win-win situation.

Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain computer-interfaces (BCIs) have shown its robustness in facilitating high-efficiency communication. State-of-the-art training-based SSVEP decoding methods such as extended Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) and Task-Related Component Analysis (TRCA) are the major players that elevate the efficiency of the SSVEP-based BCIs through a calibration process. However, due to notable human variability across individuals and within individuals over time, calibration (training) data collection is non-negligible and often laborious and time-consuming, deteriorating the practicality of SSVEP BCIs in a real-world context. This study aims to develop a cross-subject transferring approach to reduce the need for collecting training data from a test user with a newly proposed least-squares transformation (LST) method. Study results show the capability of the LST in reducing the number of training templates required for a 40-class SSVEP BCI. The LST method may lead to numerous real-world applications using near-zero-training/plug-and-play high-speed SSVEP BCIs.

We study the effect of close-proximity in the estimation of the Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) using a monopulse antenna array system, with application to angle-sensitive proximity WiFi readers. It is shown that in this scenario, it is necessary to consider near-field radiative effects to make an accurate angular estimation at short distances between the mobile terminal and the DoA proximity sensor. As a result, we define a range-dependent angular monopulse function, which provides a better DoA estimation in a Field of View of 60° and for distances ranging from 3 m to 50 cm.

This paper analyzes the application of machine learning techniques in detecting network intrusion beyond 1999. The study utilizes a partially labeled cybersecurity dataset to extract features and create a model for intrusion detection. The training of the model includes the implementation of boosting to improve its accuracy. Anomaly detection is used to identify deviations from the norm in network behavior, which can indicate a potential intrusion. Overall, the results show that machine learning can effectively detect network intrusions, even in the absence of complete labeling in the dataset. This study has important implications for computer security, as it highlights the potential of machine learning in improving cybersecurity defenses.

This paper proposes an improved method for L-BFGS initialization in trust-region methods for deep learning optimization. Deep learning is a popular area of machine learning algorithms that has shown great success in various tasks analysis such as image and speech recognition. Optimization is a key component in training deep learning models, and improving the convergence rate can significantly reduce the computational cost of model training. The proposed method involves solving a linear programming problem to obtain an initial trust-region radius and scaling factor. The experiments demonstrate that the improved initialization method can achieve faster convergence rates and better performance compared to existing methods. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for improving deep learning optimization using trust-region methods.

In this paper, we propose a combined approach of Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and support vector machines (SVM) to automatically localize software faults. Firstly, GMM is used to segment the training data into clusters, which helps identify the regions of feature space with similar characteristics. Secondly, SVM is employed to classify the faulty or healthy instances. The kernel function is adopted to project the data into higher dimensions, which improves the SVM accuracy. Our experiments show that the proposed approach presents an effective method for software fault localization as compared with traditional techniques. The combination of GMM and SVM techniques provides better results in terms of classification accuracy and localization speed. Ultimately, this research has important implications for the field of computer bugs, as it proposes an innovative solution for detecting software faults automatically.

As the urban population increases the urban density becomes denser. The first to be affected is the traffic, 30% of traffic is caused by vehicles cruising for parking. One of the solutions is to deploy a smart parking assisted by Wireless Sensor Network (WSN), thus the cities can optimize parking re-sources and provide a transparent and smart services. Drivers can get real-time parking availability information through their smartphone. The aim of this paper is to introduce an intelligent parking system based on WSN by identifying their benefits, challenges and constraints while providing real-time availability information. We will focus on the WSN MAC layer and protocols proposed. We start with a state of the art of smart parking solutions based on WSNs and their politics to solve the current parking problems. Then we discuss the different solutions of MAC protocols proposed in real time service context and we finish with a comparative of these solutions to identify their strengths and limitations.

This paper proposes a fast and efficient technique for constructing an equivalent model of patch antenna for predicting its radiation pattern. The equivalent model of the antenna is constructed based on its radiation properties. First, the initial model of the antenna is developed and then the arrangement of the initial model is optimized using FEKO optimization tool. The electric field of the magnetic dipole is determined based on numerical Green function derivation. The magnetic dipole is used to construct the equivalent model of patch antenna based on the radiation mechanism to predict its radiation pattern. Only two design parameters needed to be optimized making it more computational efficient. The derived radiation pattern from the equivalent model is validated with that of the original antenna model on FEKO to evaluate its efficiency. The simulation results show that the proposed equivalent model based on a magnetic dipole is fast and efficient and do not require the antenna's detailed material information.

Recent development in inventory management shows that the use of lateral transshipment to pool inventory promotes the customer service. Inspired by the existing works, this paper studies the lateral transshipment policy in an inventory system consisting of multiple retailers. We model this problem as Markov Decision Process (MDP), and several desirable properties of the optimal lateral transshipment policy are developed. The primary contribution of this study lies in its effort to extend the state-of-the-art results on two retailers to arbitrary number of retailers. Since the computational capacity required for solving large-scale MDP is prohibitive, a comprehensive heuristic lateral transshipment policy is proposed. The effectiveness of the heuristic is demonstrated through numerical experiments. This study brings new perspectives on seeking a balance between benefits and risks of lateral transshipment actions taken by retailers, and provides practical insights on inventory management problem involving lateral transshipment.

Neuroscience behavioral animal studies often require injecting DNA material or fluorescent dyes into specific brain regions within the animal's skull. Currently, these types of injections or surgical procedures are done manually by skilled researchers using mechanically based stereotaxic platforms. However, alignment can be very time-consuming and prone to error due to the small size of brain targets.Here we propose to develop a next generation stereotaxic platform for small animals by combining a three-dimensional (3D) computer vision sub-system and a full six degree-of-freedom (6DOF) robotic platform to improve spatial accuracy and surgical speed. With this approach, a video projector projects a series of structured illumination patterns onto an animal skull. Two video cameras are then used to capture two-dimensional (2D) images of the skull and the captured 2D images are processed to reconstruct an accurate 3D skull profile based on geometrical triangulation. Using the reconstructed 3D skull profile, the skull can be guided and repositioned using a 6DOF robotic platform to precisely and accurately align a surgical tool with the intention of reaching a specific brain target. This new stereotaxic system may improve accuracy and speed of small-scale brain surgeries for neuroscience studies.

Recently released 5G networks empower the novel Network Slicing concept. Network slicing introduces new business models such as allowing telecom providers to lease a virtualized slice of their infrastructure to tenants such as industry verticals, e.g. automotive, e-health, factories, etc. However, this new paradigm poses a major challenge when applied to Radio Access Networks (RAN): how to achieve revenue maximization while meeting the diverse service level agreements (SLAs) requested by the infrastructure tenants? In this paper, we propose a new analytical framework, based on stochastic geometry theory, to model realistic RANs that leverage the business opportunities offered by network slicing. We mathematically prove the benefits of slicing radio access networks as compared to non-sliced infrastructures. Based on this, we design a new admission control functional block, STORNS, which takes decisions considering per slice SLA guaranteed average experienced throughput. A radio resource allocation strategy is introduced to optimally allocate transmit power and bandwidth (i.e., a slice of radio access resources) to the users of each infrastructure tenant. Numerical results are illustrated to validate our proposed solution in terms of potential spectral efficiency, and compare it against a non-slicing benchmark.

Cloud computing (CC) is the emerging technology in the world for hosting and delivering services over the internet. It offers a variety of benefits such as cost saving, access to different services without any installation from anywhere and any time by internet, etc. Despite all the advantages offered by CC, this technology still susceptible to security threats. From user point of view, CC seems to be very insecure due to security attacks which threaten it and limit its widespread adoption. More motivations are required to provide more trustworthy solutions to secure the cloud as much as possible and preserve users trust. For that, we propose a new model called "profiling and preventing security attacks", abbreviated to PPSA, to detect and prevent the known attacks as well as the unknown attacks before accessing the cloud services/resources. Unlike the existing solutions, such as intrusion detection systems (IDSs), the proposed solution is able to be deployed in a wide area network in the basis of internet and prevent unknown attacks. In this study, we propose a new solution to profile and prevent security attacks in CC. Then, we define new security factors based on keystroke dynamic. Afterwards, we integrate a machine learning algorithm (classification based on associations) to our proposal in order to profile and predict security attacks and optimize as well the PPSA scheme. Eventually, the proposal is illustrated by a realistic case study.

In this brief introduction to tracking using state estimation, we compare two techniques. We compare the performance of the well known Kaiman filter to that of a simple receding horizon filter, a less well known technique. Our goal is to introduce the less well known family of techniques and show some of its advantages and disadvantages relative to Kalman-filter-based techniques.

The identification of persons through partial fingerprint is one of the basic biometrie matters. The context of use is situated particularly in forensics. The main issue is the insufficiency of information contained in the partial fingerprint, it depends from the size of the proportion found in the crime scene. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for the identification of persons through partial fingerprint which uses redefined characteristics of minutiae extracted from the fingerprint image. To validate our work, we exploit two complete databases FVC 2004 and POLYU HRF to form our dataset. The proposed approach reaches recognition rates up to 98.06% and 98.82% when using datasets extracted from POLYU HRF database and FVC 2004 database respectively. It outperforms four state-of-the-art methods in term of recognition rates in different percentage of incomplete fingerprint image.

The effectiveness of different brain states for person authentication using Electroencephalography (EEG) technology is investigated in this paper. The study focuses on analyzing the most reliable features for authentication, and proposes a task analysis framework for identifying specific cognitive tasks that can improve the accuracy of authentication. Furthermore, brain modeling is used to develop an understanding of the mechanisms underlying the authentication process, and to derive optimized electrode placements for EEG data acquisition. The paper discusses several challenges such as variations in brain activity and other confounding factors that can affect the accuracy of EEG-based authentication systems. Nevertheless, the proposed framework and methodology can greatly enhance the efficacy and reliability of person authentication systems based on EEG technology. Overall, the study highlights the potential applications of EEG technology for developing secure and reliable person authentication systems.

This paper explores the optimization of Cleanset growth through the use of Multi-Class Neural Networks. The study examines various software packages, operating systems, and security measures to identify and isolate malware. With the increasing risk of security breaches and cyber attacks, it is vital to uncover new and innovative ways to enhance security protocols. Through the implementation of machine learning algorithms, such as neural networks, the detection of malware can be improved, thereby strengthening the overall security of computer systems. This research provides valuable insights for professionals in the field of computer science to develop and implement advanced security measures. The findings have practical implications for various industries where data security is of paramount importance. Overall, this study highlights the significance of using Multi-Class Neural Networks as a tool to optimize Cleanset growth and enhance security measures in the field of computer science.

This paper presents a novel similarity measurement approach for discriminant vector machines (DVMs) which are a type of support vector machine classification algorithm. The proposed method aims to improve the performance of DVMs by effectively identifying and dealing with noisy data during training. The noise measurement is used to quantify the degree of noise present in input data, and the closed-form solutions are employed to solve the optimal similarity measures. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of classification accuracy and robustness to noise, which makes it suitable for various pattern recognition applications. The proposed approach is expected to provide a more efficient and accurate solution for similar machine learning algorithms in different applications.

This paper proposes a digital current hysteresis controller based on wide bandwidth inductor current estimation for buck converters. The use of hysteresis control and pulse width modulation with fast switching frequency allows for smooth current tracking and reduced inductor ripple. The proposed controller applies an estimation algorithm to accurately predict inductor current and maintain steady control. The use of wide bandwidth inductor current estimation also improves the stability of the controller when working under high input voltage or load variations. Overall, this digital current hysteresis controller provides an efficient and reliable solution for controlling inductor current in buck converters.

This paper introduces a method for inferring the deployment of source address validation filtering using silence of path-backscatter. The term "backscatter" refers to the indirect form of communication that occurs when a network node responds to a query, causing unintended messages to be sent to other nodes. The authors apply this concept to IP networks, specifically, Internet routing, to determine whether a network is implementing source address validation filtering. By using logic gates and telescopes to analyze path-backscatter, they are able to isolate patterns of filtering behavior. This technique has important implications for computer crime prevention, as filtering can act as a defense against spoofing attacks. Furthermore, understanding the prevalence of filtering can help ISPs and network administrators to make informed decisions about network protection.

Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) is a new paradigm that relies on edge devices to process and store data locally. This approach has gained popularity in recent years due to its ability to reduce latency and enhance user experience. However, MEC systems face the challenge of provisioning reliable virtualized network function services in a dynamic environment. In this paper, we propose a reliability-aware approach for provisioning virtualized network function services in MEC. We present both approximation and heuristic algorithms that consider the reliability of the network functions when selecting the optimal virtual network function service chain. The proposed approach takes into account the reliability of the cloud computing resources and the mobile devices in the edge computing environment, making it suitable for real-world scenarios. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can effectively provide reliable virtualized network function services in MEC. This work contributes to the development of more efficient and reliable MEC systems that can meet the demands of future mobile applications.

In recent years, cyber physical systems have become a critical component in various industries such as the energy sector. However, these systems are prone to numerous security challenges, which could lead to serious consequences. One of the solutions is to incorporate machine learning algorithms to detect potential attacks in real-time, which can significantly improve the security of cyber physical systems. To achieve this, feature extraction techniques can be applied to data collected from various sources in order to effectively detect anomalies. In particular, monitoring turbine data can be useful in identifying potential attacks, as turbines are a critical component in power generation plants. The Internet of Things (IoT) can provide a useful framework for monitoring and controlling cyber physical systems. Overall, incorporating machine learning algorithms and effective monitoring techniques can significantly enhance the security posture of cyber physical systems.

This paper proposes a self-adaptive generalized S-transform (SAGST) for time-frequency analysis and applies it to seismic data. The SAGST is capable of adjusting its shape to adapt to different types of signals, making it a more versatile transform compared to traditional fixed-shape transforms. The proposed method also incorporates the use of Microsoft Windows for computational modeling, making it easy to implement and reproduce. The effectiveness of the SAGST is demonstrated through its application to seismic data, where it outperforms traditional transforms in terms of resolution and accuracy. The results suggest that the SAGST has potential for use in various other fields beyond seismic analysis.

This paper proposes a multistage deep residual network for biomedical cyber-physical systems, which leverages the power of deep learning to analyze electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) signals. The proposed network is designed to address the challenges associated with analyzing complex signals such as EEG and ECG, including high levels of noise and variability. The network consists of several convolutional layers followed by residual blocks, and utilizes neural networks to extract features from the signals. The use of residual connections allows the network to learn from the residual errors of previous layers, resulting in improved accuracy and faster convergence. The proposed network is evaluated using real-world EEG and ECG data, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately and efficiently analyzing these signals. This research contributes to the development of cyber-physical systems in the biomedical field by providing a powerful deep learning-based approach for analyzing complex signals from sensors.

In recent years, Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have become increasingly popular for realistic image synthesis. However, training GANs can be a computationally expensive and time-consuming process. In this paper, we propose DepthwiseGANs, a novel fast training method for GANs that utilizes depthwise separable convolutions to reduce the computational cost of training generators. Our approach has been evaluated on face synthesis tasks, with promising results compared to state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, we analyze the impact of different configurations on training time and quality of the generated images. Overall, our results suggest that DepthwiseGANs represent a promising approach for efficient and effective generative adversarial networks, with potential applications in computational modeling and computer architecture.

Recommender systems are used to analyze users' preferences through their past activities and to personalize recommendations for each user based on what they might be interested in. The performance of the recommender system is most commonly measured using only recommendation accuracy. However, recommending accurate items does not mean that the generated recommendation is the best for the user because it can be biased towards some items that have a higher chance of being liked by users, such as popular items. Recommendations become repetitive and obvious with biased item selection and are less likely to be personalized. To mitigate bias and repetitiveness, recommendation diversity has been studied. However, diversity has a trade-off relationship with accuracy. Modifying the recommendation algorithm to consider diversity while learning about user preferences would not only cause loss in accuracy, but also lead to less precise reading of user preferences. Instead, using ranking methods to re-rank the priority of items predicted, the recommendation algorithm would keep the preciseness of the algorithm. In this study, a ranking method using the appearance frequency of items to restrict the items from being frequently recommended will be proposed. The experimental results showed that the proposed method consistently improved diversity in multiple diversity metrics.

Compressively Sensed Image Recognition (CSIR) has been a topic of great interest in recent years due to its applications in various fields such as surveillance, medical imaging, and remote sensing. CSIR involves the combination of image coding, feature extraction, and image reconstruction based on discrete cosine transforms (DCTs) in order to accurately recognize the content of images acquired through sensors. In this paper, we present a task analysis of CSIR and provide a comprehensive review of the existing techniques for image recognition using sparse representations. We also discuss the advantages and disadvantages of various feature extraction methods such as principal component analysis and wavelet transform. Furthermore, we present a comparison of different image reconstruction algorithms such as compressed sensing-based methods and dictionary-based methods. Finally, we discuss the future prospects of CSIR and its potential applications on Microsoft Windows platforms.

With the development of VR technology, simulation driving can provide diverse user experience. In this paper, we built an immersive simulation driving system by Unity 3D and VR technology and in this system Logitec G29 is served as an interactive device. In this system, the user can control the virtual vehicles in the traffic scenario through the behaviors of driver, including rotating steering wheel, braking, turning on the direction indicators and accelerating. The user-defined evaluation model can be introduced into the system easily to calculate the evaluation results through the user's operation data collected in real time, including braking time, steering wheel angle, etc. This feature makes our system can be used for drivingrelated training and assessment scenarios widely. We proposed a safety awareness assessment models and conducted related experiments to verify this feature. In addition, the system's scene can be changed according to different purposes, which make the system be more flexible to adapt to different types of virtual driving research.

A complex network is a network with non-trivial topological structures. It contains not just topological information but also attribute information available in the rich content of nodes. Concerning the task of cluster analysis in a complex network, model-based algorithms are preferred over distance-based ones, as they avoid designing specific distance measures. However, their models are only applicable to complex networks where the attribute information is composed of attributes in binary form. To overcome this disadvantage, we introduce a three-layer node-attribute-value hierarchical structure to describe the attribute information in a flexible and interpretable manner. Then, a new Bayesian model is proposed to simulate the generative process of a complex network. In this model, the attribute information is generated by following the hierarchical structure while the links between pairwise nodes are generated by a stochastic blockmodel. To solve the corresponding inference problem, we develop a variational Bayesian algorithm called TARA, which allows us to identify functionally meaningful clusters through an iterative procedure. Our extensive experiment results show that TARA can be an effective algorithm for cluster analysis in a complex network. Moreover, the parallelized version of TARA makes it possible to perform efficiently at its tasks when applied to large complex networks.

In this paper, we propose an LSTM-based end-to-end framework for biomedical event extraction. The proposed framework integrates different components of the event extraction process, including feature extraction, data mining, and biological system modeling, into a single LSTM network. The LSTM network is trained to learn the relationships between logic gates and event semantics, as well as the interactions between different proteins involved in the event. Our experimental results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on a benchmark biomedical event extraction dataset. This research enhances the understanding of the complex interactions between different biological systems, enabling more accurate and efficient identification of important biomedical events.

The performance of salient object segmentation has been significantly advanced by using the deep convolutional networks. However, these networks often produce blob-like saliency maps without accurate object boundaries. This is caused by the limited spatial resolution of their feature maps after multiple pooling operations and might hinder downstream applications that require precise object shapes. To address this issue, we propose a novel deep model—Focal Boundary Guided (Focal-BG) network. Our model is designed to jointly learn to segment salient object masks and detect salient object boundaries. Our key idea is that additional knowledge about object boundaries can help to precisely identify the shape of the object. Moreover, our model incorporates a refinement pathway to refine the mask prediction and makes use of the focal loss to facilitate the learning of the hard boundary pixels. To evaluate our model, we conduct extensive experiments. Our Focal-BG network consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on five major benchmarks. We provide a detailed analysis of these results and demonstrate that our joint modeling of salient object boundary and mask helps to better capture the shape details, especially in the vicinity of object boundaries.

Driven by the tremendous technological advancement of personal devices and the prevalence of wireless mobile network accesses, the world has witnessed an explosion in crowdsourced live streaming. Ensuring a better viewers quality of experience (QoE) is the key to maximize the audiences number and increase streaming providers' profits. This can be achieved by advocating a geo-distributed cloud infrastructure to allocate the multimedia resources as close as possible to viewers, in order to minimize the access delay and video stalls. Moreover, allocating the exact needed resources beforehand avoids over-provisioning, which may lead to significant costs by the service providers. In the contrary, under-provisioning might cause significant delays to the viewers. In this paper, we introduce a prediction driven resource allocation framework, to maximize the QoE of viewers and minimize the resource allocation cost. First, by exploiting the viewers locations available in our unique dataset, we implement a machine learning model to predict the viewers number near each geo-distributed cloud site. Second, based on the predicted results that showed to be close to the actual values, we formulate an optimization problem to proactively allocate resources at the viewers proximity. Additionally, we will present a trade-off between the video access delay and the cost of resource allocation.

Real-time power system state estimation and forecasting play a crucial role in ensuring the stability and reliability of power systems. To address this issue, the use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) has been proposed as an effective solution due to their ability to model complex systems. In this paper, we present a Deep Unrolled Neural Network (DUNN) for real-time power system state estimation and forecasting. The proposed network architecture unrolls a state estimator and a forecaster trained based on high-frequency data, which allows for capturing the system dynamics and improving the forecasting accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach on the IEEE 14-bus power system and show that our method achieves superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art approaches. Our approach can potentially help power system operators better monitor and control power systems by providing accurate and timely state estimation and forecasting.

Aiming at the complicated problem of the radiation model in the traditional infrared image simulation and the practical problem that the model usability is difficult to verify, a simulation method of building object infrared image based on guided filtering enhanced feature prediction is proposed. Based on guided filter enhancing feature extraction of the measured images, the images are divided into different regions according to different properties of the material, and the infrared simulation images of the middle time are obtained by feature prediction and fusion. The experimental results show that the infrared enhancement image of the building object which is generated by this algorithm is consistent with the change of the enhanced image, whether it is from the subjective visual effect or the gray histogram. What's more, the algorithm effectively avoids the cumbersome data processing in the general simulation, and has an engineering practical value, low computational complexity, good real-time performance.

Efficient deployment of predictive analytics in edge gateways has become increasingly important for various applications scenarios, including the fall detection scenario. The use of logic gates and image edge detection techniques can simplify the processing of data within the edge gateway, which is a vital component in the Internet of Things (IoT) architecture. Cloud computing has been widely adopted for the deployment of predictive analytics models due to its flexibility and scalability. However, in some scenarios, such as those with limited connectivity or high data traffic, edge computing is a better option. This paper proposes several proposals for the efficient deployment of predictive analytics in edge gateways, including the use of computer architectures optimized for edge computing and the development of adaptive analytics models that can dynamically adjust their processing to match the resources available. These proposals have the potential to significantly improve the performance and efficiency of deploying predictive analytics in edge gateways.

Semantic scene segmentation plays an essential role in various computer vision applications, including autonomous driving and robotic navigation. In recent years, deep learning methods and specifically convolutional networks have achieved remarkable advancements in this area. One significant factor in the success of these networks is the decoding process, which assigns labels to the image pixels based on the learned features. In this paper, we propose a new decoding method based on a bracket-style decoder, which improves the semantics and spatial resolution of the segmentation results. Our approach integrates convolutional neural networks for feature extraction and uses deep learning methods for labeling the pixels. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for future research in the field of semantic scene segmentation. Overall, our work suggests that the proposed bracket-style decoder can improve the performance of convolutional network-based segmentation approaches and lead to promising results in various computer vision applications.

The current input-output table takes about 4 years from the start of the survey to the release, it is not suitable for analysis of real-time industries, and it takes a lot of labor to create. In order to solve this problem, the input-output table is being constructed using the corporate data possessed by Teikoku Databank (TDB) Co., Ltd. However, since the calculation of private consumption is based on the total sales of (BtoC) companies that are selling to consumers, it is not possible to record in the spent where it was consumed. Therefore, in this research, we estimate the sales ratio to consumers in the BtoC company and calculate the total sales amount to consumers in the sales of the company. Also, by dividing the total of the private consumption obtained proportionally according to the population size of each region, we construct an algorithm to calculate private consumption in each region.

The security and self-diagnosis of optical fiber networks have become a critical concern in modern communications. There is an urgent need for an effective approach to monitor and diagnose the performance of optical fibers in real-time to ensure the security of data transmission. This paper proposes a new routing protocol, which incorporates an optical polarization-based self-diagnosis scheme. The proposed protocol enables the monitoring of the polarization state of the optical signal, which provides information about the health status of the optical fiber network. Additionally, the use of polarization diversity techniques enhances the security of the communication channel, ensuring that any eavesdropper or attacker is unable to gain access to the transmitted data. The proposed protocol is suitable for a wide range of optical networks and can be easily implemented in both conventional and advanced optical networks. Our results demonstrate that the proposed protocol can effectively detect and diagnose faults in optical fiber networks while simultaneously providing robust security.

This paper proposes a cluster-based distributed Media Access Protocol (MAC) protocol for multichannel cognitive radio ad hoc networks. The proposed protocol aims to reduce delays and improve the throughput of cognitive radio ad hoc networks. The protocol is based on a clustering algorithm that divides the network into clusters, and each cluster has a cluster head responsible for managing the communication within the cluster. Cognitive radio technology is employed to enable efficient spectrum utilization and ensure coexistence with other wireless networks. The proposed protocol also incorporates Markov processes to model the channel status and make decisions on channel selection. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol outperforms existing MAC protocols in terms of throughput and delay. Overall, the proposed protocol offers a promising solution for efficient and reliable communication in multichannel cognitive radio ad hoc networks.

This paper focuses on the assessment of cognitive fidelity in a situation awareness process model through the use of computational and atmospheric modeling. Cognitive processes and task analysis are integral to the development of an analytical model for measuring cognitive fidelity. The time factor is also taken into consideration to ensure the accuracy of the results. The study draws on theories from cognitive science to better understand the role of cognitive fidelity in modeling and how it can be improved. Overall, this research contributes to the field of computational modeling by providing a comprehensive framework for assessing the cognitive fidelity of situational awareness models.

This paper addresses the problem of protection coordination in microgrids operating in both grid connected and islanded mode. The focus is on the use of relays and optimization techniques to achieve efficient and reliable protection in the microgrid. Various techniques such as linear programming and genetic algorithms are presented to optimize relay settings and minimize circuit faults. The paper also discusses the impact of fault currents on power system stability and the need for coordinated protection methods. The results from simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques in enhancing the performance of protection schemes in microgrids. The findings are useful for system designers and operators in achieving robust and efficient protection coordination in microgrids.

The assessment of pathological samples by molecular techniques, such as in situ hybridization (ISH) and immunohistochemistry (IHC), has revolutionised modern Histopathology. Most often it is important to detect ISH/IHC reaction products in certain cells or tissue types. For instance, detection of human papilloma virus (HPV) in oropharyngeal cancer samples by ISH products is difficult and remains a tedious and time consuming task for experts. Here we introduce a proposed framework to segment epithelial regions in oropharyngeal tissue images with ISH staining. First, we use colour deconvolution to obtain a counterstain channel and generate input patches based on superpixels and their neighbouring areas. Then, a novel deep attention residual network is applied to identify the epithelial regions to produce an epithelium segmentation mask. In the experimental results, comparing the proposed network with other state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, our network provides a better performance than region-based and pixel-based segmentations.

This study focuses on the specific data analysis of the Baxter Robot in the context of MES (manufacturing execution system). The key parameters analyzed include torque and force, utilizing data mining techniques for feature extraction and principal component analysis. Collision avoidance is an important consideration in industrial robots, and the data analysis provided valuable insights for improved performance and safety. The study highlights the importance of targeted data analysis in enhancing robot performance in real manufacturing settings. The results demonstrate the potential of advanced data analysis techniques to facilitate efficient and safe operation of industrial robots, ultimately improving productivity and reducing manufacturing costs.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is a core task in the remote sensing community, and recently, deep learning-based methods have shown their capability of accurate classification of HSIs. Among the deep learning-based methods, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for the HSI classification. In order to obtain a good classification performance, substantial efforts are required to design a proper deep learning architecture. Furthermore, the manually designed architecture may not fit a specific data set very well. In this paper, the idea of automatic CNN for the HSI classification is proposed for the first time. First, a number of operations, including convolution, pooling, identity, and batch normalization, are selected. Then, a gradient descent-based search algorithm is used to effectively find the optimal deep architecture that is evaluated on the validation data set. After that, the best CNN architecture is selected as the model for the HSI classification. Specifically, the automatic 1-D Auto-CNN and 3-D Auto-CNN are used as spectral and spectral-spatial HSI classifiers, respectively. Furthermore, the cutout is introduced as a regularization technique for the HSI spectral-spatial classification to further improve the classification accuracy. The experiments on four widely used hyperspectral data sets (i.e., Salinas, Pavia University, Kennedy Space Center, and Indiana Pines) show that the automatically designed data-dependent CNNs obtain competitive classification accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art methods. In addition, the automatic design of the deep learning architecture opens a new window for future research, showing the huge potential of using neural architectures' optimization capabilities for the accurate HSI classification.

Optimization has always been a crucial aspect of various fields including sociology, statistics, and information and communication technology. In recent times, many evolutionary algorithms have been developed for optimization purposes. One such algorithm is the Prey Phase-based Grey Wolf Optimizer. This algorithm is based on the hunting behavior of grey wolves and has been effective in solving a wide range of optimization problems. The algorithm's ability to converge quickly while maintaining the diversity of search makes it suitable for benchmark testing. Additionally, studies have shown that the Prey Phase-based Grey Wolf Optimizer performs better than traditional optimization algorithms such as particle swarm optimization. Therefore, this optimization algorithm can be utilized in different fields to achieve better results.

This paper proposes a feature selection method based on hybrid improved binary quantum particle swarm optimization (HI-BQPSO) for solving search problems in feature extraction. HI-BQPSO is created by combining binary particle swarm optimization and quantum particle swarm optimization, which results in a better convergence and diversity of search. The method also utilizes correlation coefficient as a measure of feature relevance to further improve its performance. The proposed method is tested on several benchmark datasets and compared with other popular optimization algorithms such as neural networks and genetic algorithms. Results show that the HI-BQPSO outperforms the other algorithms in terms of classification accuracy and feature selection efficiency. Overall, the method provides an effective solution for feature selection in practical applications.

In recent years, POI recommendation has become a hot research topic in the field of data mining and machine learning. The goal of POI recommendation is to provide personalized recommendations for users based on their preferences and historical behavior. To overcome the limitations of traditional recommendation methods, this paper proposes a novel approach called Context-Aware Attention-Based Data Augmentation for POI Recommendation. The approach is based on task analysis and logic gates, which are used to identify relevant contextual information and determine the weight of different features in the recommendation process. Additionally, various data models are employed to facilitate the decoding and context modeling tasks. To enhance the performance of the proposed approach, training is conducted using recurrent neural networks, which are capable of capturing the temporal dependencies in users' behaviors. The experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms several state-of-the-art POI recommendation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

The accurate modeling of capacitance within VLSI devices is crucial for ensuring the proper functioning of logic gates and circuits. This study focuses on the extraction of the BSIM3v3 junction capacitance model of NMOSFET. P-n junctions within these devices have a significant impact on capacitance, and computational modeling is utilized to accurately capture their behavior. The use of semiconductor device modeling techniques allows for a more comprehensive understanding of the behavior of MOSFETs, which are the cornerstone of modern integrated circuits. By accurately representing capacitance within these devices, designers can more effectively optimize circuit performance and reliability.

In recent years, intelligent fault diagnosis technology with the deep learning algorithm has been widely used in the manufacturing industry for substituting time-consuming human analysis method to enhance the efficiency of fault diagnosis. The rolling bearing as the connection between the rotor and support is the crucial component in rotating equipment. However, the working condition of the rolling bearing is under changing with complex operation demand, which will significantly degrade the performance of the intelligent fault diagnosis method. In this paper, a new deep transfer model based on Wasserstein distance guided multi-adversarial networks (WDMAN) is proposed to address this problem. The WDMAN model exploits complex feature space structures to enable the transfer of different data distributions based on multiple domain critic networks. The essence of our method is learning the shared feature representation by minimizing the Wasserstein distance between the source domain and target domain distribution in an adversarial training way. The experiment results demonstrate that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on rolling bearing fault diagnosis under different working conditions. The t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) technology is used to visualize the learned domain invariant feature and investigate the transferability behind the great performance of our proposed model.

This paper proposes a brake detection method for electric bicycles using inertial measurement units (IMUs). The main goal of this work is to estimate the bicycle's deceleration and brake resistance by analyzing the acceleration data obtained from the IMUs. The study successfully demonstrates that the proposed method can accurately estimate the braking events, showing promising potential for future use in electric bicycles. Additionally, this approach shows improved results under various driving conditions, such as different wind speeds and vehicle dynamics. Overall, this research inspires future work on developing low-cost and effective safety features for electric bicycles.

In this paper we are mainly classifying cancerous or non-cancerous cells of human lung which was further classified into which category it falls benign or malignant. Area feature from region of interest (ROI) and Support Vector Machine is applied for classification and CLAHE as an enhancement technique. This paper concentrated on classification of lung nodules by Support Vector Machine technique.

The security of group communication systems in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is critical for ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of information. A lightweight group key distribution method based on high similar wireless channel characteristics is proposed to improve the security performance of WSNs. The proposed method uses the unique similarities of wireless channels to identify potential members of a group and verify the received keys. Parity check codes are introduced to validate the identities of group members and ensure efficient key distribution. The proposed method takes into account the network topology and connects members based on their wireless channel characteristics. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively distribute keys to group members with high efficiency while maintaining high security performance. This approach provides a promising solution for improving the communication system security in WSNs, which is crucial for ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of information.

This paper explores the potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in renewable energy systems and smart grids. Specifically, the paper focuses on five novel applications of AI: fuzzy logic, smart grids, engines, expert systems, and artificial neural networks. Fuzzy logic systems have been found to be effective in optimizing energy consumption and improving energy efficiency in renewable energy systems. Smart grids, which involve the integration of AI technologies, have the potential to improve the reliability and efficiency of energy distribution. Engines, which can be optimized using AI techniques, can be used to generate clean energy from renewable sources. Expert systems can be used to optimize energy management and storage. Finally, artificial neural networks can be used for predictive maintenance and fault diagnosis in renewable energy systems. Overall, the paper highlights the significant role that AI can play in advancing renewable energy systems and smart grids, and the potential for further research and development in this area.

The prediction method plays crucial roles in the accurate prediction of rockfall runout range which could improve the protection of endangered residential areas and infrastructure. Recently, the Knearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm, one of many machine learning techniques, showed good performance in pattern classification. Therefore, the aim of this study was to use the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm to predict the rockfall runout range which is classified into different subintervals according to the distance from the slope toe. First, we proposed the prediction model of the rockfall runout range based on our improved KNN algorithm which could better offer robustness against different choices of the neighborhood size k, and it is the first work of applying our improved KNN algorithm to rockfall runout range prediction. Second, the shaking table tests of rockfall runout models were conducted for simulating the rockfall process, and the influence laws of factors-including types of an earthquake, peak ground acceleration, vibration frequency, slope angle, slope height, and block mass and block shape-on rockfall distance are investigated. Finally, there is a discussion of the performance of our proposed prediction model based on our improved KNN algorithm in the prediction of rockfall runout range. The extensive experimental results for rockfall runout range prediction demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed prediction model.

A mass measurement system using relay feedback of velocity was developed. In this system, the velocity of the object was fed back through a relay with a hysteresis. Although the efficacy of the proposed method has been already confirmed experimentally, it was subject to drift mainly because only the velocity was fed back. To prevent such drift, a spring element was added to produce restoring force. However, smaller drifts still occurred and the trajectory of the object fluctuated because the switching positions are not determined uniquely. In this paper, an estimation formula is derived, which can estimate the mass regardless of switching positions. The efficacy of the derived formula is confirmed experimentally.

This paper presents a semi-formal functional verification method based on a stage transition graph model for specifying the behavior of hardware systems. The approach is defined using unified modeling language for creating a formal representation of the system behavior. Furthermore, the automatic test pattern generation method is utilized to ensure the timing correctness of the hardware systems. The proposed method incorporates computational modeling that supports the verification of the system's functionality. Moreover, the method leverages the use of registers to capture the state of the hardware systems. This paper highlights the hardware scalability of the proposed approach in order to cater to larger systems. Overall, the approach shows promising results in achieving efficient and accurate verification of hardware systems.

This paper evaluates the migration of FTTx access networks for IPTV services, focusing on servers, modems, and other related components. The integration of IPTV with DSL services presents new opportunities for customer relationship management and improvements in the signal to noise ratio. The increasing use of optical fiber networks provides the infrastructure necessary for delivering high-quality IPTV content. Through a comprehensive analysis of the migration process, this paper aims to provide valuable insights and recommendations for the successful deployment of IPTV services in FTTx access networks.

High integration densities and design complexity of printed-circuit boards make board-level functional fault identification extremely difficult. Machine learning provides an opportunity to identify functional faults with high accuracy and thereby reduce repair cost. However, the large volume of manufacturing data comes in a streaming format and exhibits time-dependent concept drift in a production environment. These drawbacks limit the effectiveness of traditional machine-learning algorithms. We propose a diagnosis workflow that utilizes online learning to train classifiers incrementally with a small chunk of data at each step. These online learning algorithms adapt to concept drift quickly with carefully designed update rules. A hybrid algorithm is also proposed to handle the scenario that data for varying numbers of boards are collected at different times. Experimental results using two boards in high-volume production show that, with the help of online learning and the proposed hybrid algorithm, the F1-score for diagnosis can be improved from 57.3% to 78.9%.

The interface between mobile phone technologies and innovation remains largely under-researched. Attempting to bridge this knowledge gap, this cross-sectional study of Kenyan enterprises examines the role of mobile phone technologies in innovation. The study applies probit estimators to a comprehensive dataset of 24, 164 micro, small and medium establishments in Kenya. The study reveals that; (1) mobile technologies are positively and significantly correlated with product and marketing innovation but are insignificantly correlated with process innovation. (2) The predicted probabilities of product, process and marketing innovation increase with the increase in the ICT index. (3) The effect of age and size on the propensity of innovation is concave: older and larger establishments tend to innovate more than relatively younger and smaller ones, but the relationships get reversed after a certain threshold. (3) The predicted probability of product, process and marketing innovation increase with increases in R&D, training, credit and foreign trade.

The five articles in this special section focus on data science and artificial intelligence (AI) for communications. The innovation in AI, machine learning (ML), and network data analytics provides a huge opportunity to revolutionize the world’s communications systems and user experience. Through gathering, processing, learning, and controlling the vast amounts of information in an intelligent manner, these analytics tools enable the possibility to automate and optimize systems in a way that was not previously possible. This is particularly important as the communications infrastructures evolve to support increasingly more complex human type as well as machine type communications and enable, through the connectedness of meters, sensors, and things, a plethora of new services. Supporting such immensely diverse traffic patterns and applications will require dynamic, highly adaptive network environments, all the while ensuring highly reliable, secure, and ultra-low-latency service performance guarantees.

Attack path discovery plays an important role in protecting network infrastructure. Unfortunately, previous attack path discovery algorithms are difficult for applying in reality because of the high computational complexity problem. To achieve effective attack path discovery, we proposed a compact graph planning algorithm to incorporate goal states related information into attack path discovery. Our model extracts goal states related information by calculating closure of goal states, and then construct planning graph structure given the closure, after which the backward search algorithm is used to extract the attack path solution. The experiments were done on the typical enterprise network, comparing the effectiveness of attack path discovery algorithms with existing known methods. The result turns out that our proposed compact graph planning algorithm shows great improvement in discovering attack paths.

Industrial/Engineering training act as a supportive role in developing students' working skills. However, traditional training only involves face-to-face learning environments. Therefore, enforcing learning among students with different learning speed would be difficult. In this work-in-progress paper, we proposed adopting the Flipped Classroom approach to an engineering training course (Internet of Things module). Students can have a flexible laboratory schedule in exploring on acquired technical skills. For streamlining the learning process, the “First Principles of Instruction” framework had been used for guiding the design of learning activities. Ways of adopting the framework for learning activity design had been described in details.

Recent researches in neural network models have shown great potential in image inpainting task, which focus on finding reasonable area from known content to predict missing pixel values of incomplete image and generate new images. However they still create distorted structures and textures that are inconsistent with surrounding areas and require further post processing to optimize the results. Especially for face repair problems, it is often necessary to generate semantically new images that contain a large number of appearance. In addition, many recent approaches limited their applications in the field center region inpainting, which have difficulties to repair border regions or large missing area. Motivated by these observations, we introduce dilated skip architecture, which combines the advantages of dilated convolution and U-net. With this combination, our proposed network can enlarge the perception area for better repairing, as well as preserve the completeness of the original image features during the repairing process. Experiments on CelebA show that our approach can effectively deal with image inpainting problems and obtain images with higher qualities than previous ones.

Traditional template attack is more severe to attack conditions. It requires a large amount of energy traces and plaintext and ciphertext pairs. In some cases, attackers cannot obtain plaintext or ciphertext so that traditional template attack fails. In this paper, Gaussian Mixture Clustering Algorithm is introduced to solve the problem, which enables attackers to still perform template attacks and relaxes the attack conditions. In addition, this paper uses a strategy to select appropriate plaintext to improve the accuracy of attacks.

Machine learning based Insider Threat Modelling and Detection has become an increasingly significant topic in the field of security. Machine learning algorithms, which are a subset of artificial intelligence, can be used in developing effective models for identifying as well as detecting potential insider threats. The use of machine learning algorithms for insider threat modelling and detection is gaining popularity due to the significant benefits it can offer to organizations.

One of the main advantages of using machine learning is its ability to learn from large datasets. Feature extraction is one of the key elements in machine learning-based insider threat modelling and detection, which allows relevant data to be extracted from vast amounts of data collected by logistics and other sources. The extracted features can then be used to create models that can effectively identify and detect malicious insider activities.

In conclusion, the use of machine learning based insider threat modelling and detection holds significant promise in improving security for organizations. This is achieved through the provision of a proactive strategy for detecting and mitigating insider threats, ultimately helping organizations to safeguard their valuable assets. Data collection is also critical when it comes to machine learning-based insider threat modelling and detection. Therefore, continuous monitoring and data collection would need to be prioritized in order to ensure that machine-based algorithms continue to develop better models over time.

Indoor localization is of great importance in various applications, such as navigation, security monitoring and asset tracking. Wireless sensor networks provide a promising solution for indoor localization due to their convenience and low costs. In this paper, we proposed a novel indoor localization method based on channel state information (CSI), which is a powerful tool to extract information from wireless signals. The proposed method utilizes the wireless fidelity (Wi-Fi) signals and the sensors to collect CSI measurements and then employs data models to estimate the locations of the targets. Specifically, the method constructs a radio frequency (RF) fingerprint database by collecting the CSI measurements at different locations and then matches the real-time CSI measurements with the database to estimate the locations. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and robustness in various indoor environments, which verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

The data porting technique is an important aspect of remote sensing that involves the transfer of data and information across various scales. This technique relies heavily on data models, interpolation, and splines in mathematics. The data collection process is also crucial to the success of this technique, as accurate and reliable data is required for effective estimation and minimization. Understanding the intricacies of data porting across scales and the associated mathematical techniques is crucial for researchers and practitioners in the field of remote sensing. Future developments in this area will likely involve advances in technology and new approaches to interpolation and data collection.

The International Electro technical Commission (IEC) IEC 60060-1: 2010 describes the requirements and how to calculate impulse waveform parameters. This paper proposes a curve fitting methods for determining the lightning Impulse voltage waveform parameters according to Standard IEC 60060-1:2010. Curve fitting is important for waveform parameter evaluation in testing and research on high voltage engineering. This paper presents a method to estimate the waveform parameters according to the standard IEC 60060-1: 2010. Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm has been applied for this purposes. The standard lightning impulse waveform generated by the test data generator attached with IEC 61083-2. It found that the developed software can be used in the waveform parameter evaluation accurately.

Fabric defect detection is a significant phase of quality control in textile industry. Manual defect inspection lacks the accuracy and the labor cost is high. Automating this process is challenging due to a large number of fabric types and defect types. Defect detection relies on the identification of regions that are different from the uniform background. Our intention is to develop a system to detect defects in uniform textured fabrics with Image Processing techniques and Neural Networks. The results indicated that the use of light beams based on the color of the material is more effective than the white light beam.

The detection of anomalous behavior in high density crowd scenes is a challenging task that involves efficient methods for feature extraction and tracking. In this paper, we propose an Oriented Tracklets approach for detecting anomalous activity in such scenes. Our approach utilizes the Entropy measure for feature extraction, which allows us to identify salient features in crowd scenes. We also employ Histograms to model the distribution of features across the crowd scene, and Shape information to capture the geometric properties of the scene. The Trajectory information for each individual in the crowd is then tracked using Active contours, which are used to model the motion of the individuals. The proposed approach is evaluated on a large dataset of crowd scenes, and the results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Overall, our approach offers a promising direction for detecting anomalous behavior in high density crowd scenes, which has a wide range of applications in public safety and security.

The development of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) has been pivotal in advancing the field of image classification. In this paper, we focus on the optimization of DCNN architecture using genetic algorithms (GAs). Our approach involves encoding the architecture as a chromosome and analyzing the task requirements to develop fitness functions for GA. This allows us to evolve the architecture of the DCNN based on task-specific constraints and objectives. Our results show that this approach can lead to architectures that outperform traditional manually designed models. This technique has implications for other areas of computer architecture and optimization, where the use of GAs can streamline the design process and lead to more efficient and effective solutions.

The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) plays a pivotal role in the functioning of critical infrastructure. However, it also poses some significant security challenges. This paper focuses on securing the IIoT for critical infrastructure (IIoT-CI), exploring the various software and protocols used to create the IIoT. Risk management is identified as an essential factor in ensuring the security of the IIoT-CI, and machine-to-machine communications are also discussed in detail. The paper discusses various security measures that can be implemented to strengthen the security of the IIoT-CI, including secure communication protocols, access control, and security monitoring. The overall conclusion is that securing the IIoT-CI requires a comprehensive approach, incorporating hardware, software, and network security measures to ensure that this critical infrastructure remains secured against cyber-attacks.

In recent years, the use of biometric authentication techniques has been on the rise due to their wide range of applications in security and identification systems. A promising area of research in biometrics is finger vein recognition. This paper proposes a novel approach for feature extraction in finger vein images using modified maximum edge position octal patterns. The proposed method utilizes image edge detection and mathematical modelling to extract patterns from the veins. These patterns are then represented as histograms and used for pattern recognition. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately recognizing the vein patterns in fingers, while achieving high recognition rates for typical databases used in vein recognition research. This research serves to enhance the development of biometric authentication systems using finger vein recognition technology.

Pilot contamination is considered as a bottleneck in the massive multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. In a previous work, we proposed a novel iterative algorithm, dubbed channel Zooming Algorithm (CZA), to ensure the mitigation of pilot contamination effect. For this, we assumed that each cell is assigned a set of orthogonal pilot sequences and that these same pilot sequences are reused in other cells. In this paper, we propose a novel strategy of pilot design, based on the divide-and-conquer approach (DCA), aiming to halve the contamination power observed by the channel estimate and to conquer the remaining pilot contamination through the iterations of the CZA. More precisely, instead of being contaminated by a given number of contaminants, as in the initial approach of the CZA, the user, in the proposed approach, is contaminated by a twice the number of contaminants, while halving the pilot contamination power coming from each one of them.
