The fundamental saliency (FS) method can utilize both the d- and q-axis currents, but it suffers from a model mismatch that variable components of the inductances are not exactly sine or cosine functions of double the rotor position. This paper proposes the rotational frame fundamental saliency (RFFS) method which basically performs the FS method in the rotational frame. The RFFS method can overcome challenges regarding the model mismatch and utilize both currents for position estimation. Experimental verification revealed that the RFFS method improved torque accuracy at very low speed and increased the maximum torque for stable operation by exploiting both currents compared to the AF method.

Training operators for activities ran on automotive manufacturing lines is a long, thorough and laborious process that aims to generate a correct collection of information and actions as well as adequate staff training. Schooling operators has always been costly; therefore, developing an application will facilitate learning the necessary skills. The time until an operator will become productive will be significantly shorter and the exposure to certain risks will also be removed. Learning process can be monitorized for each operator, keeping track of his progress. This allows to estimate completion time of the training and to express an overview on future work activities. At the same time, the operator will acquire skills faster, which normally require long practice and a high level of dexterity. Thus, the authors' proposal is to develop an application for the operators training, within the manufacturing lines, aiming to experiment, in a virtual environment the simulation and the orderly assembly of objects as a stack form. Also, it will be necessary to develop a glove prototype that will have the ability to manipulate and control objects in a virtual environment. The end of this paper will reveal reasons for investing and implementing a new way of teaching, making use of such an application.

This paper proposes an end-to-end approach to automatic speech assessment for people with aphasia. Using feature extraction and task analysis, the proposed method trains neural networks to recognize patterns in speech data, including the Mel frequency cepstral coefficient. The system is evaluated on several databases, with promising results indicating its potential for use in clinical settings. The end-to-end approach allows for a streamlined process for evaluating speech, providing a more objective measure of progress and potentially improving outcomes for individuals with aphasia.

The purpose of this paper is to apply the finite element method (FEM) computation results to examine the flow field obstruction in nasal airway obstruction (NAO) patients, the consistency of the blocking site, and the elucidating the NAO phenomenon. In addition, the comparison between flow pattern of NAO patients and the healthy subject during a respiratory cycle was discussed in this article. The results of this research aimed to help optimize the treatment of NAO patients regarding the positioning and size of the surgical dissection.

Betawi Traditional Food Image Detection is a significant task in the field of computer vision. In this paper, the ResNet and DenseNet architectures are employed for training and testing purposes. Deep learning algorithms such as ResNet and DenseNet have shown promising results in image classification tasks. The proposed system's shape analysis focuses on detecting the geometric structures of traditional Betawi dishes. Computer architecture design plays a vital role in achieving high performance and accuracy in image detection, and thus, it is taken into consideration. Task analysis is employed to improve the classification performance by identifying and modeling the fine-grained differences between different categories of traditional Betawi dishes. Entropy analysis is also utilized to measure the system's performance in capturing the underlying features of different food items. The proposed system's outcomes indicate that ResNet and DenseNet models can effectively detect traditional Betawi dishes with high accuracy and performance. The findings of this research may have potential applications in the food industry, particularly in the automation of traditional food preparation and enhancing food quality control.

This paper proposes an RNN-LSTM based flavor recommender framework in hybrid cloud. Cloud computing and engines are employed to enhance the overall performance of the framework. Time series analysis and measurement are utilized to collect data and optimize the prediction algorithms. The history of flavor preferences is taken into account to improve the accuracy of recommendations. Recurrent neural networks are used as the core machine learning tool to train the framework and generate predictions. The proposed framework shows promising results in flavor recommendation accuracy and speed, demonstrating the potential of utilizing cloud computing and advanced prediction algorithms for food recommendation systems. Further research can explore the integration of more data sources and the implementation of real-time data processing to enhance the performance of the framework.

Over the past few decades, LBP descriptor, which shown its high robustness in extracting discriminative features from an image, has been successfully applied in diverse challenging computer vision applications including face recognition. The efficiency and usability of the LBP operator and its success in various real world applications has inspired the development of much new powerful LBP variants. Indeed, after the appearance of the LBP operator, several renowned extensions and modifications of LBP have been proposed in the literature to the point that it can be difficult to recognize their respective LBP-related strategies, strengths and weaknesses according to a given application, and there is a need for a complete comparative study in face recognition application. This paper reviews the performance of 30 recent state-of-the-art handcrafted descriptors in face recognition through a comprehensive experimental study using widely used benchmarks. Simulated experiments on ORL, Extended Yale B and FERET databases proved that some evaluated descriptors realize good classification results which outperform many recent state-of-the-art face recognition systems.

In large scale mobile ad hoc networks, hierarchical routing by clustering of nodes is effective to reduce the load of routing. Since mobile ad hoc networks is autonomously structured, clustering must be realized in an autonomous manner. In our previous study, we have proposed an autonomous clustering technology, and have shown that stable clustering can be realized even in an environment where nodes move randomly. However, the number of nodes included in a cluster may tend to increase when user density increases like congestion in commuting hours around a train station. In this paper, by autonomously generating cluster-head nodes, we propose an autonomous clustering method. The proposed clustering can give stable cluster size that is adaptive even to dynamic environments where user density changes.

This paper presents position-specific statistics of 60 GHz vehicular channels during overtaking, with a focus on the use of millimeter wave radar and horn antennas. The Doppler effect and fading channels result in non-stationary and non-Gaussian distributions, which are modeled using a generalized function. The resulting statistics are compared to idealized models, such as the Saleh-Valenzuela model. Vehicular ad hoc networks rely on low latency communication, thus the paper analyzes the average and tail delays of the channels. Results show that the channel is highly dynamic, with quick changes in the channel properties during overtaking. The position-specific statistics provide valuable information for the design and evaluation of vehicular communication systems, especially those that utilize millimeter wave radar and horn antennas.

In this paper, we propose a novel semantic segmentation-based stereo reconstruction method that can keep up with the accuracy of the state-of-the art approaches while running in real time. The solution follows the classic stereo pipeline, each step in the stereo workflow being enhanced by additional information from semantic segmentation. Therefore, we introduce several improvements to computation, aggregation, and optimization by adapting existing techniques to integrate additional surface information given by each semantic class. For the cost computation and optimization steps, we propose new genetic algorithms that can incrementally adjust the parameters for better solutions. Furthermore, we propose a new post-processing edge-aware filtering technique relying on an improved convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for disparity refinement. We obtain the competitive results at 30 frames/s, including segmentation.

This research paper proposes a voltage-based authentication system for Controller Area Networks (CANs) using reinforcement learning techniques. The system utilizes neural networks and machine learning algorithms to map the CAN network's voltage readings with the authorized controller owners. Testing showed that the proposed system outperformed traditional support vector machine and linear regression authentication methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The study highlights the potential of reinforcement learning-based authentication systems to enhance the security of CANs in computer architecture. The results of this study have the potential to be applied to other similar network systems to improve their security features.

This paper presents the application of indirect adaptive control philosophy for inertia estimation in power systems. A mathematical model is developed to estimate the inertia of the system by making use of phasor measurement units. The proposed estimation method takes into account the power system dynamics and power electronics, allowing for accurate estimation of the system's inertia. The estimated inertia is subsequently used to improve the frequency response of the system, thus enhancing system stability. The proposed methodology is validated using simulation studies, and the results show that the developed method performs well and meets existing industry standards. Overall, this paper demonstrates the efficacy of using indirect adaptive control philosophy for accurate and efficient determination of system inertia in power systems.

Optical Character Recognition (OCR) of Arabic text from manuscripts images is virtually impossible, this is due to the semi-cursive nature of Arabic script which is very difficult to explore by algorithms and image processing methods.In this paper, we present a method of exploration and research in content of Arabic manuscript images. It's about characterizing segmented handwritten words with a set points of interest by providing a means of identification and research in these manuscripts. Each word segmented and described by key features will be compared to query words.The results of this method are encouraging in comparison with other methods, especially when it comes to the same of handwritten style used in the text.

This paper describes the development of an automated system for detecting needle puncture in a simulated cannulation task using computer vision technology. The system uses cameras to capture images of the procedure in real-time, and image edge detection algorithms to analyze the images and identify the location of the needle tip. The system has been trained using a dataset of images of successful and unsuccessful puncture attempts, and achieved high accuracy in detecting successful punctures. The system has potential applications in medical training and assessment, and can improve the safety and effectiveness of the cannulation procedure. The study also investigates the effect of blood on the accuracy of the detection system and finds that electron tubes can be used to improve the quality of images in the presence of blood. Overall, the study provides a promising approach for automatic detection of needle puncture in medical procedures.

In this paper, we propose a Learning Orientation-Estimation Convolutional Neural Network (LO-Net) for building detection in optical remote sensing images. Buildings are an important feature in remote sensing image analysis, and their detection is essential for various applications. Feature extraction plays a crucial role in building detection, and the proposed LO-Net leverages orientation estimation to improve feature extraction. The LO-Net is trained using optical imaging data and is designed to handle various types of optical sensors. We also perform a task analysis to evaluate the performance of the LO-Net on building detection. The results show that the proposed approach outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in building detection accuracy. Additionally, we implement the LO-Net using Graphics Processing Units (GPU) for efficient processing. The proposed LO-Net is a promising approach for building detection in optical remote sensing images, with potential applications in urban planning, disaster management, and environmental monitoring.

This paper presents a study on the electromagnetic response of a two-dimensional array of conducting strips that are inter-connected with columns of silver-coated micron-sized particles. The dielectrics, strips, magnetic cores, cavity resonators, conductors, and computational modeling were employed in this research to investigate the behavior of the conducting strips array. The results show that the magnetic resonance of the array is highly sensitive to the geometry of the system, which can be adjusted to optimize the electromagnetic response. Moreover, the findings demonstrate that the silver-coated micron-sized particles enhance the coupling between the conducting strips, leading to improved performance. Overall, this study provides insight into the behavior of two-dimensional arrays of conducting strips and can be useful for the development of novel electromagnetic devices.

Mental workload (MW) assessment is important for numerous mentally-demanding applications, including first responders, air traffic control, amongst others, as it quantifies the cognitive capabilities of the operator. Recently, there has been a push for wearables based MW monitoring for real-time feedback and human performance augmentation. Most previous studies have focused on immobile subjects. Realistic applications, however, rely on ambulant users under varying types and levels of physical activity. Movement artifacts are known to hamper the quality of signals measured by wearable devices, thus the impact on MW assessment in situ is still unknown. In this study, we compare the performance of several automated artifact removal algorithms for electroencephalograms (EEG), as well as the robustness of two classical feature sets, for MW assessment under varying physical activity levels.

This study proposes a method for improving the accuracy of seizure prediction using deep neural networks (DNNs) incorporating hand-crafted features. Specifically, the authors compared the performance of models built using only raw eeg signals and those incorporating hand-crafted features, such as spectral and frequency band features. Results showed that the incorporation of hand-crafted features improved the performance of the DNN models, achieving higher accuracy and recall rates. Additionally, the study conducted a correlation analysis between the hand-crafted features and epileptic seizures, demonstrating the biological relevance of the selected features. Overall, this research highlights the importance of feature engineering in enhancing the predictive ability of DNNs for seizure prediction, which may ultimately lead to improved diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy.

Mobile robots have become an important research topic due to their various applications in different fields such as manufacturing, defense, and exploration. The movement of mobile robots is crucial to their functioning, and it is essential that they are stable to perform their tasks efficiently, especially when manipulating objects. This paper presents a mathematical model for stabilizing the movement of mobile robots and manipulators using neural networks. The neural networks have been trained using libraries of neurons to predict the movements of the robot and manipulate its stability. The proposed model has been implemented and tested successfully on different mobile robots, and the results show that it efficiently stabilizes their movement. This research contributes to the field of mobile robotics by providing a stable and efficient model for controlling the movement of mobile robots and manipulators, which can be further developed for future applications.

In recent years, there has been growing interest in valence and arousal estimation in-the-wild, which involves predicting the emotional state of individuals in naturalistic settings. One approach to achieving accurate estimations is through the use of tensor methods. These methods rely on multi-dimensional arrays, or tensors, to represent the relationship between features, task analysis, and computational modeling for data models. Feature extraction is a critical component of tensor methods, as it involves distilling relevant information from the raw data. Matrix decomposition is another key aspect of tensor methods, which involve breaking down the tensor into smaller components for more efficient processing. By combining these techniques, researchers have developed robust models for valence and arousal estimation in-the-wild, which have potential applications in fields like mental health, marketing, and human-computer interaction. Overall, further research into the use of tensor methods for valence and arousal estimation in-the-wild is important for advancing our understanding of human emotion and developing valuable tools for various industries.

This paper proposes a robust compressive sensing method for multiband spectrum analysis with partial and incorrect priors. The proposed method utilizes sensors and databases to estimate and improve the accuracy of the prior information. Additionally, the proposed method employs matching pursuit algorithms and Fourier transforms to reconstruct the multiband spectrum efficiently. A mathematical model is presented to demonstrate the proposed approach, which is capable of operating with limited bandwidth and inaccurate priors. Overall, the results show that the proposed compressive sensing method is effective in reconstructing multiband spectra, even in the presence of partial and incorrect priors.

Iteratively Reweighted Midpoint Method for Fast Multiple View Triangulation is a mathematical approach for estimating the three-dimensional position of an object from images taken by multiple cameras. The method utilizes a cost function to minimize the errors in the triangulated points. The weight measurement is iteratively reweighted to improve the accuracy of the estimated points. The mathematical model is designed to address the simultaneous localization and mapping problem, where the cameras and the object move in an unknown environment. The proposed method is computationally efficient and provides fast triangulation results. The research highlights the importance of using multiple views for accurate 3D display estimation and proposes a fast and effective solution.

This paper proposes an artificial neural network (ANN) technique, using an adaptive batch training rule-based principle with weight and bias, to estimate and predict the adaptive threshold-based detection of the received molecular signals based on the current cumulative concentrations. The proposed technique considers a single transmitter (Tx Bio-NM) and a single receiver (Rx Bio-NM) biological nanomachines to exchange the molecular packets through diffusion-based molecular communication (DMC) channel. This scheme is suitable for binary On-OFF keying (BOOK signaling); where the Rx Bio-NM adapts the 1/0-bit detection threshold based on all previous received bits to alleviate the inter-symbol interference (ISI) problem and reception noise. We evaluate the proposed technique in term of the bit error rate (BER), complexity cost and molecular throughput. The performance evaluation in various noisy channel sources shows a promising improvement in the un-coded BER and a slight number of molecules in transmission can be achieved extremely massive throughput of the DMC system compared to the other threshold detection schemes in the literature.

Building automation is increasingly used to minimize energy consumption and increasing comfort and flexibility in buildings. When the KNX Association was founded in 1999 the need for security was quite low. Systems were usually not connected to the internet and so the standard lacks of nowadays common security requirements. To get an idea where the most serious problems are located in installations we present in this paper a method to calculate a risk for the different network segments. Without limiting the generality KNX is used as one example of fieldbuses. The basic concepts in the communication of fieldbus devices are present in KNX and the results can easily be transferred to other fieldbus protocols.

With the rapid development of social network services and the explosion of big data, the study of community detection has attracted increasing attention. In this paper, an incremental community detection method has been proposed, which utilizes both machine learning algorithms and heuristic algorithms to identify communities in social big data. Moreover, this method incorporates image edge detection techniques to improve the accuracy of community detection. Additionally, this method is also applicable in the Internet of Things and telecommunications fields, which broadens its usage in different domains. The experimental results have shown that the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both efficiency and effectiveness in community detection.

This paper proposes a YOLO-based system for valve type recognition and localization, aimed at enhancing the capabilities of robots in industrial environments. The system is trained on a dataset of valve images, and uses object detection techniques to locate valves in real-time systems. With the ability to recognize valves, robots can perform tasks such as turning or replacing them, while also avoiding collisions with other objects. Additionally, the real-time capabilities of the system allow for streaming media and quick responsiveness, making it a valuable tool for various industrial applications.

Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is a non-invasive technique used to monitor the heart rate of an individual from a distance using a camera. However, the accuracy of rPPG can be affected by luminance variations in the environment. In this paper, we propose a neural network-based approach for luminance variation resistant driver's heart rate monitoring using rPPG. The proposed system consists of two main parts: skin segmentation and heart rate estimation. Firstly, skin segmentation is performed using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract the region of interest from the face. Then, the heart rate is estimated using a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). The proposed system was evaluated on a dataset of 15 participants while driving a vehicle in different lighting conditions. The results showed that the proposed system outperformed traditional methods and achieved superior performance in terms of heart rate estimation accuracy. The proposed system has potential applications in the field of road safety by providing a non-invasive method for monitoring the driver's heart rate, which can be used as an indicator of driver's stress level and fatigue.

Clap-clap switches find applications in various domains such as automation and security. A clap sound can be used as a triggering signal either to switch the relays on/off, or as an alert signal for security system. However, the sound is very directive and sensitive to noise floor. Also, being an impulse, it is difficult to distinguish between a clap and other similar impulsive sounds like bang, dog-barking, coughing, etc. We propose a device for detecting clap sound which can also distinguish it from other impulsive sounds. We have used band-pass filtering in frequency domain and correlation in time domain to effectively detect and distinguish clap sound from other sounds.

E-commerce is a business activity that uses modern information technology to process cash flow and logistics to achieve transactions. Under the e-commerce environment, an item can reach to the customer accurately is a key factor to enhance the company's image. Therefore, how to efficiently select the algorithm to solve the vehicle routing problem is an urgent problem to be solved. Aiming at the problems existing in the logistics distribution of e-commerce, this paper combines the genetic algorithm with the conservation algorithm based on the maximum travelable distance of the vehicle, and uses the conservation algorithm to generate the initial solution of the genetic algorithm, and constructs the conservation genetic algorithm to solve the e-commerce environment logistics distribution path optimization problem. The simulation results show that the conservation genetic algorithm is more globally optimal than the genetic algorithm.

The visual fidelity of bleeding simulation in a surgical simulator is critical since it will affect not only the degree of visual realism, but also the user's medical judgment and treatment in real-life settings. The conventional marching cubes surface rendering algorithm provides excellent visual effect in rendering gushing blood, however, it is insufficient for blood flow, which is very common in surgical procedures, since in this case the rendered surface and depth textures of blood are rough. In this paper, we propose a new method called the mixed depth rendering for rendering blood flow in surgical simulation. A smooth height field is created to minimize the height difference between neighboring particles on the bleeding surface. The color and transparency of each bleeding area are determined by the number of bleeding particles, which is consistent with the real visual effect. In addition, there is no much extra computational cost. The rendering of blood flow in a variety of surgical scenarios shows that visual feedback is much improved. The proposed mixed depth rendering method is also used in a neurosurgery simulator that we developed.

This paper presents a study on Hegselmann-Krause Dynamics with Limited Connectivity, focusing on the steady-state and convergence of the system. The research is relevant to social network services, as it explores a mathematical model that can be used to analyze data models of social networks. The authors provide an upper bound for the convergence time of the numerical models, which can assist in the development of efficient algorithms for network analysis. The study offers insights into the dynamics of social networks and the interconnectedness of their agents. Overall, the research presented in this paper will be useful in analyzing and understanding the behavior of social systems.

This paper proposes a novel multi-attribute decision making method based on interval normal type-2 fuzzy numbers. The method employs the Euclidean distance to measure the similarity between interval normal type-2 fuzzy numbers and aggregates the preference information of decision makers to obtain the final ranking of alternatives. The proposed method combines the advantages of interval approach and normal type-2 fuzzy sets, which can handle uncertain and imprecise information more effectively. Additionally, the computational modeling of the proposed method is relatively simple, which is suitable for practical applications in various fields, such as economics, finance and other domains that require decision making based on multiple criteria. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, several indexes are used to compare it with other fuzzy decision making methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a more accurate and reliable decision making approach.

This paper presents a framework for predicting failures in ground tests on aircrafts. The framework incorporates data mining techniques, predictive models, atmospheric modeling, and data models to provide accurate predictions of potential failures in testing. The use of such a framework can greatly benefit aircraft companies by reducing the amount of failed tests and minimizing costs associated with repairs and delays. Through the integration of various data sources and models, this framework offers a comprehensive approach to predicting failures in ground testing that has the potential to improve the safety and efficacy of aircrafts.

This paper proposes an IoT tree health indexing method based on a heterogeneous neural network approach. The method is designed for feature extraction, vegetation indexing, and sensors monitoring. The proposed method uses a combination of sensors and computational modeling to create a holistic understanding of the health of trees. The heterogeneous neural network approach includes multiple layers of processing to capture the complexities and interactions within the ecosystem. The proposed method enabled the development of a comprehensive tree health index that facilitates tree management and ensures early detection of potential threats to vegetation. Overall, the proposed IoT Tree Health Indexing Method demonstrates the potential of utilizing technology to enhance vegetation monitoring and management.

This paper addresses the problem of predicting the success of motion pictures using various machine learning algorithms and comparing their performance. The study focuses on the correlation between the success of movies and factors such as social networking, computational modeling, and prediction algorithms. The machine learning algorithms used in the study are trained and tested on a dataset of previously released movies. Results from the experiment show that machine learning algorithms are effective in predicting the success of movies. Furthermore, the performance of different machine learning algorithms is compared in terms of their accuracy, precision, and recall. Overall, the study provides insight into the potential of machine learning algorithms for predicting the success of motion pictures and highlights the importance of choosing the most suitable algorithm for a given problem.

This paper proposes the design of a fuzzy controller for automatic tuning of arc suppression coils. The controller uses fuzzy reasoning and fuzzy logic to adjust the tuning of the coils based on data from current measurement. The concept of cognition is also applied, allowing the controller to learn and adapt to changes in the system. The proposed fuzzy control system was tested against existing standards and proved to be effective in maintaining stable performance of the arc suppression coils. The use of fuzzy logic and reasoning allows for a more flexible and adaptable system that can respond to changing conditions in a more intelligent manner. Overall, the design of a fuzzy controller for arc suppression coil automatic tuning offers significant advantages over traditional control methods, providing a more reliable and efficient system.

According to current energy efficiency labels, the majority of light-emitting diode (LED) lamps on the market are considered as highly efficient devices. This makes it difficult to distinguish between lamps with different operational characteristics and performance. This paper introduces a comprehensive experimental-based labeling methodology for comparing LED lamp performance with reference to two additional important characteristics: light flicker and power factor. The new labeling methodology reveals that there is high diversity between different LED lamps with different circuit topologies but also for a given topology with different design choices. General consumers and design engineers can benefit from the simple and clear information presented by the set of comparative labels when comparing LED lamp performance.

Major part of internet users are devices which are connected to each other on the internet and are exchanging data with internet brokers to receive requested services. Managing and accounting well to IoT requests needs maximum processing power, speed in data transfer and proper combining services in minimum time. This many devices in IoT, made solving problems in this area to use abilities and facilities of cloud environment. Hence combining services in cloud environment is paid attention recently. In this research we want to give an algorithm with approach of improving factors propounded in the problem combining service composition problem like number of clouds involved in giving services, number of services studied before fulfilling users requests and load balance between clouds. In this paper we use the factor, similarity measure, to find the most suitable cloud and composition plan in each phase which in addition to improving QoS metrics propounded in previous papers, it caused improving QoS metric of load balancing between clouds, prevention of formation of bottleneck in clouds entrance, decreasing the probability of temporarily failing of any of clouds and consequently increasing the users' satisfaction.

This paper proposes a novel approach to detecting water-risk zones in home video surveillance using color and texture analysis. Specifically, image color analysis is conducted through the computation of histograms of color and brightness, which allows for the identification of areas of interest that could potentially harbor water. Surface texture is also analyzed in order to determine the likelihood of water accumulation on specific surfaces. By combining these features, the proposed method is able to accurately identify and locate water-risk zones in video surveillance footage. The significance of this work lies in its potential application to home security systems and disaster prevention measures, as it provides a reliable and efficient means of detecting and alerting homeowners to potential water damage.

Process controls (basic as well as advanced) are implemented within the process control system, which may mean a distributed control system (DCS), programmable logic controller (PLC), and/or a supervisory control computer. DCSs and PLCs are typically industrially hardened and fault-tolerant. Supervisory control computers are often not hardened or fault-tolerant, but they bring a higher level of computational capability to the control system, to host valuable, but not critical, advanced control applications. Advanced controls may reside in either the DCS or the supervisory computer, depending on the application. Basic controls reside in the DCS and its subsystems, including PLCs. Because we usually deal with real - world systems with real - world constraints (cost, computer resources, size, weight, power, heat dissipation, etc.), it is understood that the simplest method to accomplish a task is the one that should be used. Experts usually rely on common sense when they solve problems. They also use vague and ambiguous terms. Other experts have no difficulties with understanding and interpreting this statement because they have the background to hearing problems described like this. However, a knowledge engineer would have difficulties providing a computer with the same level of understanding. In a complex industrial process, how can we represent expert knowledge that uses vague and fuzzy terms in a computer to control it? In this context, the application is developed to control the pretreatment and pasteurization station of milk localized in Batna (Algeria) by adopting a control approach based on expert knowledge and fuzzy logic.

Time-Step method and Station-Pair method are prominent techniques for estimation of spatial gradients. Since GBAS is meant to serve a limited area of about 50km of an airport for aircraft Precision Approach and landing, these two methods were considered for gradient estimation within the GBAS service area. Much of the work on these techniques has been reported for GPS-based GBAS applications. In this paper, the suitability of these methods to IRNSS-based GBAS applications is investigated. It is observed that since IRNSS satellites are either GEO or GSO, the time interval (At), of Time-Step method should be significantly high (30min for GSO), to obtain gradient data for GBAS' service area. With the Station-Pair method, a dense network of stations, each separated by not more than 1-2 kms is required.

In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly popular for various applications that require aerial observation. One such application is moving object detection, which involves analyzing the trajectories of objects in motion. In this paper, we propose a UAV-based approach to moving object detection using sliding-window trajectory analysis. This approach involves capturing image sequences of the scene of interest using cameras mounted on a UAV, and then using computer vision techniques for feature extraction and motion segmentation. By analyzing the trajectories of objects in the scene over time, we are able to accurately detect moving objects and track their movements. Our approach has demonstrated promising results in experiments conducted on real-world datasets. These results suggest that the proposed UAV-based method has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of moving object detection in a variety of applications.

The article titled "What is Informatics Education Students' Impression of Using Metacognitive Training System at The First Time?" aims to explore the opinions and experiences of students in the field of informatics with regards to using a metacognitive training system for the first time. The study focuses on the use of specific tools and media in training, testing and measuring the usability of the system. The results gathered from the study indicate that the use of such metacognitive training systems in informatics education is beneficial for improving knowledge retention and overall understanding of the subject matter. In addition, the article explores the importance of understanding the usability of such systems in order to make improvements and adjustments to better support learning outcomes. Overall, the article sheds light on the significance of incorporating metacognition training into the informatics curriculum to enhance the learning experience for students.

Machine learning (ML)-based traffic classification has been gaining increasing importance due to the declining port-based and payload-based approaches. However, the packet-level method is the most common measure used in the previous works, which requires additional hardware device to manage and monitor, increasing cost as well as extra works of the network personnel. In this paper, we propose a methodology to build an efficient classifier from NetFlow which is the widely applied monitoring solution among network operators in the form of flow-level. First, we analyze the per-application performance through the C4.5 decision tree with the features derived from the NetFlow records. The result shows that the accuracy obtained is as good as the packet-level method. We further propose the ensemble feature selection (FS) method to improve the classification accuracy and to reduce the computational complexity. Lastly, we present the clustering-based under-sampling combining with synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) approach to solving the problem of the concept drift and the imbalanced dataset, and we extract insights and recommendation for practical application. With the combination of proposed methods, the experiment result reports high F-measure over two traces containing the wide range of applications with low computational complexity.

With the widespread application of deep learning systems, the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) is received increasing attentions recently. By studying the distribution of neurons outputs in DNN models, we found that the behavior patterns of neurons are different for different kinds of DNNs' inputs, e.g. test cases generated by different adversarial attack techniques. In this paper, we extract the neuron behavior patterns of DNNs under different adversarial attack techniques, use them as the guidance for test case selection. Experimental results show that this method is more efficient than random technology.

This paper introduces a chattering-free, adaptive, and robust tracking control scheme for a class of second-order nonlinear systems with uncertain dynamics. First, a proportional-integral-derivative control-fast terminal sliding function is proposed to enable the advantages of both the PID and non-singular fast terminal sliding mode approaches in the field of non-singularity, fast convergence time, defined time convergence, and stability with small steady-state errors. Second, to obtain the desired control target without chattering behavior, the proposed controller with a continuous approach has been applied. In detail, the proposed controller uses an integral of a switching term and an adaptive updating law to compensate the lumped system uncertainty (e.g., disturbances, unmodeled dynamics, nonlinearities, or unmeasurable noise). Our proposed controller does not require knowledge about bound values of those anonymous components. The robust behavior and the defined time convergence have been demonstrated rigorously by the Lyapunov principle. Finally, the position tracking computer simulations have been performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the suggested controller.

This paper delves into the application of opinion mining and data mining techniques to effectively analyze the cryptocurrency market. Specifically, the study focuses on the use of these techniques in relation to Bitcoin, considering its increasing popularity and significance in the world of finance. The study employs predictive models and data models to collect and analyze data from Twitter. Data mining techniques, together with proper training and analysis, are used to derive meaningful insights and trends from the data, allowing for the prediction of future market movements. Through this study, we aim to contribute to the effective use of data mining and opinion mining techniques in enhancing market analysis of cryptocurrencies, specifically Bitcoin.

A novel technique to recognize full range of shapes of Arabic handwritten characters is presented. This is done by combining statistical and structural approaches for character recognition. The statistical method first recognizes the main body of a character using modified direction features and Support Vector Machines. Then in structural classification, dot-descriptors are used to recognize the exact shape of an Arabic character. On IfN/ENIT benchmarking database, we achieved 96.71% accuracy for character main-bodies and 94.52% accuracy on the complete characters. Our results compare favorably with the state of the art.

This paper proposes a design and implementation of a virtual service system for electric vehicle time-sharing rental utilizing multi-agent technology. The system aims to provide a more efficient and convenient rental service for electric vehicles. The study focuses on developing data models, load modeling, predictive models, analytical models, and computational modeling to optimize the performance and utilization of the system. Additionally, the study pays attention to battery management, as the battery is a significant factor in the efficiency and lifespan of electric vehicles. The proposed system integrates various technologies to ensure the effective operation of the electric vehicle time-sharing rental service. The system can also collect data on vehicle usage, further supporting the development of electric vehicle market analysis in the long term. Overall, the virtual service system proposed in this study can contribute to the widespread adoption of electric vehicles and the development of the electric vehicle industry.

This paper proposes a new approach to estimate guaranteed performance for multicore processing in the early design stage of aerospace electronics. The study focuses on timing and benchmark testing in order to generate accurate performance estimates for both software and hardware. The authors also explore the use of data mining techniques to improve the accuracy of their estimates. The proposed methodology addresses the unique challenges of designing for the space domain and aims to provide valuable insights for engineers and designers in this field. Overall, this paper highlights the importance of early analysis and estimation in the design of multicore systems for aerospace electronics.

Electronic devices have been dabbled into houses to perform automatic tasks and fulfill different needs such as illumination, cooking, air conditioning, surveillance, among others. Furthermore, those elements can collect data from the environment in order to be processed and give better products and services, so, Internet of Things capabilities arises to home, highly cohesive with domotics. However, for developing countries, smart appliances are expensive, and old fridges, washing machines, etc., are still operative, so they must not to be discarded. Other very used appliances are stoves, which work with heating methods like electrical resistances, electrical induction or natural gas. The last one is the most used in a plenty of countries, due to its advantages regarding cost, for instance. Nonetheless, bad manipulation can cause gas leakages, and furthermore, injuries to people and conflagrations, affecting human lives and assets. Thus, a need has been identified regarding gas safety of gas stoves, conserving the installed base. This work shows the results of the main research and design considerations of a new cutting-edge technology that protects people of bad manipulation of already installed or new gas stoves, including the Internet of Things in order to monitor in real-time possible gas leakages and take actions.

In this paper, we propose a deep residual learning approach for automatic modulation classification under non-Gaussian noise. We specifically consider two types of modulations, frequency modulation and binary phase shift keying. The proposed approach includes feature extraction and classification parts. In the feature extraction part, we utilize a residual network with convolutional and pooling layers to learn high-level features from the input signals. In the classification part, we use a neural network with kernel-based methods to classify the modulations. The experiments show that our approach achieves high accuracy even under high levels of Gaussian noise. Our proposed method can be applied in many practical scenarios, such as military communication systems and wireless sensor networks.

This paper discusses an approach for full-text search of files in MongoDB-based systems. The approach focuses on application programming interfaces (APIs), cloud computing, text analysis, relational databases, and search engines. The authors propose a solution that leverages MongoDB's features to index and search file contents efficiently. The solution includes an API that enables developers to integrate full-text search capabilities seamlessly. Cloud-based deployment ensures scalability and accessibility, while text analysis algorithms enhance search accuracy. The proposed system stores both metadata and file contents in MongoDB, allowing for flexible querying and retrieval. By utilizing MongoDB's document model and search engine capabilities, the proposed approach demonstrates efficient and scalable full-text search for large files in modern distributed systems.

Clustering algorithms are commonly used in data analysis to group similar data points together. A significant issue with clustering methods is that they are susceptible to noisy or mislabeled points, leading to inaccurate cluster assignments. In this paper, we propose an Adaptive Density Peaks Clustering Method (ADPCM) with Fisher Linear Discriminant, which can handle these difficulties. Our method calculates the density and position of data points using a kernel approximation for the density function, and estimates the noise level using the entropy of the data. Additionally, we introduce Fisher Linear Discriminant to improve the clustering quality by considering the correlation between features. The performance of our algorithm is evaluated using several datasets, and the results are compared to other clustering methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing algorithms, especially when dealing with high-dimensional and noisy data. The proposed method is suitable for use in various applications, such as image processing, sensor network analysis, and financial data analysis.

Mist computing puts computing on the very edge of the network. With mist computing, the computation is performed in users' devices (smartphones, laptops, etc.) sensors or wearables (something fairly common in the context of the Internet of Things). Devices which are near may be part of a mist where each of these devices contributes to computation tasks. Each of them has computation capabilities which can be used in order to run tasks from other devices. However, devices in the network must be aware of available features in order to execute tasks within a device with the necessary hardware requirements. There is a compatibility problem between tasks and devices: not all devices satisfy all tasks needs. This article proposes a mist computing framework in order to tackle this compatibility problem.

In the field of turbulence engineering, the detection and visualization of splat and antisplat events have always been critical research topics. This paper proposes a feature extraction approach for identifying these events and visualizing them using advanced data visualization techniques. The proposed methodology combines stress, heat transfer, strain, and solids data to extract meaningful features that can be used to identify splat and antisplat events. The study further shows that the proposed data visualization method is capable of effectively presenting complex flow characteristics and identifying the key features of splat and antisplat events. The findings of this research have important implications for the development of more efficient and accurate prediction models in the field of turbulence engineering.

This paper proposes a trust-based access control scheme for e-Health cloud that provides secure and reliable access control for medical services. The scheme utilizes cloud computing technology for storage and processing of medical data and measurement results, as well as sensors for monitoring patients' health status. The access control mechanism is designed based on trust levels for different entities, including patients, medical personnel, and cloud service providers. The proposed scheme also includes monitoring mechanisms to detect and respond to any unauthorized access attempts. The effectiveness of the scheme is demonstrated through simulation experiments. This trust-based access control scheme offers a secure and efficient way to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of medical data, while facilitating the delivery of high-quality medical services to patients.

As the next generation of the power system, smart grid develops towards automated and intellectualized. Along with the benefits brought by smart grids, e.g., improved energy conversion rate, power utilization rate, and power supply quality, are the security challenges. One of the most important issues in smart grids is to ensure reliable communication between the secondary equipment. The state-of-art method to ensure smart grid security is to detect cyber attacks by deep learning. However, due to the small number of negative samples, the performance of the detection system is limited. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that utilizes the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate abundant negative samples, which helps to improve the performance of the state-of-art detection system. The evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the performance of the detection system by 4%.

In recent years, social networking has grown to be an increasingly popular means of communication between individuals. As a result, there has been a growing interest in the study of social networks and their mathematical models. One approach to modeling these networks is through computational modeling using data mining techniques. Through the use of information technology, researchers can optimize their models to effectively maximize the influence within a given social network. However, such optimization requires careful consideration of the time complexity involved in generating accurate models. In this paper, we explore the influence maximization problem approach to model social networks, and investigate how mathematical models and computational modeling techniques can be used to improve the effectiveness of data mining and optimization in social networking. Additionally, we consider the challenges and potential pitfalls of using these techniques, particularly in terms of time complexity and scalability.

As aspects of our daily lives become more interconnected with the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), it is imperative that our devices are reliable and secure from threats. Vulnerabilities of Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA/WPA2) have been exposed in the past, motivating the use of multiple security techniques, even with the release of WPA3. Physical layer security leverages existing components of communication systems to enable methods of protecting devices that are well-suited for IoT applications. In this work, we provide a low-complexity technique for generating secret keys at the Physical layer to enable improved IoT security. We leverage the existing carrier frequency offset (CFO) and channel estimation components of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) receivers for an efficient approach. The key generation algorithm we propose focuses on the unique CFO and channel experienced between a pair of desired nodes, and to the best of our understanding, the combination of the features has not been examined previously for the purpose of secret key generation. Our techniques are appropriate for IoT devices, as they do not require extensive processing capabilities and are based on second order statistics. We obtain experimental results using USRP N210 software defined radios and analyze the performance of our methods in post-processing. Our techniques improve the capability of desired nodes to establish matching secret keys, while hindering the threat of an eavesdropper, and are useful for protecting future IoT devices.

This paper proposes a distributed control architecture for cascaded H-bridge converter systems. The focus of this architecture is on voltage control, while also considering the importance of communication networks and decentralized control. The proposed consensus algorithm is used to regulate voltage across each module, allowing for a more reliable and flexible system. The chosen topology of the cascaded H-bridge converter also contributes to its effectiveness in voltage control. In addition, the bandwidth of the communication network is analyzed and optimized to improve the efficiency of the system. Overall, this paper presents a comprehensive approach to the design of a distributed control architecture for cascaded H-bridge converter, which can improve the performance and reliability in voltage regulation.

This paper proposes a nonlinear subdomain and magnetic circuit hybrid model for open-circuit field prediction in surface-mounted permanent magnet machines. The proposed model can accurately predict iron loss and magnetic flux distribution, and is suitable for atmospheric modeling and integrated circuit modeling. Computational modeling is utilized to verify the accuracy of the proposed model. It is demonstrated that the proposed model is able to accurately predict magnetic fields and analytically model the behavior of these machines. The model extends the traditional magnetic circuit model by incorporating the nonlinearity of the magnetic material, and provides a more comprehensive and accurate prediction of the behavior of Surface-Mounted PM Machines. The proposed model can be used in the design of these machines to optimize their performance and reduce their environmental impact.

This study aims to explore the electromyographic (EMG) indices of muscle fatigue experienced by a chronic stroke patient with severe paralysis during upper limb motor rehabilitation. Throughout the training sessions, the muscle fatigue levels of the patient were measured using EMG signals from several muscles in the upper limb region. Time-frequency analysis was applied to the EMG data to obtain indexes related to muscle fatigue, such as median frequency and slope. The results show that severe paralysis did not prevent the occurrence of muscle fatigue during the training sessions, and the EMG indexes related to muscle fatigue were successfully obtained. These findings suggest that EMG can be a useful tool to measure muscle fatigue in severely paralyzed stroke patients undergoing rehabilitation, and may aid in the optimization of training protocols to ensure effective rehabilitation outcomes.

The health status of core router systems needs to be analyzed efficiently in order to ensure high reliability and timely error recovery. Although a large amount operational data is collected from core routers, due to high computational complexity and expensive labor cost, only a small part of this data is labeled by experts. The lack of labels is an impediment toward the adoption of supervised learning. We present an iterative self-learning procedure for assessing the health status of a core router. This procedure first computes a representative feature matrix to capture different characteristics of time-series data. Not only statistical-modeling-based features are computed from three general categories but also a recurrent neural network-based autoencoder is utilized to capture a wider range of hidden patterns. Moreover, both minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance (mRMR) method and fully connected feedforward autoencoder are applied to further reduce dimensionality of extracted feature matrix. Hierarchical clustering is then utilized to infer labels for the unlabeled dataset. Finally, a classifier is built and iteratively updated using both labeled and unlabeled dataset. Field data collected from a set of commercial core routers are used to experimentally validate the proposed health-status analyzer. The experimental results show that the proposed feature-based self-learning health analyzer achieves higher precision and recall than the traditional supervised health analyzer as well the currently deployed rule-based health analyzer. Moreover, it achieves better performance than the three anomaly detection baseline methods under the transformed binary classification scenario.

In this research paper, we analyzed what moments and activities make people happy, based on a collection of happy moments. We are focusing on specific happy moments from a collection of text responses that people have shared through the crowd-sourcing platform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk). Using crowd-sourcing to collect our data allows us to advance our understanding of the cause of happiness, by focusing on words and real human experiences. Workers of MTurk were asked to reflect on what makes them happy in a given period and share three specific moments in complete sentences. Through text-based analysis, we will look to see what other components have a role in making a specific event happy and further analyze how we can classify such words. Also, we dive deeper into specific subcategories of classifiers in an attempt to form insights about their happiness level based on specific factors. With the goal to extract features from the text in HappyDB, in this study we used the bag of words approach. Through doing so, our results were successful at predicting the happiness category, concerning both accuracy and context. Our models were able to accomplish the goal of understanding a happy moment and fit such a moment into one of the seven ground truth happiness categories we set at the beginning of this study. We finished the article with the ethical perspective of such research works and related social implications.

This paper presents a demonstration of an observability framework for cloud native microservices. Observability has become a critical aspect of modern software development, with monitoring tools becoming more sophisticated to handle the complexity of cloud computing architectures. The framework showcases how the combination of measurement tools and software architecture can provide enhanced observability in cloud computing environments. The paper outlines the challenges faced by developers in monitoring highly distributed microservices architectures, and how the proposed framework can address these issues. The framework utilizes key observability metrics, such as request latency and error rates, to provide a holistic view of the system's behavior. The demonstration highlights the importance of measuring these metrics and analyzing the data generated to enhance overall software performance. The paper concludes by discussing the potential impact this framework could have on the development of cloud computing systems in the future.

This paper proposes a Naive Bayes multi-label classification approach for high-voltage condition monitoring. The approach is based on the analysis of several key factors including electromagnetic interference, partial discharges, feature extraction, discharges, fault location and measurement. In particular, the paper presents a novel method for feature extraction that enables the classification of high-voltage conditions with high accuracy. The proposed approach is able to effectively detect and classify faults in high-voltage systems, enabling early fault detection and preventive maintenance. Additionally, the approach demonstrates excellent performance in situations where multiple faults may occur simultaneously, making it a valuable tool in high-voltage condition monitoring applications. Overall, the proposed approach represents a significant contribution to the field of high-voltage condition monitoring, and has the potential to improve the reliability and safety of high-voltage systems.

Intelligent Virtual Agents (IVAs) are becoming part of our everyday life, thanks to artificial intelligence technology and Internet of Things devices. For example, users can control their connected home appliances through natural voice commands to the IVA. However, most current-state commercial IVAs, such as Amazon Alexa, mainly focus on voice commands and voice feedback, and lack the ability to provide non-verbal cues which are an important part of social interaction. Augmented Reality (AR) has the potential to overcome this challenge by providing a visual embodiment of the IVA. In this paper we investigate how visual embodiment and social behaviors influence the perception of the IVA. We hypothesize that a user's confidence in an IVA's ability to perform tasks is improved when imbuing the agent with a human body and social behaviors compared to the agent solely depending on voice feedback. In other words, an agent's embodied gesture and locomotion behavior exhibiting awareness of the surrounding real world or exerting influence over the environment can improve the perceived social presence with and confidence in the agent. We present a human-subject study, in which we evaluated the hypothesis and compared different forms of IVAs with speech, gesturing, and locomotion behaviors in an interactive AR scenario. The results show support for the hypothesis with measures of confidence, trust, and social presence. We discuss implications for future developments in the field of IVAs.

In this paper, we present an I/O efficient distributed approximation framework to support approximations on arbitrary sub-datasets of a large dataset. Due to the prohibitive storage overhead of caching offline samples for each sub-dataset, existing offline sample-based systems provide high accuracy results for only a limited number of sub-datasets, such as the popular ones. On the other hand, current online sample-based approximation systems, which generate samples at runtime, do not take into account the uneven storage distribution of a sub-dataset. They work well for uniform distribution of a sub-dataset while suffer low I/O efficiency and poor estimation accuracy on unevenly distributed sub-datasets. To address the problem, we develop a distribution aware method called CLAP (cluster sampling based approximation). Our idea is to collect the occurrences of a sub-dataset at each logical partition of a dataset (storage distribution) in the distributed system, and make good use of such information to enable I/O efficient online sampling. There are three thrusts in CLAP. First, we develop a probabilistic map to reduce the exponential number of recorded sub-datasets to a linear one. Second, we apply the cluster sampling with unequal probability theory to implement a distribution-aware method for efficient online sampling for a single or multiple sub-datasets. Third, we enrich CLAP support with more complex approximations such as ratio and regression using bootstrap based estimation beyond the simple aggragation approxiamtions. Forth, we add an option in CLAP to allow users specifying a target error bound when submitting an approximation job. Fifth, we quantitatively derive the optimal sampling unit size in a distributed file system by associating it with approximation costs and accuracy. We have implemented CLAP into Hadoop as an example system and open sourced it on GitHub. Our comprehensive experimental results show that CLAP can achieve a speedup by up to 20× over the precise execution.

This paper presents a novel approach to robotic grasping estimation by combining evolutionary algorithms with deep neural networks. The focus is on developing inference algorithms to accurately predict the optimal grasp for a given object based on its shape and other features. To achieve this, the paper proposes several methods for feature extraction and representation that enable the network to effectively learn from a large dataset of grasping examples. Additionally, the authors demonstrate the efficacy of using a cost function to balance the tradeoff between grasp quality and robot sensing system constraints. The resulting system is capable of accurately predicting successful grasps for a variety of objects, demonstrating the potential for this approach to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of robot manipulation tasks.

Solid State Drives (SSDs) are popularly used for caching in large scale cloud storage systems nowadays. Traditionally, most cache algorithms make replacement at each miss when cache space is full. However, we observe that in a typical Cloud Block Storage (CBS), there is a great percentage of blocks with large reuse distances, which would result in large number of blocks being evicted out of the cache before they ever have a chance to be referenced while they are cached, significantly jeopardizing the cache efficiency. In this paper, we propose LEA, Lazy Eviction cache Algorithm, for cloud block storage to efficiently remedy the cache inefficiencies caused by cache blocks with large reuse distances. Specifically, LEA uses two lists, Lazy Eviction List (LEL) and Block Identity List (BIL). When a cache miss happens, if the candidate evicted-block has not resided in cache for longer than its reuse distance, LEA inserts the missed block identity into BIL. Otherwise, it inserts the missed block entry into LEL. We have evaluated LEA by using IO traces collected from Tencent, one of the largest network service providers in the world, and several open source traces. Experimental results show that LEA not only outperforms most of the state-of-the-art cache algorithms in hit ratio, but also reduces the number of SSD writes greatly.

The paper proposes optimization and merging methodology for improving hardware design space exploration using high-level synthesis (HLS) tools. The use of HLS is gaining popularity as it enables faster and more efficient design of complex hardware systems by abstracting hardware design using hardware design languages such as RTL. However, the use of HLS poses challenges in terms of tool flow and design space exploration. The proposed methodology aims to optimize RTL to C conversion, merge submodules in the design hierarchy, and improve the exploration of design space. The methodology includes a number of steps such as partitioning and mapping outputs to reduce computational cost, as well as using phased arrays to optimize performance. The proposed methodology has been evaluated using IP networks and demonstrated significant improvements in design exploration, including a reduction in run-time and an increase in useful output, highlighting the potential benefits of this approach.

The prevalence of Cloud Computing has appealed many users to put their business into low-cost and flexible cloud servers instead of bare-metal machines. Most virtual machines in the cloud run commodity operating system(e.g., linux), and the complexity of such operating systems makes them more bug-prone and easier to be compromised. To mitigate the security threats, previous works attempt to mediate and filter system calls, transform all unpopular paths into popular paths, or implement a nested kernel along with the untrusted outter kernel to enforce certain security policies. However, such solutions only enforce read-only protection or assume that popular paths in the kernel to contain almost no bug, which is not always the case in the real world. To overcome their shortcomings and combine their advantages as much as possible, we propose a hardware-assisted isolation mechanism that isolates untrusted part of the kernel. To achieve isolation, we prepare multiple restricted Extended Page Table (EPT) during boot time, each of which has certain critical data unmapped from it so that the code executing in the isolated environment could not access sensitive data. We leverage the VMFUNC instruction already available in recent Intel processors to directly switch to another pre-defined EPT inside guest virtual machine without trapping into the underlying hypervisor, which is faster than the traditional trap-and-emulate procedure. The semantic gap is minimized and real-time check is achieved by allowing EPT violations to be converted to Virtualization Exception (VE), which could be handled inside guest kernel in non-root mode. Our preliminary evaluation shows that with hardware virtualization feature, we are able to run the untrusted code in an isolated environment with negligible overhead.

This paper presents a low-cost anthropometric body scanning system that utilizes depth cameras as its main sensing tool. The system can provide three-dimensional displays of the scanned body, as well as accurate weight measurements. The use of depth cameras allows for the capture of precise measurements of body indexes, such as height, width, and length, without the need for physical tools. The system is designed to be easy to use, requiring minimal training for users. The results of our experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of this low-cost body scanning system, which may have applications in fields such as medical and fitness assessments.

The mobile edge caching is a promising way to reduce the user-perceived delay and improve the transmission data rates for the wireless networks. However, the cache capacities of base stations (BSs) tend to be limited and users' interests for the contents are diverse, which makes the content placement decision critical for the network performance optimization. Besides, due to the flexible user-BS association, it is more complicated to optimize the content delivery and placement which are coupled with each other. This paper investigates the content placement and content delivery strategies in the cache-enabled wireless networks. In particular, the effective capacity, which can characterize the end-to-end user-perceived delay and data rates simultaneously, is introduced as the user's utility metric. As the content caching and content delivery operate in different time-scales, they are investigated separately. For the content caching, a content placement problem is formulated, where both users' different active levels and diverse content preferences are considered. Due to the NP-hard nature, the problem is decomposed into two sub-problems, and an iterative association-aware content placement algorithm is proposed. For the content delivery, the user-BS association problem is formulated, and a cache-aware user-BS association algorithm is designed. The performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated based on the simulations. The numerical results show that the proposed algorithms have a better capability to cope with users' diverse active levels, and achieve a better performance in terms of effective capacity and fairness level, compared with the existing algorithms.

This paper explores the use of nonlinear memristor-based neural networks for learning processes and their potential replication in computer architecture. Memristors play a crucial role in mimicking the behavior of biological synapses, enabling the creation of artificial neural networks that can learn and adapt. In addition, the programming of these networks requires the use of bridge circuits to provide the necessary signals and input for the memristors. The potential applications of such networks in computer architecture are vast, as they can provide a powerful tool for tasks such as pattern recognition and machine learning. Ultimately, this research aims to replicate the efficiency and adaptability of biological neural networks through the use nonlinear memristors and synaptic behavior in artificial networks.

In recent years, development of an underwater observation system that is low cost and easy to operate is greatly required with the expansion of demand for marine resources survey acquiring rare metal and so on. The authors developed a free-fall type observation system of which body is glass sphere. Since the glass sphere has durability for high hydrodynamic pressure, retailed camera is able to be set inside the sphere to motion the sea environment. However, the positioning of the observation system is severe problem, because sinking motion is only provided by gravity or tidal force. To realize a low cost measurement system, we try to use MEMS IMU (Micro Electro Mechanical Systems Inertial Measurement Unit) for position estimation. The position by MEMS IMU has sensor noise and caused in large estimation error. In this paper, to reduce the estimation error, we propose the combination of optical range sensor. By adopting light rather than ultrasonic for range sensor, it is easy to adapt to systems using glass spheres. At first, sensor noise is modeled by allan variance calculated from measured stationary data, position estimation simulation using the modeled sensor data was performed. By adding the ranging data, the standard deviation of the position estimation can be reduced in (x, y) = (28.8%, 4.43%) with comparison of estimation by the sensor data of MEMS IMU and the depth sensor.

This paper presents a comparative study of three classification algorithms for handwritten digit recognition. The focus is on feature extraction and the evaluation of the Multilayer Perceptrons, Correlation and Bayes methods applied to the NIST handwriting recognition database. The experiment was carried out using standard recognition metrics, such as error rate, precision, and recall. Our results demonstrate that Multilayer Perceptrons and Correlation methods performed similarly well in terms of accuracy and efficiency, while the Bayes approach showed lower performance. Overall, this study provides insightful observations on the effectiveness of different algorithms for handwriting recognition and can aid in the selection of an appropriate classifier for this task.

The spatial and temporal distribution of active users across a given region greatly affects the activity of base stations (BSs) and the cumulative interference in a wireless network. In this letter, we propose a new approach for spatio-temporal analysis of wireless networks wherein stochastic geometry is used for the spatial domain and ON/OFF traffic models are used for the temporal domain. We illustrate the proposed approach through a mix of file transfer protocol (FTP) and video streaming (VS) traffic. With the aid of semi-Markov process, we derive the stationary probability for a given service request. Further, we develop a joint spatio-temporal model for the distribution of active users under a random BS.

This paper presents a novel nonlinear dictionary learning (DL) model to address the energy disaggregation (ED) problem, i.e., decomposing the electricity signal of a home to its operating devices. First, ED is modeled as a new temporal DL problem where a set of dictionary atoms is learned to capture the most representative temporal features of electricity signals. The sparse codes corresponding to these atoms show the contribution of each device in the total electricity consumption. To learn powerful atoms, a novel deep temporal DL (DTDL) model is proposed that computes complex nonlinear dictionaries in the latent space of a long short-term memory autoencoder (LSTM-AE). While the LSTM-AE captures the deep temporal manifold of electricity signals, the DTDL model finds the most representative atoms inside this manifold. To simultaneously optimize the dictionary and the deep temporal manifold, a new optimization algorithm is proposed that alternates between finding the optimal LSTM-AE and the optimal dictionary. To the best of authors' knowledge, DTDL is the only DL model that understands the deep temporal structures of the data. Experiments on the Reference ED Data Set show an outstanding performance compared with the recent state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of precision, recall, accuracy, and F-score.

In this paper, we propose a gene selection method for cancer classification based on a data overlap measure in microarray data. We utilize complexity theory, biomedical measurement, and machine learning techniques to extract relevant features from the data model. Our approach focuses on gene expression patterns that are most indicative of cancer progression. The proposed method highlights significant gene interactions and reduces the dimensionality of the feature space, leading to improved classification accuracy.
