Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying relevant genes for cancer diagnosis, providing a promising foundation for further research in precision medicine.

Epidural electrical stimulation (ECS) combined with rehabilitative training could improve behavioral function for stroke both in clinical and animal studies. Though the primary motor cortex (M1) ECS has some effects on recovery, the performance are not good enough and better sites for stimulation need further investigation. In this study, we compared the effects of ECS on M1 and premotor cortex (PM). Twelve rats were trained to the single-pellet retrieval (SPR) task before receiving photothrombotic ischemia model and electrodes implantation. They were randomly distributed to three groups: M1 stimulation, PM stimulation and no stimulation (Control) groups. The 100Hz monopolar cathodal stimulation were given concurrent with rehabilitation training over recovery days. The performance on SPR task were scored for analysis. Our results showed that M1 ECS had a better effect on behavioral improvement compared to the other two groups.

The emergence of Industry 4.0 revolution has increased the availability of data from various engineering components providing extensive information on different aspects of the industry. In the context of reliability and efficiency, features extracted from data can be utilized to predict performance degradation and optimizing product service as well as determining remaining useful life. The need for prediction models able to establish correlations between related variables and measured variables becomes obvious. In this work, a data driven approach is developed using a state machine concept to realize a lifetime model able to deal with the variability and uncertainties of industrial data. This concept provides a systematic solution for a system exposed to multi-state degradation by enabling the system to identify appropriate parameters autonomously, according to the state it belongs to. Due to the flexibility and scalability, this model can easily be deployed to various types of industrial data. Impressive findings using data from agricultural experiments validate the adaptability and potential of this approach as an alternative modeling strategy.

Raw signal simulation is an important tool to test the effectiveness of the system parameters and imaging algorithms. A fast raw signal simulation method for multi-circular synthetic aperture imaging is proposed based on the inverse processing of the imaging algorithm and the nonuniform fast Fourier transform. The analytical description and processing procedure are presented. Simulation results of an ideal point target and a human model demonstrate the validity and effectiveness. Compared with the common time-domain method, the proposed method can achieve equivalent performance with higher efficiency.

Correntropy has recently attracted great attention because of its robustness to non-Gaussian noise. Inspired by this robustness property, a spline adaptive filtering algorithm based on the maximum correntropy criterion (SAF-MCC) has been proposed. However, the steady-state convergence performance of the SAF-MCC has not been studied. This brief presents a steady-state performance analysis of the SAF-MCC for Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise. We derive and discuss the theoretical excess mean square error (EMSE) under these cases. Monte Carlo simulations are presented to corroborate the theoretical performance analysis results developed in this brief.

This paper presents a system applied in the automatic driving train using Case Based Reasoning (CBR) with Differential Evolution (DE). CBR was used to retrieve, reuse and revise experiences from real data during the journey. The DE was used to adapt the cases retrieved and optimize then considering multi-objective optimization. For this purpose, a train driving simulator used and the results compared the data of real train driving scenarios. Multi-objective optimization was used to reduce fuel consumption and also travel time. The results obtained concerning fuel consumption was entirely satisfactory because in some cases average savings of 45% in fuel consumption about the results obtained by human drivers. Adapting cases using the Differential Evolution approach led to a 5% gain in consumption over an adaptation of cases using Genetic Algorithm. It should also note that the time required for case adaptation was lower using Differential Evolution Algorithm than using Genetic Algorithm.

One of the main functions of battery management system (BMS) is to determine the current charge level, an incorrect estimate of which can lead to unforeseen situations in the operation of various communication systems. Due to the complexity of the analytical model of multi-cell lithium-ion storage devices, when developing algorithms for controlling them, it is effective to use fuzzy inference systems (FIS) that allow for the correction of the state of the charge level. The article presents the results, further improvement of such systems by combining several FIS depending on the state of the battery, which increases the accuracy of determining the charge state of the lithium-ion energy storage by modern BMS.

This paper focuses on the joint positioning of flying base stations and association of users using an evolutionary-based approach in order to optimize interference and signal to noise ratio. The study proposes the use of genetic algorithms to solve this optimization problem. The placement of base stations and the allocation of channels and bandwidth are critical in determining the overall performance of the network. By using the proposed approach, the authors were able to achieve significant improvements in network performance compared to traditional approaches. The study demonstrates the importance of considering the interplay between base station placement, channel allocation, and user association in order to achieve optimal network performance. Overall, this paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of wireless communications and provides new insights into the optimization of mobile networks.

An efficient representation of observed data has many benefits in various domains of engineering and science. Representing static data sets, such as images, is a living branch in machine learning and eases downstream tasks, such as classification, regression, or decision making. However, the representation of dynamical systems has received less attention. In this work, we develop a method to represent a dynamical system efficiently as a combination of a state and a local model, which fulfills a criterion inspired by the minimum description length (MDL) principle. The MDL principle is used in machine learning and statistics to quantify the trade-off between the ability to explain seen data and the model complexity. Networked control systems are a prominent example, where such a representation is beneficial. When many agents share a network, information exchange is costly and should thus happen only when necessary. We empirically show the efficiency of the proposed encoding for several dynamical systems and demonstrate reduced communication for event-triggered state estimation problems.

This paper proposes a competing risks model for analyzing the reliability of systems with multiply censored data under multivariate Weibull distributions. The Weibull distribution is a widely used parametric distribution for modeling reliability data models. Maximum likelihood estimation is used to estimate the parameters of the model. The proposed method is illustrated using a case study of fan reliability in a silicon production process. The results suggest that the proposed model performs well in analyzing the reliability of systems with multiply censored data under multivariate Weibull distributions. This study provides valuable insights for practitioners dealing with reliability problems in various industries.

Channel Coding has been one of the central disciplines driving the success stories of current generation LTE systems and beyond. In particular, turbo codes are mostly used for cellular and other applications where a reliable data transfer is required for latency-constrained communication in the presence of data-corrupting noise. However, the decoding algorithm for turbo codes is computationally intensive and thereby limiting its applicability in hand-held devices. In this paper, we study the feasibility of using Deep Learning (DL) architectures based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for encoding and decoding of turbo codes. In this regard, we simulate and use data from various stages of the transmission chain (turbo encoder output, Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel output, demodulator output) to train our proposed RNN architecture and compare its performance to the conventional turbo encoder/decoder algorithms. Simulation results show, that the proposed RNN model outperforms the decoding performance of a conventional turbo decoder at low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) regions.

Sentiment analysis is the study area in Natural language processing (NLP) that is concerned to identify the mood or opinion with in the text. This paper emphasizes on the different methods utilized for classifying the natural language text reviews in accordance with opinions expressed in text to analyze whether the extensive behavior is negative, positive or neutral. The abundance of discussion platforms, Weblogs, product reviews sites, e-commerce and social networking sites have encouraged stream of thoughts and articulation of opinions. Social media is considered to be a big platform of sentiments, reviews and opinion evaluation. Data used in this study are online product reviews collected from twitter and used to rank the best classifier for sentiments. The method of analysis on polarity classification was discussed in experimental work by using well known classifiers including Naïve byes, Support vector machine and Logistic regression for predicting the user reviews.

The theory of Rough set has proposed a method for approximating concepts by using a pair of thresholds on probability to defined three regions, namely, the positive, boundary and negative regions. These three regions generate three-way decision rules, which are acceptance, deferment and rejection decisions. In fact, the decision environment is prone to dynamic with the data changed continuously. As such, the three regions of a target decision will be changed inevitably. There are having been many studies on methods for incremental updating three-way decisions by adding or deleting objects in different threads. In this paper, we combine addition and deletion operators in a single updating step for three-way decisions in incomplete information system and mathematically proof our proposed methods.

Estimating requirements development effort is a critical activity in the software development process. Producing an accurate estimate, however, is extremely difficult, especially in the early stages of the software development process, where no clear and no complete description of the desired software behavior is available, hence leading to an estimate process with a high level of uncertainty. To handle this issue, in this paper, we present REEE (Requirements Elicitation Effort Estimation) - a framework for incrementally estimating software requirements elicitation efforts. We first categorize a project in terms of project's domain, different types of project parameters and requirements - functional requirements (FRs), non-functional requirements (NFRs), constraints and domain properties (DPs), while taking into consideration relationships among them. We then present an incremental approach to software requirements elicitation effort estimation that uses similar past projects in a case-based reasoning (CBR) model. In this approach, semantic similarity is quantified, once classification and normalization of requirements are done. To see the strengths and limitations of REEE, a dataset of 36(students') projects have been analyzed. Experimental results show that the use of REEE is a viable alternative to other cost estimation techniques, and can provide better results, with less uncertainty, for requirements elicitation effort estimation.

This paper presents a study on analyzing railway accidents' narratives using deep learning techniques. Accidents in rail transportation have always been a significant concern, and their prevention is of utmost importance to ensure safety. The paper proposes the use of deep learning and neural networks for text mining and text categorization to analyze accident narratives. The goal is to extract information from the narratives, which can assist railway operators in identifying potential hazards and taking appropriate measures to prevent accidents. The paper highlights the importance of text categorization and its potential impact on railway safety. The proposed approach provides a novel way to extract valuable information from the accident narratives, enabling organizations to improve their safety measures and prevent accidents. Overall, the use of deep learning and neural networks can significantly improve the railway industry's safety standards by providing valuable insights and preventing accidents.

This paper aims to explore the foreseeable industrial changes of automotive and transportation driven by semiconductors, with a focus on the impact on automobiles, autonomous vehicles, roads, companies, and deep learning. Semiconductors have been increasingly integrated into automotive and transportation systems, enabling the development of advanced features and increasing the efficiency of these systems. The emergence of autonomous vehicles has been a major trend in the industry, with semiconductors playing a crucial role in enabling the technology. Roads are also being transformed by the influence of semiconductors, with intelligent transportation systems and smart roads becoming more common. Companies in the automotive and transportation industry are facing significant challenges and opportunities due to the changes brought by semiconductors. Finally, deep learning is becoming increasingly important in the industry, with semiconductors providing the computational power necessary for training and inference. In conclusion, the integration of semiconductors is driving significant changes in the automotive and transportation industry, and it is crucial for companies to adapt and capitalize on the opportunities presented by these changes.

As a novel signal control method, signal Cooperative Control with traffic Supply and Demand (CCSD) is superior to the traditional control methods and could satisfy the control requirements under all traffic conditions. However, the optimization solution of CCSD cannot meet the real-time control requirement for its exhaustive search. To overcome the problem, in this paper, the optimization problem of CCSD is reconstructed by the time-varying traffic supply and demand, and the problem is reduced as a problem of space search. Then, the krill herd (KH) algorithm is introduced and employed to realize the fast solution of CCSD (named KH-CCSD). During the process of optimization, the search space representation and fitness function for the KH algorithm are constructed to satisfy the solution of CCSD. The optimal signal timing plan is obtained by an iterated search of krill swarm in a multi-dimensional time-varying space cooperatively constrained by traffic supplies and demands. The convergence and effectiveness of KH-CCSD are validated by comparing experiments, in which the convergence of KH-CCSD is tested by different initializations and KH-CCSD is compared with the Webster method and capacity-aware back-pressure (CABP) control under unsaturated, saturated, and oversaturated conditions. The experiments results show that KH-CCSD performs a fast convergence and KH-CCSD is superior to the Webster method and CABP. As a result, KH-CCSD could satisfy the application of CCSD under all traffic conditions.

Driving can be a stressful activity, especially when drivers navigate unfamiliar roads or encounter adverse road conditions. In an effort to mitigate driving-related stress, this paper proposes a novel approach to online trip recommendation based on driving behavior prediction. By incorporating data collected from various sensors in automobiles, such as speed and acceleration, predictive models can be developed to anticipate a driver's individual behavior and state of mind. Using computational modeling techniques, these predictions can then inform the recommendation of the most suitable route and travel options for the driver. Through this approach, it is hoped that driving-related stress can be effectively minimized, leading to safer and more enjoyable driving experiences for all.

High-voltage circuit breaker is one of the most critical equipment in power system, and the operating mechanism fault is the main fault state of circuit breaker. This paper uses the coil current and K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) classification methodology for diagnosing and recognizing the operating mechanism fault of circuit breaker. Firstly, to collect the coil current of normal state and common fault states, we conduct an experiment to simulate three common fault working states of operating mechanism from a 126kV SF6 circuit breaker; extract the feature vectors from the different states according to the characteristic of the close coil current; and, use KNN classification algorithm to establish the fault diagnosis model. Finally, we use the testing samples to verify the diagnosis model. The result shows that the new proposal can diagnose and recognize the fault states of the high-voltage circuit-breaker operating mechanism objectively, accurately and effectively.

This paper aims to analyze practical issues in SAR measurements of multiple-antenna transmitting devices, with a focus on estimation, antenna measurements, phase measurement, probes, phantoms, standards, and measurement uncertainty. Estimation of SAR is a crucial component in the characterization of radio-frequency energy absorbed by human tissues. Antenna measurements are essential in determining the performance of transmitting antennas. Phase measurement is required in calibrating the antenna for SAR estimation accuracy. Probes are commonly used to measure the electric field strength, which is necessary for determining SAR values. Phantoms are used as a standard measurement object for SAR measurements. Standards are important in ensuring that measurements are accurate and reliable, and regulatory limits are met. Measurement uncertainty is an inherent issue in SAR measurements, and it is essential to evaluate and reduce it to improve accuracy. Analyzing these practical issues in SAR measurements of multiple-antenna transmitting devices can aid in improving the accuracy and reliability of SAR measurements, which is crucial in ensuring the safety of human exposure to radio-frequency energy.

This paper presents a graph computation-based power flow algorithm, which is designed for large-scale AC/DC systems. The load flow is an often-studied and important problem in power system analysis, and this paper proposes a novel computational modeling approach that employs parallel processing and databases to efficiently handle the large amounts of data involved in a large-scale AC/DC system. The mathematical model used in the proposed algorithm is also discussed in detail, making use of graph theory and linear programming techniques to achieve better accuracy and computational speed. Additionally, this paper highlights the advantages of using HVDC transmission in power systems and the benefits of incorporating it into the computational model. Overall, the proposed graph computation-based power flow algorithm offers a more efficient and accurate solution for large-scale power systems compared to traditional approaches.

In recent years, Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) has been extensively researched in various languages because it aims to detect the sentiment of each aspect of the text. The ABSA problem can be divided into three subtasks as follow: the aspect detection, Opinion Target Expression (OTE) and Sentiment Polarity. In this paper, we present a Convolutional Neural Network architecture for the aspect detection for Vietnamese. The aspect detection is to aim to identify of the entity E and attribute A pairs expressed in the text (Pontiki et al., 2016). The experimental results show the superiority of our model over the winning systems on datasets of the VLSP 2018 challenge for aspect detection task. Our method achieves the F1 score of 80.40% for the restaurant domain and 69.25% for the hotel domain.

The integration of handcrafted and deep features presents a promising approach for the classification of retinal diseases using optical coherence tomography (OCT). Feature extraction is a critical step in medical diagnostic imaging, and the combination of both types of features yields better overall performance in disease identification. By training and testing the classification model using a dataset of OCT images of the retina, the integrated features demonstrate improved accuracy in the classification of various retinal diseases compared to the use of either type of feature alone. This approach has the potential for enhancing clinical decision-making in the diagnosis and management of retinal diseases. As such, the integration of handcrafted and deep features for OCT-based retinal disease classification serves as a significant advancement in the field of medical imaging.

This paper discusses the implementation of software control for a cyber-physical system in a manufacturing environment using a game engine. The production facilities are equipped with robots that are controlled using a software running on game engines. Control systems are implemented using computational modeling, which helps to optimize the operation of the robots and ensure precise movement. The game engine-based approach provides a flexible platform for controlling the robots and allows for real-time interaction with the production environment. The software also enables the robots to adjust their movements based on changes in the production environment, making the manufacturing process more efficient and effective. Overall, this software-based approach provides a promising solution for improving the control and optimization of manufacturing processes, particularly those utilizing robotics.

In recent years, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for image super-resolution (SR) to achieve a range of sophisticated performances. Despite the significant advancement made in CNNs, it is still difficult to apply CNNs to practical SR applications due to enormous computations of deep convolutions. In this paper, we propose two lightweight deep neural networks using depthwise separable convolution for the real-time image SR. Specifically, depthwise separable convolution divides the standard convolution into depthwise convolution and pointwise convolution to significantly reduce the number of model parameters and multiplication operations. Moreover, recursive learning is adopted to increase the depth and receptive field of the network in order to improve the SR quality without increasing the model parameters. Finally, we propose a novel technique called Super-Sampling (SS) to learn more abundant high-resolution information by over-sampling the output image followed by adaptive down-sampling. The proposed two models, named SSNet-M and SSNet, outperform the existing state-of-the-art real-time image SR networks, including SRCNN, FSRCNN, ESPCN, and VDSR, in terms of model complexity, and subjective and PSNR/SSIM evaluations on Set5, Set14, B100, Urban100, and Manga109.

Hardware neural networks that implement synaptic weights with embedded non-volatile memory, such as spin torque memory (ST-MRAM), are a major lead for low energy artificial intelligence. In this work, we propose an approximate storage approach for their memory. We show that this strategy grants effective control of the bit error rate by modulating the programming pulse amplitude or duration. Accounting for the devices variability issue, we evaluate energy savings, and show how they translate when training a hardware neural network. On an image recognition example, 74% of programming energy can be saved by losing only 1% on the recognition performance.

This paper presents a study on the application of analog data assimilation techniques for the assimilation of along-track nadir and wide-swath SWOT altimetry observations in the Western Mediterranean Sea. The aim of the study is to improve the accuracy of numerical models of the area by incorporating the remote sensing data from altimetry observations. The study specifically focuses on the use of computational modeling to analyze the data models and apply interpolation techniques to optimize the assimilation process. The results from the study demonstrate that the analog data assimilation methods significantly improve the accuracy of the models and provide a valuable tool for future applications in oceanography. Overall, this research contributes to advancements in the field of data assimilation and provides important insights into how remote sensing data can be effectively integrated into numerical models.

The paper considers the way for controlling a grip mechanism. A program code for controlling the movement of mechatronic complex mechanisms is presented. The software is written in the LAD programming language used for programming logical controllers Siemens s7-1200. The software model is written in the environment TiaPortal v14.1. An algorithm for calculating the time delay based on fuzzy logic has been developed and is presented. This algorithm allows increasing the productivity and reducing the energy costs of the system. The results of the experiment showing the advantages of the proposed algorithm are given.

This paper presents a primal-dual architecture for the embedded implementation of linear model predictive control (MPC). The proposed architecture utilizes field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) to accelerate the MPC computation and improve convergence. The design leverages the principles of computer architecture to efficiently compute the MPC solution using dedicated hardware modules, including adders and other important components. The proposed architecture demonstrates significant acceleration compared to traditional software-based implementations of MPC, making it ideal for real-time control applications. The paper presents experimental results that validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high performance and reliable control. Overall, this work provides a promising approach for the implementation of MPC on embedded systems that require efficient computation and optimal control.

How to make the machine better understand human language has always been a hot topic. It greatly influences the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge extraction, intelligent question answering and other nature language processing applications. For this reason, researchers put forward multilingual analysis and language modeling methods, for example, the distributed feature representation fitting for the neural network models and so on. This paper argues that language analysis and modeling should start with the characteristics of the language itself. In seeing this, we have thoroughly studied a series of basic NLP analysis techniques and present our own three-layer language processing and analysis model. This model takes into account the characteristics of language at all levels, and tries to preserve most of the attributes of the sentence. Such design deals with the analysis and representation of language from a brand new perspective, which may inspire many other applications in the field of NLP.

GANE, short for Generative Adversarial Network Embedding, is a type of machine learning model that utilizes generative adversarial networks to create predictive models. With the help of GANs, the generators within the model are able to learn the underlying structure of the data and create more accurate predictions. This is achieved through a task analysis that breaks down the data into smaller, more manageable components. Additionally, linear programming techniques are used to optimize the generators and ensure that they are producing the best possible results. GANE has been successfully applied to various fields, including image and speech recognition, and recently to gallium nitride material design. The potential applications of GANE are numerous, and the continued development of this model will undoubtedly have a significant impact on the field of machine learning.

Flower plays an extremely important role in our life, which has high research value and application value. The traditional methods of flower classification is mainly based on shape, color or texture features, and this methods needs people to select features for flower classification lead to the accuracy of classification is not very high. This paper aims to develop an effective flower classification approach using convolution neural network and transfer learning. In this paper, based on VGG-16, VGG-19, Inception-v3 and ResNet50 models were used to compare the network initialization model with the transfer learning model. The results show that transfer learning can effectively avoid deep convolution networks are prone to local optimal problems and over-fitting problems. Compared with the traditional methods, the accuracy of flower recognition on Oxford flowers dataset is obviously improved, and has better robustness and generalization ability.

In this paper, we propose a method for learning the 3D white matter microstructure from 2D histology images. We aim to bridge the gap between traditional two-dimensional displays and three-dimensional displays by using optical fiber networks and magnetic resonance imaging. Our approach involves image reconstruction and modeling of the microstructure based on microscopy data. By combining the power of optical imaging and magnetic resonance imaging, we can effectively capture the complex 3D structure of the white matter microstructure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by applying it to the reconstruction of white matter tracts in a rodent brain. Our results show that our method achieves high accuracy and robustness in learning 3D white matter microstructure from 2D histology, which has many potential applications in neuroscience research and clinical practice.

Computational Intelligence applications in banking and finance have been developed and deployed in the recent past and have been offering business solutions in both front end and back end processes in order to create efficiency and exceptional customer experience. In recent times, AI and machine learning are perceived to be the most valuable enabler to achieve competitive advantage by enhancing the decision making capabilities and transforming the banking industry. This paper will highlight the applications of AI and evaluate its utility in different functional areas of financial industry focusing primarily on automation of banking operations and customer engagement. It concludes with an analysis of how banking and financial organizations frame their environment and effectively use computational intelligence to improve their business.

This paper proposes an Adaptive Random-Selected Multi-Beamforming Estimation Scheme for Satellite-Based Internet of Things using antenna arrays. The focus is on channel estimation for MIMO communication using high-temperature superconductors. The proposed scheme is adaptive and random-selection based, which ensures accuracy and efficiency in estimating the channel models. Satellites are used as the medium for communication and the proposed scheme improves the performance of satellite-based IoT systems by accurately estimating the channels. The use of antenna arrays and the random-selection based algorithm ensures high accuracy in the estimation process. Overall, the proposed scheme has the potential to improve the overall performance of satellite-based IoT systems by improving channel estimation accuracy.

Parallel computing is an area of computer science that has gained immense popularity in the recent years. With the advent of high-performance computing systems and the need for faster computation, parallel computing has become an important topic of research. This paper provides a review and perspective on parallel computing, focusing on areas such as computational modeling, parallel programming, computers, instruction sets, pipeline processing, and data models. Computational modeling involves creating mathematical models to simulate and solve complex engineering problems. Parallel programming, on the other hand, deals with designing algorithms and programs that can execute in parallel on multiple processors. The development of computers with multiple processors has paved the way for parallel processing, in which tasks are divided into smaller sub-tasks that can be processed simultaneously. Instruction sets are the basic set of commands executed by the computer, and they have been optimized for parallel processing in modern systems. Pipeline processing is a technique that involves dividing a larger task into smaller sub-tasks that can be carried out in a sequence, resulting in faster processing. Finally, data models are used to represent and manipulate data in parallel computing systems. This paper concludes with a discussion on the perspective of future developments in parallel computing.

Commercial High-Level Synthesis (HLS) tool vendors have started to enable ways to protect Behavioral IP (BIPs) from being unlawful used. The main approach is to provide tools to encrypt these BIPs which can be decrypted by the HLS tool only. The main problem with this approach is that encrypting the IP does not allow BIP users to insert synthesis directives into the source code in the form of pragmas (comments), and hence cancels out one of the most important advantages of C-based VLSI design: The ability to automatically generate micro-architectures with unique design metrics, e.g. area, power and performance. This work studies the impact to the search space when synthesis directives are not able to be inserted in to the encrypted IP source code while other options are still available to the BIP users (e.g. setting global synthesis options and limiting the number and type of functional units) and proposes a method that selectively controls the search space by encrypting different portions of the BIP. To achieve this goal we propose a fast heuristic based on divide and conquer method. Experimental results show that our proposed method works well compared to an exhaustive search that leads to the optimal solution.

Membership inference attacks on social media health data with machine learning have become a significant concern in recent years. With the increasing adoption of data models and predictive models in social networking online, machine learning is being increasingly used to exploit training data and reveal sensitive information about individuals. The vulnerability of training data is often attributed to the fact that it can reveal a considerable amount of information about individuals, making it highly susceptible to privacy breaches. This paper examines the threats posed by membership inference attacks on social media health data with a focus on machine learning, exploring the challenges associated with training predictive models while minimizing the risk of data privacy breaches. The study also explores potential solutions to privacy vulnerabilities in training data, highlighting the need for robust privacy-preserving algorithms and techniques to mitigate the risks posed by these attacks. Overall, this work aims to raise awareness about the growing threat of membership inference attacks on social media health data and the need for better data privacy protection in machine learning.

This paper is concerned with distributed multiagent optimization with inequality and equality constraints based on exact penalty methods. In the literature of exact penalty methods, constrained optimization problem is solved through optimization of penalized objective function and, under mild assumptions, the set of the optimal solutions of the penalized objective function coincides with that of the original constrained optimization problem. Exploiting the exactness of the penalized objective function, this paper proposes a new distributed multi-agent optimization protocol which simplifies the update law of previous protocols based on exact penalty methods with equality constraints. Also more concrete proof of the convergence of the protocol is provided under the assumption of the exactness of the penalized objective function.

Feature extraction plays a crucial role in deep learning, as it provides a framework for making sense of complex datasets. In this paper, we explore the use of unsupervised representation learning using convolutional and stacked auto-encoders for feature extraction. Our analysis focuses on both domain and cross-domain feature space, with a particular emphasis on decoding and training techniques to optimize feature extraction. We also examine the efficacy of convolutional codes in image reconstruction and explore the use of visualization techniques to better understand the data. Overall, our results suggest that unsupervised representation learning using convolutional and stacked auto-encoders can provide a powerful framework for feature extraction, with important implications for task analysis in a variety of domains.

This paper presents a survey on the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods in vehicular networks (VN) for resource management. With the increasing popularity of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, the VN environment poses a unique set of challenges such as the presence of delays and interference. The authors review recent studies on MARL for VN resource management and point out the importance of task analysis in designing an optimal learning scheme. Additionally, the paper highlights the significance of MARL in managing the VN's resources such as spectrum allocation and power control. Finally, the authors discuss open research questions that need to be addressed for improved MARL-based resource management in VN. Overall, this survey highlights the potential of MARL in addressing resource management in VN and provides valuable insights on its current state-of-the-art.

This paper proposes a fuzzy method for mapping processes with communications in cloud computing. The goal is to optimize task analysis, bandwidth, and processor scheduling in cloud computing. The proposed method uses clustering algorithms and heuristic algorithms to group the program processors into clusters based on their communication patterns. The communication patterns are analyzed to determine the optimal placement of program processors in the clusters. The proposed fuzzy method is able to optimize the use of resources and improve the performance of cloud computing. Results of the experiments show that the proposed method is effective in improving the performance of cloud computing while maintaining high levels of resource utilization. Overall, this method represents a promising solution for effectively mapping processes with communications in cloud computing.

In a fog-to-cloud computing system, service function chaining (SFC) mapping is an important task that aims to efficiently allocate multiple SFC instances to a network topology. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for SFC mapping, which takes into account multiple SFC instances and their interdependencies. Our approach involves a computational modeling technique that leverages the power of cloud computing to optimize the mapping process, resulting in a more cost-effective and efficient use of cloud resources. Additionally, we examine the potential benefits of network function virtualization (NFV) and the Internet of Things (IoT) in improving SFC mapping performance. Our proposed approach is evaluated through experimental results, showing that it outperforms existing SFC mapping techniques in terms of resource utilization, network delay, and throughput. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of computer architecture and cloud computing by presenting a new approach for SFC mapping that can enable more efficient and reliable fog-to-cloud computing systems.

This paper describes the process of auto-scaling a defence application across the cloud using Docker and Kubernetes. These technologies are both based on containerization, which allows for easy deployment and scaling of applications. The cloud computing environment provides the necessary infrastructure to support this type of deployment, which is especially important for computational modeling applications that require high-performance computing resources. The application being discussed is used for training and optimization of helicopter models, and the use of Docker and Kubernetes allows for efficient and effective management of the resources required for this task. The use of virtualization in this context provides an additional layer of security and flexibility, allowing for easy migration of resources between different environments as needed. In summary, the combination of containerization, cloud computing, and virtualization technologies enables auto-scaling of defence applications to meet the high-performance computing needs of complex training and optimization tasks.

This paper proposes a method for enhancing the stability of stand-alone microgrids through demand side management techniques. The focus is on voltage, frequency, and current control, which are key parameters for proper operation of stand-alone microgrids. The paper presents an estimation algorithm for power demand and considerations of regulators for proper control of the demand side management techniques. The proposed method will benefit the operation of stand-alone microgrids and provide a foundation for further research on demand side management techniques in microgrid systems.

The development of implantable cardiac devices has revolutionized the treatment of heart diseases. However, the testing and validation of these devices present significant challenges due to the complexity of the biological system. In this context, biological system modeling provides a valuable tool for predicting and optimizing the performance of implantable devices. In particular, computational modeling of cardiac electrical activity has been widely used for closed-loop validation of pacemakers and other cardiac devices. This approach involves simulating action potentials in the heart tissue and testing the response of the device to various physiological conditions. The accuracy of the simulations depends on the quality of the models, which must take into account the heterogeneity and variability of the physiological parameters. Advances in technology, such as the use of avalanche photodiodes for high-speed optical sensing, have enabled more accurate measurement of heart beats and have contributed to the validation of the models. Overall, cardiac electrical modeling is a promising approach for improving the safety and efficacy of implantable devices.

Shadow detection and removal has become an essential task in computer vision due to its potential impact on various applications, such as object recognition, scene understanding, and image interpretation. This paper proposes a novel approach based on direction-aware spatial context features for shadow detection and removal. The proposed method utilizes feature extraction and image color analysis to capture the characteristics of the shadow regions. The training process incorporates semantics to enhance the classification accuracy of shadows. The proposed method is evaluated and benchmark tested on various datasets, demonstrating its superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods. In addition, a recurrent neural network (RNN) is employed to learn the spatio-temporal dependencies inherent in the proposed method, further improving the performance of the approach on challenging datasets. Overall, the proposed direction-aware spatial context features provide a promising solution for accurate and efficient shadow detection and removal in computer vision applications.

Security and safety have been traditionally considered as different disciplines addressed by different professionals. However, a close look at their characteristics and their analogies leads to the conclusion that they are actually interdependent. Specifically, we argue that safety requires system security and dependability.

The typical inaccuracy of data gathering and preparation procedures makes erroneous and unnecessary information to be a common issue in real-world applications. In this context, feature selection methods are used in order to reduce the harmful impact of such information in data analysis by removing irrelevant features from datasets. This research presents a novel feature selection method in the field of unsupervised learning, in which the complexity arises from the fact that the class labels cannot be used to select the most discriminative features as it is traditionally performed in supervised learning. The technique designed, which is called Kolmogorov-Smirnov test-based Unsupervised Feature Selection (KSUFS), is based on the computation of estimated feature distributions that are later compared to the original ones using non-parametric statistical tests to provide the most representative input variables. Two versions of the KSUFS are presented in this study: one of them is particularly designed to deal with standard data, in which the accuracy of the method prevalences over other of its aspects; the other version is designed to treat with big data problems, in which the computational complexity is improved due to the characteristics of this type of datasets. The KSUFS is successfully compared to other state-of-the-art unsupervised feature selection techniques in a thorough experimental study, which considers both standard and big data problems. The results obtained show that the method proposed is able to outperform the rest of reference unsupervised feature selection methods considered in the comparisons, selecting the first most influential features for standard datasets and particularly highlighting when big data problems are treated.

This paper focuses on the growing importance of big data analytics and mining for effective visualization and trends forecasting of crime data. The study investigates the use of data mining techniques, data visualization strategies, and predictive models for analyzing crime data and identifying patterns and trends in urban areas. The research findings highlight the significance of big data analytics in predicting crime trends and aiding law enforcement agencies in their decision-making processes. Moreover, the study also explores the applications of deep learning algorithms for crime data analysis and forecasting. The results demonstrate the potential of deep learning in improving predictive accuracy and enhancing the efficiency of crime analysis. The research concludes by emphasizing the critical role of big data analytics and mining in market research and providing valuable insights for policymakers to make informed decisions regarding crime prevention strategies.

The study focuses on the estimation based maximum power point control of DFIG based wind turbine systems. The system utilizes doubly fed induction generators along with mathematical models for estimation purposes. The modeling involves the dynamic equations of the rotors and stators in wind turbines. The estimation methods are used to accurately determine the maximum power points, as well as the optimal speed and torque commands for the generators. The study examines and compares several estimation techniques to evaluate their accuracy and effectiveness in controlling the wind turbine power output. The results show that the estimation based maximum power point control method can be an effective tool for improving the efficiency and reliability of wind turbine systems.

In this paper, a unified approach is proposed for the optimization of distribution grids based on real-time feedback. This approach utilizes advanced optimization techniques to achieve convergence of the system in a timely and efficient manner. The use of inverters and voltage measurement devices enables the system to adapt to changing power demands and maintain the stability of the grid at all times. Furthermore, the involvement of government agencies and power measurement tools ensures the implementation of the proposed approach in a realistic and effective manner. The significance of adopting real-time systems in the optimization of distribution grids cannot be overstated, as it provides an avenue for continuous monitoring and timely response to any issues that may arise. Overall, the proposed approach holds great potential for the optimization of distribution grids in a reliable and comprehensive manner.

In recent years, image segmentation has become an important problem in biomedical imaging due to its role in diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep learning-based approaches have shown great promise in this domain, but they still suffer from several limitations. Decoding is one such limitation that arises due to the fact that deep learning models typically use encoding schemes that are optimized for efficient feature extraction, but not necessarily for efficient decoding. In this paper, we propose a universal decoding method called the Cascade Decoder that aims to overcome this limitation. Our method is designed to work with any encoding scheme and can be easily integrated into existing deep learning models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on several biomedical image segmentation tasks and achieve state-of-the-art results. Finally, we discuss the potential of our method for applications beyond biomedical imaging, such as three-dimensional displays and prototypes.

The piezoresistive silicon based stress sensor has the potential to detect a precursor for the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) implementation in automotive electronics. One solution to enforce reliability in automotive electronics is the use of Machine Learning (ML). One or more physical parameters are being monitored, and algorithms are used to illustrate the health state and predict remaining useful life based on the current and past health information. Piezo-resistive stress sensors are employed to measure the internal stresses of electronic packages, an Acquisition Unit (AU) to read out sensor data and a Raspberry Pi as PHM server to perform evaluation. Accelerated tests in air thermal chamber are performed to get time series data of the stress sensor signals, with which we can know better about how delamination develops inside the package. In this study stress measurements are performed in several electronic packages during the delamination. The delamination is detected by the stress sensor due to the continuous change of the stiffness and the local boundary conditions causing the stresses to change. Moreover, the stress change in multiple cells can give more information regarding the delamination such as the location and its state. Data preprocessing methods to remove outliers and filter raw measurement results, and feature extraction methods to capture only meaningful information by reducing the data are chosen and applied to raw data. A logical assumption is made regarding the data behavior and delamination state, based on data analytics and with Scanning Acoustic Microscope (SAM) images confirmed the delaminated area. FEM simulation are used to provide a qualitatively physical explanation of the stress change due to the delamination. A prognostic model using neural network is trained to estimate the degradation grade. Back Propagation Neural Networks are chosen to provide a fast and quick training for the mechanical stress data.

The use of predictive models in image segmentation is a crucial part of task analysis in biomedical imaging. In this paper, we propose the combination of Mask-RCNN and U-Net for nuclei segmentation in histopathology images. The training data consists of annotated images which are used for measuring the segmentation accuracy. The proposed ensemble model achieves better segmentation results than either Mask-RCNN or U-Net alone. Our findings demonstrate the potential for computer vision techniques to improve analysis of biomedical images.

Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly growing technology that connects everyday appliances to the internet to enable smarter decision-making and enhanced functionality. Wireless communication is the backbone of IoT, allowing for seamless data exchange between connected devices. This critical evaluation paper analyses current wireless communication protocols and their suitability for IoT applications, with a specific focus on Smart cities and Wireless Sensor Networks. The study examines the effectiveness of wireless communication in the context of IoT, assessing issues such as network reliability, scalability, energy efficiency and security. The review reveals that whilst several wireless protocols are currently available for IoT, they all have certain limitations that must be addressed to achieve full functionality for IoT applications. The paper concludes by identifying the most promising wireless communication protocols for IoT, highlighting the importance of further research into IoT and wireless communication technologies to enable effective deployment in future Smart city and IoT systems.

Clustering algorithms are widely used in various text mining applications such as document categorization, sentiment analysis, and natural language processing. However, these algorithms often face search problems due to the high-dimensional nature of text data. Feature extraction is a common approach to deal with this issue by selecting a subset of relevant features. In this paper, we propose an optimization-based approach to feature selection using the Binary Multi-Verse Optimizer. The proposed technique utilizes a mathematical model to represent text data and selectively removes irrelevant features. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technique effectively reduces the dimensionality of the feature space, leading to improved clustering performance in terms of quality and efficiency. The proposed approach provides a promising direction for optimizing text clustering techniques and can be further extended to other application domains beyond text mining. In conclusion, the wheels are set in motion for future research on developing efficient and effective feature selection techniques for clustering algorithms.

Image recognition is a challenging task in the field of information and communication technology (ICT), which relies heavily on feature extraction techniques. Recently, particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been widely applied to optimize feature selection and classification performance in image recognition tasks. In this paper, we propose a deep feature screening method using PSO to select the most discriminative features for image recognition. To further improve the performance of our method, we employ an improved PSO (IPSO) algorithm that effectively balances exploration and exploitation of the feature space. Our proposed method is evaluated on a public spectroscopy dataset and compared with other commonly used feature selection methods. Results demonstrate that our method achieves superior classification performance and effectively reduces feature dimensionality. Overall, our proposed deep feature screening method using ICT cascaded with IPSO shows great potential in optimizing feature selection and improving image recognition performance.

This paper presents a new zonotopic constrained approach for the Kalman filter that takes advantage of the particular structure of the original optimization problem. This technique consists in projecting the state estimation by solving an optimization problem, to ensure that the estimated state belongs to a zonotope. Based on a classical gradient algorithm method, i.e. the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA), this paper proposes a reduced complexity approach suitable for the state estimation of systems subject to a large number of state constraints. The algorithm's speed is improved via a faster ISTA approach, called FISTA.

This paper presents a comparative study of various convolutional neural network (CNN)-based super-resolution methods for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction. The techniques analyzed in this study aim to enhance the resolution of low quality images, resulting in improved quality and clarity of MRI images. The study evaluates different approaches to feature extraction, training processes, and image resolution, utilizing deep learning-based approaches. The performance of each method is evaluated using various metrics, including peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). The results of this study highlight the effectiveness of CNN-based super-resolution methods in improving the quality of MRI reconstruction. This research provides useful insights for selecting the most suitable approach for MRI image reconstruction using deep learning-based methods, potentially leading to more accurate and efficient diagnoses in the medical field.

Virtual network function (VNF) scheduling is crucial for ensuring efficient resource utilization in network function virtualization (NFV) environments. However, VNF scheduling becomes even more challenging when delays and availability-awareness come into play. This paper proposes a novel VNF scheduling approach that takes into account delay-sensitive and availability-aware requirements. Two approximation algorithms are developed to solve the problem efficiently. In addition, a resilient VNF routing algorithm is introduced to ensure high network resilience against component failures. The proposed scheduling approach utilizes hidden Markov models to predict the future VNF performance, thus providing an accurate computational modeling of the system. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach in terms of delay-sensitive and availability-aware VNF scheduling. The proposed approach can be applied to various NFV scenarios, making it a promising solution for the future network function virtualization.

Inverted pendulum is a highly unstable, nonlinear and an under-actuated system. Its dynamics resembles many real-time systems such as segways, self-balancing robots, vertical take-off and landing aircraft (VTOL) and crane lifting containers etc. These real-time applications demand the need of a robust controller. In literature, many different control strategies have been discussed to stabilize an inverted pendulum, out of them, the most robust being fuzzy control and sliding mode control. The former is difficult to tune and has a problem of rule explosion for multivariable system, whereas the latter has a problem of discontinuity and chattering. To address the issues in fuzzy controller, a novel robust linear quadratic regulator (LQR) based adaptive-network fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) controller is proposed and implemented on the stabilization of x-z inverted pendulum. The proposed controller is able to solve the problem of robustness in the LQR controller as well as the difficulty in tuning along with rule explosion in fuzzy controller. Furthermore, the designed controller is tested for different pendulum masses and the results show that as compared with conventional PID controller, the proposed controller gives better performance in achieving lesser overshoot and settling time along with better robustness properties.

This paper proposes a novel approach for aspect extraction from customer reviews using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The method leverages features extracted from the text, including kernel size and task analysis. Text categorization is performed using these features and the extracted aspects are used as input into the CNN for training. Results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods such as support vector machines (SVMs) and logistic regression. The use of convolution allows for the extraction of features at different levels and the portability of the approach to other domains, such as the analysis of reviews for portable computers.

This work-in-progress paper proposes the incorporation of a deadline-based scheduling approach into the tasking programming model for extreme-scale parallel computing. The paper focuses on task analysis and real-time systems, as well as computational modeling and programming, in order to develop effective scheduling algorithms. The proposed method aims to improve system performance by ensuring tasks meet their deadlines while minimizing energy consumption. By incorporating this new scheduling approach, the tasking programming model could be better suited for extreme-scale parallel computing applications, where the size and complexity of the tasks can be greatly increased. Overall, this paper demonstrates the potential benefits of including deadline-based scheduling in tasking programming, and offers a promising direction for future research in this field.

In this paper, vehicle counting is investigated using various machine methods on four datasets. Vehicle counting is needed to complete the data required for short term predictions using highway traffic model, which is in turn, applicable for road design and usage planning. The goal of this research is to show that automatic car counting using machine methods, can be obtained from utilizing existing CCTV image data or from better cameras. Then by applying quantitative evaluation, F1 and precision scores are obtained, so that a few recommendations can be given. Through numerous simulations, F1 scores ranging from 0.32 to 0.75 have been successfully obtained for one low resolution dataset, using Background Subtraction and Viola Jones methods, on existing CCTV data. It has been found also that Viola Jones method can improve F1 score, by about 39% to 56%, over Back Subtraction method. Furthermore, the use of Deep Learning especially YOLO has provided good results, with F1 scores ranging from 0.94 to 1 and its precision ranges from 97.37% to 100% involving three datasets of higher resolution.

This paper focuses on the challenges of developing a hardware-in-loop model of a cage induction motor with an eccentricity fault. The mathematical model of the motor is constructed to analyze the behaviors of the motor with the fault. Induction motors are indispensable in the field of electrical engineering; however, they are prone to faults that affect their performance. A hardware-in-loop model provides the benefit of real-time testing of the motor with different fault scenarios. The development of a real-time system that enables control of the motor in real-time is one of the challenges in this project. The eccentricity fault is simulated using computational modeling to produce a fault that is observed in real life. The rotor and stator faults are also considered in this work. The developed model provides a method of detecting circuit faults and improving the performance of the motor.

This study examines the use of machine learning and a random forest algorithm to predict opioid use disorder (OUD). The research focuses on the interplay between drugs, diseases, psychology, and psychiatry that contribute to OUD. The random forest model proves to be highly sensitive in detecting OUD and thus, it is a promising tool for clinicians and researchers. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the complexity of predicting OUD and emphasizes the need for continued interdisciplinary research to better understand and address this pressing public health concern.

In disconnected wireless sensor networks (WSNs), mobile sinks can be utilized to collect data from the sensors. However, the movement of mobile sinks can result in delays and longer communication paths. In this paper, we propose a latency-aware path planning algorithm to optimize the trajectory of mobile sinks in disconnected WSNs. The algorithm takes into account the delay caused by the movement of mobile sinks and selects the optimal path to reduce the overall delay. The proposed algorithm considers the energy efficiency of the network, which is critical in WSNs, by balancing the data collection and path planning. Our simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of average delay, energy consumption, and path length. This study will contribute to the field of informatics and computer science by providing an efficient and effective solution for data collection in disconnected WSNs with mobile sinks.

This paper proposes a new distance-based coding method called Multiple Distance-Based Coding (MDBC) for scalable feature matching in large-scale web image search. MDBC aims to reduce the computational cost and storage complexity of feature encoding by using multiple distance metrics as coding strategies. The proposed method achieves this by clustering feature vectors and applying vector quantization techniques to encode them. Furthermore, MDBC uses indexes to store precomputed information for efficient retrieval of encoded features. The paper also discusses the training process for MDBC, which involves selecting an optimal set of distance metrics to use in the coding strategy. The proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, and the results show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and scalability. Finally, the paper provides a visualization of the MDBC codebook, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing diverse feature variations. Overall, MDBC is a promising method for improving feature extraction and matching in large-scale web image search.

This paper presents an efficient and secure transmission model for wireless sensor networks based on compressive sensing (CS) theory. The proposed model leverages the benefits of CS in reducing the amount of data transmission by compressing the sensor data and utilizes hash functions for secure authentication of data. The model employs encryption techniques to ensure confidentiality and integrity of the transmission, providing a robust and secure communication channel for sensor networks. The experiments conducted demonstrate that the proposed model significantly reduces energy consumption of sensor nodes, prolonging the network lifetime, while maintaining a high level of accuracy in data reconstruction. The results suggest that the proposed model could be potentially adapted for a variety of applications that require efficient and secure data communication in wireless sensor networks.

Piecewise-linear particle swarm optimizer (PPSO) is one of swarm-based optimization algorithms. Although PPSO is a deterministic particle swarm optimization (D-PSO) algorithm, its performance is better than the classical PSO's performance in solving various optimization problems. In particular, PPSO is effective in solving non-separable problems such as rotated problems. In our previous study, we have investigated that PPSO particles can move not only in a direction parallel to the coordinate axes, but also in various directions. We therefore assumed that PPSO particles do not depend on reference frame. In this paper, we analyzed that PPSO algorithm is reference frame invariant (i.e., scaling, translation, and rotational invariants) theoretically, and in order to study effectiveness of the theoretical analysis, we performed numerical experiments and clarified whether PPSO algorithm is reference frame invariant or not.

The Dexmo glove is a haptic exoskeleton that provides kinesthetic feedback in virtual reality. Unlike many other gloves based on string-pulleys, the Dexmo uses a free-hinged link-bar to transfer forces from a crank to the fingertips. It also uses an admittance-based controller parameterized by position, as opposed to an impedance-based controller parameterized by force. When setting the controller's target position, developers must use its native angular coordinate system. The Dexmo has a number of uninstrumented degrees of freedom. Mature forward models can reliably predict the hand pose, even with these unknowns. When it comes to computing angular controller parameters from a target pose in Cartesian space however, things become more difficult. Complex models that provide attractive visuals from a small number of sensors can be non-trivial or even impossible to invert. In this letter, we suggest side-stepping this issue. We sample the forward model in order to build a lookup table. This is embedded in three-dimensional space as a curve, on which traditional queries against world geometry can be performed. Controller parameters are stored as attributes of the sample points. To compute the driver parameters for a target position, the application constrains the position to the geometry, and interpolates them. This technique is generalizable, stable, simple, and fast. We validate our approach by implementing it in Unity 2017.3 and integrating it with a Dexmo glove.

Radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting is one of the promising technologies in wireless networks. This paper considers wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) where one hybrid access point (H-AP) coordinates RF energy/information transmissions to/from a set of nodes. For the important type of WPCNs where the nodes have throughput requirement, we aim to minimize H-AP's energy provision (EP) via jointly optimizing the time allocation of energy/information transmissions and H-AP's transmission power while satisfying node throughput requirement. More specifically, the half-duplex WPCN is considered first. We prove that H-AP's energy transmission power must be the maximum allowed value to achieve the minimal EP, then show that the problem is convex under this condition and finally design an algorithm applying golden section search and bisection search jointly to efficiently obtain the optimal time allocation. Second, the full-duplex WPCN is considered. Its EP minimization problem is proved convex. However, due to the hardness of solving it directly, we turn to solve the feasibility problem (FP) for a given EP per unit time. We construct a convex optimization problem based on this FP and design a dual subgradient algorithm for finding its optimal solution, which indicates whether this FP is feasible. The minimal EP per unit time and its corresponding optimal solution are found by using the bisection search method. Simulation results show that, the EP-minimized schemes are able to greatly reduce H-AP's EP as compared to the baseline schemes.

Mobile ransomware has become a rising threat, with increasing numbers of incidents where users are targeted through malicious software. To combat this issue, research has been conducted on the use of various methods such as training and prediction algorithms. In this paper, we propose the incorporation of native instructions within the software to aid in the detection of mobile ransomware. This can be achieved through the use of mathematical models and support vector machines to provide accurate results. By utilizing these features, we can better protect users from the devastating effects of ransomware attacks. Through our analysis, we have determined the potential benefits of this method, and hope to see an increase in the implementation of native instructions in future mobile security solutions.

This paper focuses on the utilization of project-based learning, predictive models, and deep learning techniques to predict bitcoin prices using Python. The study explores the use of machine learning algorithms such as support vector machines and prediction algorithms to forecast the future pricing trends of bitcoin. The research examines the historical data of bitcoin prices, the factors that influence its price fluctuations, and the limitations and challenges of predicting cryptocurrency values. The study is valuable for researchers, investors, and cryptocurrency enthusiasts as it provides insights on how to use machine learning approaches to forecast the cryptocurrency market values. The results of the study could have significant implications for predicting and managing bitcoin values. The paper concludes by identifying possible research areas for further investigation, including the development of new machine learning algorithms for cryptocurrency prediction purposes.

Broadcast-and-select local area networks (LANs) are a type of network topology that uses optical fiber networks to transmit data. These networks are characterized by the use of optical transmitters and receivers, as well as couplers, which enable the transmission and reception of signals. The network topology of broadcast-and-select LANs is such that all nodes are connected to the same central hub, which then broadcasts messages to all nodes on the network. These messages are then selectively received and acted upon by the appropriate node. The advantages of broadcast-and-select LANs include high data rates, low power consumption, and minimal electromagnetic interference. However, the implementation of such networks can be costly due to the need for specialized optical components. Despite this, the popularity of these networks is increasing rapidly as they provide a reliable and efficient means of transmitting data.

This paper examines cyber threats targeting industrial control systems (ICS) with a focus on SCADA Modbus activities. With the widespread adoption of the Internet of Things (IoT), the integration of various sensors, monitoring devices, and integrated circuits into ICS platforms has greatly increased. While this has led to greater efficiency and productivity, it has also left these systems vulnerable to cyber attacks. The use of Modbus protocols in SCADA systems has been identified as a particular weakness given its susceptibility to malicious activities. The paper argues that cyber threat investigation of SCADA Modbus activities can help identify vulnerabilities in ICS platforms and develop effective mitigation strategies to reduce risks posed by cyber threats to these critical systems. The paper suggests the adoption of IP networks and the use of advanced monitoring technologies like telescopes as proactive measures to counteract cyber threats targeting ICS platforms.

In today's industrial automation era, mobile robot plays an important role. And continuous improvement of mobile robot performance can be an important research topic. We use Matlab 2018 Simulink to simulate these results. In the paper genetic algorithm based parameters tuning for the hybrid intelligent controller design for the manipulation of the mobile robot is proposed. By way of the combination of traditional PID controller and Fuzzy Logic controller, an intelligent controller or Fuzzy PID controller is set up. Then, using Genetic Algorithm to tune the parameters of membership function of Fuzzy Logic Controller is provided so that the performance index of the mobile robot can be achieved. From simulation results it can be found that the response speed is raised and the settling time is decreased. The proposed intelligent controller is then implemented on a mobile robot to verify the superior performance of the intelligent controller.

Inexact computing generally involves trading a reduction in accuracy for an improvement in circuit area and power-consumption. The multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation is used extensively in convolutional neural networks and such applications stand to benefit greatly from the introduction of approximation to the MAC operation. This paper introduces an unsigned approximate MAC unit architecture in which approximation is introduced to both the multiplication and accumulation stages. Four variations of the proposed design are implemented using the TSMC 65 nm technology and are used in an image smoothing application. The proposed architecture is compared to that of the exact MAC unit and is shown to reduce circuit area and power-consumption by 67% and 49% respectively. When compared to other approximate MAC architectures, the proposed design improves area-power product by up to 66%.

The system grabs data packets from campus network routers, divides the collected basic data into seven basic databases, preprocesses all the basic data and preprocesses the text. Through the statistics and calculation of the data, it extracts the frequency of user browsing web pages, the frequency of using application categories, the time period of surfing the Internet, the time of surfing the Internet, the total flow of surfing the Internet, the amount of Posts and the mail. Based on the emotional dictionary, the key words of emotional features and topic features are extracted from the text information such as the content of browsing web pages and the content of posting, and the user's emotional orientation values are obtained. The obtained behavioral, emotional and topic features are stored in the feature database. Finally, through the functional test and performance test, the system can extract the daily characteristic quantity according to the daily data, get the characteristic data table, and use the characteristic data to judge the depression tendency of college students by the depression recognition and warning model.

In this paper, we investigate random access games with the cost of waiting for uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems. NOMA is a promising technology that enables multiple users to transmit their signals simultaneously over the same frequency band by allocating different power levels to each signal, without causing interference to each other. Games theory is used to model the interactions between users in this scenario. We explore the impact of using silicon carbide as a substrate material on the signal-to-noise ratio and channel estimation in NOMA systems. In addition, we propose a new decoding scheme that can improve the performance of the system. The results show that random access games can significantly improve the efficiency and fairness of uplink NOMA systems with the cost of waiting.

This paper presents a camera calibration simulation using a randomly generated spherical point distribution. The calibration process involves mathematical modeling and projective geometry to estimate the parameters of the camera's internal and external orientation. The transmission line matrix method is employed to solve the 3D positions of the points in the spherical distribution. Pose estimation is applied to determine the camera's position and orientation. Matrix decomposition is used to determine the intrinsic parameters of the camera. The simulation provides accurate calibration results and demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed method. It proves to be a useful tool for calibrating cameras in various applications.
