In this paper, we investigate various fusion methods for a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) system. Modulation recognition is a critical task in wireless communication systems, which plays a crucial role in signal identification and demodulation. The proposed CNN-based AMC system exploits deep learning techniques to classify the modulated signals accurately. The training methodology of the CNN-based AMC system is optimized to achieve better performance results in automatic modulation classification. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed fusion methods enhance the performance of the traditional CNN-based AMC system, which utilizes only a single type of feature extraction. Additionally, the proposed fusion methods demonstrate superior performance when compared with state-of-the-art AMC systems. Therefore, this paper suggests that the proposed fusion methods can improve the performance of the CNN-based AMC systems for automatic modulation classification.

This paper proposes a decoupled vector control strategy for the grid side converter, which requires less number of sensors and is capable of maintaining voltage control and load flow under imbalanced grid conditions. The mathematical model of the proposed control strategy is presented, which includes reactive power estimation for effective voltage control. The sensor systems required for this control strategy are also discussed. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is evaluated through simulations, which demonstrate its capability of maintaining voltage balance and load flow while reducing the number of sensors required. Overall, this research provides an innovative solution for improving the performance of grid side converters while minimizing the use of sensors.

This paper provides an overview and comparison of free Python libraries for data mining and big data analysis. Libraries, such as NumPy, pandas, and SciPy, are discussed and evaluated in regards to their usefulness for data science. Regression tree analysis and data visualization are also covered, as these are important tools for analyzing large datasets. Machine learning techniques, such as classification and clustering, are explored in the context of big data. Python is a versatile language that has many benefits for data mining and big data analysis, and this paper highlights the most popular libraries and tools available for these tasks. Overall, this paper is a useful resource for anyone looking to get started with data mining and big data analysis in Python.

Brain-Inspired Systems (BIS) are an emerging field of brain and intelligence sciences that studies natural intelligence models of AI and cognitive systems in one direction, and the formal models of the brain simulated by computational intelligence in another direction. A typical BIS is the cognitive robots that mimic and implement the brain through all cognitive levels. BIS provides insights for brain-machine interfaces (BMI), which may lead to novel man-machine interactions and hybrid intelligent systems. BIS may also advance classic computers from dada processors to the next generation of knowledge processors mimicking the brain. BIS will underpin a wide range of engineering paradigms such as cognitive systems, cognitive computers, cognitive robots, machine learning systems, semantic comprehension systems, big data systems, unmanned systems, self-driving vehicles and hybrid man-machine systems.

The Unrelated Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem with Sequence Dependent Setup Times (UPSDST) is a widely studied problem in the field of job shop scheduling due to its practical applications. In this paper, a mathematical model for UPSDST is proposed and genetic algorithms are utilized to solve the problem. Heuristic algorithms are also examined as a possible solution to UPSDST. The study and analysis of UPSDST has not only contributed to the foundation of job shop scheduling, but also to the fields of sociology and statistics. The difficulty of UPSDST lies in the complexity of sequencing jobs across parallel machines while considering the effect of setup times on the overall completion time. With the development of algorithms, UPSDST has become an increasingly solvable problem with practical applications in various industries.

The design and analysis of microstrip patch antennas using artificial neural networks (ANN) for terahertz application is investigated in this paper. Microstrip antennas have become popular due to their low profile, ease of manufacturing, and flexibility. The use of artificial neural networks in the design process provides a powerful tool for training microstrip patch antennas and optimizing their performance for terahertz applications. The paper explores the use of various signal processing algorithms for training the ANN model and presents the analysis of the resulting microstrip antenna performance. The potential of using ANN for designing and analyzing microstrip patch antennas in terahertz applications is demonstrated, and the results of the study show the feasibility of using ANN for optimizing antenna performance. The use of ANN in the design and analysis of microstrip patch antennas enables accurate predictions of antenna performance, and it is expected that this technology will continue to evolve and find new applications.

This paper discusses our work on using software engineering metrics (i.e., source code metrics) to classify an error message generated by a Static Code Analysis (SCA) tool as a true-positive, false-positive, or false-negative. Specifically, we compare the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forests, and Repeated Incremental Pruning to Produce Error Reduction (RIPPER) over eight datasets. The performance of the techniques is assessed by computing the F-measure metric, which is defined as the weighted harmonic mean of the precision and recall of the predicted model. The overall results of the study show that the F-measure value of the predicted model, which is generated using Random Forests technique, ranges from 83% to 98%. Additionally, the Random Forests technique outperforms the other techniques. Lastly, our results indicate that the complexity and coupling metrics have the most impact on whether a SCA tool with generate a false-positive warning or not.

This paper presents a comparative analysis of two different approaches for controlling DC-motor systems in the presence of time-delay. The first method, known as the Smith Predictor, utilizes a predictive model that takes into account the time-delay within the feedback loop. The second method, based on optimization-based controller design, aims to minimize the system's performance degradation due to the delay. The comparative analysis is carried out via computational modeling of closed-loop systems with position control. The results demonstrate that the optimization-based controller design leads to improved performance and stability, particularly in the presence of higher levels of delay. These findings suggest that the optimization-based approach may be a more effective way of controlling DC-motor systems with time-delays, providing a practical method for engineers designing such systems.

This paper proposes a log-based framework for accurately identifying the causes of system faults in software and infrastructure. The framework utilizes specialized software tools to analyze system logs generated by IP networks, servers, and computers to pinpoint the root causes of system failures, including computer bugs and other issues. By applying principles from knowledge engineering, the framework establishes a comprehensive database of fault diagnoses that can be used to improve system performance and prevent future failures. With its advanced algorithms and robust analytical capabilities, this framework is an essential tool for any organization that uses software and infrastructure systems and is looking to improve their effectiveness and reliability.

This paper presents a prototype of a home monitoring device that utilizes the Internet of Things and River Formation Dynamics-Based Multi-Hop Routing Protocol (RFDHM) to improve the efficiency and reliability of monitoring and control in smart homes. The device is equipped with robot sensing systems and wireless sensor networks that enable it to collect and process real-time data, such as temperature, humidity, and air quality. The RFDHM routing protocol is specifically designed for IoT devices and improves routing efficiency and stability by utilizing river formation dynamics. By combining these technologies, the home monitoring device can provide accurate and reliable smart home monitoring and control, offering a promising solution for the growing demand for advanced home automation systems. The proposed routing protocols are evaluated in terms of network performance and energy consumption, demonstrating their effectiveness in improving the efficiency of the home monitoring device. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the development of advanced IoT-based smart home monitoring and control systems.

Digital Screens (DS) can be considered harmful to the eyes, if used for a prolonged time, leading to such health issues as computer vision syndrome (CVS) and digital eyestrain. A wearable device able to inform the user about the time spent looking at DS could be helpful in order to suggest him the proper break timings and avoid CVS. In this study, a new Digital Screen Detection (DSD) approach using a new generation of head mounted wearable color light sensor has been proposed. Data from five subjects during common activities of daily living (ADL) in different environments (indoor, outdoor, office, meeting room) characterized by the presence of various DSs (Tablet, PC, large screen) have been acquired. The best performing machine learning algorithms already applied in a previous in-lab controlled study have been analyzed. The results showed that, in ADL context, the Random Forest algorithm reached the best accuracy in DSD with the proposed system (79.3%).

Delineation of right ventricular cavity (RVC), left ventricular myocardium (LVM) and left ventricular cavity (LVC) are common tasks in the clinical diagnosis of cardiac related diseases, especially in the basis of advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques. Recently, despite deep learning techniques being widely employed in solving segmentation tasks in a variety of medical images, the sheer volume and complexity of the data in some applications such as cine cardiac MRI pose significant challenges for the accurate and efficient segmentation. In cine cardiac MRI we need to segment both short and long axis 2D images. In this paper, we focus on the automated segmentation of short-axis cardiac MRI images. We first introduce the deep layer aggregation (DLA) method to augment the standard deep learning architecture with deeper aggregation to better fuse information across layers, which is particularly suitable for the cardiac MRI segmentation, due to the complexity of the cardiac boundaries appearance and acquisition resolution during a cardiac cycle. In our solution, we develop a modified DLA framework by embedding Refinement Residual Block (RRB) and Channel Attention Block (CAB). Experimental results validate the superior performance of our proposed method for the cardiac structures segmentation in comparison with state-of-the-art. Moreover, we demonstrate its potential use case in the quantitative analysis of cardiac dyssynchrony.

This paper discusses the design of ducted propulsors for towing autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), using propellers with specific geometries to optimize their performance. A mathematical model is developed to calculate the required torque to drive the propeller, taking into account the effects of the ducts on the flow field. Computational modeling is employed to validate the performance of the ducted propulsors, and the results indicate significant improvements in terms of thrust and efficiency. The study also explores the impact of different payloads on the performance of the AUV and the propulsors, highlighting the need to design for a wide range of operating conditions. Overall, this research improves our understanding of the design and optimization of ducted propulsors for towing AUVs, with implications for a variety of oceanographic applications.

In this paper, we propose a new model for the multi-objective multiple allocation hub network design and routing problem which contains determining the location of hubs, the design of hub network, and the routing of commodities between source-destination pairs in the given network. The selected hubs are not assumed to be fully connected, and each node and arc in the network has capacity constraints. The multiple objectives of the problem are the minimization of total fixed and transportation costs and the minimization of the maximum travel time required for routing. We propose a mathematical formulation for the multi-objective problem and present a meta-heuristic solution based on a well-known multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. Using the proposed formulation, we are able to find the optimal solution for small networks of five nodes and seven nodes. To evaluate the performance of our heuristic approach on real data, the computational experiments are conducted on Turkish postal system data set. The results demonstrate that our heuristic approach can find feasible solutions to the problem in reasonable execution time, which is less than 10 min.

Cloud computing and big data have risen to become the most popular technologies of the modern world. Apparently, the reason behind their immense popularity is their wide range of applicability as far as the areas of interest are concerned. Education and research remain one of the most obvious and befitting application areas. This research paper introduces a big data analytics tool, PABED (Project - Analyzing Big Education Data), for the education sector that makes use of cloud-based technologies. This tool is implemented using Google BigQuery and R programming language and allows comparison of undergraduate enrollment data for different academic years. Although, there are many proposed applications of big data in education, there is a lack of tools that can actualize the concept into practice. PABED is an effort in this direction. The implementation and testing details of the project have been described in this paper. This tool validates the use of cloud computing and big data technologies in education and shall head start development of more sophisticated educational intelligence tools.

In this paper, an energy efficient transport protocol is proposed to enhance the traffic capacity of complex networks. The new algorithm is derived on the basis of router betweenness centrality, which gives an estimate of traffic handled by the node as router. As one bottleneck node will degrade the traffic performance of the whole network, the improved routing aims to bypass nodes with heavy load to diminish the congestion. Particularly, depending on a parameter that controls the optimization scale, the new transport protocol can achieve smaller average path length while guaranteeing the required packet generation rate. Comparing results of previous routing strategies, it is shown that the presented improved routing strategy performs more effectively.

This paper presents a method for detecting hidden streaming cameras in indoor environments using simultaneous observation by multiple mobile handsets. The proposed method leverages the use of wireless fidelity and streaming media technologies to enable real-time monitoring in diverse settings. Feature extraction and timing analysis are employed to detect and correlate the similarity of video streams and identify the source of possible hidden cameras. Tests conducted in a workplace setting demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method in detecting streaming cameras, with detection accuracy reaching 93%. The proposed method is a promising solution for detecting hidden streaming cameras in indoor environments and can contribute to enhancing privacy and security.

A low-power and stable “static-type” neural network (NN) circuit based on CMOS and resistive synaptic devices was developed and evaluated. The circuit is composed of a comparator as a firing function for binary output, current sources, cross switches for inputs, and variable resistors for synaptic weights. Nonlinearity analysis of operating points in such circuits was performed in terms of the types of current sources and the resistance-change ratios of the variable resistors. The operation window to realize both operation stability and low power consumption of less than 1 mW for 1024 synapses was thus clarified. To improve the NN performance, memristive synaptic devices with WOx/MgO were fabricated and characterized in terms of spike-timing-dependent plasticity and nonlinear switching for learning.

Applying deep learning for medical imaging classification suffers from limited labeled data, especially for those relying on biopsy proven labels. In this work we approach this challenge by leveraging other available datasets with focus on answering what dataset can be used, and how to use them optimally. An application was considered, classifying benign or malignant colonic polyps given colonoscopy narrow-band imaging (NBI). Experiments were conducted with 5 auxiliary datasets with various characteristics, and multiple training schemes involving transfer learning, multitask learning (MTL) with a DenseNet backbone. Results consistently suggest an optimal scheme of MTL initialized from ImageNet pretrain model and followed by fine tuning on the main task. An auxiliary dataset helps better if it's not only similar in terms of imaging mechanism or fine-grained variability, but also easy to train itself. A NBI classifier trained with such scheme and auxiliary dataset improved accuracy from 62.6% (baseline without using other dataset) to 70.7% with performance on par with 5 human experts.

The aim of this project is to develop an efficient event-driven wireless sensor nodes based network for an effective and power efficient monitoring of plants health and larva population in a remote crop field. In this framework, an event-driven approach is proposed to detect larva and measure other system parameters like Acoustic Complexity Index (ACI), temperature, humidity and soil moisture. The sensors' data is collected by the front end event-driven sensing node, developed with a STM32F407VG board, via a serial port. The STM32F407VG board is based on the ARM processor. In contrast to the clock driven classical sensing nodes, the devised sensing nodes only acquire and transmits the sensors data in the case of a significant change. It significantly reduces the power consuming data acquisition and transmission activity as compared to the classical solutions. It improves the proposed solution power efficiency and autonomy as compared to the counter classical ones. The data from the node is transmitted to a base station by using a wireless ZigBee interface. The base station collects data from a group of event-driven sensing nodes. This data is transmitted to the Central Processing Unit (CPU) via the USB liaison between the base station and the CPU. On CPU this data is analyzed via the MATLAB based specifically developed application. The findings are displayed and logged on the CPU. It allows the terminal user to access this and to achieve a timely interaction and cure of the intended crop field. The system parameters are adjusted in order to achieve the effective modules integration and performance. The proposed system operation is validated with an experimental setup. Results have shown a promising system realization.

Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is a commonly implemented method in brain computer interfaces (BCIs). The traditional pattern flip paradigm has the disadvantages of easy to fatigue and high stimulation intensity. In the application of brain-controlled virtual reality(VR) systems, there are many problems such as limited by devices and the paradigm induced effect was not good. In this paper, we propose a new SSVEP-BCI paradigm based on illusory pattern motion perception. Using the basic principle of pattern peripheral drift illusion, the visual motion stimulation effect is alternately presented in double-frame graphics, and the accurate SSVEP induction effect. The brain activate degree is greater and the functional connection is stronger. The experimental results show that the new paradigm adaptability is an effective SSVEP-BCI paradigm, and it is not easy to fatigue. It can be applied to brain-controlled virtual reality system and other human-computer interactive systems.

This paper proposes a new method for accurate set-based state estimation for nonlinear discrete-time systems using differential inequalities with model redundancy. The mathematical model is based on the concept of polytopic differential inclusions and differential inequalities. By utilizing both prediction algorithms and face set computations, the proposed method is able to accurately estimate the system state even when there is uncertainty or noise present in the system. The approach is evaluated on a range of discrete-time systems using computational modeling, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The main advantage of this approach over other methods is the use of model redundancy, which allows for more accurate state estimation and provides a backup in case of failure of the primary estimation algorithm. Overall, this paper offers a new and promising approach for accurate state estimation in nonlinear discrete-time systems.

This paper proposes a solution for train localization by using unscented Kalman filters based multi sensors fusion. With the advent of sensor systems and the increased use of IP networks in rail transportation, sensor fusion has become a popular method for improving train localization accuracy. One of the most widely used approaches for sensor fusion is the Kalman filter. However, traditional Kalman filters are not suitable for non-linear systems. In this paper, we use the unscented Kalman filter, a variant of the Kalman filter that can cope with non-linear systems, to fuse data from multiple sensors. Moreover, we introduce a heuristic algorithm to improve the performance of the unscented Kalman filter. The proposed method is validated using real-world data and the results show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of localization accuracy.

This paper proposes a CUSUM-based joint jammer detection and localization approach for wireless sensor networks (WSNs) in dynamic spectrum access environments. Jamming is a significant problem in wireless communication systems where jamming signals interfere with legitimate communication signals. In dynamic spectrum access, where available frequencies are constantly changing, this problem is even more severe. In this context, the proposed approach combines sensor fusion and CUSUM-based detection to identify and locate jammers. The approach utilizes both receiver and transmitter sensors in WSNs to increase the accuracy of detection and location. Results show that the proposed approach can outperform existing jammer detection algorithms in accuracy and robustness. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating statistical and sensing techniques for improving the reliability of WSNs in challenging environments.

Satellite image semantic segmentation, including extracting road, detecting building, and identifying land cover types, is essential for sustainable development, agriculture, forestry, urban planning, and climate change research. Nevertheless, it is still unclear how to develop a refined semantic segmentation model in an efficient and elegant way. In this paper, we propose attention dilation-LinkNet (AD-LinkNet) neural network that adopts encoder–decoder structure, serial–parallel combination dilated convolution, channel-wise attention mechanism, and pretrained encoder for semantic segmentation. Serial–parallel combination dilated convolution enlarges receptive field as well as assemble multi-scale features for multi-scale objects, such as long-span road and small pool. The channel-wise attention mechanism is designed to advantage the context information in the satellite image. The experimental results on road extraction and surface classification data sets prove that the AD-LinkNet shows a significant effect on improving the segmentation accuracy. We defeated the D-Linknet algorithm that won the first place in the CVPR 2018 DeepGlobe road extraction competition.

This paper proposes a neuro-sliding control approach for the online compensation of disturbances that affect remotely operated underwater vehicles (ROVs). The proposed approach is inspired by biological neural networks and utilizes a backpropagation algorithm to continuously adapt and adjust the control parameters of the ROV's instruments and tools. The neuro-sliding control approach offers improved robustness, adaptability, and precision over traditional control methods, especially in the unpredictable and dynamic environment of the Earth's oceans. The results of simulations and experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in compensating for disturbances and improving the overall performance of ROVs. This research has significant implications for the fields of ocean exploration and underwater resource exploitation, where the success of mission-critical activities depends on the reliability and efficiency of ROVs.

We demonstrate a compact polarization decoding module with the size of 2 cm × 2 cm × 1 cm for a free space quantum key distribution based on micro-optics. The insertion loss and polarization extinction ratio (PER) of this module are <;4.6dB and >22.8 dB, respectively, and large alignment tolerance is achieved owing to multimode fiber pigtailing. The quantum bit error rate (QBER) are measured to be 0.67% with the sifted key rate of 576 kb/s at the clock rate of 100 MHz.

This paper proposes a deep cross-view convolutional feature approach for view-invariant action recognition. The proposed method extracts features from multiple views of action videos, and utilizes correlation and convolution operations to align the extracted features across different views. Covariance matrices are then computed to capture the statistical relationships among the aligned features, which are combined to generate view-invariant action representations. The experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance, indicating its effectiveness in handling the view variability problem. The proposed approach also has potential applications in other related fields such as surveillance, robotics, and human-computer interaction. This work was presented at several international conferences and published in high-impact journals, which demonstrates the recognition and impact of this research direction. The proposed approach has advantages over existing methods as it does not require camera calibration or the assumption of a specific camera setup.

This study aimed to determine the constitutive equation of BEOL Aluminum-Copper (Al-Cu) using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation and Response Surface Methodology (RSM). A mathematical model was developed to describe the behavior of the Al-Cu material under different strains and stresses. The model was then incorporated into a FEA simulation to obtain the mechanical response of the material. Plastics were included in the computational modeling to capture the true behavior of the Al-Cu material. RSM was used to optimize the parameters of the model and improve accuracy. The results showed that the constitutive equation of BEOL Al-Cu material can be accurately described using the developed mathematical model and FEA simulation. This approach can be useful in semiconductor device modeling and other fields that require accurate material modeling.

In recent years, the explosive growth of data has led to the development of Big Data analytic techniques for various applications, including Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). An IDS is a critical component of cybersecurity infrastructure that monitors the network traffic and identifies potential threats such as malware, viruses, and unauthorized access attempts. Traditional IDS systems are no longer sufficient in detecting the sophisticated, multi-vector attacks that take place at high speeds in modern networks. The emergence of Big Data analytic techniques using Machine Learning (ML) and advanced data models such as Predictive models and Anomaly detection have greatly improved IDS systems' effectiveness. These techniques enable the IDS to learn and adapt to changes in the network environment, making it possible to detect previously unknown and fast-evolving threats, reducing the false positive rate and improving the overall security of the network. This paper explores the state-of-the-art in Big Data analytics for IDS, analyzes the advantages and limitations of different data models, and provides recommendations for designing a more effective IDS system.

This work implements a hydrodynamic model-based localization and navigation system for low-cost autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) that are limited to a micro-electro mechanical system (MEMS) inertial measurement unit (IMU). The hydrodynamic model of this work is uniquely developed to directly determine the linear velocities of the vehicle using the measured vehicle angular rates and propeller speed as inputs. The proposed system was tested in the field using a fleet of low-cost Bluefin SandShark AUVs. Implementation of the model-based localization system and fusing of the solution into the vehicle navigation loop was conducted using backseat computers of the AUV fleet that run mission orientated operating suite -interval programming (MOOS-IvP). With the model-based navigation system, the maximum localization error (i.e., in comparison to a long baseline (LBL) based ground-truth position) was limited to 15 m and 30 m for two 650-second and 1070-second long missions. Extrapolation of the position drift shows that the model-based localization system is able to limit the position uncertainty to less than 100 m by the end of hour-long mission; whereas, the drift in the default IMU-based localization solution was over 1 km per hour. This is a considerable improvement by only using a MEMS IMU that generally costs less than $100. Furthermore, this work is a step towards generalizing and automating the process of hydrodynamic modeling, model parameter estimation and data fusion (i.e., fusing the localization solution with those from other available aiding sensors and feeding to the navigation loop) so that a model-based localization system can be implemented in any AUV that has backseat computing capability.

The emergence of cloud computing technology has led to a new paradigm in mobile computing where mobile handsets can be integrated with cloud resources to enable dynamic and on-demand sharing of resources. However, security remains a major concern in this model, especially in scenarios where mobile handsets need to access cloud resources through untrusted networks. In this paper, we present SMCACC, a novel dynamic secure framework that leverages cloud computing to enable mobile capabilities augmentation. Our approach uses computational modeling to optimize resource allocation and encryption techniques to ensure secure data transmission. Experiment results show that SMCACC achieves high efficiency and security in dynamic mobile-cloud environments.

Construction of an Input-Output Table Considering Business-to-Consumer Transactions by using Private Data is a paper discussing the construction of an input-output table that takes into account business-to-consumer transactions using private data. The paper focuses on the use of private data of companies in order to achieve better estimation in the construction industry. The authors suggest that data models and intelligent systems can be used to create a comprehensive database that will enable the collection of private data. The paper argues that the use of private data will lead to better estimations of consumer expenditure patterns, which will improve the accuracy of input-output tables. The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of accurate input-output tables in improving economic policymaking.

This paper proposes an embedded system design for visual scene classification, which entails the extraction and analysis of image features using histograms and support vector machines. The system utilizes cameras to capture images and computer vision techniques to process the data. The visualization of the analyzed features provides insights into the classification process and allows for the refinement of the classification algorithm. The system is designed to be efficient and lightweight, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The proposed design has potential applications in a wide range of fields, from surveillance to agriculture. Overall, the system represents a significant advancement in embedded system design for visual scene classification, providing a powerful tool for analyzing and interpreting images.

Time-series classification has always been a challenging task in computational modeling, where the accuracy of classification strongly depends on the feature extraction approach that is used. In this paper, the authors propose the use of Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) for time series analysis and classification. FCMs are widely used in biological system modeling due to their ability to represent complex relationships between variables. The authors apply FCMs to the task of classifying time-series data and compare their results to other standard approaches. Their results demonstrate that FCMs improve classification accuracy by explicitly modeling the relationships between features, and the authors conclude that FCMs are a promising alternative to current standards for time-series classification.

This paper focuses on the application of deep learning in the field of coherent MU-SIMO detection in fading channels. The aim is to develop unsupervised deep learning solutions that achieve high accuracy and robustness in the detection of signals transmitted in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems. The proposed approach leverages the use of receivers with a deep learning-based architecture to perform signal detection without the need for explicit training data. The paper also discusses the complexity theory associated with such deep learning-based solutions and highlights the benefits offered by employing unsupervised learning techniques in the context of MIMO communication systems. Overall, the results presented in this paper demonstrate the potential of deep learning to address the challenges associated with coherent MU-SIMO detection in fading channels.

Drug behavior in the body is described by using pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) models. Relationship between the drug behavior and elapsed time is complicated, and even a nonlinear regression algorithm is not easy to be applied to the identification of the relationship. In this paper, the PK/PD model is simplified for the purpose of facilitating the identification. A logistic model and a Gompertz growth model are analytically derived by applying the perturbation method to the PK/PD model which is based on the 3-compartment model. The simplified models are applied to the identification of clinical data, and it is confirmed that the errors from the PK/PD model are less than 5 %. The new models are simpler than the PK/PD model and easier to be identified. They make it possible to predict the transition of the drug effects and to be applicable to the automatic correction of affected biosignals, and so on.

This paper proposes a Geometric Adaptive Control strategy for a Quadrotor UAV that is capable of rejecting wind disturbance. The research focuses on the aerodynamics, rotors, blades, and vehicle dynamics of the quadrotor. Neural networks are used for modeling and control of the system, with particular attention paid to torque and drag. By exploiting the full dynamics of the quadrotor, this control strategy aims to improve stability and robustness, particularly in the presence of external disturbances. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller significantly improves the robustness of the quadrotor, with the wind disturbance rejection capability superior to that of traditional PID controllers. This work provides a step towards the development of more reliable, autonomous flying vehicles capable of safe and efficient operation in various environments.

This paper proposes an artificial intelligent-based method for fault diagnosis in a modular multi-level converter system. Circuit faults that occur in the system, such as open circuits, are diagnosed using signal processing algorithms and artificial neural networks. The diagnosis process involves monitoring the capacitors of the faulty submodule and analyzing the resulting data using a mathematical model. Field programmable gate arrays are used to implement the proposed fault diagnosis method, which is shown to be effective in detecting and diagnosing single-submodule open-circuit faults. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is highly accurate and reliable, and it can be applied to various modular multi-level converter systems.

The growing interest in Internet of Things (IoT) and 5G mobile communication has spurred a need for improved satellite communication networks. Low earth orbit (LEO) satellites have emerged as an alternative to traditional geostationary satellites due to their lower latency and cost-effectiveness. In this study, we analyze the traffic patterns of LEO satellite IoT networks and investigate the potential business opportunities arising from their deployment. By examining the various orbits utilized by LEO satellites, we argue that fine-tuning their parameters can help optimize both network performance as well as business returns. Our findings suggest that LEO satellite IoT networks have the potential to bridge the digital divide, revolutionize various industries, and unlock new markets in remote and rural areas.

Reversible computing is so far the only way to circumvent the Landauer limit of CPU power efficiency, thus has attracted more and more attention recently due to its prospect in energy-efficient computing. To make reversible computing possible, much ground work needs to be studied, especially on reversible algorithms. We focus on designing reversible shortest path algorithms in this paper.

Leucorrhea routine is a common way of female physiological examination, which is detected by recognizing and counting the visible components in microscopic images. At present, the research in this field is still blank. Based on the deep learning theory, an improved R-CNN model is proposed to realize the intelligent recognition of the visible components in leucorrhea microscopic images. The detection precision of the algorithm is high, reaching 93.6%, and the detection time is 300 ms. The proposed algorithm provides a theoretical basis for the realization of leucorrhea routine automation and intellectualization.

In computer science, consensus theory has been studied for decades. “Consensus” in a multi-agent system means reaching an agreement regarding a certain quantity of interest. The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a promising topology for medium- and high-power applications owing to its salient features. In MMC operation, one key point is to regulate the capacitor voltage of each submodule (SM). The SMs in MMCs are interconnected both physically and via a control system, and these SMs can be regarded as a multi-agent system, with the control objective of regulating their capacitor voltages, which could formulate a consensus problem. In this paper, through mathematical derivation, it is found that individual capacitor voltage regulation control of phase-shifted-carrier pulse-width modulation (PSC-PWM) MMC is one special case of consensus theory. Furthermore, based on the consensus theory, the influence of different communication structures on the MMC voltage regulation performance is discussed. The analysis proves that the existing one has the highest rate of convergence. The impact of current-tracking dynamics on consensus-based interpretation is also analyzed. In addition, the proportional relationship between the rate of convergence and the P controller parameter is also justified. The experiments on a seven-level down-scaled prototype are conducted to confirm the analysis.

The goal of any facility layout problem is proper arrangement of facilities without overlapping. Most of facility layout problems are two-dimensional and single-floor. In this study, facility layout problem is considered in three-dimensional and multi-floor. This will increase the flexibility of the problem. Also, many of layout problems are deterministic, while it is possible that parameters of the problem can be changeable. Therefore, robust planning should be used in overlapping constraints. We develop a mathematical model considering some flexible assumptions. In order to measure the validity of the model, we solve some examples using the appropriate software. Computational experiments show that the objective function of mathematical model increases by considering flexibility in parameters.

A mobile-based virtual try-on system is proposed to deal with the problems of high cost and conflicts between computational complexity and simulation effects. In this paper, several modules are included, such as automatic 3D face reconstruction based on a single image, auto-skinning and realtime local simulation of cloth. According to the experiments, the virtual try-on system introduced in this paper is able to achieve better fitting effects with lower constructing and computing costs, in which case good experience of mobile-based virtual try-on system is provided.

The development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has brought about a growing demand for accurate and efficient data reduction techniques in IoT nodes. In this paper, we propose a new approach to enhance the accuracy of the Shewhart-based data reduction method using piggybacking, by incorporating temperature measurement and interpolation techniques. We also incorporate prediction algorithms and explore the impact of battery limitations on data reduction. The proposed approach is based on complexity theory, which provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the behavior of wireless sensor networks in IoT. Our experimental results show that the proposed approach improves the accuracy of data reduction in IoT nodes and reduces battery consumption, making it a promising technique for data reduction in real-world IoT applications. We conclude that the proposed approach contributes to the advancement of data reduction techniques for IoT and provides a foundation for future research in this field.

The automatic segmentation of prostatic zones from T2-weighted MRI is critical for the planning and medical treatment of prostate cancer. In this study, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed for the automatic segmentation of prostate zones. The trained CNN can accurately segment the prostate gland into its corresponding regions, such as peripheral zone (PZ), transition zone (TZ), and central gland (CG). Additionally, a new patient-individual PI-Rads v2 sector map is suggested to improve the accuracy of segmentation. The proposed method achieves a high Dice similarity coefficient and classification accuracy compared to the manual segmentation of experts. This research has great potential in enhancing the efficiency and precision of prostate cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. In the future, it could be extended to other medical imaging segments and provide valuable insights into medical image segmentation in general.

The H2020 project 5G-DRIVE (5G HarmoniseD Research and TrIals for serVice Evolution between EU and China) cooperates with the Chinese twin project to trial and validate key functions of 5G networks operating at 3.5 GHz bands for enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and 3.5 GHz and 5.9 GHz bands for V2X scenarios. 5G-DRIVE will instil significant impact on the validation of standards and trigger the roll-out of real 5G networks and V2X innovative solutions driving new business opportunities and creating thereby new jobs and brand new business models. This paper presents the overall approach of 5G-DRIVE, the advances beyond the current state of the art for key 5G enabling technologies, as well as the considered use cases.

Cricket is a popular sport among a vast audience worldwide. With the advent of technology, there has been an increase in generating online cricket videos. However, as the amount of video content grows, it becomes difficult for people to watch each one of them. In this context, automatic cricket video summarization has gained significant attention. This paper proposes a multimodal approach for automatic cricket video summarization. The approach utilizes several techniques such as optical character recognition software, hidden Markov models, semantics, feature extraction, and cameras to extract relevant information from cricket videos. The proposed approach integrates different modalities such as audio, visual, and textual information to generate a comprehensive cricket video summary. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and effectiveness. Therefore, this work opens new doors for generating accurate and timely summaries of cricket videos, which can enable viewers to quickly and easily access relevant information about their favorite games.

It is difficult to realize the effective separation of signal and noise in the vibration signals, owing to the traditional signal filtering method. This paper puts forward an algorithm which was based on Hasudorff distance and nonlocal means (Hasudorff-Non Local Means, HDNLM). This algorithm makes use of Hasudorff distance more efficient than Euclidean distance distance in preserving signal details. It is aim to improve the weight model of traditional NLM of Euclidean Distance. Experimental and simulation show that: The improved NLM is superior than the simple morphology, traditional NLM, and db8 wave transform in the noise denoising of vibration signal aspect. The newly method is combined with the power spectral density, and it is well applied in the fault feature extraction of on-load tap changers.

In this paper, we propose a perspective-aware loss function for crowd density estimation, which aims to improve the accuracy of crowd counting in images with varying levels of distortion caused by perspective. The proposed method incorporates a kernel function into the training process to enhance feature extraction and adaptively adjust the loss function based on the perspective distortion. The adaptive system facilitates the generation of an appropriate weight matrix for each location in the density map, which effectively adjusts for the differences in layouts of different images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in crowd counting accuracy, particularly in images with severe perspective distortion. Our method can be used in various real-world scenarios, such as surveillance and crowd management.

We address the problem of attack detection and isolation for a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems under (potentially unbounded) sensor attacks and measurement noise. We consider the case when a subset of sensors is subject to additive false data injection attacks. Using a bank of observers, each observer leading to an Input-to-State Stable (ISS) estimation error, we propose two algorithms for detecting and isolating sensor attacks. These algorithms make use of the ISS property of the observers to check whether the trajectories of observers are "consistent" with the attack-free trajectories of the system. Simulations results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

To ensure undisrupted web-based services, operators need to closely monitor various KPIs (Key Performance Indicator, such as CPU usages, network throughput, page views, number of online users, and etc), detect anomalies in them, and trigger timely troubleshooting or mitigation. There can be hundreds of thousands to even millions of KPIs to be monitored, thus operators need automatic anomaly detection approaches. However, neither traditional statistical approaches nor supervised ensemble approaches satisfy this requirement in practice when facing large number of KPIs. A state-of-art unsupervised approach Donut offering promising results, but it is not a sequential model thus cannot deal with the time information related anomalies. Thus, in this paper we propose Bagel, a robust and unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm for KPI that can handle time information related anomalies, using CVAE to incorporate time information and dropout layer to avoid overfitting. Our experiments using real data from Internet companies show that, compared to Donut, Bagel improves the anomaly detection best F1-score by 0.08 to 0.43.

Cloud-loT Applications consist of thousands of smart devices sending sensor data to processing cloud applications. If the processing rate of the cloud application is limited it may be unable to cope with an increasing number of connected devices. If such a situation is not addressed, the cloud application is overloaded with messages, resulting in a high processing delay or loss of data. For this reason we propose a TCP-inspired congestion avoidance which reconfigures the send rate of devices at runtime aiming for a low processing delay and a high throughput. We show, that it is able to avoid congestions by adapting the send rate of devices to a fair share of the processing rate of the cloud application.

This paper proposes an I/O efficient distributed approximation framework using cluster sampling. The framework is designed to estimate the characteristics of large amounts of data efficiently by distributing the computation to a cluster of computers. The implementation of the framework is based on the Linux operating system and the use of smart phones as data sensors in urban areas. The framework employs probabilistic logic and sampling methods to produce estimates with high accuracy, while minimizing the amount of data that needs to be transferred between the computers. The proposed framework is shown to be effective in estimating various characteristics of large amounts of data, such as traffic flow and air pollution levels, in urban areas. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework to be used in a wide range of applications that require the estimation of large amounts of data in an I/O efficient manner.

This paper explores the relationship between emotions and the structure of language, specifically focusing on grammar and natural language processing. By examining the ways in which cognition and psychology influence the ways in which we use language to express emotions, the authors argue that emotions play a crucial role in shaping the rules and conventions of syntax and grammar. This leads to important implications for the field of natural language processing, which must take into account the nuances and complexities of emotional expression in order to accurately understand and classify texts. Additionally, this paper also examines the use of matrix converters and tagging in accident analysis, highlighting the potential benefits of incorporating emotional cues into these analytical tools in order to more effectively assess the psychological and emotional impact of traumatic events. Overall, this paper contributes to a growing body of research on the intersection of emotions, cognition, and language- shedding new light on the ways in which these factors shape our communication and understanding of the world around us.

This paper explores the application of the Grey Wolf Hunting Mechanism (GWHP) to improve Brain Storm Optimization (BSO) in the field of optimization. BSO is a popular heuristic algorithm used to solve complex problems in various disciplines, including sociology and statistics. The GWHP is a meta-heuristic algorithm inspired by the social behavior of wolves, which has been shown to have powerful convergence properties. By incorporating the GWHP into the BSO algorithm, the authors show that the resulting approach outperformed several traditional optimization and clustering algorithms in benchmark testing. The proposed algorithm is particularly effective in solving problems where the search space is high-dimensional or complex.

We propose a model-based deep learning architecture for the correction of phase errors in multishot diffusion-weighted echo-planar MRI images. This work is a generalization of MUSSELS, which is a structured low-rank algorithm. We show that an iterative reweighted least-squares implementation of MUSSELS resembles the model-based deep learning (MoDL) framework. We propose to replace the self-learned linear filter bank in MUSSELS with a convolutional neural network, whose parameters are learned from exemplary data. The proposed algorithm reduces the computational complexity of MUSSELS by several orders of magnitude, while providing comparable image quality.

Modern career guidance is a complex and multifaceted field that encompasses a broad range of issues related to the safety, training, personnel, psychology, industrial facilities, task analysis, and industries. Career guidance seeks to provide individuals with the knowledge, skills, and resources necessary to make informed decisions about their career paths and to navigate the challenges and opportunities that arise throughout their working lives. One of the primary concerns in modern career guidance is ensuring the safety of employees in the workplace, particularly in industries where hazards are common. Training and development programs are also critical in preparing workers for their roles, while personnel management strategies can help to motivate and retain talented individuals. Psychological factors such as personality type and aptitude can have a significant impact on an individual's career success, and career guidance professionals use a range of tools and techniques to assess these factors and provide guidance accordingly. Other important aspects of career guidance include the analysis of tasks and work processes, as well as the identification of emerging trends and issues in specific industries. Overall, modern career guidance plays a critical role in helping individuals to achieve their career goals and maximize their potential in today's rapidly evolving job market.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is profoundly influencing our daily lives in many areas, covering small devices to large network systems. An IoT system may be a set of directing rules that rearranges the usage of IoT applications. This paper details a trust management model and security of IoT systems. Trust management models and security play a critical part in IoT to protect information and devices from attacks since it supplies security for all layers and networks. This review focuses on how a trust management model has a significant function in IoT in enhancing reliability, privacy, and security. In this survey, we explained the challenges along with the solutions in terms of IoT security and privacy and recognized the main security problem in the IoT framework. In addition, this paper explored the characteristics of trust and pointed out some IoT security challenges, explaining how middleware can affect the security of IoT.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are adopted in a variety of fields where coverage enhancing is a critical challenge because of the requirements of service quality, cost, and energy consumption. Coverage-enhancing approaches have currently attracted a lot of interest owing to their superior abilities in the deployment of the WSNs, e.g., maximum coverage, minimum sensors, and minimum energy. In this paper, a differential evolution-based regional coverage-enhancing algorithm is proposed for directional 3D WSNs, which is able to maximizing coverage while minimize the number of sensors. First, a directional cone perception model is designed to better display the actual sensing performance of sensor nodes. Subsequently, the coverage region is established to describe the perceptual range of nodes. Thereafter, a three-stage coverage-enhancing method is derived, which includes the pitch angle optimization, the deflection angle optimization and the redundant node sleeping. These strategies are designed to maximize the perception range of a single sensor node, maximize the coverage rate, and minimize the number of nodes, respectively. Finally, simulation results show that our method is able to ensure better performance compared to the state-of-the-art frameworks.

Bilinear Supervised Hashing (BSH) is a powerful technique for 2D image feature extraction, which is used to generate binary codes for efficient image retrieval. In BSH, 2D displays are mapped to binary codes via feature extraction and kernelization. Linear programming is then used to optimize the mapping process and learn the optimal binary codes. The key advantage of BSH is that it can incorporate supervised information in the learning process, ensuring that the semantic similarity of images is preserved in the binary codes. This makes it particularly useful for image retrieval tasks where semantic similarity is essential. In this paper, we review the existing literature on BSH and explore its potential applications in different learning systems. We also discuss various optimization techniques that can be used to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of BSH. Our analysis shows that BSH is a promising technique for 2D image feature extraction and binary code generation, and has the potential to facilitate efficient image retrieval in a wide range of applications.

This paper presents a study on the development of a distribution network line level evaluation model. The model is based on dynamic classification combination and utilizes various algorithms including heuristic, classification, clustering, decision trees, and partitioning algorithms. The study focuses on training and modeling of the model to develop accurate predictions. The proposed model has potential applications in the optimization of distribution network operations and to improve efficiency. The results of this study indicate that the proposed model is effective in accurately evaluating distribution network line levels. Further optimization of the proposed model can be achieved by incorporating additional algorithms and conducting further comprehensive testing. Overall, this study presents a novel approach to developing a distribution network evaluation model that has the potential to be widely applied in practical situations.

We describe a methodology for extracting and identifying pores in high resolution fingerprint digital images. The key strategy is based on an image subtraction between two fingerprint images with different smoothness levels. The anisotropic diffusion filter is employed to obtain such smoothed fingerprints, in which the pores are preserved in the first fingerprint, while the second one only presents ridges and valleys, but pores are blurred. The subtraction procedure results in a difference image, in which the pores are characterized by the lower magnitudes. After that, we perform a histogram equalization for enhancing pores and a global thresholding to obtain the pores as binary regions. Finally, such binary image is post-processed for removing false pore detections. Experiments were conducted using the PolyU HRF fingerprint image set and the results showed that the proposed methodology outperformed other filtered-based pore extraction methods considering the true and false pore detection rates.

This paper proposes a novel approach, called Error Backpropagation with Attention Control (EBAC), to learn imbalanced data for regression. The method combines the traditional backpropagation algorithm with attention mechanisms, which enable the model to selectively focus on the informative features of the input data. To further improve the performance, EBAC utilizes filtering algorithms and information filters to preprocess the training data, enhancing the discriminative power of the model. In experiments, the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art regression algorithms on multiple benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of using attention mechanisms and information filters in training neural networks for imbalanced data regression tasks.

Self-driving cars are becoming popular topics in academia. Consumers of self-driving cars and vehicles have different concerns, for example, safety and security, to name a few. Also, the public sector has interests in self-driving cars such as amending policies to enable the management of self-driving vehicles in cities, urban planning, traffic management and, etc. In this paper, more than 2700 corpus are extracted from literature from several subject areas to identify latent (hidden) topics of self-driving cars. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is used for topic identification. The result of this study shows that topics identified are valid research areas such as urban planning, driver car (computer) interaction, self-driving control and system design, ethics in self-driving cars, safety and risk assessment, training dataset quality and machine learning in self-driving cars are among the topics identified. Furthermore, the network visualization of association graph of terms shows that the most frequently discussed concepts reveal that control of self-driving cars is based on algorithms, data, design, method, and model. The methods used in this study and the results can be used as decision tools, if carefully applied, in diverse disciplines that are disrupted by the introduction of self-driving cars. For future study, we plan to extend this study with a larger dataset and other data mining techniques.

Automatic seizure detection has been often treated as a classification problem that aims at determining the label of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals by computer science, as the EEG monitoring is a helpful adjunct to the diagnosis of epilepsy. In most existing work, the traditional signal energy of the EEG has been applied for classification, since the energy pattern of epileptic seizures differs from that of non-seizures. Although they are effective, the accuracy either heavily depends on additional information besides energy or is limited by the shortcoming of energy-based features. To address this issue, the proposed approach achieves the classification based on the instantaneous energy of the EEG signals instead. The proposed approach first measures the instantaneous energy related to changes in the EEG signals. Then, energy behavior over time is characterized by instantaneous energy-based features from different aspects. Finally, the classification is carried out on the features to produce output labels. By processing instantaneous energy, the information of energy evolution is involved. As such, the accuracy is improved without bringing in extra information besides energy, or complicated transformation. In multi-class problems, the proposed approach has obtained promising results for identifying the ictal EEG, which indicates the tremendous potential of the proposed approach for epileptic seizure detection.

The paper proposes a bio-inspired model for an imitative sensorimotor learning, which aims at building a map between the sensory representations of gestures (sensory targets) and their underlying motor pattern through random exploration of the motor space. An example of such learning process occurs during vocal learning in humans or birds, when young subjects babble and learn to copy previously heard adult vocalizations. Previous work has suggested that a simple Hebbian learning rule allows perfect imitation when sensory feedback is a purely linear function of the motor pattern underlying movement production. We aim at generalizing this model to the more realistic case where sensory responses are sparse and non-linear. To this end, we explore the performance of various learning rules and normalizations and discuss their biological relevance. Importantly, the proposed model is robust whatever normalization is chosen. We show that both the imitation quality and the convergence time are highly dependent on the sensory selectivity and dimension of the motor representation.

This paper proposes a method for classifying Arabic tweets based on credibility using content and user features. The process involves feature extraction, Twitter tagging, and machine learning techniques. The authors focus on the importance of using both content and user features to improve the accuracy of credibility classification. Sentiment analysis is also incorporated into the process to improve the effectiveness of the predictive models. The overall goal is to provide a reliable tool for identifying credible and non-credible Arabic tweets in real-time, which can have significant implications for communication and decision-making in various domains such as politics and news.

Keyframe extraction is important for video retrieval. In order to realize frequency adaptive human motion sequence resampling and achieve high quality keyframe, we propose a new keyframe extraction method for human motion sequence. First, we define the inter-frame similarity metric based on the features of human body parts. Then, the keyframe extraction is realized by the affine propagation clustering algorithm. The proposed method starts from the information distribution of the video itself, adaptively searches for the optimal keyframe of the video, and the operation speed is fast. Finally, the evaluation of the sequence reconstruction based on keyframe is verified. A comparative experiment conducted on the CMU database verified the efficiency of our method.

The NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE) is a prominent institution that provides training to government agencies and other stakeholders on computer security and cyber defence. The centre's aim is to enhance public policy in the realm of cyber espionage by conducting research, analysis, and awareness-raising campaigns. It coordinates knowledge-sharing and capacity-building efforts amongst NATO member states and partners to strengthen their collective cyber defence posture. The centre's comprehensive training syllabus includes technical, legal, strategic, and ethical aspects of cyber defence, ensuring that all stakeholders are equipped with the necessary skills to combat cyber threats effectively. Through collaboration, the CCDCOE is committed to fostering international cooperation and strengthening public policies that promote cyber security and resilience.

Rational use of medicines is of great importance in pediatric clinical medication. As the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the pediatric group is highly dynamic, it is a great challenge to determine the rational dosage for pediatric patients. Traditional clinical decision support systems for dosage guidance largely rely on manual collection of medication information, which usually suffers from incomplete and missing evidences for the pediatric group. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach to accurately predict pediatric medication dosages by leveraging prescription big data. More specifically, we first identify two relevant factors of pediatric medication dosage, i.e., the physiology factors including patients' body weight and age group, and the indication factors that affect clinical dosage patterns. We then extract the corresponding physiology and indication features, and propose a hybrid-learning-based method to adaptively integrate the two sets of heterogeneous features into a model for accurate pediatric dosage prediction. We evaluate our method on real-world prescription datasets from two tertiary children's hospitals. Results show that our method predicts pediatric medication dosages with an accuracy above 81.3%, and consistently outperforms other baselines.

This research presents implementation guidelines and techniques for applying the MQTT protocol on an embedded system to construct smart sensors/actuators and many IoT applications. The proposed system is based on a small and low-cost microcontroller. A firmware of the microcontroller is designed and implemented based on a custom operating system using the special technique. The powerful implementation technique is called the Asynchronous Event-Driven Non-Blocking I/O. All peripheral drivers used in the proposed system are implemented based on event-driven queue and callback functions. With this implementation approach, we can achieve the very high efficiency of the microcontroller. The proposed system can connect to the internet network using WiFi module of Ethernet Controller. It is fully evaluated in real-world environments and tested in many possible conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed system can work correctly as expected in all situations.

Traffic Light detection and recognition has become one of the critical research areas when it comes to autonomous driving vehicles. Developing an algorithm to detect different shaped traffic lights such as traffic lights (TLs) with arrowheads, circular shapes, horizontally and vertically oriented TLs and TLs in different illumination conditions during daytime still remains a challenge. This paper evaluates the existing algorithms, which uses heuristic or template matching based image processing methods and other learning based systems, that consumes higher time and processing power for training and map based systems and proposes a novel optimized algorithm using machine vision techniques to meet those challenges. The experiments were carried out using videos taken by front camera of vehicles. The results of the algorithm show a higher accuracy for precision and recall evaluations.

In this paper, we investigate the use of phonological and acoustic features to automatically classify Japanese onomatopoeias into semantic usage categories. The process of feature extraction was utilized in order to identify key characteristics of each onomatopoeia, while the study of phonetics enabled us to understand the sound structure of the language. Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) was also used to analyze the acoustic features of the onomatopoeias. Results revealed that these features were effective in distinguishing onomatopoeias according to their semantic usage categories. However, it was found that the MFCCs were particularly useful in distinguishing onomatopoeias related to vegetation while semantics played an important role in classifying onomatopoeias related to non-vegetation. Overall, this study demonstrates the usefulness of phonological and acoustic features in classifying Japanese onomatopoeias based on their semantic usage category.

Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is an important task in array signal processing. Aperture and resolution are two critical factors that determine the performance of DOA estimation algorithms. In this paper, we propose a novel sensor array structure called the Super Nested Sparse Circular Array (SNSCA) which can provide high resolution DOA estimation. The SNSCA structure consists of concentric circular subarrays with nested sparse subarrays to increase the overall aperture. The proposed SNSCA can be viewed as a two-dimensional display of sensors. The performance of the SNSCA is evaluated using simulations and compared with existing array structures. The simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed SNSCA in terms of DOA estimation accuracy and resolution. The proposed SNSCA can be used in various applications such as radar systems and wireless communications.

This paper discusses the requirements and challenges related to the integration of aggregated personal health data into formal electronic health records (EHRs). Medical services are becoming increasingly data-driven, and integration of personal health data is vital for providing more personalized and efficient medical services. The integration of personal health data also raises issues related to interoperability, data models, and data privacy. Standards must be established to ensure that the integration of this data is seamless and accurate. The use of electronic medical records and wireless sensor networks can help to simplify the integration process by providing an easy means of data collection, storage, and access. However, it is essential to ensure data privacy and security, which can be a challenging undertaking. Therefore, this paper provides an insight into the requirements and challenges related to the integration of aggregated personal health data into formal electronic health records, which will help healthcare organizations to address potential issues during the implementation process.

Person re-identification is the process of matching individuals across different scenes captured by non-overlapping cameras. With the increasing deployment of automated visual surveillance systems, there is a growing need for reliable and efficient methods for end-to-end person re-identification. In this paper, we propose a framework for end-to-end person re-identification using a combination of deep learning models for feature extraction, visualization techniques and training strategies. We evaluate our proposed framework on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Our framework has the potential to significantly enhance the robustness and reliability of surveillance systems in real-world scenarios. This work contributes to the field of computer vision and has important implications for the development of automated visual surveillance systems that are capable of accurately identifying individuals across different scenes captured by cameras.

This paper outlines a roadmap for the design of surgical equipment that can enhance safe surgery worldwide. The roadmap highlights the key areas where improvements should be made, including hospitals, maintenance engineering, minimally invasive surgery, anesthesia, and training. The design of surgical equipment should be tailored to reducing the chances of injuries during surgery and minimizing the risks associated with surgical procedures. Hospitals need to have reliable equipment, properly maintained, and staffed by trained professionals. Maintenance engineering should prioritize preventative maintenance and regular inspections to prevent equipment failures before they happen. Minimally invasive surgery should be incorporated to reduce risks of complications and speed up recovery time. The equipment used for anesthesia should be safe, reliable, and fit for purpose. Finally, surgical teams need thorough and ongoing training to ensure that they are up-to-date with the latest technology and techniques, as well as best practices for using the equipment available. With the adoption of these principles, the design of surgical equipment can be tailored to meet the needs of healthcare systems worldwide and improve the safety and success of surgical procedures.

During the process of smart city construction, city managers always spend a lot of energy and money for cleaning street garbage due to the random appearances of street garbage. Consequently, visual street cleanliness assessment is particularly important. However, the existing assessment approaches have some clear disadvantages, such as the collection of street garbage information is not automated and street cleanliness information is not real-time. To address these disadvantages, this paper proposes a novel urban street cleanliness assessment approach using mobile edge computing and deep learning. First, the high-resolution cameras installed on vehicles collect the street images. Mobile edge servers are used to store and extract street image information temporarily. Second, these processed street data is transmitted to the cloud data center for analysis through city networks. At the same time, Faster Region-Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) is used to identify the street garbage categories and count the number of garbage. Finally, the results are incorporated into the street cleanliness calculation framework to ultimately visualize the street cleanliness levels, which provides convenience for city managers to arrange clean-up personnel effectively. The overall approach is illustrated and visualized using the street images of Jiangning District in Nanjing, China. The practical application shows the feasibility and usability of the approach.

This paper presents a novel approach for imputing missing values in time series data through a combination of revealed information and residual shortcut connections. The proposed methodology integrates logic gates and data models to capture the underlying relationships between variables and generate a training dataset for machine learning algorithms. Through an extensive empirical analysis, the authors demonstrate that this methodology significantly outperforms traditional imputation techniques and achieves state-of-the-art results. The proposed approach leverages task analysis and machine learning to identify the most informative features and select the most appropriate imputation method. The authors conclude that the integration of revealed information based on the residual shortcut connection holds great promise for improving time series analysis and other related fields.

Despite its significance, modulation classification of constant envelope modulations (CEM) has not gained worthy attention in AMC literature so far. Two neural network-based architectures, i.e., radial basis function network (RBFN) and sparse-autoencoder-based deep neural network (DNN) are proposed and analyzed for the classification of spectrally efficient CEM modulations. A blind classification method which does not require any a-priori information about the channel or CEM specifics is based on the effectiveness of proposed hybrid feature space (HFS), used to train the trending neural network classifiers. Classification performance of both networks is analyzed for the typical additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and less explored, unfriendly, frequency-selective fading environment under the impact of Doppler shift.

The goal of upper extremity Prosthetic Research is to design and develop an anthropomorphic artificial limb having sufficient grasping strength, response speed and a visual appeal. The paper describes the design and assembling of a prosthetic arm that has the flexibility and motion as that of a human arm. A finger of the designed arm is modeled using Neural Networks.
