In this paper we present the multi-year collaboration between Rupprecht-Gymnasium München, a preuniversity school (K-12) in Bavaria, Germany, and MathWorks, an international scientific computing company. The school is STEM-focused and a member of the German national STEM school excellence network MINT-EC; they prepare students aged 10 to 18 for university careers. We highlight the starting motivation for the partners and describe several building blocks and initiatives including curricular and extracurricular activities for students as well as teacher training that became part of the collaboration. We also discuss future steps for the partners and how this project could be transferred to other schools.

Facial action unit (AU) detectors have performed well when trained and tested within the same domain. Do AU detectors transfer to new domains in which they have not been trained? To answer this question, we review literature on cross-domain transfer and conduct experiments to address limitations of prior research. We evaluate both deep and shallow approaches to AU detection (CNN and SVM, respectively) in two large, well-annotated, publicly available databases, Expanded BP4D+ and GFT. The databases differ in observational scenarios, participant characteristics, range of head pose, video resolution, and AU base rates. For both approaches and databases, performance decreased with change in domain, often to below the threshold needed for behavioral research. Decreases were not uniform, however. They were more pronounced for GFT than for Expanded BP4D+ and for shallow relative to deep learning. These findings suggest that more varied domains and deep learning approaches may be better suited for promoting generalizability. Until further improvement is realized, caution is warranted when applying AU classifiers from one domain to another.

This paper proposes a convex optimization-based approach to state estimation against sparse integrity attacks in sensor systems. The aim is to enhance the resilience of the sensors to such attacks by utilizing the properties of convex functions in the cost function of the estimation problem. The proposed method combines the previous measurement data with the noisy measurement data to estimate the state vector of the sensors. To handle the sparse integrity attacks, a convex optimization problem is formulated, which aims to minimize the cost function subject to the integrity constraints. The proposed method effectively suppresses the effect of the sparse integrity attacks and provides robust state estimation for the sensors. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations, which show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness against sparse integrity attacks. Overall, this paper provides a promising approach for enhancing the resilience of sensors against sparse integrity attacks through convex optimization-based state estimation.

The consumer is ultimately the key determinant of success of an organization. The need for an in-depth and objective understanding of the consumers, therefore, in terms of what runs in their minds and hearts for the way they behave and act when they go about making complex purchase decisions cannot be over-emphasized. Borrowed from the disciplines of psychology, economics and sociology, the study of consumer behavior isan interdisciplinary and continually-evolving science since long. Other data-science related areas, such as, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Neural Networks and Internet of Things are also being increasingly adopted to analyze and predict consumer behavior. This paper attempts to explore the significance of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in empowering consumer research.

Calculating text similarity is a key point in the detection of content duplication of science and technology project application documents, academic papers and degree papers. Aiming at the Chinese text similarity detection, a text similarity detection method based on Hadoop was proposed. The text to be detected and sample text are converted into a word segmentation matrix by using the word segmentation results, and the detection results are obtained by scanning and analyzing the matrix. MapReduce was used to realize the parallel optimization of the algorithm and improve the execution efficiency. Finally, an example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Hybrid testbeds are popular for testing distributed software systems, like network protocols and distributed applications, since the beginning of the 2000s. Combining physical and virtual resources for testing these networked computer systems allows to leverage the advantages and mitigate the disadvantages of either one. However, hybrid testbeds introduce novel challenges, e.g. regarding plausibility, heterogeneity, and controllability. To counter these challenges, we introduce the Hybrid Applications Testbed for Fault Injection (Hatebefi) which combines two approaches: On the one hand, Hatebefi aims to increase the plausibility by integrating hybrid testbeds with domain-specific simulators (e.g. for traffic simulation). This integration also addresses the heterogeneity of contemporary distributed applications. On the other hand, our framework allows for efficient creation and execution of complex test scenarios with a high degree of controllability by offering an event-based execution model. To demonstrate the feasibility of our approach, we implemented a basic set of arbitrarily combinable events to cover the most common scenarios. Both features combined pave the way to test distributed software systems, like Internet of Things applications involving connected vehicles or smart cities.

This paper presents the use of Unscented Transformations for Probabilistic Load Flow analysis. The problem of uncertainty in Load flow analysis is addressed by the application of random variables in the mathematical model. The estimation of the probability of different outcomes is made possible through the use of Probabilistic logic, and the Covariance matrices are used to quantify the degree of uncertainty associated with the outcomes. The use of Unscented Transformations provides an alternative to standard Monte Carlo techniques, as it can handle non-linearities with more efficiency. Overall, this approach provides a more comprehensive and accurate analysis of Load Flow that takes into account the inherent uncertainty associated with this problem.

Although deep face recognition has achieved impressive results in recent years, controversy has arisen regarding racial and gender bias of the models, questioning their deployment into sensitive scenarios. This work quantifies for the first time the demographic imbalance of popular public face datasets in terms of identity, gender and ethnicity. We also publicly release DemogPairs, a new validation set with 10.8K facial images and 58.3M identity verification pairs, distributed in demographically-balanced folds of Asian, Black and White females and males. A benchmark of experiments is carried out using DemogPairs over state-of-the-art deep face recognition models (SphereFace, FaceNet and ResNet50), in order to analyze their cross-demographic behavior. Experimental results demonstrate that studied models suffer from a very structured and damaging demographic bias. Our experiments shine a light on novel testing protocols to appropriately validate the generalization capabilities of face recognition models.

The Inertia Constant strategy has been implemented on the Mean Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm in order to optimize various mathematical functions. The aim of this study is to analyze the convergence rate of the algorithm and compare it with other optimization approaches such as Particle Swarm Optimization and MIMICs. The Inertia Constant strategy has been found to improve the optimization performance of the Mean Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm, resulting in faster convergence and better overall results. The proposed approach has been evaluated using standard benchmarks and the results indicate that it outperforms the traditional optimization techniques in terms of efficiency and accuracy. This study presents a new way of optimizing functions using a combination of the Mean Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm and Inertia Constant strategy, providing insights into the potential of the approach for a variety of optimization tasks.

This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques for fault diagnosis in induction motor drives. In particular, the study focuses on feature extraction methods which involve vibration data collected from both the stator and rotor of the motor. The approach involves using convolutional neural networks for analysis and diagnosis. The development and use of two-dimensional displays to visualize motor health is also discussed. Overall, the study demonstrates the potential of deep learning for improving the accuracy and efficiency of fault diagnosis in induction motors.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and mobile agent technology has led to the development of iAgent, an advanced system for monitoring and controlling wireless sensor networks. This system combines the autonomous capabilities of mobile agents with the intelligence of AI, offering an efficient solution for real-time task analysis and energy consumption optimization. Mobile agents equipped with intelligent algorithms are deployed to collect data from sensors and analyze it in real-time using machine learning techniques. By analyzing the data, iAgent can identify problems and execute corrective actions without requiring human intervention. The performance of iAgent is optimized using energy-efficient processing techniques, enabling it to operate for extended periods without a need for frequent recharging. This paper presents an overview of the iAgent system, highlighting its key features, including task analysis, energy consumption optimization, and real-time monitoring. The proposed system can be used in a wide range of applications, including environmental monitoring, healthcare, and industrial automation, among others. Overall, iAgent represents a significant step forward in the integration of AI and mobile agent technologies to create intelligent systems with enhanced efficiency and reliability.

This paper is concerned with path planning for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in urban environment. Distance is the fundamental goal of path planning. Besides, safety is indispensable for the riskless UAV flight. In this paper, we propose a multi-objective path planning (MOPP) approach based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to find an optimal collision-free path for UAV, considered both distance and safety. To this aim, firstly, we represent the urban environment by octree, which is an efficient and hierarchical data structure for spatial subdivision in 3D. Meanwhile, safety index map (SIM) are developed to capture obstacles in the geography map. Then, a Crowd Distance NSGA-II (CDNSAG-II) method is proposed to deal with MOPP problem. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach is able to find an optimal path efficiently under urban environment based on octrees.

A preprocessing technique is an essential in image processing. It enhances details of the image including edges before continuing further image processing. In this work, we compare three image enhancement methods for improving the contrast and details of the X-ray images that are needed for medical diagnosis subsequently. The image enhancement methods including Brightness Preserving Dynamic Fuzzy Histogram Equalization (BPDFHE), Histogram Equalization (HE), and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) were performed for purpose. Comparison of enhancing results are discussed. In this experiment, the results from the enhanced lumbar spine X-ray images show that the CLAHE technique is a technique that delivers excellent details and contrast among the other techniques.

To reveal the cognitive mechanisms is one of challenging problems in various fields of science, such as neuroscience, cognitive science, and artificial intelligence. Focusing on the cognitive mechanisms of time-series events, we present an analysis on the backward time perception with the flash-lag illusion. In the flash-lag experiment, we experience the visual illusion that a stationary flashed object is perceived to lag behind a spatially aligned moving object. When this moving object changes the direction of motion, the time reversing recognition called postdiction is observed. In other words, the postdiction is a phenomenon that the future stimulus affects the present one backward in time. Although several models have been presented to explain this illusion, the neural basis is not clear. Here we propose the assumption that the simple dual-path process in the critical states can provide the backward time perception and other important features of the visual illusion related to the flash-lag experiment. The dual-path process consists of two pathways: a fast-processing pathway and a slow-processing pathway. The backward time perception can occur as a result of the integration of the information from these two pathways. We implemented the dual-path process in the critical state using a simple lattice model and succeeded in the reproduction of the postdictive property and other features of visual illusions related to the flash-lag effect. According to the criticality hypothesis proposed by Beggs, the brain operates in the critical state. If the critical state accelerates the fast pathway and decelerates the slow pathway, simple circuits can provide the complicated cognitive functions. The concept that simple systems can realize advanced functions utilizing the critical states will contribute to the discovery of the fundamental principles of neural mechanisms and the improvement of cognitive functions of artificial intelligence.

The Next Generation Industrial Blockchain-Based Wireless Sensor Networks present a significant step towards the integration of cutting-edge technology for the Internet of Things (IoT) development. The system combines the power of wireless sensor networks with the security and transparency offered by blockchain technology. The consensus algorithm employed ensures that all transactions are verified and validated before being added to the blockchain. Moreover, the use of microprogramming supports the flexibility and scalability of the system. Digital signatures and public key cryptography ensure the integrity and non-repudiation of the data exchanged in the network. Overall, this paper highlights the potential for blockchain technology to revolutionize the development of a secure and reliable wireless sensor network for the IoT industry.

This paper proposes a pose measurement method for space noncooperative targets based on maximum outer contour recognition. The method involves feature extraction and target recognition using cameras and solid modeling techniques. It is suitable for extraterrestrial measurements and positioning of satellites. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides accurate and efficient pose measurement for noncooperative targets, which makes it a valuable tool for space exploration and satellite positioning applications. Further research can expand the method to include other types of features for more comprehensive recognition and measurement of space targets.

A bi-linear approach is proposed to efficiently design planar sparse antenna arrays with rectangular boundary. On account of practical manufacturing and cost limitation, it deals with x-y de-coupled planar sparse arrays whose array factor could be decomposed into two linear array factors. Computational cost for both radiation pattern and array synthesis accordingly is significantly reduced. It is successfully applied to design an array with low sidelobe level.

A good emotion has a great impact on health and a classification of emotions is very important to improve the quality of life. In this paper, a emotion recognition system based on CW Doppler radar with subspace KNN classifier which was selected as the machine learning algorithm to classify emotions is proposed. In the experiment, four emotions including joy, sadness, neutral, and fear were triggered by videos. The classification accuracy rates of two, three and four emotions were 85%, 74.6% and 67.4% respectively. These results suggest that the proposed scheme is suitable for non-contact emotion recognition.

This paper presents a framework for constructing upper bounds on the number of affine linear regions of ReLU feed-forward neural networks. The proposed framework leverages techniques from matrix decomposition, machine learning, and indexes for computing histograms of activations. The upper bound constructed by this framework is based on the rank of the matrix formed by the concatenation of the weight matrices of each layer. The framework can be used to analyze the behavior of neural networks during training and to guide the selection of hyperparameters. The experimental results show that the upper bounds constructed by this framework are tight and provide valuable insights into the behavior of neural networks. Overall, this work provides a valuable contribution to the growing body of research aimed at understanding the limits of deep learning models.

Cloud is a popular paradigm for providing online computing services to the end users. Recently many of the cloud service providers use containers instead of Virtual Machines (VMs) to host the applications. Using containers raises the application service availability concerns. Availability is a non-functional requirement that refers to the percentage of time the service is available for the end user. Scheduling containers (host application) on physical/virtual hosts has direct impact on the availability of the application service that is provided to the end user. According to the best of our knowledge, the existing container scheduling solutions do not directly address the availability of the application service. In this article we propose a new Availability-Aware container scheduling strategy that aims to increase the availability level of the application service in the cloud container-based platform. The strategy selects VMs and hosts that have higher availability values within constraints to schedule the containers in efficient way. We compare the proposed strategy with other container scheduling strategies that are used by Docker container platform. The results shown that the Availability-Aware strategy achieves higher service availability levels, and acceptable physical host CPU utilization.

This paper proposes a transfer function based calculation method for analyzing and mitigating radio frequency interference (RFI). The proposed approach utilizes transfer functions to characterize the couplings between various antennas, including dipole antennas, and to calculate the RFI power flowing through each antenna. The antenna measurements and magnetic moments are also taken into consideration to enhance the accuracy of the calculation. Additionally, a computational modeling method is presented to validate the calculation results. The proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for RFI analysis and mitigation in complex electromagnetic environments.

This paper proposes MulMapper, an automated FPGA-based CNN processor generator for efficient hardware acceleration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). MulMapper is based on dynamic design space exploration using a space exploration approach which exploits the trade-off between performance and resource utilization. The generator employs a range of techniques, including IP networks, Random access memory, and system-on-chip architecture. MulMapper is capable of generating FPGA-based CNN processors with high throughput and real-time processing capabilities. The proposed approach can also be used to optimize the architecture of other types of hardware systems, demonstrating its potential for application in computer architecture and hardware design. Overall, the results demonstrate that MulMapper is an effective approach for automating the design and optimization of FPGA-based CNN processors.

This paper proposed a novel approach for designing a sliding mode control system with optimized fuzzy power system stabilizer (PSS) by using the differential evolution algorithm. The proposed method was applied to the single-machine-infinite-bus (SMIB) power system and the stability of the system was analyzed using a mathematical model. The performance of the proposed sliding mode control system was compared with the conventional PSS and the results showed that the proposed method had better damping characteristics and reduced oscillations. Furthermore, the fuzzy logic approach helped to improve the stability of the system in real-time. The optimization process was achieved by employing the differential evolution algorithm which found the optimal parameters for the fuzzy PSS. The proposed sliding mode control system with optimized fuzzy PSS can effectively enhance the stability of the power system SMIB. The results demonstrated the effectiveness and the superiority of the proposed method for enhancing the stability of power systems.

In recent years, vein recognition technology has attracted attention in the field of biometrics due to its high security and reliability. This study proposes a feature extraction and recognition method for finger vein images using machine learning algorithms, such as discriminant analysis (DA) and K nearest neighbor (KNN). The focus of this research is on the development of an accurate prediction algorithm for finger vein recognition using image segmentation techniques. The features extracted from the finger vein images can be used to recognize individuals based on their unique finger vein patterns. The results of our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high performance and accuracy in finger vein recognition. These findings indicate promising potential in the development of secure biometric authentication technologies using finger vein recognition techniques.

Recommender systems have become increasingly important tools in the mobile industry for suggesting personalized content and services to mobile subscribers. The Call Data Record (CDR) based recommender system is a promising approach that utilizes data from mobile handsets to make recommendations. Collaboration among mobile operators and third-party service providers can also enhance the accuracy and relevance of the recommendations. Machine learning algorithms have been utilized for CDR-based recommender systems, which can process large amounts of data and generate recommendations in real-time. Contracts and correlation analysis can also be used to further improve recommender systems by identifying patterns and relationships among data points. Overall, CDR-based recommender systems have great potential for improving the mobile subscriber experience by providing personalized and relevant recommendations.

This paper proposes a design of Internet of Things (IoT) architecture for order picking in a typical warehouse. The architecture includes interconnected computer architecture, logistics network, cloud computing and robot sensing systems with the application of information technology. With the goal of improving order picking efficiency and reducing labor cost, multiple devices and sensors are deployed to monitor and collect data in the warehouse. The cloud computing platform provides real-time information processing and management, making the entire process more intelligent and automated. Through the integration of IoT technologies, the proposed architecture improves flexibility, accuracy and timeliness of order picking, providing a promising solution for intelligent warehousing in the era of Industry 4.0. The results show that the proposed architecture has greatly optimized the logistics operation process, and has a wide range of application prospects in the field of logistics and supply chain management.

Low power wide area network (LPWAN) technology has been widely adopted in different Internet-of-things (IoT) services. Long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) is an evolution of wireless sensor network (WSN) directed to IoT concept, mostly used in private outdoor applications. The existing LoRaWAN operates following the simple ALOHA standards. Therefore, it suffers from high packet loss and supports a very limited number of nodes. For the application of LoRaWAN in dense networks, an efficient channel access mechanism is required in order to improve the efficiency and robustness. In this paper, we investigate a modified listen-before-talk (LBT) mechanism. Specifically, we propose LoRa-BED, LoRa-BEB and LoRa-BEH, channel access protocols to reduce collisions in high density environment. Our results demonstrate that the proposed protocols significantly improve the channel utilization and efficiency with a slight increase in energy per device while sensing the channel.

The aim of this paper is to propose a novel approach for multi-label chest x-ray classification of common thorax diseases. The approach includes three important parts: feature extraction, task analysis and image classification. In terms of feature extraction, a variety of features such as Gabor filters and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) are used to extract important information from the chest x-ray images. Task analysis is the process of identifying the main tasks and sub-tasks that need to be performed to achieve the desired classification results. The proposed approach focuses on the detection and classification of multiple thorax diseases, such as pneumonia, tuberculosis and lung cancer, through the image classification stage. The classification process employs a combination of support vector machines (SVM) and decision trees (DT) algorithms. The results show that the proposed approach achieves higher accuracy rates than traditional approaches in multi-label chest x-ray classification of common thorax diseases. This study has important implications for the field of biomedical imaging and solid modeling.

Ants are believed to be workaholics, though biologists report that many ants are literally inactive in nest move. An open question on this ants swarm behavior is whether such an active-to-population rate improves or deteriorates precise and swift nest move. In this study, we use an algorithm which is based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulate ant nest move. The simulation of our PSO-based algorithm has revealed that the swarm which comprises 60% of active ants in the population obviously outperforms the swarm of full active population in both precise and swift nest move. Our simulation results are supported with the field researches carried by external ant experts.

This paper proposes a hardware-software blueprint for achieving flexible deep learning specialization. The blueprint combines machine learning and computer architecture to optimize runtime performance and task analysis for deep learning tasks. Computational modeling is utilized to optimize system performance and align hardware-software design to deep learning tasks. The blueprint is designed to promote the development of flexible and efficient deep learning systems. The proposed approach aims to address the challenges of hardware-software co-design in the era of deep learning revolution. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the hardware-software blueprint in enhancing system performance and flexibility, which can help to accelerate the adoption and deployment of deep learning systems in various industries. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive framework to guide the design of deep learning systems at the intersection of machine learning and computer architecture.

This paper presents the integration of Google Assistant into an Android application for voice control of media playback on various devices including TVs and smartphones. With the advancements in cloud computing and artificial intelligence technologies, voice control has become a popular trend in modern user interfaces. Google Assistant provides an extensive set of voice commands which can be used to simplify the media playback process. In order to demonstrate the voice control functionality, the developed application was tested on a smart phone and TV in different settings. The testing results show that the integration of Google Assistant provides an efficient and user-friendly approach for controlling various types of media playback with voice commands. Overall, the integration of Google Assistant into an Android application is a promising approach for making media playback more accessible and convenient for users.

This study develops a service quality assessment system, based on the SERVQUAL, to assess the existing service performance of interior design companies. A real case study from interior and architecture experts is applied to conduct the service quality improvement processes. The result reveals that the proposed approach can be provided a guideline for companies seeking to improve sustainable business advantages and would be an effective decision tool for interior design company strategy optimization.

Predicting the price movements of stocks based on deep learning and high-frequency data has been studied intensively in recent years. Especially, limit order book which describes the supply-demand balance of the market is used as features of a neural network. However, these methods do not utilize the properties of market orders. On the other hand, this study encodes information of time and prices of orders into images. This encoding method can take advantage of these properties. Then, we apply machine learning methods, convolutional neural network (CNN) and logistic regression (LR), to order-based features to predict the direction of short-term price movements. The results show that the execution has the highest prediction power than the order and cancellation information. Moreover, the difference between CNN and LR are small and depends on kinds of stocks.

This paper presents an approach to automatically dismantling online dating fraud by means of feature extraction, machine learning, and data mining tools. It focuses on using IP networks to detect fraudulent activities in the online dating environment. By analyzing user behavior patterns, such as language use, message content, and response time, this approach can identify and notify potential fraud cases in real-time. The proposed method integrates knowledge and techniques from sociology, statistics, and computer science to create a robust framework that can effectively address the issue of online dating fraud. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in identifying fraudulent users, suggesting a promising direction for future research in this field.

This paper presents a simulation and evaluation of LentiMark markers for accurate pose estimation in the context of camera-based systems. The use of LentiMark markers is proposed as an alternative to traditional bar code markers for pallet and task analysis. The simulation is performed using a software-based approach, which creates a virtual environment for testing the LentiMark markers' accuracy and efficiency. The evaluation of the markers is based on several criteria, including visibility, robustness, and recognition time. The results indicate that LentiMark markers outperform traditional bar codes in terms of recognition time and robustness, especially when viewed from different angles. The study concludes that LentiMark markers are a promising alternative for accurate pose estimation in applications involving pallets and task analysis, thanks to their superior performance when used with camera-based systems.

Entity resolution is a critical and challenging task in the field of data mining and knowledge discovery. DeepBlock is a novel blocking approach that leverages the power of deep learning to effectively handle entity resolution. This new approach integrates semantics, couplings, syntactics, and task analysis to provide enhanced performance in identifying and resolving entities. By analyzing the relationships between entities in complex data architectures, DeepBlock can provide a comprehensive understanding of entity relationships, even in large datasets. The use of deep learning techniques and algorithmic approaches in DeepBlock enhances its ability to perform entity resolution and can be used to solve problems in a variety of domains. DeepBlock is a promising solution for tackling practical problems in data mining and knowledge discovery, and its efficiency and accuracy make it a necessary tool for businesses and organizations that rely on data analysis to inform their decision-making processes.

This paper studies positioning fundamentals in low-power wide area (LPWA) Internet of Things (IoT), where those devices with locations known operate as anchors. A tractable model is developed to analyze localizability of target devices. A random scenario is investigated, where anchors are randomly distributed. The model first studies the positioning of a target which can be anywhere. Then, from the point of view of system level, target randomness is further considered so that the study can be conducted over the whole network area. The model has no limitations on area shape but can consider any arbitrary polygonal one. It incorporates the ability for participating anchors to coordinate transmissions, and the interference effect on positioning is theoretically investigated. The model is then extensively validated in comparison with simulations, and the effects of a set of parameter settings are investigated. Compared to the existing positioning performance studies targeting deterministic scenarios, the proposed model considers location randomness through distance distributions using a powerful probabilistic distance-based tool from geometric probability. The model considers both interference and system-related parameter settings, investigating anchor transmission coordination and traffic load, which reveals how participating anchors in general impact positioning performance in LPWA IoT.

The paper titled "Visual-Interactive Identification of Anomalous IP-Block Behavior Using Geo-IP Data" proposes a novel approach for detecting anomalous IP-block behavior using geo-IP data. This approach leverages data visualization techniques to enable users to visually identify anomalous behavior in IP networks. The authors discuss the use of routing and task analysis methods to aid in understanding complex network behavior. The paper also highlights the importance of computer-aided software engineering in developing effective network security tools. The proposed approach is supported by the development of functional computer security prototypes, which are intended to assist in identifying abnormal IP-block behavior in real-world scenarios. Overall, the paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of computer security, with potential applications in network monitoring, intrusion detection, and threat intelligence analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach for diabetic retinopathy classification through feature extraction using spherical directional features (SDF) and artificial neural network (ANN). The retina is a vital part of the eye, and biomedical imaging is an essential tool for diagnosing retinopathy in patients with diabetes. The method proposed here employs SDFs as representative features, which are extracted from retina images. These features take into account the orientation of pixels with respect to the center of the retina. Image segmentation and retrieval techniques are used to localize and extract retinal images from digital fundus images. The extracted features are fed into an ANN for classification. The proposed method is tested on a public dataset, and the results show that it outperforms traditional feature extraction methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The method can be used as a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy, reducing vision loss and improving patient outcomes.

This paper presents a strategy for controlling the spread of salmonid alphavirus (SRS) in Salmo salar. The approach is based on data mining and MALDI-mass spectrometry, which are used to identify potential pathogens and to analyze the overall health of the fish populations. The focus is on machine learning techniques, which are used to identify patterns and relationships between different variables captured by the spectrometry data. The paper demonstrates how these techniques can be used to detect viruses and other pathogens that may be contributing to the development of SRS. The results of this research provide a new framework for understanding the molecular mechanisms behind SRS and for developing more effective control strategies. In addition, the study provides valuable insights into the role of data mining and mass spectroscopy in the identification and management of disease outbreaks in aquaculture.

This paper proposes an approach for a distributed anti-malware system based on blockchain technology. The system is designed to mitigate the increasing threat of malware by utilizing distributed databases and a consensus algorithm to ensure the security of the system. The system is also able to train itself using machine learning algorithms to improve its capabilities against emerging malware threats. The use of blockchain technology provides a secure and decentralized platform for the system to operate, ensuring that the data is protected and cannot be tampered with. The system's effectiveness is based on its ability to efficiently and effectively detect and neutralize malware, providing optimal protection against cyber attacks. Overall, the proposed approach offers a promising solution to the growing concern of malware threats and security vulnerabilities in today's digital age.

Driver distraction is one of the leading causes of vehicle accidents and injury. Automated systems for identifying driver distraction are of great interest for improving road safety. This study develops a smartphone sensor based driver distraction system using an ensemble learning method. After data collection, linear velocity data is first linearly interpolated. Then, 3-axial acceleration and 3-axial gyro signals are filtered for reducing noise. Next, a sliding window is applied to IMU and GPS data collected by the smartphone for feature extraction, where temporal features are calculated. Ensemble learning of four standard classifiers is used to recognize distraction events: K-Nearest Neighbor, Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest. To evaluate the proposed approach, 24 drivers were recruited to participate in a user study, driving on a route consisting of suburban and highway driving. Driver cognitive distraction was induced by asking the driver questions while driving. The experimental results show that the best weighted F1-score of our proposed system is 87% with all smartphone sensor signals.

Cellular networks have been playing a significant role in our daily lives due to their pervasive coverage, ubiquitous availability, and reliable connectivity. However, the exponential increase in mobile data traffic has led to a significant rise in energy consumption, which has a substantial impact on the environment. This paper proposes a novel energy model for renewable energy-enabled cellular networks that can provide ancillary services to the smart grid. The aim is to reduce the overall energy consumption and carbon footprint without compromising the quality of service. The proposed model leverages renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, to power the cellular network infrastructure, and employs energy-efficient switches to optimize the network's energy consumption. In addition, the model can provide ancillary services, such as peak shaving and load balancing, to the smart grid, which can contribute to the sustainable development of green products and services. The experimental results show that the proposed energy model can achieve up to 30% energy savings while ensuring the QoS requirements of cellular networks. Overall, the proposed model provides a feasible solution to reduce the carbon footprint of cellular networks and promote the integration of renewable energy sources into the smart grid.

Majority of Defense Systems utilizes rectangular enclosures and shelters in mobile systems for carrying various equipment such as communication, surveillance, CBRN sensors, power supplies etc. The electromagnetic compatibility at sub-system level as well as at system level of such equipment is necessary in view of the operational conditions as defined in various military standards. The overall electromagnetic compatibility depends on shielding effectiveness of enclosure used in such systems. The effects of external electromagnetic interferences due to various sources, its coupling to subsystems needs to be under control. Emission control is desired depending upon the deployment and operational requirements. One such fully EM compatible rectangular enclosure is designed and developed. The analysis, simulation and test results are presented in this paper.

Many cloud encryption methods have been proposed to achieve the encryption and decryption of users' data stored on public cloud database, and there are also some studies on heterogeneous database connection access methods, but none of them can implement the users's transparent (cross-language and cross-platform) or heterogeneous access to encrypted database on public cloud. To solve these problems, we modularly comply a middleware system in a private cloud by using the Mysql protocol and heterogeneous database data integration technology, which is applied in a hybrid cloud environment to achieve the users' transparent access to heterogeneous encrypted database. We talk about the preliminary assessment on the system security. Besides, the experimental evaluation testifies the system performance through separately testing time costs for the users to execute transparent access to individual and heterogeneous encrypted database.

This paper proposes the design of an optimized CMOS ELM accelerator which can efficiently train nonvolatile memory and simulate the behavior of neurons in neural networks. The hardware architecture of the accelerator is detailed, including its parallel processing units and inference algorithms. The proposed accelerator can achieve high-speed training and inference of neural networks through its advanced parallel processing capabilities, and can effectively reduce the computational load on the main processor. The optimized CMOS ELM accelerator provides a solution for efficient neural network training and inference, which is of great significance in the field of artificial intelligence and computer architecture.

Most software defect prediction models usually assume that enough historical training instances with labels are available. Additionally, the training data and the predicted instances should share the same features to ensure the prediction accuracy. However, in practice, there are many datasets with different granularities containing information in different dimensions. Therefore, it is valuable to effectively use the small scale and different dimensions of data as training instances to improve the prediction performance of the model. We propose a heterogeneous data orienting multiview transfer learning for software defect prediction, denoted as MTDP, which can achieve different dimensions and granularities features to automatically learn labels through neural network models. With this multiview transfer method, lots of training instances are provided for software defect prediction model to ensure the effectiveness of training labels. The proposed MTDP method has four main stages: 1) build heterogeneous transfer models; 2) transfer heterogeneous instances to generate quasi-real instances; 3) label quasi-real instances through co-training and then expand the training set; and (4) construct improved software defect prediction models. The experimental results show that the quasi-real instances have similar effects compared with real instances. Moreover, the software defect prediction performance can be improved by introducing the quasi-real instances into the training dataset.

For the sake of positioning the illegal unmanned aerial vehicle operators, the paper proposes a direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on the reconnaissance plane with multiple array sensors. First, the number of unmanned aerial vehicle signals is determined by information theory criteria. Then combined support vector regression, the direction of the operator is calculated according to some approximating function through training. Finally, the location can be estimated by integrating the DOAs acquired with the array sensors on the reconnaissance aircraft. This algorithm is convenient and fast to be realized, moreover, as a result of adopting super resolution and multiple kernel learning, it can locate numerous radio signals simultaneously and performs well in the circumstance that signals impinge on the sensor array with small-angle interval, as well as the conditions of small samples and low signal to noise ratio, besides, the algorithm also applies to the array which gain-phase inconsistency exists among the sensors.

Hyperspectral image classification is a challenging task when a limited number of training samples are available. It is also known that the classification performance highly depends on the quality of the labeled samples. In this work, a cluster-based conditional generative adversarial net (CCGAN) is proposed as an effective solution to increase the size and quality of the training data set. The proposed method is able to automatically select the most representative initial samples with a subtractive clustering-based strategy, which keeps the diversity for sample generation. Moreover, compared to the traditional semisupervised classification frameworks, the CCGAN is able to generate realistic spectral profiles by considering the class-specific labels. Experiments on well-known Pavia University data set demonstrate that the proposed CCGAN can significantly boost the classification accuracy, even using a small number of initial labeled samples.

This paper proposes a hybrid approach called HAP for predicting quality of service in cloud manufacturing. HAP combines local collaborative filtering and global case-based reasoning techniques to provide accurate and efficient predictions. The problem of QoS prediction in cloud computing has been a major challenge due to the lack of knowledge about the cloud environment. HAP addresses this challenge by incorporating both local and global perspectives in its predictive models. The local collaborative filtering technique utilizes the knowledge and experiences of neighboring users to make accurate predictions for new users, while the global case-based reasoning technique considers the overall trend of the cloud manufacturing environment. The proposed HAP approach not only enhances the prediction accuracy but also promotes collaboration and cognition among cloud manufacturing stakeholders. The filtering method in HAP helps filter out irrelevant data and enhances prediction efficiency. Experimental results show that the HAP approach outperforms traditional approaches in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and scalability. The proposed HAP approach presents a promising solution for QoS prediction in cloud manufacturing.

Time series forecasting has been regarded as a key research problem in various fields. such as financial forecasting, traffic flow forecasting, medical monitoring, intrusion detection, anomaly detection, and air quality forecasting etc. In this paper, we propose a sequence-to-sequence deep learning framework for multivariate time series forecasting, which addresses the dynamic, spatial-temporal and nonlinear characteristics of multivariate time series data by LSTM based encoder-decoder architecture. Through the air quality multivariate time series forecasting experiments, we show that the proposed model has better forecasting performance than classic shallow learning and baseline deep learning models. And the predicted PM2.5 value can be well matched with the ground truth value under single timestep and multi-timestep forward forecasting conditions. The experiment results show that our model is capable of dealing with multivariate time series forecasting with satisfied accuracy.

It is troublesome to obtain the fused state estimation for multi-sensor multi-delay systems with correlated noises. The previous conventional fused estimation method uses the information, sent by several different filter, smoothers and predictors, to get one-step estimation, which increases the complexity of the method, so that it is not suitable for real application. In order to get more convenient estimators, the augmented state equation is introduced, and then an augmented steady-state Kalman estimator can be got, which conceals the time delays. Extracting the partial component of that augmented steady-state estimator yields the suboptimal estimator, which ignores the correlation between the components of the augmented estimator, but possesses more excellent rapidity and convenience compared with the previous fused estimator. Then by Sequential Covariance Intersection (CI) fusion method, a fast fusion steady-state suboptimal Kalman filter is obtained. Simulation examples show that although the proposed fusion steady-state estimator is suboptimal, its accuracy is higher than each of the local estimators and approximate to the optimal information fusion estimator.

This paper proposes a supervised learning approach for Arabic Community Question Answering system by combining semantic and lexical features. The semantic analysis aims to extract knowledge discovery and task analysis from the input and training data models. The feature extraction process then combines the semantic and lexical features to enhance the accuracy of the answers. Support vector machines are used for training the model and predicting the best answer. The results show that the proposed method outperforms other approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This study suggests that the combination of semantic and lexical features is a promising direction to improve the performance of Arabic Community Question Answering systems. Further research can be conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in other languages and domains.

This paper presents a horizontal offloading mechanism for IoT application in fog computing using microservices, with a case study of a traffic management system. The Internet of Things (IoT) is becoming increasingly prevalent, driving the need for more efficient computing architectures. Cloud computing and edge computing have been proposed as potential solutions, but they have their limitations. Fog computing, which sits between the cloud and edge, has emerged as a promising approach. Microservices architecture is an ideal approach for the development of IoT applications, enabling the decomposition of complex applications into smaller, manageable services. This paper proposes a horizontal offloading mechanism that uses microservices to distribute tasks between fog nodes, resulting in improved performance and scalability. The proposed mechanism was evaluated using a traffic management system and compared to a traditional monolithic application architecture. The results indicate that the proposed mechanism reduces processing time, enhances scalability and decreases response time, making it a promising solution for real-time systems.

There are some concerns that education professionals seek to solve. The first to be able to promote learning is through the change of pedagogical methodology, pedagogical projects of courses or new learning strategies. The second refers to people with disabilities or specific classes of users accessing digital information. This article has been published in the following languages: How are students through the use of interesting projects, such as the use of PBL methodology and how other serious connected games. The phases of PBL were applied to the development of games, aimed at improving memory, are presented and discussed in this work, as well as their results and discussions.

According to recent studies hemodynamic conditions play an important role in initiation and development of several disorders of the cerebral circulation, such as atherosclerosis and aneurysm. One of the common sites of the aneurysm formation is the middle cerebral artery (MCA). In the present study, the flow conditions in the individualized model of the MCA aneurysm are investigated in detail and correlated with the aneurysm genesis. A patient-specific model of the saccular aneurysm of MCA was derived from the real clinical imaging data. A realistic physiological pulse curve was scaled to ensure the normal inlet flow rate in the artery. A transient computational fluid dynamics simulation was performed employing the Local viscosity fluid model, which takes into account non-Newtonian blood behavior and increases a precision of hemodynamic parameters evaluation, especially at low shear rate zones. The complex flow pattern was observed in the aneurysm sac, producing a swirling blood flow. A flow impingement zone near the aneurysm fundus was characterized by the high velocity values, about 0.9 m/s, which could potentially affect the endothelial cells at this zone and contribute to further arterial wall degeneration. Moreover, the zone of low wall shear stresses (<;2 Pa) was observed on the aneurysm dome, producing conditions for further growth of the aneurysm. The results of the study are consistent with hemodynamic theory of aneurysm genesis and correlate well with available clinical data. CFD simulation could be used as an additional tool for clinical decision support during the treatment of the cerebral aneurysms.

We study the properties of the Frank-Wolfe algorithm to solve the m-EXACT-SPARSE reconstruction problem, where a signal y must be expressed as a sparse linear combination of a predefined set of atoms, called dictionary. We prove that when the signal is sparse enough with respect to the coherence of the dictionary, then the iterative process implemented by the Frank-Wolfe algorithm only recruits atoms from the support of the signal, is the smallest set of atoms from the dictionary that allows for a perfect reconstruction of y. We also prove that under this same condition, there exists an iteration beyond which the algorithm converges exponentially.

Efficient estimation and prediction for sparse time-varying underwater acoustic channels is an important problem in underwater communication systems. Channel estimation is the process of estimating the frequency response of a communication channel. The estimation of underwater acoustic channels is a challenging problem because of the Doppler effect and the presence of noise. In recent years, prediction algorithms have become increasingly popular for underwater acoustic channel estimation. Among them, matching pursuit algorithms have been shown to have good performance in sparse environments. However, the complexity of matching pursuit algorithms is high, and they are not suitable for real-time applications. Therefore, an efficient algorithm is needed that can accurately estimate and predict time-varying channels with low complexity. Complexity theory is an important tool for analyzing and comparing the efficiency of algorithms. In this paper, we propose a low-complexity algorithm for estimating and predicting sparse time-varying underwater acoustic channels. Our algorithm is based on a modified version of the matching pursuit algorithm that takes into account the time-varying nature of the channel. Simulation results show that our algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of accuracy and computational complexity.

This paper proposes a novel approach for the control of multi-phase induction machine drives based on cascaded hybrid multi-level inverters aided by fuzzy logic. The proposed control technique allows achieving high accuracy torque control and improved overall system efficiency. The use of cascade hybrid multi-level inverters allows the implementation of a flexible topology that can accommodate different stator winding configurations in multi-phase induction machines, which are widely used in high-power applications. The proposed fuzzy logic control strategy improves the performance of the multi-level inverter system by providing a more adaptive and robust control strategy that can cope with different operating conditions, including variations in rotor speed and load torque. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control technique in achieving improved performance compared with conventional control methods. This research has the potential to accelerate the adoption of multi-phase induction machine drives in various high-power applications.

A Data Centre is a physical space that groups together computer equipment such as servers, storage arrays, among other equipment. It can be used for storage, processing and data protection. The majority of data centres operate 24 hours a day, and must provide the user with guarantees in terms of security and performance. Energy consumption is therefore permanent and the level of assistance and maintenance high. Data Centres have an ecological impact that is almost invisible to many users. In this paper a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of the airflow and thermal distribution of a real data centre room with 208 racks is proposed. Two case studies are presented and simulated with a high thermal load subjected to the minimum and maximum air flow velocity, respectively. The objective is to assess if the computer room air conditioning unit (CRAC) can cool the racks of the data centre in order to efficiently refrigerate all the hot spots.

Water level control in open channels used for hydroelectric production is addressed in this paper. In order to use classical methods of controller design, a new reduced order model based on Saint-Venant equations is proposed. It is derived from irrational transfer functions developed with the WKB method for any non-uniform subcritical flow regime. The reduced model captures the first two modes. A comparison of open-loop simulations with the proposed 5th order plus delay transfer functions and with numerical non linear model is performed. The inputs of the simulations are given by on-site measurements to show the accuracy of the model in realistic conditions. Based on the resulting model, a robust tuning of controller is developed. It consists of a two-degree-of-freedom proportional integral controller. Time domain scenarii are shown to illustrate the closed-loop performance.

Label propagation algorithm (LPA) is one of the classical community detection algorithms, with high efficiency, quick speed and no need for any prior information. However, it has the disadvantage of poor stability, which causes the detection results to be random. In order to improve the stability of label propagation algorithm, an algorithm with an adjustable parameter based on clustering coefficient and label propagation is proposed in this article. The algorithm is divided into two steps. The first step is to prioritize the nodes according to their degree and clustering coefficient, and initialize the label according to the ranking result. In the process of initializing the label, only the nodes with clustering coefficient in a certain range are selected to filter out the noisy nodes. The second step is based on the first step. In order to avoid randomness, the neighbor nodes are sorted according to their clustering coefficient and degree, the optimal neighbor node is selected to update the label. By applying the algorithm to LFR artificial network data sets and real networks data sets, the results show that the algorithm reduces the randomness of the label propagation algorithm, enhances the stability and accuracy of detection result, and its adjustable parameter make it possible to have a good quality of community division for various types of networks.

Despite the importance of competency modeling for both individuals and organizations, there is a lack of a comprehensive literature review and a cartography for it. This paper aims to provide an in-depth overview of different approaches to competency modeling reported in the field of technology-enhanced com petency-based learning. This literature review is complemented by an additional overview of related initiatives toward modeling intended learning outcomes, learning opportunities, achieved learning outcome profiles of learners and competency maps. In addition, a cartography illustrating the relationships between some important models is proposed. The main purpose of this work is to provide researchers with a comprehensive review of the current status in this field as well as to highlight ongoing issues and challenges that need to be addressed.

Experimentation in the modern age, and electronic engineering teaching and learning should be efficient and effective. The first course on analog electronics appears in engineering curricula in the third semester or earlier, and laboratory experiments often suffer from student's lack of breadboard circuit manipulation and data acquisition skills, which frequently leads to erroneous results and loss of time. The pocket sized EZ-TBOARD and its associated didactic resources is an experimentation system project that speeds up learning related to basic operation and application of semiconductor transistors. By means of a reconfigurable compact design, the training board helps students to setup the major different biasing, amplification and switching schemes suggested for all kind of three terminal transistors, in order to focus the experimenter's attention on the key aspects of device and application circuit theory, enhancing the student's capacity to analyze, design and reconfigure a circuit for a required behavior. The provided educational materials cover typical analysis and design methods to observe system outputs dependency on value of circuit element parameters, instead of common circuit assembly mistakes. It is expected for the training system to become an important reference for open educational resources in analog electronics engineering.

The recent advanced in the low-cost, small-scale EEG scanners open the doors for many innovations in the domains of disease detection, social sciences, cyber security, and much more. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of using EEG signals as an indication of deception or lies. Further, we exploit one of the new EEG scanners, MUSE, to investigate its ability to provide what is needed to detect potential lies. Our experiments showed great success for the MUSE in providing what is needed for a moderate-quality lie detector, with very low-cost and complexity. Integrating machine-learning techniques into the presented results would provide a much more accurate detection opening the door for a vast number of potential applications.

This paper considers the task of indoor subarea localization by acoustic sensing. In many practical scenarios, such as ordinary office rooms, subarea localization based on a single acoustic property without subsidiaries is always tricky due to similar space physical structures. To combat the indoor subarea localization problem without any dedicated devices, we propose a framework allowing the ordinary smartphone to quickly and easily determine its indoor subarea location. The proposed structure is to first construct the multidimensional fingerprint of each environmental background audio in a room using the auditory scene analysis method; then extract the room-level fingerprint by the acoustic background spectrum method, and cluster the subarea-level fingerprints using the Pearson correlation coefficient technology; subsequently, together with the offline stage long short-term memory recurrent neuron network and online stage least variance algorithm, the effective indoor subarea localization was achieved; finally, the localization results are presented not only in text form but also in a privacy-protected color sound pattern which is built by chroma DCT-reduced log pitch. Our experiments with real-world audios, which include 96-h environment background audios of 14 different rooms, presents that the room-level localization accuracy was higher than 90% and the subarea-level accuracy could be up to 97.64%. These results strongly proved that the proposed framework could perform well even in small complicated rooms.

Currently, autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is mainly diagnosed by the observation of core behavioral symptoms. Consequently, the window of opportunity for effective intervention may have passed, when the disorder is detected until 3 years of age. Thus, it is of great importance to identify imaging-based biomarkers for early diagnosis of ASD. Previous findings indicate that an abnormal pattern of the amygdala and hippocampal development in autism persists through childhood and adolescence. However, due to the low tissue contrast and small structural size of amygdala and hippocampal subfields, our knowledge on their growth in autistics in early stage still remains very limited. In this paper, for the first time, we propose a volume-based analysis of the amygdala and hippocampal subfields of the infant subjects with risk of ASD at around 24 months of age. Specifically, to address the challenge of low tissue contrast, we propose a novel deep-learning approach, i.e., dilated-dense U-Net, to automatically segment the amygdala and hippocampal subfields. Experimental results on National Database for Autism Research (NDAR) show the advantages of our proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy. Our volume-based analysis shows the overgrowths of amygdala and CA1-3 of hippocampus, which may link to the emergence of autism spectrum disorder.

This paper discusses the development of a software apparatus for training students in the field of plasma physics. The software focuses on the concept of wave functions and the study of plasmas, as well as atomic measurements and the electric potential. Computational modeling is used to create numerical models that can be used for training and testing, and the reliability of the software is of utmost importance. The software provides students with the opportunity to learn about practical applications of plasma physics and to develop skills in using numerical models to simulate real-life situations. With the help of this software apparatus, students can gain a better understanding of the underlying principles of plasma physics, and ultimately become better prepared for work in this exciting area of scientific research.

We present a new Arabic annotation web application that aims to associate tags to the words of the vocalized Hadiths corpus. The application assures a collaborative space between many annotators. Each annotator treats one or more Hadith from his/her personal session. We analyze each Hadith using AlKhalil morphological analyzer. The annotator rectifies the analysis and assigns the accurate annotation values. Annotation includes the segmentation of a word, the POS tag, the root and the pattern. The final annotation results of the corpus are structured in XML files. We can display, also, the annotation results in a Treebank. Our tool is considered as a crowdsourcing solution that uses contributions from various annotators to obtain an annotated Arabic coprus. This resource may be used as a standard collection to experiment NLP researches.

Phishing is a security attack to acquire personal information like passwords, credit card details or other account details of a user by means of websites or emails. Phishing websites look similar to the legitimate ones which make it difficult for a layman to differentiate between them. As per the reports of Anti Phishing Working Group (APWG) published in December 2018, phishing against banking services and payment processor was high. Almost all the phishy URLs use HTTPS and use redirects to avoid getting detected. This paper presents a focused literature survey of methods available to detect phishing websites. A comparative study of the in-use anti-phishing tools was accomplished and their limitations were acknowledged. We analyzed the URL-based features used in the past to improve their definitions as per the current scenario which is our major contribution. Also, a step wise procedure of designing an anti-phishing model is discussed to construct an efficient framework which adds to our contribution. Observations made out of this study are stated along with recommendations on existing systems.

The increasing popularity of health monitoring systems has resulted in a surge of research efforts to improve their lifetime. One promising approach is to employ energy harvesting techniques to help recharge the batteries of wireless body sensor networks (WBSN) used in such systems. However, limited energy availability and dynamic environment conditions make the task of managing the limited resources a challenging one. Studies have explored the use of Markov processes to model and predict energy states and artificial neural networks to optimize dynamic slot allocation to maximize lifetime. This paper focuses on the use of dynamic slot allocation for energy-harvesting WBSN for health monitoring systems to maximize lifetime. The paper analyzes the trade-off between system lifetime and number of nodes by proposing a technique to optimize slot allocation based on the node's energy state. Through simulations, the proposed technique is shown to significantly improve system lifetime while maintaining acceptable levels of monitoring performance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in resource management for energy harvesting WBSN used in health monitoring systems.

With the increase in the number of connected objects around us, the concepts of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data are expanding to cover a wide variety of areas of application. This chapter reviews the objects of the IoT as the agents in multi‐agent systems, with the goal of modeling and implementing a multi‐agent architecture in the field of the IoT. It also reviews the different paradigms of the IoT and the links that have been established in the literature between the IoT and multi‐agent systems. In order to experiment the multi‐agent architecture in a real‐world context, the chapter then presents an application of IoT‐a through a set of connected “brick‐screens” that allows programmers to build an interactive and reconfigurable wall of screens. It illustrates this application by visiting the eco‐distributed resolution of the N‐Puzzle algorithm and applying it to the resolution of an N‐puzzle video.

This paper proposes an optimal operation approach for residential electric vehicles (EVs) using deep neural networks (DNN) and clustering-based energy forecast. The forecast is achieved through load modeling and load forecasting based on the predictive models generated through network training. The study suggests that clustering-based forecasting is more accurate than traditional load forecasting methods. The approach utilizes deep learning methods and is capable of providing optimal operation recommendations for EVs based on individual user preferences, traffic patterns, and other relevant factors. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for optimizing the operation of EVs in residential areas, and highlight the potential for future research in this field.

Inverters are widely used as electrical drive systems in many industrial applications. The inverter IGBT switch open-circuit fault; object of our study; is one type of the inverter faults that attracts the attention of many researchers. In this paper an open-circuit fault detection technique is proposed using the artificial neural network (ANN) aided by the Clarke transform. The technique is presented according to two approaches. The first approach calculates the Clarke stator currents and other quantities such as the intervals fault angles α and the trajectory surface S. Once all these quantities are obtained, they are then introduced to the ANN structure for the learning process; the output obtained from the ANN corresponds to the exact angle related to the inverter IGBT switch open-circuit fault. The second approach follows exactly the same calculation steps as the first approach except that in this case all the computation is performed within the ANN architecture. To illustrate the effectiveness of the technique and validate the results, some experimental works are conducted using a three-phase voltage inverter fed induction motor.

Three-dimensional (3D) volumetric neural image segmentation is crucial to reconstructing accurate neuron structures. However, due to the structural complexity of neurons and the diverse imaging qualities of the microscopes, it is challenging to achieve both accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, we propose a teacher-student learning framework for fast neuron segmentation. The segmentation inference is performed using a light-weighted student network which benefits from knowledge distillation of a teacher network with a higher capacity. Evaluated on the Janelia dataset from the BigNeuron project, our proposed framework achieves competitive performance for segmentation accuracy while reducing the computational cost to facilitate large-scale processing.

This paper proposes a decoupled spatial neural attention method for weakly supervised semantic segmentation, which aims to accurately segment images by studying the semantics of the objects present within them. The proposed method is based on the use of detectors that help in recognizing objects in an image, which in turn is used to train the model. The task analysis is carried out to determine the appropriate pipelines required to implement the proposed method. The use of decoupled spatial neural attention allows for the model to focus attention on the relevant parts of the image during training, leading to improved accuracy in object recognition and semantic segmentation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is shown through experiments on benchmark datasets, which demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Overall, the proposed framework can greatly benefit the field of object recognition and semantic segmentation.

BlendCAC is a novel solution that deals with the problem of Authorization in the realm of Internet of Things (IoTs). It combines the concepts of blockchain technology and smart devices to provide a secure and decentralized Capability-Based Access Control. The system appoints a smart contract as a mediator to authenticate the user's access to IoT devices. The smart contract is the key enabler that handles the authorization benefits, as well as the enforcement mechanisms attached to the said benefits. BlendCAC allows for automatic requests and access permission to be granted to smart devices, which improves the security, privacy, and interactivity of the IoT ecosystem. In essence, BlendCAC ensures that unauthorized users are denied access to devices, while ensuring that authorized users have their rights adhered to, making the ecosystem more user-friendly, secure, and efficient.

This research concerns the detection of unauthorised access within hospital networks through the real-time analysis of audit logs. Privacy is a primary concern amongst patients due to the rising adoption of Electronic Patient Record (EPR) systems. There is growing evidence to suggest that patients may withhold information from healthcare providers due to lack of Trust in the security of EPRs. Yet, patient record data must be available to healthcare providers at the point of care. Ensuring privacy and confidentiality of that data is challenging. Roles within healthcare organisations are dynamic and relying on access control is not sufficient. Through proactive monitoring of audit logs, unauthorised accesses can be detected and presented to an analyst for review. Advanced data analytics and visualisation techniques can be used to aid the analysis of big data within EPR audit logs to identify and highlight pertinent data points. Employing a human-in-the-loop model ensures that suspicious activity is appropriately investigated and the data analytics is continuously improving. This paper presents a system that employs a Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (HILML) algorithm, in addition to a density-based local outlier detection model. The system is able to detect 145 anomalous behaviours in an unlabelled dataset of 1,007,727 audit logs. This equates to 0.014% of the EPR accesses being labelled as anomalous in a specialist Liverpool (UK) hospital.

This paper explores the use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to design an effective scheduling function in Software-Defined Networks (SDN). The goal is to optimize the dispatching of packets among switches in the network while taking into account time factors and process control. Artificial neural networks are used to model the scheduling function and provide an efficient way of learning the best dispatching policy. The paper presents a detailed description of the DRL algorithm used for training and evaluates its performance in a simulated SDN environment. Results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed DRL-based scheduling function compared to traditional scheduling methods. It is concluded that DRL-based scheduling has great potential to revolutionize the way SDNs operate and open up new possibilities for the design of efficient and scalable networks.

Millimeter wave (MmWave) is a promising technology nowadays because it provides users with ultra-high data rate links with low latency time. Hence, internet of things, tactile internet and cloud computing applications which becomes an essential matter in 5G networks can be supported using it. MmWave standard, IEEE 802.11 ad, proposed using scheduled medium access control (MAC) based on time division multiple access (TDMA) to share radio resources among active mmWave users. MmWave has a highly dynamic time-variant channel with high blocking probability which highly degrades the entire system performance. Hence, applying simple channel independent scheduling schemes, e.g., round robin (RR), will be inefficient. Thus, an efficient radio resource scheduling with considering the changes in mmWave channel is needed for maximum benefit from available resources. This paper presents the performance evaluation of one of the channel sensitive scheduling schemes, proportional fairness scheduling (PFS), in downlink mmWave network by executing numerical simulation in different channel conditions and various mmWave beamwidths regarding the total system data rate and fairness between users.
