An online dual estimation algorithm is developed to jointly estimate in real-time traffic quantities such as queue lengths, occupancies and flows, as well as the parameters of a macroscopic model of a signalized junction. These parameters include turning ratios and saturation flows, together with model uncertainties. The proposed novel methodology is based on the Expectation-Maximization algorithm, modified for real-time estimation, with a Kalman filter implementing the expectation step and a multivariate gradient-based approach for the maximisation step. The algorithm is validated by simulating the typical signalized 3-arm and 4-arm junctions. This work is aimed to form a part of the adaptive control loops for traffic light systems that are able to autonomously adjust with changing traffic conditions, so as to ensure efficient vehicle flows.

Malaria is a deadly disease that can affect a large population in a short period of time. In order to prevent and control malaria outbreaks, it is crucial to predict and anticipate them. In recent years, machine learning and deep learning approaches have shown great potential in predicting disease outbreaks. This paper reviews and analyzes the use of classification algorithms and prediction algorithms in mathematical models for predicting malaria outbreaks. Furthermore, the paper specifically focuses on the role of deep learning and how it contributes to improving predictions. Humidity is identified as a key factor that affects the spread of malaria and is incorporated into the mathematical models used in the analysis. Overall, this paper provides insight into the use of machine learning and deep learning approaches in predicting malaria outbreaks and highlights the importance of considering various factors in the development of mathematical models.

The paper describes the comparison of saliency maps calculated for a specific type of images to the ground truth fixations obtained in eye tracking experiment. The images being analyzed contained camouflaged animals. Because of the camouflage, it was expected that calculation of saliency would be the hard case. Several saliency maps were compared to the ground truth with a set of standard measures and a ranking based on their averaged performance was proposed. The results reveal that for the saliency map models, images of camouflaged animals are harder to analyze than ordinary ones, although, one model - Judd - appeared to work particularly well. Additionally, susceptibility of saliency maps to the perceived difficulty of the camouflage was discussed.

Image segmentation plays a key role in many medical imaging applications, especially in Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) system for mammography. A good segmentation allows increasing the performance and efficiency of CAD system that enables the radiologist to conduct a clear diagnostic analysis and to make better decisions; this requires effective tools and techniques. This paper proposes a new method to extract the mass from the Region of Interest (ROI) based on texture features and Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering with setting c= 2, whereas the user selects the region of interest manually. The process of clustering is applying within an appropriate range limited by the maximum of intensity and a threshold defined by the big changes in the texture features levels. The proposed method is applied to Mini-MIAS database and then its performance is compared with some explored methods. In this study, the result of overlap measure (AOM) was achieved approximately 81%.

In this paper, the problem of the model parameter estimation for in-pipe walking robots has been studied. Three estimators (regressor function-based method and the least squares-based methods with and without damping) are studied and analyzed. The study is focused on the influence the sensor resolution has on the accuracy of the estimation. The influence the accuracy of the initial estimation has on the methods' performance was also discussed. Two performance functions are proposed in order to simplify the analysis. It was shown that the least squares method has a significant advantage when the exact information about the robot's state is known; however, when the sensors have finite resolution, the performance of this method changes significantly while the regressor-based method is affected much less.

Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) has attracted tremendous attention owing to its cost efficiency in electricity and sustainable development. NILM aims at acquiring individual appliance power consumption rates using an aggregated power smart meter reading. Each individual appliance's power consumption enables users to monitor their electricity usage habits for rational saving strategies. This is also a valuable tool for detecting failure in appliances. However, the major barriers facing NILM schemes are issues of accurately capturing the features of each appliance and decreasing the computing time. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a new, efficient, and accurate NILM scheme, consisting of a learning step and a decomposing step. In the learning step, we propose the fast search-and-find of density peaks (FSFDPs) clustering algorithm aimed at capturing the features of the power consumption patterns of appliances. In the decomposing step, we propose a genetic algorithm (GA)-based matching algorithm to estimate the power consumption of each individual appliance using the aggregated power reading. Using elitist and catastrophic strategies, this step reduces the searching space to achieve considerable efficiency. Experimental results using the reference energy disaggregation dataset (REDD) indicate that our proposed scheme promotes accuracy by 10% and reduces the decomposing time by half.

In recent years, water quality monitoring has become increasingly important for the health and wellbeing of both humans and ecosystems. The development of a multi-fog based water quality monitoring system using a bio-sensing platform is introduced in this paper. The proposed system utilizes sensors to capture data on various water quality parameters and cloud computing for real-time monitoring and data analysis. The collected data is stored in databases for future reference and analysis. Logic gates have been employed to provide efficient decision-making based on the data generated by the sensors. The system is highly efficient, cost-effective, and provides a suitable approach for monitoring water quality in real-time. The proposed system offers huge potential to improve water quality monitoring systems, enabling the creation of efficient strategies for water resource management.

In order to improve the performance of 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) beamforming in multi-core Radio over Fiber systems, static skew compensation is proposed as a solution. This compensation technique involves adjusting the delays between the transmitting antennas in the system to account for the differences in the antenna radiation patterns. The system also utilizes optical fiber networks to transmit the signals, which allows for higher bandwidth capabilities. Additionally, Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is used to further increase the bandwidth and improve transmission efficiency. The compensation technique involves adjusting the antenna feeds to compensate for the skew, which can significantly improve the signal quality and overall performance of the system. Overall, the integration of static skew compensation, OFDM, and optical fiber networks represent promising solutions for improving the performance of multi-core Radio over Fiber systems for 5G mmWave beamforming.

This paper focuses on the performance investigations of Adaptive Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) controlled Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF). The use of Artificial Neural Networks in SAPF systems has proven to be successful in filtering harmonics from power systems. In this study, the harmonic analysis of the SAPF system with adaptive ANN control is conducted to evaluate its effectiveness in mitigating power harmonics. The Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) technique is also utilized in controlling switch mode of SAPF system. The paper highlights the importance of proper training of ANN for effective control of SAPF system. Besides, it is also shown that adaptive ANN controlled SAPF system with SVPWM technique is able to effectively eliminate power harmonics resulting in a more reliable and efficient power system.

Image deraining is an important area in machine vision, which aims to enhance the visibility of images that have been corrupted by rain or other environmental factors. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image deraining based on weighted nuclear norm and total variation (TV) regularization. Our method uses matrix decomposition techniques and optimization algorithms to estimate the clean image from the observed rainy image. We introduce a new weighting scheme based on the nuclear norm and TV regularization, which allows us to balance the importance of low-rank structures and texture details in the rain image. To solve the optimization problem efficiently, we adopt machine learning techniques, such as stochastic gradient descent and ADMM. We validate our method on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the visibility and quality of the derailed images. Our method can be regarded as a promising solution to the problem of image deraining in machine vision.

This paper presents a case for exploiting underutilized resources in heterogeneous mobile architectures. Specifically, the paper focuses on the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) and their potential in reducing energy consumption in mobile devices. The authors analyze different tasks that mobile devices commonly perform, including kernel computations, digital signal processing, computer vision, and graphics rendering. By assessing the suitability of each task for GPU acceleration, the authors demonstrate that underutilized resources can be leveraged to provide significant energy savings. Overall, the paper presents a compelling argument for the need to exploit underutilized resources in heterogeneous mobile architectures, particularly regarding the use of GPUs. The authors suggest that future research should explore how to optimize GPU usage for specific mobile workloads, and how to design new mobile architectures that better leverage these underutilized resources.

The increasing availability of user-generated reviews for products and services has led to the development of various techniques for sentiment analysis. In this study, we propose a transfer learning framework for analyzing the sentiment of movie reviews, called STAR (Sentiment Transfer Analysis with Ratings). Our approach utilizes the variations in emotions expressed in the reviews and incorporates them into predictive models to improve the accuracy of analytical models. The proposed framework combines data mining techniques with machine learning algorithms to predict the star rating of reviews accurately. The results of our study show that the STAR framework significantly outperforms existing sentiment analysis methods and provides a more accurate prediction of the emotion expressed in user-generated content. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework has wide applicability in the field of information and communication technology, where reliable and accurate analysis of user-generated content is essential. Overall, this study demonstrates that integrating transfer learning with predictive models can lead to more accurate and effective sentiment analysis.

This paper proposes an Adaptive Neural Event-Triggered Control algorithm for Discrete-Time Strict-Feedback Nonlinear Systems. The algorithm leverages Artificial Neural Networks and Adaptive Systems to provide bandwidth-efficient and real-time control. The proposed technique triggers control actions only when necessary, leading to a reduction in control energy and improving the closed-loop system's stability. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated on nonlinear dynamical systems using a simulation-based study, and the results show that it outperforms conventional control techniques in terms of stability and control-efficiency. This study highlights the potential of event-triggered control for nonlinear dynamical systems and highlights the role of Artificial Neural Networks in providing efficient and robust control algorithms.

Telemedicine technology provides a promising approach to bring high-quality medical services to individuals regardless of geographic barriers. In telemedicine systems, medical diagnostic imaging is a major application that requires secure and efficient data sharing to achieve accurate diagnosis and timely treatment. However, the sensitive nature of medical data poses a challenge to ensuring the privacy and security of patients' health information. Blockchain and cryptography are touted as two key technologies that can address these challenges. In this paper, we propose a flexible and efficient blockchain-based ABE scheme with multi-authority for medical on demand in telemedicine systems. Our proposed scheme leverages cloud computing to enable effective data sharing while ensuring data privacy and confidentiality via blockchain and cryptography. The proposed scheme also features a multi-authority design that facilitates efficient access control and revocation of revoked users. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme provides a high level of security, is efficient in data sharing, and is capable of supporting multiple medical services in telemedicine systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive approach to logic-functional modeling of nonlinear radio engineering systems. The main focus of the study is to develop a mathematical model for such systems, which can provide a deep understanding of their behavior and performance. The paper also discusses inverse problems, which are an essential part of developing efficient solutions for these systems. Furthermore, the authors highlight the importance of grammar and integrated circuit modeling in the design process of nonlinear systems. The paper demonstrates how computational modeling can be used to simulate and analyze the performance of such systems, and how it can facilitate the exploration of various design options. Finally, the authors emphasize the role of industrial engineering in the optimization of these systems, especially in terms of improving their efficiency and reliability. Overall, this paper provides insightful information for researchers and practitioners in the field of nonlinear radio engineering systems.

Voice disorders, which can help in the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD), can be measured with acoustic tools. In this work, demographic data and vocal phonation records /a/ from the available mPower database were analyzed to identify PD patients. A parsimonious model was then found that achieved a reduction from 62 to 5 phonation characteristics, which were considered in addition to gender and age. Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Logistic Regression (LR) neural networks were used to obtain a model with high prediction capacity (area under receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC-ROC, over 0.82). This work contributes to the monitoring of EP patients from the recording of a few phonation features collected by means of a mobile phone.

In this study, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) analysis was performed on genes expression datasets of maize nested association mapping (NAM) to classify the organ-specific expression of genes. Results showed that the KNN algorithm was able to confidently classify genes into their respective organ-specific expression groups, with the "ear" organ showing the most distinct gene expression profile. The use of bioinformatics methods in gene expression analysis has enabled researchers to gain a better understanding of the genetic mechanisms underlying organ-specific development in maize. Machine learning techniques, such as the KNN algorithm used in this study, enable the testing and classification of large datasets with high accuracy. The training of such algorithms can aid in the identification of previously unknown relationships between gene expression and organ-specific development, making it an essential tool in the field of plant genetics research.

This paper proposes a kinship verification method that combines deep and tensor features through extreme learning machine (ELM) algorithm. Tensors are utilized to represent the facial images in higher dimensional space, and deep features are extracted through a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to capture the intrinsic characteristics of the facial images. The extracted features are then fed into an ELM classifier for kinship verification. The proposed method is tested on several kinship verification databases and achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in tackling the challenges of kinship verification. Furthermore, the proposed method can be applied to other visual measurement tasks and has potential for widespread adoption in various industries. The contribution of this research is presented in a number of conferences and academic publications.

As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to expand, the need for secure and efficient protocols for authentication and key exchange becomes increasingly important. The implementation of Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) protocols provides a secure method for authentication and key exchange, in which an entity can prove knowledge of a secret without revealing it. Identity-Based Authentication (IBA) further simplifies the authentication process by using an individual's unique identity as their public key. These methods protect against attacks on the anonymity of an entity in a public key system. The immune system of the IoT network can be enhanced through the use of these protocols, ensuring that only authorized entities can access the network. This paper explores the application of ZKP and IBA protocols in the IoT, highlighting their benefits in providing secure and efficient authentication and key exchange for an increasingly interconnected world.

This paper introduces the Partial-Value Association Discovery Algorithm (PAD), which is a machine learning technique that utilizes decision trees to uncover associations in data. The algorithm is particularly suited for data mining applications in the field of telecommunications traffic, where large amounts of data are generated daily. The paper also highlights the usefulness of clustering algorithms in identifying patterns in the data. The research focuses on the application of PAD in the telecommunications industry and highlights its potential to aid in systems engineering and theory. The study aims to provide insights into how PAD can be used to improve decision-making processes and enhance system performance. Finally, the paper emphasizes the importance of engineering students learning about data mining and machine learning techniques like PAD, as they have the potential to bring significant advancements to various industries.

The cloud computing concepts in last decade unexpectedly changed human's life with considerable features to convert the traditional computing to the ubiquitous one. For each untrustworthy technology like cloud, needing a great Infrastructure for Defense in confront of malicious attack is crucial subject.This paper describes some features of cloud, like service model, type of deployment model (Private, Community, Public, Hybrid), type of trust management used in the cloud and an overview of the proposed model for fuzzy trust systems helping the trust system to have more accuracy.

In the real world, an attribute value is perceived differently by different individuals. Emphasizing on this aspect, we extend the discrete choice models with perceived values that are subjective and specific to a decision-maker (DM). The proposed choice models are augmented with the parameters of an entropy function, besides the utility coefficients, to model a DM's complex choice behavior. A variety of higher order choice models are also proposed. The proposed models are further extended with a DM's reference-value for each attribute. A real and illustrative application is included.

This study investigates the changes in spontaneous activity and evoked response in dissociated neuronal networks when exposed to 100ms temporal stimulation. The biological neural networks were trained and their firing properties were observed using electrodes. The study aimed to analyze the effects of different protocols on the activity of the neurons and their ability to perform specific tasks. The task analysis revealed that the neuronal networks responded differently to various protocols, indicating the importance of optimizing stimulation parameters for specific neural tasks. This research contributes to the understanding of neuronal network activity and the design of stimulation protocols for therapeutic interventions.

Trustworthiness in an online environment is essential because individuals and organizations can easily be misled by false and malicious information receiving from untrustworthy users. Though existing methods assess users' trustworthiness by exploiting Twitter account properties, their efficacy is inadequate because of Twitter's restriction on profile and tweet size, the existence of missing or insufficient profiles, and ease to create fake accounts or relationships to pretend as trustworthy. In this paper, we present a holistic approach by exploiting ideas perceived from real-world organizations for trust estimation along with available Twitter information. Users' trustworthiness is determined by considering their credentials, recommendation from referees and the quality of the information in their Twitter accounts and tweets. We establish the feasibility of our approach analytically and further devise a multi-objective cost function for the A* search to find a quasi-optimal path between the trust evaluator and the user whose trustworthiness is being evaluated. We also propose an incentive mechanism to increase user participation in the trust evaluation process, and a threat model and trustworthiness measure of referees to thwart the possibility of providing an untruthful recommendation to inflate one's trustworthiness. The efficacy of our proposed approach is validated through experiments using Twitter data and extensive simulation in various scenarios.

This research proposes a secure data getting/transmitting protocol for wireless sensor networks (WSN) in the internet of things (IoT) using revocable storage identity-based cryptography. With the increasing number of IoT devices and the sensitive data they transmit, it is crucial to develop secure protocols that can protect data from unauthorized access. The proposed protocol leverages identity-based encryption to ensure confidentiality and integrity of data transmission. In addition, revocable storage is incorporated to allow for efficient management of revoked devices and keys. The protocol is designed to be lightweight and efficient for WSN devices with limited processing power and memory resources. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol achieves excellent performance in terms of data confidentiality, message authentication, and revocation management. This research contributes to the development of secure protocols for WSN in IoT applications and lays a foundation for future research in this area.

In today's day and age, information systems have become an integral part of academia. With the rise of technology, academic institutions have begun to rely on information systems to a great extent. However, it is important to ensure that these information systems are of high quality. The evaluation of these academic information systems quality instruments (AISQI) is crucial to determine their usability, security, and overall effectiveness. Quality models engineering has become increasingly popular to evaluate the quality of AISQI. The use of ISO and IEC standards has played a significant role in establishing quality models and ensuring the compliance of the AISQI. In addition to these standards, artificial intelligence has emerged as a promising approach towards evaluating the quality of AISQI. The usability of academic information systems instruments is another important parameter that determines their effectiveness. Hence, the development of quality models that consider usability as an essential parameter has become crucial. Overall, the engineering of quality models for the evaluation of AISQI is of utmost importance to ensure the quality and effectiveness of the information systems used in academia.

Mission Critical Services (MCS) are gaining interest among network operators to offer alternative communications than conventional trunked radio systems. They promise a simplified management of cloud and radio resources for service deployment. However, the network capabilities should be adapted for the changing conditions, to assure low-latency and reliability for such applications. This paper presents an on-going work on utilising 5G technology for Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) services. It describes some design elements and evaluates 5G ESSENCE architecture that enable mission critical applications.

Routing protocols are widely used in robot sensing systems to ensure efficient communication among multiple agents. While many routing protocols have been proposed, Q-learning-based geographic routing protocol is gaining increasing attention due to its effective optimization of packet delivery in wireless sensor networks. However, one of the challenges is the design of the reward function for the Q-learning algorithm. In this paper, we propose a reward function learning approach that adjusts the reward function based on the system's performance. The proposed approach optimizes the Q-learning-based geographic routing protocol to adapt to the dynamic environment and obtain better routing performance. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed reward function learning approach achieves better packet delivery rates and energy efficiency compared with other relevant methods. This work can provide a guideline for designing reinforcement learning-based routing protocols in wireless sensor networks.

Cloud computing platforms provide a flexible and scalable way to manage and deploy virtual resources. One of the key challenges in this field is to optimize the configuration of cloud platforms to provide the best performance to users. In this paper, we propose a method based on virtual machine technology to optimize the configuration of cloud platform resources. To evaluate our approach, we conducted a series of experiments on a cloud computing platform. The results show that our method can significantly improve the performance of cloud platform resources while reducing the amount of bandwidth required. Our approach takes into account the use case of handheld computers with limited processing power and bandwidth. We discuss the implications of virtual machining and system modeling in optimizing cloud platform resources. This research provides the basis for future work in the development of optimized configurations for cloud servers, as well as future research in cloud computing optimization. The proposed method has been presented and discussed at several conferences, including those specifically focused on cloud computing. Overall, our approach contributes to the ongoing efforts to create better cloud computing platforms and provides new insights into the future direction of this rapidly evolving field.

Community structure detection in social networks has become a big challenge. Various methods in the literature have been presented to solve this challenge. Recently, several methods have also been proposed to solve this challenge based on a mapping-reduction model, in which data and algorithms are divided between different process nodes so that the complexity of time and memory of community detection in large social networks is reduced. In this paper, a mapping-reduction model is first proposed to detect the structure of communities. Then the proposed framework is rewritten according to a new mechanism called distributed cache memory; distributed cache memory can store different values associated with different keys and, if necessary, put them at different computational nodes. Finally, the proposed rewritten framework has been implemented using SPARK tools and its implementation results have been reported on several major social networks. The performed experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed framework by varying the values of various parameters.

In recent years, stock forecasting has become an increasingly important research topic for financial analysts and investors. This paper proposes a new stock forecasting method that combines a Stacked Denoising Autoencoder (SDAE) and Backpropagation (BP) algorithm. The proposed method aims to enhance the accuracy of stock forecasting through a multilayer neural network structure that integrates the biological neural network model with predictive models. The proposed method also utilizes a training process to adapt the SDAE and BP algorithm to stock data. Additionally, we investigate the effectiveness of noise reduction techniques on stock prediction and explore the utilization of Neurons in improving forecast accuracy. Our experiments show that the proposed method outperforms traditional forecasting methods, and demonstrates the potential for the proposed method to be used in stock prediction applications. Overall, these results provide new insights into using machine learning algorithms combined with biological neural networks for stock forecasting.

In this paper, a novel low-complexity channel estimation algorithm with estimation error suppression based on the conventional least squares (LS) method is proposed for downlink narrowband internet of things (NB-IoT) systems. This algorithm suppresses channel estimation error by employing additional operations on conventional LS method without exploiting extra frequency-band resources. The potentiality of the proposed algorithm is substantiated through extensive simulations in terms of channel mean square error (MSE) and block error rate (BLER) against signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Simulation results vindicate that our proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional LS algorithm.

This paper presents a real-time application of a data-mining method with the purpose of indirect contingency screening, by rapid recognition of hazardous, reoccurring power-system operating conditions. The method, suitable for real-time applications, is demonstrated using the Slovenian power-system model for first-swing stability issues. The presented demonstration is segmented into a few parts. First, a database containing a set of pre-fault operating conditions (represented by a measurement matrix) and critical clearing times corresponding to several contingencies is constructed. Measurements matrix from the database is decomposed using the principal component analysis method and represented in a coordinate system defined by the principal components as dense clusters of points. Consequentially, monitoring real-time steady-state conditions in terms of seeking similarity to existing database clusters is facilitated (global screening). This is established by identifying the shortest Euclidean distance metric in the mentioned coordinate system. Finally, a second-stage (local) screening is applied in order to adaptively account for the fluctuating sensitivity of contingencies to variations in pre-fault operating conditions. In this manner, an accurate indication of each contingency impact is provided rapidly as long as a similar operating state exists within the database. Otherwise, the case is thoroughly investigated and added to the database as a new entry. This approach is applicable to a wide spectrum of dynamic problems, considering that problem-relevant sets of input data are available.

In this paper, we introduce a novel algorithm for analyzing and developing the in-vehicle hand-usage of a smartphone while driving. We propose the use of acceleration and angular velocity sensors for feature extraction, which captures the unique hand movements of drivers. The algorithm utilizes advanced signal processing algorithms to analyze the data and provide real-time feedback to drivers. This approach holds great potential for improving the safety of vehicles on the road, as it will enable the prevention of accidents caused by smartphone use while driving. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through extensive experimentation with different vehicles and engine types, and evaluate its accuracy under various driving scenarios. Overall, our method represents a significant step forward in the development of safer and more effective vehicle technology.

The application of mobile cloud computing has been rapidly increasing in recent years due to its potential in providing ubiquitous access to a wide range of applications and services. In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed for estimating purchase incentive of the public based on mobile cloud computing. The proposed algorithm is based on various techniques such as cloud computing, games, mathematical model, evolutionary computation, computational modeling, peer-to-peer computing, and stochastic processes. This algorithm takes into account various factors that influence purchase incentives such as customers' preferences, product features, price, promotion, and competitors' offerings. The proposed algorithm aims to optimize purchase incentives by predicting customers' purchase behavior and providing personalized recommendations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in improving purchase incentives for both customers and businesses.

In recent years, Wireless Body area network (WBAN) has become an active field of research and development because of its great potential to improve the quality of health care through continuous monitoring of health status and early detection of possible problems. One of the main issues in such network is the design of a Medium Access Control (MAC) protocol that plays a vital role for the efficient functionality of WBANs. In this article, we propose a classification of MAC protocols based on their trends and strategies in WBAN healthcare applications. Then, we explain briefly several MAC protocols and we compare them based on their salient features. The aim of the current paper is to serve as a reference for the new researchers and to provide a better understanding of the research directions in this scientific area.

The paper represents the model of AC drive control system. An analysis of conventional drive control system has been performed, its advantages and disadvantages, and preconditions for use of intelligent approaches for implementation of control systems for this kind of objects have been estimated. The intelligent system is supposed to be modeled with use of fuzzy logic controller and different inference algorithms for implementation of control laws in various control loops. Dynamic characteristics of the system both for conventional case and with use of controllers based on fuzzy set theory have been analyzed. The practicability of using the multi-cascade fuzzy systems while implementation of unified intelligent control module and different combinations of fuzzy inference algorithms has been demonstrated for complex drive systems. Application of this technology allows implementation of control system for the entire class of drive systems considering all special aspects and relationships between the coordinates in the complex control object. Additionally, modeling of spacial membership function using multi-cascade fuzzy controller will give a possibility to avoid a variety of quantitative and qualitative restrictions due to complex relations between the coordinate in such systems.

Spatiotemporal processing, including many tasks such as speech recognition, object tracking, and natural language processing, still faces great challenges. The developmental network-1 (DN-1) was proposed as a spatiotemporal processing algorithm with general purposes in the sense of turing machines (TM). DN-1 used emergent motor vectors as contexts for top-down attention, which is conducive for temporal processing. This also enables finite automaton (FA), which is the control of TM, to incrementally emerge inside DN-1. But the hidden areas of DN-1 have a fixed boundary. In the proposed new model-developmental network-2 (DN-2)-each hidden neuron automatically discovers its neuron-wise inhibition zone based on incremental statistics. Therefore, not only the number of hidden areas is dynamic, so are their interconnections. We first present this new network through a visual toy problem. Then, we conducted phoneme recognition experiments to investigate DN-2's performance in various settings. Based on the experimental results, we analyzed how the new mechanisms enabled DN-2 to automatically generate a dynamic hierarchy and improve the performance. This paper is a step toward our goal of applying DN-2 to a wide variety of spatiotemporal processing tasks.

Photovoltaic (PV) systems are nowadays one of the most wide-spread renewable energy systems in the network or grid with one purpose to improve the reliability of the grid. However, PV systems in the network also contribute a negative impact as well; when the main grid fails to supply the load and there is a part of the load energized by the PV systems while being isolated. This case is defined as islanding. If this condition cannot be detected, the load bus will experience voltage disturbance and power quality problem. This paper presents an islanding detection using Artificial Neural Network method (ANN). ANN learning data are generated from simulations under three main scenarios: power match, overvoltage, and undervoltage, with varying power factor (cos phi). Voltage signal at PCC node in load bus is classified to identify if system is in islanding condition or not. The simulation results shows that the built ANN is capable to detect both islanding and non-islanding mode.

Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) cooperation in cluster-to-cluster communication has shown improved network quality of services by utilizing less transmission power over the fading environment. This is an enhancement from the traditional cluster-based single-input single-output multi-hop relaying used in vehicular communications. In this paper, we deploy multi-hop MIMO clustering relay into vehicular communication for a two-lane road transportation scenario. We deploy precoder and receiver filter in each MIMO link that is characterized by a narrowband classical three-dimensional time-varying channel. With the aid of the precoder and minimum mean square error receiver filtering algorithm in MIMO communication, we derive the end-to-end network signal-to-noise ratio to find the optimal best path using max-min theory with equal power allocation in precoder matrices that minimizes the network mean square error. A low-cost close-optimal best path selection method is also proposed through mathematical modeling. Computer simulation results demonstrate the validity of the theoretical investigations in this work.

This paper studies a virtual resequencing problem for automobile mixed-model assembly lines, in which preassigned configurations are rearranged to cars without changing their original sequence positions. The objective is to evenly smooth the material requirements induced by the production sequence over time. A mathematical programing model is presented to describe the problem. Three heuristic procedures based on beam search are developed aiming at quickly seeking optimal or near-optimal solutions. Computational experiments show that all the proposed algorithms perform well. Among them, the iterated beam search algorithm generally has the best performance. Besides, it produces almost as good resequencing results as CPLEX in very short time durations.

This paper presents a novel integrated data compression and pulse rate measurement scheme for power reduction in Internet-of-Things (IoT) enabled wireless PPG monitoring devices. In the proposed scheme, the recorded photoplethysmograph (PPG) signal is compressed using the differential pulse code modulation and Huffman coding techniques and then the pulse rate (PR) is simultaneously extracted from the differential signal, which is the difference between the original and predicted signals. The proposed scheme achieves an average compression ratio, percentage root-mean-squared difference (PRD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and normalized cross correlation (NCC) of 4.76, 0.19%, 27.90 dB and 0.9991 respectively for the 5 s PPG signals digitized with a sampling rate of 100 Hz and resolution of 12 bits, on the three standard PPG databases (MIT-BIH SLP, MIMIC-II and CSL). Evaluation results show that the method yields peak detection rates of 98.94% and average PR measurement error of 0-2.6 samples. The proposed integrated scheme can enable timely measurement of the pulse rate (PR) and to significantly reduce the overall power consumption and therefore it is highly suited for IoT wireless wearable PPG sensors.

This paper is concerned with the sliding mode control (SMC) via finite-time stabilization (FTS) for a class of conic-type nonlinear semi-Markovian jumping systems (SMJSs). Comparing with the classical Markovian jumping systems, the transition rates of SMJSs are related to the random sojourn-time g. Based on this, a suitable SMC law for driving the state trajectories to the designed sliding surface within a finite-time interval is given. Then, the FTS over reaching phase and sliding motion phase is further proved to guarantee the FTS of the whole SMJSs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by a time-delayed Chua's circuit simulation.

This paper proposes a rule-based classifier with accurate and fast rule term induction for continuous attributes. The classifier utilizes decision trees and classification algorithms to generate accurate rules for classification. The training process involves obtaining training data and fitting a Gaussian distribution to each continuous attribute in order to calculate probabilities. The rule induction process is fast and efficient with the use of heuristic algorithms. Experimental results show that the proposed classifier outperforms other rule-based classifiers in terms of accuracy and speed. Thus, this approach can be useful for practical applications that require efficient and accurate classification of continuous attributes.

In a liberalized deregulated environment, Electric Load Power Forecasting (ELPF) is an important process in any power system network to make it an efficient, secure and customer friendly network. The proposed day-ahead ELPF models are built on a new multiple parallel inputs and output architecture with selected calendar, weather and lagged load power features. In these, the calendar and lagged load power features are kept as constants and weather as a variable feature so that influence of weather on accuracy of day-ahead ELPF can be investigated by different combinational selection of weather variables. The real time data used for this research work were collected from Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (TPDDL). The models are developed using both multivariate linear regression (MvLR) and feed forward back propagation artificial neural network (ANN) techniques which are implemented using Matlab programming environment. The performance evaluation criteria for ELPF are presented with determination of various statistical errors. The performance of each model is analyzed and the results are presented. The proposed models yield an average forecast error of 2.9% to 3.5% for day-ahead hourly forecast, throughout the year, irrespective of variations in weather. The proposed day-ahead ELPF models are evident for its simplicity, less measurement requirement and easiness in implementation with higher accuracy.

Multistatic localization is a technique for determining the position of a target using multiple receivers and radio transmitters. However, when the transmitter position is unknown, this approach becomes challenging. This paper proposes a method for multistatic localization in the absence of transmitter position information. The approach relies on estimation algorithms, which consider time delays as measurements to estimate the target's position. By using multiple receivers, the algorithm can estimate the target's position accurately. The proposed method is validated by comparing it to other approaches that rely on the transmitter position. The results show that the proposed method provides accurate position measurements, even in situations where the signal noise and the number of receivers vary. This research presents a significant contribution to the field, as it enables multistatic localization even when the transmitter position is unknown, expanding the application range of this technique.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a popular concept that intends connecting a large number of physical objects to exchange data between one another. However, the huge volume of data exchanged, the existence of resource constrained devices, heterogeneity and mobility support, challenge the design of a good network in term of performance in IoT environment. Recently, Named Data Networking (NDN) is proposed as a promising networking architecture for future Internet to effectively distribute the massive amount of automated data. NDN which features naming for communication, security, in-network caching and mobility support makes it more suitable for IoT. In this paper, we study the potential behind using the NDN in IoT environment by discussing the main beneficial NDN features for IoT. Subsequently, we discuss the proposed NDN-based IoT applications encountered in the literature, based on that we propose a taxonomy of different applications. Furthermore, we present a comprehensive survey on NDN based content forwarding strategies for NDN-IoT environments with appropriate classification.

We all are witnesses of birth of the new technology called Internet of Things (IoT). The network of things communicating not only with people, but communicating with each other generate a vast number of data called Big Data. Big Data constitute an almost inexhaustible source of knowledge for companies. Knowledge about clients, competitors, markets and whole environment. It is a great opportunity for organizations based on knowledge management to take a competitive advantage. The growing role of Knowledge Management in the organization is discussed at the beginning. Then IoT and Big Data technologies are presented as a teleinformatic background of intelligent organizations. All considerations lead to the presentation of the most important organizational implications caused by IoT and Big Data usage and new business models that can be a valuable source of competitive advantage on dynamically changing market where demand for instant information and generated knowledge is still growing and becomes a key feature in meeting the customer expectations.

For the downstream direction, the sharing is performed by the evolved node B station (eNB) and the reassembly is provided by the mobile. Long‐Term Evolution (LTE) and Wi‐Fi carrier aggregation can be implemented with collocated or remote eNB and access point (AP) entities. The radio channel operating in the licensed band supports control plane and traffic plane. If the channel is free, then the data is transmitted immediately to the beginning of the next frame. status report message is used differently for LTE access and Wi‐Fi access. For LTE access, during the recovery procedure following a cell change, it indicates a list of packet data convergence protocol (PDCP) frame numbers not received during the handover. Robust header compression (ROHC) mechanism Feedback message is related to the compression mechanism of the headers. It contains the first sequence number of the missing PDCP frames.

Summarizing cricket matches is a labor intensive task that demands a certain level of proficiency. The paper proposes a novel method for automatically detecting and summarizing important events in a cricket match. Our model takes into input the video recording of the entire cricket match and returns the most important clips of the game as the output. Techniques like optical character recognition, sound detection and replay detection have been used to extract important events such as boundaries, wickets and other playfield scenarios in a cricket match. These events are then clipped together to form the entire highlight for the cricket match. We performed several qualitative and quantitative experiments to evaluate our model. Our model achieves an accuracy of 89.45% to detect events like wickets, fours and sixes which indicates the usefulness of the model in real life scenarios.

With the increasing complexity of computer systems and networks, anomaly detection has become an essential task for ensuring system security and stability. In this paper, we propose a convolutional auto-encoder method for anomaly detection on system logs. Our approach uses two-dimensional displays to visualize the log data, and extracts meaningful features using ant colony optimization. Support vector machines and decision trees are used for classification, allowing the method to deal with both supervised and unsupervised scenarios. Experiments on real-world system logs show that our method achieves high accuracy in detecting anomalies, and outperforms several state-of-the-art algorithms. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various domains, such as network intrusion detection and cybersecurity. This study demonstrates the value of machine learning techniques in enabling effective anomaly detection, and provides a practical solution to improve system security and stability.

This paper presents a novel approach to fast and low-precision learning in GPU-accelerated spiking neural networks. The focus of this study is on the behavior of neurons and synapses, which are simulated using stochastic processes. The learning process is unsupervised, relying on the use of graphics processing units and computational modeling to achieve efficient performance. One of the main contributions of this work is the use of fast frequency control mechanisms to regulate the threshold of firing neurons, which leads to improved accuracy and faster convergence. Overall, this paper provides a promising avenue for the development of high-performance spiking neural networks, with potential applications in machine learning and artificial intelligence.

This paper proposes a novel approach to detect the start and end time of pitches in baseball videos, which enables automatic pitching trajectory analysis using computer vision. The proposed method utilizes multiple cameras to capture the game from different angles and generates a 3D trajectory for each pitch. The trajectory data can be used to develop predictive models that help coaches and players improve their gameplay. The proposed approach has been presented at several sports conferences and has attracted attention from researchers working on trajectory analysis in other sports. Overall, this research provides significant contributions to the field of sports computer vision and the analysis of trajectory data for games such as baseball.

This paper explores the use of WLAN physical layer information for intelligent contactless gesture recognition. Gesture recognition can be used in a range of applications, and this technology has gained significant attention in recent years. The authors propose a method based on Fresnel reflection and Hidden Markov models (HMMs), which provides accurate recognition of a variety of gestures. The proposed method involves the extraction of features from the physical layer of wireless fidelity (WiFi) signals, which are then fed into the HMMs to classify the gestures. The authors highlight the advantages of using WiFi signals for gesture recognition, including cost-effectiveness, low power consumption, and the availability of sensors. The results of the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, with high accuracy achieved across the tested gestures. Overall, this paper provides a significant contribution to the field of contactless gesture recognition, and the proposed method holds promise for future applications in areas such as Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) and smart homes.

In recent years, we observe an exponential growth of "Smart Industry" concept that relies on the use of software and hardware systems to analyze data from several types of smart sensors by various types of models: mathematical, computational, data, etc. A set of such virtual models, representing processes, systems and equipment is called "Digital Twins" (DTs). DTs use data gathered from the sensory systems on production lines to predict failures of machinery, optimize the quality of the products, and reduce the ecological footprint from facilities. They can be described as a sequence of jobs that perform required functionality linked together by a set of edges that represent data dependencies. To organize a flexible cloud computing support for the Digital Twin execution, we propose a concept of Micro-Workflows that combines the power of scientific workflows, the flexibility of containers technology, and robustness of the distributed streaming approach.

In today's interconnected world, electronic mail or email is an essential means of communication. However, due to numerous factors such as servers, protocols, and relays, email delivery failure can occur. This paper proposes a solution to this problem by utilizing the one-vs-all classifier. The proposed system uses training data to predict email delivery failure in real-time, enabling the user to take appropriate action quickly. The system utilizes support vector machines to improve prediction accuracy. Overall, the proposed solution provides an effective and efficient way to predict email delivery failure and help users avoid the unnecessary waste of time and effort caused by such failures.

This paper proposes a novel approach for multi-UAVs cooperative reconnaissance based on an improved harmony search algorithm. Reconnaissance is a critical task in military and civil applications, and the use of heuristic algorithms can greatly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of this process. The proposed algorithm takes into account the task analysis and search problems typical in reconnaissance scenarios, and uses linear programming to optimize the performance of the UAVs during the mission. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits excellent convergence properties and can be fine-tuned for specific mission requirements. The results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both time efficiency and mission success rate, and it has a high potential for practical implementation in real-world applications.

The combination of Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Neural Networks has been shown to be highly effective for predicting satellite images. Using convolution to analyze the images, pose estimation to adjust for movement and deconvolution to reconstruct the image, the GAN-LSTM model has been able to accurately predict future images in a real-time system. This technology also lends itself well to task analysis, where demand for heating systems can be predicted for more efficient energy usage. With the ability to learn and adapt from new data, neural networks offer great potential for improving prediction models in a variety of applications.

A Flexible Machine Vision (FMV) Inspection System has been developed that requires minimal retuning in hardware and software as applications are changed up. The flexibility of the system was evaluated by applying it to an inspection problem with three different types of small parts: plastic gears, plastic connectors and metallic coins, with minimal retuning when moving from one application to the others. The system was required to differentiate between 4 different known styles of each part plus one unknown style, for a total of 5 classes. In previous work, a hybrid Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier was developed for the connector application. When applied to the coin application, the hybrid SVM could not achieve the target performance of 95% accuracy. A new hybrid that method that combines SVM and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) or ANN-SVM classifier was subsequently developed to overcome this problem and the results are presented in this paper. The image library used in this study is available at http://my.me.queensu.ca/People/Surgenor/Laboratory/Database.html.

Intrusion detection system (IDS) is a crucial aspect in cybersecurity. The use of machine learning algorithms in IDS has become increasingly popular in recent years due to their ability to classify and identify network attacks accurately. This study proposes a hybrid Particle swarm optimization -Extreme Learning Machine (PSO-ELM) approach for IDS. The proposed approach utilizes the PSO algorithm to optimize the weights and biases of the ELM algorithm, which classifies data models, and the support vector machine algorithm for classification. The use of PSO-ELM improves the classification accuracy of IDS, making it more efficient in detecting network attacks. The results show that the proposed approach outperforms conventional machine learning algorithms in detecting different types of network attacks, thus highlighting the effectiveness of the hybrid PSO-ELM approach in IDS.

Lane detection is an important aspect of road safety as it allows for effective navigation of vehicles. This paper proposes a novel approach to lane detection of curving roads for structural highways using the straight-curve model on vision. The study focuses on the use of feature extraction and mathematical models to identify turning points and edges in the images captured by the vision system. The proposed adaptation models are shown to be efficient in detecting lane boundaries and curvature changes, improving the accuracy and robustness of the lane detection system. The findings of this study contribute towards the development of an effective and reliable lane detection system that can enhance road safety and reduce the incidence of accidents on highways. The use of image edge detection as a feature extraction technique has proven to be particularly effective in detecting lane boundary changes and curves on curving roads.

This paper proposes a second-order diffusion model for influence maximization in social networks, specifically targeting the microblogging platform Twitter. The model utilizes integrated circuit modeling and computational modeling techniques to approximate the spread of information throughout the network. To solve the optimization problem of finding the most influential nodes, heuristic algorithms are employed. The effectiveness of the proposed model is evaluated through experimental analysis and comparison to other state-of-the-art approximation algorithms. The results show that the second-order diffusion model outperforms other models in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising approach for influence maximization in social networks.

In recent years, machine learning-based positioning has been receiving significant attention from researchers due to its ability to improve accuracy and reduce cost. One of the most promising areas of machine learning-based positioning is the use of deep learning techniques. Satellite broadcasting and global positioning systems have a crucial role in enhancing the accuracy of machine learning-based positioning. Wireless fidelity and radio navigation signals have also been utilized for this purpose. Training of machine learning models has a direct impact on the accuracy and efficiency of machine learning-based positioning. The future of machine learning-based positioning looks bright as many researchers are focusing on exploring new directions in this field, including the development of hybrid approaches and the incorporation of different sensing modalities. However, some challenges need to be overcome, such as the lack of standardization in data collection and processing.

This paper presents a case study of smart farm monitoring via the Blynk IoT platform, focusing specifically on humidity monitoring and data recording. Using microcontrollers and humidity sensors, the system is able to measure humidity levels in real-time and transmit this data to the Blynk cloud. The data can then be accessed and analyzed via the Blynk mobile application, providing farmers with a powerful tool for monitoring and optimizing farm conditions. This case study showcases the potential of the Internet of Things for revolutionizing farm monitoring and management, and highlights the importance of real-time systems and mobile applications for achieving this goal. Overall, this smart farm monitoring system via the Blynk IoT platform represents a significant step forward in the quest for more efficient and sustainable agriculture practices.

This paper presents the parallelization of the Commit framework for efficient microstructure-informed tractography using CUDA technology. The graphics processing units (GPUs) are used as computational resources due to their advantage of parallel processing. The instruction sets are optimized to efficiently exploit the parallelism of GPU architecture. The kernel is designed to correspond to the compute capability of the GPU, with attention paid to data transfer between the host and device. The effectiveness of this CUDA-enabled parallelization of the Commit framework is demonstrated through computational modeling of microstructure-informed tractography. Specifically, we investigate the integrated circuit modeling of the brain using this framework, which is expected to improve the understanding of the complex structure of the brain. Overall, this paper illustrates the potential benefits of using CUDA technology for parallelization of computational frameworks in the field of neuroscience.

Virtual Reality (VR) allows users to interact with intuitive environments to manipulate games, applications and even other Internet of Things (IoT) devices. VR devices have been brought to users by different vendors, supporting different development platforms and features. Many VR applications, however, do not support simultaneous VR devices from different vendors. The few applications that support this feature are not open to developers, with little information on their implementation and application performance. Using VRTK and Unity, this paper intends to present a VR application that supports multiple VR hardware platforms with the use of the VRTK SDK along with the appropriate VR hardware SDKs. This application supports multiple users in a VR environment where they can interact with each other and with objects in the VR space. Other features such as file transfer over the VR application are also supported. Such an application is important to allow developers to design future applications that support multiple devices regardless of the vendor, creating convenient multiuser VR applications with less limitations.

This paper proposes a joint power control and sub-carrier assignment approach to maximize the total data rate for two-tier networks, where femtocells are deployed within macrocell networks. With the aim of minimizing interference between macrocells and femtocells, the proposed approach adopts OFDM modulation and resource allocation scheme. In addition, quality of service requirements are taken into consideration in the resource management process. The simulation results show that the proposed approach can effectively increase the total data rate and achieve better resource allocation compared with existing approaches. This research provides a promising solution for power control and sub-carrier assignment in two-tier networks, which could improve the performance of femtocell networks and enhance the user experience.

In this paper, we propose a deep neural network based DPD (DNN-DPD) where ReLU activation is used instead of sigmoid activation to avoid the gradient vanishing problem. The ReLU function is implemented using a half-wave rectifier that acts as the activation function for the hidden layers in the DNN-DPD. Experimental results using a Doherty PA will show that the proposed DNN-DPD can achieve an additional 3 to 4 dB of linearity compensation compared to a conventional Volterra-DPD or shallow NN. Furthermore, to achieve comparable performance to sigmoid activation, the number of multipliers can be reduced by a factor of 100. This confirms that the DNN-DPD approach has a large potential to overcome the complicated memory effects of Doherty PAs with reduced DPD complexity.

Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based prediction of driver emergency braking intention can help develop an assistance system to improve driving safety for brain-controlled vehicles. However, existing studies are focused on how to build an individual detection model for each participant. In this paper, to build a universal model, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to extract the features of brain signals and build the universal model. Experimental results from 13 subjects show that the proposed CNN-based method outperforms the linear discriminant analysis (LDA)-based method and has a comparable performance with individual models. This work lays a foundation for future developments of an EEG-based universal model of driver emergency braking intention detection.

In the field of time series analysis, entropy is a widely-used measure of complexity and irregularity of signals. Two widely-used measures of entropy are approximate entropy (ApEn) and sample entropy (SampEn). However, choosing the appropriate value for the parameter tau is crucial for accurate estimation of ApEn and SampEn. This paper discusses the choice of tau in the estimation of ApEn and SampEn entropy of electromyography (EMG), electrocardiography (ECG), and electroencephalography (EEG) signals. In addition to discussing the selection of tau, the paper also addresses the influence of Gaussian noise on the estimation of entropy measures. Overall, this article contributes to the ongoing efforts to develop reliable and precise methods for the analysis of complex physiological signals.

This paper provides an introduction to the concept of Coordinated Deep Agents for Traffic Signal control. The focus of this research is on the application of reinforcement learning techniques in traffic signal control. Moreover, the paper discusses the process of feature extraction from traffic data and the role of roads in traffic signal coordination. Real-time systems are employed in coordination with traffic signals to ensure timely and efficient traffic flow. Furthermore, the use of oscillators is analyzed to improve traffic signal coordination. As an interdisciplinary field, sociology and statistics are also utilized to provide further insight into the complexities of traffic signal coordination. This paper aims to provide an initial overview of the topic and to set the stage for future research on this important area of study.

The removal of ink from histopathology whole slide images is a crucial step in the image restoration process. This paper proposes a novel technique that combines classification, detection and image generation models to remove the ink from the images. The proposed technique consists of multiple pipelines that involve the use of convolution and image color analysis. The classification model identifies areas containing ink while the detection model locates the ink spots. Subsequently, the image generation model replaces the ink spots with the surrounding tissue texture. The proposed technique was tested on several images, and the results show a significant improvement in image quality. The models were trained using neural networks, which show promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This technique can be applied to various types of images and can potentially save time and resources by eliminating the manual removal of ink spots in histopathology whole slide images.

This paper proposes a data-driven approach for hair modeling from a single image. The method utilizes solid modeling techniques and generates three-dimensional displays of the hair. A database of hair samples is used to train a computational model that can predict the hair's shape and style from a single two-dimensional image. The model takes into account the geometry of the head and the desired position of the hair. The resulting hair model is then displayed in three dimensions, allowing for a realistic representation of the subject's hair. The proposed approach has significant potential for use in the entertainment industry and may also have applications in medical and scientific research.

This paper proposes a passivity analysis for neural networks of neutral type with Markovian jumping parameters and time-varying delay. The authors focus on the impact of delays and Markovian jumping parameters on the stability of nonlinear systems. The passivity-based criterion is formulated in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), which ensures the asymptotic stability of the neural networks. The key contribution of this work is the utilization of symmetric matrices in the passivity analysis, which reduces the complexity of computation. The proposed approach is illustrated by a numerical example using Matlab tools, and the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the passivity-based analysis in ensuring the stability of nonlinear systems. This study provides a useful framework for passivity analysis for neural networks with delays and Markovian jumping parameters, which can be extended to other types of nonlinear systems.

In order to improve the maximum throughput of wireless networks based on the COPE protocol, an improved algorithm is proposed in this study. The algorithm involves two key stages: encoding and decoding. During the encoding process, relevant information is efficiently encoded with the use of a queueing analysis method. Meanwhile, the decoding process is made more effective through the incorporation of artificial neural networks. The performance of the algorithm is evaluated through a series of simulations, and the results demonstrate an improved maximum throughput when compared to existing algorithms. This research is highly relevant to the field of information science and control engineering, with potential applications in wireless communication in various sectors. Findings from this study are presented in several conferences, providing insight and contribution to the ongoing development of wireless network technology.

This paper presents SmartWriting, a system for recognizing pen-holding gestures using a smartwatch. The system is designed to capture hand movements while writing and to recognize specific patterns associated with holding a pen. Feature extraction techniques are utilized to identify characteristic signals from sensors, such as gyroscopes, in the smartwatch. Additionally, the system focuses on capturing movement data associated with the thumb, a key factor in pen-holding gestures. Frequency-domain analysis is used to process the collected data and identify relevant patterns. SmartWriting has been tested extensively, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately recognizing pen-holding gestures. The system has many potential applications in the fields of education, healthcare, and communication, and can be used to enhance writing accuracy, detect Parkinson's disease, and enable hands-free communication for people with disabilities. Overall, SmartWriting is a promising and innovative system for gesture recognition, and has significant potential for improving the way we write and interact with technology.

As stated in the book’s preface, the author aimed to write a textbook that gives an accessible description of POMDPs, with emphasis on filtering and controlled sensing. The four parts of this book certainly achieve this objective. A nice feature of the text is that it goes into substantial depth in several areas that have not appeared previously in other works. These include structural results for POMDPs, controlled sensing and weak derivatives for reinforcement learning of MDPs, and quickest detection with social learning that involves the interaction of local and global decision makers. The book also has a wealth of examples that motivate POMDPs, including social networks, behavioral economics (risk averse social learning), adaptive radars, and optimal search. The supplementary material contains numerous problem sets and case studies, making this book an excellent text for a graduate-level course. The book is pitched at a similar mathematical level as the classic [10]. Since the text focuses only on discrete-time filtering and stochastic control (POMDPs) where the state space is the unit simplex (therefore, compact), measure-theoretic aspects [11] are not required. Partially Observed Markov Decision Processes: From Filtering To Controlled Sensing is a valuable contribution to the literature on stochastic decision-making/control and stochastic optimization, and I highly recommend it to a diverse audience, including students and researchers in electrical engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, and operations research.

In Africa there is a lack of wired infrastructure to enable the free sharing of files and information which has led to the uptake of wireless infrastructure and mobile device utilisation. Even with the abundance of wireless technology, there are still very few user-friendly approached to share files and information without incurring service provider costs to the user. This research proposes a peer-to-peer model for sharing files and information between smart devices using Wi-Fi-Direct. FileLinker is a model developed to enable the scheduling of files without the cumbersome interactions required by many other peer-to-peer sharing applications. The contribution of this work is made by making FileLinker able to pre-setup sharing schedules that enable users to collect files when they can be near the sharer. A streamlined setup method is implemented that utilises NFC to reduce user inputs, thus enabling a tap-to-whitelist device approach, built around simplicity and usability. The researchers also document and evaluate the FileLinker prototype.

The explosive growth of digital images in video surveillance and social media has led to the significant need for efficient search of persons of interest in law enforcement and forensic applications. Despite tremendous progress in primary biometric traits (e.g., face and fingerprint) based person identification, a single biometric trait alone can not meet the desired recognition accuracy in forensic scenarios. Tattoos, as one of the important soft biometric traits, have been found to be valuable for assisting in person identification. However, tattoo search in a large collection of unconstrained images remains a difficult problem, and existing tattoo search methods mainly focus on matching cropped tattoos, which is different from real application scenarios. To close the gap, we propose an efficient tattoo search approach that is able to learn tattoo detection and compact representation jointly in a single convolutional neural network (CNN) via multi-task learning. While the features in the backbone network are shared by both tattoo detection and compact representation learning, individual latent layers of each sub-network optimize the shared features toward the detection and feature learning tasks, respectively. We resolve the small batch size issue inside the joint tattoo detection and compact representation learning network via random image stitch and preceding feature buffering. We evaluate the proposed tattoo search system using multiple public-domain tattoo benchmarks, and a gallery set with about 300K distracter tattoo images compiled from these datasets and images from the Internet. In addition, we also introduce a tattoo sketch dataset containing 300 tattoos for sketch-based tattoo search. Experimental results show that the proposed approach has superior performance in tattoo detection and tattoo search at scale compared to several state-of-the-art tattoo retrieval algorithms.

Time-varying requirements of users on communication push mobile operators to increase density of base stations. However, the dense deployment of conventional static base stations (SBSs) is not always economical, for example, when periods of peak load are short and infrequent. In such cases, several flying base stations (FlyBSs) mounted on unmanned aerial vehicles can be seen as a convenient substitution for the dense deployment of SBSs. This paper focuses on maximization of user satisfaction with provided data rates. To this end, we propose an algorithm that associates users with the most suitable SBS/FlyBS and finds optimal positions of all FlyBSs. Furthermore, we investigate the performance of two proposed approaches for the joint association and positioning based on the genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO). It is shown that both solutions improve the satisfaction of users with provided data rates in comparison with a competitive approach. We also demonstrate trade-offs between the GA and the PSO. While the PSO is of lower complexity than the GA, the GA requires a slightly lower number of active FlyBSs to serve the users.

Heat storage efficiency of wood floor made by various tree species is different. Author's research group has developed the equipment for testing the thermal storage efficiency. The number of temperature sensors is few and it's difficult to construct a complete and continuous temperature field in cavity of this equipment. In this paper, BP neural network is used to predict and analyze the temperature field in the closed cavity in time and space dimensions based on the temperature data of the finite points obtained from the test. In the time dimension, the coordinate and the temperatures of 3 nodes are taken as inputs and the temperature of the fourth node is taken as the output. The results are: MRE= 0.2694%, MAE= 5.9162%,MSE= 0.4225%, $R^{2}$=0.9988. In the space dimension, the temperatures of 150 measured points are used as the model training and testing sample which can chose from geometric view. The results are: MRE=.3641, MAE =4.7817, MSE=0.5216, $R^{2}$ =0.9985. It can be concluded from above: that the BP neural network used in this paper can effectively obtain the continuous and complete temperature field inside the testing cavity of the wood floor, which provides a new theoretical support for the analysis and calculation of the thermal storage efficiency of the wood floor.

The amount of high-quality data determines the performance of the deep learning model.
