(2) 3D CNN and LSTM used in the proposed deep learning framework yields better results than that of the 3D deep feature concatenation for MVI prediction. (3) Deeply supervised loss function that makes full use of the spatially and temporally discriminative features from Contrast-enhanced MR can further improve the performance of MVI prediction.

This paper proposes wireless ad hoc network simulation based on virtual reality technology. Functional components provided by a game engine such as scene management, animation, rendering, scripting, and physics engine can provide suitable interfaces for ad hoc network simulation. Using these components, simulation of ad hoc networks can be easily implemented. The ad-hoc network simulation technology can be carried out in virtual reality by game engine, which is illustrated by advantages of the game engine and the simulation process in this paper. The workability and accuracy of the simulation scheme are demonstrated, with the metrics of comparing the experimental data with other simulation techniques commonly used.

Radomes protect antennas from structural damage due to wind, precipitation, and bird strikes. In aerospace applications, radomes often double as a nose cone and thus have a significant impact on the aerodynamics of the aircraft. While radomes should be designed not to affect the performance of the underlying antennas, they also must satisfy structural and aerodynamic requirements. In this paper, we demonstrate a multiphysics approach to analysis of airborne radomes not only for electromagnetic (EM) performance, but also for structural, aerodynamic, and bird strike performances, as depicted in figure 1. We consider a radome constructed using composite fiberglass plies and a foam core, and coated with an anti-static coating, paint, and primer. A slotted waveguide array is designed at X-band to represent a weather radar antenna. The transmission loss of the radome walls is analyzed using a planar Green's function approach. An asymptotic technique, Ray-Launching Geometric Optics (RL-GO), is used to accurately simulate the nose cone radome and compute transmission loss, boresight error, and sidelobe performance. In addition to EM analysis, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis is used to predict pressures resulting from high air speeds, which are then mapped to an implicit structural solution to assess structural integrity using the Finite Element Method (FEM). We also demonstrate damage prediction due to a “bird strike” impact using an explicit structural FEM solver. The multiphysics simulation techniques demonstrated in this paper will allow for early design validation and reduce the number of measurement iterations required before a radome is certified for installation.

Lightning is a naturally occurring phenomenon that poses a significant threat to aviation safety. Predicting lightning strikes is essential in reducing the risk of lightning-related accidents. In this research, we proposed a predictive model that utilizes the MLPNN (Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network) structure to forecast lightning at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). The model is based on atmospheric modeling and data models, which provide critical input parameters for the artificial neural networks. The proposed model is tested using real-time lightning data from KLIA, and the results show excellent predictive accuracy. The study also highlights the potential of the MLPNN structure as a tool for developing predictive models of biological systems, such as animals, and could find a range of applications, including in aviation safety.

This paper explores the concept of virtualization of production through the use of digital twin technology. The application of this technology in the context of production environments provides several benefits, including efficient computational modeling, improved process control, and solid modeling for real-time systems. This paper also highlights the importance of materials science and technology in the virtualization of production. With the help of digital twins, it is possible to simulate various production scenarios, optimizing and identifying opportunities for improvement, without the need for physical prototyping. By integrating the digital twin into the production process, companies can gain a competitive edge by improving efficiency and reducing costs. As such, this paper serves to reinforce the growing interest in the virtualization of production and the potential impact it holds for modern manufacturing.

This paper proposes a new method for low rank approximation of positive semidefinite Hankel structured matrices using Vandermonde decomposition. The optimization problem is formulated as a minimization problem and solved using iterative methods. The proposed method is shown to converge to the optimal solution and outperforms existing matrix decomposition techniques. The results are compared to those obtained using various matrix converters and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for Hankel structured matrices. Overall, this work presents an important contribution to the field of matrix decomposition and provides a new efficient method for approximating positive semidefinite Hankel structured matrices.

This letter addresses the issue of accurate object detection in large-area remote sensing images. Although many convolutional neural network (CNN)-based object detection models can achieve high accuracy in small image patches, the models perform poorly in large-area images due to the large quantity of false and missing detections that arise from complex backgrounds and diverse groundcover types. To address this challenge, this letter proposes a sample update-based CNN (SUCNN) framework for object detection in large-area remote sensing images. The proposed framework contains two stages. In the first stage, a base model—single-shot multibox detector—is trained with the training data set. In the second stage, artificial composite samples are generated to update the training set. The parameters of the first-stage model are fine-tuned with the updated data set to obtain the second-stage model. The first- and second-stage models are evaluated using the large-area remote sensing image test set. Comparison experiments show the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed SUCNN framework for object detection in large-area remote sensing images.

This paper presents a performance comparison of the new Fast Weighted Naïve Bayes classifier with other Bayes classifiers. The study was conducted using various datasets from different domains, including data mining, classification algorithms, databases, and games. The performance of the classifier was evaluated using various metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The results showed that the Fast Weighted Naïve Bayes classifier outperformed the other Bayes classifiers in terms of accuracy and F1 score. In addition, a mathematical model was developed to explain the performance of the classifier. Overall, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of the Fast Weighted Naïve Bayes classifier in classification tasks and suggests its potential applications in various fields.

Freeform surfaces exist widely in the stock cutting process of clinical prosthesis preparation, aviation, ship, and other manufacturing industries. The free-form contours of surfaces need to be packed before they are machined from raw materials. The existing methods search a contour position by rotating the contour and translating it to connect other contours for packing. The relative position between two contours will be changed after the rotation as the contour description is lack of geometric invariance. These methods easily miss the best layout position resulting in interspaces in the raw material. Moreover, this result seriously reduces the performance and efficiency of an automatic packing system. Therefore, a new packing algorithm is proposed in this paper by combining the geometric invariant description and coding matching for contours to solve the contour rotating and position connecting problems. The optimal position of a contour can be found directly and then connected by the extracted similar complement features of the contour. The experimental results show that the proposed method can greatly improve quality and efficiency of the layout, especially in the material utilization.

One of the most promising alternatives to train, compensate or rehabilitate patients after cerebrovascular accidents, spinal cord injuries, head trauma and physiological pathological tremors causing gait disorders are the motor neuroprosthestic devices (NP). However, there are not portable and flexible NP devices capable of fulfilling the requirements of different rehabilitation scenarios. In this work, the novel and flexible H-GAIT NP for lower limbs training and compensation is presented. This NP is able to detect four subphases of gait cycle and provide configurable surface stimulation patterns at each subphase. The H-GAIT NP can stimulate 4 independent channels for each subphase, allowing to reproduce diverse muscle activation patterns that can be needed in different rehabilitation scenarios. In order to validate the concept, several tests were carried on with 5 neuromuscularly intact participants and three different gait speeds in order to validate detection of the subphases. The algorithm showed an acceptable performance (over 95 % of gait) subphases successfully detected in all cases at three different gait speeds (0.7, 0.85, and 0.97 m/s). The results were consistent among participants. To show the potential use of the NP in different rehabilitation scenarios, one stimulation profile was configured for hemiplegic gait compensation.

An analysis of existing methods for solving the problems of risk assessment showed that they are based on the lack of computational capabilities and the lack of necessary information about the conditions of the problem. Therefore, in such cases it is advisable to use fuzzy mathematical methods. In this paper, we consider approaches to solving the problem of risk assessment with fuzzy source information.

The IEC 61850 standard is an approach to facilitate interoperability in distribution automation. This standard, developed by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), defines a set of communication protocols for the exchange of data between devices in automation systems. Automation systems, such as those used in electricity distribution networks, are prone to circuit faults and failures. By implementing IEC 61850, circuit breakers can be automatically controlled to restore power for customers more quickly, reducing downtime and improving reliability. This approach is gaining popularity worldwide, as it conforms to ISO standards and enables seamless communication across different communication networks. In conclusion, IEC standards and the use of automation in distribution networks represent a significant advancement in power system operations, providing greater reliability and efficiency for the end-user.

METRO-HAUL Targets the design and the building of a smart optical metro infrastructure able to support traffic originating from 5G New Radio (5G NR) networks, addressing the anticipated capacity increase and its specific characteristics e.g. mobility, low latency, low jitter, etc. This infrastructure will also support a wide variety of services and use cases with special emphasis on services from various industries vertical to the ICT.

In recent times, the unprecedented growth and development of the IP networks have greatly transformed the nature of communication and networking services. With the advent of the next generation networking technologies, the need for efficient, effective and collaborative IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) service exposure has become increasingly important. This has led to the exploration of new and innovative ways of improving the sensitivity, portability and flexibility of IMS services. One of such ways is through the use of recommender systems that leverage on predictive models to provide recommendations for IMS services. This paper proposes an event prediction-based IMS service exposure solution that utilizes recommender systems to accurately predict the future events and activities of users. The proposed system offers a collaborative and adaptive IMS service exposure framework, which ensures the provision of personalized and relevant IMS services to users. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed system is demonstrated through the use of simulations and empirical evaluations that show significant improvements in the overall quality of IMS services provided.

Humanoid robots are seen as perfect education partners for students these days. Many researchers are working on educational humanoid robots to make them more effective in educating students. One of many approaches to realize it is to make the robots educate children in two-way communication. In this case, robots can recognize students' progress and provide suitable learning materials according to their progress. In a simple scenario for basic mathematics learning, the robot educates a student on how to solve mathematical expressions. As the student understand the concepts, the robot gives some simple exercises to further improve student's ability. While completing the exercise, the partner robot supervises each mathematical expression solved by the student, acknowledges mistakes and provides correct solutions. Thus, the robot must be equipped with a system which can recognize mathematical expressions and give the solutions. Such system is an inherent foundation to build much smarter robots in delivering education to students. This paper covers detail design and implementation of the system which recognizes handwritten mathematical equations and provides the corresponding solutions. Testing results show that the system performs quite well with 97.4% accuracy with slight errors for characters with similar shapes.

This paper deals with iterative Jacobian-based recursion technique for the root-finding problem of the vectorvalued function, whose evaluations are contaminated by noise. Instead of a scalar step size, we use an iterate-dependent matrix gain to effectively weigh the different elements associated with the noisy observations. The analytical development of the matrix gain is built on an iterative-dependent linear function interfered by additive zero-mean white noise, where the dimension of the function is M 1 and the dimension of the unknown variable is N 1. Necessary and sufficient conditions for M N algorithms are presented pertaining to algorithm stability and convergence of the estimate error covariance matrix. Two algorithms are proposed: one for the case where M N and the second one for the antithesis. The two algorithms assume full knowledge of the Jacobian. The recursive algorithms are proposed for generating the optimal iterative-dependent matrix gain. The proposed algorithms here aim for per-iteration minimization of the mean square estimate error. We show that the proposed algorithm satisfies the presented conditions for stability and convergence of the covariance. In addition, the convergence rate of the estimation error covariance is shown to be inversely proportional to the number of iterations. For the antithesis M <; N, contraction of the error covariance is guaranteed. This underdetermined system of equations can be helpful in training neural networks. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the performance capabilities of the proposed multidimensional gain while considering nonlinear functions.

Recently, it has been standardized by the 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) that device-to-device (D2D) communications should use uplink resources when coexisting with conventional cellular communications. With uplink resource sharing, both cellular and D2D links cause significant co-channel interference. In this paper, we address the critical issue of interference management in the network considering a practical path loss model incorporating both line-of-sight (LoS) and non-LoS (NLoS) transmissions. To reduce the severe interference caused by active D2D links, we consider a mode selection scheme based on the maximum received signal strength (MRSS) for each user equipment (UE) to control the D2D-to-cellular interference. Furthermore, we analyze the performance in terms of the coverage probability and the area spectral efficiency (ASE) for both the cellular network and the D2D one. Analytical results are obtained and the accuracy of the proposed analytical framework is validated through Monte Carlo simulations. Through our theoretical and numerical analyses, we quantify the performance gains brought by D2D communications in cellular networks and we find an optimum mode selection threshold β to maximize the total ASE in the network. This insight is expected to provide a design guideline for D2D mode selections.

Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is a popular optimization technique inspired by the social behavior of birds and fish. However, the low convergence speed of PSO is a major limitation for PSO to be used in practical applications. In recent years, meta-heuristic algorithms have shown great promise in solving optimization problems without requiring any prior knowledge about the problem. This study proposes a novel PSO algorithm that uses fitness-based acceleration coefficients to improve the convergence speed of the PSO. The proposed algorithm is tested against benchmark test problems to evaluate its performance. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is more efficient than existing PSO algorithms in terms of convergence speed and accuracy. The proposed algorithm is expected to have significant applications in various fields such as engineering, computer science, and sociology.

In this paper, we present an efficient footprint-guided compact finite element algorithm for 3-D airborne electromagnetic modeling. Finite element analysis is a powerful tool for computational modeling of complex electromagnetic systems in nonhomogeneous media. However, the accuracy and efficiency of finite element methods are greatly affected by the choice of numerical algorithms. Our proposed algorithm uses a compact finite element method guided by footprint-based refinement to accurately model magnetic domains in nonhomogeneous media. The algorithm also incorporates solid modeling to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the simulation. In addition, we compare our algorithm with existing methods and demonstrate its superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed algorithm has important applications in a variety of fields, including magnetic separation and electromagnetic interference analysis of receivers in airborne systems.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have gained a lot of attention in recent years due to their potential applications in various fields. However, one of the major challenges in WSNs is the limited power supply of sensor nodes. To overcome this challenge, relay-based communication has been proposed as a promising solution. In this context, a new technique called adaptive relaying has been introduced, which leverages wake-up receivers and enables nodes to conserve energy. The use of relays in WSNs improves the network coverage and can also enhance the reliability of data transmission. Power demand is another critical aspect to consider in WSNs. By using adaptive relaying, the power consumption can be effectively managed and the lifetime of the network can be prolonged. This technique also enables nodes to activate and deactivate transceivers based on the availability of data to be transmitted. Furthermore, the adaptive relaying approach can be integrated with the media access protocol to improve the efficiency of channel utilization. Overall, the adaptive relaying technique has great potential to enhance the performance of wireless sensor networks by optimizing power consumption and improving the reliability of communications.

This paper evaluates modeling units and sub-word features in language models for Turkish automatic speech recognition (ASR). The focus is on the training and computational modeling of language models using data models. The paper explores different mathematical models such as probability models and their efficacy in decoding Turkish speech. The research presented in the paper suggests that a sub-word unit model incorporating long short-term memory units shows promising results, particularly in dealing with out-of-vocabulary words. The experiments conducted on a Turkish ASR dataset indicate that the proposed sub-word model outperforms the traditional word-based model. The findings in this paper emphasize the importance of selecting an appropriate modeling unit and sub-word features that are language-specific when developing language models for ASR systems.

As an important part of the aircraft, the protective shell can protect the aircraft and other payloads. But it will become an irregular body falling into water when it is abandoned. The hydrodynamic force of the irregular body is complex and hard to express. In this paper, a semi-cylindrical shell is taken as an irregular body example to study the hydrodynamic characteristics and its expression. By using the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method, the hydrodynamic force of the irregular body is obtained, and its characteristics is analyzed in detail. It can provide a basis for further research of the irregular body.

This paper attempted to study the efficiency of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with metaheuristic algorithms for electricity consumption modeling in Thailand. The objective was to compare the study between ANN with Backpropagation algorithm (ANN-BP) and ANN combined with different metaheuristic algorithms: ANN with Harmony Search (ANN-HS), ANN with Artificial Bee Colony (ANN-ABC), ANN with Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (ANN-TLBO) and ANN with Jaya Algorithms (ANN-JA) models. The models selected Population, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Imports of goods and services, Exports of goods and services as inputs. The experiment results showed that the ANN-TLBO model had optimal efficiency, while ANN-JA was one of the competitive metaheuristic algorithms that could be implemented to modelling for use in future studies.

This paper presents an experimental comparison of pure flooding and its variants on Raspberry Pi in small scale ad hoc networks. The focus of the analysis is on mobile ad hoc networks, message systems, routing protocols, packet loss and heuristic algorithms. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of flooding-based routing protocols in small scale ad hoc networks. The experiments were carried out on a Raspberry Pi cluster using a range of metrics, including packet loss and message delivery ratio. The results show that flooding-based routing protocols can be effective in small scale ad hoc networks, but can be prone to high packet loss rates. Additionally, the use of heuristic algorithms can improve the performance of flooding-based protocols. These findings provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of mobile ad hoc networks and can inform the development of more efficient routing protocols for these types of networks.

In order to discriminate the real targets, the clutter and the dense multi-false targets, we propose a factorized convolutional neural network-based algorithm for radar targets discrimination. We establish the factorized convolutional neural network model with depthwise separable convolution. To reduce the parameters of the model, we establish the simplified factorized convolutional neural network by reducing the numbers of both convolutional filters and connection nodes of fully connected layers. The result of the measured data demonstrates that, as compared with the existing model, the simplified factorized convolutional neural network has higher discrimination rate for the real targets, the clutter and the dense multi-false targets, and its parameters are less than ten percent counterpart of a recent proposed model.

This paper proposes an approximative Bayes-optimal kernel classifier based on version space reduction. The approach relies on kernel functions to map the input data to a higher dimensional space to find nonlinear decision boundaries. The proposed method builds upon the theory of Bayesian decision theory, developing a training algorithm that allows for both kernel and model selection. The approach achieves an approximative Bayes-optimal solution by iteratively reducing the version space of candidate models. The proposed method is compared to support vector machines and other approximation algorithms in the literature. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves competitive classification accuracy while also being more efficient in terms of training time. This approach can have important implications for various applications in computer science, such as task analysis and decision support systems.

This paper analyzes the influence of temporal dispersion on undersea wireless optical communication systems and proposes a technique for minimizing the negative effects through maximum likelihood estimation (MLSE). Specifically, the article considers how photonics and scattering affect the receivers of these systems and how Monte Carlo methods can be used to model the dispersion of signals. The proposed MLSE approach is able to mitigate bandwidth limitations caused by dispersion, making it a promising technique for improving the performance of undersea wireless optical communication systems. Overall, this paper contributes to the advancement of wireless optical communication and illustrates the importance of understanding the role of temporal dispersion in these systems.

Self-adaptive software has the capability to sense a change in its environment and its own behaviour, and then adjust itself accordingly during runtime to meet the desired requirements. Analysing and evaluating quality attributes is popular in self-adaptive software research. In recent years, several studies have proposed runtime models which analyse and evaluate quality attributes of self-adaptive software. This paper focuses on runtime models used for analysis and evaluation of quality attributes of self-adaptive software. Firstly, self-adaptive software, runtime models, analysis and evaluation of quality attributes based on runtime models, and related concepts are introduced. Studies describing runtime models are investigated and the meaning of runtime models used in analysis and evaluation of quality attributes of self-adaptive software is clarified. Two types of typical construction methods and their general construction processes are described. Runtime models were analysed and categorized considering multiple aspects, including type, modelling language, application scenarios, and relationship between runtime models and quality attributes. The extension mechanisms for runtime models were also analysed and extracted into two types. The weaknesses of current research are listed and analysed, with future research directions suggested.

Recently, there has been an increasing interest in utilizing recurrent neural networks such as bidirectional LSTM for genome data analysis. One of the major challenges in genomics and bioinformatics is identifying the regulatory logic gates that control gene expression. The vast amount of data generated from various genomic experiments requires efficient computational modeling and analysis tools. Bidirectional LSTM models have shown promising results in sequential analysis of genome data, providing accurate predictions of DNA binding sites and regulatory elements. These models enable the identification of hidden patterns and relationships within the genome data, providing insights into the underlying biological mechanisms. With the development of more advanced computational techniques and tools, bidirectional LSTM models are likely to become an even more powerful tool for genomic research and analysis.

It is important to understand the factors that contribute significantly to increasing the student's motivation to perform academically and their soft skills. This paper discusses the implementation of My UiTM Engineering (MUE) to help students with cumulative grade point average (CGPA) below 3.0 to obtain better results. A meaningful mind setting talk with the comprehensive module for group training was designed for this program. To understand the characteristics of students with CGPA below 3.0, a survey was distributed to a batch of new students to analyze their opinions of their self-motivation, the level of familiarization on fundamental electrical and electronic subjects and the level of soft kills they acquired throughout their study. For the older batch of students who underwent the MUE program, the results showed that 73% of them were able to increase their CGPA as compared to the previous semester after participating in the MUE program.

Nowadays Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) receive important attention in the scientific and commercial fields due to the increasing number of devices and applications concentrating on safety, efficiency and infotainment in transportation infrastructure. One of the most promising applications is the streaming of video data which presents a suitable tool especially for warning drivers and preventing dangers on roads. However, video streaming over vehicular environment is a daunting task due to high movement of vehicles and the specific requirements of video data in terms of performances and quality of service (QoS)/quality of experience (QoE). To this end, this paper presents a survey of video streaming techniques in vehicular networks and discusses the different QoS/QoE related to video streaming issues. A comparative study of QoS/QoE aware video streaming schemes classified according to the technique used is elaborated. Furthermore, major challenges in video streaming are identified as future trends of research.

The paper pays attention to particularities concerned with the defuzzification procedure in adaptive neural network based fuzzy inference systems. Specifically, the problem of constructing recursive parameter estimation algorithms is considered with regard to their convergence and stability. In the combination with various forms of the quadratic criterion, such an approach enables on to obtain strongly consistent estimation algorithms under essential generality of modeled system description; and the convergence properties are demonstrated in the comparison with conventional algorithms.

Vibration and acoustics emission based methods are commonly used in condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. However, condition monitoring of low-speed bearings may be more difficult than that of high-speed bearings due to its low signal-to-noise ratio. A detailed discussion on vibration and acoustic emission based methods implemented in recent years for fault detection and health condition monitoring of low-speed bearings is presented in this paper. The comparison of these two methods is given, and some suggestions and considerations are included as well.

In recent years, the demand for effective wireless indoor localization solutions has grown significantly due to the widespread use of wireless local area networks (WLANs). A new statistical received signal strength (RSS) model based fingerprint approach has been proposed to address this issue. This approach utilizes RSS measurements collected from wireless access points (APs) to establish a fingerprint database. The proposed model applies a statistical algorithm to map the fingerprint onto a coordinate system, enabling accurate indoor localization. The model's effectiveness was evaluated through extensive testing and comparison with other localization methods. Moreover, the proposed approach complies with the standard IEEE 802.11 WLAN protocol, making it easy to integrate with existing WLAN systems. Computational modeling and data models were utilized to enhance the accuracy and reliability of the proposed model. In summary, this statistical RSS model based fingerprint approach represents a promising solution for the practical implementation of indoor localization applications for WLAN systems.

In this paper we discuss the signal processing of a cylindrical object, a pipe (in air), subjected to random excitations by a hammer-like surface from a cam-driven motor. The overall objective of this effort is to develop real-time hardware capable of monitoring mechanical systems (structures) for potential anomalies. We briefly discuss the development process: (1) theoretical modeling; (2) sophisticated simulations; (3) analysis; (4) controlled experiments; (5) signal processing; (6) modal frequency estimation; and (7) modal tracking. The primary emphasis is on the signal processing, modal extraction and tracking for single and multi-channel data.

Sign language is physical communication for contributing the meaning instead of using voice to demonstrate communicator's opinion. This paper introduces a simple and efficient algorithm for feature extraction to recognize American Sign Language alphabets from both static and dynamic gestures. The proposed algorithm comprises of four different techniques: Number of white pixels at the edge of the image (NwE), Finger length from the centroid point (Fcen), Angles between fingers (AngF) and Differences of angles between fingers of the first and last frame (delAng). After extracting features from video images, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is used to classify the signs. The result of these experiments is achieved up to 95% recognition rate, which is clearly to be the highest accuracy comparing with the other research worked in this field.

Kernel Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression is a popular method in machine learning algorithms used for analyzing data and solving complex problems. In this study, we introduce Kernel PLS Regression II which involves projecting both independent and dependent variables into Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). This approach allows for better correlation and prediction accuracy in the analysis of large datasets. To implement this method, we propose an optimization procedure that involves selecting the optimal kernel parameters and regularization parameter via cross-validation. Additionally, we perform a comprehensive analysis of the method's performance in comparison to other commonly used regression techniques. The results show that Kernel PLS Regression II has higher predictive capabilities and effectively handles high-dimensional data. In conclusion, our proposals demonstrate the effectiveness and potential of Kernel PLS Regression II in various applications.

The target of security protection of the power distribution automation system (the distribution system for short) is to ensure the security of communication between the distribution terminal (terminal for short) and the distribution master station (master system for short). The encryption and authentication gateway (VPN gateway for short) for distribution system enhances the network layer communication security between the terminal and the VPN gateway. The distribution application layer encryption authentication device (master cipher machine for short) ensures the confidentiality and integrity of data transmission in application layer, and realizes the identity authentication between the master station and the terminal. All these measures are used to prevent malicious damage and attack to the master system by forging terminal identity, replay attack and other illegal operations, in order to prevent the resulting distribution network system accidents. Based on the security protection scheme of the power distribution automation system, this paper carries out the development of multi-chip encapsulation, develops IPSec Protocols software within the security chip, and realizes dual encryption and authentication function in IP layer and application layer supporting the national cryptographic algorithm.

This paper aims to characterize power amplifiers in the context of wide-bandwidth carrier aggregation applications under multi-tone excitation. The study focuses on power amplifiers used in radio frequency communication systems as they play a significant role in transmitting signals with high power and efficiency. The training of these amplifiers has been a challenge due to the wide bandwidth, and peak to average power ratio (PAR) that needs to be considered. The paper discusses the 3GPP (3rd Generation Partnership Project) standards for carrier aggregation and how they affect the power amplifiers. The results of the study show that multi-tone excitation has a significant impact on the linearity of power amplifiers, and measures to reduce the effect of PAR have been proposed. The findings will help to optimize the performance of power amplifiers, and improve the quality of communication systems in wide-bandwidth carrier aggregation applications.

This paper proposes a mobile-only solution for server-based qualified electronic signatures, achieved through the integration of distance measurement, lighting, fingerprint recognition, IP networks, springs, wireless communication, and wireless fidelity technologies. By utilizing these technologies, the proposed system ensures the security and integrity of electronic signatures while allowing users to sign and authenticate documents remotely using only their mobile devices. In particular, distance measurement technology is used to ensure the user is within a specified range of the document signing location, lighting technology is used to capture high-quality images of fingerprints for authentication purposes, and wireless communication technology enables the secure transmission of signed documents. Overall, this solution provides an efficient, user-friendly, and secure method for electronic signature authentication, particularly for those who need to sign documents remotely.

This study aimed to investigate the impact of pedagogical agents on students' learning experience in virtual worlds, specifically focusing on three-dimensional displays, training, visualization, and informatics. The research was conducted in an Australian context, with a particular emphasis on environmental engineering. Both quantitative and qualitative data were collected through surveys and interviews to examine the effectiveness of pedagogical agents in enhancing students' engagement, motivation, and knowledge retention. Results suggest that the use of pedagogical agents had a positive impact on students' learning outcomes, as they provided more interactive and immersive learning experiences. This study provides valuable insights into the potential of pedagogical agents in enhancing students' learning experience in virtual worlds, and highlights the need for further research in this area.

This research paper proposes an ensembling technique-based crop recommendation system to improve crop productivity by taking into consideration soil quality and suitable training strategies. The system utilizes support vector machines to predict the yield of different crop varieties, given specific soil conditions. The proposed system is trained using a dataset of soil characteristics and crop yields, and then tested on a separate dataset to evaluate its accuracy. The results show that the ensembling technique-based crop recommendation system significantly improves crop productivity, resulting in higher yields of variously recommended crops. The system can provide helpful guidance to farmers in the selection of crops that best suit the soil conditions and training strategies, which ultimately enhances overall agricultural productivity. This research provides a solution to the problem of low crop productivity and helps to ensure long-term food security.

With explosive growth of Android malware and due to the severity of its damages to smart phone users, efficient Android malware detection methods are urgently needed. As is known to us, different categories of applications divided by their functions use sensitive data in distinct ways. Besides, in each category, malicious applications treat sensitive data differently from benign applications. We thus propose TFDroid, a novel machine learning-based approach to detect malware using the related topics and data flows of Android applications. We test TFDroid on thousands of benign and malicious applications. The results show that TFDroid can correctly identify 93.7% of all malware.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become increasingly popular due to their ability to gather data and provide insights into complex systems. However, localization of sensors in these networks can be challenging and costly. This paper focuses on the accuracy/cost trade-off in solving the localization problem for WSNs. The optimization of energy consumption is also an important factor in designing these systems. A task analysis of the measurement and estimation processes is conducted to determine the most efficient and accurate methods of localization. The paper proposes an approach that balances accuracy and cost, while minimizing energy consumption, to provide an optimal solution for localization in WSNs. This approach can provide significant benefits in terms of cost savings and energy efficiency for WSNs. In conclusion, the proposed approach holds promising potential for improving localization in WSNs through cost-effective and energy-efficient methods.

With the emergence of Internet-of-Things (IoT) and ever-increasing demand for the newly connected devices, there is a need for more effective storage and processing paradigms to cope with the data generated from these devices. In this study, we have discussed different paradigms for data processing and storage including Cloud, Fog, and Edge computing models and their suitability in integrating with the IoT. Moreover, a detailed discussion on low latency and massive connectivity requirements of future cellular networks in accordance with machine-type communication (MTC) is also presented. Furthermore, the need to bring IoT devices to Internet connectivity and a standardized protocol stack to regulate the data transmission between these devices is also addressed, while keeping in view the resource-constraint nature of IoT devices.

This paper explores the concept of Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWANs) in the context of 5G, with a focus on the capability of LoRaWAN to contribute to massive Machine-Type Communications (mMTC) and the Internet of Things (IoT). The 5G mobile communication standard is expected to provide high downlink and uplink throughput, as well as scalability to accommodate a large number of devices. However, these requirements are not always applicable to low-power devices that require minimal energy consumption for extended periods of time. This is where LoRaWAN comes in, providing an efficient and cost-effective solution for LPWANs that can operate over long distances and penetrate dense urban environments. The paper also discusses key performance indicators for LPWANs, including reliability, capacity, and latency, and evaluates the capabilities of LoRaWAN in meeting these requirements for mMTC and IoT applications. Overall, this paper demonstrates the important role that LPWANs such as LoRaWAN can play in the broader context of 5G mobile communication and the growing demands of the IoT.

To guarantee high precision control and assure the reliability and safety of the railway systems operation, highly accurate measurement data from different onboard and wayside sensors are needed. This paper proposes a solution approach to obtain more accurate measurement data which are collected during train movement using an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)-based multi sensors data fusion. Several sensors that are used in the proposed approach include indoor positioning systems, radio frequency identification, and rotary encoder. Experimental results that were conducted on a train model show how the proposed method effectively able to provide more accurate measurement data about the train position.

Repair of multiple partially failed cache nodes is studied in a distributed wireless content caching system, where r out of a total of n cache nodes lose part of their cached data. Broadcast repair of failed cache contents at the network edge is studied; that is, the surviving cache nodes transmit broadcast messages to the failed ones, which are then used, together with the surviving data in their local cache memories, to recover the lost content. The trade-off between the storage capacity and the repair bandwidth is derived. It is shown that utilizing the broadcast nature of the wireless medium and the surviving cache contents at partially failed nodes significantly reduces the required repair bandwidth per node.

This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the uses of graphics processing units (GPU) and CUDA in soft-computing techniques. Soft-computing techniques such as neural networks, support vector machines, and genetic algorithms have shown great promise in solving complex problems in the field of machine learning. However, the computational requirements for these techniques can be quite high, limiting their practicality. The use of GPUs and CUDA technology has greatly improved the performance of these techniques by enabling parallel processing and utilizing the random access memory of the GPUs. The paper reviews various case studies and experiments that have been conducted to demonstrate the benefits of using GPUs for training and implementing soft-computing techniques. Overall, the results show that the use of GPUs and CUDA technology can greatly improve the performance of soft-computing techniques and enhance their practicality in solving real-world problems.

Extractive text summarization is to find the important sentences from texts and concatenates these sentences as a summary. However, sentences selected according to ranking rules are usually not coherent. Is a larger language unit such as a group of sentences or a paragraph more appropriate to be selected for summarization? This paper is to answer this question. Investigating the summarization algorithm based on ranking semantic link networks of texts, we find the following three results: 1) comparing with the summaries composed by sentences, the summaries composed by larger language units have similar ROUGE scores but have better readability; 2) using a group of sentences is more effective than using sentence and paragraph; and, 3) the quality of summaries composed by group becomes better when the average length of the source texts increases.

This paper proposes a methodology for stakeholder analysis based on stakeholder graph models, which utilizes speech data as a main source for the construction of analytical models. The analysis includes techniques such as ciphers, data mining, speech processing, semantics, and graph theory. The methodology is driven by the need to ensure that stakeholder analysis is done in a structured and consistent manner. The stakeholder graph model is used to represent the various stakeholders and their relationships, while the analysis is performed through the use of speech data, which is processed to extract relevant information. In addition, data mining techniques are employed to identify patterns in the speech data, while the use of semantics ensures that the analysis is done with a clear understanding of the meaning of the spoken words. Finally, the analysis results are presented in the form of a stakeholder graph that can be easily interpreted and used for decision-making purposes. Overall, this methodology provides an effective way to conduct stakeholder analysis, which can be applied in a variety of fields where stakeholder engagement is important.

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a respiratory disorder characterized by interruption to breathing during sleep. Usually, the OSA is more severe in the supine sleeping position. Recent studies also demonstrated that the head position may play an important role in the pathophysiology of the OSA. Therefore, monitoring the sleeping body and the head position has high clinical importance to optimize the treatment of the OSA. In this paper, three machine learning approaches were used to detect the head position during sleep in infrared images. In the first two methods, supervised classifiers were trained to estimate the head position based on different feature sets extracted from infrared images. In the third method, three different convolutional neural network (CNN) structures (ResNet50, MobileNet, and Darknet19) were trained to detect the head position during sleep. To detect the body position, the same CNN architectures were trained on infrared images. Overnight sleeping data (sleep duration =5±1h) from 50 participants (age: 53 ± 15 years, BMI: 29 ± 6 kg/m2, and 30 men/20 women) with various levels of OSA severity as measured by the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI =25±29 events/h and OSA severity: 12 normal, 13 mild, 11 moderate, and 14 severe) were collected for this paper. The models were trained on the data collected in one laboratory room from half of the participants and tested on the data from the other half collected in a different laboratory room. The best performing model (Darknet19) correctly estimated the lateral versus supine head position with 92% accuracy and 94% F1-Score and the lateral versus supine body position with 87% accuracy and 87% F1-Score.

This paper investigates the vulnerability of distributed and cooperative control in microgrids to synchronization attacks. Microgrids are small-scale power systems that are self-sufficient and can operate in isolation from the main power grid. Voltage measurement and control are crucial to ensure reliable and safe operation of microgrids. However, the distributed and cooperative nature of microgrids makes them susceptible to synchronization attacks. The paper demonstrates how malware can be used to manipulate generators and disrupt voltage control, leading to cascading failures in the microgrid. The study also highlights the importance of secure communication networks in preventing synchronization attacks. The findings of this paper provide important insights into the potential threats posed to microgrid systems and underscore the need for robust cybersecurity measures to safeguard against such attacks.

The Extended Kalman Filter (EFF) is often used for speed estimation in sensorless control of induction motors (IM). The major issue with implementation is the selection of the process of calculating system and noise covariance matrices; traditionally determined using trial-and-error “tuning” or genetic algorithm optimization. In this paper, we study the Enhanced Fireworks Algorithm (EFWA) as a method of optimizing the Extended Kalman Filter parameters for estimating the rotor speed. The EFWA algorithm explores and exploits the search space for the optimal solution by using cooperative “swarm” intelligence. A Simulink model of a system comprised of an induction motor controlled by a variable frequency drive (VFD) operating in constant volts/hertz (V/Hz) mode is used to experiment with the method under varying operating conditions. Our results indicate that EFWA optimization provides better results than the alternative state-of-the-art genetic algorithm (GA) for a comparable number of parameter set trials.

The Correlation-Based Feature Selection (CFS) algorithm has shown to be an effective method in feature selection for machine learning applications. The aim of feature extraction is to reduce the dimensionality of the datasets without loss of valuable information, and CFS achieves this goal by selecting subsets of features that are closely related to the classification algorithms. The core idea of CFS is to calculate the correlation of each feature with respect to the class attribute and eliminate features with low correlation. This process is iterated until a subset of features is obtained that maximizes the correlation with the class attribute while minimizing the correlation among features. CFS can be used in conjunction with information filters and machine learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of classification models in various domains. In conclusion, the CFS algorithm is a powerful tool for feature selection in machine learning applications, and it can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of classification models.

Social media have become increasingly popular for the sharing and spreading of user-generated content due to their easy access, fast dissemination, and low cost. Meanwhile, social media also enable the wide propagation of cyber frauds, which leverage fake information sources to reach an ulterior goal. The prevalence of untrustworthy information sources on social media can have significant negative societal effects. In a trustworthy social media system, trust calculation technology has become a key demand for the identification of information sources. Trust, as one of the most complex concepts in network communities, has multi-criteria properties. However, the existing work only focuses on single trust factor, and does not consider the complexity of trust relationships in social computing completely. In this paper, a multi-criteria trustworthiness calculation mechanism called Info-Trust is proposed for information sources, in which identity-based trust, behavior-based trust, relation-based trust, and feedback-based trust factors are incorporated to present an accuracy-enhanced full view of trustworthiness evaluation of information sources. More importantly, the weights of these factors are dynamically assigned by the ordered weighted averaging and weighted moving average (OWA-WMA) combination algorithm. This mechanism surpasses the limitations of existing approaches in which the weights are assigned subjectively. The experimental results based on the real-world datasets from Sina Weibo demonstrate that the proposed mechanism achieves greater accuracy and adaptability in trustworthiness identification of the network information.

Zero-determinant strategies provide a novel perspective for revealing the relation between a game strategy and the cost, and play an important role in effectively controlling and optimizing the costs against virus spreading in vaccination games. We explore in this paper how the social cost can be optimized when a self-interested individual adopts the newly proposed admin-cost-based zero-determinant strategy (AZDS) to unilaterally control his own cost. In contrast to the traditional belief of the conflicts between personal interest and public (social) interest, we find that the AZDS is a win-win mechanism which presents the advantage in optimizing both the individual cost and social cost simultaneously. Taking into account the differences between the individuals (nodes) in a network, we investigate the topological influence on the performance of the AZDS implemented by the administrator, and conclude that the control capability of the administrator depends on not only one's degree but also the network average degree, and the AZDS implemented by the administrators with different degrees have different sensitivities to the change of economic incentive. Some real social networks with community structure illustrate the effectiveness of the AZDS by introducing the coarse graining method.

Remote shell sessions via protocols such as SSH are essential for managing systems, deploying applications, and running experiments. However, combined with weak passwords or flaws in the authentication process, remote shell access becomes a major security risk, as it allows an attacker to run arbitrary commands in the name of an impersonated user or even a system administrator. For example, remote shells of weakly protected systems are often exploited in order to build large botnets, to send spam emails, or to launch distributed denial of service attacks. Also, malicious insiders in organizations often use shell sessions to access and transfer restricted data. In this work, we tackle the problem of detecting malicious shell sessions based on session logs, i.e., recorded sequences of commands that were executed over time. Our approach is to classify sessions as benign or malicious by analyzing the sequence of commands that the shell users executed. We model such sequences of commands as n-grams and use them as features to train a supervised machine learning classifier. Our evaluation, based on freely available data and data from our own honeypot infrastructure, shows that the classifier reaches a true positive rate of 99.4% and a true negative rate of 99.7% after observing only four shell commands.

Bacterial Foraging Optimization (BFO) is a technique inspired by the foraging behavior of microorganisms. However, traditional BFO suffers from premature convergence and a lack of adaptability to different scenarios. To overcome these limitations, an enhanced version of BFO has been proposed, called the Enhanced Bacterial Foraging Optimization (EBFO). This new approach incorporates two key components: progressive exploitation toward local optimum and adaptive raid. By using these tactics, EBFO can more effectively search for the optimal solution in various scenarios, making it a promising optimization method for a wide range of applications. In this paper, we compare EBFO with other popular optimization methods, such as genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization, and show that it outperforms them in terms of both speed and accuracy. To evaluate the performance of EBFO, we also introduce several performance indexes, including convergence speed and solution quality, and demonstrate how they can be used to assess the effectiveness of different optimization algorithms. In conclusion, the enhanced BFO algorithm proposed in this paper has significant potential for use in real-world optimization problems, particularly in fields such as sociology and statistics.

New IoT applications are demanding for more and more performance in embedded devices while their deployment and operation poses strict power constraints. We present the security concept for a customizable Internet of Things (IoT) platform based on the RISC-V ISA and developed by several Fraunhofer Institutes. It integrates a range of peripherals with a scalable computing subsystem as a three dimensional System-in-Package (3D-SiP). The security features aim for a medium security level and target the requirements of the IoT market. Our security architecture extends given implementations to enable secure deployment, operation, and update. Core security features are secure boot, an authenticated watchdog timer, and key management. The Universal Sensor Platform (USeP) SoC is developed for GLOBALFOUNDRIES' 22FDX technology and aims to provide a platform for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) that typically do not have access to advanced microelectronics and integration know-how, and are therefore limited to Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) products.

In long-term evolution (LTE) systems, there is an option to extend the size of the cyclic-prefix (CP) when the propagation environment is characterized by severe time dispersion. Such a peculiar feature makes the system more resilient against multipath distortions, but inevitably complicates the downlink synchronization task, which cannot be accomplished through conventional techniques devised for a specified CP size. In this paper, we study the problem of CP length detection in the LTE downlink in the presence of a timing uncertainty and frequency offset. In contrast to previous investigations based on heuristic arguments, our approach relies on the maximum likelihood (ML) estimation criterion. Furthermore, it accounts for the irregular LTE symbol (characterized by a different CP size), which is present in the normal CP operation mode. The resulting scheme operates in the time-domain and computes a different metric for each possible position of the irregular symbol within the observation window. Due to its flexibility, the proposed ML approach can be applied to any future multicarrier standard for the design of a CP length detection algorithm, either in the presence or in the absence of irregular symbols.

With the continuous development of the demand of electric power users, the analysis of users' electric power consumption(EPS) is becoming more and more important. The frequency of data acquisition and the dimension of data analysis are increasing, which makes the analysis of EPS behavior more precise. The development of user tag and portrait technology brings a more intuitive and concise expression to the analysis of user's EPS. Based on massive user archives, power load and EPS data, considering the user's power consumption characteristics and influencing factors, a user behavior tag library is built, and k-means algorithm is used to tag clustering to achieve different types of EPS behavior. The tag clustering results of 2000 industrial and commercial users show that the selected tags of EPS behavior is reasonable and the clustering algorithm is effective. The research results of this paper can provide powerful data support for power companies to understand the user's EPS habits, mining user's electric power needs and improve the service level.

In this paper, we address the hyperspectral image (HSI) classification task with a generative adversarial network and conditional random field (GAN-CRF)-based framework, which integrates a semisupervised deep learning and a probabilistic graphical model, and make three contributions. First, we design four types of convolutional and transposed convolutional layers that consider the characteristics of HSIs to help with extracting discriminative features from limited numbers of labeled HSI samples. Second, we construct semisupervised generative adversarial networks (GANs) to alleviate the shortage of training samples by adding labels to them and implicitly reconstructing real HSI data distribution through adversarial training. Third, we build dense conditional random fields (CRFs) on top of the random variables that are initialized to the softmax predictions of the trained GANs and are conditioned on HSIs to refine classification maps. This semisupervised framework leverages the merits of discriminative and generative models through a game-theoretical approach. Moreover, even though we used very small numbers of labeled training HSI samples from the two most challenging and extensively studied datasets, the experimental results demonstrated that spectral-spatial GAN-CRF (SS-GAN-CRF) models achieved top-ranking accuracy for semisupervised HSI classification.

Modern day mobile communication systems rely heavily on the use of multicarrier techniques such as Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) to combat the effects of multipath channels. However, in order to optimize these systems, various parameters such as delays and signal to noise ratio (SNR) must be accurately estimated. In this paper, we propose a cyclostationarity based approach for blind parameter estimation in universal filtered multicarrier. Our method effectively estimates the various parameters required for optimal system performance, and achieves improved accuracy compared to other existing methods. This approach is particularly well suited for 5G mobile communication systems where the use of OFDM as well as multicarrier waveforms are expected to become ubiquitous. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed approach in accurately estimating the parameters required for optimal system performance in a range of operating conditions.

This paper describes a high speed image retrieval method executable on smartphones in real-time. This method will enable us to develop an application of smartphones which assists the visually impaired to shoot a video of an object and to distinguish that object without using the internet. Taking a video makes a visually impaired user to put the object in the camera frame correctly, and the smartphone without the internet protects the user's privacy. Our method is constructed by ORB local features and a data structure of binary decision tree. Under the experimental environment of 3.1 GHz Intel Core i7 platform with Windows 10, our system performs 54.5 ms processing time and 96.1% accuracy. Furthermore, our method achieves 30 fps processing time on a smartphone.

This live demonstration presents a brain-inspired amygdala model. Amygdala is an area of the brain that is associated with fear conditioning, which is a type of classical conditioning. The model can learn preferences through humanrobot interactions by application of classical conditioning to the model. Additionally, to develop a high speed and low power system, we design a hardware of the amygdala model, and implemented the hardware into field programmable gate array.

In this paper, we present a multi-channel convolution neural network (CNN) for blind 360-degree image quality assessment (MC360IQA). To be consistent with the visual content of 360-degree images seen in the VR device, our model adopts the viewport images as the input. Specifically, we project each 360-degree image into six viewport images to cover omnidirectional visual content. By rotating the longitude of the front view, we can project one omnidirectional image onto lots of different groups of viewport images, which is an efficient way to avoid overfitting. MC360IQA consists of two parts, multi-channel CNN and image quality regressor. Multi-channel CNN includes six parallel ResNet34 networks, which are used to extract the features of the corresponding six viewport images. Image quality regressor fuses the features and regresses them to final scores. The results show that our model achieves the best performance among the state-of-art full-reference (FR) and no-reference (NR) image quality assessment (IQA) models on the available 360-degree IQA database.

In this paper, we propose a new mathematical model for the parameter estimation of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) that takes into account the discretization effects of digital controllers. The proposed model is capable of estimating steady-state parameters, which are crucial for the accurate control of PMSMs. Analytical models for voltage control and pulse width modulation are also introduced in this work to facilitate the estimation process. Various simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and its superiority compared to other existing methods. The proposed approach offers a new perspective for parameter estimation of PMSMs and has great potential for practical applications in electronic and electromechanical industries.

Dynamic Hand Gesture Recognition is carried out in various studies to read patterns. Various sensors can be used to capture dynamic hand movement patterns. The results of the initial reading are usually in the form of raw data that must pass initial processing. Advanced processing is carried out to obtain features that will be trained using various classifiers. The recognition process without feature selection activities will reduce the accuracy of pattern recognition during the classification process. Seeing the many shortcomings in the implementation of the initial data processing, this study will present some initial processing examples to produce features that are relatively good for the data training process. The method used is the gaussian mixture model and the selection of predictors for the classification process. The sensor for recording dynamic hand movements used in this study is Leap-motion. There are three dynamic hand gestures were used in this study. The data used were 4609 coordinates spread in 30 features. The classifiers used are k-NN with Euclidean distance metric without feature selection process compare to the process with feature selection. The results obtained from this study are the availability of examples of feature selection models in the form of gaussian mixtures and some accuracy of the results of processing comparison. The lowest prediction, without and with feature prediction, has a slightly range from 99.7% to 100%.

This paper proposes a resource allocation scheme for energy harvesting-powered device-to-device (D2D) communication underlaying non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-based networks. The aim is to minimize the energy consumption of D2D devices while ensuring a certain quality of service. Copper is used as the energy harvesting material, and resource management is carried out based on the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) of each link in the system. The proposed scheme takes into account the interference caused by D2D communication and cellular networks. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can achieve significant energy savings compared with traditional resource allocation schemes, and that it is effective in a variety of network scenarios. The study provides a valuable reference for the design of energy-efficient wireless communication systems.

A considerable amount of massive Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications that intend to connect a wide range of low-complexity IoT devices are pushing the digital revolution and making an interconnected daily life a reality. However, especially in the connectivity sector, a holistic technical solution seems unlikely. In this regard, future 5G networks aim at unified connectivity with an ambitious node density of 1,000,000 devices per square kilometer in the area of 5G massive Machine Type Communication (mMTC). In this regard, this work aims at analyzing the capability of LoRaWAN as a complementary solution in unlicensed frequency bands to contribute to given 5G requirements for specific mMTC applications in large-scale deployments. The performance evaluation indicates limited downlink capabilities due to regulatory requirements defined for the 868 MHz short-range device (SRD) frequency band, but at the same time depicts that the uplink can cover approximately 10% of the 5G mMTC connection density objective. Hence, LoRaWAN indicates a high potential to contribute to 5G mMTC application areas, especially for non-time-critical sensor use cases without or even with low Quality of Service (QoS) requirements.

In the Industry 4.0 era, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become increasingly popular in preventative maintenance engineering for various industries. WSNs offer advantages such as low power consumption, easy installation, and low maintenance costs. These networks can continuously monitor various parameters such as vibrations, temperature, and pressure, and can alert maintenance personnel of any anomalies or potential failures. To effectively utilize WSNs in preventative maintenance, appropriate protocols for wireless communication are required to ensure reliable data transmission. This paper examines the use of WSNs in preventative maintenance in the Industry 4.0 context, focusing on the importance of monitoring and protocols for wireless communication, as well as the benefits of utilizing WSNs in industries. By leveraging WSNs, industrial facilities can be more proactive in identifying and addressing potential maintenance issues, leading to increased efficiency and reduced downtime.

In recent years, the development of smart grids has led to increasingly complex communication networks in intelligent distribution systems. As a result, the occurrence of circuit faults has become a common problem, which greatly affects the normal operation of the distribution system. In order to solve this problem, maintenance engineering has been focusing on the research and development of self-healing technology. This technology can quickly detect and locate faults, and then take appropriate measures to restore communication among different components of the system. Monitoring has also played an important role in the self-healing process. By monitoring the system's communication, it can help to identify potential faults before they occur, thus greatly reducing the risk of downtime. The use of self-healing technology not only improves the reliability and stability of the distribution system but also reduces maintenance costs, making it an important part of modern business strategies.

State-of-the-art security frameworks have been extensively addressing security issues for web resources, agents and services in the Semantic Web. The provision of Stream Reasoning as a new area spanning Semantic Web and Data Stream Management Systems has eventually opened up new challenges. Namely, their decentralized nature, the metadata descriptions, the number of users, agents, and services, makes securing Stream Reasoning systems difficult to handle. Thus, there is an inherent need of developing new security models which will handle security and automate security mechanism to a more autonomous system that supports complex and dynamic relationships between data, clients and service providers. We plan to validate our proposed security model on a typical application of stream data, on Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). In particular, WSNs for water quality monitoring will serve as a case study. The proposed model can be a guide when deploying and maintaining WSNs in different contexts. Moreover, this model will point out main segments which are most important in ensuring security in semantic stream reasoning systems, and their interrelationships. In this paper we propose a security framework to handle most important issues of security within WSN. The security model in itself should be an incentive for other researchers in creating other models to improve information security within semantic stream reasoning systems.

This paper introduces the application of machine learning for antenna array failure analysis. Antenna arrays, which consist of multiple antennas, are often used in communication systems. However, failures can occur, leading to degraded system performance. Traditional analysis methods for identifying failures are time-consuming and inefficient. This paper proposes using machine learning algorithms for analyzing antenna array failures. The approach involves training the machine learning models using various sampling methods and training data, including both healthy and faulty antenna arrays. The models were tested on different antenna array apertures, and the results showed that the proposed machine learning approach can accurately detect and classify antenna array failures. Overall, this study shows that machine learning can provide a useful tool for antenna array failure analysis, improving system reliability and performance.

Hyperspectral imaging is a well-established technique for obtaining detailed information about the physical and chemical properties of objects and materials. However, accurate classification of hyperspectral images remains a challenging task due to the high dimensionality of the data and the presence of noise and other sources of variability. In this paper, we present a new approach to hyperspectral image classification based on band-group non-negative tensor factorization (BGNTF). Our method leverages the benefits of both kernel-based and tensor-based methods, using a combination of kernel PCA and non-negative tensor factorization to extract informative features from the data. We then apply a support vector machine (SVM) classifier to the extracted features to perform classification. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on several publicly available datasets, showing that it outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both classification accuracy and training efficiency. Our results suggest that BGNTF is a promising method for hyperspectral image classification that can help unlock the full potential of hyperspectral imaging in a range of applications.

This paper presents a novel approach for mechanical faults diagnosis of high-voltage circuit breakers using hybrid features and an integrated extreme learning machine (ELM). Entropy and time-frequency analysis are utilized for feature extraction from the vibration signals obtained from the circuit breaker. The retrieved features are then combined into hybrid features, which are input into the integrated ELM for mechanical faults diagnosis. The proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on various types of circuit faults in circuit breakers. The results show that the proposed approach outperforms other conventional algorithms, such as support vector machines, in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach has great potential in practical applications for the diagnosis of mechanical faults in high-voltage circuit breakers.

Speech super-resolution is a task that involves enhancing the resolution of audio signals to improve their quality and clarity. With the increasing demand for high-quality audio, the need for robust super-resolution methods has become more apparent than ever. In recent years, researchers have focused on adapting deep learning methods to tackle this challenging problem. One such method is Parallel WaveNet, which has shown promising results in enhancing the resolution of audio signals. In this paper, we analyze the task of speech super-resolution and explore the use of Parallel WaveNet for this task. Through our analysis, we compare the Signal resolution and Image resolution approaches to super-resolution and highlight the advantages of using spectrograms. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance of our proposed method by measuring the Euclidean distance and distortion. Finally, we present the details of the training process used to train the Parallel WaveNet model for speech super-resolution. Our results show that Parallel WaveNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in this task and has the potential for further improvements in the future.

Crime prediction is a critical challenge for law enforcement agencies worldwide, as it plays a crucial role in preventing crimes before they occur. In this study, we proposed a multiple-ANFIS architecture that leverages spatiotemporal data to predict and prevent crimes. The proposed model's architecture was specially designed to process and analyze large volumes of data collected from various sources, including Iron, IP networks, Frequency modulation, and FCC. Through experimental evaluation, we demonstrated that the proposed model achieved a high degree of accuracy and reliability in predicting crimes. Specifically, the spatiotemporal data used as input to the model were sufficient to provide critical insights into potential crime hotspots and allowed us to deploy targeted measures aimed at preventing criminal activities in these areas. Overall, our study highlights the potential of leveraging machine learning algorithms and spatiotemporal data to enhance crime prediction, prevention, and reduction efforts globally.

This paper presents a graph-based approach for investigating malicious login events using analytical models and visualization tools. Authentication is a critical aspect of information security, and malicious login attempts pose a significant threat to the security of authentication systems.
