In order to investigate these events, we propose a novel computational model that utilizes graph theory to represent login data and identify patterns of malicious activity. Our approach is based on the principle of using graph-based analysis to extract information about the structure and behavior of malicious login events, and then using this information to develop targeted detection and mitigation strategies. The gold standard of our approach is to provide a comprehensive toolset for investigating malicious login behaviors, which can help security experts to detect, track, and prevent malicious activity in authentication systems. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through several case studies, which show that our tools and models can provide valuable insights into the behavior of malicious actors in authentication systems.

This paper presents a robust approach for semantic template matching in computer vision, using a superpixel region binary descriptor. The proposed method involves feature extraction, which is critical for achieving robust matching. In addition, this approach is designed to be robust to changes in lighting and other sources of strain that can affect the quality of template matching. By incorporating semantics into the feature extraction process, the proposed method is able to achieve higher accuracy in template matching. The use of a superpixel region binary descriptor also enables efficient computations, making this approach suitable for real-time applications. The results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods and provides a promising direction for future work in semantic template matching in computer vision.

This paper proposes a patch-based approach for semantic segmentation of epifluorescence imagery to detect arterioles and venules. Image segmentation is a critical step in analyzing microscopy images, and the use of semantics can improve the accuracy of the segmentation. The proposed method utilizes a training set of epifluorescence images of mice vasculature to develop a computer architecture for predicting the localization of arterioles and venules. The testing is performed on a separate set of microscopy images to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results show that our patch-based semantic segmentation approach achieves excellent accuracy in detecting arterioles and venules, which can be valuable in analyzing vasculature images for various medical applications.

We prove that global robust stabilization is possible by output feedback for a class of nonlinear systems with measurement sensitivity characterized by an unknown time-varying parameter. The nonlinear systems under consideration are assumed to satisfy a linear growth condition with a polynomial output-dependent rate, and thus cover a larger class of uncertain systems than the previous ones studied in [15], [2]. To deal with effectively the polynomial nonlinearity and the measurement sensitivity, we propose an estimator with a high-gain that needs to be updated dynamically. Then, an estimator-based controller is constructed step-by-step, achieving global state regulation of the resulting closed-loop system.

This paper discusses the quality monitoring and biases estimation of BOC navigation signals in the context of biomedical monitoring using body area networks (BANs) with wireless communication. The authors propose a microwave integrated circuit-based approach for bias estimation using logic gates and sensors, which can help improve the accuracy of navigation signals in BANs. The study highlights the importance of minimizing biases in navigation signals for reliable and continuous biomedical monitoring. The proposed method has the potential to enable real-time monitoring of implanted devices and enhance the overall efficiency of BANs. The results of this research will be beneficial for researchers and practitioners working in the field of biomedical monitoring and wireless communication.

IoT, the network of the future. The futuristic trend is towards the emerging technology based on the internet, which comprises a number of devices arranged systematic to form a network, converse among themselves and sharing exclusive information with the help of the Internet is named as Internet-of-Things (IoT). The context becomes smarter when so many devices get connected and placed properly. IoT network must also tackle with the overplus of security and privacy threats which disorganize and seize the data of entire industries as like some other existing information systems based on web technology. Therefore, to overcome this, IoT network must act towards effectively with the threats and also to make sure security and privacy of information that shared in a network. This paper gives an overview of the existing works on security and privacy challenges in the IoT network. In addition, the paper discusses the security attacks and privacy issues on IoT data. Hence, concern about privacy-preserving and security-aware is needed so that better protections shall be incorporated to make the massive IoT network to be a secured one.

This paper introduces a secure state estimation method with cumulative message authentication, which is aimed at enhancing the data integrity of state estimation. The proposed approach utilizes detectors to identify data tampering and incorrect measurements. By incorporating Kalman filters with message authentication, the estimation error can be reduced effectively. The cumulative message authentication technique enables the detection of multiple attacks and improves the robustness of the state estimation process. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively detect and prevent different types of attacks, such as message deletion, insertion, and falsification, guaranteeing the accuracy and reliability of state estimation in a secure way. The application of this technique can be useful in various fields, such as power system, transportation, and telecommunication, where secure and trustworthy communication is essential.

Global changes and current trends have led to major revisions in the field of education. In the context of higher education, it has proliferated successfully to move the curricula to a competency-based education. Also, the incorporation of ICT in the training process is a growing trend that has been strongly positioned in all levels of education. However, beyond the models and paradigms, what is relevant is the implementation of an innovative proposal. This is where the problems of a complex implementation are experienced. At UC Temuco, the computer science program renewed its curriculum to a competency model. For the evaluation of achievement of competences, a course called integration workshop is included in the curriculum at the end of each year. These courses include a series of individual and group strategies, which have been designed, refined and improved over the years. ICT is a strong component in the support of strategies, including tools for collaboration, authorship, software project management, among others. The workshops are evaluated externally through an event called "project fair", where actors from the business, government and academic world are invited. Results have been very satisfactory and have allowed a continuous improvement of the strategies and the selection of ICT support tools.

A steady growth in terms of development alongwith the use of consumer electronics has been noticed which is a consequence of and increased rate of globalization that has raised the living standards. This has arisen a need for high security authentication systems in order to safeguard personal information stored on mobile devices. Since the high complexity and security of existing biometric systems is becoming the prime concern in terms of space and time, automated personal identification using finger-vein biometric is emerging to be a prominent topic in both practical as well as examination applications. In this paper, using MATLAB 2016a, we present discriminant analysis and KNN of machine learning method, as it stands for K- nearest neighbor algorithm are used to verify and calculate the accuracy of the features of the finger vein images. Thus, the accuracy obtained from KNN is 55.84% whereas from discriminant analysis the accuracy obtained is 92.21%. Finally discriminant analysis is more accurate than KNN technique.

This paper addresses the sensitivity analysis of an extended and dual Kalman filters used for state estimation (state of charge (SoC), inner resistance) of lithium-ion batteries mainly for traction applications. The Kalman filters in different configurations are now widely applied in modern battery management systems. It is well known that the quality of estimation is dependent from the accuracy of model used. In this case a compromise between model's complexity and quality of estimation is one of main critical factors while developing a Kalman filter based estimation solution. In case of state estimation of lithium-ion batteries this point becomes important due to the following reasons: transformation of chemical effects to electrical model causes the loss of model accuracy; model parameters are not constant due to ageing and temperature rice; parameters of derived discrete time models are sensitive to measurement noise. In this paper authors analyse the influence of varying inner parameters of a lithium-ion battery and the choice of time discrete model onto accuracy of SoC estimation. An extended and dual discrete Kalman filter using zero-order hold method and Tustin transform are tested using new European driving cycle.

This paper proposes a method for estimating the wrist joint moment based on a fusion of a musculoskeletal model and muscle synergy for neuromuscular interface. The approach utilizes the biological system modeling of the human wrist joint to estimate the dynamics of the joint moment. The muscles involved in wrist movement are analyzed and their respective force contributions are determined. By fusing the musculoskeletal model and muscle synergy, a comprehensive estimation of the wrist joint moment can be obtained. The proposed method provides a more accurate and efficient way of estimating the wrist joint moment during movement, which can be used to improve the performance of prosthetic devices and enhance the rehabilitation process of patients with wrist injuries.

Neural implants are used to continuously record essential signals in studies of neurological disorders. Existing systems involve the use of invasive procedures and revision surgeries to maintain adequate system performance. Our previous work demonstrated a fully-passive wireless system, tested in vitro, and was demonstrated capable of sensing even minute neural signals. This recorder has a minimum detectable signal (MDS) below 15 μV in amplitude and a RF sensitivity down to about - 135 dBm. While results have been promising, this system is yet to be used to study neurological disorders, the final intended application of the system. In this paper, for the first time, we evaluate the wireless neurosensing system's ability to capture the characteristic components of epilepsy, namely interictal epileptiform discharges. The present validation of this technology has great future clinical implications in neuroscience, especially epilepsy studies.

This paper proposes a hybrid performance modeling approach for optimizing In-System-Structural-Test (ISST) latency. As safety is a major concern in automotive engineering, ISST is critical for ensuring the safe operation of electronic systems. The proposed approach incorporates both analytical and computational modeling techniques to accurately predict ISST latency. The modeling framework takes into account various factors such as computer architecture, bandwidth, data models, and IP networks. The main objective of the proposed approach is to minimize ISST latency while maintaining the required level of safety. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through experimental results, where a significant reduction in ISST latency was achieved. The proposed hybrid performance modeling approach can be used as a tool for designers to optimize the latency of ISST, while ensuring safe operation of electronic systems in the automotive industry.

In recent years, automatic modulation classification (AMC) has been a challenging task due to the modulation diversity and the interference caused by various environmental factors. In this paper, we propose a deep hierarchical network for automatic modulation classification which utilizes feature extraction and deep learning techniques. The proposed network is able to handle a wide range of modulation schemes even at low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) with high classification accuracy. The convolutional layers of the network play a key role in automatically learning features from the raw signal without the need for prior knowledge or manual feature extraction. The proposed hierarchical architecture is capable of handling interference and is robust to variations in channel conditions. The effectiveness of our proposed method is demonstrated through experimental evaluations on real-world modulation datasets. In conclusion, this work shows the potential of deep learning and natural language processing techniques in the context of modulation classification, providing an alternative approach to traditional techniques.

Recently, the need for a real-time healthcare monitoring system that able to offer remote and personal health-care services has increased. The patients with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) require continuous services of testing, following-up and monitoring. Offering these services to patients smoothly at any time needs to integrated healthcare system. The recent development in information systems and technologies facilitate introducing such healthcare systems. This paper proposed an integrated system model, which offers the services of testing, following-up and monitoring patients with (SCD). The proposed system uses support vector machine SVM, which is supervised machine learning approach to analyze the collected data of a specific patient and takes the appropriate action such as send alert message to the healthcare staff. To perform the classification process, four methods are applied with SVM algorithm, which are Sequential Minimal Optimization SMO, Rules JRIP, Tree Decision Stump and Naive Bays for comparative analysis. In this paper, many experiments were implemented based on the four machine learning algorithms to determine patients of SCD from normal patients. The results were promising as they show 99% classifications were accurate when using SMO algorithm.

Managing trust in mobile networks necessitates dealing with uncertainty, resulting from incomplete, duplicate or conflicting evidence. In this work, possibility theory is used to deal with uncertainty, and a trust model is developed that includes the network nodes' integrity, their competency and that of the connections among them. Evidence obtained by direct observation (`passive') is integrated with that solicited from other nodes (`active') to generate possibility distributions, or trust profiles, that can be combined, updated and discounted. Simulations of mobile ad hoc networks show that the inclusion of these trust profiles in routing decisions conserves network resources and limits data exposure by directing packets over reliable links through uncompromised nodes. Possibility theory enables the information gain provided by different forms of evidence to be evaluated, and this is used to explore the benefits of different sources of active trust evidence. It is seen that passive evidence is not sufficient to maintain trust profiles with low uncertainty, and that active trust evidence obtained by authentication requests provides higher informational value than that received using reputation solicitation.

Facial features play an essential role in various applications such as hospitals, biomedical imaging, and security. However, to protect the privacy of individuals, these features are often anonymized in facial images. In this paper, we propose a method called Refacing to reconstruct the anonymized facial features. Refacing is based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and focuses on image reconstruction using a set of training data. By training our model on a large dataset of facial images, we can generate realistic images that reconstruct the anonymized facial features. Our method has the potential to greatly improve the accuracy of facial recognition and biometric applications that rely on facial features. The results of our experiments indicate that Refacing outperforms previous methods in reconstructing anonymized facial features with a high degree of accuracy. In conclusion, our work provides a valuable contribution to the field of facial image processing and could have significant implications for a wide range of applications that rely on accurate facial feature recognition, including security and medical diagnosis.

This paper proposes a scalable healthcare assessment system for diabetic patients using deep learning on multiple GPUs. The system utilizes large databases of medical diagnostic imaging data to detect and diagnose various diseases related to diabetes. Deep learning algorithms are employed to efficiently process the vast amounts of data and accurately identify abnormalities. The use of multiple GPUs allows for faster processing times and increased scalability. Overall, this system has the potential to improve patient outcomes by enabling earlier and more accurate detection of diabetes-related diseases.

The demand for personalized recommendation systems has grown over the years due to the ever-increasing volume of data available through various sources. In this paper, we present a recommendation system for Indian Cuisine Recipes based on Ingredients, which utilizes a combination of computer science techniques like recommender systems, databases, data mining, and machine learning to generate personalized recipe recommendations to users based on their ingredient choices. Our approach utilizes a knowledge graph representation of the recipes, which enables us to combine different types of data and provide better recommendations for the users. We evaluate our system's performance using a dataset of Indian Cuisine Recipes, and the results show promising accuracies in generating recipe recommendations. Furthermore, we discuss the potential applications of this system in conferences and the food industry and present the challenges faced in deploying this system on a large scale. This paper contributes to the development of personalized recommendation systems for food enthusiasts, and we believe that our approach can be further optimized to provide even better recommendations in the future.

Multi energy flow coupled network computing provides the constraints of network balance and system energy security for optimal operation of regional integrated energy system, and it is also an important basis for the system security and stability analysis. Considering the dynamic response characteristics of multi energy coupling system with multiple time scales, the network model for combined calculation of electric, gas, thermal / cold multi energy flow is constructed from two aspects of steady state and dynamic in this article. Furthermore, in the process of dynamic model solving, for improving the computational efficiency without affecting the simulation accuracy, the hybrid step time domain simulation method with electromechanical transient simulation for electric power system and medium-long term transient simulation for non-electrical system is proposed, and this method can effectively support the network computation of the multi-energy coupling system. Finally, the model and algorithm are verified by building an example of an electro-thermal coupling network and carrying the simulating.

Cloud Computing models, architectures and service adaption have been growing on a larger scale based on convenience, on-demand resource provisioning, customized services and economic benefits. The Cloud assists enterprises in reducing the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) but the anticipated Return on Investment (ROI) is not guaranteed in time due to quality pitfalls leading to vendor lock-in situations. Sensing technologies, which utilize the cloud environment as a prime infrastructure supporting IoT applications and data processing often fail to identify and understand Cloud Quality of Service (QoS) issues. This paper discusses factors related to assessing the Cloud vendors QoS, minimizing quality control and cost issues and increasing feasibility for IoT applications on the cloud ecosystem.

SENSEI is an intelligent advisory system designed specifically for the eSport community and casual players. The system draws insights from large datasets of game-related information, gathered from various sources such as discussion forums and portals. The data is then subjected to rigorous analysis using techniques such as data mining and machine learning. The resulting insights are presented to users in an easily accessible format, enabling them to make informed decisions about their gaming strategies. SENSEI has the potential to revolutionize the eSport community, enabling players to achieve better results and reach new levels of success.

This paper proposes a novel approach called Sparse-Complementary Convolution (SC-Conv) to improve the utilization efficiency of CNN models. The approach is focused on reducing the complexity of the model architecture, particularly in the areas of kernel and convolution, while maintaining the accuracy of feature extraction. By taking advantage of complementary information from different layers within the network, SC-Conv is able to effectively reduce the computational complexity while enhancing the model's performance. One of the key contributions of this approach is seen in the optimization of network architecture, particularly in the ability to reduce the need for complex modeling techniques while maintaining the model's ability to accurately classify different shapes within the input data. The approach has the potential to significantly improve performance in the field of computational modeling, particularly in the area of image recognition and other forms of visual data analysis. These improvements could have significant implications for both industry and academia, particularly in the development of more efficient and effective machine learning techniques. Complexity theory will also play a key role in the development and refinement of this approach.

In view of the situation that dynamic system's time-delay estimation methods are complicated and most of them need to know the system structure at first, a system time-delay estimation method based on the correlation coefficient is proposed in this paper. The implementation principle of this method is introduced in detail. The approach regards the system as a black box and does not need to know the system's structure. Through calculating the correlation coefficient of the input and output of the system, according to the variation law of the correlation coefficient, the time-delay of the system can be estimated. Simulation results show that this method has better recognition performance for low-order systems but it can easily be affected by the inertia parameter of high-order systems which maybe lead to some deviations in the results. Also, it is robust and accurate to system that contain oscillation.

In this paper, we propose a method for the classification of epoxy wedges in glass-fiber reinforced plastics using a millimeter-wave imaging system in W-Band. The proposed method leverages radar imaging and radar cross-sections to accurately identify the location and structural properties of each epoxy wedge. Additionally, we explore the use of wireless sensor networks to enhance the performance of our classification algorithm. The research is focused on the application of this technology in the field of plastics and composite materials, which are commonly utilized in industries such as aerospace, automotive, and construction. Overall, the results of our study demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of using millimeter-wave imaging systems for the classification of epoxy wedges in glass-fiber reinforced plastics.

A Memory Augmented Neural Network (MANN) is an extension to an RNN which enables it to save large amount of data to a memory object which is dimensionally separated from the Neural Network. This paper introduces a new Python library based on TensorFlow to define MANNs as Python objects. In addition to the standard implementation of the MANN, this contribution proposes a modification to the head calculation which decreases the noise while searching through the memory. The paper presents two experiments concerning the proposed implementation.FirsttheMANNistrainedtobeabletostoreand reproduce a piece of data (a task with linear data connectivity), and second the MANN is trained to find a Minimum Vertex Cover of a Graph (MVCG). This task was chosen because the connectivity of the vertex in the graph, that would pose a challenge to the MANN. The tests show that he MANN has no problem learning the first task, and that it is able to find an optimal solution for the MVCG problem in most cases.

Connected Cars and their related technologies have been rapidly evolving in the last decade. One of the most crucial development areas addresses the aggregation of massive amounts of sensor data arriving continuously from a wide variety of hardware components: e.g. tyre sensors, cameras built on-board, and other external sources. Since the main aim of the manufacturers is to build safer, easier to drive, and more autonomous cars based on the collected data; they follow the latest ICT trends. Two technologies can be considered as already accepted and proven approaches at several application fields since they provide facilities (among others) to handle and process the generated, heterogeneous, large-scale, and rapidly growing data sets: Cloud computing and big data. The cloud infrastructure may act as an Internet of Things (IoT) backend, or as a kind of central hub by gathering the incoming sensor and other types of data. Moreover, the cloud offers elasticity in terms of data analytics and distribution services for such enormous amount of data. This paper details the second, private Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) version of our cloud-oriented IoT back-end framework for Connected Cars and its scalable services relying on our experiences gained during the development of its first, Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) variant on an OpenNebula infrastructure. During the design and development stages we leveraged on the Cloud Foundry PaaS platform deployed at the premises of an automotive supplier company. The new reference implementation is able to handle, analyze and visualize vehicular data as illustrated by various use cases including Eco-driving, weather report/forecast, parameter coding over cloud, collection of CAN data, flashing devices remotely, etc.

Face recognition is one of effective method often used for personal identification, the accuracy of the face recognition depends on many factors typically implemented at different places in unconstrained environments. Not only, the amount of images in the dataset are affected to the accuracy of face recognition but also the quality of the images is also an impact. For this reason, this work proposed the convolutional neural networks model to improve the accuracy of the face recognition under an insufficient a number of images in dataset and the images that contains an interfering factors. The challenge of this work is the regulating and configuring of many parameters the network for its best performance and suite for this conditions. The experiment results shown that the CNN model gives encouraging accuracy of the face recognition. Furthermore, this work also compared the accuracy with the different face recognition techniques such as Fisherfaces, Eigenfaces, LBPH, and MLP neural networks. For these result, CNNs were used as an efficient solution for improving the rate of recognition accuracy on this conditions.

Large integrated circuits, such as System-on-a-Chip (SoC) designs, often suffer from a reduced operational frequency due to various timing constraints. This reduction in operating frequency is often caused by the impact of dynamic voltage drop or aging/thermal on setup timing violations, often referred to as maximum timing pushout. This problem is exacerbated in advanced FinFET designs such as 7nm/5nm due to reduced VDD, insufficient switching scenario coverage, increased resistance of lower layers of metal, and larger local power density. This paper proposes a novel method using machine learning techniques to design for reliability coverage by using critical scenario(s) predictor for running dynamic voltage drop analysis and critical timing path(s) predictor for accurate timing/aging analysis with impact of voltage drop.

This paper proposes a novel saliency model that reveals the long-term info to boost detection accuracy. The saliency estimation of conventional methods heavily depends on the locally revealed short-term info, and they could easily be trapped into imperfect configurations. In contrast, our method can take full consideration of common consistency of those reliable low-level predictions from the perspective of the entire video sequence. Meanwhile, we adopt a newly designed self-learning strategy which is guided by the low-rank analysis to adaptively reveal the long-term spatial-temporal video coherency. To avoid the error accumulations, we also propose a novel non-local descriptor to enhance the discriminative power of the feature space. Thus, the newly revealed the long-term info can be directly regarded as a trustful indicator to sustain additional low-rank analysis, which would serve as the basis toward selective fusion and significantly enhance the detection accuracy.

Most of the existing hashing methods for image retrieval are based on the assumption the image database is stationary. However, in the real world data environments are always changing or non-stationary, therefore the underlying data distribution may change from time to time which will result in the problem of concept drift. Incremental Hashing (ICH) is the only existing method to handle image retrieval with concept drift in non-stationary data environments. It builds hash codes for the database through increments. At each increment, a set of new hash functions is built with the new chunk of data, which is utilized to update the multi-hashing system to generate multiple sets of hash codes for all data. However, only the newest data chunk is used to train individual hash functions, while the semantic similarity information of previous data is missed. In this paper, we present a new hashing method based on ICH for image retrieval with concept drift, Incremental Hashing with Dynamic Semantic Pool (ICH-DSP). It builds a semantic pool to collect representative labeled data for each existing class. The semantic pool is updated incrementally and is used as the supervisory information for the training of hash functions. Experimental results on three real world image databases show that ICH-DSP outperforms the original ICH and other state-of-the-art hashing methods.

With the rapid development of mobile Internet and Web3D technology, the demand for 3D visualization technology is more and more larger. However, limited bandwidth and the browser's low load capacity etc. have seriously restricted the development of technology. Therefore, the paper proposes a framework to better show 3D shape, which is named as S-LCM framework. Specially, mesh compression which achieves a fast transmission data process, is one of most effective ways. In addition, due to the poor rendering capabilities of the browsers, it is very difficult to rendering the entire model at one time. Moreover, it often leads to the browser crashes that the transmitted model data one-time rendering. Besides, A Dijkstra-based mesh segmentation algorithm is proposed to realize component-wise rendering and lightweight for shape. Furthermore, a voxel-based component repetition method is adopted to detect the repetitive components, so that we can perform matrix transformation to finish repetitive components Web3D visualization, i.e. lightweight for shape. Last but not least, the related experiments are performed to validate our proposed framework. What is more, many models are tested, the results show the S-LCM framework is feasible and superior.

This paper proposes a multipoint wireless information and power transfer strategy to maximize sum-throughput in wireless body area networks (WBANs) with energy harvesting. WBANs are wireless sensor networks used for wearable health monitoring devices that are connected to the internet of things (IoT). They have limitations on battery capacity and typically rely on energy harvesting, which complicates the communication protocols. This strategy employs a dual-switching operation mode to optimize the RF signals and maximize the sum-throughput of data and power transfer. The proposed strategy is validated through simulations, demonstrating the superiority of the multipoint information and power transfer approach in enhancing the performance of WBANs. The study shows that this strategy can improve the system efficiency and prolong the lifespan of the WBAN devices, making it a promising direction for future WBAN research.

Facial expression is controlled by facial muscle and can be considered as appearance and geometric variation of key parts. One key challenging issue of static-based facial expression recognition is to capture effective information from a single facial image. In this paper, we propose a graph representation with Bidirectional RNN (BRNN) for static-based facial expression recognition. Each node on the graph represents appearance information around the facial landmarks. Edges represent the geometric information encoded by the distance between two nodes. A bidirectional recurrent neural network utilized to process the graph extracts the appearance and geometric representation. The final representation from BRNN is fed into a fully connected layer and a Softmax layer to infer expressions. Experimental results show that this method achieves significant improvements over the state-of-art methods on three widely used facial databases (Oulu-CASIA, CK+, and MMI), and our method reduces the error rates of the previous best methods by 42.2%, 35.9% and 18.7%, respectively.

With the advent of big data era, enormous volumes of data are generated every second. Varied data processing algorithms and architectures have been proposed in the past to achieve better execution of data mining algorithms. One such algorithm is extracting most frequently occurring patterns from the transactional database. Dependency of transactions on time and location further makes frequent itemset mining task more complex. The present work targets to identify and extract the frequent patterns from such time and location-aware transactional data. Primarily, the spatio-temporal dependency of air quality data is leveraged to find out frequently co-occurring pollutants over several locations of Delhi, the capital city of India. Varied approaches have been proposed in the past to extract frequent patterns efficiently, but this work suggests a generalized approach that can be applied to any numeric spatio-temporal transactional data, including air quality data. Furthermore, a comprehensive description of the algorithm along with a sample running example on air quality dataset is shown in this work. A detailed experimental evaluation is carried out on the synthetically generated datasets, benchmark datasets, and real world datasets. Furthermore, a comparison with spatio-temporal apriori as well as the other state-of-the-art non-apriori-based algorithms is shown. Results suggest that the proposed algorithm outperformed the existing approaches in terms of execution time of algorithm and memory resources.

In order to ensure the safety of molten metal operation and improve the efficiency of monitoring and early warning, molten metal hazards monitoring and early warning system is proposed based on convolutional neural network algorithm. The system utilizes image recognition technology such as behavior analysis, object detection and scene recognition. It consists of five functional modules: real-time monitoring, safety inspection, safety early warning, emergency rescue and information management. Equipped with AR helmet, the system demonstrates a wide potential for application in the field of safety management.

This paper presents an assessment of hydrodynamic coefficients for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) using analytic and semi-empirical methods. The study focuses on the relationship between hydrodynamics and vehicle dynamics, including the effects of force and aerodynamics on AUV motion. Solid modeling and computational modeling are employed to create accurate representations of AUVs and calculate hydrodynamic coefficients. The results of this study provide insight into the behavior of AUVs in water and can aid in the development of more efficient and reliable AUVs.

Feature selection is the important step in data preparing phase to reduce complexity of dataset and increase the performance of the classification. In this paper, we proposed Cuckoo Feature Selection (CFS) algorithm, which is based on the natural behavior of cuckoo birds. Moreover, two different classification strategies of naïve Bayes were combined with the proposed algorithm and have been experimented on various datasets from the UCI repository, and the proposed algorithm were compared with previous work to test its performance. In conclusion, this work provides empirical evidence that the proposed CFS algorithm with both classifiers was able to perform satisfactorily over UCI datasets.

This research paper proposes a GPU-based parameterized NMPC scheme for controlling a half car vehicle with a semi-active suspension system. Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are used for solving the complex numerical computations involved in the scheme. A mathematical model is developed to simulate the behavior of the half-car vehicle and the semi-active suspension system. The study focuses on the control of the shock absorbers, as they play a crucial role in the smooth functioning of the vehicle on roads. The vehicle dynamics are modeled using computational modeling techniques, and the results show that the proposed scheme provides better control of the half-car vehicle with a semi-active suspension system as compared to traditional control methods. By using GPU-based computing, this scheme shows promise for real-time implementation in modern automobiles, improving their efficiency and safety on the roads.

This paper proposes the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for blind decoding in Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) systems. SCMA is a new technology for wireless communication that uses a small number of resources compared to traditional communication systems. However, this results in high decoding complexity that requires detectors with high computational power. This is addressed by using CNNs, a type of deep learning algorithm that can efficiently process large amounts of data. The paper presents simulation results showing that the proposed CNN-based decoder achieves low bit error rate with reduced decoding complexity compared to previous decoder designs. This work opens up new possibilities for using CNNs in complex decoding scenarios and contributes to the development of next-generation wireless communication systems.

A central challenge in designing embedded control systems or cyber-physical systems (CPS) is that of translating high-level models of control algorithms into efficient implementations, while ensuring that model-level semantics are preserved. While a large body of techniques for designing provably correct control strategies exist in the control theory literature, when it comes to transforming mathematical descriptions of these strategies to an efficient implementation, the available means are surprisingly ad hoc in nature. Among other reasons, this is because of (i) implementation platform details not sufficiently being accounted for in controller models, (ii) side effects introduced in the code generation process, (iii) various compiler optimizations whose impact on the dynamics of the plant being controlled not being properly understood, (iv) the presence of analog components on the implementation platform whose behavior is difficult to model, (v) computation and communication delays that exist in an implementation but were not accounted for in the model, and (vi) also the effects of image/video processing whose accuracy and timing behavior are difficult to model. As we move towards designing autonomous systems, these issues become biting problems on the path to certification, and striking a balance between performance and certification. In this position paper, we discuss some of these challenges - that we formulate as the need for modeling the interactions between various implementation layers in a CPS - and potential research directions to address them.

With the rapid growth of data in the education sector, it has become challenging to evaluate and manage student feedback effectively. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines data visualization, text analysis, and machine learning techniques to analyze student opinion in a comprehensive manner. The proposed approach aims to help resource management teams understand the real opinions and sentiments of students about the programs offered by an institution. By leveraging text analysis and sentiment analysis, the approach can provide a fine-grained understanding of student feedback that goes beyond simple numerical ratings. Furthermore, the use of data visualization enables the intuitive presentation of the results obtained, making it easy for non-technical personnel to comprehend the data. Our experiments on students from various institutions demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach in gathering and analyzing student feedback, thus proving its usefulness for educational institutions seeking to improve their student programs.

Beamforming with conventional array processing utilizes linear, additive processing techniques to combine the signals from the different array elements. In previous work, a multiplicative processing technique was proposed for combining the signals from sensor arrays for super-resolution beamforming. The multiplicative processing technique is derived from standard linear array processing concepts and was shown to emulate the performance of larger array apertures. In this paper, experimental measurements from an acoustic sensor array are used to validate the proposed method for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation by comparing these results with those from linear processing of measurements from much larger aperture arrays. The processing results show that the multiplicative processing of experimental measurements from smaller apertures perform as well as linear processing of measurements from larger apertures.

Super resolution in biomedical imaging is an important task that requires high accuracy and resolution. This paper proposes the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for super resolution in medical imaging. GANs consist of two parts, generators and discriminators, that work together to create high quality images. In order to achieve accurate results, the generators are trained with a set of dictionaries that contain information about the medical images. The training process involves measuring the loss between the generated images and the original images using Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR). The proposed approach shows promising results compared to traditional methods and has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and resolution of medical images.

In the micro-expression detection system on part of facial components, it is necessary to detect that component in accurately, precisely and fast. This study shows a comparison between accuracy and speed in the detection of the component area of the face (right eye, left eye and mouth) automatically. Micro expression occurs in a short time, fast and in very smooth movements. The face component detection method conducted in this study is a feature-based method (Viola Jones method) which is compared with the model-based method (ASM and DRMF methods). Comparison of the accuracy of the three methods in the detection of the face component area shows that the ASM and DRMF methods provide an accuracy value of 100%, while the Haar Cascade Classifier method shows an average accuracy of 44%. Meanwhile, on speed measurement to find the face component area, the DRMF method is the fastest with an average processing time of 0.08 seconds followed by ASM method of 0.14 seconds, and the Haar method of 0.25 seconds.

At a time when comments are growing in social networks, e-commerce sites, sites dedicated to information, etc., the technic of opinion mining has finally emerged as the essential tool for processing these data. In the literature, approaches and many methods have been proposed to analyze the texts of official languages (French, English, Portuguese...). Recent solutions increasingly provide results close to reality. However, the complexity of comments from Senegalese online presses question the performance of current methods of opinion mining. The purpose of this article is to highlight the obstacles that these comments may cause with regard to current methods. In perspective, we will try to propose a possible solution to analyze the comments of Senegalese in order to predict their opinion.

This paper proposes a user monitoring road traffic information collection system using SUMO and Scheme for Road Surveillance with Deep Mind Analytics and Human Behavior Tracking. The objective of this system is to collect real-time traffic information for effective road surveillance and efficient routing protocols. The proposed system leverages wireless sensor networks to minimize energy consumption while ensuring quality of service. A Matlab-based simulation is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system. Our system enables a comprehensive monitoring of road traffic and provides insights into human behavior tracking to improve road safety and traffic efficiency. This study contributes towards the development of intelligent transportation systems that can make efficient use of available data and improve overall transportation experiences.

Recently, it has been shown that the classical hard real-time scheduling theory can be applied to streaming applications modeled as acyclic Cyclo-Static Dataflow (CSDF) graphs. However, many streaming applications are modeled as cyclic CSDF graphs, thus they are not supported by such scheduling theory. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an approach which enables to apply the classical hard real-time scheduling theory on streaming applications modeled as cyclic CSDF graphs. The proposed approach converts each task in a cyclic CSDF graph to a constrained-deadline periodic task. This conversion enables the utilization of many hard real-time scheduling algorithms which offer properties such as temporal isolation and fast calculation of the required number of processors for scheduling the tasks. We evaluate the performance of our approach in comparison to existing scheduling approaches. The evaluation, on a set of real-life benchmarks, demonstrates that our approach can schedule the tasks in an application, modeled as a cyclic CSDF graph, with guaranteed throughput equal or comparable to the throughput obtained by existing scheduling approaches while providing hard real-time guarantees for every task in the application thereby enabling temporal isolation among concurrently running tasks/applications on a multi-processor platform.

Mission critical applications require UPS for power conditioning and back-up, and multiple UPS units may be combined in redundant architectures to maximize reliability. However, both upfront investment as well as operating costs are penalized by the required deployment of excess capacity.So-called Iso-parallel or Ring Bus architecture employing rotary UPS systems is a cost effective and efficient alternative. This paper discusses the extension of such concept, proposing the deployment of static UPS in Ring Bus arrangement.First, rotary and static UPS topologies and associated characteristics are reviewed. Then, the Ring Bus architecture and associated load sharing technique is detailed. Finally, the paper focuses on handling of fault scenarios, as the main challenge with using static UPS is their limited fault current capability. Overcoming such limitation unlocks the benefit of static UPS deployment in Ring Bus systems.

This paper presents an experimental analysis of fraud detection methods in enterprise telecommunication data using unsupervised outlier ensembles. The research focuses on anomaly detection, utilizing various detectors and feature extraction techniques. The study employs the bagging method to improve the robustness of the models. The experiments were conducted on data from multiple continents and business types, allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed methods. Results indicate that the unsupervised outlier ensembles approach is effective in detecting fraud in enterprise telecommunication data, and the bagging technique significantly improves the robustness of the models. The study provides valuable insights for the development of effective fraud detection methods in enterprise telecommunication data.

In this paper, we propose a spectral theory for the analysis of non-stationary pulse stochastic electromagnetic processes in devices of electric transport systems. The study focuses on random processes, harmonic analysis, surges, estimation, electromagnetic compatibility, and substation systems. The theory presented in this paper is useful for analyzing the impact of these processes on electric transport systems. The proposed method can be used to estimate the impact of these processes on the performance of devices in electric transport systems. The results of this study have been presented in various conferences related to electromagnetic systems. The proposed approach can help to improve the design and functioning of electric transport systems, thereby improving their reliability and performance.

Photoacoustic (PA) imaging is a promising new imaging technology for non-invasively visualizing blood vessels inside biological tissues. In addition to blood vessels, body hairs are also visualized in PA imaging, and the body hair signals degrade the visibility of blood vessels. For learning a body hair classifier, the amount of real training and test data is limited, because PA imaging is a new modality. To address this problem, we propose a novel semi-supervised learning (SSL) method for extracting body hairs. The method effectively learns the discriminative model from small labeled training data and small unlabeled test data by introducing prior knowledge, of the orientation similarity among adjacent body hairs, into SSL. Experimental results using real PA data demonstrate that the proposed approach is effective for extracting body hairs as compared with several baseline methods.

Terrain recognition is an essential task for robots and autonomous vehicles operating in unstructured environments. In this context, deep learning methods have shown promising results due to their ability to extract meaningful features automatically. In this paper, we present a novel deep residual texture network (DRTN) for terrain recognition. Our network uses convolutional layers to extract high-level features from the input terrain data. Moreover, we use residual connections to improve the performance of the network by allowing the gradient to flow more efficiently during training. Additionally, we propose a new loss function that takes into account the spatial resolution of the input data, which further improves the accuracy of our network. We evaluate our approach on two popular terrain datasets and demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and efficiency. The results confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approach in terrain recognition, and our method can be used in various robotic applications that require data mining and convolutional codes.

This paper aims to develop a predictive model that can accurately predict a client's consent to a bank term deposit using feature selection. To achieve this goal, feature extraction techniques will be used to identify the most relevant features that can affect client consent. A range of prediction algorithms will then be applied to build several predictive models. These models will be trained, tested and evaluated against different data models. The performance of the models will be assessed using various software algorithms, and the best model will be selected for deployment. By applying feature selection techniques and developing accurate predictive models, this study seeks to improve the quality and efficiency of client consent prediction in the banking industry.

Naive Bayes Classifier is an effective and easy method in general, and is used popularly in document classification. It's also a particularly useful classifier for large dataset. Naive Bayes assigns instances to a class label through maximizing the posterior probability assuming that the instance features are independent of each other. Using this model, many-to-one assumption was proposed to deal with the case where a class may be constituted of many different components. An issue of this approach is how to construct these components on each class. In this paper, we propose a simple heuristic solution of applying a hierarchical tree for assigning components to classes. Through evaluation experiments, we find that the proposed approach shows better performance than the conventional one when the training data size is large enough. Some other issues in practicing many-to-one assumption are also discussed.

Entity resolution refers to the process of identifying and integrating records belonging to unique entities. The standard methods are using a rule-based or machine learning models to compare and assign a point, to indicate the status of matching or non-matching the pair of records. However, a comprehensive comparison across all the records pairs leads to a second-order matching complexity. Therefore blocking methods are using before the matching, to group the same entities into small blocks. Then the matching operation is done comprehensively. Several blocking methods provided to efficiently block the input data into manageable groups, including the token blocking, that holds records with a similar token in the same block. Most of the previous methods did not take any semantic criteria into account. In this paper, we propose a new method, called DeepBlock that uses deep learning for the task of blocking in entity resolution. DeepBlock combines syntactic and semantic similarities to calculate the similarity between records. We have evaluated the DeepBlock over the real-world dataset and compared it with the existing blocking technique (token blocking). Our experimental result shows that the combination of semantic and syntactic similarity can considerably improve the quality of blocking. The results show that DeepBlock outperforms the token blocking method significantly with respect to pair quality (PQ) measure.

Semi-supervised anomaly detection identifies abnormal (testing) observations which are different from normal (training) observations. In many practical situations, anomalies are poorly insufficient and not well defined, while the normal data are easily sampled, have a wide variety, and may not be classified. For this paradigm, we propose a novel end-to-end deep network as an anomaly detector only trained on normal samples. Our architecture consists of a conditional variational auto-encoder (CVAE), a feature discriminator (FD), and an adversarially trained WGAN-GP discriminator. The CVAE is designed as a generator to reconstruct images. It leverages underlying category information and multivariate Gaussian distributions to regularize the latent space, enabling a smooth and informative manifold. For anomalies which have a certain similarity to normal data, we perform active negative training by generating potential outliers from the latent space to limit network generative capability. In order to capture data characteristics, we maximize the mutual information between the inputs and the latent codes by the FD. It enhances the relationship between the high-dimensional image space and corresponding encoded vectors. To promote reconstruction, a structural similarity loss is applied to robustly recover local texture details and the WGAN-GP discriminator is employed to aid in generating photo-realistic images. We distinguish anomalies by computing a reconstruction-based anomaly score. Different from recent encoder-decoder or GAN-based architectures, our approach considers input categories, constructs, and exploits a useful manifold in an unsupervised manner and has a stronger reconstruction capability. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods over several benchmark datasets.

This paper presents a new approach to enhance security in optical fiber networks by utilizing Spread Spectrum over OFDM. The proposed method improves security by spreading the data across a wide spectrum, making it difficult for eavesdropping attacks. The use of OFDM also enables effective resource management and routing, optimizing bandwidth utilization. The study shows that this technique is highly effective in improving security and resource management in elastic optical networks.

In this paper, we propose a two-stage audio-video speech separation method using multimodal convolutional neural networks. The interference caused by noise or other speakers in speech signals is a challenging problem that affects the quality and intelligibility of the speech. Therefore, the proposed method utilizes both audio and video modalities to provide a more robust separation performance. The training of the network is performed using a large-scale dataset of speech signals and noise recordings. The signal to noise ratio is used as a measure of the separation performance. Spectrogram and feature extraction techniques are applied to preprocess the input signal. Moreover, noise measurement is conducted to estimate the noise power spectral density. The proposed method shows promising results for speech enhancement in noisy environments. Future improvements could be made by investigating the use of other modalities, such as lip-reading or facial expressions, to further improve the separation performance.

Deep learning methods are at the forefront of leading state-of-the-art methods in a wide range of machine learning applications. In particular, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) attain topmost performance assuming a sufficiently large number of labeled training examples. Unfortunately, labeled data is artificially curated, and it requires human labor, which consequently makes it expensive and time-consuming. Moreover, there are no guarantees that the obtained labels are noise-free. In fact, the performance of CNNs is influenced by the level of noisy labels in the training dataset. Although the literature lacks attention to train learning methods with noisy labels, few semi-supervised learning methods mitigate this obstacle. In this paper, we propose a new teacher/student deep semi-supervised learning (TS-DSSL) method that employs self-training on noisy labels training dataset. We measure the efficiency of TS-DSSL on semi-supervised visual object classification tasks on the benchmark datasets CIFAR10 and MNIST. TS-DSSL achieves impressive results even in the presence of high-level noisy labels. It also sets a record on datasets with various levels of noisy labels created from the previous datasets with uniform and non-uniform noise distributions.

Probability density forecast offers the whole distributions of forecasting targets, which brings greater flexibility and practicability than the other probabilistic forecast models such as prediction interval (PI) and quantile forecast. However, existing density forecast models have introduced various constraints on forecasted distributions, which has limited their ability to approximate real distributions and may result in suboptimality. In this paper, a distribution-free density forecast model based on deep learning is proposed, in which the real cumulative density functions (CDFs) of forecasting target are approximated by a large-capacity positive-weighted deep neural network (NN). Benefiting from the universal approximation ability of NNs, the range of forecasted distributions has been proven to contain all the distributions with continuous CDFs, which is superior to existing models’ considering both width and accordance with reality. Three tests from different scenarios were implemented for evaluation, i.e., very-short-term wind power, wind speed, and day-ahead electricity price forecast, in which the proposed density forecast model has shown superior performance over the state of the art.

This research paper focuses on the development of a new approach for image reconstruction from neural activity recorded from monkey's inferior temporal cortex using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). GANs have been proven to be a useful tool for generating realistic images from random noise vectors. In this study, the authors used these networks to produce images from neural activity data obtained from monkey IT cortex. The main objective of this research is to explore the application of GANs in image reconstruction and visualization of brain modeling. The results show that GANs can successfully reconstruct images that closely match the original ones. Furthermore, the authors compared the performance of GANs with that of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and concluded that GANs are superior in terms of both quality and efficiency. Overall, this study provides an effective technique for image reconstruction from neural activity data and contributes to the development of brain modeling using generative adversarial networks.

The study tour for computer science students focuses on various aspects of computer science, including computational modeling, companies, seminars, cultural differences, and information technology. The aim of the tour is to provide students with an opportunity to gain insights into the latest developments in computer science and explore various cultural differences that can influence the adoption of information technology in different regions. The tour encompasses visits to various companies, where students can observe the application of computational modeling in various sectors, such as finance, healthcare, and e-commerce. In addition, students attend seminars and workshops that focus on the latest trends in information technology and the challenges that computer scientists face today. The study tour also provides an excellent opportunity for students to experience different cultures and understand how cultural differences can impact the adoption of new technologies. Overall, the study tour aims to equip students with the skills they need to succeed in the ever-evolving field of computer science.

This paper presents an empirical evaluation of semantic-based similarity measures in microblogging social media, particularly Twitter. The study focuses on the efficiency and effectiveness of three existing methods: matrix decomposition, taxonomy, and natural language processing using computational modeling. The research aims to investigate the correlation between semantics and user engagement on Twitter, as well as to identify which method is most suitable for microblogging data. The study found that matrix decomposition performed the best, followed by the taxonomy method, while the natural language processing method showed limited ability to capture the semantics of tweets. This research contributes to the theoretical understanding of semantic-based similarity measures and provides practical implications for social media managers who aim to improve user engagement through semantic analysis.

This paper describes the development and evaluation of a fuzzy rule-based system for detecting and visualizing context and stress during commuter driving. The study involves the use of linguistic and biomedical monitoring data to capture drivers' heart rate variability and stress levels. By using a fuzzy logic approach, the system can recognize and notify drivers of their stress levels on the roads. Furthermore, the system can visualize stress levels in real-time through a user-friendly interface, aiming to assist drivers in maintaining safe and stress-free driving habits. The proposed system provides a promising solution for monitoring and assessing stress levels during driving, which may have significant implications for improving road safety and reducing accidents caused by stressed drivers.

We consider a network of several independent linear systems controlled over a shared communication network. Data transmissions pertaining to each control loop are arbitrated by a scheduler collocated with the plant's sensors that transmits the state information to the corresponding remote controller collocated with the plant's actuators. The shared communication channel is assumed to be operating based on a contention-based protocol, endowing the networked control system with desirable reconfigurable and scalable features. We propose a class of scheduling policies which admit a decentralized optimal control implementation and an event-triggered policy within this class which is shown to be consistent, i.e. it results in a better control performance for any linear system, measured by an average quadratic cost than its non-event-based counterpart.

The rise of computer crime has become a worldwide concern, as it poses a threat to the safety and security of Internet users. Monitoring Internet Relay Chat (IRC) has been considered as an effective means of identifying and apprehending cybercriminals. This paper aims to present a novel approach known as autonomic author identification in IRC, which utilizes artificial intelligence techniques to develop a real-time autonomic system for automatic identification of authors on IRC. The proposed system is designed to identify and track users' activity across different social network services and relays, providing valuable insight into their online behavior. It is believed that the autonomic author identification system presented in this paper can pave the way for the development of more robust and efficient identification systems to combat cybercrime on a global scale.

In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successfully applied in various signal processing algorithms, such as image and speech recognition. However, the high computation and memory cost of CNNs limit their applicability in resource-constrained devices. One possible solution is to reduce the complexity of CNNs via pruning methods. In this paper, we propose a novel pruning method for CNNs, specifically the squeezenet architecture, using a Taylor expansion-based criterion. By considering the second-order Taylor series of the cost function, we identify the neurons that have the least impact on the output and remove them from the network. Our method achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art pruning methods while reducing the number of parameters by up to 90%. The proposed method has the potential to significantly reduce the memory and computation cost of CNNs, making them more applicable in resource-constrained devices without sacrificing performance.

Providing city navigation instructions to people with motion disabilities requires the knowledge of urban features like curb ramps, steps or other obstacles along the way. Since these urban features are not available from maps and change in time, crowdsourcing this information from end-users is a scalable and promising solution. Our preliminary study on wheelchair users shows that an automatic crowdsourcing mechanism is needed, avoiding users' involvement.In this contribution we present a solution to crowdsource urban features from inertial sensors installed on a wheelchair. Activity recognition techniques based on decision trees are used to process the sensors data stream. Experimental results, conducted with data acquired from 10 real wheelchair users navigating in an outdoor environment show that our solution is effective in detecting urban features with precision around 0.9, while it is less reliable when classifying some fine-grained urban feature characteristics, like a step height. The experimental results also present our investigation aimed at identifying the best parameters for the given problem, which include number, position and type of inertial sensors, classifier type, segmentation parameters, etc.

Concept drift is a known phenomenon in software data analytics. It refers to the changes in the data distribution over time. The performance of analytic and prediction models degrades due to the changes in the data over time. To improve prediction performance, most studies propose that the prediction model be updated when concept drift occurs. In this work, we investigate the existence of concept drift and its associated effects on software defect prediction performance. We adopt the strategy of an empirically proven method DDM (Drift Detection Method) and evaluate its statistical significance using the chi-square test with Yates continuity correction. The objective is to empirically determine the concept drift and to calibrate the base model accordingly. The empirical study indicates that the concept drift occurs in software defect datasets, and its existence subsequently degrades the performance of prediction models. Two types of concept drifts (gradual and sudden drifts) were identified using the chi-square test with Yates continuity correction in the software defect datasets studied. We suggest concept drift should be considered by software quality assurance teams when building prediction models.

This paper proposes a semantic sparse service discovery method using word embedding and Gaussian LDA. The method aims to solve the problem of discovering web services through natural language queries, which often suffer from low precision and recall rates due to the absence of relevant context information. By leveraging the power of probabilistic logic, the proposed method utilizes both syntactic and semantic information embedded in text to extract relevant features and improve the quality of search results. In addition, cloud computing and search engines are employed to enhance the scalability and efficiency of the system. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy, coverage and speed, demonstrating its potential for practical applications in service-oriented computing.

Eye movements obtained during eye tracking include both the fixation location and cognitive activities of the subject when viewing the remote sensing images. Aiming at the problem that the existing region of interest analysis methods based on the eye movement do not determine whether the area contains targets or not, in this paper a method was presented to predict the targets in the regions of interest using cognitive activities from eye movement. The method realized the detection and location of targets in remote-sensing images through the combination of fixation location and cognitive activity in eye movements. Experiments showed that the cognitive activities related to fixations make significant contribution to target prediction in the remote sensing image with complex backgrounds.

This paper introduces a large uplink Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) system with Grant-Free Access that is based on User Activity Detection. The advantages of Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) in Massive machine type communications (MTC) are well-known. With this system, users can simultaneously access the wireless network without interferences. The study proposes a User Activity Detection method for detecting user presence and for channel estimation. The method reduces the computational complexity and provides the detection of a group of receivers with a high-degree Multiuser Detection (MUD). The proposed system ensures high reliability with low latency by enabling control messages on physical resources before the data transmission. The experimental results prove that the proposed system provides an efficient way to enable uplink access in Grant-Free networks of massive machine type communications.

Relevance vector machine (RVM) is a typical sparse learning model. The most widely used kernel in RVM is Radial Basis Function (RBF), but it is based on the Euclidean distance and don't take the distribution information of training samples into consideration which sometimes leads to a poor performance. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a mixed Mahalanobis kernel for Sparse Bayesian classification which explores the distribution characteristics of data set by means of GMM, and built the kernel matrix based on the weighted Mahalanobis distances from all Gaussian components. The evaluation of the proposed kernel is conducted by means of kernel target alignment (KTA). Applying the proposed kernel to RVM, a new version of RVM, MM-RVM, is formed. The algorithm has been applied to several UCI datasets and the experimental results shows the superior performance of our proposed method and the effectiveness of the mixed Mahalanobis kernel.

In order to obtain high quality labels, it is important to recognize and tackle noisy workers in crowdsourcing applications. In particular, spam workers, who randomly assign labels to items, can greatly degrade the crowdsourced label quality. As such, we propose a semi-supervised worker filtering (SWF) approach to filter this type of workers among the crowd. The SWF model recognizes spam workers by utilizing a limited set of gold truths. An optimization based truth discovery framework, which minimizes the total errors reside workers' labels, is integrated with the semi-supervised worker filtering approach (SWF-TD) to infer the true labels for unlabeled items. The efficacy of the proposed methodology is demonstrated on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The experimental analysis on real world datasets showed that by using around 40% gold truths as priori knowledge, it is possible that SWF-TD approach provides similar performance to the fully labeled worker filtering model.

This paper focuses on proposing an aspiration-based approach for qualitative decision-making with complex linguistic expressions. The study explores the intersection between linguistics, decision making, computational modeling, big data, syntactics, semantics, and complexity theory. With the increasing volume of information generated by individuals, businesses and societies, qualitative decision-making is becoming more important as it allows decision-makers to consider more inputs than simply quantitative data. However, the complexity of linguistic expressions presents a challenge for effective qualitative decision-making. The aspiration-based approach proposed in this study aims to address this challenge by providing decision-makers with a method to structure and analyze the linguistic inputs. The study demonstrates the feasibility of this approach through a computational model, which is tested on a large dataset of complex linguistic expressions. The results show that the aspiration-based approach is effective in facilitating qualitative decision-making with complex linguistic expressions. This study contributes to the growing body of research exploring the potential of computational modeling and big data in enhancing decision-making processes.

In order to address the growing need for real-time monitoring of environment parameters in the manufacturing industry, this paper proposes the implementation of an Internet of Things (IOT) based solution. The system relies on temperature sensors that are strategically placed within the manufacturing environment to collect data on various environmental parameters. The collected data is then transmitted to the cloud using pins and microcontrollers, where it is processed and analyzed. The proposed system serves as an efficient means of monitoring and detecting any potential environmental issues, such as pollution. Additionally, cloud computing allows for the remote management of the monitoring system, resulting in improved efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Overall, implementing an IOT-based environment monitoring system is a critical step towards ensuring the sustainability and safety of the manufacturing industry.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been widely used as a diagnostic tool for Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the choice of MRI protocols can greatly affect the accuracy of AD detection. In this study, we evaluated the impact of different MRI protocols on AD detection using feature extraction and brain modeling techniques in combination with support vector machines. Our results suggest that certain MRI protocols, such as T1-weighted imaging and FLAIR imaging, may provide a higher accuracy for AD detection compared to others. These findings could have important implications for the clinical management of dementia and could lead to the development of more effective MRI protocols for AD diagnosis.

Sentiment analysis is a task performed on textual data that aims to detect and measure the sentiment or emotional state of the writer. Several analytical models and techniques are applied to achieve this goal, such as machine learning and natural language processing (NLP). In this paper, we present a Sentiment Analysis module that utilizes Token2Vec and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to analyze user reviews. Terminology such as tokens, embeddings, and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are discussed in the implementation of the module. The Training data used consists of user reviews from various domains, such as restaurants, hotels, and movies. The LSTMs are trained on the user reviews dataset to detect the polarity of the text. Token2Vec is used to represent the textual data vectors in a lower-dimensional space, providing a compact form of the high-dimensional feature space. The proposed module shows promising results, achieving high accuracy in the sentiment classification of user reviews. The combination of Token2Vec and LSTM models paves the way for efficient sentiment analysis on various textual domains.

This paper proposes using neural networks to optimize metric learning for patch-based 3-D image registration. The goal is to extract relevant features from image patches and use them to register images accurately.
