This approach involves considering small patches of the image, which are easier to align than larger regions. The extracted features are then used to create a metric that optimizes the registration process. The proposed method shows promising results on medical imaging datasets with significant improvements in registration accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art methods. This approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy of image registration in medical imaging applications.

The aim of this paper is to present the application of six Multi-Criteria Decision Making techniques to evaluate information system success. These methods are Weighted Sum Method (WSM), Weighted Product Method (WPM), Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), Revised AHP, technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) and Simple Multi-Attribute Ranking (SMART), which are applied to a set of ten alternatives. The criteria are chosen from DeLone and McLean information system success model. Therefore, the results of this application show that sophisticated method such as TOPSIS is better than the others used methods in terms of selection and evaluation even if we applied the same problem and implemented the same maker's preferences.

In order to improve the efficiency of life-saving equipment training and ensure the safety of trainees, this paper analyzes the functional requirements of the ship lifesaving training system and designs the overall structure of it. With two collaborative working modes designed, a method of multi-role collaborative training is proposed to achieve multiuser training which is very flexible. The system has built a virtual database of scene and taken the method of regularly acquiring and sending data to solve the problem of collaborative simulation. The three-dimensional modeling software and Unity3D engine are used to build scenes of fire, stormy waves, wrecks and men overboard etc. A series of lifesaving process are simulated. Finally, the virtual training system of free-fall lifeboat is developed. The system is stable by tested, possessing a good training effect.

This paper proposes an open-loop approach for selective harmonic detection from the single-phase power system under changeable frequency environment. It consists of a frequency tracking algorithm relying on a fixed tuned demodulation method and a selective harmonic detection scheme based on an adaptively tuned cascaded delayed signal cancellation (CDSC) strategy. It can be easily arranged to detect one or several harmonic(s) from the input signal contaminated by different harmonics. The open-loop configuration makes the proposed technique robust, free of interdependent loop, easy tuning, and unconditionally stable. The real-time utilization of trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions is also avoided in the technique. When compared with the discrete Fourier transform and CDSC-based technique reported in the technical literature, it demands less computational effort and can create faster dynamics and better steady-state accuracy in the estimated frequency. The usefulness of the technique is confirmed by simulation and real-time experimental results.

The inverse projection of vector fields, also known as vector field reconstruction, is an essential tool for visualizing and analyzing complex data sets. In this paper, we focus on the application of this technique to two-dimensional displays, such as maps and images. One major challenge in vector field reconstruction is uncertainty, particularly when dealing with sparse or noisy data. To address this issue, we discuss various interpolation methods and harmonic analysis techniques that can be used to improve the accuracy and reliability of the reconstructed vector fields. Additionally, we explore different approaches to dimensionality reduction, which can help reduce the complexity of the data and improve computation efficiency. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of computational modeling and data visualization techniques in capturing and communicating complex information. By leveraging these tools, we can gain deeper insights into the behavior and underlying structures of vector fields, paving the way for advances in fields such as fluid dynamics, meteorology, and materials science.

Proportional-Derivative-Integral (PID) controllers have been used for many kinds of systems in academia and industry. Multiple off-line approaches are available for PID tuning. However, physical systems which are subjected to continuous parametric changes and external disturbances require a robust PID controller with continuous auto-tuning. Quadcopter is the perfect example of such system which requires a robust control for stable flight operation. In this paper, a robust PID controller is presented for flight control of quadcopter. The proposed PID tuning algorithm continuously adjusts PID parameters which minimizes tracking error using artificial neural network consisting of a single hidden layer. Sigmoid function is used as activation function. Back-propagation algorithm is used to obtain optimized weights. Comparative analysis of three types of training algorithms (Bayesian regularization, Lavenberg-Marquardt and scaled conjugate gradient) against different number of neurons of hidden layer is performed to obtain minimized Mean Square Error (MSE). The effectiveness of proposed control scheme is witnessed for roll, pitch, yaw and altitude control of quadcopter.

This paper proposes an audio-visual embedding approach for cross-modal music video retrieval through supervised deep CCA. The method aims to extract and correlate audio and visual features that are semantically relevant to music mood in order to improve the retrieval performance. The proposed method involves feature extraction from audio and video components, computation of cross-modal correlations, and visualization of the learned embeddings. The paper presents a computational modeling framework that accounts for the architecture of the proposed technique. The methodology has been tested on a database of music videos, where the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of retrieval accuracy. This work is significant because the proposed method can be used as a valuable tool for applications such as video recommendation and multimedia retrieval, where correlations between audio and visual components of media can improve the result quality.

Nodes in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) perform every day more critical operations. Originally, sensor nodes were connected in closed networks, where they only collected data and sent them to a central server to be processed. However, with the arrival of the fourth industrial revolution and the era of Cyber-Physical Systems, Wireless Sensors Networks are employed in a large catalogue of applications, many of them critical: traceability, ambient intelligence, biological signal control, etc. At the beginning, simple encryption techniques were enough, but as more sophisticated applications are proposed, protection schemes turn also more complex. In particular, schemes based on digital signatures, hash functions and Public Key Infrastructures are extensively implemented. Nevertheless, all these solutions present a very important problem: nodes must store a secret key. As future systems will be unmanaged and be deployed in remote places without surveillance, the use of ROM memories where keys are stored in a permanent way is a critical risk. Therefore, in this paper we propose a new scheme for signature delegation in WSN, based on magnetic Physical Unclonable Functions (PUF). PUF take advantage of any physical properties to build private keys which are inaccessible and impossible to replicable; what added to the intrinsic complexity magnetic phenomena will enable us to define an inviolable signature scheme. A simulation scenario is also defined to validate the usability and performance of the proposed framework.

Twitter sentiment analysis has become a hot research topic in recent years. Most of existing solutions to Twitter sentiment analysis basically only consider textual information of Twitter messages, and struggle to perform well when facing short and ambiguous Twitter messages. Recent studies show that sentiment diffusion patterns on Twitter have close relationships with sentiment polarities of Twitter messages. Therefore, in this paper, we focus on how to fuse textual information of Twitter messages and sentiment diffusion patterns to obtain better performance of sentiment analysis on Twitter data. To this end, we first analyze sentiment diffusion by investigating a phenomenon called sentiment reversal, and find some interesting properties of sentiment reversals. Then, we consider the inter-relationships between textual information of Twitter messages and sentiment diffusion patterns, and propose an iterative algorithm called SentiDiff to predict sentiment polarities expressed in Twitter messages. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to utilize sentiment diffusion patterns to help improve Twitter sentiment analysis. Extensive experiments on real-world dataset demonstrate that compared with state-of-the-art textual information based sentiment analysis algorithms, our proposed algorithm yields PR-AUC improvements between 5.09 and 8.38 percent on Twitter sentiment classification tasks.

Traffic classification is an invaluable tool which can category network traffics into a number of traffic classes according to various parameter settings. It can not only provide better QoS, but also protect the security of networks. In this paper, the methods of traffic classification are analyzed and summarized based on machine learning through three aspects: supervised machine learning, unsupervised machine learning, and semi-supervised machine learning. Finally, we suggest several strategies to improve the accuracy and scalability of traffic classification.

In the existing research of power quality disturbance (PQD) identification, the efficiency of signal processing is low and cannot meet the needs of practical application analysis. Furthermore, due to the lack of effective analysis of features, the complexity of classifiers is increased, and the efficiency of classification reduced by the redundant features. In this paper, in order to overcome these shortcomings, a PQD recognition method based on image enhancement techniques and feature importance analysis is proposed. First, PQD signals are converted into gray images, and three image enhancement techniques include gamma correction, edge detection, and peaks and valley detection are used to enhance the disturbance features. Then, the disturbance features are extracted from the binary images, and the original feature set is constructed, the classification ability of each feature is measured by Gini importance. Based on the descending order of the Gini importance, the sequence forward search (SFS) method is used for feature selection to determine the optimal feature subset. Finally, random forest (RF) classifier is constructed by the optimal feature subset to identify the PQD signals. The results of the simulation and contrast experiments show that the new method can determine the optimal classification subset, which recognizes the PQD signals effectively in different noise environments. Furthermore, the new method has higher signal processing efficiency compared with the EMD and ST methods.

The detection of useful information from radar data is a crucial task for meteorological radar imaging. Feature extraction is an important process in the analysis of radar data as it enables the identification of important patterns or features within the data. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for feature extraction in image analysis tasks. In this paper, we propose a convolutional autoencoder based feature extraction approach for radar data analysis. The proposed method utilizes the convolution operation to extract relevant features from the input data, followed by the autoencoder to generate compact and informative feature representations of the input data. The proposed approach has been tested on a real-world radar dataset, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in feature extraction and classification tasks. Therefore, our proposed method shows great potential for applications in the field of meteorological radar imaging, especially for the detection and extraction of relevant features from radar data.

Driving fatigue is one of the significant factor cause road accidents which often result in huge socio-economic loss to the country. The real-time, accurate driver fatigue and drowsiness detection can bring down the accident rate. This paper verify the superiority of the deep learning approaches over machine learning methods for driver fatigue detection using electrocardiography (ECG). Heart rate variability (HRV) derived from ECG, and directly controlled by the autonomic nervous system is a promising indicator for real-time driver fatigue estimation. The classification system use time domain, frequency domain and nonlinear HRV features to ensure high accuracy and detection rate. This study conducted on 10 healthy individuals in simulator driving environment. The deep learning architecture based on Stacked Autoencoders achieve an accuracy above 90% to determine the perceived fatigue in drivers.

We demonstrate that a ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based spiking neuron is capable of mimicking various spiking and bursting patterns characteristic of cortical neurons. We propose a compact model to describe the dynamical behavior of such FeFET-based spiking neurons. This model captures the current-voltage dynamics of the FeFET and the critical voltages of its hysteretic region. It is aimed at system-level modeling and simulation of biomimetic networks of the FeFET neurons that are ideal for neuromorphic computing.

Neuronal activity analysis of the brain for epileptic seizure detection. This neuronal activity is recorded in electroencephalogram (EEG) data. Present work focused on two temporal based features of EEG signal, including statistical and morphological features. The discriminating potential of extracted features is examined by using logistic regression classifier and validated by 10 fold cross validation. The result of the proposed method is found as 99.38, 99.58, and 99.48 percent of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy respectively by using EEG data of University of Bonn, Germany.

Breast cancer and heart diseases are among the leading causes of death worldwide. Biomedical imaging technologies such as mammography have been widely used for early detection of breast cancer. However, accurate diagnosis of these diseases still poses a significant challenge. In recent years, deep learning-based methods have been successfully applied to medical image analysis, particularly using convolution neural networks (CNNs). This paper proposes a novel approach for enhancing the detection of breast cancer and heart diseases by using a multi-view convolution neural network with swarm search-based hyperparameter optimization. The proposed method effectively combines multiple viewpoints of an image to improve the accuracy of disease detection. Additionally, a swarm search-based hyperparameter optimization framework is used to optimize the performance of the network. The proposed method demonstrates improved accuracy in detecting heart diseases and breast cancer compared to existing methods. In conclusion, this study highlights the potential of using deep learning-based methods for enhancing the detection of medical conditions and presents a promising approach for improving the accuracy of biomedical imaging diagnosis.

Sensor localization is an important branch of wireless sensor networks. Traditional positioning algorithms rely on line-of-sight (LOS) transmission between transmitters and receiver to achieve high positioning accuracy. However, these methods may result in large error if they are fed with nonline-of-sight (NLOS) measurements. Since the errors caused by NLOS are always positive, a Cayley-Menger determinant (CMD) based NLOS identification and mitigation algorithm is proposed in this paper, referred to as CNIM. Firstly, all anchors are grouped and NLOS detection algorithm is carried out for each group to detect whether there exist NLOS signals. Then the specific LOS and NLOS anchors are identified by traversing the detection results of all groups. Finally, only LOS anchors are used to estimate the sensor location in combination with LS/RWGH localization algorithms. Simulations are conducted to investigate the performance of CNIM in comparison with other conventional algorithms. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Mobile Ad hoc Network (MANET) is a group of networked mobile devices working in a cooperative manner, which are deployed in situations like fire disaster and earthquake rescue. Due to usage these devices quickly run out of battery power in critical situations thus, fail in packet transmission in an ad hoc network. The energy or lifetime of ad hoc networks has been a topical research issue, and many proposals have been put forward to address this. Power-Efficient Gathering in Sensor Information Systems (PEGASIS) and Dynamic State algorithm are two research works with unique energy efficiency concepts that if harmonized and refined, will deliver a better optimized energy efficient routing protocol for MANETs. This study therefore, proposes PEGADyn - a hybrid version of PEGASIS and Dynamic State algorithm into a new energy-efficient routing protocol for ad hoc networks. PEGADyn creates a virtual grid classification of nodes based on the current location of nodes, and this is followed by a cluster formation of nodes in each virtual grid created. In each cluster and virtual grid formed, cluster heads (CHs) and designated cluster heads (dCH) are selected based on their energy levels. CHs and dCHs are used for communication between clusters and virtual grids. The use of CHs and dCHs limits communication overheads among nodes hence, reducing the energy expended and thus, increasing the network lifetime. A simulation comparison of PEGADyn with PEGASIS and Dynamic State shows PEGADyn to be more optimal in extending network lifetime and maintaining network throughput.

This contribution presents the development of a decision support system to be used by telecommunications engineering students in selecting a suitable frequency filter design tool. System design follows the expert system paradigm and implements multi-criteria decision modelling using the Decision Matrix method, and combines set theory based option filtering with the MAUT method for option ranking. The expert system inference engine is rule based, while the knowledge base is designed as a Decision Matrix and implemented in a relational database. The user interface is to offer two types of user experience for beginners and advanced users. The system is developed as an integrated part of a telecommunications engineering online learning system, and is designed to be open-ended to incorporate additional filter design tools and decision criteria.

Human locomotion recognition methods based on electromyography (EMG) signals have not shown robust and accurate classification performance. This is due to the limitations of EMG signals such as its stochastic nature and sensitivity to placement of the sensors, as well as the number of sensors, feature extraction and classification algorithms. In this paper, a robust classification approach with only two features derived from EMG signals is developed to recognize locomotion activities and detect changing speeds. The root means square (RMS) and energy of the EMG signals are the features adopted in this method. The energy of the EMG signal is extracted using energy kernel method. The proposed approach uses a low number of sensors and features, online unsupervised classification, and is generalizable to different lower-limb muscle groups. To evaluate the benefits of the proposed approach, it is initially tested on a public dataset of five participants with two EMG sensors on biceps femoris and gastrocnemius, doing separate trials on the treadmill at various speeds and slopes. We performed additional experiments on two participants with EMG sensors on vastus laterialis and vastus medialis, as treadmill speeds changed online within each trial. The proposed approach achieved significant classification accuracy (above 90%) using the standard unsupervised K-means clustering, for both locomotion activity and speed recognition with the public dataset and our collected data.

We present a novel heuristic first order method for large-scale mixed-integer programs, more specifically we focus on mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic programs. Our method builds on Lagrangian relaxation techniques and Hopfield Neural Networks. For illustration, we apply this method to an economic load dispatch problem and compare with two convex approximation techniques.

Jamcloud is an innovative approach to utilizing traffic jams as an opportunity for computational modeling. The advent of cloud computing and 5G mobile communication has opened up new avenues for turning repetitive idle time into productive computing gains. Jamcloud leverages the onboard intelligence of modern automobiles and mobile handsets to create analytical models of traffic congestion patterns. An efficient utilization of this idle time can lead to significant advancements in traffic management systems, predictive maintenance algorithms, and autonomous vehicles. With the help of cloud computing, huge amounts of data can be processed in real-time which will allow us to better understand traffic patterns and make smarter decisions about how to manage them. Overall, Jamcloud presents a promising opportunity to not only improve our transportation infrastructure but also benefit our society in countless ways.

This paper proposes a novel approach for automatic sleep stage detection based on heart rate variability (HRV) spectrum analysis. Sleep is a crucial physiological process that affects overall health and well-being. Electrocardiography (ECG) and heart rate variability (HRV) are widely used to study sleep and its related disorders. The proposed approach utilizes support vector machines (SVM) as a classification algorithm, with feature extraction and spectral analysis of HRV signals. Our experimental results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and robustness in detecting sleep stages. The advantages of this approach are its non-invasiveness and low cost, as well as its potential for clinical use. In summary, this study provides a new perspective on automatic sleep stage detection by exploring the use of HRV signals in conjunction with classification algorithms.

This paper presents a novel Connected Component Analysis hardware architecture suitable for high-performance heterogeneous image processing embedded systems. The target application referenced along the work is the Automated Traffic Sign Recognition for next generation Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems. In such a field, a high throughput rate is mandatory to obey high-speed camera input frame rate. The proposed architecture executes a complete Connected Component Analysis by just one scan of the input image; therefore, it reaches performances higher than several existing hardware designs. When implemented on a Xilinx Zynq Z7045 SoC, our design allows a throughput rate of 212 Mpixels/s to be reached using 18144 LUTs and 5005 FFs, which correspond to less than 9% and 1.5% of the available resources.

Recently the rapid developments in entertainment such as 3D movies and video games, causing the phenomenon of cybersickness to be a very serious topic among health experts. Cybersickness occurs when the human exposure in virtual environment so that it can cause negative effect like headache, fatigue, eyestrain and vomiting. It can disturb the physical and physiological of the human if it is not minimized properly. Many studies have been done to investigate cybersickness using several methods. One of the most common method is using Electroencephalograph (EEG). However, previously there were not many studies that explored time domain feature extraction in investigating cybersickness. In this paper, Nine healthy participants (7 male and 2 female) were measured using EEG during playing 3D video game. Time domain feature extraction, such as statistical features (e.g., mean, variation, standard deviation, number of peak) and power percentage band were implemented to recognize cybersickness. The frequency band alpha $(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$ and beta ($\beta$) was extracted for all channels. Then, we do the feature selection to improve the performance of cybersickness recognition using K-Nearest Neighbor and NaÏve Bayes classifier. We classified the result of feature extraction in order to investigate cybersickness symptoms or not. According to our research, the use of three feature extractions (i.e., variant, standard deviation, and number of peak) are the best feature for cybersickness recognition. The accuracy was 83,8% using Naive Bayes classifier. This result could improve the accuracy by 6% compared with the one that using five feature extractions.

This paper proposes a novel mathematical model for predistortion in wireless communication systems, called the Square-Root-Based Memory Polynomial Model. The model is specifically designed for concurrent dual-band digital predistortion and aims to reduce the computational complexity of existing models. The complexity theory is discussed in detail, and the advantages of the new model in terms of computational efficiency are demonstrated. Nonlinear distortion is a fundamental concern in wireless communication, and the proposed model provides a solution that minimizes distortion caused by nonlinearities in the system. Overall, the paper presents a fresh approach to computational modeling in wireless communication and offers a highly promising solution for improving the efficacy of predistortion techniques.

Virtual reality (VR) technology has shown great potential in enhancing training experiences for various fields, including building and construction. This study aims to evaluate alternative input techniques for VR training in the context of building and construction, focusing on the use of theodolites and headphones for tracking and audio input, respectively. The study was conducted in Australia, using different hardware setups for VR simulations. The results indicate that the integration of theodolites and headphones can significantly improve the accuracy and effectiveness of VR training in building and construction. Specifically, theodolites provide precise tracking of movements and positions, while headphones offer realistic audio cues that enhance learning and immersion. Overall, the study highlights the importance of selecting appropriate input techniques for VR training and suggests potential directions for future research in this area.

This paper addresses the onboard locally centralized conflict resolution problem of heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with variable headings. First, the geometric properties of the conflict resolution problem are analyzed in a two-dimensional (2-D) space. By mapping the nonlinear safe separation constraint to the sine value space, a linear constraint for safe separation is established for pairwise conflicting UAVs. Then, a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model is built to cope with the conflict resolution problem of heterogeneous UAVs, where the objective is to minimize the overall costs. A coordination coefficient $\lambda $ is defined to enhance the coordination performance between UAVs. The proposed MILP model is extended to the conflict resolution problem of UAVs in a 3-D space. By using the CPLEX solver, the MILP model can be efficiently solved. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The simulation results show that the proposed approach can generate conflict-free solutions more efficiently when compared with the existing short-term coordination algorithm. The proposed approach is able to realize UAV coordination in highly congested air traffic and satisfies the onboard conflict resolution requirement.

The research article discusses the pre-processing of nonlinear output regulation with non-vanishing measurements. The study focuses on the design of regulators for steady-state behavior in closed loop systems. Linear systems are commonly used in output feedback control, but measurement uncertainty can significantly affect the performance of the controllers. In contrast, nonlinear systems can provide better control performance but are challenging to analyze due to their complexity. Therefore, the article presents a pre-processing strategy that incorporates the advantages of linear systems and nonlinear systems, resulting in improved controller design. Overall, the research demonstrates the importance of pre-processing for advanced control strategies in non-linear systems.

This paper presents a feed-forward neural network implementation using a network on chip (NoC) on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). The design is intended for large neural networks with hundreds of neurons in each layer. It is one of the first publications that fully realizes a large neural network using NoC-based communication. A dedicated NoC is implemented to handle many interconnections among neurons. The design uses multiple processing elements (PE) to exploit the parallelism available in neural network layers. Different PE configurations are implemented and evaluated for area, power consumption and performance. Implementation and experimental results for a handwritten digit recognition system show that using a large neural network with NoC interconnect allows system scalability with scalable performance. The design achieves the maximum performance of 1339 FPOPs/cycle on a Xilinx Virtex-7 XC7VX485T FPGA. Its latency is 18-times faster than an Intel i7-3.4 GHz CPU running Matlab for this application.

This paper reviews the current issues surrounding the blocking of malicious domains, or "blacklisting", and the role of servers and IP networks in this process. Various tools and techniques utilized for blacklisting are discussed, including IP blocking, DNS sinkholing, and URL filtering. Phishing attacks are identified as a particularly concerning type of malicious activity, as they seek to obtain sensitive information from unsuspecting victims. The importance of effective and efficient blacklisting cannot be understated in today's digital landscape, as cyber threats continue to evolve and adapt. Further research and improvement of current blacklisting methods is crucial in order to effectively combat these malicious activities and protect users from harm.

The optimization of restorative capacity is of paramount importance for complex infrastructure networks, particularly in light of increasing demands for resilience in systems such as power and transportation. Creating reactive plans is often insufficient, necessitating proactive planning and optimization efforts towards bolstering restorative capacity. Planning and optimization processes that consider critical infrastructure and complex networks can be particularly effective in achieving desired outcomes. This paper explores the interplay between planning, optimization, and restorative capacity in complex infrastructure networks, highlighting the importance of considering key factors such as resilience, power systems, transportation, and critical infrastructure. By recognizing the central role of optimization in achieving desired outcomes, stakeholders can more effectively develop and implement strategies for enhancing the restorative capacity of complex infrastructure networks, resulting in more robust, reliable, and resilient systems that can better withstand and recover from shocks and stresses.

Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks (IWSNs) are emerged as flexible and cost-efficient alternatives to the traditional wired networks in various monitoring and control applications within the industrial domain. Low delay is a key feature of delay-sensitive applications as the data is typically valid for a short interval of time. If data arrives too late it is of limited use which may lead to performance drops or even system outages which can create significant economical losses. In this paper, we propose a decentralized optimization algorithm to minimize the End-to-End (E2E) delay of multi-hop IWSNs. Firstly, we formulate the optimization problem by considering the objective function as the network delay where the constraint is the stability criteria based on the total arrival rate and the total service rate. The objective function is proved to be strictly convex for the entire network, then a Decentralized Primal-Dual (DeP-D) algorithm is proposed based on the sub-gradient method to solve the formulated optimization problem. The performance of the proposed DeP-D is evaluated through simulations and compared with WirelessHART network and the results show that the proposed DeP-D can achieve at least 40% reduction in the average E2E delay.

A log statement is used to record important runtime behavior of software systems for diverse reasons, which is inevitable to develop most of the software systems. However, developers do not tend to deeply consider an appropriate log level in their source code. In order to address the issues, this paper proposes an automatic approach to validating log levels in Java in consideration of the syntactic as well as semantic features. We first build up the Word2Vec model and generate semantic and syntactic log feature vectors, then train the machine learning classifiers to automatically validate the log levels. For the evaluation, we collected six open source projects of the message-oriented middleware domain, and obtained the 88% precision and the 87% recall respectively.

This paper proposes a Fully Convolutional Sequence Recognition Network (FCSRNet) for efficient and accurate water meter number reading. The FCSRNet consists of two main components: feature extraction and sequence recognition. The feature extraction component utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract discriminative features from the input images. The sequence recognition component employs a computational modeling approach based on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to perform character recognition and produce the final output sequence. The proposed FCSRNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Task analysis reveals that the proposed network is highly robust to noise and distortion in input images, making it suitable for real-world scenarios. Overall, the FCSRNet offers a promising solution for water meter number reading and can serve as a basis for further research in related image recognition tasks.

The proponents of Aspect Oriented Software Development (AOSD) methodology have done a tremendous amount of work to bring out the positive effects of its adoption using quantitative assessment. A structured assessment of the methodology requires a well-defined quality model. In this paper, an AI agent based quality model has been proposed to evaluate the effect of aspectization. The model has been applied on already existing and equivalent versions of object oriented and aspect oriented case study application, university automation software. Specific metrics for the software design properties have been measured using AI agents for the different versions and were used to infer upon the effect on quality. Based on the initial measurement, it was found that aspectization has positively improved all the three quality attributes defined in the quality model. The attributes of evolution and reusability showed significant improvement in quality due to the effect of aspectization.

This paper proposes a self-powered IoT device based on energy harvesting for remote applications. The device incorporates supercapacitors and energy harvesting technology to power temperature sensors and wireless communication in a remote setting. By utilizing this technology, the device can operate indefinitely without the need for external power sources. The implementation of wireless sensor networks further enhances the flexibility and reliability of the system. The device is designed to utilize lithium-ion batteries as a backup power source for exceptional scenarios. The integration of these technologies creates a revolutionary self-powered device with the potential to drastically reduce the cost of remote monitoring and surveillance applications. The proposed IoT device can be used in various fields such as environmental monitoring, healthcare, transportation, and agriculture.

Bearings are the main components of the modern machinery. Poor operating environment often makes them prone to failure, which may cause significant economic losses and catastrophic disasters. Once the incipient fault appears, the machinery will not operate correctly, and even go down. Therefore, detecting their incipient fault as soon as possible is useful for bearing prognostics and health management. According to stochastic resonance theory, the weak signal can be enhanced with the assistance of proper noise in a proper nonlinear system. Therefore, stochastic resonance is suited for fault diagnosis. In this paper, an adaptive mono-stable stochastic resonance based on cuckoo search is proposed for incipient bearing fault diagnosis. The exponential type single-well system is used as the nonlinear system of the mono-stable stochastic resonance. The bearing fault signal after pre-processing is processed by the mono-stable stochastic resonance. The cuckoo search is used to search the optimal parameters of the nonlinear system. The signal-to-noise ratio is used as the evaluation of stochastic resonance. Finally, we conducted two bearing fault test to validate the effectiveness of proposed methods. The results meet the expected effect of the proposed methods.

The paper investigates the feasibility of utilizing unlicensed spectrum for device-to-device (D2D) communications underlaying cellular networks, particularly in the context of Long Term Evolution (LTE) and Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) technologies. The study focuses on evaluating the trade-offs between using licensed versus unlicensed spectrum in terms of throughput, geometry, and stochastic processes. The authors conducted simulations to compare the performance of D2D communications in both scenarios using various network scenarios, such as cellular networks with high and low traffic loads. The findings indicate that while unlicensed spectrum offers better throughput and lower signal attenuation in certain network scenarios, it also poses a higher risk of interference and signal degradation. Therefore, the decision to use unlicensed spectrum for D2D communications in cellular networks should be based on a careful assessment of the specific network environment and the nature of the communication needs.

In a time-to-event model, Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) analysis is the most frequently used method for estimating overall survival. However, the CoxPH analysis is limited to explaining only single or partial risk effects among clinicopathological factors. We introduced DeepCoxPH, a risk score estimation strategy based on deep learning (DL) and CoxPH, to improve the risk stratification for overall survival analysis. The abstracted weight from the DL and the hazard ratios from the CoxPH were transformed into the risk score estimation in the fully adjusted model. The DeepCoxPH exhibited more comprehensive risk weight estimation for overall survival. The DeepCoxPH was applied to predict ten-year overall survival in breast cancer. A Kaplan-Meier curve revealed that the DeepCoxPH improved discrimination of high- and low-risk stratification in both short- and long-term breast cancer for overall survival. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of the risk score estimation based on machine learning and parametric-statistical analysis aimed at identifying risk stratification for overall survival through the consideration of comprehensive risk effects among multiple clinicopathological factors.

In this paper, we propose a uniform and variational deep learning (UVDL) method for RGB-D object recognition and person re-identification. Unlike most existing object recognition and person re-identification methods, which usually use only the visual appearance information from RGB images, our method recognizes visual objects and persons with RGB-D images to exploit more reliable information such as geometric and anthropometric information that are robust to different viewpoints. Specifically, we extract the depth feature and the appearance feature from the depth and RGB images with two deep convolutional neural networks, respectively. In order to combine the depth feature and the appearance feature to exploit their relationship, we design a uniform and variational multi-modal auto-encoder at the top layer of our deep network to seek a uniform latent variable by projecting them into a common space, which contains the whole information of RGB-D images and has small intra-class variation and large inter-class variation, simultaneously. Finally, we optimize the auto-encoder layer and two deep convolutional neural networks jointly to minimize the discriminative loss and the reconstruction error. The experimental results on both RGB-D object recognition and RGB-D person re-identification are presented to show the efficiency of our proposed approach.

This paper proposes a linearized ADMM method for nonconvex nonsmooth optimization with convergence analysis. The method focuses on optimizing convex functions with the use of linear programming and lagrangian functions. The proposed method is particularly useful in machine learning and signal processing algorithms, where optimization is a critical component. The convergence of the method is analyzed and proven, making it a reliable choice for optimization problems that require fast and efficient solutions. Overall, the linearized ADMM method presents a promising approach for nonconvex nonsmooth optimization that can be applied across various fields.

This work focuses on the development of a control strategy of grid-connected photovoltaic power system. The study proposes to compare the use of standard PI type regulators with fuzzy self-tuned PI regulators. This comparison is made for different climatic conditions. In addition, a fuzzy logic MPPT tracker is used to track the maximum power point (MPP) available from PVs array. Simulation results achieved from MATLAB/Simulink environment are presented and discussed to verify the performance of the strategy and the controllers studied. They confirm that the fuzzy logic technique is efficient in terms of accuracy and response time. They allow particularly reducing the harmonic injection rate.

Image segmentation is the process of dividing an image into multiple segments or regions of interest. In the medical field, this technique is used for the accurate detection and diagnosis of lesions and other abnormalities in various organs of the body. In particular, segmentation of retinal lesions in fundus images is crucial for diagnosing and monitoring the progression of certain eye diseases such as diabetic retinopathy. This paper proposes a novel approach called Learning Mutually Local-Global U-Nets for High-Resolution Retinal Lesion Segmentation in Fundus Images. The proposed method utilizes a U-Net architecture with mutually local-global connections for training and decoding. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and speed. The proposed approach has potential applications in the early detection of diabetic retinopathy and other retinal diseases, leading to better treatment and management of such conditions.

This paper presents a Raspberry Pi-based event-driven attendance tracker that employs webcams, cloud computing, smart phones, Google services, and motion detection techniques to achieve quasi-real-time tracking of attendance. The system can monitor attendance of individuals in different locations and send notifications to registered smartphones via cloud. The system architecture consists of a Raspberry Pi that controls multiple webcams and motion detectors, captures images and sends them to the cloud for processing. Google's Cloud Vision API is used to analyze the images and detect faces. Attendance is marked when a face is detected and matched with known faces in the database. The system monitors power demand to optimize energy usage of the system. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it an ideal solution for attendance tracking in various environments.

The application of deep learning in mobile devices has greatly improved the accuracy and efficiency of activity recognition. In this study, we propose an approach that utilizes sensor arrays on smart phones to collect the data for developing a deep learning model. The collected data is preprocessed and transformed into suitable data models for training and testing the deep learning model. The proposed approach shows promising results in accurately recognizing various physical activities, such as walking, running, and cycling. The feasibility of this approach is demonstrated by integrating the trained model into an Android software to recognize physical activities in real-time. This research provides a foundation for the development of more robust and accurate activity recognition systems for mobile devices, which has important implications for applications such as healthcare, fitness monitoring, and security.

Cryptocurrency is playing an increasingly important role in reshaping the financial system due to its growing popular appeal and mechant acceptance. While many people are making investments in Cryptocurrency, the dynamical features, uncertainty, the predictability of Cryptocurrency are still mostly unknown, which dramatically risk the investments. It is a matter to try to understand the factors that infiuence the value formation. In this study, we use advanced artificial intelligence frameworks of fully connected Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Recurrent Neural Network to analyse the price dynamics of Bitcoin, Etherum, and Ripple. We find that ANN tends to rely more on long-term history while LSTM tends to rely more on short-term dynamics, which indicate the efficiency of LSTM to utilise useful information hidden in historical memory is stronger than ANN. However, given enough historical information ANN can achieve a similar accuracy, compared with LSTM. This study provides a unique demonstration that Cryptocurrency market price is predictable. However, the explanation of the predictability could vary depending on the nature of the involved machine-learning model.

This paper presents a methodology to learn the evaluation function for RoboCup soccer simulation using humans' choice as training data. The proposed approach leverages the use of two dimensional displays to represent different game scenarios in order to allow users to provide feedback regarding their preferences for each situation. The collected data is then utilized to train an evaluation function through the application of reinforcement learning techniques. The evaluation function can be used by multi-agent systems to make more informed decision making during games. This methodology has been tested and evaluated in a simulated soccer environment, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the performance of the participating agents. The proposed approach can be used to facilitate the development of more robust and intelligent multi-agent systems not only in the domain of soccer simulation, but also in other domains that require automated decision making processes.

With the Industry 4.0 revolution, the inclusion of wireless communications with real-time requirements has been gaining popularity in industrial applications. As existing wireless technologies do not fully satisfy the stringent requirements of the most critical industrial applications, wired, centralized networks are often used. However, when the application requires mobility, there is no other way than to use wireless communications. Further, in applications where the topology changes dynamically and a large number of devices are mobile, centralized protocols are less suitable. Unfortunately, most decentralized medium access protocols are not predictable, and thereby not able to fulfil the real-time requirements. To address these challenges, in this paper Self-Organizing Time Division Multiple Access (STDMA) is analysed to assess its suitability for use in industrial applications. The analysis has been carried out through simulations under a multipath dispersed time-variant industrial channel while subject to a variable Doppler shift. To this end, several metrics such as channel access delay, slot occupation distribution (SOD), packet losses and packet inter-arrival time (PIAT) have been evaluated, using OMNeT++ in combination with the VEINS framework.

The use of aerial platforms for wide area surveillance has become increasingly prevalent due to their ability to cover large areas in a short amount of time. However, the detection of targets from cluttered environments, such as buildings or trees, can be challenging. To overcome this challenge, radar technology has been utilized for its ability to penetrate through these obstructions. Machine learning algorithms have been applied to radar data to enhance surveillance capabilities. Semantics and feature extraction have been used to identify and distinguish targets from clutter, leading to more accurate and efficient surveillance. In particular, the application of machine learning to wide area surveillance from aerial platforms has yielded promising results in enhancing the detection and identification of targets while reducing false alarms.

The main purpose of farming is to yield healthy crops without any disease present. It is very difficult to visually presume the health of cotton leaf. To overcome this problem, a machine learning based approach is proposed which can assess the image of the leaf of the plant and detect the disease and the quality of the cotton plant using machine learning approach. The main approach of the research is to detect the different diseases of cotton by applying artificial neural network tool, which apply image pre-processing method to process the image and based on colours changes on the image the main portion of the affected leaf is highlighted and detect the type of disease based on data.

This article presents a new approach called DNA-SeAl for improving the performance of privacy-preserving DNA alignment in the context of cloud computing. The proposed method leverages sequential analysis to optimize sensitivity levels, ultimately achieving better alignment results while ensuring maximum data privacy for the users. The authors specifically focus on the fields of bioinformatics and genomics, where DNA sequencing and alignment are crucial for understanding the structure and function of genetic material. The use of cloud computing has become increasingly popular in these fields, but concerns persist regarding the confidentiality and security of sensitive genetic data. The privacy-preserving features of DNA-SeAl address these concerns, while the sensitivity optimization ensures the effectiveness of the alignment process. Overall, this article offers valuable insights into the intersection of cloud computing, bioinformatics, and data privacy.

Parkinson's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects millions of people worldwide. The accurate and timely diagnosis of Parkinson's is a crucial aspect of its management. In recent times, the Luria's Alternating Series Tests (LAST) have gained popularity as an effective method of Parkinson's disease diagnostics. The tests involve measuring various kinematics and acceleration parameters, as well as feature extraction and image edge detection techniques. The object segmentation approach is particularly important, as it enables the isolation of important features from background noise. Testing is carried out using specialized equipment, and data processing is facilitated through sophisticated analytical tools. The detailed analysis of LAST tests thus provides an important diagnostic tool in the detection of Parkinson's disease. Further research is essential in identifying the specific parameters that are most indicative of Parkinson's disease to refine this diagnostic tool. The use of LAST tests would significantly contribute to early diagnosis and improved management of Parkinson's disease.

The increase in the number and quality of technologies has imposed on education in general new forms of learning, some with less relevance, but others with recognized results in the educational and scientific community. The Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC)are an example of one of these technologies with recognized results because that seems to contribute to the acquisition and mastery of digital competences in the context of the realization of the teaching-learning process supported by the networks. It is in these networks that all the participants in the educational process interact and collaborate with all, cultivate connections, debate the themes, present their criticisms, update their knowledge, acquire new skills, make decisions, but generically develop as members of a connectivist community. Based on these assumptions, in this research we intend to make a review of the literature to identify the aspects that, in detriment of regular education, to encourage the teachers to adopt the MOOC as technology for their professional development and to carry out the process of teaching and learning. Thus, through an exploratory research, characterized as documentary, we use the main sources of information, in this case scientific articles published on the subject to understand the relevance and contribution of the MOOC in an educational universe supported by technologies. In general, the results, although preliminary because of temporal limitations issues in accompanying the rapid evolution of the scientific production of knowledge, suggest that on the one hand the teachers opt for MOOC education for the ease of distance learning; on the other hand, adopt the MOOCs for the acquisition of digital skills oriented to the new challenges.

Long Range (LoRa) network is emerging as one of the most promising low-power wide-area (LPWA) networks, since it enables the energy-constraint devices distributed over wide areas to establish affordable connectivity. However, how to implement a cost-effective and flexible LoRa network is still an open challenge. This paper aims at exposing a feasible solution of design and implementation, allowing users to conveniently build a private LoRa network for various IoT applications. First, several typical application scenarios of LoRa network are discussed. Then, the LoRa system architecture is presented with the functionality of each component. We address the hardware design and implementation of LoRa Gateway, which is the bridge between LoRa nodes and LoRa network server. Especially, this paper contributes by proposing an improved software architecture of LoRa network server whose source codes are open on GitHub. Under the architecture, LoRa network server is divided into four decoupled modules and uses the messaging system based on streaming data for the interaction between modules to guarantee scalability and flexibility. Finally, the extensive experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of LoRa networks in typical environments.

This paper proposes a multi-hop cooperative computation offloading approach that addresses the challenges of industrial Internet of Things (IoT) - edge - cloud computing environments. The proposed approach leverages the advantages of edge computing and cloud computing to improve the quality of service and reduce computational load. To achieve this, a task analysis is conducted to determine the optimal offloading strategy for each task. A computational modeling approach is used to develop a multi-hop system that optimally distributes tasks among edge servers and cloud servers. A distributed algorithm is implemented to ensure efficient task allocation and to reduce the computational load on individual servers. The proposed approach enables efficient computation offloading and reduces latency, improving the overall system performance. The results demonstrate that the multi-hop cooperative computation offloading approach is a promising solution for overcoming the computational limitations of industrial IoT-edge-cloud computing environments.

This paper presents an analysis of network techniques and cybersecurity for improving the performance of big data IoT and cyber-physical communication internetwork. The study focuses on the implementation of multiprotocol label switching (MPLS) as one of the network techniques to improve the quality of service and reduce network congestion. Complex data structures like big data and cyber-physical systems have resulted in the need for more advanced computer architectures to support their processing and analysis. The Internet of Things (IoT) is considered an essential element in the inter-networking of these systems as it provides a platform for their integration and communication. Security is also considered a critical factor in ensuring the efficient functioning of these systems, especially in real-time systems where a delay could result in significant consequences. The paper, therefore, provides an overview of relevant cybersecurity measures that can be implemented to protect these systems from security threats. Overall, the study emphasizes the importance of network techniques and cybersecurity in enhancing the performance of big data IoT and cyber-physical communication internetwork.

In this paper, a new Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture is proposed for synthetic Urdu and English character recognition in natural scene images. The features are extracted using three separate sub-models of the CNN which are then fused in one feature vector. The network is purely trained on the synthetic character images of English and Urdu texts in natural images. For English text, the Chars74k-Font dataset is used and for Urdu text, the synthetic dataset is created by automatically cropping the image patches from four background image datasets and then putting characters at random positions within the image patch. The network is evaluated on a combined synthetic dataset of English and Urdu characters and the separate synthetic characters of Urdu and English datasets. The experimental results show that the network performs well on synthetic datasets.

This paper presents an evaluation of an asynchronous task-based dataflow approach for Uintah, with a focus on task analysis, runtime, computational modeling, scalability, multicore processing, and software. This approach offers several benefits, including improved performance and scalability on modern hardware, reduced memory usage, and enhanced coding flexibility. The evaluation of this approach included a series of experiments using different computational models and architectures, which demonstrated the benefits of the approach in terms of scalability and performance. Additionally, the results of the evaluation showed that this approach is particularly well-suited for multicore processing, with significant speedup gains observed on multi-core platforms. Overall, our findings suggest that an asynchronous task-based dataflow approach holds great promise for enhancing the capabilities of Uintah and other computational modeling software, particularly in the context of increasing demands for high-performance computing and large-scale simulations.

MAMoC-Android is a novel approach for the offloading of computation tasks in Android applications. Cloud computing servers are utilized for this purpose, and MAMoC-Android provides adaptive computation offloading across multiple sites. This approach takes into account dynamic factors such as changes in servers, smart device batteries, and engines. Task analysis is used to identify the most optimal offloading location at runtime. By offloading computation tasks from the client smart phone to the cloud servers, battery life is preserved and overall application performance is improved. MAMoC-Android offers an efficient and cost-effective approach to offloading computation in Android applications, resulting in improved user experiences and application performance.

Antenna design is a complex and challenging area of research that requires multi-parameter modeling techniques to achieve optimal performance. In this paper, we propose a new approach for antenna design using artificial neural networks (ANN) for training and testing. By using ANN, we can effectively model antenna radiation patterns and solid modeling for various frequencies, materials and structures. The proposed technique also enables us to model ultra wideband antennas using computational modeling, which is an important aspect of antenna design. Our results show that the proposed method significantly improves the performance of antenna design and can be used for a wide range of applications in the field of wireless communication. The use of ANN in antenna design has the potential to revolutionize the field and pave the way for developing more complex and sophisticated antenna structures.

A precise curvature-based, averaged modelling technique for two-phase switched-capacitor (SC) DC-DC converters is proposed. The generalized technique provides a complete characterization of the converter at steady-state for all operating conditions. From this model, a simple expression for the output impedance is obtained which relates the slow-switching limit and fast-switching limit impedances to the total output impedance. This expression can be used to accurately compute the output voltage without deriving the converter's state equations. The modeling technique is applied on a 1:1 SC converter topology and compared with existing steady-state models. The accuracy of the model is validated through simulations and experimental measurements.

The ubiquitous use of wireless communication has led to an unprecedented increase in the demand for high-speed network services. As such, service providers are continuously looking for innovative ways to optimize their network infrastructure to offer better service quality and generate more revenue. In this paper, we propose a Task Allocation Algorithm for Profit Maximization in NFC-RAN, which leverages the latest developments in computer architecture, cloud computing, and signal processing algorithms to allocate tasks efficiently. Our algorithm is built on the principles of complexity theory and enables service providers to allocate resources based on the task analysis and radio frequency requirements of each user. We also present a novel approach to resource management, which enables service providers to efficiently allocate resources while minimizing the network's power consumption. Overall, our approach improves the performance and profitability of the network while providing better quality and reliability of service to the end-users.

This paper focuses on the planning and scheduling of restoration efforts provided by infrastructure networks in the aftermath of disruptive events. Two mathematical formulations are presented to assign restoration crews to disrupted components and maximize network resilience progress in any given time horizon. In the first formulation, the number of assigned restoration crews to each component can vary to increase the flexibility of models in the presence of different disruption scenarios. Along with considering the assumptions of the first formulation, the second formulation models the condition where the disrupted components can be partially active during the restoration process. We test the efficacy of our formulations on the realistic dataset of 400-kV French electric transmission network and 32 realistic size datasets illustrating scale-free, small-world, lattice, and random networks. The results indicate that the proposed formulations can be used for a wide variety of infrastructure networks and for real-time restoration process planning.

In recent years, smart contracts have gained significant attention due to their potential to enhance the transparency, automation, and security of transactions in various domains. However, the detection and analysis of smart contracts present several challenges due to their bytecode-only nature and complexity. In this paper, we propose ScanAT, a feature extraction and deep learning-based approach for identifying bytecode-only smart contracts with multiple attribute tags. Our method leverages convolutional neural networks for training and classification, enabling the detection of smart contracts with multiple attributes, including those related to blockchain data and programming languages. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms benchmark techniques in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our approach can contribute to the development of more secure and efficient smart contracts by enabling their detection and analysis at scale.

This letter proposes a new output-constrained robust adaptive controller for a class of uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems. In the adaptive control synthesis, Nussbaum gain is introduced, which not only ensures the closed-loop stability of the system in presence of unknown control directions but also enforces the asymptotic tracking of the reference signal under non-parametric plant uncertainties. The output constraints are enforced by carrying out a novel transformation, which transforms the constrained system into an equivalent unconstrained system. It is proven that the closed-loop system is asymptotic stable in the sense of Lyapunov and the output of the system will remain bounded by the imposed output constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed control design is demonstrated through extensive simulations.

Synchronization plays an essential role in processing information and decisions by neurons and their networks in the brain, and it is useful to study the synchronization of neuron networks, as a part of the process of understanding the functionality of both healthy and diseased brains. In the past, most studies had developed control schemes relating to synchronization problems which were limited to two or three neurons, which cannot depict the dynamic synchronization behavior of neuron networks. In this paper, we investigated the synchronization issues associated with a ring-structured network of FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) neurons, under external electrical stimulation, and with single- and dual-state gap junctions. In addition, the gap junctions (coupling)s and ionic gate disturbances were included in the dynamics of this FHN neuronal network, making our work both more realistic, and more challenging. Thus, each neuron in this network was influenced synaptically by its neighboring two neurons. A simple, robust, and adaptive control scheme, for both a single- and the dual-gap-junction network has been proposed, which will compensate for the nonlinear dynamics without direct cancelation to achieve synchronization. Sufficient conditions to guarantee synchronization of both membrane potentials and recovery variables were derived by using Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, the proposed scheme was validated, and its efficacy was comprehensively analyzed through numerical simulations.

In this paper, a method to synthesize controllers using finite time convergence control barrier functions guided by linear temporal logic specifications for continuous time multi-agent dynamical systems is proposed. Finite time convergence to a desired set in the state space is guaranteed under the existence of a suitable finite time convergence control barrier function. In addition, these barrier functions also guarantee forward invariance once the system converges to the desired set. This allows us to formulate a theoretical framework which synthesizes controllers for the multi-agent system. These properties also enable us to solve the reachability problem in continuous time by formulating a theorem on the composition of multiple finite time convergence control barrier functions. This approach is more flexible than existing methods and also allows for a greater set of feasible control laws. Linear temporal logic is used to specify complex task specifications that need to be satisfied by the multi-agent system. With this solution methodology, a control law is synthesized that satisfies the given temporal logic task specification. Robotic experiments are provided which were performed on the Robotarium multi-robot testbed at Georgia Tech.

As technological innovation continues to evolve, cloud computing has emerged as a powerful tool to enable automation of computational modeling. This study explores the use of cloud automation to run large-scale quantum chemical simulations, by leveraging runtime environments and web services to parallelize simulations and enhance the scalability of software packages. With the ever-growing demand for faster and more efficient computational modeling, this approach promises to significantly reduce computational costs and enhance simulation throughput. The findings of this study demonstrate the potential of cloud automation to revolutionize the field of computational chemistry, enabling researchers to run complex simulations quickly and easily. This study provides a valuable framework for researchers to leverage cloud computing infrastructure and web services to enable efficient and scalable quantum chemical simulations.

This paper proposes a high-capacity reversible data hiding algorithm for encrypted images using bit plane partition and MSB prediction. The proposed method combines the advantages of data mining, encryption, and prediction methods to achieve high capacity and robustness. The algorithm first divides the encrypted image into bit planes and then partitions the bit planes based on their statistical properties. The MSB prediction technique is then applied to embed data into the extracted bit planes. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in terms of capacity, image quality, and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. This algorithm can be applied to various applications, including streaming media and image coding, where secure and efficient data hiding is required.

This paper focuses on the development and implementation of a machine learning-based detection system for identifying Command and Control (C&C) channels, with a particular emphasis on the Locked Shields Cyber Defense Exercise. The system uses the Random Forests algorithm for classification and features extraction, using various network parameters and metadata to detect malicious traffic associated with botnets and privacy-invasive software. As computer crime continues to be a growing concern, this system provides a valuable tool for identifying and taking action against potential threats. Furthermore, the system's ability to conduct digital forensics on detected traffic allows for a better understanding of the intricacies of C&C systems and their related attacks. Overall, this paper showcases the importance of machine learning-based solutions in the field of cybersecurity and the need for continued research in this area.

This paper presents a new method to classify Thai main dish and soup by Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM). An entropy-based algorithm is used to extract the food area from the background. A GLCM texture analysis algorithm is used to calculate features vector of food. The GLCM algorithm can calculate an energy, a homogeneity, and a correlation to be featured. The three parameters are used for classification. Support Vector Machine technique is used for classification. The experimental result showed 100 percent of sensitivity and specificity for main courses, 89.9 percent of sensitivity and specificity and 99.44 percent of accuracy. This is the first method that can classify Thai main dish and soup.

Sentiment analysis has become a prominent research area owing to the growing volume of user-generated content. To provide more effective and robust analysis, aspect-based sentiment analysis has been proposed. This task involves identifying the sentiment towards a particular aspect of a product or service. One of the commonly used techniques for aspect-based sentiment analysis is computational modeling using Hidden Markov Models. However, recent studies have shown that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) achieve better results compared to HMMs. In this paper, we explore the effectiveness of adding external features to the CNN model for aspect-based sentiment analysis. We propose a data model that includes semantic and syntactical features in addition to the embedding of words. Our experiments show that adding external features significantly improves the performance of the CNN model. This study contributes to the ongoing research on sentiment analysis and provides a promising direction for future studies.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have achieved great success in various computer vision tasks due to their strong ability in feature extraction. The trend of development of CNN architectures is to increase their depth so as to increase their feature extraction ability. Kernel Support Vector Machines (SVM), on the other hand, are known to give optimal separating surfaces by their ability to automatically select support vectors and perform classification in higher dimensional spaces. We investigate the idea of combining the two such that best of both worlds can be achieved and a more compact model can perform as well as deeper CNNs. In the past, attempts have been made to use CNNs to extract features from images and then classify with a kernel SVM, but this process was performed in two separate steps. In this paper, we propose one single model where a CNN and a kernel SVM are integrated together and can be trained end-to-end. In particular, we propose a fully-differentiable Radial Basis Function (RBF) layer, where it can be seamless adapted to a CNN environment and forms a better classifier compared to the normal linear classifier. Due to end-to-end training, our approach allows the initial layers of the CNN to extract features more adapted to the kernel SVM classifier. Our experiments demonstrate that the hybrid CNN-kSVM model gives superior results to a plain CNN model, and also performs better than the method where feature extraction and classification are performed in separate stages, by a CNN and a kernel SVM respectively.

This paper proposes a novel approach to secure energy efficiency in wireless communication systems, leveraging the Poisson point process distributed jammers. With the increasing prevalence of the Internet of Things, security advancements are becoming more critical. Jamming has been identified as a promising technique for securing wireless communication networks. The paper considers the security implications of jamming in such networks and proposes using distributed jammers to improve the system's energy efficiency. The paper draws on the concepts of physical layer security and antenna theory to optimize the jamming strategy. The study also examines power demand considerations in mitigating the potential negative effects of jamming on overall power consumption. The paper concludes that the proposed approach can improve the security and energy efficiency of wireless communication systems in the Internet of Things era.

This paper investigates the use of biometric ultra wideband (UWB) radar for the estimation of breathing frequency and heart rate. The proposed approach involves the use of radar antennas to monitor the chest area and extract the corresponding signal. The signal is then processed in order to estimate the frequency of the breathing signal as well as the heart rate. The frequency estimation algorithm utilized is based on the Hilbert transform and is found to be highly efficient for the estimation of both breathing frequency and heart rate. The results obtained from the experiments demonstrate the potential of UWB radar as a non-contact and cost-effective approach for biometric monitoring. This research provides strong evidence for the practicality of UWB radar in biometric monitoring for a range of applications.

This paper discusses the development of high quality intra-frame prediction techniques for future video standards. Specifically, the authors propose a mathematical model based on least-squares approximation surfaces to improve prediction accuracy. They also investigate the gain achieved by employing this technique compared to traditional prediction algorithms. To achieve optimal results, a thorough training process is required. The proposed technique has significant potential for improving video coding and streaming media, which have become increasingly ubiquitous in recent years. The authors suggest that their approach can provide a more efficient and effective solution for managing the data-intensive demands of modern media applications. Their findings demonstrate the importance of constantly exploring new and innovative methods for improving the accuracy and quality of video coding and processing.

The emergence of the high-efficiency video coding (HEVC) standard enables people to enjoy high definition (HD) video content; meanwhile, HD videos, tamper detection has become a crucial issue and gradually aroused people's attention. The detection of double HEVC compressed videos with the same coding parameters is challenging since the recompression traces are inconspicuous. To deal with this issue, a novel method based on the intra prediction mode is proposed in this paper. First, the quality degradation mechanism is analyzed to facilitate the selection of classification features and the source of error in intra coding is fully considered to establish the equivalent error model. Second, the feature model of double HEVC compression detection, which is mainly based on the statistical feature of intra prediction mode, is proposed. Finally, the experiment is carried out in 720p and 1080p HEVC videos instead of low-resolution (CIF or QCIF) videos. Experimental results have demonstrated better efficiency of the proposed method in comparison to the state-of-the-art methods. Besides, the proposed method is more robust to various encoding configurations.

In this paper, we introduce a 5G K-Simulator consisting of a link-level simulator (5G K-SimLink), a system-level simulator (5G K-SimSys), and a network simulator (5G K-SimNet).
