The 5G K-Simulator is open source to solve the waste of human and material resources consumed in simulator development in the continuous management and performance analysis/verification of wireless communication technology. The code of the 5G K-Simulator is developed with a modular and flexible methodology so that users can easily change or extend it according to their purpose. In addition, we provide a web-based simulator platform that allows users to more easily use. The 5G K-Simulator assures objectivity through verification by a beta test of experts group. Using 5G K-Simulator, universities, research institutes, and industries can easily perform the development of 5G technology and verification of it. Moreover, it can also be used to develop vertical industry and application services technologies related to 5G wireless/mobile communication. Furthermore, we hope that it will become the basis of the simulator for technical analysis and verification of communication system after 5G.

Image annotation is a crucial task in the field of computer vision, which involves labeling images with relevant keywords for efficient retrieval and analysis. However, traditional labeling methods rely heavily on manual efforts and require a large amount of data, time, and cost. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called "Context Aware Image Annotation in Active Learning with Batch Mode," which leverages ontologies and context-aware services to automate the labeling process while reducing the training efforts. The proposed method involves an active learning strategy that selects the most informative unlabeled images for labeling, and a batch mode algorithm that annotates a batch of images at once, thus making the process more efficient. Additionally, the method incorporates image segmentation techniques to improve the accuracy of the annotations. The proposed approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing the labeling time and increasing the accuracy of the annotations. Task analysis shows that our approach is suitable for a wide range of image annotation tasks, making it a promising solution for real-world applications.

Estimation of human movement state is an important research area in recent years. With the rapid development of smartphone technology, it has become possible to estimate human movement state by using smartphone sensor information without the need of the traditional Global Positioning System (GPS). In this paper, we propose a machine learning approach, based on Support Vector Machines (SVM), to estimate the human movement state using smartphone accelerometer and magnetic sensors data. The SVM model is trained to categorize human movement state into different types of legged locomotion, such as walking and running. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for the estimation of human movement state without GPS. Furthermore, we also explore the impact of different data models on the performance of the proposed approach, indicating the importance of choosing an appropriate data model for the task of human movement state estimation.

Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has emerged as a promising solution to enhance the performance and facilitate the deployment of computation-intensive applications in mobile handsets with the assistance of nearby servers, which can provide computational and storage capabilities. The successful deployment of these applications depends on the placement strategy used for the servers at the edge of the network. The efficiency and stability of the MEC system have a direct impact on the user experience and the overall performance of the system. This paper explores the performance and stability of application placement in MEC system by considering various factors such as heuristic algorithms, cloud computing, computational modeling, and containers. The study provides insights into the most appropriate and efficient strategies that can be used for server selection and placement in the MEC system. The results of the study suggest that the use of appropriate algorithms, models, and techniques can significantly enhance the efficiency and stability of the MEC system, and ultimately provide better user experience to mobile handset users.

As of late, the significance of moderate access to dependable equipment, programming assets and minimizing the support expenses and security concerns have energized vast foundation supervisors and organizations to relocate to distributed computing i.e. to cloud computing. The cloud services are running the world at a good pace. The paper presents the two services of cloud that is salesforce.com and Force.com and also the functionality of these services by introducing a ticket booking desktop application for metro rail users using Salesforce.com and Force.com. Salesforce.com is a suite of CRM (Customer Relationship Management) tools which are designed to help big and small businesses dramatically improving their customer service, retention rates, purchase analysis and much, much more. Salesforce provides both SaaS and PaaS cloud services. Force.com is the platform provided by salesforce, is used for application development.

This paper addresses an important issue in passive sensor systems - the estimation of time-varying rotational biases, which can significantly affect the accuracy of extraterrestrial measurements. The research proposes a theoretical framework for deriving the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for the estimation of such biases. The approach employs maximum likelihood estimation and takes into account noise measurements in order to improve accuracy. The proposed method is analyzed and validated through simulation studies, which demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately estimating rotational biases in different scenarios. The results show that the CRLB can be used as a useful benchmark for evaluating the performance of estimation algorithms for rotational biases in passive sensor systems. The proposed method has significant practical implications, as it can contribute to improving the accuracy of extraterrestrial measurements, particularly in applications such as azimuth determination.

In energy efficient system designs, LED lighting leads to reduction in global energy demand. This paper proposes a high brightness, high efficiency, dimmable LED driver based on linear current regulator technology for DC grid distribution systems. The proposed driver has excellent characteristics like highest lumen per watt, long lifetime, high reliability, compact, low cost, both environmental and user friendly which makes it suitable for lighting applications. Steady state and small signal model of the proposed driver are performed which helps in minimizing ground current and accurate compensator design, respectively. These two modelling approaches result in the optimization of both footprint and cost of the driver. The performance of the proposed 20W driver is modeled using real-time simulation in spice software. Experimental prototype is developed to validate the performance of the proposed driver for different dimming levels and achieves a maximum efficiency of 97%.

Data integration is a widely-used technique in wireless sensor networks. Security-aimed goals consisting of getting assurance about universality and correctness of data in data integration, while sensors are deployed in an enemy environment are truly vital. In this article, we have indicated that usage of the Bloom filters can satisfy our security goals. Furthermore, this technique, in comparison with existing methods, produces fewer overloads.

This paper proposes a machine learning-based recommendation trust model for machine-to-machine communication in peer-to-peer computing. The rise of machine-to-machine communications requires an efficient mathematical model to ensure the reliability and security of communication. However, traditional computational modeling methods cannot cope with the complexity of the network. Therefore, machine learning techniques are employed to enhance the accuracy of the trust model. The proposed model is able to effectively evaluate the trustworthiness of the communication parties and provide recommendations for trustworthy partners. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the model in enhancing the security and reliability of machine-to-machine communication in peer-to-peer computing.

Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is a technique used in sensor arrays to determine the direction of arrival of a signal. In this paper, a non-iterative DOA estimation technique utilizing discrete Fourier transform interpolation is proposed. The technique involves the use of discrete Fourier transforms to estimate the DOA of a signal incident on a sensor array. The proposed method is advantageous because it eliminates the computational complexity associated with iterative techniques. The interpolation technique used in the proposed method allows for better resolution in the estimation of DOA. The results of simulations conducted indicate that the proposed technique achieves accurate DOA estimation with reduced computational complexity compared to other techniques. The proposed technique is therefore suitable for real-time applications, and can be used as an alternative to existing iterative techniques.

This paper investigates the performance of machine learning algorithms on balanced data usage for training and testing. The study focuses on the use of different machine learning algorithms and predictive models for training and testing to determine the most effective methods for balanced data usage. Specifically, the study evaluates the effectiveness of these algorithms on predicting outcomes with balanced datasets, as compared to imbalanced datasets. The results indicate that using machine learning algorithms tailored for balanced data usage can increase the accuracy of predictive models. These findings suggest that incorporating a balanced data approach into machine learning algorithms and predictive models can lead to more accurate and reliable predictions. Further research is necessary to explore the full potential of balanced data approaches for machine learning and predictive modeling.

This paper presents a novel approach to area occupancy counting using sparse structural vibration sensing. The proposed method involves utilizing sensors to detect and measure vibrations in buildings or other structures, which can then be used to estimate the number of occupants in the area being monitored. This technique has potential applications in a range of fields, from legged locomotion to monitoring buildings for safety and security. By using vibrations as a source of data, this approach offers a non-intrusive and cost-effective method for estimating occupancy levels, making it an attractive option for a variety of applications. The results of this study provide insights into the potential of sparse structural vibration sensing for area occupancy counting, highlighting its potential as a valuable tool for monitoring and measuring occupancy in a range of contexts.

The evaluation of near-field scattering in practical electromagnetic applications is a key concern for researchers in antenna technology. In this study, we propose a FFT-accelerated method for efficient computation of near-field scattering using the method of moments. A major challenge in this approach is the management of large sparse matrices. Our proposed method employs a set of observers to reduce the numerical burden of matrix operations. By using integral equations, we obtain an accurate and efficient description of the electromagnetic scattering phenomenon. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through a range of computational modeling experiments on antennas and scattering problems. This work presents a significant advancement in the computation of near-field scattering, with implications for a range of electromagnetic applications.

Since years, road collisions are a public issue which needs to be dealt. In this regard, the researchers have worked on developing autonomous vehicles. In this way, the number of collisions have been reduced to a great extent. But their is a need to develop the autonomous simulator which helps to pretest the autonomous vehicles in different road scenarios before launching them in the market. Hence, in this research work, we propose an autonomous simulator which helps to pre-train the autonomous vehicles in the real world. The effectiveness of the simulator has been proved through performing extensive experiments.

This paper presents a smart ECG holter monitoring system that utilizes a smartphone for electrocardiography (ECG) measurements. The system utilizes Bluetooth technology to connect electrodes to the smartphone and utilizes the Internet of Things (IoT) to send data to a cloud server. The system is designed to monitor heart beats continuously and detect any abnormal heart rhythms. The system is easy to use and can be implemented in clinics and hospitals for remote monitoring of patients. The use of smartphones for ECG measurements allows for a more convenient and affordable method of monitoring heart health. The IoT technology enables the system to transmit data wirelessly and in real-time, which is crucial for accurate monitoring. This system could significantly improve the quality of care for those with heart conditions and pave the way for more advanced medical technologies.

A lot of progress has been made on the object detection field, and it is difficult for researchers to decide which architecture is suitable to their specific task. The work in this paper aims to compare and analyze various detection models and then obtain an appropriate model for the traffic sign detection task. Two main components of a detection model are meta-architecture and feature extractor, and we will explain these two parts on the paper. Experiments show that the behavior of the detection model is strongly affected by the choice of architecture and feature extractor. Also, Region-based Fully Convolutional Networks (R-FCN) architecture can achieve better performance than Faster Regions with Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) and Single Shot Detection Network (SSD) in traffic sign detection task.

This paper proposes a method for object recognition in forward looking sonar (FLS) images using transfer learning. The method involves feature extraction and image recognition, which are key components of the proposed approach. To accomplish this, synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) data is first segmented to create a dataset of images. Task analysis is then performed to identify the objects of interest in the dataset. Feature extraction is employed to extract high-level features from the segmented dataset, which are used to train a convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN is used for object recognition in the FLS images. The proposed method achieves high accuracy and performs well under different conditions, making it a promising approach for object recognition in FLS images. Overall, the method proposed in this paper can serve as a framework for object recognition and classification in various underwater applications.

A frequency-weighted balanced truncation technique for two-dimensional (2-D) separable denominator discrete-time systems is presented that is applicable with single-sided and double-sided weights. The proposed method is straightforward and efficient than the existing methods as the computation of controllability and observability Gramians doesn't require solutions of Lyapunov inequalities and iterative algorithms. The simulation results of numerical examples are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Now a day the requirement of controllers in every field of engineering is exponentially increased. From the conventional area of controllers, PID controller is widely used. Any practical system consist of combination of sub-systems and these sub-systems behave as non-linear systems. To control any non-linear system, conventional PID is not so successful from stability point of view. To improve the efficiency of this fractional order PID controller, this is further controlled with fuzzy logic controllers (FLC). Implementation of FLC improves the efficiency as well as the stability of system.

This paper proposes a novel deep learning system, called Deep Inception-Residual Laplacian Pyramid Networks, for accurate single-image super-resolution. The system is designed to reconstruct high-resolution images from their low-resolution versions with superior accuracy. To achieve this, the authors employ a multi-scale image decomposition technique based on Laplacian equations and integrate it into the training of the convolutional neural network. This approach allows the network to learn better image representations and reduce the computational complexity of the super-resolution process. The proposed network is also equipped with residual connections and inception modules, which further enhance its performance. Experimental results show that the proposed system outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of speed and quality. The approach presented in this paper is expected to improve the performance of various image reconstruction tasks, such as image deblurring and denoising.

With the rapid development of information technology, video surveillance system has become a key part in the security and protection system of modern cities. Especially in prisons, surveillance cameras could be found almost everywhere. However, with the continuous expansion of the surveillance network, surveillance cameras not only bring convenience, but also produce a massive amount of monitoring data, which poses huge challenges to storage, analytics and retrieval. The smart monitoring system equipped with intelligent video analytics technology can monitor as well as pre-alarm abnormal events or behaviours, which is a hot research direction in the field of surveillance. This paper combines deep learning methods, using the state-of-the-art framework for instance segmentation, called Mask R-CNN, to train the fine-tuning network on our datasets, which can efficiently detect objects in a video image while simultaneously generating a high-quality segmentation mask for each instance. The experiment show that our network is simple to train and easy to generalize to other datasets, and the mask average precision is nearly up to 98.5% on our own datasets.

The number of applications and services hosted in the cloud are increasing continuously due to important new perspectives and new business models. Unfortunately, these new perspectives faces new requirements not addressed in legacy application (multi-tenancy, scalability, etc.) that leads to complex re-engineering phases in order to migrate existing software into a cloud environment. Quality assurance is a crucial aspect to consider starting from an evaluation phase of porting feasibility of a legacy application. This paper proposes a way to estimate the feasibility of a re-engineering for an application that should be migrate to a cloud. We evaluate software engineering aspects as loose coupling, multitenancy, database characteristics, etc to allow software engineering to evaluate and plan action to migrate legacy application.

Smart farming is an emerging trend in modern agriculture that involves the use of advanced technology such as the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, and monitoring systems to enhance crop yield, reduce waste, and improve overall efficiency. However, with the increasing use of technology in farming comes the risk of cyber security breaches. This paper analyzes the cyber security challenges faced in smart farming and identifies ways in which these challenges can be addressed to ensure that the system remains secure. The focus of this research is on the security of data-related devices and the importance of maintaining data integrity. In addition, the paper highlights the significance of soil conservation as a key aspect of smart farming and emphasizes the need for security measures to be implemented in soil monitoring devices. The study emphasizes the importance of computer security in smart farming applications and the need to develop secure and reliable systems for protection against cyber threats in order to promote sustainable and efficient agriculture practices.

In this paper we propose a new distributed multiparty consensus for multi agent systems with a leader follower framework. The agents in multi-party consensus are separated in different parties, but with in a party the agents synchronize with each other, but different parties have different orientation. So far the alignment is formulated by using complex numbers [1] [2]. Instead of complex valued Laplacian for a connected graph, we propose a matrix sharing technique to obtain different orientation between parties. The weight matrix will contain the scaling and orientation information among the parties. A sufficient condition is developed to obtain multi-party consensus. By using fixed time control technique a multi-party consensus controller is realized. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

This paper presents a robust rotor speed sensorless control strategy for induction motor. The main purpose is to overcome the instability issue for zero/low speed operating mode while considering that the rotor resistance is subject to uncertainties or variations. A Modified Model Reference Adaptive System speed estimation scheme is presented, and its sensitivity to stator resistance mismatches is investigated. The proposed approach introduces a discrete reference and adjustable models of the motor. Moreover, an adaptive discrete speed estimation scheme is synthesized on the basis of the extended Kalman filter technique. The proposed sensorless control scheme is tested using the professional Hardware simulator AMEsim (LMS). The obtained results confirm the superiority and ability of the proposed method compared to the classic Model Reference Adaptive System speed estimation scheme to guarantee a good dynamic performances and a stability of the control loop for low/zero speed operating mode and under stator resistance mismatches.

Intrusion detection is a critical task in ensuring the security of software systems. Traditional methods for intrusion detection often require manual configuration and exhibit limitations in their ability to interpolate between known patterns of attacks. In this paper, we propose a solution that employs Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) in order to effectively classify intrusion attacks. Our approach utilizes clustering algorithms to determine the optimal number of clusters in our training data before training our RBFNN. The RBFNN then learns the underlying pattern of attacks and is able to effectively interpolate between different attack patterns. Our proposed approach shows significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency over traditional intrusion detection methods. Overall, we believe that this approach can significantly improve the security of software systems and help organizations better protect their assets from cyber attacks.

This paper presents a fault-tolerant control approach for a robotic system to address the performance degradation of actuators. The proposed method guarantees prescribed performance even in the presence of faults in actuator components. The approach is based on a combination of Lyapunov methods and neural networks. Fault tolerant systems are necessary for robotic systems, as performance degradation can occur due to wear and tear, environmental factors, or other causes. The proposed approach is able to compensate for these factors and ensure the robotic system continues to operate within a prescribed performance range. The use of neural networks allows for adaptive control to compensate for unknown factors, and the Lyapunov method provides stability guarantees. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through simulation results. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the development of fault-tolerant control for robotic systems.

A robust adaptive controller that consists of a well-known PI controller and a robust frequency estimation in parallel was presented to cancel unknown sinusoidal disturbance in a stable linear time invariant system. The convergence of frequency estimation, the accurate cancellation of disturbance and the asymptotic stability of the overall feedback control system are analyzed by slow integral manifold and averaging method. The key advantages include asymptotically convergent cancellation for disturbance with much low frequency, the asymptotic stability of the whole error feedback system independent to the parameters of the plant and robust applicability in engineering. Simulation results validate the transient convergence performance and the steady-state anti-noise performance as well as the action of parameters of the proposed algorithm.

The increase in the spectral and spatial information of hyperspectral imagery poses challenges in classification due to the fact that spectral bands are highly correlated, training samples may be limited, and high resolution may increase intraclass difference and interclass similarity. In this paper, in order to better handle these problems, a Caps-TripleGAN framework is proposed by exploring the 1-D structure triple generative adversarial network (TripleGAN) for sample generation and integrating CapsNet for hyperspectral image classification. Moreover, spatial information is utilized to verify the learning capacity and discriminative ability of the Caps-TripleGAN framework. The experimental results obtained with three real hyperspectral data sets confirm that the proposed method outperforms most of the state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents a novel hybrid time synchronization architecture for the distribution network with limited communication resources. Firstly, the synchronization architecture is based on the Wireless Networks for Industrial Automation (WIA) and IEEE-1588 protocols. Based on this architecture, the time synchronization problem of the entire network for the large scale deployment of PMU in complex distribution network can be solved. Furthermore, focusing on the wide-area measurement demand of distribution network, a time synchronization mechanism for WIA wireless network is designed, and then the composition and operation principle of the WIA-and-IEEE-1588-based hybrid time synchronization architecture is introduced. The experimental results have verified the feasibility of the scheme.

Gait recognition is a computer vision problem complementing other identification problems such as face or iris recognition. Unlike other identifiers, gait is based on the motion of body points and thus it can be captured by Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS). In this work, we explore the possibility of gait recognition in the event stream by visualizing it and applying the existing method which achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks. During the investigations several related problems such as moving object detection and human pose estimation are considered as auxiliary ones. Several algorithm settings are evaluated and compared. The obtained results show that all the problems can be solved in event-based data with high quality, which is close to the quality achieved on conventional colored videos.

This paper presents a preliminary investigation on the prediction of next-use mobile apps using app semantic representations. Through the analysis of smart phones' history, semantics and predictive models, data models are established as an important component of pervasive computing. In particular, training data and predictive models are proposed as major factors that can impact the performance of the prediction task. The research effort in this study is aimed at investigating the feasibility of predicting the next-use app on mobile devices, based on the semantic relationships between different apps. The results suggest that the performance of the predictive models is highly dependent on the quality and quantity of the training data. The authors argue that the establishment of an efficient data acquisition and processing system is critical for the success of this research endeavor. Finally, the paper sheds light on the significant potential of app semantic representations in shaping the future of pervasive computing.

We developed a distributed data mining system to elaborate on a decision concerning the cause of urban traffic congestion via emerging connected vehicle (CV) technology. We observe this complex phenomena through the interactions between vehicles exchanging messages via vehicle to vehicle communication. Results are based on real-time simulation generated scenarios extended from the real-world traffic travel and activity patterns simulation cologne scenario. We evaluate a voting procedure that provides deeper insights using cooperation between vehicles, belief functions (BF) aimed at improving representation of information and a data association technique (DAT) aimed at data mining and extracting the association rules from the exchanged messages. Methods are tested and compared using a microscopic urban mobility simulator, SUMO, and a network simulator, ns-2, for the simulation of communication between CVs. Compared with the back-propagation algorithm (BP) extensively used in the past literature, our performance evaluation shows that the proposed methods enhance the estimation of the cause of congestion by 48% for the proposed VP, 58% for the BF, 71% for the DAT, and 70% for β-DAT. The methods also enhance detection time from 7.09% to 10.3%, and β-DAT outperforms BP by approximately 1.25% less false alarms triggered by the network, which can be significant in the context of real-time decision making. We show that a market penetration rate between 63% and 75% is enough to ensure satisfactory performance.

Fuzzy sets emerged in 1965 in a paper by Lotfi Zadeh. In 1969 Ruspini published a seminal paper that has become the basis of most fuzzy clustering algorithms. His ideas established the underlying structure for fuzzy partitioning, and also described and exemplified the first algorithm for accomplishing it. Bezdek developed the general case of the fuzzy c-means model in 1973. Many branches of this tree grew from 1969 to 1993. Then another watershed paper in fuzzy clustering appeared: Krishnapuram and Keller?s work on possibilistic clustering. This tree has also developed many branches, and together, these two topics comprise two thirds (of the conceptual field) of soft clustering (the other third belongs to probabilistic clustering in its many guises). Another important class of fuzzy and possibilistic methods, known as generalized clustering, were later developed, based on the idea of stressing the internal nature of clusters rather than solely on metric notions or on the sharing of some significant traits. This article reviews some of the key highlights of fuzzy and possibilistic clustering. This is not a comprehensive survey: that would require an article the size of an encyclopedia and an army of well-informed authors. The best we can do here is to give readers a small glimpse of the overall reach and span of Zadeh's idea in the vast jungle that is fuzzy cluster analysis.

Security is one of the important properties and it plays a vital role in all area even in human life. Wireless Sensor Node (WSN) is connected by means of the Internet of Things (IoT). The IoT is very keen towards the area of security research. In our work, we clearly discuss the concept of data transmission in IoT devices or IoT systems. When a data get transmitted from sensor node to client it can be theft by some intruders there exist lack of security. In order to overcome this issue, the security concept of revocable storage identity-based encryption was defined and used here. The wireless sensor nodes were employed here with the internet for data transfer and there exist some security protocol to avoid interrupting. We had proposed a system called revocable storage identity-based encryption technique where it provides a valid secret key to transfer data from sensor node to client for a particular session period. The main advantage of using this concept which will reduce the complexity of the encryption process for both the sensor node and the client. With the help of this technique, the system gets protected and high level of security is enhanced.

Pushing contents to users with device-to-device (D2D) data sharing is considered as a promising solution to overcome backhaul congestion. However, this model is associated with critical issues which are user selfishness in terms of sharing personal resources and security concern when connecting with strange devices. Therefore, in this paper, we propose the notion of random D2D connection where the probabilities that the devices are connected for receiving or sharing data are manipulated by users themselves. Moreover, these probability values can also be treated as variables to be optimized. Based on that, we address the backhaul congestion issue and formulate it as a non-convex optimization problem. Two solving schemes are proposed based on primal decomposition and the alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm, respectively. In addition, these methods are designed in both centralized and distributed manners. Besides that, the congestion probability expression is derived in the special case giving an upper bound for the performance of our presented solution. The numerical results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Under frequency load shedding (UFLS) is well known and widely used emergency control scheme to prevent system instability under disturbances that cause large imbalance between load and generation. A properly design UFLS scheme should be able to shed the minimum amount of load necessary for a safe and smooth transition of the system from emergency conditions to a normal operating state. This paper presents an optimal adaptive under frequency load shedding using Neuro-Evolution Algorithm. The proposed method is able to determine the necessary of load shedding for several disturbances. This method has been tested on WSCC 3-machine, 9-bus system and compared with the conventional method.

Prostate segmentation in MR images is an important task in biomedical engineering, which has great significance for the diagnosis and treatment of prostate disease. In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown outstanding performance in image segmentation tasks. However, the problem of insufficient training data limits its practical application. To address this issue, multi-atlas techniques have been widely used to improve the segmentation accuracy. In this paper, we propose an automatic prostate segmentation method combining deep learning and multi-atlas techniques. Specifically, we train a deep neural network using a large amount of training data and use it to generate a binary probability map. Then, we integrate this probability map with the multi-atlas label fusion method to obtain the final segmentation result. The proposed method shows promising performance in terms of shape accuracy and probabilistic logic, and it outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy. The experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed method for prostate segmentation in MR images.

Source location based on polarization angle information is a research hot spot in the field of shallow distributed source localization. The near-field P-wave and S-wave aliasing are severe and the polarization characteristics of the wave group are poor, making it difficult to extract the polarization angle, an important source localization parameter. To address the above difficulty, this paper proposes a method that is based on high-resolution parabolic Radon transform (HRP-Radon) and incorporates adaptive covariance matrix (ACM) to extract the polarization angle information of the wavefront. First, a data set is constructed from the data acquired by the sensor array, and this data set is morphologically corrected against the first break time information. Second, the time domain data set is converted into the Radon domain by HRP-Radon, and the direct P-wave is extracted from the aliasing information by use of the focusing characteristics of the P-wave and S-wave and the phase characteristics of the far-field P-wave. Third, a model is built using the ACM algorithm to extract the direct P-wave angle information and the angle extraction is assessed using a metric-polarization method. The numerical simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method is able to extract the wavefront angle information of the blasting near-field aliasing signal and determine the source location from the polarization angle information. This method is of practical value to the field of underground space.

The payment of a subscription-based model for the cloud service is regularly operated with the association of the bank as a centralized trustful third party. This system taxes the parties involved by requiring them to pay high transaction costs to the bank. In this paper, we propose a protocol to enable Fixed Subscription and Pay As You Go Subscription payments in the cloud service without the use of the third party. We achieve this goal by decentralizing the payment with blockchain. In return, this decentralized system generates low transaction costs. We implement our idea in the form of two smart contracts in Ethereum network. We also evaluate the security properties of our protocol. Based on the performance analysis, we can argue that all of the operations in the smart contract produces reasonable gas costs and the contracts are usable in the real network.

This paper proposes a unified representation and registration method for heterogeneous sets of geometric primitives in the context of three-dimensional displays and shape analysis. The method utilizes eigenvalues and eigenfunctions to describe the global structure of geometric primitives and achieve a convergence in the registration process. The proposed method also has potential applications in simultaneous localization and mapping using cameras. Overall, this study introduces a powerful tool for the analysis and processing of complex three-dimensional data sets.

This paper highlights the significance of modeling in the field of energy production and propelling machines. Various models have been developed to analyze and optimize systems such as boilers, turbines, and marine vehicles for efficient and sustainable energy production. Computational modeling has enabled researchers to simulate complex systems and evaluate their performance under different conditions. Water heating systems have also been investigated using analytical models to improve their efficiency. Furthermore, studies on propulsion systems have emphasized the role of modeling in understanding the behavior of fluids and designing efficient propulsion mechanisms. Overall, this paper showcases the importance of modeling in advancing energy production and propulsion systems for a cleaner and more sustainable future.

Breast cancer is a significant medical issue and timely detection can be critical in improving the survival rate of patients. In this study, we propose a hybrid approach for breast cancer classification in mammograms. The approach uses a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and Radial Basis Function (RBF)-based Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for classification. The CNNs are trained to extract high-level features from mammogram images which are then used as input to the RBF-based SVMs. The proposed approach was evaluated on a large mammography dataset and results showed that our method outperformed other state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and F-measure. The proposed hybrid approach provides an accurate and reliable tool for diagnosing breast cancer using mammography images. It is expected that this approach will contribute to the improvement of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment.

The traditional convolutional neural network usually initializes the weights of all network layers at one time before network training, and then updates the weights of the network by back-propagation algorithm to improve the accuracy of the network during network training. However, with the increase of network depth, the computational cost of this method will increase dramatically and the test accuracy will be affected. In order to solve this problem, a method of gradually reinitializing the weights of each layer is proposed, that is, after a certain training period, the weight of the previous layer is determined and remain unchanged, then initialize the weights of all subsequent layers, repeat this step until the weights of all layers are determined. In order to verify the performance of the method, a series of experiments were carried out on the CIFAR10 dataset. The results show that the accuracy of the network is improved by 9% and the training time is reduced by 29%. It shows that the method can improve the accuracy of the network and reduce the training time.

In this paper, we present a live demonstration of a FPGA-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) accelerator that implements filter-wise-optimized bit precision. The proposed architecture optimizes the precision of each filter in the CNN, achieving higher accuracy with lower hardware cost. Quantization techniques are used to reduce the bit precision while preserving the network performance. The FPGA-based CNN accelerator is designed using Field Programmable Gate Arrays, and it is able to classify images with high accuracy. The classification algorithms used in the CNN are able to recognize and categorize objects in images, making it suitable for image classification tasks. The proposed approach provides an efficient hardware solution for implementing CNNs, and it can be used in various applications, such as surveillance systems, autonomous vehicles, and robotics. Overall, the live demonstration showcases the effectiveness of hardware acceleration techniques in computer architecture, enabling efficient and accurate image classification using FPGA-based CNN accelerators.

In this paper, we propose a QoS-Constrained Energy-Efficient AF Two-Way Full-Duplex Relaying scheme with massive antennas, which takes into account the relays, MIMO communication, interference, signal to noise ratio, quality of service, receiving antennas, and channel estimation. The proposed scheme is designed to optimize the energy efficiency of a multi-antenna full-duplex relay system while ensuring QoS constraints are satisfied. Specifically, we develop an iterative algorithm to jointly optimize the relay beamforming, the source and relay transmit powers, and the receiving antenna weights. We also consider interference from neighboring cells and channel estimation errors in the relay beamforming design. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in achieving a high energy efficiency while satisfying the QoS constraints. Additionally, we compare our scheme with state-of-the-art schemes, showing that it achieves significant energy savings while maintaining a high-quality transmission.

This paper proposes a method for predicting access intervals in tightly coupled memory systems. Maximum likelihood estimation is used to model the probability distribution of access intervals. The proposed method takes into account the characteristics of program processors, random access memory, and mobile communication networks. The prediction of access intervals can be used to improve the performance and energy consumption of the memory system. The experimental results show that the proposed method provides accurate predictions of access intervals with high throughput and low energy consumption.

The article explores the topic of k-Truss Decomposition for Modular Centrality, which aims to measure the Weight of a network's edges to understand diffusion processes and identify important Bridges in Complex networks. To achieve this, the authors propose Detection algorithms and Computational modeling techniques that improve the Computational efficiency of the process. Through experimentation, they demonstrate that this approach outperforms previous methods in accurately identifying modular structures and detecting influential entities within networks. This research contributes to our understanding of efficient weight measurement in Complex networks and has the potential to aid in the analysis of diffusion processes in various fields such as social sciences, biology, and economics.

Low-latency transmission is required by services emerging in today's optical communication networks, such as machine-to-machine communication. As transmission distances are now reaching several thousands of kilometers, the propagation latency in optical fiber cannot be ignored. In this study, we propose a solid-type low-latency optical fiber that has lower group delay than conventional silica core fibers. Numerical analyses and measurements show 0.3% lower group delay than a conventional silica core fiber, and its excellent optical properties include its large effective area, low nonlinearity and low loss comparable to that of conventional single mode fiber.

This paper presents a fundamental comparison of various design aspects of vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) charging systems. The focus is on the comparison of three types of charging systems, namely batteries, inductive charging, and wireless communication. The design aspects that are compared include circuit synthesis, finite element analysis, and couplings. Moreover, this paper highlights the importance of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) in the implementation of V2V charging systems. The advantages and disadvantages of each charging system in terms of efficiency, convenience, and cost are discussed. Through this evaluation, the paper aims to suggest the most viable and practical V2V charging system design for the future of electric vehicles.

In recent years, modern artificial intelligence network technologies, specifically cloud computing, have revolutionized the field of artificial intelligence. Cloud computing has enabled developers to create more complex and sophisticated AI algorithms and systems that were previously impossible due to computational limitations. Additionally, advances in robot kinematics and the use of tools like Matlab have bolstered the development of AI technologies. These technologies are not only improving our ability to create autonomous systems, but have also had an impact on the broader field of computing. As the need for powerful and specialized computing increases, cloud computing is likely to become even more integral to the development of artificial intelligence technologies in the future.

This paper proposes an OEE improvement method based on TOC in order to enhance the efficiency of production. The method focuses on analyzing and optimizing various indexes related to production performance, such as machine availability, performance efficiency, and product quality rate. In addition, distributed Bragg reflectors are utilized to experimentally validate the improved OEE, which demonstrate significant improvement in efficiency. Furthermore, computational modeling and entropy methods are explored to provide insights into the semiconductor device modeling and mechanical engineering aspects of this method. Overall, this proposed method provides a comprehensive framework for improving the OEE of production, and has the potential to greatly benefit manufacturing industries.

In cache-enabled heterogeneous cloud radio access networks (HC-RANs), mobile station (MS) association for multimedia content delivery should consider both the content caching location and the wireless channel quality. This paper studies economically optimal MS association to tradeoff the cache-hit ratio and the ratio of MSs with satisfied quality of service (QoS). When the associated enhanced remote radio unit (eRRU) stores the requesting content, the content can be fetched directly from the local cache. Otherwise, fronthaul has to be used to fetch the content. The use of fronthaul resource and cache is treated as costs, and payments of QoS-satisfied MSs are treated as incomes. Thus, the economic MS association is formulated as an optimization problem to maximize the system utility, i.e., total profit of the network operator, which is defined as the difference between incomes and costs. A belief propagation-based method is employed to solve the problem on a developed factor graph. Simulation results show that the proposed economically optimal MS association achieves much higher profit than the existing schemes and works well in the network with various loads. Moreover, the profit of the proposed scheme can be improved with inter-cell interference coordination. For the case with extremely skewed content popularity, the proposed scheme can avoid MS overloading at eRRUs storing most popular multimedia contents. Furthermore, it can support more MSs with satisfied QoS, which leads to a higher profit.

The development of real-time infrastructureless indoor tracking for pedestrians using a smartphone has become an important area of focus in recent years. This technology relies on a combination of sensors, cameras, and gyroscopes to accurately track the movements of individuals inside buildings. The ability to visualize this tracking data is critical to understanding pedestrian behavior and estimating future movements. By utilizing real-time systems and target tracking methods, it is feasible to create a comprehensive understanding of how individuals move through indoor spaces. This paper explores the current state-of-the-art in infrastructureless indoor tracking using smartphones and discusses potential future developments.

This paper proposes hardware architecture for a fuel estimation algorithm suitable for SoC FPGA. The architecture utilizes 32-point single precision floating point representation. A resource constraint scheduling algorithm is elaborated to synthesize an area efficient architecture. The floating point arithmetic is implemented using commercial IP. Synthesis results for the Virtex-6 FPGA family reveal that the proposed architecture consumes 1655 slices, has a latency of 71 ns and consumes 0.15 µJ. Additionally, the present work describes a software implementation of the fuel estimation algorithm using Zynq-7000 SoC.

The lack of measurements in distribution grids poses a severe challenge for their monitoring: Since there may not be enough sensors to achieve numerical observability, so load forecasts (pseudo-measurements) are typically used, and thus an accurate state estimation is not guaranteed. However, estimation is required to control distribution grids, given the increasing amount of distributed generation. Therefore, we consider the problem of optimal sensor placement to improve the state-estimation accuracy in large-scale, 3-phase, coupled, unbalanced distribution grids. This is a combinatorial optimization problem whose optimal solution is unpractical to obtain for large networks. We explore the properties, such as convexity and modularity, of different metrics in the context of optimal experimental design, to propose and compare several tight lower and upper bounds on the performance of the optimal solution. Moreover, we show how to use these bounds to choose near-optimal solutions. We test the method on two IEEE benchmark test feeders, the 123-bus, and the 8500-node feeders, to show the effectiveness of the approach.

The ID3 algorithm is one of the most popular decision tree algorithms which is mainly used in the classification task. There are many pieces of research about improving the ID3 algorithm by using various strategies. We improved the ID3 algorithm by addressing the equally important attributes problem in our previous work. In this paper, we extend our previous algorithm by changing the attribute selection to allow the neighboring second-place important attributes to be combined with the most important attributes. The proposed algorithm is tested on four standard benchmarks from the UCI repository. The experimental results indicate the significant reduction in the maximum depth and the classification depth of the decision tree. In addition, the testing time is also reduced while the classification accuracy is satisfying stable.

This paper proposes an approach for abnormality detection in electrocardiography (ECG) using a hybrid feature extraction technique. The proposed method employs both discrete wavelet transforms and support vector machines to extract key features from ECG signals. The extracted features are then classified using data mining techniques to determine whether any abnormalities are present. The method is tested on a dataset of ECG signals, and the results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The study demonstrates the efficacy of the hybrid feature extraction approach for identifying abnormal ECG signals, which may help facilitate early detection and intervention for cardiac-related disorders.

Facial age estimation is a challenging task due to the complex and non-linear relationship between facial features and aging. In this paper, we propose a structure-based human facial age estimation framework that operates under a constrained condition. The framework involves feature extraction using task analysis and employs both neural networks and support vector machines as the base model. The accuracy of the proposed framework is evaluated on a pediatric age group dataset. The results indicate that our framework can effectively estimate the facial age of children with high accuracy. The proposed framework can be used for various applications such as missing children identification, forensic analysis, and age-based marketing.

The interpretation of power flows from a probabilistic perspective is an important topic in the development algorithms of complex network theory for power system analysis, as it is conceived as the theoretical foundation for many new techniques such as machine learning and artificial intelligence. In this paper, we first show that power flow can be mathematically represented as the equilibrium of probabilistic energy movements on a graph. We demonstrate that such an equilibrium can be reached if the energy movements follow the commonly known random process of Markov chains. This work advances the current state of the art by showing a way that connects the power flow models and the random walk models of complex networks. Moreover, several new insights on the electrical betweenness centrality measures used in power grid vulnerability analysis are presented from this new probabilistic perspective.

Machine learning (ML) on edge computing devices is becoming popular in the industry as a means to make control systems more intelligent and autonomous. The new trend is to utilize embedded edge devices, as they boast higher computational power and larger memories than before, to perform ML tasks that had previously been limited to cloud-hosted deployments. In this work, we assess the real-time predictability and consider data privacy concerns by comparing traditional cloud services with edge-based ones for certain data analytics tasks. We identify the subset of ML problems appropriate for edge devices by investigating if they result in real-time predictable services for a set of widely used ML libraries. We specifically enhance the Caffe library to make it more suitable for real-time predictability. We then deploy ML models with high accuracy scores on an embedded system, exposing it to industry sensor data from the field, to demonstrates its efficacy and suitability for real-time processing.

In order to increase the capacity and improve the spectrum efficiency of wireless communication system, this paper proposes a rate-based iterative one-to-one matching game algorithm to realize multi users access an energy-harvesting small cells considering NOMA (non-orthogonal multiple access) in heterogeneous cellular networks. First, we use a heuristic clustering based channel allocation algorithm to assign channels to small cells and reduce the interference. Then we model user access problem as an iterative one-to-one matching game with rate as its utility, where one user matches with one small cell at each matching game and so is the small cell. After that, we propose an algorithm to iteratively enable users to access small cells in terms of proposed matching game and prove its stability. Finally, a power allocation algorithm to reallocate transmission power for each user is presented to fully use the harvesting power. Simulation results show that this algorithm outperforms OMA (orthogonal multiple access) system in efficiency besides improving the system capacity.

Emojis have evolved as complementary sources for expressing emotion in social-media platforms where posts are mostly composed of texts and images. In order to increase the expressiveness of the social media posts, users associate relevant emojis with their posts. Incorporating domain knowledge has improved machine understanding of text. In this paper, we investigate whether domain knowledge for emoji can improve the accuracy of emoji recommendation task in case of multimedia posts composed of image and text. Our emoji recommendation can suggest accurate emojis by exploiting both visual and textual content from social media posts as well as domain knowledge from Emojinet. Experimental results using pre-trained image classifiers and pre-trained word embedding models on Twitter dataset show that our results outperform the current state-of-the-art by 9.6%. We also present a user study evaluation of our recommendation system on a set of images chosen from MSCOCO dataset.

We have conducted a national survey of computing education at Japanese universities in 2016. We then developed computing curriculum standard J17 for the departments majored in computing. In this paper, we perform a comparison analysis between achievement and requirements for computing program. We collect requirements for computing programs through a survey at five J17 curriculum development committees: CS, CE, SE, IS and IT. We also compare the achievement of existing computing programs and the requirements of the committees using the proposed framework. Reasons of the differences are analyzed also in this paper. Furthermore, we find many computing programs which do not correspond to neither of the requirements. Although the analysis is performed under the context of Japan, it can also be applied to computing education at other countries.

Pedestrian detection, which has broad application prospects in video security, robotics and self-driving vehicles etc., is one of the most important research fields in computer vision. Recently, deep learning methods, e.g., Region Proposal Network (RPN), have achieved major performance improvements in pedestrian detection. In order to further utilize the deep pedestrian features of RPN, this paper proposes a novel regional proposal network model based on feature fusion (RPN_FeaFus) for pedestrian detection. RPN_FeaFus adopts an asymmetric dual-path deep model, constructed by VGGNet and ZFNet, to extract pedestrian features in different levels, which are further combined through PCA dimension reduction and feature stacking to provide more discriminant representation. Then, the low-dimensional fusion features are adopted to detect the region proposals and train the classifier. Experimental results on three widely used pedestrian detection databases, i.e, Caltech database, Daimler database and TUD database, illuminate that RPN_FeaFus gains obvious performance improvements over its baseline RPN_BF, which is also competitive with the state-of-the-art methods.

Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorder that often persists into adulthood. However, as lacking objective measures, several studies have questioned the stability in diagnosing of ADHD from childhood to adulthood. In this study, we propose a novel feature selection framework based on functional connectivity (FCs) pattern, the so-called ‘FS_RIWEL,’ which could classify ADHD from age-matched healthy controls (HCs) with $\sim 80$% accuracy (both for children and adults). More importantly, the feature space learned from child ADHD dataset can discriminate adult ADHD from HCs at $\sim 70$% accuracy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform a cross-cohort prediction between the adult and child ADHD using FC features. In addition, the most frequently selected FCs indicate that ADHD exhibit widely-impaired FC patterns in frontoparietal, basal ganglia, cerebellum network and so on suggesting that FCs may serve as potential biomarkers for ADHD diagnosis.

When considering agricultural industry paddy is principal food in Asian countries. Measuring the quality of rice is main challenge in agricultural industry. Quality of the rice depends on the output of the rice mills and according to the rice category, quality measurements can vary. Nowadays evaluation of rice quality is mostly doing by manually but it is relative, time consuming, costly and may be varying from person to person. This paper describes the process of rice category identification by using guided visual feature based machine vision approach. Segmented rice seed images are the basic inputs and pre-processing is done to the images of rice seeds. By using these pre-processed image samples, morphological features are extracted and by using original color image samples, color features are extracted. Then features are optimized for getting highest accuracy of classification. Extracted optimized features are given to the artificial neural network model and this neural network model is trained according to the training rice seed images. This proposed method is able to identify rice category of unknown rice seeds sample and it is able to give rice category as final output. Overall method is shown an average accuracy of 82.21%.

This paper is mainly to solve the path planning problem of swarm robots. If swarm robots work in the same environment at the same time, it is necessary to have appropriate planning methods to enable individuals in the group to complete their tasks. The solution is to use the artificial bee colony algorithm for the problem of robot path planning. Because the artificial bee colony algorithm has a high efficiency to solve the optimization problem, it tries to solve the problem of robot path planning in a distributed manner. The concept of organizing robots achieves efficient task of information processing and group working in the environment.

This paper presents an innovative user profiling algorithm enhanced by ontologies and application feedback. The proposed technique leverages ontologies and semantic web technologies to effectively capture the user's interests, preferences, and behavior patterns. The algorithm is based on a combination of data mining and hidden Markov models (HMMs), which allows it to extract relevant features from user interactions with applications. It also utilizes data and analytical models to learn user preferences and behaviors over time, enabling it to provide personalized recommendations to users. The proposed approach has been evaluated using a dataset of user interactions with different applications, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately and efficiently profiling users. Overall, this research has significant implications for personalized recommender systems and other intelligent systems that require accurate user profiling.

In the field of fault diagnosis of rolling bearings, feature extraction is a critical step. This paper proposes a feature extraction method based on Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Fast-Kurtogram for detecting bearing faults. The proposed method involves using band-pass filters and the VMD method to decompose signals at different scales, followed by Fast-Kurtogram to extract the fault feature. Several experiments were conducted on rolling bearing datasets, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in bearing fault diagnosis, as it can extract the fault feature and reduce the interference of other signals. Compared with traditional time-domain analysis methods, the bandwidth of the proposed method is relatively narrow, which can effectively improve the identification accuracy of the extracted fault features.

This paper discusses the challenges and opportunities for enabling city-scale Internet of Things (IoT) through the use of base stations and wireless sensor networks. The deployment of sensors in urban environments presents a number of challenges, including limitations in battery life, available bandwidth, and interference from other wireless communication devices. However, the benefits of IoT for urban planning and resource management make such challenges worth addressing. This paper presents solutions for improving sensor battery life and reducing interference through the use of better protocols and communication technologies. Furthermore, it explores the potential for IoT to aid in the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and other environmental improvements. Overall, this paper offers insights into the challenges and opportunities of city-scale IoT and provides recommendations for its successful implementation.

This paper proposes a uniform service description and contextual access control framework for ensuring trustworthy cloud computing. The framework includes a contract-based approach to specifying service properties and requirements as well as a privacy-aware access control model for dictating who and under what conditions have access to cloud services. Computational modeling techniques are employed to codify and evaluate the trustworthiness of cloud services and to adapt access control policies to changing contextual conditions. The paper concludes with several specific proposals for implementing the framework and outlines future research directions for enhancing the security and trustworthiness of cloud computing environments.

The development of knowledge graph ontology has gained significant attention in recent years due to its usefulness in semantically connecting diverse information. Ontologies allow for a standardized representation of knowledge in a domain, making it easily accessible and interoperable between various applications. In this paper, we propose a complex network-based analysis of knowledge graph ontology structure. The analysis is based on a resource description framework (RDF) and web ontology language (OWL) and aims to identify knowledge patterns that can enhance cognition. Moreover, this study focuses on identifying the interconnectedness of key concepts and their roles in shaping the knowledge structure. By examining the topology of knowledge graphs, we can understand the mechanics of how knowledge is aggregated and how it is related to distinct entities or domains. This work will be presented at conferences and may provide a deeper understanding of the switches used to simplify the knowledge representation and improve knowledge management. Overall, it is expected that this study will contribute to the development of novel approaches in knowledge graph ontology analysis.

Convolution Neural Network (ConvNet) offers a high potential to generalize input data. It has been widely used in many application areas, such as visual imagery, where comprehensive learning datasets are available and a ConvNet model can be well trained and perform the required function effectively. ConvNet can also be applied to network intrusion detection. However, the currently available datasets related to the network intrusion are often inadequate, which makes the ConvNet learning deficient, hence the trained model is not competent in detecting unknown intrusions. In this paper, we propose a ConvNet model using transfer learning for the network intrusion detection. The model consists of two concatenated ConvNets and is built on a two-stage learning process: learning a base dataset and transferring the learned knowledge to the learning of the target dataset. Our experiments on the NSLKDD dataset show that the proposed model can improve the detection accuracy not only on the test dataset containing mostly known attacks (KDDTest+) but also on the test dataset featuring many novel attacks (KDDTest-21) - about 2.68% improvement on KDDTest+ and 22.02% on KDDTest-21 can be achieved, as compared to the traditional ConvNet model.

This paper presents a Modified Radau Collocation method for solving Optimal Control Problems (OCPs) with nonsmooth solutions. The focus is on understanding the Lavrentiev Phenomenon and its effect on the search space. The OCPs considered in this study are relevant to Aerospace Electronics, requiring optimization of standards for systems governed by differential equations. In Part I of the paper, the authors investigate the effects of non-smoothness of the solution on the convergence behavior of the collocation method. The search problems arising in the optimization of the solution are also analyzed. The proposed approach seeks to mitigate the effect of the Lavrentiev Phenomenon and improve the efficiency and accuracy of the solution. The effectiveness of the Modified Radau Collocation method is demonstrated through numerical examples, highlighting its superiority over existing approaches.

The Internet of Things is growing at a dramatic rate and extending into various application domains. We have designed, implemented, and evaluated a resilient and decentralized system to enable dynamic IoT choreographies. We applied it to maintaining the functionality of building automation systems so that new devices can appear and vanish on-the-fly.

This paper presents an optimal fault-tolerant control approach for a class of nonlinear systems by using a zero-sum differential game. The method utilizes game theory to design controllers and establish cost functions that can handle potential actuator failures. The authors focus on the stability analysis of nonlinear systems subject to possible actuator failures through robust control techniques. The proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations, which illustrate its capability in achieving fault-tolerant control of nonlinear systems while ensuring effective compensation for actuator faults. The results suggest that the game-theoretic approach is effective in handling the challenges of controlling nonlinear systems under possible disturbances and uncertainties. Overall, this study contributes to the development of advanced fault-tolerant control techniques that can be widely applied in various engineering fields.

Neighbor discovery, meaning that a node receives other nodes' radio frequency (RF) signals to be aware of their existence, is an indispensable procedure in Internet of Things (IoT)-oriented peer-to-peer (P2P) networks with energy-limited nodes. The main objective of neighbor discovery methods is to improve the energy efficiency, since node energy is usually very limited. As the neighborship maintaining time is very short in the mobile networks, neighbor discovery should be achieved in a very energy-efficient manner. The existing neighbor discovery methods only consider the received RF signals from other nodes (or neighbor table information derived from the received RF signals) as the basis of neighborship evaluation. The neighborship evaluation is inaccurate when the single source of neighbor information is employed. Inaccurate neighborship causes incorrect active slot scheduling and low energy efficiency of neighbor discovery. This paper proposes a generalized and probabilistic neighborship evaluation model to unify a variety of neighborship information in IoT-oriented P2P networks into neighborship probability values. Based on the model, we propose an energy-efficient neighbor discovery middle-ware algorithm by carefully replanning active slots of nodes according to the neighborship probability. The simulation evaluation results show that our proposed method decreases the average discovery delay by up to 11.46%, approximately, compared with other methods at the same energy budget.

The rapid depletion of global fossil fuel resources has necessitated urgent research for renewable energy sources. Nowadays, there are many forms of renewable energy, the most commonly used are: solar, wind and hydraulic. Wind water pumping system is considered as a promising application of renewable energy industry sustained by the increased interest on sustainable development and the reduction of greenhouse effect.This paper focuses on developing of pumping system supplied by wind turbine source; and to reach the maximum power point (MPPT), this technique is based on Artificial Neural Network to get better performance especially because these intelligent techniques do not require a precise model, we added to our system a battery and DC voltage controller based also on ANN.Finally, simulation results are given to show the effectiveness and feasibility of the approach.

This paper proposes an effective search method called DoPS, which is based on the combination of Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Sampling (RS) techniques. DoPS is designed to efficiently solve search problems in data mining applications, where the data often features complex, multi-modal distributions. The kernel-based classification algorithms used in SVM make it well-suited for handling such issues. Additionally, the application of RS can significantly improve the speed of search and help reduce the potential for getting trapped in local minima. The authors conducted a series of experiments to evaluate the performance of the DoPS method and compared it to other state-of-the-art methods. Results show that DoPS outperforms existing methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling complex search problems. Overall, DoPS provides a promising solution for data mining applications that require efficient and accurate search algorithms.

Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a common disease that affects the small blood vessels of the heart. Accurate classification of patients with CMD is essential for effective treatment and management of the disease. In this paper, we propose a solid modeling approach for generating data models of patients with CMD based on pain symptoms and diagnostic tools. We explore the use of computational modeling techniques and natural language processing methods to extract relevant features from patient data. In addition, we demonstrate the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in accurately classifying patients with CMD. Our results show that our approach can improve the accuracy of CMD diagnosis and provide new insights into the disease. This study has important implications for the development of personalized treatment regimens for patients with CMD.

This contribution discusses the power handling issues related to the effective exploitation of time-modulated arrays (TMA) for multi-sine wireless power transmission (WPT), in the UHF band. It is shown that the co-design of the antenna array and of the nonlinear feeding network is a mandatory procedure during which both the slow modulation switching regime and the fast RF regime need to be simultaneously accounted for. The resulting final topology has to be determined as the best compromise between the on- and the off-states switches conditions. We also discuss the rules to select the proper device for switching operations over a wide range of power levels. Finally the performances are provided in terms of the far-field behavior of the entire TMA designed for multi-sine WPT.

The optimization of wind farm layout has been an important research topic for many years due to the significant impact it can have on the power output and efficiency of wind energy systems. In this paper, we propose a mathematical model that incorporates real coded multi-population genetic algorithms to optimize wind farm layouts. This approach has been shown to be effective in producing solutions that provide a more favorable balance between the number of wind turbines, the wind speed at each turbine location and the total power output of the wind farm. The model takes into account various factors such as the geographical location of the wind farm, the size of the wind turbines, and the prevailing wind speed in the area. Using this approach, we were able to generate optimized wind farm layouts that have shown significant improvements in the overall power output and efficiency of the wind energy system. These findings are highly relevant and can be used to inform the development and implementation of wind energy systems in future renewable energy projects.

This paper introduces a new approach for malware clustering using the family dependency graph. The proposed method involves monitoring Windows systems to extract distinctive features of malicious software, which are subsequently used for training and classification. By representing malware as nodes in a graph and their relationships as edges, the family dependency graph allows for efficient clustering of similar malware based on their shared characteristics. The approach is evaluated using several databases and exhibits promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method has potential applications in the field of security, where identifying and classifying malware is a critical component of protecting against cyber attacks.

In this paper, we propose closed-form approximations for coverage and rate in a multi-tier heterogeneous network in Nakagami-m fading. Our focus is on interference management in cellular networks. Simulation results for the downlink of Rayleigh channels show the accuracy of the proposed approximations for coverage probability and rate outage probability. We also investigate the impact of signal to noise ratio (SNR) on the achievable coverage and rate of the system. The derived expressions for coverage probability and rate outage probability provide insights into the performance analysis of the multi-tier heterogeneous network with interference. The results can be useful to design interference management strategies and evaluate the performance of next-generation cellular networks.

In this article, we present system for dynamic dimensional music emotion recognition (MER) and comparison of the system efficiency depending on different audio features. Experiments were performed on the database provided within the Emotion in Music task of MediaEva12015 benchmark (EiMME2015). In addition to the baseline features that were defined by the EiMME2015 organizers and included in the development data, we selected two-dimensional cepstral coefficients (TDC), linear prediction (LP) based coefficients, and the group of musical descriptors to evaluate their discriminative properties for recognition of music emotion.
