The experiments show that a combination of the EiMME2015 baseline features, LP coefficients and proposed set of music features significantly increases system performance for both arousal and valence emotional dimensions.

When designing complex cyber-physical systems, engineers have to integrate numerical models from different modeling environments in order to simulate the whole system and estimate its global performances. Co-simulation refers to such joint simulation of heterogeneous models. If some parts of the system are physically available, it is possible to connect these parts to the co-simulation in a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) approach. In this case, the simulation has to be performed in real-time where models execution consists in periodically reacting to the real (physically available) components and providing periodic output updates. This paper deals with the parallelization and scheduling of real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop co-simulation of numerical models on multi-core architectures. A method for defining real-time constraints that have to be met is proposed. Also, an ILP formulation as well as a heuristic are proposed to solve the problem of scheduling the co-simulation on a multicore architecture while satisfying the previously defined real-time constraints. The proposed approach is evaluated for different sizes of co-simulations and multi-core processors.

Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (Massive MIMO) is expected to be one of the key feature technology for the next cellular communication networks due to its significant benefits in terms of energy efficiency and increased spectral. To fully exploit these advantages, an accurate estimation of the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) between each transmit-receive antenna pair is crucial. In literature, it has been demonstrated that wireless communication tends to have a sparse structured CIR in delay and/or spatial domains. Several channel estimation strategies have exploited the sparsity in the massive MIMO channel based on additional assumptions on shared common support between uplink channels. In this paper, we propose a general approach which highlights the individual sparsity in the different uplink channels without any other additional assumption. To achieve this purpose, a training sequence, also known as pilot sequence and compressed sensing based CIR estimation techniques have been proposed for the massive MIMO sparse uplink channels. In order to underline the performance of proposed techniques, a comparison in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) and Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) is performed with other CS algorithms. The simulation results have shown that proposed algorithm presents a performance gain between 5 dB and 10 dB in terms of NMSE, and a gain of 1dB to 9dB in terms of BER.

This paper presents a high-precision lightning detection system designed for Thailand, which features integrated circuits, cloud computing, and real-time sensors. This system is primarily focused on tracking storms and detecting lightning to minimize potential damage to airports and other infrastructure. The lightning detection technology outlined in this research paper delivers precise data and real-time analysis of incoming storms and lightning, thereby generating alerts to relevant personnel who must make quick decisions. Additionally, the system can be used as an early warning system for residents in areas prone to lightning strikes. The integrated circuits used in the system allow for increased precision, while cloud computing facilitates real-time data transmission and processing. Overall, the proposed technology is a step towards improving the safety of the population and minimizing the damage caused by lightning in Thailand.

The drastic rise of data in the World Wide Web (WWW) causes the problem for the data organization and usability of data in real life. Through constant innovations, the WWW has become a part of our everyday life and is routinely used to reach other people through various web-based applications. This paper reveals a novel similarity measure which helps to retrieve more relevant documents from the repository thus contributing considerably to the effectiveness of Web Information Retrieval (WIR) system. Bio-inspired PSO methodology is used to retrieve the top ranked documents with a reduced response time and optimizes WIR process, hence contributes to the efficiency of the system. This paper also demonstrates a comparative study of the proposed system with the existing method. Experiments are conducted on CACM collections. Better precision-recall rates are achieved than the existing system.

In recent years, the proliferation of embedded devices within the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to a growing sense of urgency in developing effective security mechanisms. One approach to enhancing the security of embedded devices is the detection of firmware vulnerabilities through code similarity analysis. Feature extraction plays a key role in this process by identifying characteristic patterns within firmware code as a means of identifying vulnerabilities. The staged method of code similarity analysis for firmware vulnerability detection provides a comprehensive framework for conducting this type of analysis, comprising three stages: feature extraction, similarity measurement, and inspection. The method leverages microprogramming techniques to identify similarities between firmware code, delivering accurate and reliable results. The staged method holds tremendous promise in enhancing security for IoT-enabled devices and operating systems, and has the potential to prevent significant security breaches and data loss.

This paper focuses on the pedagogic organization of part-time studies in Network and Telecommunications at the bachelor level. The program is designed for students who are already employed in the industry or who want to pursue an education in the field while balancing work and other commitments. The curriculum is structured to provide a comprehensive understanding of the telecommunications industry, including topics such as networks, protocols, and security. Additionally, the program is designed to provide students with practical training and opportunities to work with the latest technologies. Companies play an important role in this program as they provide students with real-world experience through internships and other training opportunities. Contracts are also an essential component of the program as they ensure that students are able to balance their work and study commitments. Schedules and finance are also crucial considerations as students need to be able to manage their time effectively and ensure that they are able to pursue their education while maintaining their financial stability. Overall, this paper highlights the importance of effectively organizing part-time studies in Network and Telecommunications at the bachelor level in order to provide students with the skills and knowledge needed to succeed in the industry.

In this paper, we propose a regularized kernel-based method for identifying local modules in dynamic networks. The proposed method leverages the structure of the network by defining a kernel on the network nodes and regularizing the kernel using covariance matrices. The method also incorporates MISO communication to enable the identification of modules with multiple outputs. We employ Gaussian processes to model the dynamics of the network and use splines to interpolate the kernel matrices in time. Our approach is validated using computational modeling and experimental datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying local modules in dynamic networks. The proposed method provides a robust and efficient framework for studying complex systems, and can be applied to a wide range of applications in fields such as biology, economics, and social networks. The mathematical model presented in this paper provides a powerful tool for understanding the behavior of complex systems and identifying important features that may be overlooked by traditional methods.

Skin lesions are a common problem that can be indicative of various medical conditions. Skin lesion segmentation is an important task in biomedical imaging. Accurate segmentation of lesions in skin images is a challenging task due to variations in the appearance of skin lesions such as melanoma. In this paper, we propose a multi-stage framework with a context information fusion structure for skin lesion segmentation. The proposed framework comprises of two stages: the first stage involves the extraction of lesion candidates, while the second stage refines the segmentation results. We incorporate context information fusion into our framework, which involves extracting features from different scales and integrating them into a final segmentation result. Our approach achieves accurate segmentation results and reduces the measurement errors. Additionally, we use a deep learning-based approach for training our model, which further improves the segmentation accuracy. The proposed framework can be applied to other biomedical imaging applications and can potentially aid in early detection and diagnosis of skin lesions.

In recent years, Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) have become increasingly popular due to the need for better road safety and management. One of the most critical aspects of VANETs is the Quality of service (QoS), which ensures the efficient and reliable transmission of data. Routing protocols play a vital role in maintaining QoS, and the failure of roadside units (RSUs) can cause significant delays in data transmission. To overcome this problem, an Intelligent Cluster Head Selection Routing (ICHSR) technique has been proposed, which selects a more reliable cluster head to manage data transmission in case of RSU failure. This technique reduces the delay in data transmission and achieves better QoS. The Long Term Evolution (LTE) technology is used to support high-speed data transmission in VANETs. The proposed ICHSR technique is compared with other conventional routing techniques, and it performs better in terms of delay and bandwidth utilization. Overall, the ICHSR technique can effectively improve QoS in VANETs, especially in the case of RSU failures.

Efficient Virtual Network Function Placement (VNF) is a critical issue, especially for Poisson arrived traffic, which can lead to delays and overloading of servers and middleboxes in IP networks. This paper proposes a heuristic algorithm for the efficient placement of VNF, which considers the available resources and the traffic patterns. The algorithm maximizes the utilization of resources and minimizes the delays by placing the VNFs as close as possible to the source of the traffic. The proposed algorithm is evaluated through simulations based on standard traffic patterns and shows significant improvements compared to existing solutions. Furthermore, a programming model for the implementation of the proposed algorithm is presented, which can be easily integrated into the existing network infrastructure. As a result, this paper provides a practical solution for efficient VNF placement in IP networks, which can lead to significant improvements in network performance and user experience.

The internet of things (IoT) is being used more and more in our lives and this area attracts interest in studying new methods. One of these methods is mesh networking technique, which is increasingly becoming more popular and is suitable for use in places where wired connectivity is unavailable. Researchers are mostly focused on developing new and efficient services for systems running on this method, but the management of devices on mesh networks remains as an important issue. The management of an increasing number of devices can become inexhaustible. IoT management is to monitor and take action on the communication from and between connected devices and also control the devices from a remote server. This is similar to traditional network management when mesh network devices are considered. There is also a critical precaution for objects which is to complete administrative operations securely. In this article we have adapted a protocol, that is mainly used in traditional network management, for using in the management low powered personal area network (LoWPAN). We made some experimental analysis and compared our approach with other well-known IoT protocols for device management perspective.

In recent years, mobile advertising has gained popularity as a mean for publishers to monetize their free applications. One of the main concerns in the in-app advertising industry is the popular attack known as “click fraud”, which is the act of clicking on an ad, not because of interest in this ad, but rather as a way to generate illegal revenues for the application publisher. Many studies evaluated click fraud attacks in the literature, and some proposed solutions to detect it. In this paper, we propose a click fraud detection model, hereafter CFC, to classify fraudulent clicks by adopting some features and then testing using KNN, ANN and SVM. In fact, based on our experimental results, the different featured classifiers reached an accuracy higher than 93%.

This paper focuses on the use of the 2-D matrix pencil method for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of signals received by antenna arrays. DOA estimation is an important technique in many signal processing applications, and is especially useful in antenna arrays when trying to determine the direction from which incoming signals are arriving. The matrix pencil method is a popular approach for DOA estimation, and the 2-D version extends its capabilities to frequency estimation as well. This paper discusses the underlying geometry of the directive antennas and outlines the signal processing algorithms necessary to apply the method to antenna arrays. The resulting estimates of DOA and frequency provide valuable information for a variety of applications, including wireless communications and radar.

This paper presents the use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in estimating the parameters of Mixed Weibull Distributions. The Weibull distribution is a common statistical probability distribution used in the analysis of reliability and life data. Parameter estimation in Weibull distribution has been predominantly performed using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). However, MLE can be inadequate in handling complex data sets with uncertainty and irregularities. Thus, this study proposes the use of PSO as a nonlinear least squares estimation technique to determine the parameters of the Mixed Weibull Distribution. The results show that the proposed PSO method is more efficient and accurate in parameter estimation compared to MLE. Furthermore, the study provides a comprehensive overview of the Mixed Weibull Distribution, its properties and distribution functions. Overall, this research contributes to the development of methods for reliable parameter estimation in the analysis of complex data sets using the Weibull distribution.

The Ring Bus Architecture with Static UPS is a reliable and cost-effective solution for critical power applications that require uninterrupted power supply. This system incorporates Uninterruptible Power Systems (UPS) and inductors to ensure a stable power supply and protect the load during circuit faults. The system is designed with fault current limiters and reactive power compensators to improve power quality and protect the connected devices. The network topology of the Ring Bus Architecture is configured as a ring, which enables power to be supplied from multiple sources and ensures redundancy. The use of IP networks for communication between the devices enhances the flexibility and accessibility of the system. The significant advantages of the Ring Bus Architecture with Static UPS for critical power applications make it a perfect solution for facilities and businesses that require reliable and continuous power supply.

This paper presents a study on detecting Java compiled malware using machine learning techniques. Java is a programming language commonly used in the development of applications, including malicious ones. The proposed approach focuses on feature extraction and machine learning algorithms to identify features that can differentiate between benign and malicious Java code. The use of machine learning algorithms offers a high level of accuracy in the detection of malware, which is essential for maintaining security in computer systems. The results show that the proposed approach can effectively detect Java compiled malware with high accuracy, making it a valuable tool for security analysts and practitioners in the field. Overall, the study highlights the importance of using machine learning to detect malicious software and the potential of this technology to enhance the security of computer systems.

The Model of Acceptance and Use of Information Technology (or TAM) is a framework for understanding how individuals perceive and utilize information technology. This model has been widely used in research on a variety of topics related to information systems, including adoption and usage behaviors. The theoretical underpinnings of TAM are rooted in cognitive psychology and social psychology, and the model includes a set of constructs that help to explain why users may or may not accept and use new technologies. This model considers the instruments and hardware associated with the technology in addition to the organizations that are involved in its use. By employing computational modeling techniques, researchers are able to test and refine the TAM framework, increasing its usefulness in guiding information technology adoption and usage research.

Fringe projection profilometry (FPP) is a popular optical 3-dimensional (3D) scanning method. However, existing FPP methods often suffer from the ambiguity problem that only the wrapped phase information can be measured while the true phase information is required for 3D measurement. Although various phase unwrapping methods were suggested to recover the wrapped phase in FPP methods, most of them will fail when the target objects have complex structures. To solve this problem, we propose in this paper to embed the fringe pattern with a set of textural patterns to encode the period order of the true phase information. During the offline phase, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained to learn a set of filters that will be activated when they see the code patterns. When the encoded fringe image is captured, the modified morphological component analysis is first performed to extract the code pattern. It is then decoded by the trained CNN to estimate the K-map, which contains the period order of the true phase information. Experimental results show that the proposed method can measure the 3D profile of objects with abrupt jumps in height profile, where the conventional approaches often fail to perform. It also has a much higher computational efficiency due to the effective utilization of GPU by CNN.

The Australian Defence Forces (ADF) including the army, navy and air force often share resources. This is the case for helicopter training where the resources are often people, e.g. instructors. Understanding the current and future needs of the helicopter pilot training continuum is challenging. New students are continually entering the Defence services as trainees/cadets; passing or failing exams at specialist flying schools; progressing through or leaving the Defence services and potentially becoming trained pilots or instructors that can subsequently train future students. This continuum has an associated optimisation challenge. The ATHENA platform has been developed as a strategic discrete event simulation, optimisation and analysis system for manpower planning with specific focus on addressing the needs and demands of this helicopter pilot training continuum for the ADF. ATHENA has been developed as a simulation platform running on a Cloud infrastructure. This paper introduces ATHENA and describes the way in which the platform leverages container technologies to auto-scale across the Cloud with focus on the Kubernetes orchestration technology.

This paper proposes a novel approach for dynamic provisioning and monitoring of resources in cloud infrastructure networks, using regression-based techniques. The research focuses on the key areas of cloud computing, resource management, monitoring and dynamic scheduling, with the ultimate goal of providing responsive and optimal resource allocation to meet the demands of applications and services running in cloud environments. The proposed solution relies on linear regression and virtual machine monitors to build a mathematical model that predicts resource demands and allocates resources accordingly. The approach is designed to be flexible, scalable and adaptable to different types of cloud infrastructures. The results show that the proposed approach is effective in reducing resource wastage and improving overall system performance in cloud infrastructure networks.

The reliable and effective diagnosis of rolling bearing faults is crucial for ensuring the safe operation of rotating machinery. This paper proposes an adaptive fault frequency band detection method for rolling bearing fault diagnosis, based on indexes such as the resonant frequency, wavelet transforms, feature extraction, and harmonic analysis. Specifically, the proposed method adaptively detects the fault frequency band by identifying the varying resonant frequency of the rolling bearing, and uses the wavelet transform to extract the fault features from the vibration signals. Through comprehensive evaluation and comparison with existing methods, it is demonstrated that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and reliability in rolling bearing fault diagnosis. The research results have important practical implications for the maintenance and optimization of rotating machinery, providing a novel approach for effective fault diagnosis and maintenance decision-making.

This paper proposes a Fuzzy Echo State Neural Network (FESNN) with a Differential Evolution Framework for Time Series Forecasting. The aim of this research is to develop a predictive model for time series analysis that integrates the concepts of biological neural networks and computational modeling. The approach involves using reservoirs to represent the dynamics of the input signal and employs analytical models to forecast future values. To further improve the prediction accuracy, a Differential Evolution Framework is applied to optimize the FESNN parameters. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FESNN with the Differential Evolution Framework outperforms other existing algorithms in terms of forecasting accuracy and stability. This research offers a promising approach to enhancing the accuracy and reliability of time series forecasting, which has significant implications for numerous application areas such as finance, environmental prediction, and automation systems.

This paper focuses on the study of decision-making system for power grid consistency planning, which includes various aspects such as planning, power grids, cloud computing, computational modeling, databases, business, and computer architecture. With the increasing complexity of power grid systems, the need for an efficient and effective decision-making system is becoming more and more important. This paper analyzes the current state of decision-making systems for power grid consistency planning and proposes a new approach that incorporates cloud computing, computational modeling, and databases to optimize the decision-making process. The proposed system is expected to improve the accuracy and efficiency of decision-making, reduce costs, and enhance the overall performance of power grid systems. The study also explores the business implications of implementing the proposed system and discusses the necessary computer architecture and infrastructure to support it. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the development of decision-making systems for power grid consistency planning and offers practical recommendations for the industry.

Task deployment has become a hot topic for load balancing in edge computing. In view of the problem that most of the hosts are overloaded in the edge computing, the central load is unbalanced. Much work focuses on the load balancing of the cloud data center or the short-term load balancing of edge data centers. In order to solve the host selection problem of task deployment in joint cloud data centers with edge computing while achieving the overall long-term load balancing, this paper utilizes that the deployment mode of joint cloud model, on this basis, proposes a deployment strategy HEELS based on the analysis of heuristic task clustering method and glowworm swarm optimization algorithm. Its main idea consists of two parts. First, the task with large resources in the current task set is filtered out by the clustering analysis, and the task offloading technology is exploited to upload the result to the cloud computing center for deployment and calculation. Then, the optimized GSO algorithm is exploited in the edge computing center, and the idea of SCA is combined into the optimization of step size so that the optimized GSO algorithm has an adaptive step size, achieving better global search ability in the early stage and better local convergence ability in the later stage. The experimental results show that compared with the existing research, HEELS realizes better load balancing effect and makes the joint datacenter more green and efficient.

Device-to-device (D2D) communication is a critical component of smart cities and cellular networks. Resource management in D2D communication often involves joint power control and channel allocation to minimize interference and maximize energy efficiency. In this paper, we propose a two-stage energy-efficient approach for joint power control and channel allocation in D2D communication. The first stage involves a power control algorithm that applies a graph-based approach to minimize interference and the second stage involves a channel allocation algorithm that applies a stochastic optimization approach to maximize energy efficiency. Simulation results show that the proposed approach can significantly improve the energy efficiency of D2D communication systems while reducing interference. This approach has practical applications in future D2D communication technologies and can contribute to the development of more sustainable and energy-efficient smart cities.

Raw data of point cloud is often noisy and with topological defects (such as holes), which cause problems including faulty connection and inaccurate structure. As a result, the surface reconstruction of point cloud data is a highly challenging problem. This work proposes a novel method, which improves the surface quality compared with existing methods. Our method combines both the local detailed features and the global topological information during the reconstruction process. To facilitate the feature refinement, we first pre-process the point cloud data by relocating each point, upsampling the point data, and optimizing normals to enhance the features and geometric details. We then identify the topological information by segmenting the geometry and constructing curve skeletons for each part and guide the surface reconstruction with the skeletons by minimal user interaction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods with various examples, where our reconstruction can fill out missing data and preserve sharp features.

This paper presents a comparative study of two popular evolutionary optimization techniques - Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Simulated Evolution (SE) - for the task of object recognition. GA and SE are both used to optimize the training of shape recognition models by minimizing the Euclidean distance between the model's prediction and the actual object shape. The experiments conducted in this study demonstrate that both GA and SE can significantly improve the accuracy of object recognition models, but GA outperforms SE in terms of optimization efficiency. This means that GA can achieve the same level of accuracy with fewer iterations, making it a more efficient optimization technique. These results are important for computer science researchers and practitioners interested in applying evolutionary optimization techniques to object recognition tasks.

Dynamic EEE (Energy Efficient Ethernet) coalescing is an important technique for reducing both delays and energy consumption in Ethernet networks. Heuristic algorithms have been developed to address this issue, but they may not always yield optimal results. Therefore, analytical models have been proposed to predict the effectiveness of heuristics and to provide bounds on the achievable energy savings. To further improve the performance of EEE coalescing, tuning methods have been developed to adjust the parameters of the heuristic algorithms. Computational modeling has also been used to analyze the impact of EEE coalescing on network performance, taking into account factors such as traffic patterns, packet sizes, and other network characteristics. With the continued growth of Ethernet networks, it is important to develop effective and efficient techniques for reducing delays and energy consumption, and dynamic EEE coalescing is a promising approach.

This paper presents a Vectored-Bloom Filter implementation on FPGA for IP address lookup. IP networks have become increasingly large and complex, requiring efficient IP address lookup methods. Computer architecture and hardware design are crucial in achieving high throughput and low latency for lookup operations. The proposed Vectored-Bloom Filter is implemented on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA), offering high performance in IP address searching. The filter architecture utilizes a combination of multi-segment and multi-stage Bloom filters, achieving a significant reduction in memory requirements while maintaining high throughput. An evaluation of the proposed design demonstrates that it provides superior results compared to existing techniques. The implementation is suitable for hardware acceleration of IP address lookup in network switches and routers, providing a substantial improvement in information filtering and network performance.

This paper presents a compiler for deep neural network accelerators that is capable of generating optimized code for a wide range of data parameters. The compiler works by utilizing a hand-crafted computation kernel and integrating it with hardware acceleration techniques. The kernel is designed to support deep learning applications and can handle large-scale data transfers efficiently. The compiler also utilizes Monte Carlo methods to optimize energy efficiency, resulting in reduced energy consumption without sacrificing performance. Overall, the proposed compiler is capable of generating efficient code for a variety of data-intensive applications, making it a useful tool for researchers and practitioners alike.

The present paper proposes a novel method to detect replay attacks in speaker verification systems by leveraging non-voiced segments and decision level feature switching. The proposed method involves feature extraction techniques such as mel frequency cepstral coefficients and reverberation correction. Additionally, the system employs the use of switches at the decision level to dynamically select between different feature sets for better accuracy. A mathematical model is developed which employs a Gaussian mixture model to train the system and classify signals as genuine or replayed. The proposed system has been tested on a publicly available database and has been shown to outperform existing methods in terms of accuracy. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating non-voiced segments and decision level feature switching for replay attack detection in speaker verification systems.

It is crucial for doctors to fully understand the interaction between drugs in prescriptions, especially when a patient takes multiple medications at the same time during treatment. The purpose of drug drug interaction (DDI) extraction is to automatically obtain the interaction between drugs from biomedical literature. Current state-of-the-art approaches for DDI extraction task are based on artificial intelligence and natural language processing. While such existing DDI extraction methods can provide more knowledge and enhance the performance through external resources such as biomedical databases or ontologies, due to the difficulty of updating, these external resources are delayed. In fact, user generated content (UGC) is another kind of external medical resources that can be quickly updated. We are trying to use UGC resources to provide more available information for our deep learning DDI extraction method. In this paper, we present a DDI extraction approach through a new attention mechanism called full-attention which can combine the UGC information with contextual information. We conducted a series of experiments on the DDI 2013 Evaluation dataset to evaluate our method. Experiments show improved performance compared with the state of the art and UGC-DDI model achieves a competitive F-score of 0.712.

The uses and applications of VR and AR technologies have been widespread in the last few years. One of its most important areas of use is the use of virtual and augmented reality in education, learning and training. Hence, this research paper examines the latest developments and the scientific findings in the field of augmented software industry, its applications, and uses in teaching, learning and training. Tens of augmented reality applications, their areas of application, and practical uses were studied with the aim of: Identifying strengths and weaknesses and selecting the appropriate ones in teaching, learning and training. To achieve the objectives of the research: The method of content analysis based on the applied approach was used, The researcher recommended: It is necessary to adopt the application and usage of augmented reality technologies in education, learning and training at the highest levels, and recommended the use of a set of software and platforms that would enhance the quality of teaching, learning and training and improve its outcomes.

This paper presents work-in-progress research focused on improving the scheduling of mixed-criticality tasks by varying processor speed. The authors utilize task analysis and computational modeling to optimize processor scheduling for mixed-criticality tasks. The proposed approach utilizes switches to efficiently manage runtime and dynamically schedule tasks using approximation algorithms. The authors are currently in the process of analyzing the effectiveness of the approach through simulations and its potential for practical implementation. The results of this research can have significant impacts on improving the scheduling of mixed-criticality tasks in real-time systems.

Voice conversion has been an important research area in recent years due to its wide range of applications, such as in speech recognition and synthesis. This paper proposes a novel approach to voice conversion based on cross-domain features using variational auto encoders (VAE). The proposed system involves two stages, namely training and decoding. In the training stage, the system performs feature extraction on the training data using neural networks, and then learns the mapping between source and target features using a VAE. This mapping is then used in the decoding stage to generate converted speech. Task analysis and Gaussian distribution are also employed in the system to improve the accuracy and naturalness of the converted speech. The proposed system has been evaluated on a database of speakers with different accents and achieved promising results in terms of subjective and objective measures. The proposed approach has the potential to be applied to a variety of voice conversion tasks and can be a useful tool in many different fields.

This paper investigates the neural correlates of haptic training using electroencephalography (EEG). Haptic interfaces play an important role in training humans for tasks that require hands-on experience, and this study focuses on the neural mechanisms which contribute to skill acquisition. Task analysis is performed to study the trajectory of performance improvement, and robot sensing systems are used to provide feedback from the training. The results reveal changes in EEG power spectra and coherence within specific cortical regions during training, highlighting the role of cortical plasticity in skill acquisition. The study provides insights into the neural correlates of haptic training, and future research can emphasize on developing more effective and efficient training methods based on the findings of this study.

This paper proposes a Dilated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for image classification. The convolution operation, which extracts features from images, is carried out using a kernel that is dilated for more comprehensive feature extraction. The proposed model is based on the use of data models and computational modeling to adapt to different image recognition tasks. The training of the model is carried out using the backpropagation algorithm to optimize the model's parameters. This model can effectively extract features from images for classification, achieving competitive classification accuracy on popular image datasets compared to other state-of-the-art models. In summary, the proposed dilated CNN model shows promise for improved image classification using advanced feature extraction techniques.

The Distributed Event-Triggered Gradient Method is a novel approach for solving constrained convex minimization problems in distributed systems. This method employs a peer-to-peer computing architecture where each node executes a local optimization algorithm based on the Gradient methods. The convergence of the algorithm is guaranteed by a event-triggered mechanism that reduces the communication burden between agents. The proposed method is particularly useful in cases where the computation, communication or storage resources are limited, and the constraints are not known in advance. Moreover, the method is well-suited for problems that involve linear programming, where the objective function is a linear combination of convex functions. The effectiveness of the distributed event-triggered gradient method is demonstrated through numerical simulations, where it outperforms the traditional centralized methods in terms of execution time and communication cost. In summary, this method can be considered as a viable solution for solving large-scale optimization problems in distributed systems with limited resources and communication channels.

In this case study, we develop a stacked ensemble learning method to predict the extraction efficiency of the porous network. We generate the porous network data using computational fluid dynamics numerical method. Based on this data we train several machine-learning models. The machine learning models are then used to train a super model on the predictions. Our results show that the stacked ensemble learning is significantly more efficient than every single machine-learning model. The finding of this approach has direct applications in understanding the extraction of oil from porous media.

This paper studies the effect of parasitic components on the dynamic performance of power stages in DC-DC PWM buck and boost converters operating in continuous conduction mode (CCM). The resistance of these components can significantly impact the steady-state and transient behavior of the converter, affecting its output voltage and current. A mathematical model is developed to analyze the effects of parasitic components, including the inductor parasitic resistance and the MOSFET on-resistance. Computational modeling is used to simulate the behavior of the converter under different load conditions. The results show that parasitic components can introduce significant disturbances in the converter's output voltage, especially at high frequencies. The effect of these components on the converter's dynamic performance is more pronounced in buck converters than boost converters. Load modeling is also considered to evaluate the effects of parasitic components in more realistic scenarios. This study provides valuable insights into the design and optimization of pulse-width modulation converters, highlighting the importance of accurate modeling of parasitic components to achieve optimal performance.

This paper provides a critical review on the state-of-the-art pedestrian and evacuation dynamics so as to comprehensively comprehend the motion behaviors of pedestrians from observations to simulation aspects. Types of typical data collection methods, namely the field survey, the controlled experiment, and the animal experiment, are classified, and the connections and differences of these three observation methods are explored. Pedestrians' complex behaviors characterized by the self-organization phenomena and movement data characterized by the fundamental diagram are then studied after the data collections, which can be used to calibrate and validate the pedestrian models. The mathematical models for pedestrian dynamics from both tactical level and operational level are also highlighted. The simulation data produced by the mathematical models could further reproduce pedestrian behaviors during the observations and contribute to decision makings for improving the evacuation efficiency. The applications of pedestrian models for behavior analysis, evacuation simulation, and layout design are also presented. Some challenges and future directions in the pedestrian and evacuation dynamics are also put forward. Findings presented in this study are helpful for researchers who want to understand the pedestrian and evacuation dynamics and to perform further research in this field.

In this study, we investigate the influence of the number of training samples on the Inverse Kinematics (IK) solutions obtained by Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). The training process is crucial to the performance of ANNs in IK solutions since it determines the accuracy and generalization ability of ANNs. Our experiments demonstrate that increasing the number of training samples can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of the ANNs in IK problems. Furthermore, we show that the ANN-based IK approach is comparable to or even outperforms the traditional analytical methods, especially for complex robotic systems with high degrees of freedom and non-linear kinematics. Our work sheds light on the potential of ANNs for IK solutions and provides insights into the optimal training strategies for achieving high performance. It also contributes to the understanding of the similarities and differences between Artificial Neural Networks and Biological Neural Networks in terms of kinematics resolution and end effector control.

In this paper, we propose a movie recommendation system that utilizes collaborative filtering algorithms combined with Doc2Vec. Our approach leverages the power of deep learning for feature extraction and training analytical models. By applying collaborative filtering and Doc2Vec, our system is able to recommend movies to users based on their preferences and behaviors. We believe that this approach is superior to traditional movie recommendation systems, which often rely solely on collaborative filtering or content-based filtering. Our system takes into account both similarities between movies and similarities between users to make more accurate recommendations. We evaluate the performance of our system using a real-world data set and achieve significant improvement over traditional methods. Our results suggest that incorporating deep learning techniques into recommendation systems is an effective approach for improving recommendation accuracy.

The tremendous growth in ubiquitous sensor networks and IoT has led to Human Activity Recognition (HAR) emerging to be an exciting challenge. Machine learning approaches proposed in this direction have proved to be competent solutions. HAR data treatment in a recurrent form, and further analysis using deep networks such as RNNs or LSTM is largely unexplored. In this work, we treat data generated from a smart home setup towards HRA, as a series of events and perform feature extraction using a the popular LSTM variant of LSTMs. We use the Aruba dataset from the CASAS project [2]. We apply LSTM to extract features and perform annotations. Additionally we apply standard classification techniques to recognize and evaluate the different activities in the newly annotated data. From experimentations using our method we can achieve annotation accuracies of up to 79.5% which is 13.6% better than other state-of-the-art solutions.

Personal authentication is a critical component of modern society's reliance on technology. One promising method for authentication is the use of electrodes and electromyography (EMG) to identify an individual's unique muscle signals. In this paper, we explore the potential for using dry electrodes and convolutional neural networks (CNN) to accurately recognize the muscle signals of the lips. This method could have significant applications in a variety of fields, including the Internet of Things and secure online authentication. Our results suggest that this approach shows promise for providing a reliable and accurate means of authentication that is both non-invasive and accessible. We believe that this research has significant implications for the future of secure authentication and look forward to sharing our findings and recommendations at upcoming conferences.

We aim for a robot capable to learn sequences of motor policies to achieve a field of complex tasks. In this paper, we consider a set of interrelated complex tasks hierarchically organized. To address this high-dimensional mapping between a continuous high-dimensional space of tasks and an infinite dimensional space of sequences of policies, we introduce a framework called "procedure", which enables the creation of sequences of policies by combining previously learned skills. We propose an active learning algorithmic architecture, capable of organizing its learning process in order to achieve a field of complex tasks by learning sequences of primitive motor policies. Based on heuristics of goal-babbling, social guidance, strategic learning guided by intrinsic motivation, and the "procedure" framework, our algorithm can actively decide on which outcome to focus and which exploration strategy to apply. We show that a simulation industrial robot can tackle the learning of complex motor policies and adapt this complexity to that of the task at hand. Owing to its exploration strategies, it can discover the levels of difficulty of the tasks, and learn the hierarchy between tasks so as to combine simple tasks to complete a complex task.

There have been increasing interests in employing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) such as drones for telecommunication purpose. In such networks, UAVs act as base stations and provide downloading service to users. Compared with conventional terrestrial base stations, such UAV-BSs can dynamically adjust their locations to improve network performance. However, there exists two important issues in UAV networks, handoff overhead and UAV deployment. The handoff overhead issue is particularly important for UAVs because UAV BSs are connected to cellular BSs via wireless backhaul links, which are costly in terms of spectrum usage and energy consumption. Hence, it is highly desirable to eliminate any unnecessary handoff to minimise the waste of wireless backhaul. The UAV deployment, on the other hand, introduces a new tool for radio resource management, since BS positions are open for network optimisation. In this paper, a smart user association algorithm, named reinforcement learning handoff (RLH), is devised to reduce redundant handoffs in UAV networks and two methods of UAV mobility control are designed to co-operate with the proposed RLH algorithm to optimise the system throughput. In the RLH algorithm, users perform handoffs according to the reward of a reinforcement learning process. In UAV deployment two UAV mobility control methods are proposed respectively base on the SNR estimation and based on the K-Means approach. According to our simulation results, the RLH algorithm can reduce the number of handoffs by 75%.

In this paper, we introduce an automated vision-based system which consists of an image grabbing mechanism and an inspection method for detecting and classifying defects on the surface of leather fabric. The proposed inspection method treats errors like scars, scratches and pinholes. In the defect detection process, several image processing algorithms are employed to extract image features and locate defect's positions on leather surface. In the defect classification process, these collected features are used to classify the type of defect based on SVM algorithm. Experimental results show that the detected defects are localized according to their real-positions on leather surface. The size and type of detected defect are also accurately determined.

Computational complexity and storage are the two main constraints while performing real-time simulation of power electronic circuits. Matrix inversion in each time step required by nodal analysis based solvers is generally not possible in real-time simulation. Instead, the inversion of system matrix is computed and stored before the actual simulation starts. When there are several switches in the circuit being simulated, it is required to store 2 power N matrices (for N switches), and storage can become a bottleneck. In this paper, a new scheme is proposed wherein only a single inverse admittance matrix is required to be stored (for N switches), which is updated using Woodbury formula to obtain the inverse admittance matrix for the current switch states. The computational cost can be further reduced if more inverse admittance matrices are allowed to be stored. The proposed scheme is demonstrated with case studies of a few representative examples.

Communication range in passive radio-frequency identification (RFID) front-end devices is a critical barrier in the real-world implementation of this low-cost technology. Purely passive RFID tags power up by harvesting the limited RF energy transmitted by the interrogator, and communicate by backscattering the incident signal. This mode of communication keeps manufacturing costs below a few cents per tag, but the limited power available at the tag undermines long-range deployment. In this paper, we present an approach to use photovoltaics (PV) to augment the available energy at the tag to improve read range and sensing capabilities. We provide this extra-energy to the RFID integrated circuit (IC) using minimum additional electronics yet enabling persistent sensor-data acquisition. Current and emerging thin-film PV technologies have significant potential for being very low-cost, hence eliminating the barrier for implementation and making of PV-RFID wireless sensors. We reduce the long-range PV-RFID idea to practice by creating functional prototypes of: 1) a wireless building environment sensor to monitor temperature and 2) an embedded tracker to find lost golf balls. The read range of PV-RFID is enhanced eight times compared to conventional passive devices. In addition, the PV-RFID tags persistently transmit large volumes of sensor data (>0.14 million measurements per day) without using batteries. For communication range and energy persistence, we observe good agreement between calculated estimates and experimental results. We have also identified avenues for future research to develop low-cost PV-RFID devices for wireless sensing in the midst of the other competitive wireless technologies, such as Bluetooth, ZigBee, long range (LoRa) backscatter etc.

Face verification is still a big challenging problem due to the different image conditions such as expression, pose, and illumination. To address these challenges, we propose a new Deep Leaning structure called Localized Deep-Norm CNN. Our model focuses on finding the correlations of features inside the sub region of each learning face by adding a localized feature normalization layer. The model can recover all the important correlated features of face images. Intuitively, the Localized Deep-Norm CNN model mimics the primary visual context of the learned face image by combining the localized extracted features representations. The local relational face features are extracted and normalized by assigning each sub-block to a local CNN model. Then, the global features are constructed by combining these localized high-level features to one fully connected layer to produce the final feature space of 4608d dimensions. In our model, two different optimization techniques are proposed to optimize the loss functions. The first optimization modifies the SoftMax loss function by using a cosine similarity metric instead of Euclidean inner-product layer. The second optimization is done by combining different loss functions with different metric learning. Our model achieves robustness accuracy of 99.19% in characterizing the similarity of multiple faces which is 0.16% improving on the LFW performance results.

This paper proposes a finite-time fuzzy control approach for stochastic nonlinear systems. The considered systems are inherently nonlinear and subject to stochastic disturbances. Stability criteria are developed to ensure asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Fuzzy logic is utilized to design the controller, which can adapt to the system dynamics and uncertainties. The proposed control scheme is able to achieve finite-time stability, meaning that the system state converges to the equilibrium point in a finite amount of time. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in controlling stochastic nonlinear systems. The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, such as robotics, biomedical engineering, and aerospace engineering, where adaptive systems are necessary to cope with uncertainties and disturbances.

Many safety-critical applications that utilize the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) demand highly accurate positioning information, as well as highly integrity and reliability. Due to GNSS signals are easily distorted by the interferences or disturbances, the signal quality monitoring (SQM) is necessary to detect the presence of dangerous signal distortions. In this paper, we developed an SQM software for binary offset carrier (BOC) modulated navigation signals. Firstly, the models of BOC signal with ideal and distortion are presented respectively. Then the architecture of SQM software is proposed. Moreover, the effect of the white gaussian noise (WGN) and the front-end filter on the correlation peak of the receiver is analyzed. Finally, the biases induced by the signal distortion are evaluated. The experiments simulate the relationships between the code phase shift and the normalized correlation value in the case of the signal digital distortion and the analog distortion. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SQM method can effectively monitor the signal distortion and accurately estimate the correlation peak deviation caused by the distortion.

In this paper we introduce a general and systematic approach to achieving robust tracking control for nonlinear systems with non-vanishing uncertainties, along with the complete rejection of non-vanishing uncertainties and user-assignable convergence rate. Furthermore, the convergence rate can be pre-specified faster than exponential or nearly as fast as any prescribed finite time if needed. The key design tool is the utilization of a time-varying feedback gain through a time-varying scaling function that satisfies certain conditions. A general way to construct such time-varying rate function is given such that the different yet assignable convergence rates can be achieved.

This letter proposes a novel pilot spoofing attack detection scheme by introducing an auxiliary node as a trusted user, which also participates in the uplink training process and assists to detect pilot spoofing in multiple-input single-output systems. To do so, we design an efficient three-phase uplink training method, with which a malicious user can be reliably detected. In contrast to the existing methods involving two-stage uplink–downlink training, our method relies only on the uplink training stage. Meanwhile, our new scheme detects spoofing attack without altering pilot signals, which is also beyond the competence of the existing methods. Numerical results show that our method improves the detection probability significantly.

This paper focuses on the implementation of optical character recognition (OCR) for handwritten mathematical expressions in educational humanoid robots. The success of character recognition in humanoid robots relies heavily on the accuracy of image segmentation and the utilization of biological neural networks. Through the training of neurons, the OCR system is able to accurately recognize and interpret complex mathematical expressions written by hand. The use of OCR in humanoid robots has significant implications for educational settings, as it allows for the automation of the evaluation of student work and the provision of personalized feedback tailored to each individual. In conclusion, the implementation of OCR in humanoid robots presents a promising avenue for further research and development in the field of educational technology.

This paper proposes the optimisation of a hybrid power supply (HPS) design by implementing a Genetic Algorithm (GA). Single-source renewable energy systems (RES) are associated with low capacity factor, high capital costs and intermittency. Combining two or more power sources, whether renewable or non-renewable, increases the system's reliability in terms of power consistency, reduces fuel emissions and is a more sustainable and financial viable solution overall. A grid-connection and a battery storage system can further increase the dispatchability of the system. The design of each HPS can become more complex due to the location and stochastic availability of renewable energy sources. A GA is developed to solve this sizing problem. The objectives of the algorithm are: minimizing the loss of power supply probability, maximizing usage of renewable energy and minimizing capital and life cycle costs. A GA is developed to incorporate operational and dispatch strategies and a techno-economic and trade-off analysis is done to study the advantages and disadvantages of different combinations. This can help develop a methodology to choose the most suited HPS for the location and resource availability. The in-house GA will be compared with HOMER design software to highlight the similarities and differences between the two design strategies.

This paper discusses the use of the time domain finite element method for Maxwell's equations, which is a numerical technique for solving electromagnetic problems. The Maxwell equations are mathematical models that describe the behavior of electric and magnetic fields, and their solutions are essential for understanding phenomena such as propagation and electromagnetic waves. Finite element analysis is a powerful tool for the computational modeling of complex electromagnetic systems, as it enables the discretization of the problem domain into small finite elements that can be accurately solved using numerical methods. Time-domain analysis is particularly useful for studying dynamic systems, where changes over time can be observed and analyzed. Magnetic domains and other related effects can be accounted for using this approach, leading to a comprehensive understanding of electromagnetic phenomena. Overall, the time domain finite element method is an important tool for the simulation and analysis of electromagnetic systems, and has broad applications in fields such as telecommunications, electronics, and materials science.

This paper outlines a novel Python library for the development of Memory Augmented Neural Networks (MANNs). The library is designed to allow for the efficient creation of mathematical models of MANNs, which can be used for a variety of applications in the field of artificial intelligence. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) form the foundation of the library, with additional features such as memory management, task analysis, and magnetic head control being incorporated for enhanced performance. The library includes a comprehensive implementation of writing functionality for MANNs, which allows users to specify the memory capacity of a network and write input data to it in a structured format. Overall, the library represents a significant step forward in the field of MANNs, and will be a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners alike.

This research constructs an experimental system for upper limb stroke ill persons. It can apply to any dwelling for patient practices. The idea of stroke rehabilitation system is applied International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health structure and includes Barthel scale for ill person's health evaluation. These systems are designed by IOT and Android APP system to control the rehabilitation system. The findings demonstrate that it can work effectively for the patients at home. This study can collect patients' data from every day rehabilitation and send these data to medical cloud. These data can be analyzed statistically and converted to Microsoft Excel files to drop bar charts for visually display. The system reports can upload to medical institution cloud computing systems for doctors' reference. This study demonstrates the implementation of results and provides program codes for readers' reference.

This paper presents a new approach to training manipulators for games using image-based feedback and deep reinforcement learning. The goal is to create a robotic arm representation that can learn and adapt to various game scenarios. The proposed technique involves the use of solid modeling to create a virtual environment, which is then fed to a neural network that receives image-based feedback from the game engine. The neural network is trained using reinforcement learning and is able to learn complex actions and behaviors. The results show that this approach can effectively train robotic arms for games, with performance comparable to traditional approaches. The approach is also highly adaptable and can be used in a variety of gaming scenarios. Overall, this paper presents a promising technique for developing more advanced and versatile robotic arm representations for games using image-based feedback and deep reinforcement learning.

This paper proposes an optimal lead compensator design for a two-loop control system of a linear DC motor. The control system is modeled using mathematical models, and the lead compensation technique is employed. Moreover, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the lead compensator parameters. The proposed design ensures that the control system provides accurate and stable control of the DC motor. The paper also discusses the biological cell-inspired algorithm used in optimizing the parameters which is characterized by their ability to explore a large search space in a short time. Furthermore, linear programming is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed design. The results show that the optimal lead compensator design yields superior performance in comparison to conventional designs. Therefore, the proposed methodology can be useful in developing effective and efficient control systems for DC motors.

This paper proposes a robust fine tuning methodology for designing optimal PID controllers with guaranteed robustness in process control applications. The proposed methodology utilizes an optimization technique and sensitivity analysis based on computational modeling. The approach is designed to ensure robustness of the tuning process to parameter uncertainties, including modeling errors, measurement noise, and external disturbances. The paper presents a detailed design methodology for fine tuning and robust optimization of PID controllers. The proposed methodology involves the use of a set of design objectives and constraints to determine the optimal tuning parameters. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving robust and optimal PID controller designs with high performance and robustness. The proposed methodology can be further extended to other control systems, and can add value in addressing the challenging issues of parameter uncertainty and robustness in control systems.

This paper presents a FPGA-based device-level electro-thermal modeling approach for the floating interleaved boost converter used in fuel cell hardware-in-the-loop applications. The proposed technique leverages the integrated circuit modeling of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) along with a computational modeling framework to simulate the electrical behavior of the converter in real-time. Transient analysis techniques are utilized to capture the dynamics of the switch devices, and the electro-thermal modeling approach allows for a more accurate prediction of IGBT temperature profiles. The resulting model can be used to predict the performance of the converter under various operating conditions and identify potential failures due to overheating of the devices. The proposed approach is validated through experimental testing, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting the electro-thermal behavior of the converter. Overall, this work presents a novel technique for improving the performance and reliability of fuel cell systems by providing accurate device-level modeling capabilities for real-time systems.

In order to mitigate the long processing delay and high energy consumption of mobile augmented reality (AR) applications, mobile edge computing (MEC) has been recently proposed and is envisioned as a promising means to deliver better Quality of Experience (QoE) for AR consumers. In this article, we first present a comprehensive AR overview, including the indispensable components of general AR applications, fashionable AR devices, and several existing techniques for overcoming the thorny latency and energy consumption problems. Then we propose a novel hierarchical computation architecture by inserting an edge layer between the conventional user layer and cloud layer. Based on the proposed architecture, we further develop an innovative operation mechanism to improve the performance of mobile AR applications. Three key technologies are also discussed to further assist the proposed AR architecture. Simulation results are finally provided to verify that our proposals can significantly improve latency and energy performance as compared to existing baseline schemes.

We propose an attentive neural network for the task of named entity recognition in Vietnamese. The proposed attentive neural model makes use of character-based language models and word embeddings to encode words as vector representations. A neural network architecture of encoder, attention, and decoder layers is then utilized to encode knowledge of input sentences and to label entity tags. The experimental results show that the proposed attentive neural network achieves the state-of-the-art results on the benchmark named entity recognition datasets in Vietnamese in comparison to both hand-crafted features based models and neural models.

Wireless sensor networks have emerged as an important technology with myriad applications in different fields. One of the main challenges in wireless sensor networks is the filtering of the data to ensure that only relevant and useful data are transmitted to the base station. This paper proposes a multipath selection method for en-route filtering in dynamic wireless sensor network. The proposed method utilizes routing and network topology to select an efficient path for data transmission. Additionally, vehicle dynamics are taken into account to ensure that the appropriate path is selected based on the movement of the vehicles. Authentication is also included in the method to ensure the integrity and security of the transmitted data. The proposed method is evaluated through simulations and the results show that it is highly effective in reducing the transmission times and energy consumption in a dynamic wireless sensor network. This method can be useful in various applications such as environmental monitoring, traffic management, and disaster relief efforts.

The accurate measurement of quantum systems is essential for practical applications such as quantum communication and computation. Boolean tomography is an effective method for measuring quantum states based on a limited number of measurements. However, the quality of measurements depends on the number of end monitors utilized in the process. In this paper, we investigate the measurement coverage for Boolean tomography with limited end monitors. We present a theoretical analysis of the relationship between the number of end monitors and the measurement coverage. We also perform numerical simulations to verify our theoretical results. Our findings demonstrate that with a smaller number of end monitors, the measurement coverage is reduced, leading to a lower quality of measurements. This research has practical implications for the design and implementation of Boolean tomography for quantum systems in various applications, such as frequency modulation, Internet of Things, green computing, social computing, blockchain, and information technology.

This paper proposes a nonparallel voice adaptation, a form of speech processing, which utilizes a voice profile with a mean dataset, paired with auxiliary sets generated from a stylized quantization from a single recording where only the target voice subject is required to train beforehand aimed towards real-time applications. Conventional methods suffer from complexified training where two or more speakers must be trained in parallel, thus impractical for actual real-time uses. Our quantized data is used to produce sound-indexes, a signature for each sound-frame for comparing speakers. Prosody is sustained by translating the input's power in the current frame into the corresponding output frame real-time. The design was tested with an English voice profile and the rate of matching output and frames were measured to determine a factor of fragmentation, which is the degree of unsuccessful segments. Results showed diverse fragmentation, complementing the input length. Basic input ranged in the very good 5-6% fragmentation range, while convoluted input up to 26%. The average matching time was 176 milliseconds. Future work focuses on improving performance and decreasing fragmentation.

Face recognition is a widespread technology that has been successfully applied in various fields. However, plastic surgery represents a challenging issue in this context. In this study, we propose a patch-based approach for face recognition under plastic surgery. The proposed method is based on feature extraction from specific facial regions, or patches, in order to compensate for changes in facial appearance due to surgery. We focus on the discrete cosine transform (DCT) as a powerful tool for feature extraction. Moreover, we use several databases containing pre- and post-surgery images to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach. The results show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. We also investigate the effect of different training schemes on the performance of the proposed approach. Our findings suggest that the proposed method can be trained efficiently using only a small set of representative samples. Overall, our study provides a promising solution for face recognition under plastic surgery, which can be applied in various real-world applications.

This paper presents a study on user-defined modeling of the Voltage Source Converter-High Voltage Direct Current (VSCHVDC) transmission system using the Power System Simulator for Engineering (PSS/E) software. The aim of this study is to develop mathematical and analytical models, as well as algorithms for load modeling and computational modeling of the VSCHVDC transmission system. The study proposes user-defined models for control and protection systems, as well as the converter and DC systems that form the VSCHVDC transmission system. The proposed models were verified against realistic system scenarios and were found to be accurate. This study can contribute to the development of more efficient and reliable power transmission systems, as well as to the optimization of power system operations.

In this paper, we propose a new scalable architecture of smart telemetry system based on IoT (Internet of Things) devices, it uses cellular (SMS solution) and internet (TCP/UDP Solution) networks to transmit, in real time, data to or from supervised and controlled system. Here, we try, for example, to collect measurements data from the flammable gas, temperature sensors and DC motor. This proposed work takes advantage of being scalable and also proposing a solution to solve temperature, redundancy and electromagnetic compatibility problems, which are the critical parameters in the majority of applications based on IIoT (Industrial IoT) solutions. The proposed smart telemetry system is promising and could play an important role in reducing repairs costs and improve efficiencies in preventive and predictive maintenance. Consequently, manufacturing and logistics environments could increase their productivity by using IIoT technologies to anticipate maintenance needs to prevent equipment failures and avoid unscheduled downtime.

This work has two objectives to be achieved. The first goal is to evaluate the performance of a Webservice in the cloud environment by analyzing the sending of images to mobile devices focused on social networking applications. From this evaluation, the second objective proposes strategies to mitigate the effects of delays in the display of these images, in order to optimize the quality of the service. The methodological process consisted in the planning and execution of experiments to evaluate the performance of different scenarios with different amounts of images, resolutions and database for storage. The Eucalyptus platform was defined as the Cloud environment, and a Webservice sending persistent images in NoSQL Databases to a mobile device. The results highlight that the parameter that influences the performance of the image consumption in mobile devices through the WebService is the processing of the images in the mobile device itself. The results obtained confirm that to optimize the image consumption performance in mobile devices, it is necessary to build efficient and adherent algorithms for image processing on the device screen.

The Unified Systolic Convolution Array Architecture (USCA) is a novel design for accelerating the execution of sparse neural networks. The USCA architecture leverages a systolic array to accelerate convolution and deconvolution operations, and employs kernel-level parallelism to perform computations in parallel. The architecture also utilizes registers to eliminate data transfer overhead and improve computational efficiency. Moreover, the USCA architecture incorporates computational modeling to optimize performance, enabling the system to achieve better acceleration than existing approaches. As a result, the proposed architecture provides an efficient, unified solution for accelerating sparse neural networks.

Image fusion techniques are applied to the synthesis of two or more images captured in the same scene to obtain a high-quality image. However, most of the existing fusion algorithms are aimed at single-mode images. To improve the fusion quality of multi-modal images, a novel multi-sensor image fusion framework based on non-subsampled shearlet transform (NSST) is proposed. First, the proposed solution uses NSST to decompose source images into high- and low-frequency components. Then, an improved pulse coupled neural network (PCNN) is proposed to process high-frequency components. Thus, the feature extraction effect of the high-frequency component is meliorated. After that, a sparse representation (SR) based measure, including compact dictionary learning and Max-L1 fusion rule, is designed to enhance the detailed features of the low-frequency component. Finally, the final image is obtained by the reconstruction of high- and low-frequency components via NSST inverse transformation. The proposed method is compared with several existing fusion methods. The experiment results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other algorithms in both subjective and objective evaluation.

This paper presents the design and implementation of a high gain off-body antenna, which is based on linear to circular polarization using a dielectric meander-line. The proposed antenna is intended for use in underground mining communications, where wireless communication is often challenging due to the harsh and complex environment. The dielectric meander-line acts as a frequency selective surface, which enhances the gain of the antenna and makes it more resistant to interference. The antenna also features a unique polarization property, which allows it to effectively overcome the signal attenuation caused by the human body in body area networks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves a high gain off-body wireless communication link, which can significantly improve the communication reliability and quality in underground mining scenarios. This work provides a promising solution to the wireless communication challenges in underground mining, and could also inspire new research ideas in the field of off-body antennas based on dielectrics.

The TanDEM-X mission (TDM) is a spaceborne radar interferometer which delivers a global digital surface model (DSM) with a spatial resolution of 0.4 arcsec. In this letter, we propose an automatic workflow for digital terrain model (DTM) generation from TDM DSM data through additional consideration of Sentinel-2 imagery and open-source geospatial vector data. The method includes the automatic and robust compilation of training samples by imposing dedicated criteria on the multisource geodata for subsequent learning of a classification model. The model is capable of supporting the accurate distinction of elevated objects (OBJ) and bare earth (BE) measurements in the TDM DSM. Finally, a DTM is interpolated from identified BE measurements. Experimental results obtained from a test site which covers a complex and heterogeneous built environment of Santiago de Chile, Chile, underline the usefulness of the proposed workflow, since it allows for substantially increased accuracies compared to a morphological filter-based method.
