The proposed method outperforms existing methods on multiple benchmark datasets, indicating its potential in improving the performance of recommendation systems. In addition, the paper also discusses the importance of collaboration and standards in the field of computational modeling for the development of efficient recommendation systems. Furthermore, the paper highlights the relevance of social networking in shaping user preferences and behavior, which should be taken into account by any recommendation system.

A large body of recent works has focused on understanding and detecting fake news stories that are disseminated on social media. To accomplish this goal, these works explore several types of features extracted from news stories, including source and posts from social media. In addition to exploring the main features proposed in the literature for fake news detection, we present a new set of features and measure the prediction performance of current approaches and features for automatic detection of fake news. Our results reveal interesting findings on the usefulness and importance of features for detecting false news. Finally, we discuss how fake news detection approaches can be used in the practice, highlighting challenges and opportunities.

In this paper, we investigate the integration of the Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technology into the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based wireless system. In particular, we study the joint NOMA power allocation, user pairing, and UAV deployment (placement) for this wireless system. To gain insight into the optimal structure of this problem, we derive the optimal power allocation and UAV placement to maximize the sum-rate of the two-user (one NOMA pair) network. We then address the general setting with multiple NOMA pairs where users must be paired into two-user groups using NOMA. For this setting, we optimize the user pairing, power allocation, and UAV placement to maximize the minimum sum rate for individual user pairs. Solving this optimization problem optimally requires exhaustive search over all possible pairing scenarios, which has very high complexity. To overcome this challenge, we propose a heuristic pairing algorithm based on the minimum sum-of-squared-distance criteria whose pairing result is then applied to perform optimal power allocation and UAV placement. Through numerical studies, we show the significance of UAV placement optimization and the fact that the proposed heuristic user pairing scheme achieves close-to-optimal performance.

This paper proposes an end-to-end answer selection method using an attention-based bi-LSTM network. The approach leverages the strengths of task analysis, information retrieval, and feature extraction to improve the accuracy of the answer selection process. The use of logic gates and semantics allows for a more intelligent understanding of the input data, which is then processed using a recurrent neural network. The proposed method shows promising results in comparison to existing methods, proving to be an effective and efficient way to select the best answer from a given set of candidates.

This paper presents an adaptive rate electrocardiography (ECG) acquisition and analysis system for the efficient diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. The system integrates various techniques, including finite impulse response (FIR) filters, artificial neural networks (ANNs), interpolation, feature extraction, and support vector machines (SVMs), to accurately capture ECG signals and extract meaningful features for disease classification. Furthermore, the system is designed to operate on Microsoft Windows operating system and can adapt to the changing heart rate of patients. The proposed system has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of cardiovascular disease diagnosis, and thus contribute to better management and treatment of this debilitating disease.

This paper presents experimental results on using deep learning techniques to identify agricultural pests. The focus of this study is on training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) using deep learning algorithms to identify pests in a sustainable manner. Agriculture is a critical sector for many economies worldwide, and the use of technology has the potential to enhance sustainable development in this sector. Therefore, the application of deep learning techniques in identifying pests can have a positive impact on sustainable agriculture. The study presents promising results in identifying pests using deep learning techniques with convolution being the most effective method. Additionally, mobile applications have been developed to help farmers identify pests in real-time, further enhancing pest management strategies. Overall, this research highlights the potential for deep learning techniques to identify pests in agriculture and contribute to sustainable development in this vital sector.

Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disease that affects the central nervous system. Early diagnosis and accurate prediction of PD play a vital role in the treatment and management of the disease. This paper proposes a U-Healthcare system for the pre-diagnosis of Parkinson's disease from voice signals. The system includes the use of feature extraction and support vector machines, as well as machine learning algorithms, which are used to build a predictive model. The radio frequency technique is used to process the voice signal and extract various features used for pre-diagnosis. Additionally, brain modeling is employed to better understand the disease and to optimize the pre-diagnosis method. This U-Healthcare system can significantly improve the accuracy of PD pre-diagnosis, and it has great potential in the field of healthcare.

This article presents a theoretical framework to study finite-time and fixed-time input-to-state stability of nonlinear systems using the implicit Lyapunov function formulation. This approach allows to determine stability, robustness and convergence type of a given system without relying in an explicit Lyapunov function.

This paper presents the implementation of the greenhouse service control protocol using Python on Raspberry PI. The protocol ensures efficient communication and coordination among the different components of the greenhouse service system. This study focuses on the utilization of protocols, intelligent sensors, and actuators in the design of green products for effective control of plant growth conditions. The use of IP networks provides a platform for remote monitoring and control of the greenhouse service system. The efficient handling of payloads is an essential aspect of this protocol, ensuring the accurate delivery of data and instructions to the different components of the system. The implementation of this protocol will significantly impact the greenhouse industry, providing an effective and efficient means of controlling plant growth conditions, leading to increased yields and better quality produce.

Over the past years, Internet of Things (IoT) has been emerging with connected and smart things that can communicate with each other and exchange information. Similarly, with the emergence of Industry 4.0, the industrial world is also undergoing a strong evolution by connecting devices, sensors and machines to the Internet. In this paper, we investigate the integration of these two domains and examine the interconnection of two of the promising interoperability standards in these domains, namely OPC Unified Architecture and Lightweight Machine-to-Machine (LwM2M) protocol. For this purpose, we introduce an efficient and scalable approach, based on Docker Containers, for the cross-domain integration and interoperation. Besides, we also demonstrate and validate our interoperability approach by means of real world implementations and also theoretical and practical analysis.

Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC), Steered Response Power-PHAse Transform (SRP-PHAT) and Generalized Cross Correlation (GCC) are the well known techniques for Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation, using microphone array. However, in real time scenarios, these techniques encounter limitations such as computational complexity and thresholding difficulties. In this paper, a novel and robust method is introduced in which DoA is estimated using the concept of subarray decomposition to provide better performance with effective thresholding and minimal computational complexity.

With the development of the cloud computing and big data, massive data based computing and storage have emerged as core technologies. Moreover, a key problem to ensure data availability and analysis accuracy is the data integrity which has received extensive attention. Compared to the mature solution in the batch computing, the data integrity in the stream computing did not receive due attention. However, the characters of timeliness, volatility, suddenness and disorder of big data make the data integrity in the stream computing a very difficult problem. Based on the framework of current general stream computing system, in this paper, we construct an externally data integrity tracking and verification system for the real-time tracking and analysing of the data content and processing path of each message, and the discovering of the data integrity problem. We use the common cryptographic algorithm to construct a universal data integrity tracking and verification scheme outside the stream computing system to ensure the integrity and consistency of the data. Then we give the formal security analysis in standard model, and perform simulations in cloud environment. Results show that the proposed system can verify data integrity efficiently without compromising the efficiency.

Fraud detection methods are continuously developed to defend criminals. They allow us to identify quickly and easily the frauds. In this work, we will focus on the problem of fraud detection in banking transactions. A single algorithm may not be suitable for every problem. Therefore, selecting an algorithm that performs best in a given situation is very crucial. In this work, we give a comparative analysis of four algorithms: Simple Anomaly detection algorithm, Decision Tree algorithm, Random Forest algorithm and Naïve Bayes algorithm. We use the machine learning library (MLlib) of Apache Spark to handle credit card fraud detection. The data used in our simulation is generated randomly following a normal distribution, this data includes two features Price and Distance that allow us to distinguish anomalies and valid transactions. The performance is analysed based on the parameters of the Total Running Time and the Accuracy. The results proved that the Random Forest algorithm gave the best results and the simple anomaly detection algorithm gave the worst results.

Service composition is the main operation mode of cloud manufacturing (CMfg), but it is vulnerable to exceptions. To keep the robustness of service composition at processing stage in cloud manufacturing, this paper investigated the whole execution process of service composition, and established an adaptive adjustment framework of it. This framework consists of anomaly detection, anomaly diagnosis and anomaly handling. This framework is driven by data, which are collected from the weakest links of the service composition through Internet of things (IoT) technology and monitoring technology. Besides, all data processing and the adjustment strategies are operated by the cloud manufacturing platform.

The development of the Unified Educational Cyber Environment has paved the way for improved training and educational programs for engineer personnel. This electronic learning platform provides an integrated system for students to access interactive workstations and documentation to enhance their learning experience. In addition, the Unified Educational Cyber Environment also incorporates testing functionalities to assess students' knowledge and understanding of engineering concepts. Through the implementation of this innovative system, the quality of engineer personnel training can be significantly improved. Future research should focus on the effectiveness of this platform in different learning environments and the identification of strategies to optimize its use.

Mobile terminals usually have access to the Internet via a wireless station such as a Wi-Fi access point (AP). If the number of such terminals connected to the same station/AP increases, their throughput decreases because they share bandwidth of the station/AP. To solve this problem, some traffic distribution mechanism among terminals is necessary. In this paper, we propose a dynamic traffic distribution system among multiple mobile terminals connecting to the Internet via a special VPN server with MultiPath TCP (MPTCP). In this scheme, the VPN server keeps track of conditions of all stations/APs and switches some paths between the VPN server and some terminals accordingly. Simulation experiments shows that the proposed method can distribute traffic among multiple terminals effectively.

The fundamental problem of heat transmission in the closed volume of inert gas is an essential issue for the development of heating systems that utilize LED lamps. The challenge arises due to the heat transfer through the substrates and crystals that often lead to thermal instability and decreased efficiency. To address this problem, computational modeling has been applied to understand the temperature distribution and heat transport in such systems. Through simulation and analysis, researchers can identify the major factors affecting the heat transmission process and optimize the design of the heating system. The proposed approaches have shown significant improvements in thermal management and enhanced the overall performance of LED-based heating systems.

The heterogeneous network composed of small cell base stations (SCBSs) and macro base stations (MBSs) has been widely deployed to alleviate the load of conventional MBSs, which may also cause severe interference and large energy consumption. The existing literature generally focus on the heterogeneous networks either without cooperation or with cross-tier cooperation. In this paper, we introduce a central controller and mobile edge cloud (MEC) servers and propose a heterogeneous network with SCBSs cooperation, i.e., the intra-tier cooperation. A novel load balancing metric instead of the simple access probability ratio is introduced. Based on the utility theory, we comprehensively evaluate several important performance metrics such as connectivity probability, load balancing, and energy efficiency to optimize the overall performance of the network. Moreover, in the special case of allowing partial connectivity, the discrete stochastic optimization algorithm is proposed so that the software-defined networks (SDNs) controller can adjust network parameters with the help of MEC servers to maximize the overall energy efficiency. The simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach is valid to optimize the network in accordance with the user requirements. This paper provides a useful reference for the practical deployment of software-defined heterogeneous networks where the energy efficiency is increasingly becoming a key concern.

In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), fault tolerance is a critical issue that needs to be addressed to ensure reliable operation. This paper presents a statistical study of the energy and time costs associated with fault tolerance in multilevel and EDCR (Enhanced Density and Connectivity Recovery) protocols. These protocols are used in fault-tolerant routing in WSNs. The study is conducted through simulations of different network scenarios. The results show that the multilevel protocol is more energy-efficient but slower compared to the EDCR protocol. On the other hand, the EDCR protocol is faster but consumes more energy. The study provides insights on the trade-offs between energy consumption and time delay in fault-tolerant systems in WSNs. This information can be used by researchers and designers to select the appropriate fault-tolerant protocols for their WSN applications. Overall, this study is a valuable contribution to the area of computer networks and the design of fault-tolerant systems.

This article introduces a novel low-cost smart system of networked nodes, based of narrow beam Far Infrared (FIR) sensors, which can detect and locate strong heat sources, such as fire, in real-time. This system is able to detect approaching wildfires, and can be used in combination with active fire protection mechanisms, such as water sprinklers, in order to attempt to sustain the advance of the flame front. The prime objective of this work was to develop a solution to proactively protect small areas of interest: isolated homes, small villages, camping sites, music festivals, etc. Experiments conducted with real fire validated the proposed solution.

In this paper, a novel polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) classification method is proposed, which integrates both pixel-based and patch-based classification techniques. The main focus of this method is to accurately classify buildings and vegetation mapping in the SAR image by considering the scattering properties of the objects. The proposed method involves first training a pixel-based classifier using a Convolution Neural Network (CNN), which can classify pixels based on their scattering properties. Following this, patch-based classification is performed, where each patch is classified based on its constituent pixels classification. The proposed method is evaluated using SAR data, and the results show that the method is effective in accurately classifying buildings and vegetation mapping. The method is a useful contribution to the field of radar polarimetry and has the potential to be used in a variety of applications such as urban planning, disaster management, and environmental monitoring.

Since mankind stepped foot on this planet, the proper use as well as management of water has been a topic of much debate as well as caution for everyone. For residential communities, water management is extremely important and managing a huge system is hard. Hence, we have brought forth a system where the water flow and level can be monitored by mobile application and allows access to for certain users with privileges to access the motor controls as well as other community members to raise an issue against water contamination, water leakage, low water flow etc and check the water status. The status of the raised issue can also be tracked. As mobile phones are owned by all these days, this system creates a well-established communication between them and their society is regarding water management.

This paper proposes a novel SOCP-based automatic visual fingerprinting method for an indoor localization system. The proposed method utilizes databases, visualization, and cameras to create three-dimensional displays to accurately estimate a user's location. The method integrates visual odometry and estimation techniques with convex functions to improve the accuracy and efficiency of indoor localization. The proposed method uses a combination of different fingerprints, including visual elements, such as walls, doors, windows, and other environmental objects, to create a unique identifier for each location. The method is able to adapt to changes in the environment as new fingerprints are added to the database. The results show that the proposed method outperforms other localization methods with an average error rate of less than 1 meter in indoor environments. The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, such as robotics, indoor navigation, and augmented reality.

Technology Four Wheel Mobile Robotic is a choice with a variety of the functions in the industry and the application of the other, reliability and intelligence system of wheeled mobile robot become an option on a 4.0 generation industry. Stabilization of four-wheel mobile robot is an important case for the system control of the mobile robot. This paper presents system identification process of Four Wheel Mobile Robot (FWMR). In the first phase, it is investigating a part of the system as multi-input single output (MISO) system. The current and duty cycle of motors as input, and speed of rotation wheel as outputs. Model of Four Wheel Mobile Robot is constructed by parametric models in system identification. There are two parametric models used in this study, those are autoregressive exogenous (ARX) and autoregressive moving average exogenous (ARMAX). The models were designed using m-file of the parametric model. The best result models Four Wheel Mobile Robot are ARX model with first-order structure (FIT= 98,11% and ARMAX model with second order structure (FIT= 95,30%. The ARX model shows the best model for Four Wheel Mobile Robot (FWMR) system.

This paper discusses the use of quality obfuscation as a means of protecting hardware intellectual property (IP). The approach involves injecting a controlled degradation into the design of logic gates, which results in a reduction in observability and increased difficulty in reverse engineering. The authors propose a quality of service metric that can be used to determine the level of degradation that will provide the appropriate level of protection while maintaining the required reliability. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through simulation results on various IP networks. The authors conclude that quality obfuscation provides an error-tolerant and adaptive means of protecting hardware IP without sacrificing performance or reliability.

Distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack is an attempt to make an online service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic from multiple sources. Therefore, it is necessary to propose an effective method to detect DDoS attack from massive data traffics. However, the existing schemes have some limitations, including that supervised learning methods, need large numbers of labeled data and unsupervised learning algorithms have relatively low detection rate and high false positive rate. In order to tackle these issues, this paper presents a semi-supervised weighted k-means detection method. Specifically, we firstly present a Hadoop-based hybrid feature selection algorithm to find the most effective feature sets and propose an improved density-based initial cluster centers selection algorithm to solve the problem of outliers and local optimal. Then, we provide the Semi-supervised K-means algorithm using hybrid feature selection (SKM-HFS) to detect attacks. Finally, we exploit DARPA DDoS dataset, CAIDA “DDoS attack 2007” dataset, CICIDS “DDoS attack 2017” dataset and real-world dataset to carry out the verification experiment. The experiment results have demonstrated that the proposed method outperforms the benchmark in the respect of detection performance and technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (TOPSIS) evaluation factor.

This paper proposes a novel approach for condition monitoring of machines using fused features from empirical mode decomposition (EMD)-based local energy with deep neural networks (DNN). The feature extraction technique involves the use of EMD-based local energy to decompose the signals from sensors into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). The IMFs are then used to calculate the energy of the local signals, which are fused together to create the final feature set for the DNN. The DNN is then trained using the feature set and signal processing techniques to ensure accurate and efficient classification of machine conditions. The proposed approach is ideal for real-time systems and holds great promise for maintenance engineering, as it has the potential to significantly reduce downtime and maintenance costs. Overall, the study demonstrates the effectiveness and potential of combining feature extraction, neural networks, and signal processing techniques for condition monitoring in industrial applications.

With low cost and high mobility, drones are envisioned to be an important contributor to emergency communications. In this paper, we consider a unique drone aided emergency communication deployed in hills and mountains areas, where power-constrained drones serve as relays to improve the uplink sum rates via amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying. The channel models between drones and ground users in this communications and the ground users distributions are greatly different from that in conventional relay networks, while drones have their coverage areas and capacity constraint. By taking these specific characteristics into account, we formulate the joint power and subcarrier allocation problem to maximize the uplink throughput in the drone aided emergency communications under constrains to the transmit power budget for each drone and the number of accessed users on each subcarrier. Due to the intractability of the formulated problem, it is decomposed into two subproblems: power allocation optimization and subcarrier allocation optimization. Then a joint resource allocation algorithm is proposed. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the others.

This paper focuses on optimizing contextual feature learning for mitosis detection using Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks (CRNNs). To achieve this, the authors propose a novel approach for feature extraction that encodes spatial and temporal information of the mitotic cells by utilizing both convolutional and recurrent layers. In terms of computer architecture, the CRNN is designed to combine the strengths of both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), making it robust to variations of object location, scale, and orientation. The proposed method is evaluated on microscopy videos with three-dimensional displays, and experimental results show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in detecting mitosis. The authors also analyze the effectiveness of different kernel sizes in feature extraction and conclude that larger kernel sizes generally capture better spatial information while smaller kernel sizes are more sensitive to fine-grained details. Overall, the proposed CRNN method with optimized contextual feature learning provides a promising solution for accurate and efficient mitosis detection in biomedical applications.

In this paper, we propose a fuzzy-model-based output feedback sliding-mode control method for discrete-time uncertain nonlinear systems. The output feedback approach is utilized to address the issue of unmeasured system states, and a fuzzy system is employed to approximate the uncertain nonlinear system. The sliding mode control technique is used to stabilize the closed-loop system and ensure robustness in the presence of uncertainties. Lyapunov methods are applied to analyze the stability of the proposed control scheme. The proposed controller is implemented on a silicon-based platform, and simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach in stabilizing the system and compensating for uncertainties. Overall, the proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for control of discrete-time uncertain nonlinear systems using fuzzy systems and sliding mode control.

We propose a tool-use model that can detect the features of tools, target objects, and actions from the provided effects of object manipulation. We construct a model that enables robots to manipulate objects with tools, using infant learning as a concept. To realize this, we train sensory-motor data recorded during a tool-use task performed by a robot with deep learning. Experiments include four factors: (1) tools, (2) objects, (3) actions, and (4) effects, which the model considers simultaneously. For evaluation, the robot generates predicted images and motions given information of the effects of using unknown tools and objects. We confirm that the robot is capable of detecting features of tools, objects, and actions by learning the effects and executing the task.

This survey paper investigates the use of high resolution satellite images for river water pollution analysis. Rivers are an important source of freshwater for human consumption and livelihood. However, water pollution has become a growing concern due to industrialization and urbanization. The availability of satellite data provides a valuable tool for monitoring water quality by capturing images over a large spatial area. The paper presents a review of existing literature on the application of satellite images for river water pollution analysis. The survey explores various techniques and methodologies adopted for feature extraction, image color analysis, and task analysis. The paper highlights the importance of image resolution in achieving accurate results. Overall, this survey paper underscores the potential of high resolution satellite images as a powerful tool for monitoring water quality in rivers and provides valuable insights for future research directions in this domain.

In recent years, with the increasing amount of textual data on the Internet, cross-language text keyword extraction has become a popular research topic. This paper proposes a method for cross-language text keyword extraction based on information entropy and TextRank. The method combines the advantages of information entropy and TextRank algorithms to improve the accuracy of keyword extraction. In terms of data mining, feature extraction and training data, the method utilizes the training corpus to extract relevant features and train the model. The results show that the proposed method outperforms other existing methods in terms of precision and recall. The method proves to be effective in dealing with multilingual data and can provide valuable insights for research in this field.

The remote method of diagnosing the technical condition of complex electromechanical systems is an important research field that focuses on the development of advanced techniques for monitoring these systems. Electromechanical systems are complex dynamic systems that are used in a wide range of applications such as industrial automation, robotics, and transportation systems. Object recognition is a key component of the remote diagnosis process, which involves the use of biological neural networks to identify and analyze the system's components. Process control is another critical aspect of the remote diagnosis process, which requires the integration of control systems and microprocessors to ensure the reliability of the system. Overall, the remote method of diagnosing the technical condition of complex electromechanical systems is an important research area that will continue to be of great importance in improving the efficiency and reliability of these systems.

This paper discusses the problem of identifying and tracking the resonant frequency of a cylindrical object amidst noisy vibrational response. The proposed method utilizes multiple signal classification and frequency estimation techniques to accurately identify the frequency of the object's resonant vibration. Real-time systems are employed to continuously monitor the object's vibrational response and track any changes in its resonant frequency. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through experiments conducted on a test cylindrical object. The results indicate that the proposed method can successfully identify and track the resonant frequency of the object even in the presence of significant noise. The significance of this research lies in its potential application in structural health monitoring and damage detection of various engineering structures.

Rotating missiles using the GNSS/SINS integrated navigation system are overloaded during launch and require powering up after launch. Therefore, it is necessary to achieve inflight alignment under high dynamic conditions. With this background, as the key technology of inflight alignment, the measurement method of roll angle has been paid more and more attention by researchers. In this paper, the roll angle estimation method of GNSS/SINS integrated navigation system based on least square method is studied. First, the principle and calculation process of this method are deduced in detail. Then it was simulated and analyzed according to the ballistic characteristics. Finally, a semi-physical simulation was performed using a turntable. The results show that this method is simple, high accuracy, good in real-time ability and has a high application value.

The security of industrial control systems (ICS) has become a growing concern worldwide, with many attacks being reported in recent years. In response, the SCTM multi-view detecting approach has been developed to counter ICS attacks. This method integrates the use of integrated circuits, data models, and machine learning for training and monitoring purposes, and also incorporates techniques such as tagging and valve manipulation to improve its efficacy. The SCTM approach employs a multi-layered approach which provides improved visibility and awareness of attacks against ICS systems. This paper details the SCTM approach, outlining its core features and how they work together to bolster security against malicious attacks. By taking a proactive and comprehensive approach to ICS security, the SCTM method offers a viable solution for safeguarding critical infrastructure from hackers and cybercriminals.

This paper presents a survey of networking applications applying the software defined networking (SDN) concept based on machine learning. The focus is on the use of classification algorithms and numerical models to achieve improved network performance and optimization. The application of SDN architecture along with machine learning techniques has enabled better management and control of network traffic, resulting in more efficient communication and reduced network congestion. The paper also explores the use of prediction algorithms in SDN-based networks to predict network behavior, plan network resource allocation, and enhance overall network performance. Finally, the paper discusses computer architecture considerations when designing SDN-based networks that use machine learning algorithms, with particular emphasis on scalability, reliability, and performance. Overall, this survey provides insights into the ways in which SDN and machine learning can be integrated to improve networking applications, and highlights the challenges that must be addressed to enable the widespread adoption of these techniques in network design and management.

Pterygium is a common eye disease that can eventually cause blindness. It is important to detect the disease in its early stages to prevent severe damage to the eye. In this paper, we propose a method for the detection of pterygium disease using forward chaining and Viola Jones algorithm. The system was designed to be an expert system capable of efficiently training and testing images for disease detection. Feature extraction was performed using the Viola Jones algorithm to identify the characteristic patterns associated with pterygium disease. The system was trained using available datasets on known cases of the disease to increase accuracy in detection. The software was developed for integration with renewable energy sources to reduce power consumption during testing. The results of our proposed method show a significant improvement in the detection of pterygium disease compared to traditional methods, which can ultimately prevent blindness in affected individuals.

This paper attempts to autonomously identify neuronal activity patterns in dissociated neuronal networks using a multi-layered artificial neural network. The biological neural networks of rats were subjected to electrical stimulation and electric variables measurement, from which feature extraction could be performed. Microelectrodes were used to record the activity patterns of these neurons, which were then used as input for the artificial neural network to classify and identify the patterns. The results show that the multi-layered artificial neural network was able to identify the different neuronal activity patterns with high accuracy. This study provides a promising direction for developing automated systems for identifying and analyzing neuronal activity patterns, which has potential applications in the field of neuroscience research.

The process of web scraping is done by using an application called scraper. Various tools have been built to facilitate the process of scraper development, but these tools can only be used by programmers, while users who need web scraping not only programmers but also non-programmers. Non programmer referred to in this research is someone who is able to run the computer through the shell and less experienced in programming. It takes a suitable approach in the construction of scrapers by non-programmers. Therefore, in this research will be built scrapingDSL, a domain specific languages that can be used by non-programmers to build scraper. Scrapers built using scrapingDSL must be able to do web scraping against all types of websites with different structures and should be easy to understand, write and modify. To build a scrapingDSL that can meet those needs, the researcher analyzed the tools used in web scraping to determine the right tool for the scrapingDSL engine, analyzed the website structure to determine the need for the scrapingDSL and the translator application, and analyzed the the website content retrieval flow to determine the required language scrapingDSL elements. At the end of the study a test was conducted to determine whether scrapingDSL could be used by non-programmers to build scrapers. Testing is done by requesting 12 non-programmer respondents to build scraper using scrapingDSL.

The rapid progress in artificial intelligence technologies based on deep and convolutional neural networks (CNN) has led to an enormous interest in efficient implementations of neural networks in embedded devices and hardware. We present a new software framework for the development of (approximate) convolutional neural networks in which the user can define and use various data types for forward (inference) procedure, backward (training) procedure and weights. Moreover, non-standard arithmetic operations such as approximate multipliers can easily be integrated into the CNN under design. This flexibility enables to analyze the impact of chosen data types and non-standard arithmetic operations on CNN training and inference efficiency. The framework was implemented in C++ and evaluated using several case studies.

In a large braking environment, the head of the pilot would collide with the head up display (HUD) because of the aircraft pilot's body leaning forward under inertia. And the preload of the HUD determines whether the head is injured during the collision. Therefore, it is necessary to design a test component for investigating the influence of the mounting preload on head injury during the collision. Consideration of pilot safety, in this paper, the motion characteristics of the pilot is analyzed, and a component of head injury criteria tester for head impact test is established. Given the short-time and high-speed characteristics of the head impact, the driving method adopted hydraulic ejection. This method effectively solves the problems of space limitation and non-reusability in traditional methods. The computational fluid dynamics model and kinematic model of human body are used in this study to simulate the acceleration process. The AMESIM simulation model is set up to study the influence of key parameters on the velocity, angle and acceleration of the system collision moment, to optimize the system parameters and to be verified through experimental studies. The ultimate objective is to achieve that the linear velocity is 11 m/s when the test component rotates at a specified angle. This research can be referred to in the design of a component HIC tester and the study on optimization of fluid flow dynamic characteristics.

Since 2011, due to the growth in the amount of information, the innovation of learning algorithms and the improvement of computer technology make the application of artificial intelligence feasible in a wide range of fields. This paper presents a sketch classifier technique with deep learning models. We use the depth-wise convolution layer to lighten the deep neural network. The result shows the improvement in approximately 1/5 of computation. We use Google Quick Draw dataset to train and evaluate the network, which can have 98% accuracy in 10 categories and 85% accuracy in 100 categories. Finally, we realize it on STM32F469I Discovery development board for demonstration. The system can achieve real-time implementation of sketch classification.

Internet of things is a network of internet-connected things which are capable to gather and interchange information by using ingrained sensors. The things in Internet of Things may be any item, an animal or a person. A unique identifier is given to each entity like object, person or an animal and all the things are capable to transfer the information over a network without needing human-to-computer or human-to-human cooperation. IoT provides many services, however on the further hand threats regarding the security are also growing. This research work will implement the access control policy on each node of IoT by using context awareness. The context aware approach is included to intelligently monitor the context and behavior type of the IoT nodes in the network, which is further used to determine the rate of data transfer among the network nodes. The nodes that will not follow the policy according to the context will not be provided the access to the network resources under this access control framework. This work will simplify the node recognition procedure by using the ontology, which will be used to describe the node identity, node's network performance and data transmission procedures.

Edge computing is the emerging architectural paradigm extending cloud technologies to the logical extremes of the network for on-demand and delay-sensitive services. However, once service placement on edge-enabling resources has been dealt with, a new challenge arises: how to process enormous volumes of streaming data to provide query-driven analytics while still satisfying the delay-critical servicing requirements. To overcome this challenge we introduce StreamSight, a framework for edge-enabled IoT services which provides a rich and declarative query model abstraction for expressing complex analytics on monitoring data streams and then dynamically compiling these queries into stream processing jobs for continuous execution on distributed processing engines. To overcome the resource restrictive barriers in edge computing deployments, StreamSight outputs the query execution plan so that intermediate results are reused and not continuously recomputed. In turn, StreamSight enables users to express various optimization strategies (e.g., approximate answers, query prioritization) and constraints (e.g., sample size, error-bounds) so that delay-sensitive requirements relevant to their deployment are not violated. We evaluate our framework on Apache Spark with real-world workloads and show that leveraging StreamSight can significantly increase performance by 4x while still satisfying all accuracy guarantees.

This paper proposes an unsupervised event detection and on-off pairing approach for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) using Detectors, specifically for home appliances. The aim is to identify events in home appliance usage and pair them with the corresponding appliance, allowing for the disaggregation of aggregated power consumption data. This approach involves identifying and separating steady-state and non-steady-state aggregates, and applying testing and training to separate events from noise. The proposed method achieves promising results in event detection and appliance identification, making it a valuable contribution to the field of NILM.

Cloud computing is a distributed platform that offers dynamic provisioning of on-demand resources to the users. The rapid growth of cloud computing is due to its adaptive nature that brings enormous benefits to the organizations. OpenStack is a cloud operating system used to build public and private clouds. OpenStack consists of a number of interconnected entities that are combined to govern the processing of compute, network and storage resources. Resource scheduling in OpenStack deals with provisioning of compute resources. Nova-scheduler is a component of OpenStack Compute service which is responsible for resource scheduling. The default nova-scheduler used in OpenStack is Filter Scheduler. The scheduling approach presently used is ineffective in terms of cost, resource usage and energy cost per server. To address these issues, we propose a SLA (Service Level Agreement)-aware resource scheduling strategy which provides better gain to both customers and cloud service providers. We carry out the experiments using real-time multinode private cloud setup. The results reveals the effectiveness of the designed resource scheduling model.

As the amount of data being generated continues to grow, the need for effective tools to analyze and visualize this data becomes increasingly important. In this paper, we introduce an interactive system that uses Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for exploratory visualization and data association extraction in a data lake. This system combines the power of machine learning with signal detection techniques to enable users to quickly and easily explore and analyze large datasets. The system utilizes histograms to display the relationships between different data points, allowing users to easily identify patterns and anomalies within the data. By leveraging the power of data lakes and big data technologies, the system is able to handle large amounts of data and provide fast and responsive visualizations. Overall, this interactive system provides a valuable tool for exploring and analyzing data in a variety of fields, from scientific research to business analytics.

This paper proposes a method for estimating useful traffic loss rate based on network layer measurement. The aim of this method is to enhance the quality of experience for network users by providing more accurate estimations of packet loss rates. The proposed method works by estimating the loss rate of useful traffic at the receivers rather than directly measuring packet loss on the network. This allows for more accurate estimations of the impact of packet loss on the user experience. The use of this method is particularly important in the context of network neutrality as it allows for more precise measurements of traffic management practices that may be impacting user experience. Overall, this method has the potential to improve the accuracy of traffic engineering and network management in IP networks.

The demand-controlled ventilation as an advanced control approach is one of the recent developments in smart building technologies. The aim is the optimization of energy consumption, occupant comfort and air quality based on cost-effective, flexible, scalable, and low-power wireless sensor and actuator networks that facilitate monitoring and control of the building automation system. However, the device nodes and communication routes are error-prone due to various types of faults. When a fault arises in the network or in the nodes, the sensor nodes may produce erroneous data and the actuator nodes' behavior can differ from their expected action on the physical plant. Therefore, this study successfully explicates a novel fault injection framework as a tool that scholars can simply monitor the behavior of this system in the occurrence of different types of faults which are artificially injected or add their own desired type of fault to this framework. Then, authors indicate the fault-error-failure propagation model in component level and system level. The final aim of authors is to use this framework for their future research of testing fault detection and diagnosis methods. This demand-controlled ventilation and heating system is created based on wireless sensor and actuator networks which is more compatible with reality as the wireless communication is very prevalent nowadays and this wireless model is validated by the previous cabled model. The literature research by the authors indicates the excellence of the ZigBee protocol for building automation. In the result section, some samples from the behavior of the system in healthy-mode and faulty-mode in the format of temperature signals as the controlled variable and the comparison of energy consumption of heating system in healthy mode and different faulty modes are shown.

This paper proposes a new method for online Chinese handwriting recognition that utilizes time sequence information. The incorporation of this information allows for better accuracy and recognition rates. The study specifically examines the impact of interference that may result from the use of macrocell and microcell networks, sensors, radio access networks, computer architecture and relays. By addressing the potential sources of interference, the proposed system is able to perform well in a variety of settings. The results of the study demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately recognize Chinese handwriting in both online and offline modes, and could have implications for a range of applications in fields such as education, business, and technology. Overall, this study provides new insights into potential methods for improving the accuracy and reliability of handwriting recognition systems, and highlights the importance of considering different sources of interference in the development of these systems.

In this work, we propose an infrared visual inertial odometry (VIO) algorithm for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) for both daytime and nighttime. It utilizes images from a single downward-looking thermal camera, and uses a laser scanner to measure relative distance to determine the scale factor. The scale recovery process consists of a comprehensive logic flow to try out measurements into a homography decomposition with a multi-plane constraint, obtaining the results with minimum error, making the algorithm more robust. Moreover, other modifications, such as keyframe idea and pruning KLT tracker with sub-regions further improves the performance. Besides, the results are fused with an on-board IMU through an EKF-based sensor fusion framework. This infrared visual inertial odometry algorithm can still navigate UAVs during the missions when GPS is down or not reliable or under poor illumination condition.

In this paper, we investigate the ergodic secrecy capacity of multiuser hybrid satellite-terrestrial relay networks with multiple eavesdroppers. We focus on fading channels and examine the effects of satellites, signal to noise ratio, and security on the performance of the system. We also propose a channel model for the relay networks in order to analyze their behavior in detail. Our results show that the proposed scheme is effective in improving the security of the hybrid satellite-terrestrial relay networks with multiple eavesdroppers. Furthermore, we provide insights into the parameters that affect the system's performance, such as the number of satellites and the signal to noise ratio. Our research contributes to the understanding of the design of secure communication systems for satellite-terrestrial relay networks, which have significant potential in a variety of applications, including disaster relief and military operations.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a concept that allows the networking of various objects of everyday life and communications on the Internet without human interaction. The IoT consists of Low-Power and Lossy Networks (LLN) which for routing use a special protocol called Routing over Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL). Due to the resource-constrained nature of RPL networks, they may be exposed to a variety of internal attacks. Neighbor attack and DIS attack are the specific internal attacks at this protocol. This paper presents an anomaly-based lightweight Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on threshold values for detecting attacks on the RPL protocol. The results of the simulation using Cooja show that the proposed model has a very high True Positive Rate (TPR) and in some cases, it can be 100%, while the False Positive Rate (FPR) is very low. The results show that the proposed model is fully effective in detecting attacks and applicable to large-scale networks.

This paper proposes a 2.5D Faster R-CNN model for distance estimation. The model utilizes two dimensional displays and cameras to capture images of solid modeling objects. The estimated distances are used for monitoring purposes, such as in TV or surveillance applications. The proposed model achieves higher accuracy compared to existing 2D object detection methods and can be extended to three-dimensional displays for improved estimation. The results show that the proposed 2.5D Faster R-CNN model holds great potential in the field of distance estimation.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of pose-based human activity recognition using hidden Markov models. The review focuses on feature extraction, computational modeling and solid modeling for activity recognition. The authors discuss how three-dimensional displays and pose estimation can be applied to enhance video analysis. Based on an analysis of previous research, the authors suggest that the use of hidden Markov models as a computational tool is highly effective for recognizing human activities using pose-based features. In addition, they suggest that incorporating pose estimation and solid modeling can significantly improve recognition accuracy. This review provides valuable insights for researchers interested in pursuing pose-based human activity recognition using hidden Markov models.

With the advent of cloud computing and the increasing connectivity of devices at the edge of the internet, closing feedback control loops over the cloud is becoming a reality. This is especially the case when computationally expensive algorithms, such as model-predictive control for nonlinear plants, are used to optimize performance. In view of this, these algortihms often delegate most of the computations to the cloud. A major roadblock to closing feedback control loops over the cloud, however, is ensuring privacy of the exchanged data. Further exacerbating this difficulty is the need to minimize the computational overhead of enforcing privacy so as not to degrade control performance. In this paper, we propose several methods for enforcing data privacy using symmetry transformations. We address three different scenarios: a) the cloud has no knowledge about the system being controlled; b) the cloud knows what sensors and actuators the system employs but not the system dynamics; c) the cloud knows the system dynamics, its sensors, and actuators. The proposed methods allow us, in all of these three scenarios, to successfully execute control over the cloud without revealing private information (which information is considered private depends on the considered scenario). The advantage of these methods lies in their generality, which makes them applicable to a wide class of systems and with low computational overhead.

An ECG signal carries vital information that can be used for detecting various arrhythmia conditions. In this work, we have developed an algorithm to detect the R peaks of the ECG signal based on the Pan Tompkins Algorithm. Further, the work has been extended to a first level approximation to detect various arrhythmia conditions. Further to compute the QRS complex, the Q and S points based on the R-peaks are detected. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, the MIT/BIH arrhythmia database is used as a source for the ECG signals and the reference for R peak annotations. The algorithm provides the metric of False Detection Rate (FDR) to be 1.289%, Sensitivity to be 99.492% and Positive Predictivity to be 99.293%. After detecting the complete QRS complex, the entire QRS complex is set to zero in order to detect the P and T waves from the signal. Hence, this work provides a specific approach of P, Q, R, S and T wave detection of an ECG signal in a real-time environment. The algorithm is further ported to a low-cost ECG monitoring wearable patch to show the effectiveness of the approach.

In recent years, trajectory analysis has become a research hotspot in the fields of data mining and pattern recognition. To effectively analyze movement patterns, clustering methods are commonly used. However, traditional clustering algorithms require prior knowledge of the number of clusters and may suffer from the curse of dimensionality. This paper proposes a non-parameter sub-trajectory clustering algorithm based on entropy. The algorithm can automatically determine the optimal number of clusters, and effectively deal with the high dimensional trajectories. By using a sorting method known as the "elbow rule", the optimal number of clusters can be determined. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other traditional methods in terms of clustering performance and efficiency. The algorithm can be used in various trajectory analysis applications, such as urban traffic analysis, human mobility analysis, and environmental monitoring.

Individuals may change their opinion in effect of a wide range of factors like interaction with peer groups, governmental policies and personal intentions. Works in this area mainly focus on individuals in social network and their interactions while neglect other factors. In this paper we have introduced an opinion formation model that consider the internal tendency as a personal feature of individuals in social network. In this model agents may trust, distrust or be neutral to their neighbors. They modify their opinion based on the opinion of their neighbors, trust/distrust to them while considering the internal tendency. The results of simulation show that this model can predict the opinion of social network especially when the average of nodal degree and clustering coefficient are high enough. Since this model can predict the preferences of individuals in market, it can be used to define marketing and production strategy.

High computational requirements are commonly associated with the hydraulic simulation of large-scale water distribution. The convergence of the cumbersome iterative procedures involved has been a well-debated issue for the past decades. The large-scale and non-linear properties pose a great hindrance towards the development of online applications for water distribution network (WDN) analysis and pressure control thereof. Consequently, there has been a great interest in the deployment of model-free techniques to mimic the rather computationally expensive non-linear hydraulic simulations. As the hydraulic simulation based research is still being conducted, the advantages of model-free techniques make them more suitable alternatives. Artificial neural networks (ANN) is one of the most successful model-free methods for WDN analysis and management. In this paper, a literature synopsis of existing applications of model-free approaches in water distribution is presented. The technical advantages of applying such technique in a large-scale non-linear network are brought up in this paper.

The efficient management of resources in cellular networks is vital for the overall quality of service. The allocation and reuse scheme of physical cell identifications plays a significant role in this regard. This paper proposes a novel approach based on the maximum degree first coloring algorithm for efficient allocation and reuse of physical cell identifications. The scheme employs clustering algorithms to group similar mobile handsets, enabling effective identification and reuse of physical cell identifications across multiple base stations. The proposed approach ensures accurate object recognition and improved resource management, leading to better quality of service in cellular networks. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated using simulations, which reveal significant improvements in resource utilization while maintaining high-quality service levels. Overall, the proposed allocation and reuse scheme is a practical solution to the resource management challenges faced by cellular networks.

During the last decade, the Internet plays a vital role in our day to day life. The quality of online services such as e-banking, e-rail, e-health has been enhanced due to modern communication technology. Telecare Medical Information System(TMIS) one such online service provides facilities to the patient in which both telecare server and patient communicate with each other over existing public network connections. Unlike the traditional medical system, TMIS ensures that the patient can get health care services via the Internet at home. In this paper, we have designed a privacy authentication scheme for TMIS based on the cloud. Further, the formal verification of the proposed scheme using Real-Or-Random model shows the efficiency of the proposed approach against passive and active attacks. The low computational and communicational cost shows that the scheme can be deployed for computing application and mobile communication.

Nonlinear systems have been widely used in various fields due to their complex and inherent characteristics. Observers play an important role in estimating the state variables of nonlinear systems. However, the estimation error may occur due to modeling uncertainties or external disturbances. In order to solve this problem, a new observer for nonlinear systems is proposed in this paper. The proposed observer is designed based on the convergence theory of Lyapunov, which guarantees the estimation error to converge to zero asymptotically. Moreover, the proposed observer is applied to power systems for real-time state estimation. The simulation results show that the proposed observer can achieve high estimation accuracy with fast convergence speed. Therefore, the proposed observer has great potential for practical applications in control systems.

This paper proposes the use of augmented reality (AR) technology in the field of maintenance engineering. Specifically, the paper explores the application of AR for task analysis, real-time systems, and image recognition in machine maintenance. The benefits of using AR technology in maintenance tasks include increased efficiency and accuracy, as well as the ability to more easily train maintenance personnel. This paper also emphasizes the importance of using videos in conjunction with AR technology in order to provide comprehensive training to maintenance personnel. Ultimately, the integration of AR technology into maintenance engineering can lead to improved maintenance processes and reduced downtime.

This paper discusses the directed control of discrete event systems with $\mathbf{LTL} [\mathcal{F}]$ specifications. The authors propose the use of game-based approaches, specifically automata games, to analyze and synthesize controllers for these types of systems. The history and current state of research in the field of discrete event systems and control systems is also discussed. The paper focuses on the importance of system recovery and the labeling of events in order to improve the effectiveness of the control strategy. Overall, this paper offers insights into the innovative use of games and automata in the control of discrete event systems and highlights the need for careful labeling and the importance of system recovery.

Electronic instrument transformers are expected to play a significant protection and control role in the future smart grids. This paper aims at improving the performance and accuracy of electronic instrument transformers that are replacing the conventional current and potential transformers in the future digital substations. One of the main issues associated with the electronic instrument transformer is its poor thermal stability that affects the accuracy of the measurements. In this paper, to overcome this issue, a new wireless temperature measurement and compensation technique is proposed. In this technique, the operating temperature of the electronic transformer is continuously monitored and its impact on the measurements is compensated in real-time. The experimental results reveal that the proposed technique can effectively improve the thermal stability and measurement accuracy of the electronic instrument transformers.

We present embedded devices memory elements - from core registers to off chip-use, type and architecture before summarising their features regarding extraction techniques at scale. We list recent and on-going attack platform methodologies prior analysing their pros and cons. Particularly of importance, we address combined attack approaches, signal processing techniques and the challenges of low cost extraction methodologies. Above all, we characterise beam-based extraction techniques, starting from sample preparation before concluding on in-situ memory content extraction limits and countermeasures.

In recent years, image de-blurring has been a challenging task in the field of image processing. This paper proposes a natural image de-blur algorithm based on motion modeling and feature point matching. The kernel of the proposed algorithm is a combination of motion blur and Gaussian blur. By estimating the motion parameters in the input blurry image and generating a kernel using motion modeling, the algorithm is able to restore the original image. In addition to kernel estimation, the algorithm also utilizes color information to enhance the image restoration result. The proposed algorithm achieves image registration and edge detection through feature point matching to better handle the image de-blurring problem. Experimental results on a set of natural images show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and metrics. The proposed algorithm is computationally efficient and can be applied to a wide range of natural images, making it potentially useful for various real-world applications such as surveillance, photography, and medical imaging.

In this paper, we present a study on direction finding and signal characterization of unknown emitters using dipole antennas and antenna arrays. Our approach utilizes the principles of direction-of-arrival estimation to accurately identify the source of these unknown signals. The focus of this study is on the application of this technology to the Global Positioning System (GPS) in order to counteract potential jamming and interference from unauthorized transceivers. We present prototypes of our antenna arrays and discuss their performance and limitations in real-world scenarios. By characterizing the signals emitted by these unknown sources, we aim to provide valuable insights into their nature and potential purpose, which can aid in identifying and preventing security threats. Overall, this study presents promising results for the use of antenna arrays in the detection and characterization of unknown emitters, with potential applications in a wide range of fields beyond GPS security.

With the success of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in computer vision tasks, Steganalysis, the technique of detecting hidden secret messages within images, is moving away from Feature Engineering to Network Engineering. Deep neural networks are being proposed to model and capture the weak embedded signals, in such a low Signal-to-Noise (SNR) scenario. In this paper, we propose a novel Convolutional Neural Network based on aggregated residual transformations, which generate stronger image representations helpful for steganalysis. The architecture has very few hyperparameters to set and focus on increasing the classification accuracy while keeping the depth and number of parameters fixed. The residual skip connections further help preserve the weak embedded signals and improve the gradient flow. We evaluated our proposed CNN on BOSSbase against S-UNIWARD and HILL steganographic algorithms with different payloads. Comparing with the state-of-the-art Deep Residual Learning (DRN) based on Residual Learning and the SRM plus Ensemble, our proposed CNN gives a better classification Accuracy.

The prediction of daily stable warfarin dosage for a specific patient is difficult. To improve the predictive accuracy and to build a highly accurate predictive model, we developed an ensemble learning method, called evolutionary fuzzy c-mean (EFCM) clustering algorithm with support vector regression (SVR). A dataset of 517 Han Chinese patients was collected from the data of The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University and dataset of International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium for training and testing. In EFCM+SVR, we adopted SVR to build a generalized base model (SVR model). To achieve an accurate prediction on patients with large dosage, we proposed an EFCM clustering algorithm that can be used to cluster the training set and designed a clustering model on clusters and centroids. The SVR and clustering models were integrated into an ensemble model by stepwise functions. In the experiment, three artificial neural networks, SVR, two ensemble models, and three regression models were used as comparators to the EFCM+SVR model, which obtained the smallest mean absolute error (0.67 mg/d) in warfarin dose prediction and the largest R-squared (43.9%). The model achieved satisfactory prediction in terms of the percentage of patients whose predicted dose of warfarin was within 15% and 20% of the actual stable therapeutic dose (15%-p of 36% and 20%-p of 46.6%).

Location estimation is significant in mobile and ubiquitous computing systems. Considering the influence of measurement error caused by time difference of arrival (TDOA)/angle of arrival (AOA) hybrid location algorithm and the nonlinear optimization problem encountered in the location estimation, in this paper, a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm based on the chaos theory is proposed for the hybrid location of mobile location estimation. Taking the TDOA/AOA hybrid location algorithm for mobile location estimation as the object, the proposed algorithm greatly improves the location performance and accuracy of mobile location estimation. First, the estimation function of the mobile station is obtained by the maximum likelihood method, and then the initial population of PSO is generated by using the estimation function of the mobile station as a fitness function. The chaotic optimized particle swarm optimization algorithm (CPSO) is used to solve the optimal solution of the optimal position of the population and obtain the optimal mobile location position estimation, which makes the TDOA/AOA location algorithm have better location performance. The simulation results have demonstrated that the performance of the proposed method compared with the traditional Chan algorithm, the Taylor algorithm, and the TDOA/AOA hybrid location algorithm, the proposed algorithm can reduce the impact of error on the location accuracy, achieve a balance of global and local search capabilities, and have a faster convergence speed and more accurate positioning accuracy.

This brief studies the control problem for nonlinear systems with uncertain actuator failures and input quantization. First, a hysteretic quantizer is applied to reduce chattering in the quantized signals. Then, using the backstepping technique, a finite-time fault-tolerant controller is designed. In addition, the control input is quantized by the hysteretic quantizer. It is proved that the global finite-time stability can be ensured for the nonlinear systems with uncertain actuator failures and quantized input signals. Finally, the simulation example of the hydraulic system is presented to verify the established control method.

This paper proposes a method for accurate fashion style estimation by utilizing a novel training set and removing unnecessary pixels. The process involves feature extraction, training, and estimation using semantic segmentation and convolutional neural networks for image recognition. The results show that the proposed method achieved higher accuracy in fashion style estimation compared to existing methods while reducing the computational cost. The removal of unnecessary pixels reduced the noise in the images and minimized the interference with the training process, leading to better performance in fashion style classification. Overall, this work provides a promising approach for accurately estimating fashion styles, which has a wide range of practical applications in the fashion industry.

Mining Treatment-Outcome Constructs from Sequential Software Engineering Data is an important study in the field of software engineering which aims to improve the effectiveness of software testing and bug fixing processes. The paper focuses on the use of data mining techniques to identify treatment-outcome constructs from sequential software engineering data. The study uses itemsets to represent the various software engineering actions and their outcomes. The analysis is performed on large-scale software defect datasets obtained from two open source repositories. The results of the study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying and predicting effective treatments for computer bugs in software engineering. The study provides important insights into the use of data mining techniques in software engineering, and demonstrates the potential of these techniques in improving the quality and efficiency of software testing and development processes. Overall, this paper contributes to the ongoing efforts to improve the reliability and quality of software engineering products and practices.

This paper presents an example of applying machine learning algorithms in additive manufacturing. The study focuses on the use of decision trees for training purposes. The training dataset consists of different facial features that were printed using three-dimensional printing techniques. The decision tree algorithm was applied to the dataset to train the model, which was then tested on a new set of data. The results were promising, indicating that machine learning can be applied effectively in additive manufacturing to improve product quality and reduce manufacturing costs. This study highlights the potential of machine learning algorithms in the field of additive manufacturing and encourages further research in this area.

Feature engineering is one of the key technologies in the research of search advertisigng recognition. Most of the existing search advertising methods are selected according to the prior knowledge, which is too subjective to be popularized. Taking the advertisement of Ali search advertising as the research object, a feature processing method based on the pre-analysis of store and user data is put forward, and then the conversion rate is predicted with XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting). Experiments show that compared with other priori Feature Engineering, the proposed method can significantly improve the prediction results.

The success of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems is largely determined by the level of training and management support provided to users. This paper investigates the role of training and management support in the success of ERP systems in organizations. The study draws on adaptation models to examine the impact of training and management support on ERP adoption, implementation, and use. The research suggests that organizations with strong training and management support are more likely to achieve successful ERP outcomes. Additionally, the paper highlights the economic benefits of investing in training and management support for ERP systems. The findings suggest that organizations should prioritize training and management support for their employees in order to achieve successful implementation and adoption of ERP systems.

This paper introduces how to infer trust relationships from billion-scale networked data to benefit Alibaba E-Commerce business. To effectively leverage the network correlations between labeled and unlabeled relationships to predict trust relationships, we formalize trust into multiple types and propose a graphical model to incorporate type-based dyadic and triadic correlations, namely eTrust. We also present a fast learning algorithm in order to handle billion-scale networks. Systematically, we evaluate the proposed methods on four different genres of datasets with labeled trust relationships: Alibaba, Epinions, Ciao, and Advogato. Experimental results show that the proposed methods achieve significantly better performance than several comparison methods (+1.7-32.3% by accuracy; p <; <; 0:01, with t-test). Most importantly, when handling the real large networked data with over 1,200,000,000 edges (Ali-large), our method achieves 2,000× speedup to infer trust relationships, comparing with the traditional graph learning algorithms. Finally, we have applied the inferred trust relationships to Alibaba E-commerce platform: Taobao, and achieved 2.75 percent improvement on gross merchandise volume (GMV).

In an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) based multi-cellular WiMAX system, a suitable base station is obtained by cell search. In the cell search technique, in addition to timing and frequency synchronization, the detection of the frame start position is another basic task that the mobile terminal must successfully complete before establishing a communication link with the base station. In this work, we propose a dual correlation algorithm to improve the accuracy of frame detection synchronization. In order to reduce the influence of channel fading under low SNR, we also propose a scheme for joint blind channel estimation and equalization. Compared with the existing scheme, the obtained scheme can obtain better frame detection system performance at a low signal to noise ratio.

This paper proposes a novel method for motion information overall sensing of wearable robot based on virtual inertial measurement unit. The robot sensing systems integrated with neural networks and computational modeling are widely used to design and control wearable robots. However, the existing methods often suffer from the high complexity of kinematics and legged locomotion. To tackle this issue, the proposed method utilizes the virtual inertial measurement unit to sense the motion information overall, which significantly simplifies the process of the robot sensing systems. Besides, the method can also reduce the computational cost of the robot control system and improve the accuracy of the wearable robot control. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively sense the motion information of wearable robots and achieve robust control of legged locomotion. Overall, this study provides a valuable insight into the design and control of wearable robots and paves the way for future research in this field.
