For this, a predictive controller with inherited input-to-state stability and robustness is designed; the controller is based on the so-called flexible control Lyapunov functions and makes use of a newly developed method to model the network-induced data-packet dropouts effect as a disturbance. The flexibility of the control Lyapunov function is constrained by means of a new less conservative solution. The method's efficiency was tested in simulation on an electric power-assisted steering system controlled through controller area network and the results are promising.

We consider signal detection in subspace interference with partial prior knowledge of the subspace. The problem was recently considered by Li et al., where a subspace knowledge with learning (SKL) Bayesian model was proposed to leverage partial and uncertain knowledge of the subspace bases. The SKL, however, is based on the assumption that the subspace bases are a subset of a known overdetermined dictionary defined on a densely sampled frequency grid. Due to the so-called grid mismatch problem, i.e., the subspace bases may not be exactly on the frequency grid, there is a need to develop solutions that can exploit approximate prior knowledge, i.e., knowledge of frequency grid points close to the true frequencies but the latter themselves. In this paper, we extend the work by Li et al. and develop a modified SKL (mSKL) algorithm to exploit partial, approximate, and uncertain prior knowledge for subspace estimation and target detection. The mSKL is a Bayesian inference algorithm that can reject incorrect subspace bases, recover missing bases, and benefit approximately correct bases in the prior knowledge set. For computational efficiency, the recently introduced generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) is employed in the mSKL for efficient update of some posteriors. The resulting scheme, referred to as the mSKL-GAMP, is shown to offer competitive subspace recovery and target detection performance over a range of alternative methods in various scenarios with different grid mismatch levels.

This research presents a novel approach for improving the power quality of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems using an active power filter (APF) with an improved fuzzy logic control maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm. The proposed system is designed to tackle the issues of voltage and current harmonic distortion, which are commonly found in PV systems. The improved fuzzy logic control MPPT algorithm is used to optimize the PV system's output by continuously adjusting the operating point of the system. Furthermore, voltage control is implemented by using the APF to regulate the voltage level of the PV system. The harmonic analysis of the system is done by calculating the power harmonics in order to evaluate the performance of the APF. The results show that the proposed system effectively reduces the harmonic distortion in grid-connected PV systems, thus improving the power quality of the system. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of using active filters and fuzzy logic control MPPT algorithms in designing power harmonic filters for PV systems.

This paper introduces Apollo, a hybrid recommender system designed specifically for museums and cultural tourism. Apollo takes into account cultural differences and recommends exhibits and activities accordingly. The system utilizes machine learning and adaptation models to improve recommendations over time. Additionally, Apollo considers sociological factors and statistics, including user behavior and preferences, to build accurate data models. The implementation of Apollo could greatly enhance the experience of museum visitors and cultural tourists by providing personalized and culturally-relevant recommendations.

This paper explores the effects of utilizing extended stochastic gradient descent algorithms on improving latent factor-based recommender systems. The research is based on various data models and stochastic processes, which provide the necessary tools for accurate predictive models. The study focuses on optimizing recommender systems, which use standards and prediction algorithms to provide efficient recommendations to users. The authors analyze multiple aspects of the convergence of stochastic gradient descent algorithms, such as the learning rate, batch size, and regularization, to improve the robustness and efficiency of the system. The experiments conducted demonstrate that the extended stochastic gradient descent algorithms significantly improve the performance of latent factor-based recommender systems by reducing the root mean square errors of the predicted ratings. These results prove the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms in tackling the challenges of complex data models and enhancing the performance of recommender systems for better user experiences.

This paper introduces the Behavioral Blocks Model (BBM) for complexity-reduced modeling of Radio Frequency Power Amplifiers (RFPA). BBM is a mathematical model that aims to reduce the associated complexity of RFPA modeling by dividing the system into smaller, more manageable blocks. This method allows for faster computation times and greater bandwidth in RFPA estimation. The use of adaptation models in conjunction with BBM further improves the model's estimation accuracy. The paper also discusses the application of complexity theory in RFPA modeling and introduces the concept of power generation modeling. The proposed BBM approach has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of RFPA modeling in the field of radio frequency engineering.

Bayesian state estimation, a widely used estimation technique for power distribution systems, requires the knowledge of the underlying distribution of the system. However, in many cases, this distribution is unobservable. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to tackle this problem via deep learning. Specifically, we leverage the power of neural networks to learn the unobservable distribution from the available data collected by smart meters. This allows us to perform accurate state estimation without relying on prior knowledge of the underlying system distribution. Our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets and demonstrates its effectiveness in real-world applications. The application of deep learning in Bayesian state estimation opens up new possibilities for addressing challenging problems in power distribution systems.

Road Trail Classification using Color Images for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation is a research study that focuses on the development of an effective road trail classification system for autonomous vehicles. The research is based on the utilization of color images and artificial neural networks to classify roads and trails. To achieve this, the researchers have utilized different methods of feature extraction and visualization, to enhance the classification accuracy of the system. The study has made use of databases of images and sensors, to test the performance of the classification system under different conditions. The results indicate that the proposed approach is highly effective for road and trail classification, and it can be a valuable tool for autonomous vehicle navigation. The study can be further enhanced by exploring more advanced techniques for feature extraction, sensor fusion, and neural network optimization.

This paper deals with a PV array fed water pumping system operated by a mechanical sensorless induction motor drive. The recurrence of PV power outage causes the disturbance in water pumping. One possible solution is to use a utility grid as a backup source. The power is delivered by the grid in case the PV array is unable to meet the required power demand. A current multiplier approach is developed for unidirectional power flow control through a power factor improved boost converter. The utilization of reduced number of sensors makes the system cheap. The proposed system enables a consumer to get a rated quantity of water regardless of duration or the climatic condition. Simulated and test results justify the suitability of the system under different operating conditions.

This paper proposes a robust bang-bang controller (RBC) based on the high-gain nonlinear observer for a nonlinear system with intermittent disturbances. The intermittent disturbances are able to model the system faults and sudden changes of operating conditions of practical nonlinear systems. A bang-bang constant funnel controller (BCFC) is employed, and the largest control capabilities of the control system is explored to stabilize the nonlinear system against the disturbances. The BCFC functions with the estimates of tracking error of control target and its derivatives estimated with a high-gain state observer, which eliminates the requirement on the derivative calculations of the system output tracking error. The error convergence of the observer is verified. The closed-loop stability of the RBC is proved in a bounded-input bounded-state sense. Simulation studies are undertaken with a single-machine infinite-bus (SMIB) power system to test the performance of the RBC.

This paper presents a review on Sentiment Lexicons, more specifically the application of sentiment analysis, data mining and task analysis in the field of feature extraction in social networking platforms. Sentiment analysis is a widely studied and deployed tool to understand people's opinions on a specific topic or product. Data mining is used to extract knowledge and hidden patterns from user-generated content, which has become abundant due to the popularity of social media. Task analysis is necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of different sentiment lexicons and determine the best way to analyze and classify sentiment. Feature extraction methods have been developed to identify relevant information and improve the accuracy of sentiment analysis. This paper also discusses the role of social networking platforms in sentiment analysis, and some of the challenges that need to be addressed to effectively use sentiment lexicons in online communication. Finally, the paper covers some of the significant conferences that have been held in this field, which provide valuable insights and knowledge on sentiment lexicons and their applications.

This paper presents an unsupervised approach for segmenting Vietnamese words using Hidden Markov models (HMMs) and the Viterbi algorithm. The use of probability and linguistic features in the decoding process accurately segments words without the need for labeled data. The Viterbi algorithm is used to decode the segmentation by finding the optimal word boundary for each segment. The paper provides a detailed task analysis and applies a labeling scheme to evaluate the performance of the algorithm. The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in unsupervised word segmentation with a relatively low time complexity. This approach can be applied to other languages with similar characteristics and provides a promising solution for unsupervised word segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for detecting roads from images using edge segmentation, morphological operations, and image color analysis. The proposed method starts with an image segmentation to identify potential road areas. Then, image edge detection is applied to extract the edges of the potential road areas. Next, morphological operations are performed to refine the road edges and remove unwanted noise. To further enhance the accuracy of road detection, feature extraction and filtering techniques are employed. Finally, image color analysis is utilized to differentiate roads from other objects, such as buildings and trees. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in road detection compared to other state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed method can be applied to various applications, including autonomous driving and road network mapping.

As the world transitions toward 5G mobile communication and beyond, ensuring the security of wireless networks is of utmost importance. This requires robust authentication protocols that protect against malicious attacks and unauthorized access to sensitive information. Additionally, the advent of cloud computing further accentuates the need for strong security measures to prevent data breaches and protect user privacy. Therefore, there is a pressing need for researchers and policymakers to collaborate and develop effective security solutions that can keep pace with the rapid evolution of wireless networks and emerging technologies. Only through strategic planning and cross-sector collaboration can we achieve a secure and resilient 5G ecosystem that can withstand the threat landscape of today and beyond.

This paper presents two efficient Quality of Service (QoS)-based approaches for a resource splitting strategy across multiple Cloud providers. Cloud computing has become a popular paradigm for delivering services over the Internet, allowing customers to access various resources such as software applications, processing power, and storage. In this context, supporting high QoS levels is critical to ensure that the customer's experience is satisfactory, and this is especially relevant in multi-cloud scenarios. The proposed approaches are based on peer-to-peer computing and computational modeling techniques, which take into account the network topology, delays, and other substrates that affect the QoS in multi-cloud environments. The results of the experiments carried out show that both approaches are effective in improving the QoS of the services provided by multiple Cloud providers. Overall, the findings presented in this paper are relevant for researchers and practitioners who are interested in implementing QoS strategies in multi-cloud environments.

In recent years, data mining and stochastic processes have become popular fields of research for discovering reusable fragments in workflows. The PSM-Flow algorithm, or Probabilistic Subgraph Mining, is a new approach to this task that utilizes probabilistic logic and computational modeling to perform image edge detection and image color analysis. This algorithm is ideal for exploring issues related to resource management and workflow modeling and has a high degree of accuracy and effectiveness. This paper discusses the theoretical background, methodology, and experimental results of the PSM-Flow algorithm, which offer valuable insights into the application of probabilistic subgraph mining in discovering reusable fragments in workflows. The findings presented in this paper have the potential to impact research in several industries, such as resource allocation, data mining, and stochastic processes.

This paper investigates the effectiveness of thin-slicing of speech for clinical depression detection. The study focuses on speech recognition and feature extraction techniques, which are important components of the classification algorithms used in this research. The study was conducted in hospital and educational settings and involved the use of support vector machines, which are commonly utilized in wearable computers. The results showed that thin-slicing of speech can be an effective tool for detecting clinical depression and can be utilized in various settings to help individuals struggling with this condition. The findings of this study have important implications for the use of technology in the diagnosis and treatment of depression, and may lead to the development of more effective interventions in the future.

In this paper, we present a novel Blocked Maximum Correntropy Criterion (BMCC) algorithm for cluster-sparse system identifications. The proposed algorithm combines the advantages of correntropy criterion and block sparsity. We also adopt the use of kernel function to address the nonlinearity in the system. The BMCC algorithm is implemented by alternating optimization, where the optimization variables are updated by exploiting the block sparsity and kernel property. Numerical simulations show that the proposed algorithm achieves better estimation accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art algorithms. The convergence of the BMCC algorithm is also proven theoretically. The proposed algorithm has potential applications in clustering algorithms, circuits and systems, and indexes. Moreover, it can effectively deal with systems with high dispersion.

Manual classification of IT service desk tickets may result in routing of the tickets to the wrong resolution group. Incorrect assignment of IT service desk tickets leads to reassignment of tickets, unnecessary resource utilization and delays the resolution time. Traditional machine learning algorithms can be used to automatically classify the IT service desk tickets. Service desk ticket classifier models can be trained by mining the historical unstructured ticket description and the corresponding label. The model can then be used to classify the new service desk ticket based on the ticket description. The performance of the traditional classifier systems can be further improved by using various ensemble of classification techniques. This paper brings out the three most popular ensemble methods ie, Bagging, Boosting and Voting ensemble for combining the predictions from different models to further improve the accuracy of the ticket classifier system. The performance of the ensemble classifier system is checked against the individual base classifiers using various performance metrics. Ensemble of classifiers performed well in comparison with the corresponding base classifiers. The advantages of building such an automated ticket classifier systems are simplified user interface, faster resolution time, improved productivity, customer satisfaction and growth in business. The real world service desk ticket data from a large enterprise IT infrastructure is used for our research purpose.

Osteoarthritis is a disease of knee joint, indicated from the biochemical changes and thinning of the knee joint cartilage, which can be seen using T2Map MRI and Density-weighted Protons sequence. These tools detect the thickness changes that occur in the cartilage layers which can identify the presence of osteoarthritis and its severity. However, the immediacy of the result of these tools, whether the patient has osteoarthritis or not, is quite low. This paper presents the classification of osteoarthritis disease into three classes of severity using the random forest method. This model can be used to predict the accuracy of osteoarthritis data by 86,96% in diagnosing the disease. The data of 33 patients with osteoarthritis in Cipto Mangunkusumo National Hospital of Indonesia were used.

Security of industrial control systems is a well-known issue, and it has become stringent given the vulnerabilities of the widely available, modern communication technologies, and new paradigms such as Internet of Things. Another related issue concerns the redundancy of an interconnected industrial system, while distributing the data processing capabilities in separated physical or geographical components of a SCADA-based system. Our paper deals with some of the security issues, within the Distributed Network Protocol (DNP3). In the context of Intelligent Electronic Devices acting as Remote Terminal Units (RTU), we have studied the ways in which data integrity and data-origin authentication is handled in SCADA architectures, and found that the benefits offered by electronic signatures can be incorporated within such architectures, while preserving the performance criteria. Modern RTUs are capable to handle networks of sensors, to fusion their acquired data and deliver this data through a secure communication line to a master terminal unit. We have proposed a new architectural solution by modifying the Link Protocol Data Unit of DNP3, such that support for data integrity and data-origin authentication is ensured by means of electronic signature.

Multi-agent systems have been widely studied in recent years, given their potential to solve complex and distributed problems. In this context, consensus algorithms play a fundamental role in achieving global agreement among the agents. Heuristic algorithms have been proposed to enhance the performance of these consensus algorithms. This paper proposes a proportional dynamic consensus algorithm that takes into account the power demand of each agent in an open multi-agent system. The trajectory of the agents is estimated by the algorithm, which improves the stability analysis of the consensus. The results show that the proposed algorithm performs better than other consensus algorithms, and provides a better estimation of the trajectory of the agents. The proposed algorithm is a promising solution for open multi-agent systems and can be applied in various fields, including transportation systems and energy demand management.

Tool-path optimization has been applied in many industrial applications, including subtractive manufacturing likes drilling and additive manufacturing likes 3D printing. The optimization process involves finding a time-efficient route for tools to visit all the required sites, which is often computationally intensive. In practice, heuristics and meta-heuristics are used to generate sub-optimal results within reasonable durations. The aim of this work is to use artificial neural networks to yield better tool-paths.

In Cloud Radio Access Networks (Cloud-RANs), efficient resource management is crucial to ensure Quality of Service (QoS) requirements are met while maximizing energy efficiency. In this paper, we propose a Relational Reinforcement Learning-based approach for autonomous cell activation in Cloud-RANs. The proposed method leverages the power of reinforcement learning to take autonomous decisions pertaining to cell activation and deactivation based on QoS and resource utilization metrics. The use of relational learning enhances the ability to represent and reason about complex scenarios, while the inclusion of energy efficiency metrics ensures that the system is optimal from a power consumption perspective. Our proposed approach is evaluated on a simulated testbed comprised of a set of microprocessors distributed across a cloud computing infrastructure. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in QoS while reducing energy consumption compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Overall, our work presents a promising direction for the design of autonomous and energy-efficient Cloud-RANs.

The selecting of artificial intelligence (AI) technology for control of mobile robots is a critical area of research for various industries. The integration of AI in control systems has enhanced the performance of mobile robots in executing tasks. The application of task analysis in the selection process is significant in identifying the suitable technology for control of mobile robots. Service robots are increasingly being used in industrial engineering, thus the need to select the ideal AI technology to control them is essential. This paper explores the use of AI in controlling mobile robots, the various control systems available, and the importance of task analysis in selecting the most appropriate technology. The research findings unveil the advantages of using AI in controlling mobile robots and the significance of the selected AI technology in enhancing service robots' productivity.

We propose a user-oriented language to enable users to specify interconnections between heterogeneous objects in the Internet of Things (IoT). Based on the idea of the use case specification technique in software engineering, our language provides users with a natural language like syntax to allow them to specify when or under what conditions they want which objects to be connected. To support this language, we have also developed a transformation mechanism that automatically translates users' specification into the source code. We have evaluated this language through an experiment and a survey. The main contributions of this paper are: 1) a simple natural language that enables the users to specify which objects to connect and when and 2) a transformation mechanism that automatically translates users' specifications into source code and dynamically attaches the code to relevant applications. This paper represents a first step in bringing the IoT closer to their users.

This article evaluates the current situation regarding the development of Intelligent Agents. First, it introduces and explains in detail all of the defining characteristics of an agent, and how each trait separates an AI from a normal software code. Then, this article examines what Intelligent agents must possess in order to be successful, and outline the main problems that it faces. Finally, a few real-life examples are given in order to demonstrate the goals and purposes of a few different types of agents.

Content Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) is a challenging ground to retrieve the images based on feature description and extraction. Salient image features are the potential candidates to search and index the images based on primitive features. This paper presents a novel way to extract and describe the image features based on their object and color signatures. Gaussian of variance is used along with image convolution and the resultant features are approximated using matrix hashing. The high range frequency feature information is then separated to carry out the spatial indexes. High resolution images from versatile image semantic groups are resulted in massive image signatures which are computation effective. Principal component analysis is performed on these feature vectors to obtained reduced statistical information. These grey level information carriers are then combined with RGB channel based spatially arranged features to possess to color and object information. Bags-of-Word (BoW) architecture is applied to these information carriers to index and retrieve the images. Competitive results show that the proposed method outperforms in many categories of benchmarks Caltech-101 and Corel-1000 datasets. The proposed method shows outstanding results in complex and occluded image categories.

This paper proposes an Intelligent Traffic Control System that is based on cloud computing and big data mining. The system leverages cloud computing to process large amounts of traffic data to generate predictive models for real-time traffic management. The predictive models enable the system to make informed decisions by analyzing historical traffic data, current traffic flow, and transportation patterns. The system also uses job shop scheduling algorithms to optimize traffic flow in real-time by adjusting traffic light timings based on traffic load and traffic congestion. The system's big data mining capabilities enable it to analyze vast amounts of data in real-time to predict traffic patterns and make intelligent decisions about traffic control. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the proposed Intelligent Traffic Control System, including its architecture, algorithms, and implementation details. The results of the experimental evaluation of the system show that it can significantly reduce traffic congestion and improve overall traffic flow. The system shows great potential for enhancing urban transportation and reducing traffic-related problems in smart cities.

This study examines the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) news reports on corporate operating performance forecasting using a large database of publicly-listed electronics firms in Taiwan. By executing latent topic modelling, we can break down CSR news reports into multiple dimensions and then examine which dimension(s) affects operating performance. To offer decision-makers with a comprehensive, overarching view of the corporate's operations, the data envelopment analysis (DEA), that can handle multiple input and multiple output variables simultaneously, was conducted to generate the performance rank. The analyzed results were then fed into support vector machine (SVM) to construct the model for performance forecasting. The inherent parameters were decided by harmony search (HS) algorithm. The proposed approach, supported by real samples, can assist both internal and external stakeholders in allocating scarce resources to specific CSR dimensions to enhance a corporate's growth potential as well as to achieve a win-win situation.

This paper presents a methodology for the forward estimation of thermal risk in offshore wind farm cables under scenarios where the farm is overplanted for economic purposes. A dynamic thermal rating assessment of the cable is proposed to estimate the thermal effects of probable load current scenarios considering actual temperatures. Calculated future temperatures are used to estimate the probability of the cable being overheated. Due to the ability of the method to estimate forward thermal risk, unnecessary power curtailment can be reduced while avoiding thermal damage to the cable. Simulated results of online thermal risk estimation and curtailment show additional power delivery of 7.26%, 9.16%, and 9.67% per year for a 6%, 9.9%, and 13.7% wind farm overplanting, respectively. The additional power is calculated compared to the annual power delivered (Wh/year) with the use of the traditional continuous rating limits for the case studied.

Forecasting of consumer electricity usages plays an important role to make total smart grid system more reliable. As the activities of individual residential consumers has many uncertain variables, it is hard to accurately forecast the residential load levels. For planning of the electrical resources and to balance demand and supply, accurate forecasting tasks are critical. This paper presents Deep Neural Network (DNN) based short term load forecasting for Residential consumers. In this work, we compare the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) value for residential electricity dataset using different types recurrent neural network (RNN). Our preliminary results indicate that Long short-term memory (LSTM) based RNN performed better compared with simple RNN and gated recurrent unit (GRU) RNN for a single user with 1-minute resolution based on one year of historical data sets.

This paper proposes an SDN-enabled value-based traffic management mechanism in resource-constrained sensor devices. The mechanism aims to ensure a high quality of service and efficient bandwidth utilization by utilizing SDN switches. The performance evaluation of the proposed mechanism shows that it is effective in resource management and can significantly improve the network's overall performance. A mathematical model is also proposed to prove the correctness of the proposed mechanism. The mechanism is designed specifically for wireless sensor networks, which typically have limited resources, making efficient resource management even more critical. The proposed mechanism provides an effective solution to this problem and is an essential step towards the development of more efficient and reliable wireless sensor networks.

A new approach for designing a decentralized observer to estimate the un-measurable states of a discrete-time large-scale Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy system is considered in this paper. The interconnection terms of the large-scale system in this study is with an arbitrary nonlinear form and unnecessary to satisfy the bounded constraints. On the basis of the Lyapunov theory, the conditions for observer design which are expressed under the framework of LMIs are derived in the main theorems. Finally, an example is introduced to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

This paper proposes a secure transmission scheme in millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless power transfer (WPT) unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) relay networks. The system uses a golden code pre-coding technique to enhance channel capacity and also ensures reliable data transmission by minimizing the distance between UAVs and ground nodes. Additionally, an optimal UAV deployment algorithm is proposed, which takes into account both energy and security constraints. The system also incorporates beamforming technology to improve antenna directivity and thereby achieve high system efficiency. Furthermore, to guarantee secure communications, a physical layer security scheme is employed by employing beamforming and artificial noise techniques. Simulation results show that the proposed system can significantly improve the security and energy efficiency of the mmWave SWIPT UAV-based relay network, and achieve better performance compared to existing approaches.

This paper presents a high precision algorithm of network time synchronization based on machine self-learning. Synchronization accuracy and stability are crucial for telecommunication networks, and this algorithm aims to improve both by incorporating machine learning techniques. The algorithm models network delays and load, which can significantly impact synchronization accuracy, with a focus on manufacturing simulations. The methodology involves training a machine learning model to predict synchronization errors based on historical data, and then incorporating the model into the synchronization algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves synchronization accuracy and stability, particularly in high load scenarios. Overall, this work contributes to the development of more efficient and reliable network synchronization methods that can be applied in various industries.

Even though face recognition has been a widely explored area for last many decades, real time face recognition is still, a challenging issue due to variations in pose, illumination, occlusion, aging and expression. In addition, with advancement of technology in medical field variation in faces due to plastic surgery has also emerged as a new challenge to face recognition. Furthermore, compared to other challenges mentioned such as pose, illumination etc., the facial plastic surgery changes some of the facial features permanently making face recognition under plastic surgery even more complex problem. In this paper, we proposed a patch-based face recognition using k-NN classifier for plastic surgical faces. Experimentation is carried on IIIT-D plastic surgery face database for three different facial surgeries such as, Rhinoplasty, Blepharoplasty and Lip-augmentation to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach.

In this work, we focus on building style transfer, which transforms ruin or old buildings to modern architecture. Inspired by Gaty's and Goodfellow's style transfer and generative adversarial network (GAN), we use CycleGAN to conquer this type of problem. As we know, image style transfer usually generated unexpected artifacts. To avoid the artifacts and generate better images, we add so called “perception loss” into the network, which is the feature loss extracted by VGG pre-trained model. In the part of “cycle” structure, we adjust cycle loss by changing the ratio of weighting parameters. Finally, we collect images of both ruin (or old) and modern architecture from websites and use unsupervised learning to train the model. The experimental results show our proposed method indeed realize the modern architecture style transfer for ruin or old buildings.

The upward trend in using both Cloud computing and Internet of Things (IoT) is changing the way of conceiving information and communication systems. We can talk about IoT Cloud to indicate a distributed complex system which is able to provide IoT-as-a-Service (IoTaaS). At the edge of the system, multisensors electronic devices make smart the “things” they control also enabling the interconnection with a remote Cloud infrastructure, platform, or software through the Internet. In such scenario, achieving energy-aware IoTaaS is a challenge which needs appropriate choices in all the environmental, economic and ethical aspects of sustainability. The use of Fog computing can help to discover new business opportunities taking into account the above “green” goal. In this paper, we discuss the advantages from using Fog computing to offer energy-aware IoTaaS in sustainable smart environments. Moreover, we present an experimental use case proving the feasibility of our proposal.

We propose and evaluate the deployment of multi-core Erbium-Ytterbium-doped fiber amplifiers in conventional multi-fiber-based optical transport networks. We demonstrate system feasibility and show that design strategies like launched power adaptation and core-to-span connection optimization ensure good performance for different realistic links.

Many important and critical applications use wireless sensor/actuator networks (WSAN). These applications are spanning widely that range in several environments, including industrial, commercial, and residential. Most of these applications need a certain level of real-time communication in addition to reliable data delivery service. Data distribution service (DDS) is a known standard for supporting real-time distributed systems based on the publish/subscribe model. The DDS specification offers two disparate quality-of-service levels of data reliability, namely: best-effort and fully-reliable. TinyDDS is a lightweight and partial porting of DDS middleware to sensor-based platforms, specifically for platforms with limited resources. However, TinyDDS in its current form lacks the reliability support for data delivery. In this paper, we extended the DDS data reliability service and integrated it into TinyDDS, which resulted in Reliable TinyDDS. Moreover, we provide a prototype and comprehensive performance evaluation of the reliability functions taking into account: number of hops, number of publishers, and several other network parameters. The achieved results indicate that reliable data delivery in real-time for WSAN is possible with optimized system parameters, such as retransmission time-out value of 400ms and number of hops not exceeding 10 for an end-to-end delay ranging from 10 to 100s of milliseconds.

This paper provides an overview of artificial intelligence technology, which refers to machines that can perform tasks that would typically require human intelligence. One key application of AI is software development, which involves using algorithms to automate tasks such as data processing and analysis. Methods such as task analysis and pattern recognition are used to improve AI accuracy and efficiency. AI is also used in social media platforms such as Facebook to personalize content and recommendations. In gaming, AI is used for sophisticated player controls and game simulations. Furthermore, AI has been studied in the field of sociology for its impact on employment and societal impacts. As AI technology continues to develop and expand, it is poised to revolutionize various industries and shape the future of technology.

Soft robotics has become an important field of research due to its potential to create robots that can operate safely and effectively in close proximity to humans. In this paper, we present the design and development of a novel SMA actuated multi-DOF soft robot. The robot is able to perform a variety of movements thanks to its multi-DOF design, which is actuated by SMA springs. The force generated by the springs is used to control the robot's movement, allowing for precise control of its motion. We also present a detailed analysis of the robot kinematics, which is used to ensure that the robot moves in a predictable and safe manner. Finally, we describe how the robot was fitted with neurons, which allow it to learn and adapt to new tasks.  Overall, this paper demonstrates the potential of soft robotics and highlights the importance of developing new and innovative designs in this field.

This paper presents a new approach for determining the impact of lightning strike currents on transmission network elements failures, based on fuzzy logic (FL) and expert systems. The location of lightning strike is determined by means of lightning location system (LLS) and failures in the transmission network, sorted by type of the equipment, are obtained from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. The input data set includes two sets. The first set consists of lightning strike locations and current values between the cloud and the ground. The second set consists of current values from SCADA system before and after the fault, protection tripping information, and the state and position of the switches. The proposed FL-based solution is based on a fuzzy decision-making system (DMS), including both data sets in order to provide a power system operator (PSO) with a precise and accurate decision needed in time of emergency. The described model has been tested for functionality and correct results have been obtained, which confirms the membership function (MF) assessment and proves the efficiency and authenticity of the proposed DMS.

This paper proposes a network optimization approach for differentiated Quality of Service (QoS) traffic in a Software-Defined Networking (SDN) environment for point-of-presence (PoP) data center traffic. With the increasing adoption of data centers, ensuring QoS is paramount for maintaining an acceptable user experience for applications such as streaming media. The proposed approach addresses the challenges of bandwidth allocation and delay reduction in IP networks by optimizing the serving path selection and bandwidth of edge PoPs. Based on simulation results, the approach effectively reduces end-to-end delays and enhances QoS for streaming media traffic in the SDN environment. The proposed approach provides a promising solution for data center operators to optimize their network performance and maximize user satisfaction.

We evaluated a deep learning-based data demodulation method for multi-level recording data in holographic data storage. This method demodulates reproduced data as pattern recognition using a convolutional neural network. The network learns the rule of demodulation in consideration of optical noise that deteriorates the quality of reproduced data. Unlike with a conventional hard decision method, the learnt network demodulated the noise-added data accurately and decreased demodulation errors.

Lightning impulse parameter estimation is critical to ensuring electrical safety standards. This paper proposes a novel nonlinear least squares algorithm to estimate the parameters of lightning impulse currents. The algorithm is based on the mathematical model of lightning impulse currents using oscillators. To optimize the estimation process, particle swarm optimization is applied to effectively search the optimal solution space. The proposed algorithm significantly improves the accuracy and stability of lightning impulse parameter estimation compared to conventional algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm and its potential for application in the electrical industry.

We propose an embedded/integrated feature selection method based on neural networks with Group Lasso penalty. Group Lasso regularization is considered to produce sparsity on the inputs to the network, i.e., for selection of useful features. Lasso based feature selection using a multi-layer perceptron usually requires an additional set of weights, while our Group Lasso formulation does not require that. However, Group Lasso penalty is non-differentiable at the origin. This may lead to oscillations in numerical simulations and make it difficult to analyze theoretically. To address this issue, four smoothing Group Lasso penalties are introduced. A rigorous proof for the convergence of the proposed algorithm is presented under suitable assumptions. To verify the effectiveness, a three-step algorithmic architecture is adopted in implementation. Experimental results on several datasets validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed method.

Airborne Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is a popular active remote sensing technology that has been developing very rapidly in recent years. To solve the problems of low filtering accuracy of airborne LiDAR point clouds in complex terrain environments and avoiding too much human intervention, this paper proposes a point cloud filtering method based on active learning. In the proposed method, the initial training samples are acquired and marked automatically by multi-scale morphological operations. In so doing, no training samples are selected and labeled manually, i.e., the training samples are added gradually according to the oracle used in active learning. In this paper, the oracle is set to a sigmoid function of residuals from the points to the fitted surface. Subsequently, the training model is revised progressively using the updated training samples. Finally, the classification results are further optimized by a slope-based method. Three datasets with different filtering challenges provided by the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS) were used to test the proposed method. Comparing with the other ten famous filtering methods, the proposed method can achieve the smallest average total error (5.51%). Thus, it can be concluded that the proposed method performs very well toward different terrain environments.

Lightweight Temporal Compression (LTC) is an energy-efficient lossy compression algorithm that maintains a memory usage and per-sample computational cost in O(1). The method provides a trade-off between compression ratio and accuracy using an error bound. In this paper, we present the Refined LTC (RLTC) algorithm, which uses a binning approach to widen the search space and increase the LTC's compression ratio and reduce its dynamic energy consumption, which is characterized by CPU computations and radio transmissions, without compromising the error bound. The proposed RLTC algorithm adds negligible overhead to the memory usage and latency of LTC. Experimental results on an environmental sensor dataset have shown that the LTC's compressed byte stream can be further reduced in size by up to 18%, while the dynamic energy consumption is reduced by 9.5% on average.

This paper investigates the issue of sampled-data stabilization for Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy memristive neural networks (FMNNs) with time-varying delay. First, the concerned FMNNs are transformed into the tractable fuzzy NNs based on the excitatory and inhibitory of memristive synaptic weights using a new convex combination technique. Meanwhile, a switched fuzzy sampled-data controller is employed for the first time to tackle stability problems related to FMNNs. Then, the novel stabilization criteria of the FMNNs are established using the fuzzy membership functions (FMFs)-dependent Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. This sufficiently utilizes information from not only the delayed state and the actual sampling pattern but also the FMFs. Two simulation examples are presented to demonstrate the feasibility and validity of the proposed method.

This review paper focuses on the effect of deep breathing on the interaction between sympathetic and parasympathetic activities with special attention given to heart rate variability, entropy, time series analysis, electrocardiography, training, and frequency-domain analysis. It is evident from extensive research that deep breathing can have a positive effect on the balance between the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system, resulting in improved heart rate variability and reduction in entropy. Time series analysis has been used to identify the optimal duration and frequency of deep breathing exercises for maximized benefit. Electrocardiography has provided insight into the changes in heart rate variability and cardiac autonomic modulation associated with deep breathing. Training programs implemented for patients with chronic diseases have demonstrated improvements in cardiovascular health outcomes when incorporating deep breathing exercises. Frequency-domain analysis has demonstrated the modulation of the sympathetic and parasympathetic activities during deep breathing exercises as evidenced by changes in the spectral power of heart rate variability. Overall, the application of deep breathing exercises provides a low-cost and effective intervention for promoting cardiovascular health by enhancing the interaction between the sympathetic and parasympathetic activities in the body.

This paper presents a crowdsourcing approach for segmenting the kidney on CT scans, which is a critical step in many biomedical imaging applications. The proposed method uses volunteers to segment kidneys in CT scans and then aggregates their results to create a high-quality segmentation. The submission is verified by a group of experts to ensure the quality of the submitted segmentation. The proposed method also includes the development of training data and standards to achieve a higher level of accuracy for segmenting the kidney on CT scans. The experimental results show that the proposed method is effective and produces accurate segmentation results. This method has great potential to be widely used in biomedical imaging and can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of segmenting the kidney on CT scans.

We focus on the problem of crosstalk-aware lightpath provisioning in a dynamic, spectrally and spatially flexible optical network, in which spectral super-channels are carried over multi-core fibers with distance-adaptive transmission. The problem involves establishing a lightpath for a connection such that the inter-core crosstalk (XT) between the new lightpath and any exiting lightpaths does not cause the quality of transmission of any of these light-paths to be below an acceptable level. To this end, we analyze and compare two broad classes of schemes that aim to ensure acceptable XT levels in the network. The first is based on static/worst-case XT, whereas the second uses dynamic/ precise XT estimation. These methods are implemented in a dynamic XT-aware routing, spatial mode, and spectrum allocation algorithm that solves the lightpath-provisioning problem efficiently with the goal of minimizing bandwidth blocking. Extensive simulation experiments performed in realistic network scenarios indicate that the utilized XT estimation methodology has a significant impact on network performance, with the precise XT approach favored over the worst-case XT strategy.

LiveFace is a multi-task convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for fast and accurate face authentication. The system performs task analysis on input images and extracts relevant features for face recognition and authentication. Training the neural networks involved in LiveFace has resulted in fast and accurate performance for feature extraction and authentication. Compared to other face authentication systems, LiveFace has achieved improved accuracy and speed due to its advanced training methods and multi-task approach. In summary, LiveFace provides a robust and efficient solution for face authentication, utilizing the power of neural networks and task-specific analysis.

Vehicular transportation networks are formed by interconnection of multiple networks leading to a particular class of complex networks called multi-layer networks. These networks are formed due to interaction between vehicles, vehicles and infrastructure (like a cloud), and data exchange at the infrastructure level. The interaction between these networks, and particularly the dependency of the networks formed between the infrastructure and on-road (possibly connected) vehicles at different geographical areas, affect the behaviour of all the elements in these networks. An integrated architecture of vehicular transportation networks for a multi-commodity heterogeneous traffic in an urban scenario is proposed in this paper. The heterogeneity exists due to different detection abilities of vehicles, owing to connectivity facilities and sensing capabilities, and the mode of driving (autonomous or manual) in the vehicles. Considering the multi-layer network architecture, the interconnection between the infrastructure network and the vehicle mobility network is studied. Using game theoretic tools, the impact of path prediction via infrastructure network on decision-making in vehicles and vice-versa is analyzed. The problem is formulated and modelled as a repeated Stackelberg game with incomplete information.

Educational Data Mining (EDM) is a field that utilizes data mining techniques to extract knowledge from educational data. One of the key components of EDM is the data collection process, which involves collecting data related to various aspects of education. Data collection is accomplished through various methods including surveys, observations, experiments, and other related means. This paper aims to review the data collection process in educational data mining by exploring the methods used to collect and analyze data in the field. The paper will cover different types of data models, software tools used in data mining, and statistical methods employed in data analysis. Furthermore, the impact of sociological factors on data collection processes in the educational landscape will also be discussed. The review will provide a comprehensive understanding of data collection in EDM and its importance in the educational arena.  Overall, this paper will serve as a valuable resource for educators, researchers, and data analysts working in the field of educational data mining.

This paper proposes an approach for optimizing Assume-Guarantee Contracts (AGC) in the design of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). Contracts are formal specifications that define the expected behavior of a system, and AGCs are used to compose and verify multiple contracts for CPS design. We present a computational modeling framework to represent CPS and AGCs, which can be used to generate an optimization problem based on linear programming. Our approach includes the use of optimal control techniques to improve the performance of the system while satisfying the specified contracts. We illustrate the effectiveness of our approach in the design of autonomous vehicles, where we show how our optimizations lead to better performance and safety of the vehicles. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of CPS design by providing a systematic method for optimizing AGCs, which can help engineers to develop reliable and efficient CPS.

Deep Class-Wise Hashing is a novel method proposed for image retrieval. It leverages the power of deep neural networks to learn a semantics-preserving binary code for each image. The proposed method employs a class-wise loss function during training that encourages similar images to have similar binary codes. This not only preserves the semantic information but also helps in visualizing the learned features. The optimization is formulated as a non-convex problem that is solved using stochastic gradient descent. The performance of the proposed method is compared with several state-of-the-art techniques on popular datasets. The results show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of retrieval accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed method also achieves better visualization of learned features, making it easier to interpret the results. The proposed method has significant implications for image retrieval tasks in various domains, and it is expected to be a valuable addition to existing techniques for similarity measurement.

Saving data stored and transferred is a critical topic in modern era, especially after the evolution in the numbers of surveillance cameras in the world. So an extra level of compression is needed to contribute in solving the problem of the huge data produced by those cameras. The proposed system: “An Efficient multi-view panoramic imaging and Extra Compression of surveillance cameras' footage using Stitching” (ECS) aims to contribute in the solution of this problem by merging feature extraction stitching techniques with geometric relational matrix calculations. ECS creates a new real-time efficient stitching algorithm to minimize the sending and storing of the redundant pixels between the footage of the surveillance cameras. The limitations of using stitching on video footage and not on still images is due to the high complexities of stitching algorithms; the proposed system, in this paper, uses the projective affine transformation matrix between images of camera footage to reduce this limitations. The work presented in this paper introduces, for the first time, an algorithm to reconstruct images of each camera from the panoramic view. The experimental work of this research tests multiple feature extraction algorithms for stitching; Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), Speed Up Robust Feature (SURF) and Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) with different order of stitching, and the amount of compression per image after reconstruction is analyzed. Moreover, the panoramic view is mostly a better monitoring option rather than multiple monitors in complex surveillance cameras' control rooms. Experimental results show that the proposed method could be faster than other state-of-the-art image stitching methods and accurate panoramic image. The system also gives a better visual effect in a large view panorama due to the high speed real time stitching introduced in this paper.

Transmission of data among constrained wireless sensor devices is critical due to its limited resources such as power, bandwidth, memory, and processing. These data, generated from sensing different physical events with diverse traffic types, have to reach their destinations with a specific Quality of Service (QoS) requirement. With the increasing usage of sensors in the various Internet of Things applications, there is a need to address the resource allocation for handling these critical data while satisfying their respective QoS requirements. In this work, we implemented a Value-based Utility traffic management mechanism using Software Defined Networking (SDN) to cope with QoS requirement in constrained sensor devices. The SDN-enabled mechanism ensures that the demands of sensor data are satisfied by managing traffic while allocating queue resources among flows through a centralized controller, which utilizes network packet statistics. We evaluated the performance of the proposed mechanism in a simple and low-cost OpenFlow testbed with various sensor devices having different QoS requirements. Results show that each wireless sensor device achieved the level of satisfaction based on their required resource network utility.

DOMdiff is a methodology for identifying and classifying Inter-DOM modifications in XML documents utilizing machine learning algorithms such as decision trees. This methodology has been implemented in a monitoring system for web pages, servers and urban areas. The approach is able to detect and analyze multiple types of Inter-DOM modifications, including attribute, text and structural modifications. The implementation also includes a novel feature optimization module that improves the performance of the decision tree algorithm. The usage of this system on real-world examples has provided evidence of its effectiveness and versatility, making it a valuable tool for a variety of applications.

In this paper, the authors propose a Siamese Generative Adversarial Network (SiGAN) for identity-preserving face hallucination. The task of face hallucination involves enhancing low-resolution facial images to high-resolution ones, while preserving the identity of the person in the image. SiGAN consists of a pair of twin generators trained with adversarial loss to produce high-resolution images that are indistinguishable from real images, and a perceptual loss that ensures that the generated images preserve the identity of the original image. A Siamese network is used to compare the identity of the reconstructed image with the original one. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of image resolution and face recognition accuracy. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on benchmark datasets, and the proposed architecture can also be applied to other image reconstruction tasks. Generative adversarial networks have shown significant potential in image synthesis, and SiGAN is a promising application of GANs for the specific task of identity-preserving face hallucination.

This paper proposes a Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) method to solve nonlinear filtering problems in medium-high dimension. The approach utilizes heuristic algorithms that incorporate a mathematical model to efficiently solve real-time systems. The proposed method has been demonstrated to exhibit fast convergence with stochastic processes. To enhance the accuracy of the filtering process, discrete wavelet transforms are applied to decompose the high-dimensional data into a lower dimensional space. The combination of the POD method and the wavelet transforms allows for efficient and accurate filtering of high-dimensional data. This study makes a valuable contribution to the advancement of non-linear filtering techniques and provides practical implications for various fields with real-time processes.

This study proposes the use of an Integer Genetic Algorithm (IGA) for the optimal allocation and sizing of shunt capacitor banks in radial distribution networks. The main objective is to enhance reactive power management and improve load flow characteristics. The proposed algorithm is inspired by the principles of Biological Cells and Genetics Algorithms, which provides a unique and efficient approach to obtain the optimal results. The allocation and sizing of the shunt capacitor banks are considered as a combinatorial optimization problem with integer variables. Therefore, the IGA is the most efficient and effective method to solve this problem. The proposed method is validated through simulations on a 33-bus radial distribution network. The results demonstrate that the suggested approach provides better reactive power management, including reduction in power losses and voltage profile improvements. The study highlights the importance of using intelligent techniques such as the IGA to solve power system problems in sociology and statistics, particularly in the area of capacitors.

In this paper, we propose a novel Chandrasekhar-based Maximum Correntropy Kalman Filtering (CMCKF) algorithm with adaptive kernel size selection. The objective of this algorithm is to estimate the state of a dynamic system from noisy measurements. The proposed algorithm uses the Chandrasekhar representation to isolate the noise in the measurements, and the Maximum Correntropy Criterion (MCC) to estimate the state. The kernel size is chosen adaptively based on the covariance matrices of the state and measurement noise. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through simulations and comparisons with other state-of-the-art algorithms. The results show that the proposed CMCKF algorithm outperforms other Kalman filters in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness to measurement noise. The proposed algorithm provides a new direction for further research in state-space methods and approximation algorithms, and has potential applications in various fields such as robotics, navigation, and signal processing.

Device-to-Device (D2D) communication system is increasingly applied as an essential element in serving and supporting the Internet of Things (IoT) devices at the 5G mobile networks. Since a potential D2D pair can switch between different modes (i.e. direct and cellular communication mode), there is a challenge in identifying mode selection between communicating devices. This study aims to increase the capability of the D2D communication system in the IoT devices to match the user and network operator demands. This study aims to design mode selection mechanism based on Multi-Attribute Decision Making (MADM) theory to address the above challenges. So, the mode selection mechanism is based on Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) technique to intelligently choose and switch among the available modes. The performance of the proposed model, which can be applied in the network to enhance the quality of service for meeting user demands is tested. The improvement in the performance of the proposed mechanism is verified when the user is moving in the network at different speed rates from 5 to 40 km/h compared with Received Signal Strength (RSS) approach and Joint Mode approach. The improvement in the performance of the proposed mechanism can be obtained and compared with those of two other approaches. The results show that the proposed model has an excellent performance at different speed rates based on evaluation metrics which are delay, throughput, SINR and delivery ratio.

This paper proposes an improved robust adaptive fuzzy neural network control algorithm for unmanned marine vehicles. The algorithm combines the strengths of fuzzy control, fuzzy neural networks, control systems, heuristic algorithms, adaptive systems, adaptation models, and marine vehicles. The algorithm has been validated with simulation experiments, and the results show that the proposed algorithm achieves better performance than the traditional control algorithm. The algorithm can effectively control the heading of unmanned marine vehicles in complex and uncertain marine environments. The proposed algorithm can also adapt to unknown disturbances and adjust the control parameters in real-time to ensure the stability and robustness of the control system. In summary, the proposed algorithm can provide a reliable and effective solution for the heading control of unmanned marine vehicles, which has important practical significance for the application of unmanned marine vehicles in various marine fields.

In this paper, the testing for the extent of the lightning voltage that occurs from the actual low voltage distribution line is presented. Simulations are performed using MATLAB Simulink environment. Analyses are Implemented in two scenarios. In the first scenario, the system is considered without any Surge Arresters along the powerline; and in the second scenario the effect of appropriate Surge Arresters connected to the network is observed. The results of simulations show that in the first case, lightning overvoltages exceed the withstand level of the powerline's insulators. Therefore, the overvoltages must be reduced. In the second scenario, one set of surge arresters is installed along the distribution line and their impact on excessive lightning is analyzed in different cases.

Hydroponics is the practice of growing plants and crops in soilless culture. It is becoming more prevalent nowadays because of decreasing available land due to urbanization, and the various advantages it has as compared to soil-based farming. To study and optimize the various factors that affect plant growth in hydroponics set-ups (such as ambient temperature, light intensity, humidity, etc.), a hybrid sensor network system, with both wireless (6LoWPAN) and wired (CAN Bus) components, was proposed. The proposed system was then implemented using off-the-shelf devices such as the CC2650 MCU, MSP432 launchpad, Digilent PMOD CAN, and the Raspberry Pi 2. The total number of 6LoWPAN nodes in the intended application setup was shown to be reduced by 87.26% compared to fully-wireless setup. The system was shown to be functional and the packet drop rate when time interval between messages is 800ms drops to almost 0%. An initial design for the visualization of the web application was also presented.

This paper proposes and analyzes a mmWave sparse channel estimation technique for OFDM systems that uses the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm. This greedy algorithm retrieves one additional multipath component (MPC) per iteration until a stop condition is met. We obtain an analytical approximation for the OMP estimation error variance that grows with the number of retrieved MPCs (iterations). The OMP channel estimator error variance outperforms a classic maximum-likelihood (ML) non-sparse channel estimator by a factor of approximately 2L̂/M where L̂ is the number of retrieved MPCs (iterations) and M the number of taps of the Discrete Equivalent Channel. When the MPC amplitude distribution is heavy-tailed, the channel power is concentrated in a subset of dominant MPCs. In this case OMP performs fewer iterations as it retrieves only these dominant large MPCs. Hence for this MPC amplitude distribution the estimation error advantage of OMP over ML is improved. In particular, for channels with MPCs that have lognormally-distributed amplitudes, the OMP estimator recovers approximately 5-15 dominant MPCs in typical mmWave channels, with 15-45 weak MPCs that remain undetected.

For the suppression of transient artifacts in time series data, we propose a non-convex generalized fused lasso penalty for the estimation of signals comprising a low-pass signal, a sparse piecewise constant signal, and additive white Gaussian noise. The proposed non-convex penalty is designed so as to preserve the convexity of the total cost function to be minimized, thereby realizing the benefits of a convex optimization framework (reliable, robust algorithms, etc.). Compared to the conventional use of L1 norm penalty, the proposed non-convex penalty does not underestimate the true amplitude of signal values. We derive a fast proximal algorithm to implement the method. The proposed method is demonstrated on the suppression of artifacts in near infrared spectroscopic (NIRS) measures..

This paper presents a database of gesture attributes for zero-shot learning in gesture recognition. The annotations of the database incorporate semantics, shape and other attributes for training models to recognize new gestures without the need for additional training data. The benchmarks testing results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional systems in recognizing unseen gestures. Training models based on these gesture attributes can provide enhanced performance stability and generalization. Furthermore, visualization techniques are employed to analyze and interpret the learned attributes of the gestures. Overall, the proposed gesture attribute database offers a promising solution for gesture recognition with zero shot learning, enabling advanced applications in human-computer interaction, multimedia, and robotics.

This paper presents an analysis of vessel behaviors in costal waterways using big AIS data. The study employs artificial intelligence, graphical models, and distribution functions to better understand the navigation patterns and trends of vessels. Moreover, the research applies parallel processing techniques to handle the massive amount of sea measurements obtained from the AIS data. By analyzing vessel behaviors using big AIS data, the study can provide insights into improving the transportation system in costal waterways. The research findings can help to enhance the performance of navigation services and optimize maritime traffic management in costal waterways. Overall, the use of big AIS data along with artificial intelligence and parallel processing techniques is a promising approach for advancing the field of transportation analysis.

This paper proposes a framework for modeling time-varying proximal dynamics in multi-agent network games. The authors introduce a cost function that captures the trade-off between achieving individual objectives and maintaining connectivity in the network. They then develop a new convergence analysis for the framework based on a Lie derivative approach. The proposed framework has applications in various games, such as collision avoidance and coordination among robot sensing systems. The authors show that their framework can lead to better performance and faster convergence in these games compared to existing models. Overall, this paper provides a promising direction for modeling dynamics in multi-agent network games with practical implications in robotics and control systems.

This paper presents a Weighted Feature Fusion (WFF) approach for emotional recognition in variable-length speech using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Feature extraction plays a critical role in detecting emotions accurately, and the proposed WFF method allows for the selection and combination of discriminative features from various speech representations (e.g., spectrogram, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients). The DNN framework employs a multi-layered architecture with various neural network models (e.g., Convolutional Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory) and includes a novel feature gating mechanism at each layer to enhance the contribution of relevant features. The proposed WFF-DNN method was evaluated on a database of emotional speech recordings, achieving superior performance to other state-of-the-art methods. The results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in facilitating emotion recognition in speech, and suggest its potential for realizing practical applications in data mining and speech technologies.

This study aimed to investigate the shared effects of active body weight support (BWS) and robot-applied resistance/assistance on temporal gait parameters and gait related muscle activity. Legged locomotion is critical for human movement, and forces play a crucial role in regulating leg movements during walking. The study employed a training program that utilized a robot sensing system to provide resistance and assistance, effectively altering force levels during gait. The results suggest that this approach can be effective in improving gait parameters, such as stride length and step width, as well as increasing muscle activity in the lower limb. The findings have practical implications for designing therapeutic approaches for gait rehabilitation, as well as for understanding the role of force in maintaining healthy legged locomotion. Future research should focus on exploring the optimal training parameters and examining the long-term effects of this approach.

Image segmentation is a crucial task in biomedical imaging that usually requires high semantic and structural understanding of the target objects. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called APCP-NET, which is an aggregated parallel cross-scale pyramid network designed specifically for CMR segmentation. Our method utilizes convolution and semantics information to extract more representative features while maintaining the spatial resolution of the image. We train our model using a multi-scale decoder that fuses features from different scales to obtain a more comprehensive and accurate result. Our experiments show that APCP-NET outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, and significantly reduces computational complexity. The proposed approach has the potential to improve the diagnosis rates of various biomedical imaging applications.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) is been a huge evolution (growth) in the current years. The growth is particularly because of the availability or requirement of small size sensors, which senses the environment with the help of tiny size sensor nodes and which is used in the communication of sensed data. WSNs are usually contains huge number of huge sink nodes and a sensor nodes. The multipath routing technique is the important task in the WSN for reliable transfer of data simultaneously by reducing delay and congestion. The multipath routing protocols improves Quality of service (QoS) and load balancing in addition to the reliable communication in the network. This survey gives a brief introduction about the multipath routing and the classifications of the various geographic multipath routing protocols based on the routing information (data) update mechanism using local or global heuristics knowledge. A comparison between these protocols in terms of various routing parameters for path maintenance, path discovery, traffic distribution is described for each class of geographic multipath routing protocols.

This paper focuses on utilizing narrative text from Electronic Health Records (EHRs) for early warning models of chronic disease. It proposes a method for extracting medical terminology and diseases from these records through the use of specialized libraries and convolution techniques. The paper also investigates text categorization and feature extraction for improved accuracy of disease detection. By leveraging the wealth of information found in EHRs, this research aims to improve diagnosis and assist in the early identification and prevention of chronic diseases. This approach has the potential to revolutionize healthcare by providing physicians with a powerful tool for detecting and diagnosing chronic diseases earlier, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes.

This paper explores the promotion of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) in higher education, utilizing the Innovation Diffusion Theory as a guiding framework. Various technological innovations are examined and compared, with a focus on the benefits and challenges presented by MOOCs. The paper specifically addresses the role of organizations in facilitating the promotion of MOOCs, with an emphasis on the need for continued training of educators and administrators to better understand the use and impact of these technologies. Furthermore, the paper proposes a biological system modeling approach to understanding the diffusion of MOOCs and other technological innovations in higher education. Finally, the role of information technology in supporting the promotion of MOOCs is discussed, with a focus on the potential benefits of using big data and other analytical tools to track user engagement and assess learning outcomes. Overall, this paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the promotion of MOOCs in higher education and provides useful insights for educators, administrators, and other stakeholders interested in implementing these technologies effectively.

In this study, we propose an adaptive Fourier linear combiner (FLC) based on a modified least mean kurtosis (LMK) algorithm for canceling the sinusoidal noise signals from the desired signals. In the proposed framework, the weight coefficients of the FLC are adjusted by using the modified LMK algorithm instead of the conventional least mean square (LMS) algorithm. The fundamental reasons for using the proposed LMK algorithm in the FLC are that it provides a fast convergence rate, a lower steady-state error and a robust behavior against sinusoidal noise distributions. The performance of the proposed FLC algorithm is assessed on the noise canceling problem by comparing that of the conventional FLC based on the LMS algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FLC based the modified LMK algorithm outperforms its conventional LMS algorithm in terms of the convergence rate and the steady-state error.

Multipath is the dominant source of error in indoor positioning systems, since the reception of multipath can significantly distort the shape of the correlation function used for time-delay estimation. When a band-limited signal is used, the range resolution is often insufficient to decompose the overlapped received signals. This paper presents a multipath mitigation algorithm for ATSC DTV signal-based positioning systems. The algorithm combines sample interpolation with a multipath signal delay estimator based on an equalizer which periodically suppresses a specified number of the lowest-magnitude equalizer weights. The goal of the new equalizer is to more accurately predict the channel response. MATLAB simulations were carried out to demonstrate the proposed method and was confirmed with field-test data. The proposed approach can reduce the range estimation resolution by 60% compared to the Fourier limit.

A perspective is provided to compare the reliability requirements of Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM) for digital memory application and neuromorphic computing application. Retention and endurance are considered as the two key metrics to evaluate the impact on neural network training. Statistical measurements and network simulation demonstrate that the retention and endurance degradation behaviors of analog RRAM are quite unique when implementing on a neuromorphic computing system. New evaluation method is therefore needed for reliability test.

This paper explores the perceived needs and gains from an industrial study in cloud testing automation, specifically focused on testing in the context of cloud computing. The study aimed to measure the effectiveness of various tools and automation techniques in detecting computer bugs in cloud-based applications across different browsers. The results indicate a strong need for cloud testing automation, as it offers greater speed, efficiency, and scalability than manual testing methods. Additionally, the use of automation tools in cloud testing can lead to significant cost savings and improve the overall quality of the testing process. Overall, this study highlights the importance of cloud testing automation and the potential benefits it can provide in improving the reliability and performance of cloud-based applications.

Error correction in quantum cryptography based on artificial neural networks is a new and promising solution. In this paper the security verification of this method is discussed and results of many simulations with different parameters are presented. The test scenarios assumed partially synchronized neural networks, typical for error rates in quantum cryptography. The results were also compared with scenarios based on the neural networks with random chosen weights to show the difficulty of passive attacks.

In this paper, we propose a method for constructing a clone code case library based on bugs in software systems. Cloning, which refers to the practice of copying existing code and reusing it, has long been recognized as a potential source of bugs in software systems. Our approach focuses on using data mining techniques to collect and analyze information about bugs in order to identify and extract cloning patterns. We then use these patterns to construct a library of clone code cases that can be used as a resource for maintenance engineering. This library can help developers quickly and efficiently identify and fix bugs in their software systems, thus reducing the time and effort required for maintenance activities. Our approach has been evaluated on several real-world software systems, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness and practicality. The proposed method can be easily adapted to other software systems and can be further extended to improve the performance and scalability of the library. Overall, this study provides a useful method for constructing a clone code case library based on bugs, which has the potential to improve software maintenance engineering.
